articles.title: Giant magnetoresistance rectification by Néel vector dynamics
articles.title_zh: 通过尼尔矢量动力学进行巨磁阻整流
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We observe room-temperature giant magnetoresistance (GMR) rectification driven by Néel vector dynamics in synthetic antiferromagnets. During spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance, the out-of-phase (optical) mode makes the relative angle between the two sub-moments oscillate, producing a rectified voltage due to GMR. This component is isolated from anisotropic and spin Hall magnetoresistance contributions by its angular symmetry, with its voltages scaling linearly with microwave power. We extract a GMR coefficient of 0.18-0.20 % from the rectification, which agrees with independently measured dc magnetoresistance. Reversing the Néel vector with a dc current changes the sign of the GMR rectification voltage in a non-volatile and controlled manner.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们在合成反铁磁体中观察到由尼尔矢量动力学驱动的室温巨磁阻（GMR）整流。在自旋扭矩铁磁共振期间，异相（光学）模式使两个子力矩之间的相对角度振荡，从而由于 GMR 产生整流电压。该组件通过其角对称性与各向异性和自旋霍尔磁阻的贡献隔离，其电压随微波功率线性缩放。我们从整流中提取出 0.18-0.20% 的 GMR 系数，这与独立测量的直流磁阻一致。用直流电流反转尼尔矢量，以非易失性和受控方式改变 GMR 整流电压的符号。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们在合成反铁磁体中观察到由尼尔矢量动力学驱动的室温巨磁阻（GMR）整流。在自旋扭矩铁磁共振期间，异相（光学）模式使两个子力矩之间的相对角度振荡，从而由于 GMR 产生整流电压。该组件通过其角对称性与各向异性和自旋霍尔磁阻的贡献隔离，其电压随微波功率线性缩放。我们从整流中提取出 0.18-0.20% 的 GMR 系数，这与独立测量的直流磁阻一致。用直流电流反转尼尔矢量，以非易失性和受控方式改变 GMR 整流电压的符号。

articles.title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
articles.title_zh: CsPbI3 中碘空位对相互作用的应变相关动力学：DFT 和机器学习分子动力学研究
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Iodine-vacancy migration and association are important factors in the structural stability of halide perovskites. Although neighboring vacancies have been suggested to form energetically favorable pairs, their stability and reconfiguration under finite-temperature lattice deformation remain unclear. Here, we combine machine-learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) and density functional theory (DFT) to investigate neighboring iodine vacancies in tilted CsPbI3 under isotropic and biaxial strain. The MLMD trajectories reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of short-time hopping fractions on strain, with strong isotropic compression favoring point-like separation and tension promoting pair-preserving relay hopping. Notably, biaxial compression produces distinct orientation-dependent responses: vacancy pairs initially aligned with the compressed plane preferentially undergo separation, whereas those perpendicular to the plane predominantly exhibit relay hopping. Complementary static calculations using DFT and the SevenNet-0 potential yield repulsive interactions for all configurations examined. These findings highlight the importance of finite-temperature dynamics and strain-dependent local geometry in understanding vacancy-pair stability and reconfiguration in halide perovskites.
articles.abstract_zh: 碘空位迁移和缔合是卤化物钙钛矿结构稳定性的重要因素。尽管相邻的空位被认为可以形成能量上有利的对，但它们在有限温度晶格变形下的稳定性和重构仍不清楚。在这里，我们结合机器学习分子动力学 (MLMD) 和密度泛函理论 (DFT) 来研究各向同性和双轴应变下倾斜 CsPbI3 中的邻近碘空位。 MLMD 轨迹揭示了短时跳跃分数对应变的非单调依赖性，强各向同性压缩有利于点状分离，而张力促进了成对保留中继跳跃。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 碘空位迁移和缔合是卤化物钙钛矿结构稳定性的重要因素。尽管相邻的空位被认为可以形成能量上有利的对，但它们在有限温度晶格变形下的稳定性和重构仍不清楚。在这里，我们结合机器学习分子动力学 (MLMD) 和密度泛函理论 (DFT) 来研究各向同性和双轴应变下倾斜 CsPbI3 中的邻近碘空位。 MLMD 轨迹揭示了短时跳跃分数对应变的非单调依赖性，强各向同性压缩有利于点状分离，而张力促进了成对保留中继跳跃。值得注意的是，双轴压缩产生明显的方向相关响应：最初与压缩平面对齐的空位对优先经历分离，而垂直于平面的空位对主要表现出中继跳跃。使用 DFT 和 SevenNet-0 进行互补静态计算，对所有检查的配置产生排斥相互作用。这些发现强调了有限温度动力学和应变相关的局部几何形状在理解卤化物钙钛矿中的空位对稳定性和重构方面的重要性。

articles.title: Frustrated Magnetism from Dimerized S = 1/2 Co²⁺ in Rose-Phase Na₂CoP₂O₇
articles.title_zh: 玫瑰相 Na2CoP2O₇ 中二聚化 S = 1/2 Co²⁺ 的受挫磁性
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11772v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the growth of high-quality single crystals and the magnetic, thermodynamic, and dielectric properties of rose-phase Na₂CoP₂O₇, a low-symmetry magnet in which corner-sharing Co²⁺ dimers form an approximately triangular network. Magnetic measurements reveal dominant antiferromagnetic interactions and pronounced anisotropy among effective S=1/2 Co²⁺ moments. Broad low-temperature maxima in the magnetic susceptibility and heat capacity suggest the development of short-range magnetic correlations below approximately 4 K. The large separation between the absolute Curie--Weiss temperatures and the characteristic correlation temperature indicates strong magnetic frustration arising from competing interactions within the coupled-dimer network. Applied magnetic fields suppress these anomalies and reduce the recovered magnetic entropy, suggesting further enhancement of frustration under field. A systematic magnetodielectric response closely follows the field dependence of the magnetization, indicating coupling between magnetic and dielectric degrees of freedom. The low lattice symmetry enables multiple inequivalent exchange pathways and anisotropic interactions while relaxing symmetry constraints on coupling among spin, lattice, and dielectric degrees of freedom. These results establish rose-phase Na₂CoP₂O₇ as a platform for exploring frustrated quantum magnetism and coupled functionalities in effective S=1/2 magnets.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们报告了高质量单晶的生长以及玫瑰相Na ₂ CoP ₂ O恤的磁性、热力学和介电性能，这是一种低对称磁体，其中角共用Co ²恤二聚体形成近似三角形的网络。磁学测量揭示了有效S = 1/2 Co ² ”矩之间的主要反铁磁相互作用和显着的各向异性。磁化率和热容量方面的广泛低温最大值表明，在大约4 K以下会发展短程磁相关性。绝对居里-魏斯温度和特征相关性温度之间的较大分离表明，耦合二聚体网络内相互竞争的相互作用产生了强烈的磁挫折。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们报告了高质量单晶的生长以及玫瑰相Na ₂ CoP ₂ O恤的磁性、热力学和介电性能，这是一种低对称磁体，其中角共用Co ²恤二聚体形成近似三角形的网络。磁学测量揭示了有效S = 1/2 Co ² ”矩之间的主要反铁磁相互作用和显着的各向异性。磁化率和热容量方面的广泛低温最大值表明，在大约4 K以下会发展短程磁相关性。绝对居里-魏斯温度和特征相关性温度之间的较大分离表明，耦合二聚体网络内相互竞争的相互作用产生了强烈的磁挫折。施加的磁场抑制了这些异常并降低了恢复的磁熵，这表明磁场下的挫折感进一步增强。系统磁介质响应密切跟随磁化的场相关性，表明磁和介电自由度之间的耦合。低晶格对称性实现了多个不等价交换途径和各向异性相互作用，同时放松了自旋、晶格和介电自由度之间耦合的对称性约束。这些结果为探索有效S = 1/2磁体的挫折量子磁性和耦合功能提供了一个平台。

articles.title: Supercurrent-controlled magnon transport via suppression of the superconducting gap
articles.title_zh: 通过抑制超导间隙实现超电流控制的磁振子输运
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding interactions between different low-energy excitations is a central theme in condensed-matter physics. Magnons and superconducting condensates represent two distinct macroscopic quantum states, yet their mutual interaction remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate supercurrent-controlled magnon transport in a ferromagnet/superconductor heterostructure. We observe that the magnon transport signal decreases as the supercurrent increases. This suppression originates from a supercurrent-induced reduction of the superconducting gap, which enhances magnon dissipation into the superconductor via Bogoliubov quasiparticles. Our results provide direct experimental evidence of a supercurrent-controlled interaction between magnons and quasiparticles in the superconductor. The approach used in this study relies on supercurrents, enabling magnon modulation without Joule heating. These findings establish a new route to control magnons via superconductivity and pave the way for energy-efficient magnonic devices.
articles.abstract_zh: 理解不同低能激发之间的相互作用是凝聚态物理学的中心主题。磁振子和超导凝聚态代表两种不同的宏观量子态，但它们之间的相互作用在很大程度上仍未被探索。在这里，我们展示了铁磁体/超导体异质结构中的超电流控制的磁振子输运。我们观察到磁振子传输信号随着超电流的增加而减少。这种抑制源于超电流引起的超导能隙减小，从而通过博戈留波夫准粒子增强了磁振子耗散到超导体中。我们的结果提供了超导体中磁振子和准粒子之间超电流控制相互作用的直接实验证据。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 理解不同低能激发之间的相互作用是凝聚态物理学的中心主题。磁振子和超导凝聚态代表两种不同的宏观量子态，但它们之间的相互作用在很大程度上仍未被探索。在这里，我们展示了铁磁体/超导体异质结构中的超电流控制的磁振子输运。我们观察到磁振子传输信号随着超电流的增加而减少。这种抑制源于超电流引起的超导能隙减小，从而通过博戈留波夫准粒子增强了磁振子耗散到超导体中。我们的结果提供了超导体中磁振子和准粒子之间超电流控制相互作用的直接实验证据。本研究中使用的方法依赖于超电流，无需焦耳加热即可实现磁振子调制。这些发现建立了一条通过超导控制磁振子的新途径，并为节能磁振子设备铺平了道路。

articles.title: The Photonic Bath at Infinity: Foundations, Derivations, and Consistency Checks
articles.title_zh: 无限远的光子浴：基础、推导和一致性检查
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The photonic bath at infinity represents the unbounded electromagnetic environment as an effective reservoir in the nonequilibrium Green's function (NEGF) formalism. It accounts for outgoing radiation and incoming electromagnetic fluctuations, allowing radiative transport to be described consistently. We clarify how environmental fluctuations are incorporated without double-counting the outgoing radiation response already contained in the free retarded Green's function. We develop four complementary approaches to deriving the bath self-energy: infinitesimal environmental absorption, semi-infinite leads, inversion of the free Green's function, and sesquilinear forms with outgoing radiation boundary conditions. In particular, we present an explicit three-site matrix inversion for a planar geometry and introduce a sesquilinear form that relates the bath self-energy to the Silver--Müller radiation condition. We establish the connections among these approaches and obtain explicit bath self-energies for one-dimensional, planar, and spherical geometries. The resulting bath self-energies reproduce the Planck spectrum, the Stefan--Boltzmann law, and radiation pressure, and provide the radiative contribution required for energy conservation in photon NEGF.
articles.abstract_zh: 无穷远处的光子浴将无界电磁环境表示为非平衡格林函数（ NEGF ）形式中的有效储层。它考虑了传出的辐射和传入的电磁波动，从而可以一致地描述辐射传输。我们阐明了如何在不重复计算自由延迟Green函数中已包含的输出辐射响应的情况下合并环境波动。我们开发了四种互补的方法来导出浴池自能：无穷小的环境吸收，半无限引线，自由格林函数的反演，以及具有射出辐射边界条件的半线性形式。特别是，我们提出了平面几何形状的显式三位矩阵反演，并引入了一种半线性形式，将浴自能与银-穆勒辐射条件联系起来。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 无穷远处的光子浴将无界电磁环境表示为非平衡格林函数（ NEGF ）形式中的有效储层。它考虑了传出的辐射和传入的电磁波动，从而可以一致地描述辐射传输。我们阐明了如何在不重复计算自由延迟Green函数中已包含的输出辐射响应的情况下合并环境波动。我们开发了四种互补的方法来导出浴池自能：无穷小的环境吸收，半无限引线，自由格林函数的反演，以及具有射出辐射边界条件的半线性形式。特别是，我们提出了平面几何形状的显式三位矩阵反演，并引入了一种半线性形式，将浴自能与银-穆勒辐射条件联系起来。我们建立了这些方法之间的联系，并获得了一维、平面和球形几何形状的显式浴室自我能量。由此产生的浴自能量再现了普朗克光谱、Stefan-Boltzmann定律和辐射压力，并提供了光子NEGF节能所需的辐射贡献。

articles.title: How Path Integral Diffusion Decides a Finite Spin Glass
articles.title_zh: 路径积分扩散如何决定有限旋转玻璃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When an AI diffusion-type generator samples a frustrated spin glass, which macroscopic alternatives does it decide first, and when? We study this for bridge-diffusion models of the Path Integral Diffusion (PID) type started from a point source. We show that every isotropic PID is a time-changed Gaussian stochastic localization, and conversely every signal-to-noise schedule is realized by a PID protocol. What a continuous-time generator decides therefore does not depend on the protocol, which only sets when and at what cost. We describe the generator's state by its partial commitments: the probabilities it assigns, at each moment, to nested classes of configurations fixed by the target. The partial commitments are martingales that move only along class contrasts. Their ensemble average gives the information about each level at an exact rate set by squared magnetization contrasts. Each split is decided, approximately, like a binary Gaussian channel at signal-to-noise ratio 1.04/λ_P, with λ_P the leading eigenvalue of the parent's correlation matrix. The theory is applied to Bethe-lattice and Sherrington--Kirkpatrick (SK) glasses with up to 64 spins. It is observed generically that a trajectory first shifts its weight to one of the two mirror halves of the zero-field measure and then to the glassy classes inside it. These classes appear near the glass transition and keep their identity on cooling. Nested glassy levels have similar λ_P and are decided together, so a trajectory commits in one or two distinct events---the mirror choice and a compound glassy decision---which separate further with coupling and size, as the spectra predict. For a generator that takes finitely many steps, the protocol matters through the late, local stage rather than the macroscopic decisions.
articles.abstract_zh: 当人工智能扩散型发生器对沮丧的自旋玻璃进行采样时，它首先决定哪些宏观替代方案，以及何时决定？我们研究了从点源开始的路径积分扩散（ PID ）类型的桥扩散模型。我们证明了每个各向同性PID都是一个随时间变化的高斯随机定位，相反，每个信噪比调度都是通过PID协议实现的。因此，连续时间生成器决定的内容不取决于协议，协议仅设置何时以及以何种成本进行设置。我们通过其部分承诺来描述生成器的状态：它在每个时刻分配给目标固定的嵌套类配置的概率。部分承诺是只沿着阶级对比移动的貂。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 当人工智能扩散型发生器对沮丧的自旋玻璃进行采样时，它首先决定哪些宏观替代方案，以及何时决定？我们研究了从点源开始的路径积分扩散（ PID ）类型的桥扩散模型。我们证明了每个各向同性PID都是一个随时间变化的高斯随机定位，相反，每个信噪比调度都是通过PID协议实现的。因此，连续时间生成器决定的内容不取决于协议，协议仅设置何时以及以何种成本进行设置。我们通过其部分承诺来描述生成器的状态：它在每个时刻分配给目标固定的嵌套类配置的概率。部分承诺是只沿着阶级对比移动的貂。他们的集合平均值以平方磁化对比度设定的精确速率提供有关每个级别的信息。每个分割大致像信噪比为1.04/λ_P的二进制高斯信道一样被决定，其中λ_P是父相关矩阵的前导特征值。该理论应用于Bethe-lattice和Sherrington-Kirkpatrick （ SK ）眼镜，最多可旋转64圈。一般观察到，轨迹首先将其权重转移到零场测量的两个镜像半之一，然后转移到其内部的玻璃类。这些类出现在玻璃转换附近，并保持其冷却特性。嵌套的玻璃质水平具有相似的λ_P ，并且是共同决定的，因此轨迹在一个或两个不同的事件中提交-镜像选择和复合玻璃质决策-正如光谱预测的那样，它们通过耦合和大小进一步分离。对于需要有限步骤的生成器，协议在后期、局部阶段而不是宏观决策中起重要作用。

articles.title: Magnetotropic signatures of Fulde-Ferrell Pairing in a Pauli-limited superconductor
articles.title_zh: Pauli-受限超导体中Fulde-Ferrell配对的向磁性特征
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resonant torsion magnetometry measures the angular curvature of the free energy and is sensitive to magnetic anisotropy. We calculate its response for a clean Pauli-limited superconductor with single-plane-wave Fulde-Ferrell pairing. Field rotation drives a first-order transition from the uniform condensate into the finite-momentum phase and a continuous transition into the normal state. The first-order line produces a sharp softening whose integrated weight is fixed by the magnetization jump, so the dip alone does not identify finite momentum. The distinguishing response is a broad softening inside the Fulde-Ferrell phase, caused by relaxation of the gap and pairing momentum, followed by a finite step at the upper critical field.
articles.abstract_zh: 共振扭转磁强计测量自由能的角曲率，对磁各向异性敏感。我们计算了具有单平面波Fulde-Ferrell配对的干净的泡利限制超导体的响应。场旋转驱动从均匀冷凝物到有限动量相的一阶过渡，并连续过渡到正常状态。一阶线产生锐利软化，其积分重量由磁化跳跃固定，因此仅倾斜不能识别有限动量。区别性反应是Fulde-Ferrell相内广泛的软化，由间隙的松弛和配对动量引起，然后在上临界场的有限步骤。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 共振扭转磁强计测量自由能的角曲率，对磁各向异性敏感。我们计算了具有单平面波Fulde-Ferrell配对的干净的泡利限制超导体的响应。场旋转驱动从均匀冷凝物到有限动量相的一阶过渡，并连续过渡到正常状态。一阶线产生锐利软化，其积分重量由磁化跳跃固定，因此仅倾斜不能识别有限动量。区别性反应是Fulde-Ferrell相内广泛的软化，由间隙的松弛和配对动量引起，然后在上临界场的有限步骤。

articles.title: Where reconfiguration makes a structure stronger
articles.title_zh: 重新配置使结构更强大
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanical metamaterials can reconfigure on command and learn, so adaptation is a central promise of the field. Can reconfiguration make a metamaterial stronger? The answer depends on the comparison. Against the best fixed design of the same mass, the advantage of reconfiguring is often exactly zero. Reconfiguring helps only if the self-stress the actuators add lowers every member at its limit simultaneously. It vanishes where a member at its limit is one no self-stress can change, which the geometry fixes, or where those members are coupled so that lowering one raises another, which depends on the geometry and the loads together. Where neither block applies the gain can be large, as in a twelve-spoke hub with its worst member utilisation reduced by 29.1%. Whether reconfiguration is worthwhile is decided by how the self-stress of a structure meets the members setting its capacity under load, and can be tested in advance.
articles.abstract_zh: 机械超材料可以根据命令重新配置和学习，因此适应是该领域的核心承诺。重构可以使超材料更强大吗？答案取决于对比。针对相同质量的最佳固定设计，重新配置的优势通常为零。只有当致动器增加的自应力同时降低每个构件的极限时，重新配置才会有所帮助。当构件处于其极限时，它会消失，没有自应力可以改变，几何形状固定，或者这些构件耦合在一起，以便降低一个构件会提高另一个构件，这取决于几何形状和负载。如果两个区块都没有应用，则增益可能很大，例如在十二辐轮毂中，其最差成员利用率降低了29.1%。

articles.title: Spatial effects of Kuramoto modeling on the power-grid frequencies
articles.title_zh: Kuramoto建模对电网频率的空间效应
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatial coupling and heterogeneity can generate complex power-grid frequency dynamics. We investigate the contributions of spatial structure, intrinsic nonlinear dynamics, and external driving using the Kuramoto model (KM), with and without uncorrelated noise, and compare its predictions with real-grid measurements. We analyse one month of 100 ms frequency measurements from 16 Hungarian transmission-grid sites and simulate the KM on a 387-node transmission network and two-dimensional lattices. The measured power spectra exhibit two scaling regimes, with exponents of approximately 1.63 and 2.23. One-second frequency increments decorrelate rapidly, while correlations of their local inverse variance decay slowly, initially as a power law, τ⁻⁰.²⁶⁽²⁾, up to 15 minutes. A superstatistical Gaussian mixture based on measured local variances captures much of the non-Gaussian increment distribution, but not the rare extreme events. We also estimate the non-stationary long-time frequency autocorrelation exponent. KM simulations on low-dimensional networks exhibit algebraically decaying autocorrelations and power spectra, consistent with the measurements and the Wiener-Khinchin relation in the steady state. On the heterogeneous transmission network, partial synchronization and frequency locking produce persistent spatial patterns and multi-peaked frequency distributions. However, neither deterministic KM dynamics nor independent Gaussian driving reproduces the measured spectra and increment statistics simultaneously. Moreover, empirical frequency fluctuations are largely shared across substations, whereas simulated fluctuations mainly reflect relative node motion. These findings suggest that spatially coupled nonlinear dynamics contribute to observed frequency fluctuations alongside external driving, including 15-minute power dispatches.
articles.abstract_zh: 空间耦合和非均匀性会产生复杂的电网频率动态。我们使用Kuramoto模型（ KM ）研究空间结构、固有非线性动力学和外部驱动的贡献，有无不相关噪声，并将其预测与实际网格测量结果进行比较。我们分析了来自16个匈牙利传输电网站点的一个月100毫秒频率测量值，并在387节点的传输网络和二维晶格上模拟了KM。测量的功率谱表现出两种缩放模式，指数约为1.63和2.23。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 空间耦合和非均匀性会产生复杂的电网频率动态。我们使用Kuramoto模型（ KM ）研究空间结构、固有非线性动力学和外部驱动的贡献，有无不相关噪声，并将其预测与实际网格测量结果进行比较。我们分析了来自16个匈牙利传输电网站点的一个月100毫秒频率测量值，并在387节点的传输网络和二维晶格上模拟了KM。测量的功率谱表现出两种缩放模式，指数约为1.63和2.23。一秒钟的频率增量迅速去相关，而其局部逆方差的相关性衰减缓慢，最初作为幂定律， τ * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *基于测量的局部方差的超统计高斯混合物捕获了大部分非高斯增量分布，但不捕获罕见的极端事件。我们还估计了非平稳长时间频率自相关指数。低维网络上的KM模拟显示出代数衰减的自相关和功率谱，与稳态下的测量和维纳-欣钦关系一致。在异构传输网络上，部分同步和频率锁定产生持久的空间模式和多峰频率分布。然而，无论是确定性的KM动力学还是独立的高斯驱动，都不能同时再现测量的光谱和增量统计数据。此外，经验频率波动主要在各变电站之间共享，而模拟波动主要反映相对节点运动。这些发现表明，空间耦合的非线性动力学与外部驱动（包括15分钟的电力调度）一起导致观察到的频率波动。

articles.title: Scaling up spin complexity in ultracold assembled molecules: association and quantum chemistry of Cr-bearing diatomics
articles.title_zh: 扩大超冷装配分子的自旋复杂性：含铬硅藻的缔合和量子化学
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The availability of ever more atomic elements in the ultracold regime potentially enables the extension of molecule assembly well beyond bi-alkali systems to targeted chemical species for novel quantum science and technologies. The concurrent need for single-quantum-state control and molecular constants from emphab initio calculations, especially for previously unexplored species, creates a trade-off between complexity and feasibility. Here, we address this challenge and exploit inter-isotope Feshbach spectroscopy as a tool to study three chromium-bearing diatomics (⁶Li^XCr, ⁵⁰,⁵²Cr₂, and ⁵³Cr₂) at different levels of complexity. The extracted molecular properties, including the number of vibrational levels and the dispersion coefficients, allow us to assess quantum chemistry methods. Moreover, our understanding of atomic scattering allows us to assemble LiCr and Cr₂ molecules and clarify the observed association pathways with quantum state selectivity. Our results suggest unique prospects for the Li-Cr and Cr-Cr systems, and, more importantly, the experimental viability of a wider class of assembled high-spin molecules for many-body physics and precision measurements.
articles.abstract_zh: 超冷体系中越来越多的原子元素的可用性可能使分子组装远远超出双碱系统的范围，扩展到新型量子科学和技术的目标化学物质。同时需要从头开始计算单量子态控制和分子常数，特别是对于以前未探索的物种，在复杂性和可行性之间进行权衡。在这里，我们应对这一挑战，并利用同位素间费什巴赫光谱作为工具，在不同复杂度水平下研究三种含铬硅藻组学（ Li ^ XCr、XCr、XCr、Cr ₂和Cr ₂ ）。提取的分子特性，包括振动水平的数量和色散系数，使我们能够评估量子化学方法。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 超冷体系中越来越多的原子元素的可用性可能使分子组装远远超出双碱系统的范围，扩展到新型量子科学和技术的目标化学物质。同时需要从头开始计算单量子态控制和分子常数，特别是对于以前未探索的物种，在复杂性和可行性之间进行权衡。在这里，我们应对这一挑战，并利用同位素间费什巴赫光谱作为工具，在不同复杂度水平下研究三种含铬硅藻组学（ Li ^ XCr、XCr、XCr、Cr ₂和Cr ₂ ）。提取的分子特性，包括振动水平的数量和色散系数，使我们能够评估量子化学方法。此外，我们对原子散射的理解使我们能够组装LiCr和Cr ₂分子，并用量子态选择性澄清观察到的缔合途径。我们的研究结果表明了Li-Cr和Cr-Cr系统的独特前景，更重要的是，更广泛的组装高自旋分子用于多体物理和精密测量的实验可行性。

articles.title: Lattice Commensurability and Majorana sectors of Pfaffian--Anti-Pfaffian interfaces
articles.title_zh: Pfaffian的Lattice Commensurability和Majorana扇区--Anti-Pfaffian接口
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Pfaffian and anti-Pfaffian non-Abelian fractional quantum anomalous Hall states in half-filled moiré lattice systems. Owing to crystal-momentum conservation modulo a reciprocal lattice vector, these lattice systems admit coupled-wire constructions of the two phases without requiring spatially varying magnetic-field-induced momentum shifts. For the resulting Pfaffian--anti-Pfaffian interface, a Umklapp process can gap the counter-propagating charge sector, while the remaining four co-propagating Majorana modes naturally group into two sectors organized by translation symmetries. Our results show that lattice commensurability qualitatively changes the coupled-wire accessibility of non-Abelian states while providing a microscopic momentum structure that directly constrains their edge and interface dynamics.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们研究半填充莫尔晶格系统中的Pfaffian和抗Pfaffian非阿贝尔分数量子异常霍尔态。由于晶体动量守恒模为倒数晶格矢量，这些晶格系统允许两相的耦合线结构，而不需要空间变化的磁场诱导动量偏移。对于由此产生的Pfaffian-反Pfaffian界面， Umklapp过程可以间隔反传播电荷扇区，而其余四个共同传播的Majorana模式自然分为两个由平移对称性组织的扇区。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们研究半填充莫尔晶格系统中的Pfaffian和抗Pfaffian非阿贝尔分数量子异常霍尔态。由于晶体动量守恒模为倒数晶格矢量，这些晶格系统允许两相的耦合线结构，而不需要空间变化的磁场诱导动量偏移。对于由此产生的Pfaffian-反Pfaffian界面， Umklapp过程可以间隔反传播电荷扇区，而其余四个共同传播的Majorana模式自然分为两个由平移对称性组织的扇区。我们的结果表明，晶格相称性定性地改变了非阿贝尔状态的耦合线可达性，同时提供了直接约束其边缘和界面动力学的微观动量结构。

articles.title: Plasmon excitations in monolayer stanene
articles.title_zh: 单层檀香烯中的等离子体激发
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12212v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monolayer stanene exhibits strong intrinsic spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and notably distinct low-energy band features involving both Γ and K valleys together with strong electron-hole asymmetry among group-IV monolayers. Its plasmonic properties and external-field tunability remain largely unclarified. Here, we systematically investigate its high-energy plasmon structures and low-energy collective excitation modulated by temperature, electrostatic doping and perpendicular electric field. Calculations use a sp³ tight-binding model with SOC and sublattice staggered potentials, combined with the finite-temperature multiband Lindhard function under the random-phase approximation. Besides the π and π+σ plasmon known in graphene/silicene, stanene supports two new high-energy plasmon branches. For low-energy plasmons, thermal excitation extends the accessible energy-momentum range while preserving high quality factors and collective coherence. Electrostatic doping yields distinct plasmon behaviors: moderate doping gives K-valley dominated intraband sqrtq Dirac plasmons; heavy electron doping retains sqrtq dispersion via Drude contributions from Γ and K valleys; heavy hole doping triggers interband transitions near the Γ point, producing new σ-σ and σ-σ^* interband plasmon modes and complex multi-branch spectra. Furthermore, the perpendicular electric field enables continuous tuning of the sqrtq plasmon via band reconstruction below 0.3 V/Å and induces extra plasmon modes near band-gap closure. These tunable low-energy plasmons span terahertz-to-mid-infrared frequencies, promising for nanophotonic applications.
articles.abstract_zh: 单层stanene表现出强的固有自旋轨道耦合（ SOC ）和明显的低能带特征，涉及Γ和K谷，以及IV族单层之间的强电子空穴不对称性。其等离子体调制性质和外场可调性在很大程度上仍未得到澄清。在这里，我们系统地研究了其高能等离子体结构和受温度、静电掺杂和垂直电场调制的低能集体激发。计算使用具有SOC和亚晶格交错电位的sp ³紧密结合模型，并结合随机相位近似下的有限温度多频带Lindhard函数。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 单层stanene表现出强的固有自旋轨道耦合（ SOC ）和明显的低能带特征，涉及Γ和K谷，以及IV族单层之间的强电子空穴不对称性。其等离子体调制性质和外场可调性在很大程度上仍未得到澄清。在这里，我们系统地研究了其高能等离子体结构和受温度、静电掺杂和垂直电场调制的低能集体激发。计算使用具有SOC和亚晶格交错电位的sp ³紧密结合模型，并结合随机相位近似下的有限温度多频带Lindhard函数。除了石墨烯/硅烯中已知的π和π + σ等离子体， stanene还支持两个新的高能等离子体分支。对于低能量等离子体，热激发可扩展可获得的能量-动量范围，同时保持高质量因素和集体一致性。静电掺杂产生不同的等离子体行为：中等掺杂赋予K谷主导的带内sqrtq狄拉克等离子体；重电子掺杂通过Γ和K谷的Drude贡献保留sqrtq色散；重空穴掺杂触发Γ点附近的带间跃迁，产生新的σ-σ和σ-σ ^ *带间等离子体模式和复杂的多分支光谱。此外，垂直电场能够通过低于0.3 V/Å的波段重建连续调谐sqrtq等离子体激元，并在带隙闭合附近诱导额外的等离子体激元模式。这些可调低能等离子体跨越太赫兹到中红外频率，有望用于纳米光子应用。

articles.title: Designed atomic displacements for finite-temperature phonons from few force calculations
articles.title_zh: 通过少量力计算为有限温度声子设计原子位移
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finite-temperature phonons are usually fitted to first-principles forces in randomly displaced supercells, and each force calculation can be expensive. We introduce special optimal thermal cells (SOTCs), in which the displacements are designed rather than drawn at random. Our design, SOTC-D, starts from a harmonic trial model. It gives every supercell phonon mode its quantum-thermal amplitude, chooses the sign of each mode so that the force constants are best determined, and pairs each configuration with its inverse so that cubic forces cancel. Updating the trial leads to the self-consistent harmonic solution. Cells that match displacement correlations instead give good thermodynamics but not better dispersions. For eleven crystals, eight force calculations reproduce the effective dispersions within 0.03-0.31 THz, and SOTC-D is the most accurate of five designs in 9 of them. After one trial update, it beats random sampling in all crystals at 4-16 calculations and two-iteration stochastic sampling (sTDEP) in all at eight (supercell basis). On model potentials, the self-consistent form needs 2-16 times fewer calculations than the stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation in 13 of 14 cases. With the HSE06 hybrid functional, it is ahead of pooled sTDEP at 4-16 calculations in Si and NaCl, and it gives the thermal expansion of Al within 3% of experiment at 300K. The method has limits: in Al and Si cells of more than 100 atoms, sTDEP is more accurate beyond 4-16 calculations (not so in NaCl up to 16); for dynamically stabilized bcc Zr, the outcome depends on the seed; and above 400 K, the free-energy curvature is not resolved.
articles.abstract_zh: 有限温度声子通常被拟合到随机位移的超级单元中的第一原理力，并且每个力计算都可能是昂贵的。我们引入了特殊的最优热电池（ SOTC ） ，其中位移是设计的，而不是随机绘制的。我们的设计SOTC-D从谐波试验模型开始。它为每个超级单元声子模态提供量子热振幅，选择每个模态的符号，以便最好地确定力常数，并将每个配置与其反比配对，以便三次力抵消。更新试验将导致自洽谐波解决方案。相反，与位移相关性匹配的细胞可以提供良好的热力学性能，但不能提供更好的分散性。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 有限温度声子通常被拟合到随机位移的超级单元中的第一原理力，并且每个力计算都可能是昂贵的。我们引入了特殊的最优热电池（ SOTC ） ，其中位移是设计的，而不是随机绘制的。我们的设计SOTC-D从谐波试验模型开始。它为每个超级单元声子模态提供量子热振幅，选择每个模态的符号，以便最好地确定力常数，并将每个配置与其反比配对，以便三次力抵消。更新试验将导致自洽谐波解决方案。相反，与位移相关性匹配的细胞可以提供良好的热力学性能，但不能提供更好的分散性。对于11种晶体， 8种力计算再现了0.03-0.31 THz范围内的有效色散， SOTC-D是其中9种设计中5种设计中最准确的。在一次试验更新后，它在4-16计算时在所有晶体中击败随机抽样，在8计算时在所有晶体中击败两次迭代随机抽样（ sTDEP ） （基于超级细胞）。在模型电位上，在14个案例中有13个案例中，自洽形式所需的计算量比随机自洽谐波近似值少2-16倍。借助HSE06混合功能，它在Si和NaCl的4-16计算中领先于汇集的sTDEP ，并且在300K的实验中，其Al的热膨胀率在3%以内。该方法具有局限性：在100个原子以上的Al和Si电池中， sTDEP在4-16计算之外更准确（在NaCl中不超过16 ） ；对于动态稳定的bcc Zr ，结果取决于种子；并且在400 K以上，自由能曲率未得到解析。

articles.title: Topological phases and scattering protected by projective chiral symmetry
articles.title_zh: 由射影手性对称保护的拓扑相位和散射
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The bulk-boundary correspondence states that topological properties of a bulk material guarantee the existence of protected edge modes, oftentimes associated with the attractive property of backscattering immunity. In this Letter, we consider a time reversal invariant classical system with both translation and chiral, or sublattice, symmetries. We show that when these two symmetries anti-commute, the material exhibits a topological phase protected by the same invariant as type D topological superconductors. We realize such a system experimentally and observe the existence of the associated edge modes in an acoustic network. Our measurements are in excellent agreement with theoretical predictions from discrete lattice models. Finally, we show that these edge modes are immune to backscattering for perturbations consisting in two subsequent identical defects.
articles.abstract_zh: 体边界对应指出，体材料的拓扑特性保证了受保护边缘模式的存在，通常与后向散射抗扰度的吸引特性相关联。在这封信中，我们考虑了一个同时具有平移和手性或亚晶格对称性的时间反转不变经典系统。我们表明，当这两种对称性反交换时，材料表现出与D型拓扑超导体相同的不变量保护的拓扑相位。我们通过实验实现了这样一个系统，并观察到声学网络中相关边缘模式的存在。我们的测量结果与离散晶格模型的理论预测非常吻合。最后，我们表明这些边缘模式对由两个后续相同缺陷组成的扰动免疫后向散射。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 体边界对应指出，体材料的拓扑特性保证了受保护边缘模式的存在，通常与后向散射抗扰度的吸引特性相关联。在这封信中，我们考虑了一个同时具有平移和手性或亚晶格对称性的时间反转不变经典系统。我们表明，当这两种对称性反交换时，材料表现出与D型拓扑超导体相同的不变量保护的拓扑相位。我们通过实验实现了这样一个系统，并观察到声学网络中相关边缘模式的存在。我们的测量结果与离散晶格模型的理论预测非常吻合。最后，我们表明这些边缘模式对由两个后续相同缺陷组成的扰动免疫后向散射。

articles.title: Multichannel Phonon Interconversion Drives 90 Polarization Rotation for Stable Domain Walls in Hafnium Oxide
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Polarization rotation is a fundamental mechanism in ferroelectric materials, yet how such rotation arises microscopically in fluorite ferroelectrics and gives rise to distinct domain walls (DW) remains unresolved. Phonon modes offer a microscopic route to such structural transformations, as geometric orientations can modify their frequencies, dispersion relations, and vibrational eigenstates when their characteristic wavelengths become comparable to relevant physical dimensions. Here, by combining condensed phonon mode decomposition with first-principles calculations, we investigate the origin of 90 polarization rotation in the ferroelectric phase of HfO2. Using the cubic parent phase as reference, we show that polarization rotation originates from multiple symmetry equivalent phonon modes of distinct eigenstates at different wavevectors in the Brillouin zone, whose coupling and cooperative reorientation continuously evolve to generate distinct 90 Pca21 variants and switching pathways. Among the 90 variants, the lowest-energy switching pathway through the Pmn21 exhibits an energy barrier comparable to, but slightly lower than, that of the 180 polarization reversal pathway through the P42/nmc phase, indicating that 90 polarization rotation is an energetically accessible alternative switching route. We further analyze 90 DW and find that frustrated phonon modes emerge at the wall center, where the coexistence and competition of condensed modes promote local reconfiguration of the lattice distortions, contributing to the elevated DW energies. Importantly, experimental observations with STEM imaging provide direct evidence of atomic mode distortions in stable 90 DW, consistent with the theoretically identified low-energy DW. These findings provide the fundamental structural mechanism underlying 90 switching dynamics, competing domain-wall physics, and macroscopic ferroelectric behavior.

articles.title: Defects and Structural Evolution in CrSBr: Machine-Learning Potentials for Atomistic Simulations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The layered van der Waals semiconductor CrSBr combines intrinsic magnetic order with semiconducting and optical properties, making it a promising material for multifunctional electronic and photonic applications. Understanding how defects and structural transformations affect its properties under experimentally relevant conditions, however, remains challenging for first-principles simulations due to the relevant length and time scales. Here, we develop and benchmark machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for the Cr-S-Br system, enabling large-scale atomistic simulations of CrSBr with accuracy approaching that of density functional theory (DFT). The charge-aware variant qNEP achieves near-DFT accuracy in predicting lattice constants, formation enthalpies, vacancy energetics, and the anisotropic pressure response of o-CrSBr. Nudged elastic band calculations reveal that pre-existing S vacancies lower the Cr Frenkel-pair migration barrier by up to 1.1 eV, providing an atomistic mechanism for beam-induced Cr redistribution and structural transformations. Displacement threshold calculations further show that Br is the most susceptible species to electron-beam-induced displacement, identifying the relative ease of removing different atomic species. Together, these results establish a validated computational framework for investigating atomic-scale disorder and structural transformations in CrSBr, providing a basis for defect engineering in materials for future magneto-optoelectronic applications.

articles.title: Positronium resonance of electric monopoles in quantum spin ice
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum spin ice attracts considerable attention due to its remarkable low-energy properties, described by the effective gauge theory, which mimics the quantum electrodynamics (QED). The ``effective" QED in quantum spin ice is beyond the ``real" QED in our universe in many respects. Above all, the effective QED hosts two kinds of gapped particles, the electric monopole, in addition to the magnetic monopole. Among the two monopoles, the electric monopole is of purely quantum origin, and its character has not been well resolved. In this work, we focus on the Rokhsar Kivelson point of the quantum dimer model, as the low-energy description of the quantum XXZ model on a pyrochlore lattice, and address the excitation spectrum of the electric monopoles, by combining the quantum Monte Carlo simulation with the stochastic analytical continuation. Most strikingly, the electric monopole spectrum exhibits clear double-peak structure, corresponding to the bound states and scattering states of electric monopoles. The lower-energy peak is attributed to the exciton-like bound state of an electric monopole pair, a signal of positronium in quantum spin ice. We found that the flippable loop operator serves as a local physical observable to excite a pair of electric monopoles, implying that monopoles can be detected through lattice or optical response.

articles.title: Tuning correlated states in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene with magnetic encapsulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rhombohedral graphene multilayers provide a flexible platform for correlated physics associated with their flat-band electronic structure.While a variety of correlated states appear in these systems as a function of bias and electrostatic doping, promoting specific correlated flavor symmetry breaking states remains a challenge. Here we show that magnetic encapsulation by CrGeTe₃ achieves this in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene, by using switchable exchange couplings induced by ferromagnetic substrates. We show that correlations in rhombohedral multilayers at charge neutrality strongly renormalize the exchange proximity splitting,giving rise to collective spin modes whose character is switched by the parallel or antiparallel alignment of the encapsulation. We further show that upon doping of the flat bands, spin triplet f-wave superconducting solutions emerge, whose layer and spin selectivity is controlled by the magnetic encapsulation, hosting in-gap excitations at the edges. Our results establish magnetic alignment as a means to control spin symmetry breaking and unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral pentalayer graphene.

articles.title: Ultrafast Liquid Jet X-ray Total Scattering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: X-ray free-electron lasers (XFELs) provide the temporal resolution needed to extend total scattering and pair distribution function (PDF) analysis to investigate structural dynamics on femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales. We recently demonstrated that high-quality total scattering data and PDFs can be obtained from individual XFEL pulses; here, we take the next step towards time-resolved studies of structural dynamics in solution. Using the Materials Imaging and Dynamics (MID) instrument at the European XFEL, we obtain total scattering data up to Qₘₐₓ = 16.4,mathringA⁻¹ from both conventional capillary samples and, critically, from samples delivered by a liquid jet. Despite the large air and solvent backgrounds inherent to this setup, PDFs suitable for quantitative structural analysis are recovered from liquid dispersions and molecular clusters in solution. We further demonstrate pump-probe total scattering from CsPbBr₃ nanocrystals in a liquid jet, resolving a fluence-dependent photoinduced isotropic lattice strain. Additionally, empirical potential structure refinement (EPSR) of XFEL total scattering data from an aqueous Keggin cluster reveals site-specific hydration environments and enables three-dimensional mapping of the surrounding solvent structure. Together, these advances open the door to tracking not only ultrafast structural changes in solution, but also the evolving solvent environments that govern molecular behaviour and reactivity.

articles.title: Atomically Sharp Magnetic Domain Walls beyond Micromagnetics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Atomically narrow magnetic domain walls can arise in ultrathin magnetic films, van der Waals magnets, and systems with reduced effective exchange stiffness due to competing exchange interactions. As their width approaches the atomic lattice spacing, the continuum approximation underlying micromagnetics becomes increasingly unreliable. We investigate the structure and stability of such domain walls in a one-dimensional nearest-neighbor J-K-D spin-lattice model incorporating Heisenberg exchange, uniaxial anisotropy, and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI). In the absence of DMI, we demonstrate analytically a continuous transition to an atomically sharp easy-axis wall at the critical exchange-to-anisotropy ratio J/K = 3/2, characterized by the softening of a localized Hessian mode. Atomistic spin-dynamics simulations confirm this transition and reveal that fitting discrete wall profiles with the conventional micromagnetic solution, as commonly done in experimental analyses, underestimates the exchange interaction and overestimates the anisotropy. Finite DMI removes the perfectly collinear wall as a stationary configuration, replacing the transition by a smooth crossover toward a strongly localized but canted wall that approaches the collinear easy-axis configuration only asymptotically in the strong-anisotropy limit. We derive an analytical expression for the DMI-induced canting in this regime and demonstrate its strongly enhanced canting response near the critical ratio. These findings establish the limitations of micromagnetic descriptions of atomically narrow domain walls and suggest opportunities for controlling their structure through anisotropy and DMI.

articles.title: Kagome Flat Bands from Self-Assembled Water on Non-van der Waals 2D Materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials are governed not only by their intrinsic electronic structure but also in particular by their surface chemistry and interactions with the environment. The surfaces of non-van der Waals (non-vdW) 2D materials are intrinsically reactive and may require chemical stabilization under realistic experimental conditions. Here, we perform a systematic first-principles study of water passivation of non-vdW 2D materials and demonstrate that molecular water adsorption is energetically and dynamically favored for a wide range of systems. Rather than dissociating, water molecules frequently remain intact and form adsorbed ordered surface overlayers. These overlayers can adopt a kagome lattice geometry, leading to the emergence of flat electronic bands directly at the valence-band edge. Analysis of the electronic structure reveals a strong intermolecular coupling between neighboring water lone pairs within this kagome topology, while the locked molecular orientations simultaneously produce an electrostatically frustrated surface potential. These findings establish water not only as a stabilizing agent but also as an active element for electronic structure engineering of non-vdW 2D surfaces.

articles.title: Lattice dynamical properties and interatomic force constants of transition metal oxide perovskite superlattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we investigate the construction of efficient model potentials for perovskite heterostructures by transferring relevant dynamic quantities from bulk systems and short-period superlattices. Through first-principles calculations, we provide a comprehensive analysis and comparison of the dynamical properties of different perovskite-based superlattice structures, including (PbTiO3 )n /(SrTiO3 )m superlattices, (ATiO3 )n /(AO) 2 superlattices, and An+1 Tin O 3n+1 Ruddlesden-Popper phases, where A can be Sr, Ba, or Pb. We demonstrate that as the thickness of these structures increases, the dynamical properties of the perovskite blocks converge rapidly towards their bulk counterparts. We discuss this convergence in terms of phonon density of states in reciprocal space and inter-atomic force constants in real space. Our findings suggest a straightforward strategy for developing transferable model potentials that accurately capture the dynamics of layered oxide compounds with progressively thicker layers.

articles.title: Revealing laser-induced modification of weak ferromagnetism through a spin-reorientation phase transition in iron borate Fe₃BO₆
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the iron oxide Fe₃BO₆ weak ferromagnetism stems from competing contributions from two-site Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions (DMI) and from on-site anisotropies at the two 4c and 8d types of nonequivalent Fe³⁺ sites. As a result, spin reorientation (SR) transition Γ₂ → Γ₄ in Fe₃BO₆ uniquely comprises 90^circ spin switching and a 35% change of weak ferromagnetic moment. We explore ultrafast kinetics of such a transition as a proxy for weak ferromagnetism contributions modified by femtosecond laser pulses. Using magneto-optical pump-probe technique we reveal that the SR transition is triggered by an abrupt decrease of the weak ferromagnetic moment in the Γ₂ phase, and relate it to the laser-induced modification of the DMI and anisotropy contributions to the spin canting. By tuning the pump pulse phonon energy between different optical absorption ranges, we show that laser-driven impact on spin canting possesses a nonthermal character and is achieved through the charge-transfer transitions 2p→3d within Fe³⁺O²⁻₆ octahedra rather than by localized 3d→3d transitions at Fe³⁺. The decreased weak ferromagnetic moment controls the threshold and the latency of the SR transition, as well as a final state. The latter is achieved via the precessional switching to the Γ₄ phase activated by the laser-induced heating. Final state is found to be a coexistence of Γ₄ and Γ₂ phase with modified spin canting persisting even at hundreds of picoseconds.

articles.title: Scalable operating currents in amorphous W-N/FePt superconducting rectifiers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate high-efficiency, field-free superconducting diode behavior in W-N/FePt bilayers fabricated entirely by sputtering at room temperature. The devices combine amorphous W-N superconducting thin films with a 48-nm-thick FePt layer exhibiting remanent stripe-domain magnetization. We used lithographically patterned microbridges to compare W-N/FePt bilayers with single-layer W-N reference films at three nominal W-N thicknesses (18, 24, and 28 nm). The bilayers exhibit superconducting transition temperatures of approximately 4.1-4.3 K. At zero applied magnetic field, the current-voltage (I-V) characteristics exhibit pronounced nonreciprocity, controlled by the orientation of the in-plane remanent FePt magnetization relative to the transport current. The diode response is maximized for perpendicular alignment, reverses polarity upon magnetization reversal, and is strongly suppressed when the magnetization is aligned with the current. This behavior is consistent with asymmetric vortex entry and motion governed by the magnetic stray fields generated near the bridge edges. At 3 K with the remanent magnetization perpendicular to the current, increasing the W-N thickness from 18 to 28 nm widens the current interval between the dissipation thresholds for opposite polarities from about 0.3 to 1.55 mA. All three bilayers exhibit diode efficiencies of approximately 75-80% in this configuration.

articles.title: Schottky barrier height modulation and memristive behavior in a mechanically exfoliated MoS₂ flake with multiple lateral electrodes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Van de Waals materials possess great potential as core active materials for novel electronics, optoelectronics, and sensing applications. In particular, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) and other low-dimensional materials, such as hexagonal boron nitride and binary oxides exhibit memristive behavior, making them attractive candidates as building blocks for resistive memories and neuromorphic computing devices. In this work, we investigate two-terminal lateral memristors based on mechanically exfoliated few layer MoS₂ flakes. We study the influence of the Schottky barrier height (SBH) as a function of the contact area. We report different SBHs from 60 meV up to 208 meV in the same MoS₂ flake and analyze the effect of the SBH in the memristive-like J-VDS curves and the observed non-volatile/volatile resistance switching. Our results highlight the importance of contact engineering to obtain different memristive properties in MoS₂-based devices.

articles.title: Holonomy, Spectral Topology, and Detailed Balance in Classical and Open Quantum Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Band topology and non-Hermitian spectral theory are now applied to mechanical metamaterials, chiral active fluids, stochastic networks, and open quantum systems. We give a tutorial synthesis organized by holonomy and by one question: what can the spectral data of a linear generator reveal about detailed balance? Three holonomies recur: the Berry phase of a band, the Burgers vector of a dislocation (the integrated torsion of the defect geometry), and the cycle affinity of a Markov network (the holonomy of the connection ln(Wᵢⱼ/Wⱼᵢ)). We rederive the Chern numbers Cₘ=m(sgn,Ω+sgn,νₒ) of a compressible odd-viscous fluid and restate the dislocation zero-mode count of Paulose, Chen, and Vitelli as a pairing of integrated torsion with topological polarization. Our central message is that spectral topology can obstruct detailed balance but does not determine the magnitude of dissipation. Detailed balance is self-adjointness in the inner product fixed by the stationary state, so a non-real eigenvalue, an exceptional point (EP), or a nonzero point-gap winding number of a Markov generator rules it out and forces entropy production σ>0, with σge k_B j²/D for any current, whereas a real, diagonalizable spectrum does not in general certify it. In the Hatano-Nelson ring, which is normal yet has complex spectrum, σ sweeps (0,infty) at fixed winding number. EPs need a separate assessment of the dynamics: with generalized detailed balance including time-reversal parity, an EP is compatible with equilibrium only through time-reversal-odd dynamics, as at critical damping of a Langevin oscillator, whereas an EP of a system with only even variables, such as an odd elastic medium, certifies a nonequilibrium steady state; in both cases σ is analytic across the EP. We propose benchtop tests for each statement.

articles.title: Topological states in fractals through a self-similar tensor network encoding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensor network methods have been instrumental in addressing exponentially large many-body problems. Most recently, these techniques have also been applied to single-particle tight-binding Hamiltonians, allowing observables to be evaluated on exponentially large lattices. Here, we show that the scale-separated nature of these methods allows for a natural encoding of self-similar structures, such as the Sierpiński gasket, a scale-invariant fractal with Hausdorff dimension log 3/log 2 approx 1.58, yielding an exact and compact representation of Hamiltonians on such lattices. Using this encoding, we study a Chern insulator, the flux kagome model, confined to this fractal geometry, and develop methods to investigate its topological states within a tensor network framework. This allows us to reach much higher fractal generations than would otherwise be possible with dense-matrix methods, resolving the density of states of a deep fractal with over 100 million sites. Furthermore, the larger structures allow us to resolve topology in smaller gaps, suggesting that these methods could be instrumental in understanding the interplay between topology and non-integer dimensionality.

articles.title: Quotient Index for Symmetry-Protected Zeros and the Tenfold Way in Mackey's Construction of Super Corepresentations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Symmetries that anticommute with a Hamiltonian can protect zero modes by obstructing their removal through symmetry-compatible perturbations. We formulate this obstruction as a quotient of the additive group of symmetry representations by the image of the map that forgets a compatible representation grading. To compute the quotient, we use Mackey's method to construct all irreducible super corepresentations of finite graded symmetry groups, allowing antiunitary operations and projective factor systems. Starting from the unitary Hamiltonian-preserving normal subgroup, this construction yields two complex and ten real structural types, characterized by residual Altland--Zirnbauer symmetry algebras. The residual and induced graded modules have isomorphic graded commutants, and their represented symmetry algebras share a graded Morita class that is super opposite to that of the commutant. We derive character criteria that identify these types. Exhaustive enumeration of the restriction relations gives independent sector contributions 0, Z, or Z₂, with only integer factors in the purely unitary case. In the finite semisimple setting, the complete index vanishes if and only if all zero modes can be lifted by a symmetry-compatible perturbation. Applications to one-dimensional end states and interpolation cylinders of disordered boundary Dirac theories recover protected multiplet counts and connect the quotient to bulk topology and sigma-model topological terms using bulk--boundary correspondence, texture-index theorems, and fermion-phase calculations.

articles.title: Quantum benchmarks for magnetic energies and transition temperatures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting magnetic ordering temperatures requires accurate exchange interactions and an appropriate treatment of spin thermodynamics. Here we assess these requirements through complementary quantum Monte Carlo benchmarks. For five insulating antiferromagnets, we compare ferromagnetic-antiferromagnetic energy differences from diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) and density functional theory with references reconstructed from inelastic neutron scattering (INS) exchanges. DMC underestimates these references but achieves a mean absolute error comparable to the best-performing functionals tested. Separately, we directly test the previously proposed (S+1)/S rescaling of classical Monte Carlo temperatures against quantum stochastic series expansion simulations for 17 compounds using corresponding INS-derived Heisenberg Hamiltonians. Rescaling reduces the mean absolute classical-quantum temperature difference from 81.7 to 8.2 K, with a mean absolute percentage difference of 5.9 %. These results establish a direct quantum benchmark for the rescaling within the tested models and emphasize that improvements in electronic magnetic energy scales should be accompanied by attention to quantum spin thermodynamics.

articles.title: Spin-valve effect through electrostatic coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a spin-valve effect in which an insulating magnetic van der Waals multilayer controls the conductance of an adjacent non-magnetic conductor by electrostatic coupling, without transport-electrons entering the magnetic layers. The coupling is induced by the variations of the electronic structure when the relative orientation of the magnetization of adjacent monolayers changes from parallel to antiparallel, modifying both the dielectric constant and band alignment. We consider two types of coupling and device concepts: charge transfer to a graphene monolayer and capacitive coupling in a single-electron transistor. We use density functional calculations to assess the magnitude of the effect in various materials, including CrI₃, CrBr₃, CrCl₃ and NiBr₂. We predict magnetoresistance ratios in the range of 1.14-1.20 for the charge-transfer device and up to 10³ in the single-electron transistor.

articles.title: Harmonic origin of local symmetry breaking in PbTe revealed using machine-learned potentials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use machine-learned interatomic potentials combined with higher-order interatomic force constant models to show that finite-range polar correlations in PbTe are driven by long-range harmonic interactions rather than lattice anharmonicity. Our molecular dynamics simulations reveal a spatial polar correlation range exceeding 50 Å at low temperatures and decreasing with increasing temperature. Selective interatomic force constant mapping demonstrates that crystal anharmonicity usually associated with the formation of polar nanoregions suppresses polar correlations. Instead, long-range harmonic interactions extending to 13 Å are necessary to reproduce the spatial coherence of local dipoles. In reciprocal space, these extended harmonic interactions correspond to high curvature of the transverse optical (TO) phonon branch at the Γ point. Comparison with isostructural NaCl connects these extended interactions to local underscreening of predominantly Coulombic forces. Our results provide a key microscopic description of finite-range polar correlations and a framework for understanding local symmetry breaking in centrosymmetric materials.

articles.title: Compensation Domain Walls in Ferrimagnets as Spin-Torque Oscillator Candidates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin-torque nano-oscillators are promising nanoscale microwave sources, yet their performance is often limited by narrow operational ranges and sensitivity to device parameters. Here, we numerically investigate the dynamics of compensation domain walls in ferrimagnetic systems driven by spin-transfer torque as a microwave source candidate. These walls arise in structures with adjacent regions of different compensation character, where the competition between exchange and Zeeman energies under an applied magnetic field stabilizes a distinct magnetic texture. We demonstrate steady current-driven rotation of compensation domain walls over a broad range of current densities within the model. To elucidate the underlying mechanism, we develop a collective-coordinate model and derive an analytical expression for the oscillation frequency, which quantitatively reproduces the dependence on current and magnetic field observed in micromagnetic simulations. Our results identify compensation domain walls as a candidate platform for tunable spin-torque nano-oscillators with intrinsic field-induced confinement.

articles.title: Higher tensor network states in two spatial dimensions: fundamental theorem for open boundary conditions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a class of two-dimensional tensor network states obtained by categorifying matrix product states. This procedure leads us to consider bond spaces provided by a 2-vector space associated with the 2-cells of the underlying lattice. Tensor network representations are then defined as module categories over the free monoidal category on a monoidal signature encoding the lattice geometry. We prove a fundamental theorem stating that two representations generating the same states with suitable open boundary conditions are equivalent as module categories. Finally, we introduce a notion of 2-injectivity, a categorified analogue of the injectivity condition for matrix product states.

articles.title: Ground-state phase diagram of the spin-1/2 Heisenberg zigzag ladder with anisotropic Γ term revisited
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the spin-1/2 Heisenberg antiferromagnet with an anisotropic Γ term on a zigzag ladder, which can be exactly mapped to the spin-1/2 XYZ zigzag ladder by a spin rotation. This model has recently attracted considerable interest as an effective model for the quasi-one-dimensional magnetic semiconductor YbCuS₂. For the model, the ground-state phase diagram was previously proposed by Saito and Hotta [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 166701 (2024); Phys. Rev. B 110, 024409 (2024)]. We systematically reexamine the phase diagram through complementary numerical and analytical approaches, including exact diagonalization, the density-matrix renormalization group method, and low-energy effective theories. We thereby demonstrate that when the anisotropic Γ term is present, the model exhibits the Néel, dimer, ferromagnetic, and double-Néel phases, all of which have a finite excitation gap. The gapless Tomonaga-Luttinger-liquid (TLL) phase appears only in the isotropic case where the Γ term is absent. We also confirm that the transitions between the Néel and dimer phases and between the Néel and ferromagnetic phases are continuous transitions governed by Gaussian criticality with central charge c=1. The TLL parameter characterizing the critical states at the Gaussian transitions is estimated numerically.

articles.title: Finite temperature and pressure structural relaxations including zero-point motion and anharmonicity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: At finite temperature and pressure, the equilibrium structure of a crystal minimizes the Gibbs free energy rather than the static Born-Oppenheimer energy. We present WARP (Wyckoff-constrained Anharmonic Relaxations at Pressure and temperature), a symmetry-constrained, variable-cell relaxation based on the stochastic temperature-dependent effective potential method, including anharmonicity and zero-point motion. Every position update is projected onto Wyckoff positions and every strain onto symmetric strains, so a relaxation can raise the symmetry but never lower it. For aluminum, the thermal expansion follows measurements at cryogenic temperatures, including the quantum plateau below 50 K. For lanthanum hydrides at megabar pressures, equations of state agree with phonon-based and path-integral calculations, and LaH₁₀ relaxes from its rhombohedral static minimum to the observed cubic phase, also with a machine-learned potential fine-tuned on 150 supercells. For brucite, Mg(OD)₂, lattice parameters, bond distances and thermal expansion agree with neutron diffraction, and the O-D isotope effect is captured.

articles.title: Universal semiclassical drift velocity of magnetic edge channels
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic edge channels, arising at the edge of a two-dimensional electron gas in a magnetic field, are topologically protected and propagate unidirectionally along the edge. Their group velocities at the Fermi level, being averaged harmonically, result in drift velocity, which is related to the edge density of states, quantum capacitance, and the velocity of edge magnetoplasmons. Using semiclassical quantization of electron skipping orbits, we show that the drift velocity equals 1/2 of the electron Fermi velocity in the limit of a large number of edge channels crossing the Fermi level. This result, being universal for a hard edge and for isotropic dispersion, is checked numerically for massive electrons and for massless electrons in graphene. The drift velocity at smooth electrostatically defined edges lacks such universality. In the case of anisotropic dispersion, the semiclassical drift velocity at the hard edge reduces to a coordinate-velocity correlation along the cyclotron orbit.

articles.title: High Pressure Material Phase Identification with Gaussian Kernel Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12840v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase identification is a computational task involving the classification of material structure using the positions of atoms. Using data from Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations, our task is to identify the material phase of a set of atoms, based on how the simulations predict their positioning relative to each other. By leveraging existing research on mechanistic neural network theory, particularly Neural Tangent Kernels (NTK), we develop a new and efficient method for classifying simulated material samples. Our method involves defining a set of "atom detectors" that are given positions around the origin in cartesian coordinates. The sum of Gaussians centered at each atom is calculated at each atom detector, and is used as the input to a neural network. We present theoretical and experimental evidence to show that this method is highly effective and efficient at the task. Our method obtains better or similar accuracy scores to commonly used methods while having a major computational speedup.

articles.title: Tetragonal-to-orthorhombic distortion in CeRh₂As₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: CeRh₂As₂ is best known for its two superconducting phases, which are observed when a magnetic field is applied along the c axis of its tetragonal unit cell. The emergence of superconductivity, with Tc approx 0.31K, is preceded by an ordered state (phase I), with an ordering temperature T₀ approx 0.46K. The precise nature of the order parameter in phase I is still unknown, although evidence of dipolar ordering was found. To investigate a possible symmetry breaking at T₀, we conducted longitudinal thermal-expansion measurements along the crystallographic [100], [010], [110], and [1overline10] directions on a single-crystalline sample cut into an octagonal shape. Our results demonstrate the breaking of the fourfold in-plane symmetry below T₀, evidencing a small tetragonal-to-orthorhombic distortion (orthorhombicity δ sim 10⁻⁷). The breaking of the tetragonal symmetry at T₀ might imply that the superconducting order parameter that develops within phase I cannot be multi-component. More generally, the distortion places restrictions on the possible order parameters for phase I.

articles.title: Magnetic behavior of the 5d¹ Re-based double perovskite Sr₂ZnReO₆
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.04071v4 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The subtle interplay between spin-orbit coupling, exchange interactions, and cation ordering can lead to exotic magnetic states in transition-metal ions. We report a comprehensive study of the Re-based (5d¹) ordered double perovskite oxide Sr₂ZnReO₆ combining synchrotron x-ray diffraction (XRD), magnetic susceptibility, muon spin relaxation (μSR) measurements, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. XRD reveals that Sr₂ZnReO₆ crystallizes in the monoclinic structure (space group P2₁/n) at low temperature. Magnetic susceptibility data indicate a transition below sim13 K, with M--H loops showing ferromagnetic-like hysteresis and an unusually high coercive field of 23 kOe at 2 K. Zero-field μSR measurements detect static and spatially disordered internal fields below T_M simeq  12 K, consistent with a canted antiferromagnetic ground state determined by detailed DFT and force-theorem in Hubbard-I calculations. The reduced high-temperature effective moment (sim0.76~μ_B) and very small static moment (lesssim 0.2~μ_B) derived from μSR analysis and local-field simulations indicate a decisive role of spin-orbit coupling. Through a combined experimental and computational approach we unambiguously determine the canted antiferromagnetic order in Sr₂ZnReO₆, showing that a very small ordered moment coexists with an exceptionally large coercivity. These results underscore the crucial role of spin-orbit coupling and orbital ordering, providing new insights into magnetism in 5d¹ double perovskites.

articles.title: Experimentally Grounded Machine Learning of PrecursorSurface-Reactant Chemistry in Atomic Layer Deposition
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10024v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Whether a precursor-substrate-reactant combination yields an atomic layer deposition (ALD) process is still settled by trial-and-error experiments. Here we introduce AJIN (ALD Joint Interpretable Network), a machine-learning framework that learns this decision from experimental outcomes. We compiled 560 experimentally observed ALD and area-selective ALD outcomes spanning 76 precursors, 27 substrates, 20 reactants and 25-620 degrees Celsius. Following the ALD cycle, AJIN predicts adsorption from graph-neural-network embeddings of the precursor and substrate with temperature, and deposition by adding the reactant. The best model (CHGNet-MLP) reaches balanced accuracies of 79.2% for adsorption and 84.8% for deposition and transfers partially to unseen precursors. SHAP and ablation analyses show that substrate chemistry governs adsorption, whereas precursor, substrate and reactant all contribute to deposition. Tested against our laboratory's ALD experiments, AJIN correctly predicted 83% of new-substrate cases and 71% of new precursor-substrate adsorption cases, providing an experimentally grounded tool for prioritizing ALD and area-selective ALD chemistries.

articles.title: Entanglement percolation enhanced by the power of choice
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10119v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum communication networks are best supported by maximally entangled states, but imperfections in entanglement generation and distribution generally limit the distributed states to being only partially entangled. Therefore, protocols typically consisting of local operations and classical communication are required to create suitably entangled networks. Here, we introduce a power-of-choice (PoC) protocol based on reversing the selection criteria in the Achlioptas process previously considered in classical explosive percolation. The resulting PoC protocol anticipates the entanglement percolation transition, thereby reducing the entanglement resources needed to establish quantum communication. Notably, in contrast to explosive percolation, the PoC protocol admits an implementation using local information with no appreciable loss of performance.

articles.title: Regev's Reduction Reaches Reconstruction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10283v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Regev's reduction uses a quantum Fourier transform to carry out reductions between various problems related to lattices and codes. We apply it to the problem of sampling from Gibbs distributions of certain classical spin glass Hamiltonians, which can equivalently be thought of as cost functions for average-case instances of an optimization problem called D-regular max-k-LINSAT. This problem becomes hard at low temperature. Here, we use a quantum decoding algorithm called Belief Propagation with Quantum Messages (BPQM) to solve the decoding problem arising from Regev's reduction. Our main contribution is a proof that the minimum temperature reachable using Regev+BPQM is exactly equal to the reconstruction threshold temperature for noisy channels transmitting signals on a tree network. This equality can be understood via Renes' duality between classical and quantum channels, which we use to show that quantum decoding is possible exactly when classical reconstruction on the dual problem is impossible. Mézard and Montanari identified this reconstruction temperature with a dynamical glass transition predicted by the one-step replica-symmetry breaking (1RSB) cavity equation. It is conjectured that local samplers such as Metropolis Monte Carlo and Glauber dynamics cannot equilibrate efficiently below this reconstruction temperature but may do so above it; our large numerical experiments show close agreement with this prediction across hundreds of different problem parameters. Therefore, our results rigorously show that Regev+BPQM reaches a temperature for which, to our knowledge, there is no matching classical guarantee, and brings Regev+BPQM to the conjectured limit of efficient Gibbs sampling by classical local dynamics.

articles.title: 2D polaritons for Squeezing and Shrinking Light
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10754v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) materials have emerged as an extraordinary platform for polaritonics, given their remarkable ability to confine light to deep sub-wavelength scales. However, as material thicknesses reach the nanometer limit, macroscopic electrodynamic models become inadequate for the description of light-matter coupling in 2D materials, leaving a significant gap in our understanding of 2D polaritons. In this work, we develop a comprehensive quantum microscopic framework that describes 2D polaritons through a general, scale-less Hamiltonian. Starting from the quantum properties of a polarizable 2D surface, we derive collective excitations and we identify both transverse electric magnetic modes existing outside the light cone. Our results demonstrate that these 2D systems facilitate a powerful synergy between extreme wavelength shrinking and intrinsic quantum squeezing of electric field quadratures. By establishing this theoretical roadmap, our work provides the essential architecture for controlling non-classical states of light at the nanoscale, opening new avenues for high-precision quantum sensing and the development of next-generation optoelectronic devices

articles.title: One Measurement, Many Fronts in Kitaev and Cluster Chains
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10912v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A projective measurement of one site in the ground state of a quantum chain disturbs the chain in two ways: learning the outcome shifts distant expectation values at once, through ground-state correlations, and the measurement erases the correlations between the measured site and the rest. Both changes travel outward. We solve this problem exactly for the Kitaev chain, the cluster chain in a transverse field, and the Kitaev chain with power-law couplings, and we find that far from the measured site every quadratic observable responds through a front. Where the front is and how fast it broadens depend only on the quasiparticle dispersion. How strong it is depends on two operators: how strongly the measured one creates the fastest quasiparticles and how strongly the observed one detects them; if either factor vanishes, the front is weaker and decays faster. One measurement therefore launches many fronts, one per observable, with a common position and width but different decay laws. In the Kitaev chain the density and the bond energy, the two terms of its nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian, respond to one density measurement with decay laws that trade places between the topological and the trivial phase; in the cluster chain, measuring a symmetry-odd spin instead of a symmetry-even one changes the critical decay law at a fixed Hamiltonian; and with power-law couplings the width law itself changes. All decay laws and profiles are obtained in closed form.

articles.title: Deterministically fabricated C-band single-photon sources based on quantum dot circular Bragg grating cavities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10988v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Telecom-wavelength quantum light sources are essential components for scalable fiber-based quantum networks, where on-demand emission of single photons is required for high secret key rates. Here, we demonstrate the deterministic integration of metal-organic vapor-phase epitaxy (MOVPE)-grown C-band InAs/InP quantum dots into circular Bragg grating resonators. The integrated emitters exhibit a radiative lifetime of T₁ = (1400 ± 50)~ps and a spectral linewidth of Δ EFWHM = (41.0 ± 4.0)~mueV. Under non-resonant excitation, we measure a post-selected single-photon purity of (0.95 ± 0.02) and a raw two-photon interference visibility of V₁₂ₙₛ = (35 ± 2)%, which increases to (70 ± 18)% under temporal post-selection. We discuss strategies to improve photon indistinguishability, including radiative-rate engineering, charge stabilization, and more selective excitation. Our results combine MOVPE growth, deterministic device integration, and telecom C-band emission, providing a route toward scalable semiconductor quantum light sources for fiber-based quantum networks.

articles.title: Toward universal excited-state machine-learned potentials: a local excitation Hamiltonian for size consistency and transferability
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials could make excited-state simulations across chemical space routine, but excitation energies, unlike ground-state energies, are not sums of atomic contributions. The excited states of noninteracting molecules are the union of their states, which pooled multistate readouts reproduce at best for the lowest state. We introduce LEH-MACE, whose excitation energies are the eigenvalues of a local excitation Hamiltonian assembled from atom-centred blocks, so this union holds exactly. We generated TD-DFT energies and forces for about 300,000 equilibrium, thermal, and excited-state geometries of over 100,000 molecules. LEH-MACE's advantage over direct readouts grew with the distance from the training data and was largest above S₁, with about half their S₂ and S₃ errors for long conjugated oligomers. For molecule pairs, only LEH-MACE kept its single-molecule accuracy, while a softmin readout remained superior for S₁ dynamics of larger chromophores. Exact size consistency is thus one step toward such potentials.

articles.title: Bridging Gaps with Tensor Networks: From the Haldane Gap and Beyond
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11049v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Proofs generated by large language models are often difficult to understand, generalize, or formalize directly. Here we verify, digest, and formalize OpenAI's computer-assisted proof of a uniform gap in the periodic spin-1 Heisenberg chain using tensor-network diagrams and Lean 4. Reading the partition-function network along space and imaginary time shows how finite-ring bounds propagate across doubled lengths and inverse temperatures to all longer even rings, sharpening the spin-1 bound from the same finite inputs by a factor of 19 to Δ_L > 0.0729 for all even L ≥ 36. We identify reflection positivity as the general condition behind the proof and certify uniform gaps in seven additional spin chains and ladders. More broadly, digesting machine-generated proofs into transparent physical mechanisms yields sharper bounds, broader theorems, and reusable formal verifications.

articles.title: A Microscopic Model Underpinning Macroscopic QED in Active Media
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11557v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a microscopic foundation for macroscopic quantum electrodynamics in active media. Starting from a driven three-level system, we derive an effective two-level description with nonequilibrium stationary populations and employ a quantum central limit approach to obtain collective Langevin dynamics. This construction yields the electromagnetic susceptibility and quantum noise-current correlations from the same microscopic stationary state, providing a direct connection to the reservoir operators of conventional macroscopic quantum electrodynamics. We show that the optical response is governed by the population difference, whereas the noise correlations depend separately on the populations of the two levels. Consequently, at optical transparency, the imaginary part of the susceptibility vanishes while quantum fluctuations remain finite. We interpret the resulting noise statistics in terms of an effective reservoir occupation and a purification involving two vacuum modes, and establish a corresponding effective-temperature fluctuation--dissipation relation. Finally, we demonstrate that the residual fluctuations at transparency can induce finite heating of a nearby quantum probe.

articles.title: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11805v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the learning of homogenized constitutive laws for inelastic heterogeneous materials, aiming to replace costly concurrent unit-cell simulations with surrogates that generalize across loading histories and microstructures. We focus on the recurrent neural operator framework, motivated by the explicit form of homogenized Kelvin--Voigt linear viscoelasticity. In this framework, internal variables enable a Markovian approximation of loading-history dependence, and neural operators represent the microstructure-dependent constitutive response. For periodic Kelvin--Voigt viscoelasticity, we prove a universal approximation theorem showing that the model can approximate the homogenized constitutive law to any prescribed accuracy, uniformly in time and over a wide set of admissible strain trajectories and microstructural property fields, in two and three dimensions. This comprises a significant extension of the existing, somewhat limited, one-dimensional theory that uses explicit solutions for piecewise constant materials. Instead, in two and three dimensions, we adopt a more versatile approximation based on the spectral representation of the memory kernel that arises from homogenization. This also enables us to give an explicit bound on the internal-variable dimension, sufficient for approximation, exhibiting logarithmic growth in the inverse relative stress error and in material contrast. Numerical experiments on viscoelasticity and crystal plasticity complement the theory, illustrating the roles of internal-variable dimension and sample complexity in learning homogenized responses from unit-cell data. Theoretical results are formally verified in Lean 4.

articles.title: Discretising 2D Fermionic CFTs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11807v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the exact fixed-point tensor construction of Cheng et al. to fermionic minimal models, providing an analytic construction of fixed-point tensors for fermionic rational conformal field theories. The fermionic fixed-point tensor is defined as a correlation function of boundary-changing operators on a triangle, with careful treatment of fermionic parity and spin structure. Boundary tensors are also constructed and combined with triangle tensors to form strips, enabling the extraction of scaling dimensions for boundary-changing operators. The construction incorporates modified weights for shrinkable boundary conditions, systematic depiction of spin structures, recovering both the Neveu-Schwarz and Ramond sectors. As a benchmark, our tensor with a minimal truncation of descendant levels yields convergence to the exact bulk scaling dimensions of many low energy states for the free Majorana fermion (c=1/2), demonstrating the efficiency of approximate fixed point tensors from boundary changing operators.
