We also make use of a more general description of fermionic CFTs based on fermionisation of rational bosonic CFTs, and make a generic prescription for discretisation making use of their connections to modular tensor categories. We show that the discretised spin structures on a spin surface naturally recover the signs needed to recover the R/NS sectors. We propose that the collection of OPE coefficients of the discretised 2d CFT can be naturally interpreted as a state-sum of spin-TQFTs, analogous to the bosonic case. This work provides analytically computed starting points for tensor network simulations of fermionic critical phenomena.

articles.title: AI-Driven Discovery of Entanglement Witness in Spin Hamiltonians
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11935v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Entanglement is a crucial resource in quantum science and engineering, but detecting it in many-body states from experimentally accessible observables remains challenging. Here we introduce EntNet, an AI-driven framework to discover compact combinations of spin observables that accurately distinguish entangled from fully separable many-body mixed states in one-dimensional spin-1/2 chains governed by short-range Hamiltonians. We construct local-unitary-invariant representations of measurable Pauli correlators up to four-body order, sparsely select 16 candidate invariant feature channels, and learn their spatial structure using a Transformer architecture with rotary positional embeddings. Using only expectation values of these low-order observables, EntNet achieves >98% recall on certified entangled states with near-zero false-positive rates on separable states. Remarkably, it exhibits transferability across system sizes and distinct Hamiltonian families, including frustrated and disordered spin models, with minimal loss of accuracy. Beyond detection, EntNet provides physical insight into entanglement detection by revealing a selective spatial organization of pair correlations, while its finite-temperature decision boundary tracks the excitation gap of Jordan-Wigner quasiparticles. These results establish a transferable and physically interpretable framework for data-driven discovery of entanglement witnesses from local correlation functions.

articles.title: Extending the reach of real-space real-time TDDFT: new developments in the Octopus code
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Octopus is an open-source package implementing time-dependent density functional theory in a real-space, real-time formulation. Here we report on the developments since our previous contribution to the Special Topic Issue on Electronic Structure Software [J. Chem. Phys. 152, 124119 (2020)]. New exchange-correlation functionals extend the range of systems that can be treated, while advances in relativistic and all-electron methods open the door to core-electron spectroscopy. New capabilities for lattice dynamics - stress-tensor calculation, geometry optimization, support for machine-learned force fields, and phonon calculations - enable a fully ab initio description of light-induced lattice dynamics in real time. We also present developments that move beyond the dipole approximation, capturing light-matter interaction more faithfully. Improved methods for exciton dynamics complement a set of algorithmic advances - new propagation schemes, imaginary-time evolution, and a refactored grid handling more than a billion points - that together substantially improve performance and scalability. Combined with technical improvements such as AMD GPU support and a modernized build system, these developments consolidate Octopus as a versatile, high-performance platform for exploring electronic excitations, light-matter interaction, and nonequilibrium dynamics in molecules, nanostructures, and extended systems.

articles.title: Matrix-vector models for the 3D Ising CFT
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The construction of three-dimensional conformal field theories (3D CFTs) using interacting fermions in the lowest Landau level on a sphere has recently proven remarkably efficient, while it differs from that of conventional field theories on the fuzzy sphere. Focusing on the 3D Ising CFT, we consider a class of models that are defined by deformed Hamiltonians specified by a function which controls how the interaction is damped at high angular momenta, and this class includes the original model. We show that each model in the class can be reformulated in a basis-independent manner as a matrix--vector quantum-mechanical model, and, upon integrating out the fermionic vectors, as a matrix model. We then focus on a Gaussian choice, for which the bosonic matrices acquire a heat-kernel propagator whose width is controlled by a parameter ξ. Through exact diagonalization with the number of fermions up to 16, we find that the low-energy spectra of the deformed Hamiltonians at criticality agree with those in the 3D Ising CFT for a range of ξ. We thus obtain matrix-model realizations of the 3D Ising CFT that, in contrast to conventional fuzzy-sphere field theories, show no sign of UV/IR mixing in the low-lying spectrum.

articles.title: Resetting-based designated information distribution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a network of n nodes under random gossip dynamics, we show that by introducing the additional resetting mechanism (with rate β) to a designated subset of r nodes, the expected sum of all node values is asymptotically equal to tfracnr times the sum of the initial values of the r designated nodes, in the small-β and long-time limit. We also analyze the convergence speed to this asymptotic state and provide an approximate high-probability confidence interval for the expected sum at finite time t and finite β. Operationally, we propose a protocol that distributes the initial node values over the designated subset evenly (up to a prescribed precision), by appropriately turning on and off the resetting dynamics. Our work not only offers insights into classical problems such as distributed computing and network control, but also serves as a potential foundation for designing quantum algorithms that prepare desired states in quantum networks using only local operations.

articles.title: UniHam: A Large-Scale SOC-Complete Dataset and Benchmark for Hamiltonian Learning in Materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12509v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate prediction of electronic Hamiltonians would enable broad property inference while avoiding the high computational cost of Density Functional Theory (DFT). However, progress toward general-purpose materials foundation models is limited by a data bottleneck: existing Hamiltonian datasets are typically small, lack structural diversity, and often omit essential relativistic physics such as spin--orbit coupling (SOC). We therefore construct UniHam, a large-scale Hamiltonian dataset and benchmark suite comprising 100,000+ DFT-computed complex-valued Hermitian Hamiltonians with full SOC, covering 72 elements and a wide range of crystal geometries and symmetries (spanning diverse lattice types and space-group families). Building on UniHam, we benchmark two representative state-of-the-art models under a standardized protocol and introduce complementary evaluation metrics that jointly assess three dimensions: (i) Hamiltonian reconstruction accuracy, (ii) out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization across composition/symmetry shifts, and (iii) the ability to support downstream property prediction from the predicted Hamiltonians. Experiments on UniHam demonstrate that the proposed benchmark and metrics effectively differentiate model capabilities, revealing intrinsic SOC- and element-dependent failure modes, large variations in compositional OOD robustness, and the necessity of spectral-level evaluation to assess whether Hamiltonian predictions reliably support downstream electronic-structure properties. Overall, UniHam provides a reproducible, SOC-complete benchmark that can sharpen model comparisons and accelerate the development of next-generation foundation models for quantum materials.

articles.title: Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics-Guided Machine-Learning Potentials for Mapping Nitric Oxide Interactions with Oxygen-Covered Graphite
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Exploratory ab initio molecular dynamics is used to construct machine-learning interatomic potentials for NO interactions with highly oriented pyrolytic graphite at 33% bridge-site oxygen coverage. Representative configurations sampled across surface temperatures and incidence energies provide reference energies and forces for training and validation. The selected potential enables relaxation of 300 adsorption configurations and construction of spatial and angular interaction maps. These maps reveal increasingly restricted attractive regions during vertical approach and reduced short-range repulsion upon molecular reorientation. The resulting adsorption geometries and interaction landscapes guide further first-principles sampling toward refining potentials for NO oxidation dynamics.

articles.title: Persistent A-homotopy of Complex Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09967v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how loop classes in a network change when cycles up to a prescribed length are declared contractible. The resulting sequence of quotient groups contains the fundamental group of the clique complex at length three and the graph A-fundamental group at length four. Its mod-two abelianisation has a barcode whose death scales are the lengths in a minimum cycle basis. This separates the choice of a network filtration from the choice of local loop relations and provides a computable connection between persistent A-homotopy and persistent homology. We illustrate the construction on lattices, Watts--Strogatz networks and nine benchmark networks. Filling the plaquettes of a periodic square lattice recovers the fundamental group of the torus. In the Watts--Strogatz simulations, the normalised largest death scale falls below the normalised mean path length over the sampled range, while most clique-homology classes survive the square relations at small rewiring probabilities. The power grid has fewer surviving classes but a longer tail of death scales than five degree-preserving randomisations. We also examine connectivity graphs of maximal cliques in ego networks. Explicit certificates establish non-trivial A-classes even though the original ego clique complexes are contractible. The group construction and its linear summary answer related but distinct questions about which loop relations a network model permit.

articles.title: Cosmic Corpses: Dead stars as Factories of the most Extreme Objects in the Universe
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The apparent serenity of the night sky conceals a long history of stellar evolution, in which gravity and the properties of matter determine the remarkable fates of stars. In this pedagogical account, we discuss white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes, explaining how quantum mechanics, nuclear interactions, and General Relativity govern their formation and distinctive properties. We also highlight the possibility of primordial black holes, which may have formed from rare large density fluctuations in the early Universe, and briefly discuss their potential role as constituents of dark matter.

articles.title: Finite-amplitude wave dynamics in weak-field-equivalent nonlinear electrodynamics in (2+1) dimensions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine finite-amplitude wave propagation in (2+1)-dimensional nonlinear electrodynamics using Born-Infeld, logarithmic, and quadratic polynomial models whose Lagrangians agree through quadratic order in the electromagnetic invariant. Despite this weak-field agreement, characteristic and linearized analyses on homogeneous magnetic background reveal distinct propagation speeds and hyperbolicity domains. In the weak-background limit, the first coefficient at which Lagrangians differ also controls the leading nonlinear variation of the simple-wave characteristic velocity. Exact right-moving simple-waves, corroborated by finite-volume evolution, show rigid Born-Infeld propagation but finite-time gradient catastrophes in the logarithmic and polynomial models, substantially earlier in the latter for matched pulses. These catastrophes can occur while the field remains finite and the system remains hyperbolic, showing that weak-field agreement does not determine finite-amplitude dynamics.

articles.title: Magnetohydrodynamic spectra and line invariants in the presence of axions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A new form of the mean-field equations for magnetic fields, which accounts for the interaction with axions, is studied. It is shown that the asymptotic ergodic invariants of magnetic field lines play a key role in the evolution of magnetic fields, which determine the type of the magnetohydrodynamic spectrum of the solutions.

articles.title: Beyond node strengths: the topological content of weighted bipartite networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weighted bipartite networks encode the topology and intensity of interactions between two disjoint sets of nodes. However, it is unclear whether the observed pattern of connections is already explained by node interaction volumes or contains additional structural information. Here we introduce a hierarchy of maximum-entropy models for continuous weighted bipartite networks that preserves node strengths alone, strengths and global density, or strengths and the complete degree sequence. Across economic, technological, ecological, social and lexical systems, we find that strength constraints alone are generally insufficient to reproduce empirical structures. Yet the missing topological information is often low-dimensional: a single constraint controlling network density frequently provides the most parsimonious description, whereas networks with stronger residual degree heterogeneity require node-specific constraints. Beyond downstream inference, we also show how the choice of topological resolution changes which interactions and projected relationships are identified as statistically significant. Our results indicate that topology is essential, but often compressible, in the statistical modeling of weighted bipartite networks, and provide a scalable computational framework for fitting, sampling, model selection and validation within a common workflow.

articles.title: Test beam results for machine-learning-based reconstruction of resistive silicon sensors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10194v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The advent of Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (LGADs) and AC-coupled Low-Gain Avalanche Diodes (AC-LGADs) as candidate technologies for four-dimensional tracking has moved part of the reconstruction burden onto the analog waveforms of the sensor, in which the charge shared between electrodes encodes the impact position well below the electrode pitch. Recovering that position is a continuous, non-linear inverse problem. Transient Current Technique measurements characterize this problem at fixed injected charge and high signal-to-noise, whereas a minimum-ionizing beam adds Landau fluctuations in the deposited charge under detector operating conditions. We report test beam results for full-waveform reconstruction of an AC-LGAD of 500 μm pitch read out on a 2×2 pad matrix, exposed to the 120 GeV pion beam of the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) and read out alongside a six-plane MIMOSA-26 telescope. The telescope is aligned, and its per-plane resolutions are calibrated in situ, giving a track pointing resolution of about 2.5 μm per axis at the device, so that the measured residual is the sensor response rather than a convolution with the reference. We then compare two analytic estimators, the parameter-free charge-imbalance formula and a fitted linear matrix inversion, with the topology-agnostic transformer developed for resistive silicon sensors. Over the full active pad, the transformer reaches a median total position with up to factor 3 improvement. Within the charge-sharing core, the three methods converge to the floor of this sensor at the achieved signal-to-noise.

articles.title: Magnetosonic Solitons Driven by a Moving Charged Source: Two-Fluid Modeling and PIC Validation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop and validate a one-dimensional electron-ion two-fluid model, self-consistently coupled to Maxwell equations, for magnetosonic structures generated by a moving charged source. The model is independently benchmarked against kinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations to assess its ability to reproduce electrostatic and electromagnetic responses. In the zero-magnetic-field limit, the electrostatic precursor structures are validated using the Korteweg--de Vries amplitude--width invariant. For a finite magnetic field, the frequency and propagation speed of the far wake are consistent with the low-frequency fast-magnetosonic branch, providing a linear benchmark for the electromagnetic response. The model reproduces the transition from a wake-dominated regime to localized forward precursors as the source velocity exceeds the magnetosonic speed, and to source-locked pinned structures at higher velocities. Independent PIC simulations recover the principal features of these regimes, supporting the validity of the two-fluid description for the parameters considered. By retaining separate electron and ion dynamics, electron inertia, and charge-separation effects, the validated model provides a framework for investigating source-driven plasma-wave structures across a broader range of plasma conditions and source-magnetic-field geometries, with potential applications to interpreting plasma-wave signatures associated with moving charged objects in space plasmas.

articles.title: Self-organization of magnetic islands and zonal magnetic fields driven by slab microtearing modes in the absence of magnetic shear
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-organization in collisional microtearing turbulence is investigated using gyrokinetic simulations in a slab geometry without equilibrium magnetic shear. Unlike magnetically driven conventional tearing instabilities, microtearing instabilities are driven by the electron temperature gradient. Electron temperature fluctuations are found to contain most of the gyrokinetic free energy. Although magnetic perturbations contribute little to the free energy, the magnetic field structure plays a crucial role in the nonlinear evolution of microtearing turbulence. Zonal magnetic fields emerge spontaneously through the nonlinear interaction between magnetic perturbations and electron temperature fluctuations. These zonal fields provide an effective magnetic shear that enables magnetic islands to form despite the absence of equilibrium magnetic shear. The electron temperature profile is flattened within the islands. This flattening reduces the instability drive and is expected to promote turbulence saturation.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal Energy Consistency Enables Reliable Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics from Diffusion Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) extends molecular simulations to length and time scales inaccessible to atomistic models, but building thermodynamically faithful CG potentials remains a longstanding challenge. Energy-based diffusion models (EBDMs) provide a promising route for learning CG potentials through their zero-time energy. However, CGMD driven by diffusion-learned potentials can produce equilibrium ensembles that deviate substantially from the target distribution. We show that the zero-time distribution error is bounded by the sum of the spatial score error and temporal energy-derivative error, whereas conventional diffusion objectives directly supervise only the spatial component. Based on this finding, we introduce Spatiotemporal Energy Consistency (STEC) supervision, which complements spatial score matching by explicitly constraining temporal energy derivatives. We derive an exact and tractable objective for this temporal component, avoiding the substantial computational overhead associated with previous regularization schemes. Across peptide and fast-folding protein systems, STEC-trained EBDMs accurately reproduce equilibrium distributions with free-energy errors within chemical accuracy, while supporting stable long-time simulations that recover key metastable transition patterns. On held-out octapeptides, STEC reduces free-energy errors by more than 5-fold relative to the strongest competing baseline, while achieving a median production-cost reduction of approximately 1,700-fold relative to atomistic molecular dynamics under a defined structural-coverage benchmark. These results establish STEC as a scalable framework for learning thermodynamically reliable CG force fields for increasingly complex biomolecular systems.

articles.title: Coupled plasmonic Fabry-Perot resonances modulating electromagnetic enhancement at a silver nanowire-nanoparticle junction proved by surface-enhanced fluorescence spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigated the surface-enhanced fluorescence (SEF), which is the broad background spectrum underlying the surface-enhanced resonant Raman scattering of dye molecules, emitted from junctions between silver nanoparticles (NPs) and nanowires (NWs). We found that the electromagnetic enhancement factors (FR) derived from the SEF exhibited spectral modulation, such as complicated oscillatory structures. This property became clearer when the emission polarization was perpendicular to the long axis of the NWs. The FR spectra of the long and short NWs exhibit fine and broad oscillatory structures, respectively, when the NPs are positioned near the NW centers. When the NPs were near the NW ends, a combination of fine and broad structures was observed. Numerical calculations of the position-dependent FR spectra successfully reproduced these properties, indicating that the spectral properties originated from the interaction between two plasmonic Fabry-Perot (FP) resonators within the NW, separated by a NP. Based on this result, an analytical model of coupled FP resonators was developed to evaluate these spectral features using experimentally measured NW lengths and NP positions while varying the inter-resonator coupling efficiency. This analysis revealed that the interference and superposition of the two FP resonances resulted in these complex spectra, the energy of which was radiated by the localized plasmons of the NPs.

articles.title: Effect of Turbulence and Inhomogeneities on the Propagation of Kinetic Scale Waves
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Context. Electromagnetic ion-scale waves are well known to occur in the solar wind. Eikonal (WKB) like effects may play an important role in the interplay between the propagation and local kinetic plasma dynamics of ion cyclotron waves. Aims. This Letter aims to explore the interplay of ICW propagation with turbulence and local kinetic plasmas using ray tracing equations for ICWs in a moving medium, in which turbulent gradients are present. Methods. Parker Solar Probe observations of ICWs in the solar wind are studied using ray equations in a moving medium. Gradients in the dispersion relation responsible for WKB evolution of ICW are constrained and compared with a Parker spiral model. Results. The empirical gradients, which contain turbulent motions, greatly enhance the efficiency of WKB effects. However, the typical refraction rates are significantly slower than expected quasilinear evolution of the observed wave populations, which suggests that local kinetic physics dominates over nonlinear expansion effects. Conclusions. Turbulence can effectively increase WKB effects due to gradients caused by nonlinear interactions. In the solar wind these gradients are not sufficient to substantially change an individual ion-scale ICW over its lifetime. Incorporating kinetic effects of expansion may help advance the understanding of generation and absorption of ICW and their role in heating in the solar wind.

articles.title: Exact analytic anisotropic three-dimensional equilibria with nested magnetic surfaces, confined drift orbits and without spatial symmetry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Exact toroidal fluid and kinetic equilibria with nested magnetic surfaces and no continuous symmetry are of great interest in laboratory, astrophysical and space plasmas. Their existence and stability have been open in physics and mathematics for decades. We construct such anisotropic-pressure equilibria by applying the Clemente transformation to exact vacuum fields. They connect smoothly to these fields on a fixed regular domain and preserve a regular magnetic axis, perfectly nested surfaces and spatially varying rotational transform. To our knowledge, the sheared configurations are the first exact anisotropic equilibria combining these properties with positive pressures and a positive firehose margin. The fixed-boundary Chew--Goldberger--Low (CGL) quadratic energy splits into a nonnegative vacuum-field term and a local pressure term, nonnegative for p_perp/p_parallel <= (3+sqrt21)/2 ~ 3.79. For p_parallel >= p_perp each configuration minimizes the finite-amplitude CGL energy over smooth boundary-fixed ideal material deformations. For the current-free configurations, physical guiding-center distributions produce these pressures within the same bound, with no free energy for magnetic-moment-conserving electrostatic perturbations. Trapped particles inherit the vacuum field's second adiabatic invariant at a rescaled magnetic moment, so local closed action contours carry over. The equilibrium code DESC reproduces them from the exact solution. Kinetic stability for surface-dependent rescalings and against general nonlinear electromagnetic perturbations remains open.

articles.title: Analysis of Solid Boron Injection for ITER
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Since ITER will now operate with a full tungsten divertor and first wall, the ITER Organization is considering boron wall conditioning schemes to getter oxygen and reduce tungsten sputtering to avoid excessive radiation to ensure that ITER can reach and sustain high- performance plasma operation. ITER has adopted Glow Discharge Boronization (GDB) in deuterated diborane (B₂D₆) as its main technique, which can only be performed in the absence of magnetic fields, but has also requested a study to determine how effective solid boron injection (SBI), which can be performed during plasma operation, using either an Impurity Powder Dropper (IPD) or a boron pellet injector, might be as a risk mitigation to achieving Q=10. Solid impurity injection has been used for decades as a wall conditioning technique on numerous tokamaks and stellarators around the world. The study presented here begins to assess SBI on ITER by first quantifying the boron source term across a particle size scan from 1 μm to 5 mm diameter and an injection velocity scan from 5 -- 200 m/s for several ITER plasma conditions: 1) Start of Research Operations (SRO) diverted L-mode, 2) Q=10 H-mode, and 3) low plasma current and low power limiter operation. Modeling of the ablation, transport, erosion and redeposition of solid boron is being carried out with the Dust Injection Simulator (DIS), the Neutral Gas Shielding (NGS), EMC3-EIRENE and WallDYN3D models. In the first steps presented here, the DIS and NGS models are compared for calculating the boron source term that is then used as input to EMC3-EIRENE and will later be used with WallDYN3D.

articles.title: Rescene-ESM: an Earth system model built around a frozen AI weather model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Earth system models underpin climate projections, but their cost limits how many scenarios, ensemble members and impact pathways can be explored. Machine-learning weather models forecast as skillfully as physics-based models at a fraction of the cost, yet coupled to an ocean they have produced weak El Nino variability or have learned it from climate-model output, and none carries the climate through rivers to the people exposed to it. Here we present Rescene-ESM, an Earth system model whose coupler, YAHO, yokes a frozen 20.8-million-parameter AI weather model to physically formulated ocean, sea-ice, land, river, carbon and energy components constrained by observations. Adding the couplings one at a time shows what each contributes: over a climatological ocean the AI atmosphere varies from year to year by a third of the observed amount over the oceans, and an interactive mixed layer, an equatorial wave ocean, the residual of the observed sea surface temperature (SST) equation as stochastic forcing and the land's moisture flux raise this step by step and bring El Nino and its teleconnections, leaving the mean climate almost unchanged. The full model simulates about 1,000 years per day on one graphics processing unit, holds the observed climate for a thousand years without drift, reproduces the observed 1979-2022 global warming, carries forced change with a physically based structure around the frozen network (transient climate response 1.60 K), routes runoff to 212 river gauges with a median seasonal-cycle correlation of 0.79 and, driven by emissions, separates the heatwave exposure of an SSP1 and an SSP3 world by a factor of 4.7 in 2081-2100, three-quarters of it through the warmer climate.

articles.title: Combining rock typing and NMR logging to estimate permeability in complex carbonate formations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Estimating intrinsic permeability from nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) logs is difficult in heterogeneous carbonates because a single calibration may not represent distinct pore systems. We evaluated whether flow-zone-indicator (FZI)-based rock typing improves empirical calibration of the modified Schlumberger-Doll Research (SDR) model in the Arbuckle Group, Kansas. The analysis used 470 depth-matched core-permeability and NMR measurements from the Wellington and Cutter wells. FZI calculated from measured permeability and NMR-derived porosity was grouped using K-means clustering. Six clusters were identified, but one singleton cluster was excluded, leaving five rock types for SDR calibration. Relative to the global model (without clustering), rock-type-specific calibration reduced testing root mean square log-transformed error (RMSLE) from 1.215 to 0.240-0.427 and increased coefficient of determination (CD) from -0.106 to 0.578-0.924. The fitted porosity exponents ranged from 0.053 to 0.521, indicating that porosity provided limited additional information in some rock types and that the SDR parameters should be treated as empirical calibration quantities. Because measured permeability was used to calculate the FZI before the within-cluster splits, these results represent conditional performance for samples with known FZI membership, not blind permeability prediction. Field implementation will require a permeability-independent method for assigning rock types.

articles.title: Regulating pedestal pressure profile by microtearing modes in the EAST tokamak
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The pedestal pressure profile plays a critical role in determining the overall confinement of tokamak fusion plasmas. This letter reports the first evidence on regulating pedestal pressure profile by microtearing modes (MTMs) via limiting the pedestal gradient, which was thought to be limited by kinetic ballooning modes over the last decades. This is observed in an ITER-baseline-like target plasma in the EAST tokamak. MTMs arrest the recovery of pedestal electron temperature (and hence pressure) by clamping its gradient at a critical value while leaving the density profile essentially unaffected. Global fluid and local gyrokinetic simulations confirm the excitation of MTMs when the pedestal electron temperature gradient exceeds a threshold value in this experiment. This finding reveals MTMs as an alternative electromagnetic micro-instability that imposes an additional constraint in determining the pedestal structure in tokamaks.

articles.title: Offline Evaluation of Information-Theoretic Adaptive Bayesian Vector Magnetometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An information-theoretic adaptive Bayesian framework for jointly estimating the longitudinal and transverse components of a magnetic field from the time-resolved optical response of a cold ⁸⁷Rb ensemble is presented. A linearly polarized continuous-wave probe drives the D₂ F=1 → F'=0 transition, producing coherent population trapping (CPT) lineshapes whose width, contrast, and transient dynamics depend sensitively on the ambient magnetic field. The full temporal signal, including early-time transient signal and the steady-state absorption, is compared against a precomputed Maxwell-Bloch forward model. The joint posterior distributions of the longitudinal and transverse components of the magnetic field are updated sequentially, while marginalizing over instrumental nuisance parameters arising from the finite resolution of the magnetic bias coil supply. At each step, the applied longitudinal bias field is chosen to maximize the expected Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between the current prior and the anticipated posterior, the expected information gain. As a proof of principle, the protocol is validated in post-processing on pre-recorded experimental scans, and both field components converge to well localized field estimates with weak correlation between them, consistent with the distinct dependence of the CPT resonance position and lineshape on the field components. These results establish an information-theoretic framework for joint vector field estimation from transient cold-atom spectroscopy. However, there exists a systematic forward-model discrepancy, showing that posterior concentration alone does not establish accuracy and motivating nuisance-parameter inference in future online implementations.

articles.title: High-sensitivity sensing technology of 10 MHz radio frequency electric field based on Rydberg atoms
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To address the pressing need for high-sensitivity, miniaturized electric field sensors in the short-wave communication band (3-30 MHz), this study proposes and demonstrates a radio frequency electric field quantum sensing scheme based on cesium atomic Rydberg states and the electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) effect. The scheme employs an all-infrared optical design, utilizing 852 nm probe light, 1470 nm dressing light, and 780 nm coupling light to efficiently prepare the 49P3/2 Rydberg state in a room-temperature cesium vapor cell, which is then probed non-destructively via ladder-type four-level EIT spectroscopy.

articles.title: Hydrograd v2.0: a differentiable two-dimensional shallow-water model on unstructured meshes with steady and unsteady adjoints for calibration and closure learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Hydrograd v2.0, a significantly improved differentiable 2D shallow-water model written in Python with JAX. The model solves the shallow-water equations on the unstructured meshes of production models such as SRH-2D and HEC-RAS 2D with a well-balanced, positivity-preserving finite-volume scheme that handles wetting and drying. Gradients are tailored to the type of problem. Steady states are found by Newton's method with an exact sparse Jacobian obtained by graph colouring, and their gradients follow from the implicit function theorem at the cost of one linear solve. Unsteady flows are differentiated in reverse mode with checkpointing, or with an implicit time integrator whose gradient costs about two forward runs. All gradients agree with finite differences, to about 10⁻⁸ for steady flows. On the Savannah River case, the steady water surface differs from that of SRH-2D by 4.7,mm (root mean square). Steady closure learning was 96 times faster than differentiating through time marching and reached a lower loss. An inflow hydrograph was inverted from stage records with a peak error of 2,%. In an unsteady roughness calibration, a singular value decomposition analysis of the sensitivity matrix showed that the stage records at the gauges are 70 to 160 times more sensitive to the total resistance of the reach than to its distribution among the roughness zones, which explains why only a gauge layout with gauges in every zone recovered all five roughness values. On one GPU, a mesh of 512,000 cells takes 7.6,s for a forward run and 51,s for a gradient.

articles.title: Estimating Permeability of Carbonate Rocks from NMR T2 Distribution and Formation Factor Using a Physics-Based Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) logging provides a nondestructive method for characterizing pore structure and fluid distribution in reservoir rocks. Conventional permeability models, such as the Schlumberger-Doll Research (SDR) and Timur-Coates (TC) equations, have been widely used to estimate permeability from NMR T2 relaxation time distributions. However, these empirical models require calibration against core-measured permeability, and their fitted coefficients often vary substantially across lithologies and pore systems. In this study, we formulate and evaluate an NMR-informed implementation of a physics-based permeability relationship derived from critical path analysis (CPA) by linking the characteristic pore length scale to the dominant NMR relaxation time. We estimate permeability (k) using NMR T2 distributions and electrical formation factor (F) for 14 carbonate rock samples collected from the Morro do Chaves Formation in the Sergipe-Alagoas Basin, Brazil. We compare the predictive performance of this formulation with that of calibrated SDR and TC models. The proposed CPA-NMR formulation achieves a root mean squared logarithmic error (RMSLE) of 0.56 without calibration against measured permeability from the investigated formation. These findings indicate the potential of combining NMR relaxation measurements with electrical formation factor for physics-based permeability estimation. Further evaluation using independent datasets is needed to assess applicability across formations and lithologies.

articles.title: Three-dimensional polarization of thermal fields at arbitrary distances from thin-film emitters
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances have shown that thermal radiation can exhibit strong polarization in both the near and far fields. However, most existing studies focus on paraxial far-field emission, where polarization can be described using conventional two-dimensional (2D) Stokes parameters. Non-paraxial thermal radiation, with three nonzero vector components, requires a fully three-dimensional (3D) polarization description. This work develops a generalized theoretical method for analyzing thermal-radiation polarization at arbitrary distances from an emitter. Fluctuation-dissipation theory is employed to determine the 3×3 coherence matrix of the thermally emitted electromagnetic field, from which generalized 3D Stokes parameters are obtained. This method is applied to planar slabs composed of isotropic, anisotropic, and nonreciprocal materials. The results reveal distinct polarization behavior across the near- and far-field regimes. Near-field polarization is strongly influenced by evanescent waves and polariton dispersion, whereas far-field polarization is primarily governed by polarization-dependent radiative properties, including differences between transverse-electric (TE) and transverse-magnetic (TM) emission. Slab thickness further modifies polarization by controlling supported modes and interference effects. In addition, circular polarization, which vanishes in reciprocal slabs, is observed in n-type doped InAs under an external magnetic field that breaks reciprocity. This work provides a unified framework for characterizing the polarization of thermal electromagnetic fields from the extreme near field to the far field.

articles.title: Robust Implicit Neural Representation for Multiparameter Elastic Full-Waveform Inversion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiparameter elastic full-waveform inversion (EFWI) provides a powerful means of reconstructing subsurface elastic properties, but its practical application remains challenging because of strong nonlinearity, parameter crosstalk, and the different sensitivities of seismic data to individual elastic parameters. We develop a robust implicit neural representation (INR) framework for multiparameter EFWI, using continuous neural representations to parameterize the subsurface model and provide an effective model-space constraint during inversion. Within this framework, we systematically investigate different elastic parameterizations and demonstrate that parameterization plays a critical role in controlling parameter coupling and inversion stability. Among the tested formulations, combining P-wave velocity (Vp), P-wave impedance (Ip), and the Vs/Vp ratio provides the most robust overall performance, yielding improved parameter separation and more reliable reconstruction of elastic properties. We evaluate the proposed approach on the Marmousi and Overthrust models under increasingly challenging inversion conditions and further apply it to the field Volve ocean-bottom-node dataset. Both synthetic and field-data results demonstrate that the INR-based formulation, together with the Vp-Ip-Vs/Vp parameterization, improves inversion stability, suppresses parameter cross-talk and inversion artifacts, and produces geologically coherent multiparameter models. These results highlight the importance of jointly considering model representation and physical parameterization in multiparameter EFWI and demonstrate the potential of robust INR-based inversion for complex synthetic and field seismic applications.

articles.title: A Mathematical Multiscale Framework for Nonlinear Modeling of the Heliosphere
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11999v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The inner heliosphere is a highly nonlinear continuous medium where macroscopic ideal magnetohydrodynamics is inextricably coupled with microscopic, fully developed stochastic turbulence. State-of-the-art global 3D numerical solvers, while proficient at capturing the large-scale propagation of extreme space physics phenomena such as coronal mass ejections and corotating interaction regions, are computationally constrained by grid resolution and fundamental partial differential equation formulations. Consequently, they inherently do not resolve the local small-scale turbulent cascade, magnetic intermittency, and localized thermodynamic anomalies. To bridge this fundamental scaleseparation gap, this paper presents a novel mathematical and numerical framework that harmoniously integrates global heliospheric structures with local turbulent physics. The framework generates a highly realistic synthetic continuous medium by superimposing a stochastically driven nonlinear turbulent cascade onto a bimodal deterministic background flow. This cascade reproduces theoretical constraints for fractional power spectral densities, magnetic compressibility, and small-scale intermittency via a discrete multiplicative binomial cascade (p-model). This multiscale continuous background is dynamically perturbed by analytical models of large-scale nonlinear transients, including kinematic shock steepening, continuous current sheet topological reversals, and solar ejecta formalized as asymmetric force-free magnetic flux ropes. By generating exact spatio-temporal arrays across arbitrary distributed coordinates, this unified mathematical model overcomes the spatial degeneracy of single-point observations and provides a computationally efficient analytical baseline for performance models supporting future in-situ multi-spacecraft heliospheric missions, which are currently in their feasibility study phase.

articles.title: SATE: Transferable Spin-Adapted Neural Wavefunctions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate prediction of molecular reactivity requires both accurate and computationally efficient description of electron correlation and spin across various molecular geometries and electronic states. We introduce SATE, a spin-adapted transferable neural wavefunction architecture with effective core potentials. SATE combines a transferable neural wavefunction, the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, and effective core potentials into a single foundation model architecture pretrained on compositions containing selected elements from hydrogen to bromine. After pretraining and adaptation, our model is able to predict 3d transition-metal spin-state gaps, bond dissociation energies, and reaction energies by addressing two key issues. First, including the core potentials into the model allows us to reduce the number of explicitly treated electrons. Second, using spin-adapted antisymmetrization enforces the prescribed total spin by construction. By testing our model with 3d transition metal chemistry, we evaluate our model's description of strong electron correlation and competing electronic states in such compounds. We find that pretraining improves most tested component energies at matched adaptation budgets, while improvements in spin-state gaps, dissociation energies, and reaction energies remain system dependent. Ultimately, our work lays the foundation for more accurate and transferable modeling of molecular systems by combining the computational efficiency of effective core potentials with explicit control over total spin.

articles.title: Heterogeneous Acceleration of TRIMEG++ code using OpenMP for Gyrokinetic Simulations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Turbulent transport largely determines the performance of magnetic-confinement fusion devices such as tokamaks, and gyrokinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations are a principal tool to predict it. Advancing up to hundreds of millions of markers and solving large sparse field systems at every time step makes whole-device simulations among the most expensive in plasma physics. GPUs can accelerate this workload, but porting a complex code requires restructuring its parallelism and memory traffic, ideally without a separate version per vendor. In this work, the gyrokinetic code TRIMEG-C1, whose unstructured triangular mesh and high-order finite elements cover both the confined core and the open-field-line edge of the plasma, is rewritten in C++ as TRIMEG++ and fully offloaded to GPUs with OpenMP target directives, so that one portable code base runs on both AMD and NVIDIA hardware. The particle-to-grid projection is offloaded in its standard and field-aligned formulations, the PETSc-based field solver runs on the GPU through the library's backends, and, together with the previously offloaded particle pusher, every stage whose cost scales with the marker count runs on the GPU. All speedups are node-to-node comparisons against a 256-core CPU node (2x AMD EPYC 9754). On the TCV-X21 tokamak reference case, the offloaded kernels reproduce the CPU results to a relative accuracy of 1e-11, and the full simulation runs 4.1-6.1x faster on a node with two AMD MI300A and 2.1-3.0x faster on a node with four NVIDIA A100, with the speedup growing with problem size. The MI300A, with shared CPU-GPU memory, needs no explicit data transfers, whereas the A100 needs them managed by hand. These results show that directive-based offloading can accelerate a complex gyrokinetic code across GPU vendors, making whole-volume tokamak simulations with hundreds of millions of markers practical on a single GPU node.

articles.title: Data-Driven Conservation Laws for Newtonian Systems: Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Eisenhart-Duval Geometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a Physics-Informed Neural Network approach for the data-driven reconstruction of the symmetries and conservation laws of Newtonian dynamical systems, based on the geometrization of the dynamics through the Eisenhart-Duval lift. Within the Eisenhart-Duval lift, the symmetry conditions reduce to the linear Killing or Conformal Killing equations of the extended metric. We combine a Hamiltonian neural network, which reconstructs the potential function from the data, with a random-feature neural network, which solves the symmetry conditions for the collineations of the extended geometry. From the learned vector fields we construct the Lie algebra and, through Noether's theorem, the corresponding conserved quantities, while the derivation of the curvature invariants for the extended geometry provide allow us to perform an independent consistency test. We apply the method to the one-dimensional Ermakov-Pinney equation and to the one-dimensional harmonic oscillator, with and without a quartic perturbation, by using different level of noise in the phase-space data. For the Ermakov-Pinney equation, the three Killing vectors of the flat extended plane, and the corresponding nonlocal conservation laws, are recovered for, while for the harmonic oscillator, the ten conformal Killing vectors which form the so(3,2) Lie algebra are determined for noise levels up to 10%. When the quartic term is added, the broken symmetries are identified as approximate symmetries.

articles.title: Magnetized plasma modulator for polarization-tunable ultrahigh-power single-cycle lasers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultrahigh power lasers with tunable polarization and few-cycle duration have long been considered the holy grail of high-power laser science, as they push light-matter interactions into an entirely new physical regime. Yet such pulses remain far beyond the reach of conventional solid-state optics and technologies. Here, we introduce a novel magnetized plasma modulator that boosts linearly polarized lasers from petawatt to exawatt powers while simultaneously enabling tunable polarization, offering a promising approach for high-power laser development. This is achieved in density-tailored plasmas by combining dispersive compression of a chirped picosecond laser pulse with magneto-chiral group-velocity splitting in a few-Tesla magnetic field. It can generate circularly or elliptically polarized pulses with extremely high compression ratios (over 1000) and extremely short durations (down to the single-cycle level) in a compact and efficient manner. These findings demonstrate a feasible pathway toward exawatt-class few-cycle lasers with tunable polarization, opening new avenues for a wide range of cutting-edge research and applications.

articles.title: N-Layer quasi-geostrophic modons in a vertically sheared flow
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12433v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modons, or dipolar vortices, are a form of propagating vortex solution consisting of two counterrotating regions of fluid and moving together under self-advection. They are common features of the upper ocean that can remain stable over long times, thereby transporting fluid over large distances. Here, we present a semi-analytical method for finding modon solutions in a vertically-sheared background flow using the multi-layer quasi-geostrophic framework. This method works for arbitrarily many fluid layers and builds on our previous studies of multi-layer modon solutions. We present three example of modons in a background flow, highlighting the effect of varying relative potential velocity between layers and the impact of depth-dependent potential vorticity gradients arising from surface deformation and velocity shear.

articles.title: Effects of pulse durations in atom interferometry with double Raman diffraction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12586v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Double Raman diffraction is a key enabling technique for future space missions relying on atom interferometry that offers enhanced sensitivity and intrinsic suppression of systematic effects. This diffraction mechanism naturally arises when employing a retro-reflection configuration in microgravity, but then accelerations can no longer be determined through a frequency-chirp scan. As a consequence, measurements become much more sensitive to systematic effects associated with pulse timing and duration. Indeed, the finite pulse duration can introduce additional phase shifts and small modifications of the arm trajectories, which are critical sources of error in high-precision measurements. In this work, we present the first complete analytical results of these effects for double Raman diffraction, building upon previous work for single diffraction and extending the standard literature. Our analysis determines the impact of finite pulse durations on the full interferometer sequence, quantifying the shifts of the atomic wave packets' trajectories and the acquired phases. The description relies on a comprehensive framework describing matter-wave propagation in terms of central trajectories and centered wave packets, and can be easily incorporated into relativistic treatments. Furthermore, we make use of group theoretic methods that are particularly useful when accounting for residual accelerations and frequency chirps, which are also relevant for ground-based applications. Our study includes time-dependent accelerations and frequency chirps, gravity gradients, retardation effects, AC Stark shifts induced by the Raman pulses, and external forces such those due to magnetic fields or temperature gradients in the black-body radiation.

articles.title: FAIR Universe Weak Lensing ML Uncertainty Challenge: Dataset and Cosmological Inference Competition
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10228v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weak gravitational lensing is a powerful cosmological probe that enables direct mapping of the matter distribution and precise constraints on the fundamental parameters governing structure formation in the universe. In recent years, machine learning has shown strong potential for extracting cosmological information from weak-lensing data beyond traditional summary statistics. However, progress has been limited by the lack of standardized benchmarks that capture the complexity of the dataset, simulator imperfections, and various systematic biases encountered in realistic analyses. To address this gap, we present the FAIR Universe Weak Lensing Machine Learning Uncertainty Challenge, one of the NeurIPS 2025 competitions, as a benchmark dataset and evaluation study. Our dataset reflects realistic weak-lensing observations, incorporating multiple systematic biases, and thereby providing a controlled testbed for robust cosmological inference under uncertainties. We summarize the main methodological advances developed by the winners of our challenge, including data augmentation with conditional optimal transport, an AI-agent-driven approach for parameter inference, ensemble learning, Vision Transformer-based architectures, and physics-informed feature integration. By unifying the benchmark dataset and the winning solutions, this work provides a community resource for developing and evaluating machine learning methods for weak lensing cosmology and, more broadly, for scientific inference under systematic uncertainties.

articles.title: Universal Approximation by Equivariant Message-Passing Graph Neural Networks with a Bilinear Readout
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10772v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove universal approximation for the bilinear-readout equivariant message-passing network (BREMP), a reference architecture for equivariant graph neural network interatomic potentials. Its layers combine equivariant convolutions with affine maps, and its readout forms invariants from products of the equivariant features. We construct a one-layer feature that determines the local environment up to permutations of atoms of the same type. The construction uses spherical harmonic filters of degree no larger than the largest number of neighbors at a common distance from the center. Iterating the construction recovers the environment reachable in as many hops as there are layers, using the same bound on filter degrees at the layer cutoff. The readout approximates every continuous invariant function of the features uniformly on compact sets. Together these give universal approximation of atomic energies at a prescribed physical range using a shorter layer cutoff. We assume that, throughout the admissible class, message passing reaches all neighbors in each physical environment within a common number of layers. Finally, DPA4, an interatomic potential architecture in production use, inherits this result by approximating the BREMP layers constructed in the proof and realizing the bilinear readout.

articles.title: SWXAI: A Unified Multimodal Explainability Library for Space Weather Forecasting and Heliophysics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10861v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Space weather forecasting and heliophysics increasingly rely on machine learning models that process heterogeneous inputs such as multi-viewpoint multi-wavelength solar images and rasters, multivariate time series, spatial annotations, and tabular event-level data. However, explainability workflows remain fragmented across libraries, model interfaces, and output formats, limiting reuse and reproducibility. We present SWXAI, an open-source library that unifies explainable AI (XAI) workflows for image, time-series, and tabular data in space weather forecasting and heliophysics. SWXAI provides a common, extensible interface across commonly used vision, time-series, and tabular learning models, with validation, adaptation, and persistent explanation objects. It also includes domain-grounded examples, reproducible notebooks, tests, and documentation, enabling users to inspect outputs, swap models or explainers, and extend workflows to new heliophysics datasets. SWXAI reduces modality-specific engineering overhead and supports comparable, reusable explanations across heterogeneous scientific machine learning pipelines. A benchmark against direct backend implementations shows that SWXAI substantially reduces the code users write to produce an explanation, with no practical runtime cost.

articles.title: Online Imitation Learning for Stabilizing Vlasov--Poisson Plasmas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10870v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the problem of controlling instability in the Vlasov--Poisson plasma systems, a fundamental challenge for nuclear fusion control. Motivated by the partial observability of plasma states in practice, we investigate imitation learning algorithms that learn from a fully-observable expert controller, but operate under macroscopic measurements. We theoretically establish a separation between online and offline imitation learning --- even a small behavior cloning error leads to error compounding that exponentially amplifies instability over time. By way of contrast, the online imitation learning loss can polynomially control the stability of rollout trajectories. We then propose a DAgger-style algorithm that learns the stabilizing controller under partial observability. Simulation results on a 1D Vlasov--Poisson system demonstrate that our algorithm can effectively stabilize plasma instabilities over longer time horizons than behavior cloning.

articles.title: Probing Exotic Electron-Electron Interactions via Adiabatic Spin Inversion in MRFM
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11367v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Light bosons beyond the Standard Model can mediate exotic spin-dependent interactions between electrons, motivating sensitive searches at short distances. We propose a magnetic resonance force microscopy (MRFM) scheme that exploits oscillating-cantilever-driven adiabatic reversals (OSCAR) of electron spins to convert these interactions into measurable mechanical signals. The ferromagnetic tip serves as both a dense polarized-spin source and a source of magnetic-field gradients, enabling force detection without magnetic shielding between the source and sensor. Within a linearized treatment of the coupled spin-mechanical dynamics, we derive resonance-frequency shifts associated with the V₂ and V₃ interactions and a second-harmonic force signal arising from the velocity-dependent V₈ interaction. We further investigate interrupted-OSCAR differential detection and distance-dependent measurements to discriminate exotic signals from conventional magnetic backgrounds. Using representative parameters from ensemble and single-spin MRFM experiments, we estimate the projected sensitivity under specified noise and statistical assumptions. The results suggest that the proposed scheme could provide complementary sensitivity to short-range spin-dependent interactions, with the potential to improve existing constraints on V₂ over selected submicrometer interaction ranges. Our study establishes adiabatic spin-inversion MRFM as a promising approach to probing exotic electron-electron forces.

articles.title: Scalable Bayesian Optimization for Efficient Exploration of Moire Patterns
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12010v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large materials design spaces often contain rare high-performing configurations that are difficult to identify through trial-and-error exploration or purely representative machine-learning (ML) sampling. In this work, we present FruBO, a flexible Bayesian Optimization framework for accelerating the discovery of optimal configurations in computationally demanding materials design problems. As a case study, we investigate multilayer Moiré patterns generated by the superposition of six rotated hexagonal lattices, where the objective is to identify the rotational conformation that maximizes pore-size uniformity, quantified using the Jain fairness index. The resulting benchmark contains 600,000 unique configurations and exhibits a highly skewed objective distribution, making the global optimum difficult to locate by random sampling. We compare random exploration, Gaussian Process-based Bayesian Optimization, and Bayesian Optimization using a lightweight CatBoost surrogate with committee-based uncertainty estimation. Random sampling identifies the global optimum only after 533,012 evaluations, requiring approximately 31 hours, while Gaussian Process-based BO becomes impractical due to GPU memory exhaustion after 290 acquired samples. In contrast, FruBO with CatBoost identifies the global optimum after 1,470 acquired samples and approximately 1.15 hours. These results demonstrate that scalable surrogate models can substantially improve the feasibility and efficiency of BO in large nanomaterials design spaces.

articles.title: Topological Deep Learning Challenge 2026: Bridging the Gap
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper describes the 2026 edition of the Topological Deep Learning Challenge: Bridging the Gap, hosted at the second Topology, Algebra, and Geometry in Data Science (TAG-DS) Conference. Where previous editions grew the modelling and data ecosystem of Topological Deep Learning (TDL), this edition set out to place Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Topological Neural Networks (TNNs) side by side under a single evaluation pipeline. Participants implemented recent state-of-the-art architectures in TopoBench, with Track 1 covering GNNs and Track 2 covering TNNs. They evaluated these implementations on shared synthetic benchmarks generated with GraphUniverse, which independently controls homophily, average degree and degree-distribution heaviness. The challenge yielded 68 qualifying submissions from 34 teams, spanning the graph, simplicial, cellular, hypergraph and combinatorial domains. For the first time, submissions were also tracked on a public leaderboard, which we summarize and analyze here. Our analysis finds that the differences between the submitted tracks are strongly task-dependent: the mean accuracy gap is modest on community detection, while on triangle counting the Track 1 mean error is 1.85 times the Track 2 mean. Several structurally informed GNNs also outperform the Track 2 mean on triangle counting.

articles.title: fNIRSAtlas: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Classification
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is a promising modality for brain-computer interfaces and cognitive state decoding, but progress in machine learning for fNIRS has been limited by small, isolated datasets and inconsistent evaluation protocols. We introduce fNIRSAtlas, the largest open benchmark for fNIRS classification to date, comprising 23 classification tasks from 19 public data collections, spanning diverse experimental paradigms, including motor execution, motor imagery, mental arithmetic, working memory, and emotion recognition. fNIRSAtlas provides a fully automated pipeline from raw data to evaluation and defines standardized benchmark tasks for both cross-subject and within-subject classification, ensuring reproducible comparison of methods. We evaluate a variety of baseline models from fNIRS and related neuroimaging and time-series machine learning literature on the benchmark. Our results demonstrate that performance varies substantially across tasks and that methods validated on limited data -- especially deep learning approaches -- often fail to generalize beyond their original evaluation. fNIRSAtlas serves as an extensible, open, and reproducible benchmark to support more robust and cumulative progress in machine learning for fNIRS data. Our code and data can be found at https://fnirsatlas.github.io.

articles.title: Transferring local rib responses to new component geometries in sheet forming with a graph-based Transformer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sheet metal components often consist of a global geometry, such as the corner radii and forming depth of a corner component, and local features added to it. During forming, both affect material flow. A surrogate learning all their combinations may need large training data. However, the same local feature type is often used on many global geometries. This study therefore partly decouples local features from the global geometry. The local-feature effect is first learned on one global geometry, needing fewer simulations than learning all combinations, then transferred to other global geometries via transfer learning, which can need fewer target simulations than training from scratch. A baseline-conditioned residual surrogate, R-BiLoGo, is proposed for ribs on the side walls of hot-stamped corner components. Its inputs are the baseline response and the geometric perturbation introduced by the ribs. Its outputs are the changes in displacement and thinning from the baseline. R-BiLoGo gave lower errors than a hierarchical graph-based model and a Transolver-based model on the source geometry, and on two of three selected target geometries after transfer. Across the 22 target geometries, transfer learning with 20 target simulations gave errors similar to or lower than training from scratch with 80 target simulations for about half of the targets. With the same 80 target simulations, transfer learning reduced errors for 95% of targets. The effect of the global geometry on transfer was studied with four parameter-free geometric descriptors and controlled variations across 4 corner subclasses. The benefit of transfer decreased with increasing surface distance and high-curvature change between source and target, and for targets shallower than the source. These trends were also seen in other corner types with a different magnitude.

articles.title: Projected Neural Additive Models as Universal Approximators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural additive models (NAMs) offer interpretability but lack expressivity due to their rigid additive structure, whereas multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) achieve universal approximation at the cost of transparency. We establish the first theoretical foundation for projected neural additive models (PNAMs), which augment NAMs with a learnable linear transformation boldsymbolT to capture cross-variable interactions. While standard NAMs cannot approximate even the simplest interaction term χ₁ χ₂ because their cross-derivatives are identically zero, we prove that PNAMs are universal approximators and characterize the minimum number of projections required for exact polynomial representation. Furthermore, we derive an approximation rate of O(M⁻s / ⁽N ⁻ ¹⁾) for C^s functions (i.e., functions with s continuous derivatives), where M denotes the number of projections and N the input dimension; this rate is known to be optimal for ridge function approximation. To recover interpretability from the projected inputs, we introduce structured sparsity regularizers and post-hoc symbolic regression techniques that enable global input ranking, parameter pruning, and the conversion of learned bases into compact analytical expressions. Experiments on knot theory invariants, MNIST, and phase field fracture mechanics demonstrate that PNAMs match or surpass similar architectures in accuracy while discovering salient features and yielding symbolic models with orders of magnitude fewer parameters.

articles.title: Fast Accurate Quantum Monte Carlo without Metropolis Adjustment
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In quantum systems, physical quantities of interest can be expressed as expectation values of a probability distribution, which allows their estimation by Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods. This approach, an instance of Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC), plays a central role in obtaining predictions of system properties relevant to condensed matter and high energy physics. The use of Hamiltonian dynamics to design a Markov kernel, known as Hybrid or Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC), is widespread in quantum applications. In this context, it is standard to use an HMC kernel that is ``adjusted'' with the Metropolis-Hastings (MH) criterion, so that estimates of expectations converge to their true value in the limit of infinite sample size. However, recent work in computational statistics suggests that an emphunadjusted HMC kernel can be significantly more efficient, while safely maintaining an asymptotic bias which is small relative to the error arising from the variance of the finite sample size. We adapt this approach to the QMC setting, focusing on a challenging and high-dimensional emphspin-fermion model of a quantum phase transition. We find that unadjusted methods outperform adjusted HMC in terms of effective sample size per gradient call, while retaining accurate results.

articles.title: Semiprime Factorization with Discrete Diffusion and Beam Search: Scaling Laws
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that transformer architectures trained with discrete denoising diffusion and decoded via guided test-time beam search can learn to recover the prime factors of semiprime integers directly from data. Our approach establishes a new frontier for learning-based semiprime factorization, successfully factoring 68-bit integers-a substantial advance over the prior 56-bit state of the art. While computationally less efficient than classical factoring algorithms, our model requires no domain-specific number-theoretic priors and learns purely from training examples. In practice, the diffusion model acts as a generative prior, identifying promising factor candidates where exact verification or lattice-based post-processing can complete the factorization. Furthermore, we derive empirical scaling laws relating approximation quality to training data volume, model size, and test-time computation. In contrast to language, problem size is the key driver of scaling behavior. Achieving a fixed accuracy on a held-out test set requires compute that scales exponentially with bit length. Consequently, our findings pose no threat to security, as the projected compute cost required to factorize cryptographically relevant integers remains prohibitive.

articles.title: Rethinking How to Leverage Cheap Physics for Data-Efficient Neural Operators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural operators learn mappings from PDE inputs, such as initial conditions and coefficient fields, to the corresponding solutions. Once trained, they can rapidly predict solutions for new inputs. However, obtaining input-solution pairs for supervised training often requires expensive numerical simulations, whereas PDE inputs and governing equations provide inexpensive physical information. This raises a question: how can cheap physical information reduce the need for labeled solutions? A natural approach is to use physics to select inputs for labeling, but our acquisition experiments show no consistent advantage over random sampling. This observation motivates exploring an alternative: using cheap physics to improve neural operator initialization before supervised training. We propose Physics-Informed Initialization (PI-Init), a simple yet effective method that pretrains neural operators on unlabeled inputs using physics-informed losses and retains the learned parameters for supervised fine-tuning on the labeled dataset. A linearized analysis shows that pretraining can improve downstream prediction accuracy by reducing initialization errors that limited labeled data cannot effectively correct. Experiments across diverse PDE benchmarks and neural operator architectures demonstrate improvements in predictive accuracy, out-of-distribution generalization, and label efficiency. Representative results show error reductions of up to 62.7% at the same label budget and comparable or better accuracy with 90% fewer labels, relative to supervised-only training.

articles.title: Can Time Series Foundation Models Serve as Surrogates for Power Systems Dynamic Simulation?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-fidelity dynamic simulation is essential for scientific and engineering applications, but its computational cost limits large-scale scenario screening. We investigate the use of pretrained time-series foundation models (TSFMs) as computationally efficient surrogates to address this limitation. In-context learning and post-training strategies, including retrieval-augmented reference sample selection and physics-informed regularization, are considered in the investigation. Results are benchmarked against a traditional AI model representative of the state-of-the-art in the domain. Experiments using an open-source TSFM and data from a simulated 9-bus power system indicate promising results. Retrieval augmentation improves in-context learning performance, and fine-tuning leads to superior results compared to the traditional AI model, especially when including physics-informed regularization. The fine-tuned TSFMs achieve lower errors and improved computational costs compared to the traditional AI model, and a 563× speedup compared to the original physics-based simulation.

articles.title: Plug-and-Play Verifier for Decoupling Process Reward in Stabilizing Long-Horizon Agentic Reasoning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stabilizing long-horizon reasoning requires intelligent agents to sustain useful progress across successive reasoning steps and tool interactions. Such agents are typically trained with reinforcement learning (RL), where actor-critic RL uses a learnable critic network to estimate step advantages, while critic-free methods such as GRPO eliminate critic models and rely mostly on the group variants of sparse outcome-only rewards. Both reward types leave partially useful failed trajectories either implicit or indistinguishable from entirely unproductive ones, and as reasoning horizons grow, it becomes difficult to maintain consistent reasoning trajectories. In this work, we propose a plug-and-play verifier framework for stabilizing long-horizon reasoning through explicit verification of intermediate reasoning artifacts. Specifically, the framework decouples process verification through a unified interface that extracts intermediate reasoning artifacts from agent running trajectories, evaluates them using domain-specific verifiers, and aggregates the verification scores as bounded process reward. Then, we combine our dense verified process rewards and the sparse outcome rewards through a two-stage post-training schedule. We showed that with plug-and-play verifiers, we further stabilize the reasoning steps as last-mile self-reflection and self-consistency. Typical evaluation on HotpotQA using Qwen3.5-4B achieves a superior accuracy (60.18%), outperforming the standard GRPO baseline (57.73%). Our results suggest that plug-and-play verifiers provide a modular approach to learn more stable and reliable reasoning behaviors over long horizons.

articles.title: Two-Sided Conformal Evidence Sets for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can surface passages that support a claim, contradict it, or fail to address it, yet existing calibrated grounding methods are typically one-sided and model only supporting evidence. We introduce Conformal Evidence Sets (CES), a two-sided framework that returns separate support and refutation sets with finite-sample inclusion coverage of at least 1-α on each side under exchangeability; a Bonferroni union yields joint coverage of at least 1-2α. On labeled candidate pools from the contrastive VitaminC benchmark, CES closely tracks nominal coverage across α!in!0.05,0.10,0.15,0.20,0.30, with maximum deviations of 3.0 percentage points for support and 5.4 for refutation, and reaches essentially the same empirical coverage--size frontier as a test-tuned fixed-threshold heuristic without any test exposure. Stress tests mark the boundary of that guarantee: under FEVER distribution shift both sides under-cover, by up to 12.7 percentage points, and support-side group-stratified recalibration substantially reduces the support gap. Scorer swaps, hard-negative retrieval, cross-dataset transfer, and a live end-to-end pilot expose a clear separation: when exchangeability holds and relevant evidence is retrieved, evidence inclusion remains calibrated even with an imperfect scorer, whereas the support/refute verdict tracks scorer quality directly. Calibrated evidence coverage and reliable verdicts are therefore distinct properties and should be reported separately.

articles.title: Dynamic State Estimation from Sparse PMUs via Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operators
