articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a physics-informed graph neural operator for power system dynamic state estimation. From a sparse, intermittent measurement window at a few generator buses, the operator estimates the rotor-angle and speed trajectories of all machines, unmeasured ones included, in one forward pass. A graph-attention encoder processes the measurements, and the swing equations are imposed as a hard constraint or as a soft one with a learned correction that absorbs model errors. It is trained on simulated measurements, without state labels. With several phasor measurement units, masked training hides one from the input but keeps it in the loss. On four transmission systems, simulations show that the operator is the most accurate estimator that neither optimizes per scenario nor uses state labels, except on the smallest system at large model errors, where tuned Kalman smoothers are better. Networks trained on simulated states are more accurate on the two smallest systems but not on the 118-bus system, where the operator is faster and more accurate than hard-constrained moving-horizon estimation. Under model errors, it matches or outperforms an optimization-based benchmark at a fraction of its cost. The results hold for a detailed machine model with exact parameters seen only through voltage phasors.

articles.title: Spectral Bias Reduction in Local Gated ReLU Architectures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural networks trained by gradient-based methods learn the low-frequency content of a target function faster than its high-frequency content. This spectral bias is well documented, but it is much less clear which architectural choices mitigate it and which cannot. We study the question for shallow ReLU models linear in their trainable parameters, where each mode is learned at a rate given by a Gram-matrix eigenvalue, and for a general symmetric bilinear form a(·,·), so that least-squares regression (a= the L² inner product) and variational or physics-informed losses (a= the H¹ energy form) are two instances of one analysis. Within this framework we propose gated local ReLU dictionaries, obtained by multiplying each ReLU feature by a hat partition-of-unity weight, in the spirit of partition-of-unity finite elements and overlapping Schwarz methods. The resulting Gram matrices are block-banded for any local bilinear form, with a block-Toeplitz interior whose matrix-valued symbol governs the spectrum. The two forms then behave very differently. For L² regression, the symbol is bounded away from zero, the ratio is uniform in the number of windows, and the measured spread of frequency-dependent learning rates falls from 1.9×10⁵ to 4.5 at matched model size. For the H¹ stiffness matrix, the symbol vanishes at zero frequency: gating leaves the Θ(N²) conditioning intact and inverts the frequency ordering instead of removing the bias. A preconditioner built from the same interior stencil will fix the spectral bias, showing that architecture alone is not enough. Experiments on 1D regression and Poisson problems confirm the dichotomy, and the regression effect persists when the hidden-layer parameters are trained as well.

articles.title: EEGFaceSem: An EEG Benchmark with Paired Generative Latents for Semantic Visual Modeling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used to measure brain activity for brain-computer interface applications for its non-invasive nature and high temporal resolution. However, progress in modeling the neural responses to visual semantics has been limited by a reliance on fixed image collections that lack the fine-grained control needed to isolate fine-grained changes in visual features and their relation to perception. In this work, we present EEGFaceSem, a large-scale dataset pairing high-quality EEG with photorealistic face images synthesized from a generative model. We provide the generative latent vector for each stimulus, enabling research into the continuous mapping between a visual latent space and neural representations. Each participant's brain responses were recorded while they attended to specific semantic features (e.g., smiling, hair color) in a rapid serial visual presentation paradigm. The dataset contains EEG signals from 30 participants, totaling 67,200 time-locked EEG recordings. We present benchmarks for single-trial semantic classification under single-subject, cross-subject, and subject-adapted settings, as well as for cross-subject voting that aggregates per-stimulus predictions across participants. We further demonstrate the dataset's unique utility with two complementary applications: deriving semantic directions in the latent space for brain-supervised image editing, and conditioning a generative model on brain-decoded labels for brain-supervised image generation. Our dataset paves the way for advancing brain-computer interfaces (BCI) for semantic-level visual saliency detection and brain-supervised generative modeling. Our dataset and code are openly released at OSF (https://osf.io/2guk3/) and at HuggingFace https://huggingface.co/datasets/yefllower/EEGFaceSem.

articles.title: PIA: Agentic Physics-Informed Runtime Anomaly Detection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Runtime anomaly detectors for cyber-physical systems are either learned as black boxes from normal data, which miss stealthy manipulations that keep every signal inside its normal range, or derived by hand from physical models, which requires expert effort for every plant. We introduce physicsinformed agents (PIA), in which a large language model agent writes the detector itself as a set of physical residuals, such as pump characteristics, tank mass balances, and controller logic, and refines every candidate against normal operating data through an evaluation workbench before deployment. The result is a compact, human-readable detector that runs in milliseconds and names the component behind each alarm. On the BATADAL water distribution attack benchmark, PIA with Claude Opus 5.5 reaches an F1 of 0.878 on the test attacks against 0.504 for the strongest of six statistical and deep baselines, keeps detecting attacks concealed by replayed and offset sensor readings, and attributes every detected test attack to the attacked component. Ablations show that testing hypotheses against data is decisive: agents that write residuals from the plant description alone lose up to 0.28 F1, whereas agents that see only anonymized signals recover most of the physical structure.

articles.title: Learning Actionable Information Landscapes for Multimodal Active Sensing in Hawkmoths
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Animals integrate information across sensory modalities to guide exploration, suggesting that they maintain internal estimates of where actions are expected to reduce uncertainty. However, how such action-conditioned information maps are learned from multimodal sensory experience remains unclear, as previous studies have been largely confined to unimodal sensing frameworks. We introduce a multimodal predictive-coding framework for learning uncertainty-reduction maps from visual and mechanosensory observations in hawkmoth flower interaction tasks. A variational generative model trained on simulated environments recovers modality-specific information landscapes over the action space, capturing how visual patterns, surface geometry, and mechanosensory cues shape the value of exploratory actions. These learned maps are consistent with several features of hawkmoth behavior, including nonzero tracking offsets, probing along visual patterns, and geometry-dependent exploration. Applying the model to behavioral data from flower tracking and nectary search, we find that natural trajectories tend to occupy regions of high uncertainty reduction in these learned maps. Building on these observations, we develop an uncertainty-gated lexicographic algorithm that switches between information gathering and reward exploitation based on perceptual uncertainty. In nectary search, uncertainty gating improves learning relative to exploit-only, ϵ-greedy, fixed-time, and uncertainty-calibrated non-lexicographic controls, with better generalization and robustness to sensory and curvature shifts. These results link information landscapes learned through generative modeling to biological sensing and embodied exploration.

articles.title: MCSA: Multi-Cutoff Spectral Aggregation in SO(3) Equivariant GNNs for Interatomic Potentials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials (MLIPs) based on Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNNs) have achieved remarkable progress in atomistic modeling. However, accurately representing atomic interactions across different spatial scales remains challenging. In this work, we investigate the radial spectral properties of SO(3)-equivariant message passing and establish that the cutoff radius controls the characteristic spatial-frequency scale of radial interactions. Based on this analysis, we propose Multi-Cutoff Spectral Aggregation (MCSA), a plug-and-play module that aggregates radial kernels with different cutoff radii to enrich multi-scale geometric representations. To achieve efficient implementation, we exploit the compact support of radial kernels to fuse cutoff-dependent radial weights before angular tensor-product operations, avoiding redundant angular computations while preserving rotational equivariance. Extensive experiments across representative EGNN backbones demonstrate consistent improvements in energy, force, and stress prediction, as well as enhanced accuracy in higher-order properties, including phonon dispersion and lattice thermal conductivity. Further evaluations on layered materials with distinct interaction scales demonstrate the effectiveness of physically motivated cutoff selection. Code is available at: https://github.com/JF-Tan/MCSA.

articles.title: ALETHEIA: A Multi-Frequency Eddy Current Pulsed Thermography Dataset for Neural Operator Learning in Nondestructive Testing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11252v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning neural solvers for spatiotemporal partial differential equations (PDEs) under real-world constraints remains a key challenge in scientific machine learning, especially for inverse tasks with sparse and noisy boundary observations. We present the Aletheia dataset, the first 3D benchmark for learning data-driven solvers in the context of nondestructive testing (NDT). The dataset simulates eddy-current-induced heating in conductive solids and models the resulting transient heat propagation governed by the heat equation. Aletheia contains over 4,700 high-resolution samples across 10 excitation frequencies (1-100,kHz), each providing volumetric heat source and temperature fields over time. It supports both forward prediction of temperature evolution and inverse reconstruction of internal heat sources or defects from surface infrared measurements. Real infrared thermography data from cracked rail specimens are included for calibration and comparison. We define four canonical tasks on both regular and irregular grids and benchmark them using various neural operators. Aletheia establishes a unified platform for evaluating neural PDE solvers under realistic NDT conditions, enabling progress in reliable, data-driven inverse modeling. The dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/sherlock-0327/ALETHEIA.

articles.title: Building heterogeneous multistep workflows in automated microscopy: reward design and knowledge transfer for autonomous structure property discovery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous microscopy can turn fast acquisition into scientific progress when it decides not only where to measure, but also what information to acquire, at what scan rate, and when to recalibrate the instrument. We develop a budget constrained framework for such multistep structure-property workflows. It combines explicit scientific rewards, action costs, instrument observation models, transfer of pre experiment knowledge into the online campaign, and evaluation kept independent of the controller. The transferred knowledge includes predictor accuracy and computational cost, empirical learner maturity functions that weight model-derived rewards, and drift characteristics established before controller training. Using a real electron energy-loss spectroscopy dataset, we run two complementary campaigns. In the first, the controller chooses between imaging and spectroscopy, image size, and scan speed. In the second, the instrument drifts and the controller also decides when to recalibrate. The campaigns show that response discovery and structure-property learning favor different surrogate models and acquisition strategies. They also show that simple acquisition rules form strong, practical baselines. Independent error analysis reveals where model uncertainty is and is not a reliable learning signal. In the drift campaign, explicit registration greatly improves positional accuracy, and the framework measures what this costs in spectroscopy throughput. Together, these results provide a reproducible way to design, compare, and audit autonomous experiments, and they define what microscopes must provide for deployment: independently executable actions, characterized scan and detector responses, timestamped registration telemetry, and complete action records.

articles.title: Deep backward multistep high-order regression methods for high dimensional nonlinear parabolic partial differential equations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a deep backward multistep high-order regression (MHDBR) method for semilinear parabolic partial differential equations through their backward stochastic differential equation representations. The method combines multistep time discretization with regression targets formed by conditional expectations. Under explicit regularity, starting-value, forward-approximation and network-moment assumptions, we prove an error bound separating time discretization, conditional Monte Carlo sampling and neural-network approximation. The analysis assumes exact population minimization; finite-training-sample generalization and optimization errors are not included. For generators independent of the gradient variable, suitably constrained GroupSort networks and sufficiently large conditional sample sizes give order J in the stated nodal L² error norm. The required network sizes depend on dimension, so this result does not establish dimension-independent complexity. We present a reproducible time-discretization test satisfying the analytical assumptions and three broader neural-network benchmarks, whose relation to the assumptions is discussed explicitly.

articles.title: Amortized Bayesian Experimental Design with In-Context Knowledge Conditioning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Amortized Bayesian experimental design (BED) enables real-time design strategies by shifting acquisition cost offline, but existing methods remain tied to the prior and task distribution they were trained on and cannot exploit additional information available at deployment. We introduce in-context amortized BED with unified knowledge encoding (IMBUE), a BED framework that admits external knowledge at deployment through a unified in-context interface. IMBUE accepts two forms of such knowledge without retraining, namely user-specified prior knowledge and observations from previous instances of the experiment. Both are encoded as additional input tokens and processed in-context with the accumulated observations by a shared Transformer, and a learned reliability filter scores each external token against the observations and excludes inconsistent ones. Across four benchmarks, IMBUE accelerates early-stage information acquisition when the external knowledge is reliable, and remains close to the no-external baseline when it is not.

articles.title: Breaking the sqrtd Communication Barrier in Federated Sampling with Adaptive Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work proposes the Adaptive Federated Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (AFHMC) for Bayesian federated learning (FL) tasks. The prior work on HMC applications for FL achieves O(sqrtd/ϵ) communication cost under log-convex distributions, already demonstrating its advantage over the Langevin dynamic-based counterpart. Based on a refined analysis, this paper further reveals the benefit of HMC for the FL regime by incorporating a control mechanism for local node shifts. We prove that AFHMC at most requires O(d/ϵ²¹/³) communication cost up to a logarithmic term, which is significantly better than the existing results. Moreover, the proposed method adapts to client heterogeneity. Under low-heterogeneity settings (i.e., the target sampling precision ϵ² is higher than the heterogeneity level), the communication rate of AFHMC can be as good as O(log(d/ϵ²)), resembling the communication costs for FL optimization tools. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first logarithmic communication complexity result for federated sampling, even though it requires low heterogeneity. Numerically, we also justify AFHMC's advantage under the low-heterogeneity regime. Our code is available at https://github.com/laaaarrywang/Adaptive-Federated-HMC

articles.title: Deep-Learning-Assisted Bayesian Inference for Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11922v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) pose a major challenge to Bayesian parameter inference because of their complex, highly multimodal likelihood surfaces. Locating narrow high-likelihood regions is particularly difficult without knowledge of the true source parameters, which is unavailable in real observations. We develop a deep-learning-assisted Bayesian inference framework that combines neural-network-guided parameter-space localization, particle swarm optimization, and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling. Applied to simulated six-month EMRI signals, the framework recovers posterior distributions in close agreement with reference MCMC analyses initialized near the true parameter values, without requiring such knowledge for initialization. Once the neural network has been trained, the complete inference pipeline takes approximately 10 hours per signal.

articles.title: Two-Phase Rapid Simulation-Based Inference with Differentiable Simulators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12422v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Rapid Simulation Based Inference (RSBI), a diffusion-based variational approach to likelihood-free Bayesian inference that achieves high sampling efficiency under large prior-to-posterior volumes. RSBI builds on advances in Schrödinger Bridge (SB) diffusion sampling to handle multi-modal posteriors, with an initial likelihood supplied by a distance measure via a differentiable simulator. The key innovation of this initial surrogate likelihood is that it gives a highly efficient proposal distribution, replacing sequential rounds of other methods with an efficient one-shot proposal. Subsequent refinement then transports the proposal to the true posterior as specified by the simulator and the original prior. The SB sampler is warm-started from the proposal, and its energy is corrected by a neural likelihood ratio that is learned only where the proposal places mass. As a variational method, RSBI does not suffer from prior leakage commonly observed in standard sequential posterior estimation methods. To improve mode coverage we optionally utilize the well-tempered meta-dynamics framework, which also encourages exploration of the prior volume. We observe strong performance on standard SBI benchmarks, particularly when the prior volume is increased relative to the ground truth posterior, achieving a performance degradation of only sim5% on Two Moons under a highly constrained simulation budget. Additionally, we evaluate RSBI's performance for gravitational wave ring-down posterior estimation, in a real-world physics benchmark inspired by black hole spectroscopy.

articles.title: Out-of-the-Box Tabular Foundation Models for Bayesian Optimization in Materials Discovery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bayesian optimization is widely used in active learning loops for materials science. Gaussian processes serve as the de-facto surrogate model family, but require task-dependent kernel choices and can lack the modeling capacity for complex relationships. Tabular foundation models (TFMs) have recently emerged as the state-of-the-art for predictive tasks on structured data, without requiring bespoke kernels or hyperparameter tuning. We evaluate two TFMs, TabPFN and TabICL, as out-of-the-box surrogate models on two standard materials science benchmarks, comparing against a large field of baselines encompassing Gaussian processes, random forests, and CatBoost. Our findings indicate that TFMs are highly competitive surrogate models across the two benchmarks, without task-specific training for active learning or GP kernel selection. Our results motivate developing TFMs further as surrogates for active learning in materials discovery.

articles.title: Computationally sufficient statistics for Ising models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.12449v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Learning Gibbs distributions using only sufficient statistics has long been recognized as a computationally hard problem. On the other hand, computationally efficient algorithms for learning Gibbs distributions rely on access to full sample configurations generated from the model. For many systems of interest that arise in physical contexts, expecting a full sample to be observed is not practical, and hence it is important to look for computationally efficient methods that solve the learning problem with access to only a limited set of statistics. We examine the trade-offs between the power of computation and observation within this scenario, employing the Ising model as a paradigmatic example. We show that the couplings of the model can be learned to a desired accuracy from statistics whose order grows linearly with the ell₁ width of the model and only logarithmically with the inverse of the accuracy. In particular, for a fixed accuracy, the required order is proportional to the width. This allows us to infer the model's structure, using statistics whose order grows logarithmically with the inverse of the weakest coupling, and also to learn its magnetic fields. When the width and the accuracy are fixed, the running time is polynomial in the number of variables. We also discuss a setting where prior information about structure of the model is available and show that the learning problem can be solved efficiently with even more limited observational power.

articles.title: A Topological Encoder Decoder Framework for Temporal Graph Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most temporal graph learning methods reduce future prediction to discriminative inference over past interactions, focusing on edges or node labels for a largely persistent set of nodes. This view breaks down when new nodes and edges appear, since the future graph becomes a new object with changing size, composition, and structure. We address this gap by framing temporal graph prediction as an inverse topology problem. Instead of predicting edges directly, we first predict a multiscale topological descriptor of the future graph and then reconstruct a plausible future snapshot that realizes this descriptor under inductive constraints. This approach makes global structure and node churn explicit prediction targets and produces forecasted graphs that downstream tasks can evaluate without retraining. Across 14 temporal graph datasets, we evaluate our method, TOPOGED, on node, link, and graph property prediction and compare it against state-of-the-art temporal graph models. TOPOGED significantly improves node-level forecasting accuracy over the strongest baseline, with a macro average of 0.49 versus 0.05. It also outperforms baselines in 60% of graph-structure metric evaluations and substantially increases macro-average edge prediction metrics, from near-zero to 0.12. Our results show that topology-guided graph forecasting can predict inductive future snapshots whose structure supports multiple downstream evaluations.

articles.title: Agentic discrete-event simulation for manufacturing system design: an open 3D simulator, a benchmark and an industrial case
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The design of manufacturing systems relies on discrete-event simulation (DES) models that experts still build in tool-specific interfaces. AI agents can now write simulation code, but every model they write from scratch is new, unverified software. We present SimuLean, an open-source 3D DES simulator on the Unity engine designed to be programmed by AI agents: its modelling semantics are verified once, in the platform, and the agent builds and studies one model through domain-level commands, in the 3D scene or headless; physically simulated durations are calibrated for fast headless studies. We evaluated it on 18 manufacturing modelling tasks, from single machines to published production lines. A frontier agent built valid models in 93 of 108 attempts (86%), in about two minutes each; on the benchmark's interface version, two frontier agents built 105 of 108 models through domain commands alone, so that each comes with a record of how it was built. Every residual failure was silent - a model that builds and runs but answers wrongly - and only comparison with reference models revealed them all. In an industrial case, one agent working alone rebuilt, verified and studied a robotised welding workshop from a published study, in SimuLean and in SimPy. Comparing them with the published, expert-built model exposed an error in it; against the corrected model, the agent-built models agree within 1%. One agent can already build complete, realistic and traceable models for the design of manufacturing systems; independent reference models are what make them trustworthy.

articles.title: A Gamified Framework for Conflict-Driven Design: Discovering Strategies for Collaborative Resilience with Multi-Agent Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conflicting stakeholder objectives make it difficult to coordinate investments in urban resilience. We model conflict-driven urban design as a non-zero-sum digital board game in which stakeholder agents allocate scarce resources and balance individual payoffs against shared urban development and resilience objectives. We use multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to train policies and examine their behavior across three settings. On a 4 x 4 board, learned policies reach about 84% of the total return found by a simulated annealing benchmark. On an 8 x 8 board with spatial and resource constraints, trained agents favor projects that improve resilience in self-play. In a 12 x 12 simulation initialized from historical maps of Tatsumi, Tokyo, trained agents achieve a mean total score of 452.1, compared with 357.3 for a random-policy baseline across 10,000 simulation runs. Gains in adaptability, sustainability, flood resistance, and greenery come with reductions in vitality and density. A human-in-the-loop interface supports replay and lets participants take over stakeholder decisions, providing a testbed for exploring these trade-offs in participatory urban planning.

articles.title: GOPR-CAD: Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning for CAD Generation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating accurate CAD models requires substantial engineering expertise and careful control of geometry, topology, and mechanical constraints. Text-to-CAD aims to simplify this process, but current LLM-based methods often generate CAD programs directly. Language models remain unreliable when producing long code while coordinating coupled geometric, topological, and dimensional constraints. Consequently, executable programs may still produce structurally incorrect models, which execution rate and rendered appearance may fail to reveal. To address these limitations, we propose GOPR-CAD, an agentic Text-to-CAD pipeline based on Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning. A language model acts as a decision agent over encapsulated CAD operations and progressively constructs an executable operation graph, which a deterministic compiler converts into the final CAD model. This separation requires no additional training and supports different language models. To evaluate structural fidelity, we construct MHCAD, a benchmark of 300 standard mechanical part requirements derived from Machinery's Handbook. Their explicit structures enable reference-free STEP/B-rep evaluation. GOPR-CAD achieves 82.7% Structural Yield on MHCAD, and 87.2% Structural Yield on an external CADPrompt subset.

articles.title: State Media at Retrieval Time: A Large-Scale Audit of Russian State-Aligned Sources in AI Chatbot Responses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Pravda Network is a Russian state-aligned media aggregator, with over 110 websites and more than 15 million articles published since 2023. Given its prolific and repetitive output, emerging scholarship argues that the Pravda Network was built to influence AI systems. We conduct a large-scale audit of leading AI chatbots to understand: (1) the retrieval rates of Pravda Network articles, (2) the conditions of retrieval, and (3) whether chatbot responses affirm or caveat this content. We build a 10,000 prompt corpus from sampled Pravda Network headlines varied along two dimensions (headline rewording and user skepticism) and query 11 AI chatbots via the web interface (n=104,997 completed responses). Overall, we find susceptibility to Pravda Network retrieval to be infrequent---appearing in 7.3% of responses---and highly platform dependent---with three chatbots responsible for 94% of retrievals (You.com, Claude, and Copilot). Among the frontier models, Claude is an outlier: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Meta AI retrieved no Pravda Network articles, likely indicative of a domain-level filtering policy. All 11 chatbots, however, retrieved other Russian state-aligned media to some degree (median=13.56% of responses). When Pravda Network articles are surfaced, caveat rates vary widely by platform (from 5.3% to 76.2%), with You.com providing the fewest caveats. We also identify the tactic of headline washing: where 9.92% of sampled Pravda Network headlines attribute their reporting to other, often more credible, media outlets, while the articles themselves are republished from Russian state-aligned media. We discuss headline washing's potential to launder state media as independent reporting. With this audit, we provide a systematic analysis of AI chatbots' susceptibility to Russia's latest attempt to manipulate the information environment.

articles.title: ACROSSVAM3.0: Resource-Bounded 4D Scene Construction and Adaptive Surface Association
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Combining video generation, dynamic reconstruction and monocular SLAM requires consistent coordinates, explicit handling of missing outputs and predictable memory use. We present AcrossVAM3.0, an offline system that converts text, images or monocular RGB video into a versioned point representation. Frozen components run sequentially on one GPU; map corrections update cameras, points and trajectories together. The coordination layer adds no neural parameters. Three fresh input-mode runs completed with a maximum sampled task-process-tree GPU footprint of 17.14 GB. In a frozen 16-scene video suite, every scene yielded a 4D reconstruction and 15 yielded a non-empty SLAM map. Strict cross-window matching reduced local surface error but lost long-range track coverage on TAP-Vid-DAVIS. We therefore developed multi-hypothesis adaptive surface chaining (MHAC), which retains several candidate matches and an explicit missing state. After selection on disjoint development data, MHAC improved Average Jaccard over a position-only baseline by 0.1394 on a frozen ten-video holdout (95% bootstrap interval [0.1074,0.1689]). Across 265 RoboTAP videos, the mean paired gain was 0.0610 ([0.0510,0.0715]), with 215 wins, one tie and 49 losses. These results support resource-bounded scene construction and an external tracking gain under the tested protocol. They do not establish metric scale, semantic identity or high-fidelity novel-view rendering.

articles.title: Enhancing Multi-Step Chemical Mechanism Prediction with Graph-Guided Preference Data
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting multi-step chemical reaction mechanisms requires identifying plausible intermediates and correctly ordering the elementary reaction steps. Existing computational methods focus on single-step elementary reaction prediction, limiting their ability to generalize to unseen reaction spaces. We introduce a graph-guided framework for multi-step chemical mechanism prediction that leverages a chemical mechanism knowledge graph (ChemMechKG) to guide large language models (LLMs). To improve pathway prediction, we develop a graph-aligned reaction mechanism predictor (GRMP) that uses graph neural networks to generate synthetic candidate pathways for pathway optimization. During inference, we design a relation retrieval (RR) module to extract relevant graph evidence from the KG for pathway refinement. Experiments show that GRMP achieves the highest pathway accuracy among all compared methods on ChemMechQA and oMe-Gold, reaching 48.1% and 57.9%, respectively. On a fixed sample of 110 out-of-distribution reactions from ChemMechQA-Hard, GRMP achieves 36.4% top-1 pathway accuracy. LLM-as-Judge and human assessment further demonstrate its ability to generalize to unseen reactions.

articles.title: Fairness Explanations Improve Fairness In Human-AI Decision Making: an empirical evaluation of parole decision-making
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09924v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Both humans and AI exhibit systemic biases, yet little is known about how interface design can foster fairness in hybrid human-AI decision-making. This paper introduces a method for extracting fair data samples from biased datasets and adapts a fairness-explanation technique to highlight potential AI bias during decisions. We conducted a within-subjects study (n=48) where non-experts made decisions across three conditions: independent human judgment, unexplained AI assistance, and AI assistance augmented with visual ethnic-bias explanations (Fair-XAI). To isolate effects, the AI conditions provided systematically balanced recommendations. Results show that fairness explanations significantly reduced both sex and ethnic bias compared to human-only decisions. Fair-XAI also marginally improved fairness over balanced AI recommendations while enhancing task performance. These findings demonstrate that fairness-centered explanation interfaces can meaningfully shape user behavior, providing concrete design insights for developing equitable and accountable human-AI systems.

articles.title: Federated Lightweight Transformer for Network-Layer Cyberattack Detection in O-RAN
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09992v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) improves radio access network flexibility through disaggregation, open interfaces, and programmable RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs). However, the same openness and distribution increase the attack surface and make centralized intrusion detection difficult to scale across heterogeneous RAN sites. This paper presents a federated lightweight Transformer framework for privacy-preserving network-layer cyberattack detection in O-RAN. Each participating site trains a compact Transformer locally on temporally ordered network-flow records, while only model parameters are shared with a federated coordinator. To model realistic site heterogeneity, the client datasets are partitioned according to a Dirichlet distribution, resulting in non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) local data. The local detector uses feature projection, positional encoding, multi-head self-attention, feed-forward layers, and temporal pooling to classify five network-layer attack categories: ICMP, Slowloris, SYN, TCP-ACK, and UDP. Experiments on the NetsLab 5G O-RAN intrusion-detection dataset show an overall accuracy of 94.89 % and a macro-F1 score of 81.09 %.

articles.title: Transfer learning-enhanced physics-informed neural networks for efficient simulation of river flood in complex large-scale river systems
articles.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have shown considerable potential for solving hydraulic problems by integrating governing physical laws into neural network optimization. However, their application to real-world river flood remains challenging because of the high computational cost associated with nonlinear and non-convex PINN optimization. Conventional PINNs are generally initialized without task-specific hydraulic knowledge, each new hydraulic scenario requires optimization from an uninformed initial state, resulting in repeated training and substantial computational expense. This study proposes a transfer learning method that can significantly improve the prediction accuracy and training efficiency of PINNs for complex river floods under varying flood events. A transfer learning-enhanced PINN (TL-PINN) framework is developed, in which a data-driven neural network is first trained on a source flood event. The optimized parameters are then transferred to initialize the PINN for target flood events, followed by optimization using a composite physics-informed loss function. The proposed framework is evaluated on a real-world river reach with complex channel geometry and highly unsteady flood processes through three numerical experiments. TL-PINN is compared with three conventionally initialized PINNs using PyTorch Default Initialization, Orthogonal Initialization and Xavier Normal Initialization. TL-PINN consistently maintains superior performance under limited labeled-data conditions and under more severe and complex flood inflows. The results indicate that the transferred parameters provide an effective initialization, leading to improved prediction accuracy and optimization efficiency. These findings demonstrate that transfer learning might significantly enhance the real-world applicability of PINNs for efficient and accurate river flood simulations under varying flood events.

articles.title: A Novel Onboard Syngas-Assisted Cold-Start Strategy for Methanol-Fueled Spark Ignition Engines
articles.abstract: Alternative fuels are emerging as promising energy sources for the power and transportation sectors due to their potential for high performance and lower emissions. The growing demand for clean energy and the need to reduce dependence on fossil fuels in the automotive sector have increased the utilization of alternative fuels. However, cold-start challenges associated with alternative fuels, especially methanol, remain a serious limitation. The onboard production of syngas, consisting mainly of hydrogen and carbon monoxide, can help overcome these cold-start issues. Methanol-derived syngas can be utilized in onboard automotive applications to address cold-start problems at ambient temperatures below 15°C. Due to its high energy content, low ignition energy requirement, and cleaner combustion characteristics, hydrogen plays an important role in overcoming cold-start challenges, even at extremely low ambient temperatures down to − 50°C. Carbon monoxide also possesses favorable combustion properties, which assist in achieving stable and efficient combustion of the fuel-air mixture. The introduction of syngas (H₂/CO ratio of 67/33 by mole fraction) during the initial few minutes of engine operation, particularly for the first 3–4 minutes, can help achieve the required in-cylinder pressure of more than 6 MPa and an in-cylinder temperature of approximately 2400 K. These conditions promote proper combustion and enable the engine to reach stable operating temperatures within a short time. Subsequently, methanol fuel can be introduced together with syngas for a few additional minutes, after which the engine can transition to fully methanol-fueled operation.

articles.title: The Promptification of the Search Bar: Evidence of a Behavioral Spillover from Generative AI
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have produced documented behavioral changes across information tasks, raising the question of whether they have also changed how users formulate requests to the legacy search bar. This study documents a durable structural shift in the syntactic register of web search queries following LLM diffusion, a shift termed “the promptification of the search bar” and characterized through panel co-movement and temporal precedence at population scale. Using 196,500 weekly US search-frequency observations from Google Trends across 25 semantic categories and 30 intent markers (2021 to 2025), this study classifies intent query markers into three classes of increasing conversational delegation and estimates their differential response to LLM diffusion. Conversational delegation rose by 58.7% after a structural break in June 2023, moving from no relation with LLM diffusion to tight co-movement, with temporal precedence running from diffusion to query syntax and not the reverse. An epoch decomposition shows the shift was established roughly eleven months before the platform deployed its own generative layer within the legacy tool, and the elasticity to LLM diffusion declined rather than increased after deployment, the opposite of what a platform-driven account predicts. The shift is strongest in domains serving cognitively complex needs, deepens over time as longer, more elaborate conversational forms standardize, and replicates worldwide. These findings are consistent with a spillover from LLM use into the legacy search bar: freed by exposure to conversational machines, users are returning to the natural register that keyword era had compressed, and the legacy interface is adapting to a behavior it did not create.

articles.title: Sustainable Production of Magnetic Activated Carbon from Agricultural Waste for the Adsorption of Cationic and Anionic Dye in Single, Binary and Ternary System
articles.abstract: The simultaneous removal of dyes from industrial wastewater remains a significant challenge, particularly because the mechanisms governing dye co-adsorption are not yet fully understood. In this study, magnetic activated carbon (MAC) was prepared through a simplified chemical modification process and employed as an adsorbent for the removal of malachite green (MG) in single- and multicomponent dye systems. The adsorption behaviour of MG in the presence of other dyes was investigated to evaluate the interactions and competitive effects during co-adsorption. The experimental results showed that the adsorption capacities in multicomponent systems were generally comparable to those observed in single-solute systems. The adsorption kinetics was best described by the pseudo-second-order model in both single and multicomponent systems, with coefficients of determination (R2) approaching unity. Furthermore, the extended Langmuir model, freundlich and Dubinin Rdushkevich adequately described the equilibrium data for the co-adsorption process. The maximum adsorption capacities for MG, MG + BBE 133, MG + NR, and MG + NR + BBE 133 were 16.86, 23.31, 14.41, and 10.36 mg/g, respectively. The observed variations in adsorption capacity indicated the presence of both synergistic and antagonistic effects, depending on the dye combination, with antagonistic behaviour evident in the binary system containing MG and NR. The co-adsorption process was potentially governed by hydrogen bonding, π–π stacking interactions, and electrostatic interactions between the dyes and the MAC surface. Overall, the findings highlight the potential of MAC as an effective adsorbent for dye removal from aqueous solutions and provide insights into the interactions influencing dye adsorption in multicomponent systems.

articles.title: ZnO-functionalized sugarcane bagasse biochar for enhanced photocatalytic removal of paracetamol: structural, optical, and interfacial charge-transport properties
articles.abstract: Functionalized semiconductor/carbon nanocomposites offer promising opportunities for photocatalytic environmental remediation by combining pollutant adsorption with enhanced charge separation and transport. In this work, we synthesized a ZnO-functionalized biochar composite (ZnO@BC) by thermally converting zinc hydroxychloride anchored onto a sugarcane bagasse-derived carbonaceous framework. X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive spectroscopy confirmed the formation of crystalline hexagonal wurtzite ZnO nanostructures, with an average crystallite size of approximately 28.9 nm, distributed throughout the porous biochar matrix. Nitrogen adsorption–desorption analysis revealed a predominantly microporous structure with a specific surface area of 74.15 m² g⁻¹. The optical band gap decreased slightly from 3.22 eV for commercial ZnO to 3.18 eV for ZnO@BC, while the Urbach energy decreased from 110.3 ± 1.6 to 49.3 ± 0.8 meV, indicating reduced optical disorder in the composite. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy revealed an 11.7% increase in low-frequency conductance under illumination, consistent with enhanced photoinduced charge transport through the ZnO/biochar interface. The ZnO@BC composite achieved 78.5% paracetamol removal after 60 min of irradiation, with an apparent pseudo-first-order rate constant of 0.0207 min⁻¹, compared with 43% removal and 0.0079 min⁻¹ for commercial ZnO. Radical-scavenging experiments indicated relevant contributions from hydroxyl and superoxide radicals, with a secondary contribution from photogenerated holes. The results demonstrate that integrating ZnO with sugarcane bagasse biochar provides a functional hybrid interface with enhanced photocatalytic performance and promising potential for pharmaceutical-contaminant removal.

articles.title: SBOA-GI: A Physics-Informed Enhancement of the Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm for Gravity Inversion, with an Honest Assessment of Its Limits on Field Data from the Charak Salt-Dome Province, Zagros, Iran
articles.abstract: Metaheuristic optimization is now common for interpreting potential-field geophysical data, yet most published variants are validated only on noise-free synthetic models. This study introduces SBOA-GI, a creatively redesigned, physics-informed variant of the recently proposed Secretary Bird Optimization Algorithm (SBOA; Fu et al. 2024): rather than applying SBOA unmodified, we reconceive four of its five update rules around the ill-posedness, unequal parameter sensitivity, and depth–amplitude trade-off of gravity inversion — to our knowledge the first SBOA variant conceived for a potential-field inverse problem rather than generic benchmarks. The redesign combines Latin-hypercube/opposition-based initialization, self-adaptive differential mutation, sensitivity-weighted Lévy flight, a Lévy–Cauchy stagnation-escape mechanism, physically bounded exploitation with an embedded local Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) polish, and a shrinking-bound restart loop. SBOA-GI, standard SBOA, particle swarm optimization (PSO), and LM were compared on synthetic fault, sphere, and horizontal-cylinder models (0/5/10% Gaussian noise, 30 runs each) and on real Bouguer gravity data (875 stations) from two salt-dome anomalies near Charak, Zagros fold-thrust belt, Iran. At zero noise, SBOA-GI cut parameter RMSE roughly eleven orders of magnitude versus standard SBOA; the gain shrank to negligible at 5% noise and reversed at 10%, showing its refinements mainly speed convergence rather than raise the noise-limited accuracy ceiling. On real data, contrary to expectation, classical LM gave the lowest and most stable misfit (≈ 2.16 and ≈ 1.25 mGal RMS) at a fraction of the metaheuristics' cost, reflecting a smooth misfit surface and the well-known depth–amplitude trade-off. We report this transparently as evidence for the practical limits of metaheuristic enhancement in gravity inversion.

articles.title: Geophysical evidence of structural and topographic controls on the Tulancingo Valley aquifer system, Central Mexico
articles.abstract: The Tulancingo Valley aquifer, located in southeastern Hidalgo state, central-eastern Mexico, is one of the most overexploited groundwater resources. To characterize its hydrogeological framework and the mechanisms driving deviations in the static water level, an integration of gravimetric data, transient electromagnetic (TEM) soundings and electrical resistivity tomography (ERT) was implemented. Residual gravity data delineate prominent NW-SE and NE-SW structural lineaments associated with the Acoculco caldera and regional normal faulting, while resistivity models identify two hydraulically connected systems separated by a faulted volcanic aquitard: a shallow aquifer (up to 20 m depth; ~2–15 Ω·m) and a heavily exploited deep regional aquifer (reaching depths of 130–250 m; ~2–20 Ω·m). The regional structural features exert a primary control on the hydrodynamics of the deep aquifer. These fault and fracture networks lead to hydraulic connectivity and partitioned groundwater flow, directly influencing the spatial distribution of static water level variations. Projections indicate that under this structurally controlled flow regime, current extraction trends will drive water deficits to 23.64 Mm³ and 31.64 Mm³ by 2030 and 2050, respectively. These findings provide a geophysical base for sustainable groundwater management in structurally complex aquifer systems.

articles.title: Graphene-oxide modified TiO2 composite thin films for improved catalytic H2 evolution in NaBH4 hydrolysis and dye removal under UV illumination
articles.abstract: This study reports the fabrication of graphene oxide (GO)-modified TiO2 thin films with enhanced catalytic performance for H2 evolution via NaBH4 hydrolysis and photocatalytic methylene blue (MB) dye removal under UV irradiation. Among the investigated GO concentrations, the sample containing 100 µg of GO per 1 mL of TiO2 slurry paste (TiO2-100) exhibited the best performance in both processes. Specifically, MB removal increased by approximately 14%, while the hydrogen evolution rate improved by approximately 27.3%. The enhanced MB removal can be associated with enhanced electron transfer and suppressed charge recombination in TiO2-100, while the enhanced H2 evolution may be associated with changes in surface chemistry and improved interfacial interactions between the catalyst and aqueous reactants. The obtained results demonstrate the good potential of GO-modified TiO2 thin films as low-cost catalysts for environmental remediation and hydrogen generation applications.

articles.title: Simulation-Driven Machine Learning for Ring Rolling: A Proof of Concept on Transfer and Hybrid Learning Approaches
articles.abstract: Finite element analysis (FEA) is widely used in forming technologies to enhance process modeling and generate process-level insight. However, discrepancies between numerical simulations and experimental or industrial reality remain, depending on both the specific process and the simulation setup. When machine learning (ML) models are trained exclusively on FEA-generated data, these discrepancies are implicitly embedded in the training dataset and may limit the model’s predictive reliability on real process data. Motivated by the complementary strengths and limitations of heterogeneous data sources, this study investigates hybrid approaches that aim to maximize data utilization when experimental data is scarce and improve model performance rather than relying on a single data source. Accordingly, the paper examines the integration of FEA data, the most commonly used simulation data type, into machine-learning-based modeling of experimental ring rolling processes. In this regard, two major concepts are considered: hybrid training and transfer learning. This proof of concept discusses the methods on two different use cases: A general introduction and elaboration of an unsupervised representation learning task in the radial-axial ring rolling (RARR) process, as well as the supervised prediction of the out-of-roundness error in the tangential cold ring rolling (TCRR). Metrics are evaluated across tasks and methods, mechanisms analyzed, and applications presented. Ultimately, this study establishes a simulation-informed machine learning framework for ring rolling, showing that transfer learning and targeted data pre-processing can effectively bridge FEA-based knowledge and real process data to improve predictive modeling performance.

articles.title: Crustal heat supply beneath Zibo constrained by borehole observations and alternative thermal property models
articles.abstract: The partitioning of crustal radiogenic heating and basal heat input beneath Zibo remains uncertain. We assess how crustal structure and thermal properties affect deep temperatures and heat partitioning, using the published Linyi model as a regional reference. Temperature profiles from borehole ZB-ZK1, thermal-property data for 92 regional rock samples and a geoscience transect were combined in two one-dimensional conductive models based on P-wave velocity and lithological analogues. The models share upper boundary conditions, including the adopted terrestrial heat flow of 64.6 mW m⁻², and incorporate temperature-dependent conductivity. Effective upper-crustal conductivity was calibrated by assigning 585°C to the published magnetic-source bottom at 24.74 km. The 100–200 m borehole interval yields a geothermal gradient of 17.03°C km⁻¹. V and L1 yield Moho temperatures of 693.7 and 678.3°C at 31.06 km, crustal radiogenic contributions of 21.26 and 28.65 mW m⁻² and residual Moho heat flows of 43.34 and 35.95 mW m⁻², respectively. These Moho heat flows bracket the published Linyi value of 38.88 mW m⁻², reversing the inferred Zibo–Linyi ranking between scenarios. Matching the common deep temperature therefore constrains geotherms without uniquely determining the crustal and basal heat contributions, which depend on prescribed layering and radiogenic heat production. These results provide a conductive baseline for geothermal assessment at Zibo and identify formation-specific thermal properties and deep equilibrium temperatures as priorities for regional heat-supply comparisons.

articles.title: Larvicidal activity and molecular interactions of furoquinoline alkaloids from Araliopsis soyauxii with wild-type and G119S mutant acetylcholinesterase of the malaria vector Anopheles gambiae
articles.abstract: The use of synthetic insecticides has led to target-site mutations such as G119S in acetylcholinesterase which is a major threat in Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes’ control. To obtain alternative sources of novel bio-friendly insecticides, our study investigated the larvicidal activity and molecular interactions of four alkaloids isolated from Araliopsis soyauxii (Rutaceae) Nkolbisine, Tecleaverdoornine, Kokusaginine, and Flindersiamine against insecticide-susceptible and resistant An. gambiae populations. The alkaloids of the A. soyauxii were obtained from stem barks using column chromatography and characterized by NMR spectroscopy. Using WHO larvicidal bioassays protocol, the susceptible Kisumu strain and field collected strains of An. gambiae populations characterized as carrying G119S Ace-1 mutation were exposed to the purified alkaloids. Molecular interactions analysis was conducted via Molecular docking and MM-GBSA analysis. Nkolbisine was the most potent, with LC50 values ranging from 51.63 mg/L to 60.12 mg/L across various strains at 24 h. Tecleaverdoornine was also very active and Kokusaginine and Flindersiamine followed. Our docking results revealed that Nkolbisine and Tecleaverdoornine had a positive binding affinity to wild-type as well as mutant AChE, with docking of scores − 8.94 and − 7.75 kcal/mol (wild-type) and − 9.25 and − 7.90 kcal/mol (mutant), respectively. Interactions such as hydrogen bonding with catalytic residues (GLU448, SER283) and π-π stacking were conserved in aromatic residues (TYR493, TRP441). MM-GBSA analysis, showed that Nkolbisine (-46.27 to -29.39 kcal/mol) interacts favorably with both enzymes. Hence, Nkolbisine and Tecleaverdoornine are eco-friendly potential larvicidal candidates that can be used against both susceptible and resistant populations of An. gambiae for larval control in endemic settings.

articles.title: Machine Learning-Assisted Prediction of Brilliant Green Removal from Water Using CaTiO 3 Photocatalysis: Bayesian Optimization, SHAP Explainability, and Robustness Assessment
articles.abstract: Brilliant Green (BG)-contaminated wastewater threatens aquatic ecosystems by limiting light penetration, disrupting photosynthesis, and exposing organisms to potentially toxic compounds, raising broader environmental and human-health concerns. This study presents an explainable machine-learning framework for predicting BG removal during CaTiO3-assisted photocatalytic water treatment. Using 63 published experimental observations for the 2:7 precursor composition, six regression models Decision Tree, Random Forest, Extra Trees, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, and CatBoost were evaluated through Bayesian hyperparameter optimization and repeated cross-validation. Although Extra Trees achieved marginally higher holdout accuracy, CatBoost was selected for its superior repeated-validation performance, achieving a test R2 of 0.9884, RMSE of 3.4629 percentage points, and mean cross-validation R2 of 0.9697. SHAP analysis identified degradation time (60.57%), initial BG concentration (32.12%), and catalyst dosage (7.31%) as the principal contributors to model predictions. Feature-combination analysis reinforced this hierarchy, while CatBoost retained a test R2 of 0.9778 under 10% Gaussian noise. Predicted BG removal (89.32%) closely matched the reported experimental value (88.46%). These findings provide a promising foundation for future experimental validation, broader catalyst screening, and interpretable optimization of photocatalytic wastewater treatment.

articles.title: Uncertainty Aware Prediction of Near Complete Brilliant Green Photodegradation over CaTiO 3 Using Hybrid Machine Learning and Kinetic Modeling
articles.abstract: Brilliant Green (BG) is a persistent cationic dye that can harm aquatic environments by reducing light penetration, disrupting photosynthesis, altering microbial activity, and causing toxicity. Because BG degradation depends on interacting operating conditions, accurate prediction and optimization remain challenging. In this study, we analysed 90 previously published CaTiO3 photocatalytic observations using an integrated machine-learning and kinetic framework. Twelve regression models Extra Trees, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, CatBoost, XGBoost, HistGradientBoosting, SVR, GPR, KNN, Elastic Net, Ridge, and PLSR were optimized using Bayesian search and evaluated through five-fold cross-validation and held-out testing. XGBoost achieved the strongest individual performance, with mean CV R2 of 0.9844 and test R2 of 0.9796. An XGBoost-GPR hybrid improved test R2 to 0.9809, with RMSE and MAE of 3.4058 and 2.4556, respectively. SHAP analysis identified degradation time as the most influential predictor. Since measured removal reached only 89.53%, direct models could not reliably predict near-complete degradation. Therefore, pseudo-first-order rate constants were modeled using SVR. The framework identified a 2:7 CaCO3/TiO2 ratio, 200 mg catalyst, and 10 ppm BG for 99.9% removal in 275.6 min. Bootstrap uncertainty analysis yielded a median time of 251.7 min.

articles.title: Multi-Element Analysis of Commercial Cigarette Tobacco in Türkiye by ICP-MS: Manufacturer-Related Differences and Multivariate Compositional Patterns
articles.abstract: Elemental concentrations were determined in 27 commercial cigarette tobacco samples from six manufacturers in Türkiye, with emphasis on manufacturer-related differences and multivariate compositional patterns. Thirteen elements (As, Ba, Cd, Co, Cr, Cu, Mn, Mo, Ni, Pb, Ti, V, and Zn) were quantified by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS). Given the non-normal distribution of most elemental data, group differences were assessed using the Kruskal–Wallis H test with Dunn–Bonferroni post-hoc comparisons; interelement associations were examined by Spearman correlation, and multivariate structure was explored through PCA and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA). Mn exhibited the highest mean concentration (135.67 mg/kg), followed by Ba (66.56 mg/kg), Zn (30.30 mg/kg), and Ti (26.55 mg/kg), whereas Cd (0.36 mg/kg) and Pb (0.37 mg/kg) occurred at lower concentrations. Significant manufacturer-related differences were identified for 10 elements (p < 0.05). Strong positive correlations were observed between Ti–V (ρ = 0.965), Cu–Ti (ρ = 0.883), and Cu–V (ρ = 0.864). The first two principal components explained 64.61% of the total variance, and HCA identified two major clusters comprising 19 and eight samples. Complete manufacturer-specific separation was not achieved, suggesting that within-manufacturer variability in raw material sourcing and blending may be comparable in scale to between-manufacturer differences. The results confirm that ICP-MS combined with multivariate statistics offers a practical framework for exploratory characterization of commercial tobacco elemental profiles.

articles.title: Fabrication of RGO@MnS/NC composite electrodes with stable and highrate capability for efficient sodium storage
articles.abstract: Abatract MnS has drawn growing interest as an anode material for high-performance sodium-ion batteries, owing to its attractive theoretical capacity and favorable redox reversibility during the conversion-type reaction. Nevertheless, substantial volume expansion and sluggish reaction kinetics of MnS upon cycling processes trigger particle pulverization and rapid capacity fading. RGO@MnS/NC composites are fabricated through oxidative polymerization combined with carbothermal reduction–sulfurization. During the synthesis, MnS/NC nanoparticles are in situ immobilized on conductive RGO nanosheets. When employed as an anode material for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), the rationally engineered RGO@MnS/NC composites exhibit a stable reversible capacity of 140 mAh g− 1 over 1200 long-term cycles under a high current density of 5 A g− 1. The outstanding cycling stability and rate capability of RGO@MnS/NC originate from its unique structural design. On one hand, MnS nanocrystals immobilized on RGO suppress particle agglomeration, expedite electron/ion transport, and facilitate adequate electrolyte penetration. On the other hand, the outer NC shell creates abundant active sites and further accelerates ion and electron transfer in the electrode. Benefiting from these advantages, RGO@MnS/NC composites hold great potential as a favorable anode material for advanced SIBs.

articles.title: Monitoring-network change reshapes long-term Water Quality Index inference: A dual-frame analysis from Ghana
articles.abstract: Purpose. Long-term water-quality records are widely used to judge whether rivers and other water bodies are improving or deteriorating, but interpretation becomes difficult when the monitoring network itself changes through time. Using Ghana’s national Water Quality Index (WQI) record, we investigate two sources of apparent long-term change: variation over time at consistently monitored locations and changes in the set of stations contributing to the national record. Methods. We analysed 41 surface-water stations across 20 reported years from 2005 to 2025 using a dual-frame design that compares the changing national network with a fixed panel of 19 long-running stations. The analysis combined robust station-level trends, multiplicity control, persistence screening, endpoint sensitivity, and leave-one-station-out analysis. Results. After 2010, the full-network median exceeded the fixed-panel median in 13 of 16 reported years, with a median difference of + 1.55 WQI units. The fixed panel itself also showed a broad low-score period from 2012 to 2018, with the strongest negative departure in 2013. Station-level trends were heterogeneous, none remained significant after multiplicity correction, and four stations met the primary persistent-poor criterion. Conclusions. Monitoring-network change and temporal variation within a fixed station panel can coexist. We therefore propose Dual-Frame Monitoring Inference (DFMI), which reports contemporary network conditions alongside a stable sentinel panel and station-specific evidence. DFMI offers environmental agencies a practical way to make long-term monitoring records more comparable, transparent, and useful for management as observation systems evolve.

articles.title: PBE-assisted machine learning of HSE06+SOC photovoltaic efficiency in halide perovskites
articles.abstract: Hybrid-functional calculations with spin–orbit coupling (HSE06 + SOC) provide more accurate electronic properties of halide perovskites than semilocal PBE calculations but are substantially more expensive. Here, we assess whether low-cost PBE information improves machine-learning (ML) prediction of HSE06 + SOC band gaps and spectroscopic limited maximum efficiency (SLME). Using a public dataset of 243 pure and mixed ABX₃ perovskites, we compare seven ML model families using nested cross-validation with random, chemical-system-grouped, and B-site-grouped splits. PBE inputs substantially improve SLME prediction: the mean absolute error decreases from 0.68 to 0.45 percentage points on chemical-system-grouped splits, with the best model achieving 0.36 percentage points. Δ-learning provides no advantage over direct learning. However, performance deteriorates when the B-site chemistry is absent from training, and conformal intervals become under-calibrated. An audit of the source labels further shows that the HSE06 + SOC SLME is strongly constrained by the HSE06 + SOC band gap and approaches a saturation near 16%, because the reported spectrum was generated by shifting the PBE absorption spectrum. These findings highlight both the value and limitations of PBE-assisted ML for multi-fidelity prediction of perovskite properties.

articles.title: IoT‑Based Legacy Home for Energy Optimization and Control in Real‑Time
articles.abstract: The electricity sector has seen substantial modifications, from generation to consumption, due to the development of intelligent technology. There is a global increase in the need for more energy. With the limitation of energy resources and the pollution due to carbon emissions related to electricity generation and usage, energy-efficient systems are a must. Demand-oriented home management systems are feasible solutions for efficient energy consumption. This research proposes the framework's algorithm Internet of Things concept to monitor, optimize, and adapt energy usage in real time for homes with non-smart devices. A control unit prototype has been implemented using a Raspberry Pi, Arduino, and current sensors. A website is created with a graphical user interface that allows the user to monitor and limit energy consumption demand. A database for storing information about any device connected to the prototype is being developed. The stored data is the permissible limit of electricity consumption, the consumption of each machine, and its operating time, in addition to calculating the monthly bill according to its tariff rate. When the prototype model is applied to the demand limit of electricity consumption in three scenarios (1.5, 2.5, and 3.5 kW/h), the experimental findings show electricity consumption reduction in real time by up to 41%, 25%, and 10%, respectively, in summer and 61.5%, 53%, and 42.5% in winter.

articles.title: A Reconfigurable Ferroelectric Acoustic Computational Primitive for Analog In-Memory Computing
articles.abstract: The growing computational demands of artificial intelligence (AI) have renewed interest in emerging nonvolatile memory (eNVM) crossbar array technologies for in-memory computing to reduce the energy cost of moving data between processors and memory. Here we report a computational primitive that merges ferroelectric memory and acoustic resonators in a single platform: Ferroelectric memory Embedded in Nanoscale Acoustic resonators (FENA). We experimentally demonstrate over 100 nonvolatile analog admittance states arising from partial ferroelectric polarization switching in lithium niobate resonators. The devices exhibit highly symmetric potentiation and depression characteristics, which directly impact computation accuracy, favorable dynamic range and linearity, and low projected read and write energies after scaling. We further propose a radio frequency (RF) peripheral readout architecture that extracts frequency- and phase-sensitive effective conductance states to offer an expanded state space and hardware-level reconfigurability. System-level evaluation using the NeuroSim multi-layer perceptron (MLP) simulator demonstrates the suitability of FENA for both online and offline neural-network training, with scaled devices achieving competitive 84% and 92% classification accuracies, respectively.

articles.title: Exact many-body wavefunction of the Kondo model with time-dependent interaction strength
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.05640v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum integrability has been applied to a large variety of low dimensional Hamiltonians in Quantum Field Theory, Condensed Matter Physics, and Statistical Mechanics to obtain exact expressions for the spectrum and thermodynamics of these systems. In most of these studies the coupling constants are constant in time. Here we present an exact solution of the nonstationary Schrödinger equation for the Kondo Hamiltonian with a time-dependent spin-exchange coupling J(t) of the form λ t + p(t) ± sqrt(λ t + p(t))² + 16/3, where p(t) is an arbitrary periodic function, under periodic boundary conditions. Unlike previously studied time-dependent integrable models, which are rooted in the classical Yang--Baxter structure and associated Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equations, our approach is based on the quantum Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov framework and the quantum Yang--Baxter algebra. Our results broaden the domain of time-dependent integrability to a genuinely quantum class of models and provide new tools for exploring coherent nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated systems.

articles.title: Real-time dynamics with bead-Fourier path integrals. II. Bead-Fourier RPMD
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.09961v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Feynman path integrals (PIs) have found many uses in approximate quantum dynamics methods for efficiently calculating real-time quantum correlation functions. The PIs typically take the form of discrete imaginary-time slices along a closed path, where the slices form the ``beads'' of a ring polymer (RP) necklace. Some methods, such as centroid molecular dynamics (CMD), use the RP to generate an effective potential for the dynamics, while others, like RP molecular dynamics (RPMD), directly utilize the RP in real-time dynamics in order to incorporate approximate quantum effects. The standard, discretized bead forms of CMD and RPMD may require a large number of RP beads to obtain accurate results for systems with strong quantum effects and at low temperatures. In Paper I (J. Chem. Phys. 2025, 163, 144123), we introduced the bead-Fourier (BF)-CMD method, where we utilized the inclusion of a Fourier sine series to reduce the number of beads needed to converge the CMD effective potential up to eightfold. In this work, we extend RPMD to incorporate BF-PIs in the form of BF-RPMD. We study several implementations of the BF-RPMD method through the calculation of correlation functions for both linear and nonlinear operators. We found that the effectiveness of this method is sensitive to both the type of system and the form of the operators being studied. Our results show that this method is able to produce results on par with standard RPMD, with at worst a twofold and up to an eightfold reduction in the number of beads by including two to three Fourier components.

articles.title: Detecting the Onset and Progression of Spinodal Decomposition using Transient Grating Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.06659v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spinodal decomposition can degrade corrosion resistance and embrittle materials. The ability to quickly, conclusively, and non-destructively detect the onset of spinodal decomposition before catastrophic materials degradation would represent a significant advance in materials testing. We demonstrate that spinodal decomposition can be detected in binary Fe-Cr alloys via modulus stiffening using in situ and ex situ transient grating spectroscopy (TGS). The key mechanistic insight is the non-linearity in elastic moduli as function of Cr content renders a spinodally decomposed Fe-Cr alloy stiffer than an equivalent solid solution for a certain range of initial chromium compositions. We confirm the presence of spinodal decomposition in the 36 at.% chromium alloy using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), linked to known spinodal decomposition energetics, and show via atomistic simulations that elastic modulus stiffening is expected after spinodal decomposition in the 36 at.% chromium alloy. The results of this study suggest the potential use of TGS as a practical tool for non-destructive evaluation of key materials susceptible to such degradation.

articles.title: Topology of the Fermi surface and universality of the metal-metal and metal-insulator transitions: d-dimensional Hatsugai-Kohmoto model as an example
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.13050v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The earlier theory citeChitov:2025 of the quantum phase transitions related to the change of the Fermi Surface Topology (FST) is advanced. For such transitions the Fermi surface as a quantum critical manifold determined by the Lee-Yang zeros, the order parameter P as the d-volume of the Fermi sea, and the special FST universality class were introduced in citeChitov:2025. The exactly solvable Hatsugai-Kohmoto (HK) d-dimensional (d=1,2,3) model of interacting fermions is analyzed. We explore the relation between the Lee-Yang zeros, the Luttinger and the plateau (Oshikawa) theorems. The validity of the Luttinger theorem in the HK model is confirmed. It is shown that the order parameter P and the FST universality class describe the transitions between metal and band/Mott insulators, as well as the Lifshitz and van Hove gapless-to-gapless transitions. The gapless phases are established to be the ferromagnetic Fermi liquids (metals), where the quantum critical manifold is also a locus of ferromagnetic order with spontaneous breaking of the rotational symmetry occurring at T=0. In addition to the conventional paradigm with a continuous order parameter, we apply the homology theory to analyze the FST transitions. They are critical points of the Morse function. To quantify FST we use the Euler characteristic, which is calculated for each phase of the HK model. We claim that the FST universality class is robust with respect to interactions and other model details, under the condition that the conduction band function is smooth and the critical points are non-degenerate.

articles.title: Anharmonicity Driven by Vacancy Ordering Unlocks High-performance Thermoelectric Conversion in Defective Chalcopyrites II-III₂-VI₄
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.16477v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Defective chalcopyrites have recently emerged as promising thermoelectric materials because their ordered intrinsic vacancies can profoundly reshape both lattice dynamics and electronic structure. Here, we present a comprehensive theoretical investigation of the lattice thermal and carrier transport properties of II-III₂-VI₄ defective chalcopyrites by combining first-principles calculations with machine-learning interatomic potentials. We show that vacancy ordering enhances lattice distortion, leading to strong anharmonicity and metavalent bonding. The interplay of soft low-frequency phonons, strongly negative Grüneisen parameters, and a substantially enlarged four-phonon scattering phase space results in four-phonon-scattering-dominated heat transport, yielding ultralow lattice thermal conductivity. Meanwhile, systematic anion substitution at the VI-site provides an effective route to tune the electronic structure: reduced anion electronegativity weakens metal-anion hybridization, shifts anion p states upward, narrows the band gap, and thereby improves electrical transport. Benefiting from this synergy between vacancy-induced phonon suppression and anion-regulated electronic optimization, CdGa₂Te₄ exhibits an ultralow lattice thermal conductivity of 0.19 W·m⁻¹K⁻¹ and a high room-temperature ZT of 0.957. This work not only predicts defective chalcopyrites as a promising platform for high-performance thermoelectrics but also provides a practical design strategy by integrating vacancy ordering, higher-order phonon scattering, and anion-dependent band engineering.

articles.title: Thermodynamic demonstration of tetracriticality and multicomponent superconductivity in UTe₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.17905v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The candidate topological superconductor UTe₂ exhibits a complex phase diagram with multiple superconducting states, and the nature of their coexistence is not yet resolved. In particular, the apparent observation of two intersecting second-order phase boundaries at a triple point in the pressure-temperature phase diagram is thermodynamically forbidden. This suggests either a hidden phase transition or a fundamental misunderstanding of the superconductivity in this material. Here we observe an additional phase boundary that is characterized by an upward jump in the sound velocity. This is direct thermodynamic evidence for a phase transition in which superconducting order is lost on cooling. Our results establish a tetracritical point beyond which the ambient and pressure-induced superconducting order parameters form a multicomponent state. We use the measured phase diagram to demonstrate that strong competition between the two superconducting order parameters drives the loss of order when cooling, and leads to phase locking that suppresses superconducting fluctuations. These findings provide the definitive magnetic field-pressure-temperature phase diagram of UTe₂ and establish a thermodynamic foundation for multicomponent superconductivity.

articles.title: Light induced magnetization in d-wave superconductors
