articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.18134v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a microscopic theory of the inverse Faraday effect in weakly disordered s- and d-wave superconductors. The Keldysh--Nambu quasiclassical formalism is extended to retain the particle-hole asymmetric terms, and the dc current induced by monochromatic radiation is computed to second order in the field and to first order in the wave vector, with elastic impurity scattering treated in the Born approximation. At finite wave vector the radiation induces an oscillation of the order parameter amplitude -- the Schmid--Higgs amplitude mode -- that is linear in the field. It is driven by the component of the electric field along the photon wave vector and appears for both s- and d-wave pairing. The amplitude mode contribution to the static magnetization sets in at ω=2Δ and diverges as (ω-2Δ)⁻¹ for an isotropic gap, whereas for d-wave pairing it is finite at all frequencies and changes sign near ωapprox 2sqrt2Δ. This contribution is of the first order in the particle-hole asymmetry, and it is not enhanced by the disorder scattering rate. The orbital magnetization that exists already in the normal state and the contribution of the charge imbalance are not evaluated.

articles.title: Vortex order in magnetic frustrated GeNi₂O₄ and GeCo₂O₄ spinels
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.20029v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the search for new spin textures based on singular magnetic objects like Bloch-points or vortices, spinel compounds emerge as an interesting playground due to the interplay between magnetic anisotropy and complex interactions that extend well beyond first neighbors on a pyrochlore lattice. Based on an exploration of the exchange interaction phase diagrams of members of the GeB₂O₄ family with B=Co and Ni, we show, using simultaneous modeling of inelastic neutron scattering measurements and single-crystal neutron diffraction data, that a 2-k magnetic structure may be stabilized in these compounds. This leads to a short period spin vortex crystal, a variant induced by the magnetic anisotropy of the 3-k Bloch-point structure predicted for isotropic spins. Our study rationalizes the formation of these multi-k spin textures in frustrated antiferromagnets, as well as their anisotropy-dependent evolution.

articles.title: Nitrogen-doped W0.75Re0.25 Superconducting Nanowire Single Photon Detectors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.25597v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Nitrogen-doped Tungsten-Rhenium superconducting alloys were recently proposed as a promising material platform for superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs), offering a favorable balance between high normal state resistivity and tunable superconducting properties. In this work, we report on the fabrication and characterization of SNSPDs based on thin W0.75Re0.25 films deposited by reactive DC magnetron sputtering in a mixed Ar/N2 atmosphere. Meander detectors with 70 nm linewidth exhibit saturated internal detection efficiency (IDE) up to 1310 nm and 85.3% IDE at 1550 nm at 2.5 K, with sub-nanosecond rise times, decay times of the order of a few nanoseconds, and timing jitter of 73.2 ps measured with room temperature amplifiers.

articles.title: Demagnetization effect on magnetic noise measurements in spin ice materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.25993v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Magnetic noise spectroscopy provides direct access to spontaneous time-dependent magnetization fluctuations in correlated magnetic systems, including spin liquids, spin ices, and spin glasses. Here we investigate how demagnetizing fields shape the magnetic noise spectra measured in spin ice. By combining magnetic noise and ac susceptibility measurements on single-crystal spin ice samples with different sizes and shapes, we show that magnetic noise, like linear response, is strongly renormalized by sample geometry. As a consequence, measured noise spectra do not directly yield the intrinsic fluctuation spectrum, and demagnetization corrections cannot in general be determined from noise data alone. Instead, sample geometry must be treated as a central experimental control parameter for accessing intrinsic dynamics. These results establish the role of boundary conditions in fluctuation spectroscopy and provide a framework for quantitatively comparing noise measurements with microscopic theories of spin dynamics.

articles.title: Advances in electrical contacts to single crystals of emerging materials for transport measurements
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.00173v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Transport measurements that probe electrical resistivity of a material under varying external stimuli, such as temperature, magnetic field, optical illumination, and gate voltage, are among the most important experimental techniques in condensed matter physics. These measurements provide critical insights into the fundamental electronic properties of materials. In recent years, they have facilitated the discovery and exploration of intriguing physical phenomena (e.g., superconductivity and quantum oscillations) and unique device functionalities (e.g., photoresponse and electrostatic gating effects) in various emerging materials, particularly in the form of single crystals. However, unlike large-scale wafers or thin films, newly synthesized single crystals often pose substantial challenges in establishing reliable electrical contacts due to their irregular geometries, limited dimensions, inherent structural characteristics, and potential susceptibility to degradation. In this review, we highlight recent technological advancements in the fabrication of high-quality, lithographically defined multi-terminal electrodes on both exfoliable and non-exfoliable single crystals for transport measurements. Our work provides a practical guide for researchers seeking to select appropriate contact-fabrication strategies tailored to unique characteristics of emerging crystals.

articles.title: Anharmonic lattice dynamics and superconductivity in strained bulk and surface niobium
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.02730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using first-principles calculations, we investigate how homogeneous strain and crystallographic surface orientation modify the vibrational and superconducting properties of niobium. For bulk Nb, tensile strain strongly softens the phonon spectrum and enhances the electron--phonon coupling, increasing the superconducting transition temperature from 9.5 K at equilibrium to 14.5 K at sim!6% lattice expansion. For the low-index Nb(001), Nb(110), and Nb(111) surfaces, harmonic phonon calculations exhibit imaginary modes, showing that anharmonic lattice effects are essential. To treat these effects efficiently, we train Nb-specific machine-learning interatomic potentials on bulk and slab first-principles configurations and use them to accelerate stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation calculations, thereby obtaining anharmonically renormalized phonon modes that are combined with density-functional perturbation theory electron--phonon matrix elements to construct the Eliashberg spectral function. Among the clean free-standing slabs considered here, Nb(001) exhibits the strongest electron--phonon coupling and the highest calculated transition temperature of 10.0 K, while Nb(110) and Nb(111) show progressively reduced pairing strength. Finally, by analyzing the Eliashberg spectral function and the functional derivative δ T_c/δα²F(ω), we identify the phonon energy ranges most effective for superconducting pairing. Our results show that strain, surface termination, and anharmonic phonon renormalization provide complementary and interrelated microscopic routes for tuning superconductivity in Nb.

articles.title: An Extensible Agentic Framework for Expert-Level Automation of Atomistic Simulations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.09422v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Traditionally, atomistic simulation has been constrained by the computational scaling limits of ab initio methods and the parameterization overhead of empirical force fields. The recent emergence of universal machine learning interatomic potentials has significantly mitigated these bottlenecks, offering near-quantum accuracy and generalizability across diverse chemical spaces at a fraction of the computational cost. However, this shift has relocated the bottleneck to the human dimension: time-consuming mechanical processes, such as input preparation and data analysis, now dominate the research lifecycle. We introduce Paimon, a Platform for Agentic Integration in Materials Optimization and Nanoscale-simulations. Through hundreds of trials on an expert-level liquid electrolyte simulation, we show that Paimon substantially improves the reliability of agentic workflows by suppressing silent errors: plausible yet physically incorrect results. Paimon accommodates a new capability without modifying the agents already present, which we demonstrate by integrating an externally developed scientific agent. As an agent harness for atomistic simulations, Paimon affords researchers a continuous, science-centric workflow throughout the entire simulation lifecycle.

articles.title: Anatomy of fast current-induced skyrmion motion in synthetic antiferromagnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.09948v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The high mobility of current-driven skyrmions in synthetic antiferromagnets (SAFs) is widely explained by the macroscopic suppression of the skyrmion Hall effect through gyrotropic force compensation. This established view, however, overlooks a concurrent and significant reduction in the Gilbert damping parameter α, a key factor in the Thiele equation governing skyrmion velocity. Here, we show that this damping attenuation originates from a reconfigured magnon-electron scattering landscape. Using a microscopic s-d model, we demonstrate that the strong antiferromagnetic interlayer Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) exchange coupling in SAFs increases the magnonic gap of skyrmion collective modes, thereby suppressing the thermal magnon population and, consequently, the magnon-electron scattering rate that dominates damping in metallic ferromagnets. Our work establishes a dual-mechanism framework to fully explain the superior kinetics of SAF skyrmions: the macroscopic topological effect rectifies the motion direction, while the microscopic dissipation mechanism reduces the drag. This synergy enables high-speed and efficient motion, providing a fundamental elucidation of the enhanced mobility reported in recent studies such as the work by Pham et al. [Science 384, 307-312 (2024)].

articles.title: A Differentiable DFT-Based Framework for Inverse Materials Design
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.25502v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Discovering solid-state materials with target properties remains a central challenge in computational materials science. Existing data-driven approaches rely on training data and may generalize poorly outside the training distribution. Here we develop a first-principles inverse-design framework that requires no training data. It integrates reverse-mode automatic differentiation (AD) into the Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker method combined with the coherent potential approximation (KKR-CPA), in which elemental concentrations serve as continuous optimization variables. Reverse-mode AD computes all concentration gradients in one backward pass, enabling optimization over dozens of candidate elements. Any differentiable quantity computable within KKR-CPA can serve as an optimization objective. We demonstrate this generality in permanent-magnet and half-metal design, identifying candidates such as (Nd₀.₉₈₃Pr₀.₀₁₇)(Co₀.₇₂Fe₀.₂₈)₂Fe₃ and FeMn(As₀.₈₃P₀.₁₇), respectively. We also synthesized materials with five SmCo₅-based compositions selected during optimization for higher magnetization. Their measured magnetization agreed closely with calculated values. Our framework offers a first-principles route to designing materials with target properties.

articles.title: Bright and Dark Excitons in CrSBr: Local Ligand-Field Character and Band-Coherent Optical Selection Rules
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.08355v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Magnetic van der Waals semiconductors such as CrSBr host an intricate exciton landscape. Quasiparticle self-consistent GW theory with electron-hole ladder vertex corrections (QSGWc) has established the gap and the character of the bright XA (1.34 eV) and XB (1.8 eV) excitons. Why these bright excitons coexist, within a few tens of meV, with companions orders of magnitude darker has remained unexplained. Here we show that brightness is fixed by a symmetry of the structure: a mirror-glide exchanges the two Cr atoms of each layer, every exciton has a definite parity under it, and bright and dark partners are its even and odd members. The even sector carries the b-axis dipole; the odd sector is suppressed by about three orders of magnitude. The dark partners of XA and XB occupy the same region of k-space as the bright states, and dark states such as the one at 1.50 eV are dipole-forbidden by inversion symmetry. Frenkel and Wannier-Mott labels describe what an exciton is made of, but brightness is decided by symmetry and by the coherent addition of transition dipoles. This bare structure is the reference for magnon, phonon and photon couplings.

articles.title: Coupled Magnetic and Lattice Excitations in Multiferroic Ba3HoRu2O9: Insights from Neutron Scattering, Raman Spectroscopy, and Machine-Learned Phonon Calculations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.23490v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Inelastic neutron scattering (INS) spectra of correlated 4d-4f multiferroic oxides are difficult to interpret because magnetic, crystal-field, and lattice excitations frequently overlap in energy. The hexagonal 6H perovskite Ba3HoRu2O9 provides an ideal platform to investigate this interplay owing to the coexistence of Ru2O9 molecular units and localized Ho3+ moments. To identify the contributions from these different excitations, we combine INS with linear spin-wave calculations, crystal field analysis, Raman spectroscopy, and machine-learned force field (MLFF) phonon calculations. A magnetic excitation below 6.2 meV, observed only in the low-temperature magnetic phase, is reproduced by linear spin-wave theory with intradimer Ru-Ru and Ru-Ho exchange of comparable size and a Ho single-ion anisotropy, and is therefore consistent with a collective spin-wave excitation of the coupled Ru-Ho magnetic network. At higher energies, broad excitations centered near 20, 39, 70, and 90 meV are observed that persist far above the magnetic ordering temperatures. The magnetic part of the 39 meV excitation, isolated by subtracting the Bose-corrected high-temperature data, follows the Ho3+ magnetic form factor. Crystal-field calculations based on the Stevens formalism place a group of strong Ho3+ transitions in this energy range, while Raman spectroscopy and MLFF phonon calculations identify optical phonons with comparable energies. Together, these complementary results show that the broad INS feature near 39 meV arises from overlapping Ho3+ crystal-field excitations and lattice vibrations. These findings establish a microscopic framework for understanding the interplay between spin, crystal-field, and lattice degrees of freedom in this multiferroic 4d-4f compound

articles.title: Critical Phases of the extended isotropic XY chain with four-spin interaction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.29006v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using the Jordan-Wigner transformation we calculate exactly the ground state and low-temperature thermodynamic properties of the spin S=1/2 isotropic XX chain with four spin interaction. In terms of the equivalent spinless fermion (SF) representation the system is viewed as a lattice fermion gas with nearest-neighbor (J) and next-next-next-neighbor (Jast/4) hopping. It is shown that with the increase of four spin coupling, at Jastc = 4J/3 the system experiences the Lifshitz type topological phase transition characterized by the tripling of Fermi points. The quantum phase transition (QPT) point marks transition from a gapless spin-liquid phase of standard XX chain into again a gapless spin-liquid phase with different character of power-low decay of spin correlations. At the transition point the free fermion dispersion relation shows flattering at Fermi points, what determines singular character of density of states ρ(ω)sim (ω/J)⁻²/³ and as a consequence unconventional temperature dependence of heat capacity of the system Csim (T/Jast)¹/³, and singular magnetic susceptibility of the system χ(H)sim (H/Jast)⁻²/³. In the case of alternating magnetic field the system is characterized by the rich ground state phase diagram which contains fully polarized (ferromagnetic), gapped antiferromagnetic (AFM) and spin liquid phases. At the transition point from the gapped AFM phase into the gapless polarized spin liquid phase the system shows rapid increase of magnetization msim(H-H_c)¹/⁶ and magnetic susceptibility a singular behavior as χ(H)sim (H-H_c)⁻⁵/⁶.

articles.title: Memory-dependent electronic friction for nonadiabatic dynamics at metal surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.12572v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Electronic excitation induced by nuclear motion is a key energy dissipation channel in chemical dynamics at metal surfaces. Here, nonadiabatic effects can be treated via molecular dynamics with electronic friction, where they act as frictional drag and fluctuation force contributions. Commonly, the Markov approximation is imposed, so memory effects are ignored. A theoretical formalism is presented to evaluate tensorial and configuration-dependent electronic friction memory kernels from first principles. We evaluate friction kernels for Newns--Anderson Hamiltonian models as well as within Kohn--Sham density functional theory and analyse their mathematical properties and configuration dependence. These friction kernels capture memory effects that arise from frequency and configuration dependence and are used to study energy loss in hyperthermal atomic and diatomic scattering studied via the classical path approximation. Memory effects lead to an increase of vibrational and a reduction of translational energy loss in the case of nitric oxide scattering on Au(111), leading to an increase of directional anisotropy of friction. Importantly, memory-dependent evaluation of electronic friction removes the need to define a single effective Markovian friction coefficient from the structured frequency-dependent electronic response.

articles.title: Localized Excitons and Exciton-Phonon Coupling in Antiferromagnetic AgCrP2S6
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.18394v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: AgCrP2S6 combines a low-symmetry thiophosphate framework with an antiferromagnetic Cr sublattice and nonmagnetic Ag sites, where covalency and magnetic localization compete in the low-energy optical response. Using single-crystal x-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, lattice-dynamical calculations, and self-consistent vertex-corrected many-body methods, we determine its structural, electronic, and excitonic properties. The material remains monoclinic from 100 to 300 K, with low-temperature Ag-site disorder, and is dynamically stable. Many-body calculations find a reduced quasiparticle gap relative to Cr trihalides, yet the lowest excitons stay predominantly local: a weakly bright, strongly anisotropic Frenkel exciton near 1.4 eV with dominant onsite d-d character and ligand-assisted d-p admixture. In the C2h setting this state is mainly Bu, with Ag diagonal and Bg bright-dark phonon coupling channels. Stronger p-d hybridization narrows the gap, while antiferromagnetic exchange and Ag dilution suppress intersite coherence. Cation substitution and ligand-ion engineering thus provide a transferable handle for tuning exciton localization in related 2D magnets, with implications for boson coupling and spintronics.

articles.title: Linker Functionalization and pH Tuning Enhance Solar-Driven Catalytic CO₂ Reduction in MOF-5
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.02256v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The wide band gap of metal-organic framework (MOF) 5 constrains its use in photocatalytic carbon dioxide (CO₂) reduction despite its high porosity and favorable mass-transport properties. Adopting a state-of-the-art first-principles approach, we systematically investigate the effects of volumetric strain, metal-node substitution, linker functionalization, and pH control as knobs to improve the CO₂ photocatalytic ability of MOF-5. Strain and metal-node substitution negligibly affect the gap, whereas linker functionalization narrows it into the visible range via in-gap states while preserving reduction-side alignment at pH = 0. The resulting reduction energetics are strongly sensitive to both linker functionalization and pH. Halogenated and hydroxylated frameworks provide access primarily to HCOOH, CO, and HCHO under alkaline conditions, principally with the Mg and Zn nodes, whereas COOH functionalization offers the broadest thermodynamic accessibility across the full CO₂ reduction sequence. NH₂ retains thermodynamic feasibility for all target reduction pathways but with larger overpotentials, while NO₂ generally yields unfavorable reduction energetics. Crucially, within the COOH series, the choice of the metal node tunes the fundamental gap by over 1 eV with only minor changes in the reduction overpotentials, placing Sr- and Ba-based architectures as the most favorable ones for broad product selectivity with visible-light excitation. Linker functionalization substantially reduces the spatial overlap of the frontier states, promoting photoinduced charge separation. Taken together, these results establish linker functionalization and solution pH as complementary design levers for independently tuning light absorption and CO₂-reduction energetics in MOF-5, establishing a rational and viable route for designing efficient MOF-based photocatalysts.

articles.title: Neural Modal Decomposition: Architectural Priors from Observables
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.14402v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many engineering building blocks behave as multi-port linear time-invariant systems. RF cavities, photonic devices, and superconducting quantum chips, despite their different underlying physics, all share a common mathematical structure for their port-level response. Each entry of the response matrix is a sum of contributions from a small number of intrinsic resonant modes, the pole-residue form. A model capable of predicting such responses for arbitrary geometries and arbitrary port configurations, while simultaneously extracting the underlying eigenmode structure, could therefore offer a design principle potentially applicable across all these domains. We propose a neural framework that learns this modal decomposition end-to-end, supervised only by system-level observables and without supervising the modal parameters themselves. The architecture decomposes into a port-independent pole predictor and two port-dependent coupling predictors whose outputs are combined entry-wise, separating intrinsic from port-dependent features. This factorization yields a single trained model that generalizes to port counts unseen during training, whereas direct regression needs a separate model for each port count, with an output size that grows as O(N²). Although the modal parameters are never supervised, the freely parameterized poles converge to the physical resonances, in agreement with poles extracted by the AAA rational approximation algorithm. We instantiate the framework in radio-frequency electromagnetic surrogate modeling. A model trained only on 2-port data accurately predicts N-port responses unseen during training.

articles.title: Detuning-Controlled Vibrational Autler--Townes Passage toward Single-Sublevel Orientation of Nonpolar Molecules
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.01715v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Single-sublevel preparation would give collision and surface-scattering experiments access to oriented molecules, yet established orientation methods either require a permanent dipole moment or select only partially. We introduce all-optical Autler--Townes state-selective adiabatic passage (ASAP), in which a detuned infrared field dresses a rovibrational transition, and the selected dressed branch is mapped adiabatically onto one magnetic sublevel as the field vanishes. We resolve the magnetic-sublevel-selected rovibrational Autler--Townes doublet of the R(0) transition of ¹³CO₂ and show that the coupling strength and detuning set both its separation and the partition of the bare-state composition between its two components. The spectral selectivity of the target dressed branch reaches 97% at a coupling detuning of -1.2~MHz. A density-matrix model calibrated against these spectra returns, for the dressed molecules, a target-sublevel population approaching 0.9 over a broad range of coupling powers and detunings.

articles.title: Global MHD simulations of the solar convective zone using a volleyball mesh decomposition. I. Pilot
articles.abstract: arXiv:2211.09564v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Solar modelling has long been split into `internal' and `surface' modelling because of the lack of tools to connect the very different scales in space and time, as well as the widely different environments and the dominating physical effects involved. Significant efforts have recently been put into resolving this disconnect. We address the outstanding bottlenecks in connecting internal convection zone and dynamo simulations to the surface of the Sun, and conduct a proof-of-concept high-resolution global simulation of the convection zone of the Sun, using the task-based DISPATCH code framework. We present a new `volleyball' mesh decomposition, which has Cartesian patches tessellated on a sphere with no singularities. We use our new entropy based HLLS approximate Riemann solver to model magneto-hydrodynamics in a global simulation, ranging between 0.655---0.998 R_odot, with an initial ambient magnetic field set to 0.1 Gauss. This paper describes the methods and the pilot runs of the setup. The mesh decomposition exhibits neither unwanted artefacts, nor noise build-up. The simulations develop convective motions with complex, turbulent structures. Small-scale dynamo action twists the ambient magnetic field and locally amplifies magnetic field magnitudes by more than two orders of magnitude within the initial run-time.

articles.title: Kerr-athermal baths enhance cooling in quantum refrigerators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2311.10499v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a three-qubit quantum refrigerator, with a three-body interaction enabling cooling of the target qubit, coupled to harmonic oscillator baths prepared in stationary Kerr-athermal states. The reservoir occupation probabilities are specified by a Kerr-type preparation Hamiltonian, while the bath dynamics during operation are harmonic. We show that these reservoirs lower the steady-state temperature of the cold qubit relative to the thermal-bath reference. The improvement of steady-state cooling is distinct from that of the minimum transient temperature, which is not universally enhanced. In a parameter regime where the thermal reference exhibits only transient cold-qubit cooling, the engineered Kerr-athermal baths can produce a steady-state temperature below the initial value. We also investigate the dependence of the steady-state temperature and minimum attainable temperatures on the anharmonicity in the bath state. Analysis of bath-currents reveals lower steady-state temperatures with nearly unchanged coefficients of performance, revealing that reservoir engineering leads to cold-qubit cooling.

articles.title: Origins of suppressed self-diffusion of nanoscale constituents of a complex liquid
articles.abstract: arXiv:2404.17756v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Understanding and ultimately controlling the transformations and properties of nanoscale systems, from proteins to synthetic nanomaterial assemblies, is limited by the inability to uncover their dynamics on their characteristic length and time scales. Here, we nevertheless demonstrate this ability using MHz X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy (XPCS) -- directly elucidating the characteristic microsecond-dynamics of density fluctuations of semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs), not only in a colloidal dispersion but, more importantly, in a liquid phase consisting of densely packed, yet mobile, NCs with no long-range order. We find the wavevector-dependent fluctuation rates in the liquid phase are suppressed relative to those in the colloidal phase and relative to observations of densely packed repulsive particles. We show that the suppressed rates are due to a substantial decrease in the self-diffusion of NCs, which we attribute to explicit attractive interactions. Using coarse-grained simulations, we find that the extracted shape and strength of the interparticle potential explains the stability of the liquid phase, in contrast to the gelation observed via XPCS in many other charged colloidal systems. This work opens the door to elucidating fast, condensed phase dynamics in complex fluids and other nanoscale soft matter, such as densely packed proteins and non-equilibrium self-assembly processes, in addition to designing microscopic strategies to avert gelation.

articles.title: Quantum could solve AI energy drain, says tech founder
articles.abstract: Quantum computers could curb the vast energy demands of artificial intelligence data centers with their ability to run complex calculations, one of the tech's pioneers told AFP.

articles.title: Upgraded microscope can now watch individual quantum particles in motion
articles.abstract: Energy can be carried in a number of ways: by electrons, the particles that underpin all modern electronics, as well as by quasiparticles, the results of different particles interacting with one another at the quantum level. Columbia chemist Milan Delor has been watching these different forms of energy flow with an instrument called stroboSCAT, a unique microscope that uses strobe-like light pulses to capture particles and quasiparticles as they move through different materials.

articles.title: New perovskite system extends room-temperature spin polarization via successive quantum wells
articles.abstract: A research team led by Lu Haipeng, a professor in the Department of Chemistry at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST), has achieved a breakthrough in preserving spin information for optoelectronic technologies. The team has developed a perovskite chiral multiple quantum-well system that maintains spin polarization approximately 300 times longer at room temperature. The study opens new possibilities for future quantum technologies and next-generation spin-based applications. The study was published in the journal Nature Photonics.

articles.title: Light reflecting within thin films can masquerade as molecular signals in perovskite solar materials
articles.abstract: An infrared signal thought to reveal how molecules in perovskite solar materials respond to light-generated charges can arise largely from the way light travels through the thin film itself, a new theoretical study shows. Jun Nishida, assistant professor at the Institute for Molecular Science (IMS), Japan, found that light-generated charges alter how infrared light is reflected and transmitted within the film layers, producing sharp features that resemble changes in molecular vibrations even when the vibrations themselves are unaltered.

articles.title: Atomic defects leave telltale optical fingerprints in quantum material
articles.abstract: The tiny atomic defects so important for future quantum technologies can be difficult to spot. Fortunately, they leave behind some clues. The defects can alter how a material responds to light, producing a distinctive optical fingerprint that scientists can measure. The challenge is figuring out which fingerprints belong to which defects.

articles.title: Quantum interference keeps two atoms bound despite enough energy to break apart
articles.abstract: How can something remain intact when it should naturally break apart? This question has been addressed by researchers at RPTU. Their work has led to the experimental observation of an unusual quantum state in which two atoms remain bound together even though they possess enough energy to separate. The results have been published in the journal Nature Physics.

articles.title: Manufacturing Complex Structures Through Interfacial Self-Organization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional manufacturing constructs three-dimensional geometries through localized material deposition, removal, or shaping, with fabrication effort greatly increasing with geometric complexity. Here, we introduce a manufacturing approach in which target geometry is encoded into sparse wireframe scaffolds that guide liquid self-organization through interfacial forces. We apply a computational framework that approximates arbitrary target geometries using constant-mean-curvature surface domains and extracts their boundaries to construct the scaffolds. Under neutral buoyancy conditions, curable liquids injected into these scaffolds self-organize into the prescribed geometries, which are subsequently solidified into mechanically isotropic structures with optically smooth surfaces. We demonstrate the fabrication of complex anatomical models and topology-optimized structures featuring intricate branching geometries, internal cavities, and integrated materials. This approach opens new possibilities for scalable fabrication of complex geometric designs.

articles.title: Hierarchical Design of Ambidirectional LCE Sheets for Three-State Gaussian Shape Morphs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modulation of surface curvature is a commonly exploited strategy to achieve adaptability within natural and synthetic systems where structure governs function. While Gaussian curvature of inextensible surfaces is fixed, surfaces made of extensible materials can adapts their Gaussian curvature under strain, unlocking capabilities such as locomotion, dynamic coloration, and tunable stiffness. This feature is commonly exploited to develop soft actuators capable of complex functionalities; however, traversing the entire spectrum of Gaussian curvature was previously difficult to achieve without the use of multi-material constructs or spatially varied stimulus fields. In this work, we present a strategy for generating a diverse range of dynamic Gaussian shape morphs using multiphase liquid crystal elastomers (LCEs) as ambidirectionally deforming building blocks. Taking advantage of the materials sequential contraction and elongation during phase transitions, we design and investigate the deformation response of radially aligned flat LCE sheets which consecutively morph into negatively and positively curved flat surfaces in response to monotonically increasing temperature. We then investigate the influence of mesoscale asymmetry and macroscale geometry on curvature magnitude and bending symmetry, thereby demonstrating that a single form factor can be programmed to undergo a rich library of deformation behaviors. Finally, inspired by the strategy of cephalopods to couple mechanical deformability to dynamic optical properties, we fabricate a structurally colored LCE sheet which couples its dynamic Gaussian curvature to a dynamic color-changing response. This approach offers a route toward adaptive structures capable of multistate shape reconfiguration for applications in soft robotics, deployable systems, and responsive surfaces.

articles.title: Conductance scaling in nanopore arrays: disentangling roles of pore arrangement and reservoir geometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The scaling of electrical conductance with the number of nanopores, N, in an array is of fundamental importance for applications in membrane separation and ion transport across biological membranes, and has been the subject of longstanding disagreement in the field. Combining finite element calculations with theory, we resolve this disagreement for pores with negligible surface charge by showing that two previously conflicting predictions are each correct in their own limiting reservoir geometry: cuboidal reservoirs commensurate with the interpore spacing, for which the conductance scales linearly with N, and infinite reservoirs, for which the scaling is sublinear in N for closely spaced pores. We show the transition between these limits with increasing reservoir size and, for infinite reservoirs, we show that a simple analytical model from electrical contact theory is mathematically equivalent to an existing point-charge capacitance model for nanopore arrays and validate its applicability against finite element and method-of-moments calculations. Using this model, we derive a characteristic coupling length, ell_c,95, the interpore spacing at which the array conductance reaches 95% of that of the same number of independent pores. ell_c,95 scales linearly with pore diameter d, and grows with N as simlog N for linear arrays and simsqrtN for square arrays, so that pore coupling persists to surprisingly large separations in large arrays. Our work provides a general framework for predicting nanopore array conductance as a function of pore arrangement and reservoir geometry, of importance to nanofluidics research and the targeted design of functional devices.

articles.title: Controlled Oxidation of Tellurium Nanoparticles for Telecom Detection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface oxidation plays an important role in governing charge transport in semiconductor nanoparticle assemblies. Here, we investigate the optoelectronic properties of solution-processed tellurium (Te) nanoparticle ensembles prepared through gradual ambient-air exposure. Structural and spectroscopic analyses reveal interconnected elemental Te nanoparticles with coexisting alpha-TeO2 and hydroxyl-containing surface species, exhibiting a lower relative contribution of oxidized Te than previously investigated forced-air-oxidized ensembles. The resulting photodetectors demonstrate photoresponse at 405, 532, and 1550 nm, with maximum responsivities of 10.1, 14.4, and 8.5 mA/W, respectively. At 1550 nm, the device exhibits rise and fall times of 17.7 and 40.2 s, respectively, and an estimated shot-noise-limited specific detectivity of 1.3 * 10⁶ Jones. These findings highlight the importance of controlling surface oxidation to balance interparticle charge transport and dark-current suppression, offering insights for the development of solution-processed Te-based photodetectors for short-wave infrared applications.

articles.title: Current-voltage characteristics of layered cuprate superconductors with intrinsic Josephson junctions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A brief review of the results for the current-voltage characteristics study in highly anisotropic cuprate superconductors is presented, considering the existence of the intrinsic Josephson effect in multilayer HTSC compounds. We analyzed the observations of multi-branch current-voltage characteristics for current in the c-direction both for the hole-doped and electron-doped cuprate SCs wich conveniently viewed as a strack of intrinsic Josephson junctions, where the CuO2 layers serve as superconducting plates and the buffer layers as dielectric interlayers. It was shown that the tunneling characteristics of intrinsic Josephson junctions in optimally doped p- and n-type cuprates indicate a predominantly d-wave symmetry of the order parameter, demonstrating high conductivity in the subgap regime: U < 2delta/e. The analysis carried out confirms the theoretically predicted power-law dependences U ~ I^gamma with gamma = (0.33 - 0.50) in the hole-doped Bi- and Tl-compounds, which is typical for SCs with monotonic dx²-y² - wave symmetry of the order parameter and with gamma = (0.70 - 0.76) for electron-doped SCs with a non-monotonic d-wave symmetry within the framework of the two-band/two-gap model.

articles.title: Atomically abrupt sp-sp² all-carbon heterojunction preserving the electronic identity of constituent allotropes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Covalently integrating distinct carbon allotropes with atomic precision remains, to date, elusive, despite the clear advantage of combining complementary functionalities while preserving their electronic identities. Here, we realize an all-carbon lateral heterojunction combining (sp²) armchair graphene nanoribbons (GNRs) and sp-sp² hydrogenated graphdiyne (hGDY) on Au(111) through Fe-mediated hierarchical on-surface synthesis. Low-temperature scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy combined with density-functional theory reveal an atomically abrupt (<0.5 nm), asymmetric type-I interface. Redistribution of an edge-localized GNR state onto the first hGDY unit demonstrates local electronic continuity, whereas their characteristic electronic structures re-emerge immediately beyond the interface. Calculations further indicate that heterojunction formation weakens the interaction of both constituents with the underlying Au(111) substrate, widening their gaps and reducing adsorption-induced interfacial polarization. These results establish lateral covalent integration as a route to engineer atomically defined electronic interfaces and substrate coupling in all-carbon nanostructures.

articles.title: Coherent Electrometer Using Hybridised Double Quantum Dot - Resonator States
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Probing the change in conductance or reactance of a charge sensitive system using an rf cavity is a standard way of doing fast single-charge electrometry. In this article, we present a detector concept which is instead based on coherent interaction. We show that the coherent interaction between a microwave resonator and double quantum dot gives rise to a fast, highly sensitive electrometer. The coherent electrometer achieves a state-of-the-art readout speed, resolving two charge states with SNR of 11.7 in 16 μs, with a readout signal two orders of magnitude lower in power than previously required to reach this speed. In this way, heating of the sample becomes negligible. Thanks to its sensitivity and low dissipation, the coherent electrometer opens up the avenue for quantum limited charge detection with nanosecond speed and minimal back-action.

articles.title: Fabrication and Characterization of Flexible In2O3 Thin-Film Transistors on Mica Substrates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flexible oxide-semiconductor thin-film transistors (TFTs) with high field-effect mobility (uFE > 70 cm²/Vs) are required for next-generation flexible displays. Polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs are promising candidates; however, conventional flexible substrates such as plastics are not suitable because their fabrication typically requires relatively high temperatures (~350 deg.C). In this study, we used mica as a flexible substrate to fabricate polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs, motivated by previous demonstrations of crystalline oxide growth on mica. The resulting TFTs exhibited a uFE of approximately 75 cm²/Vs. The devices maintained gate-modulated operation after 10³ flex-out bending cycles at a 5 mm radius, whereas flex-in cycling caused early electrical failure, likely due to In2O3 film degradation. The TFTs also operated normally after exposure to 85 deg.C and 40% relative humidity for one day. These results demonstrate that mica substrates enable high-mobility, flex-out-compatible In2O3-based TFTs.

articles.title: Momentum-Resolved Kondo Hybridization of Nonsymmorphic Dirac-Derived Bands in CeAgBi₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How symmetry-constrained conduction states acquire heavy-quasiparticle character is a central question in correlated quantum materials. Combining angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, Ce 4d → 4f resonant photoemission, and first-principles calculations, we investigate the nonsymmorphic Kondo lattice CeAgBi₂. We identify quasi-two-dimensional Bi-square-net-derived bands consistent with calculated Dirac crossings and nodal lines. Resonant photoemission resolves a nearly dispersionless Ce 4f band near the Fermi level, establishing Kondo heavy-quasiparticle states. Its pronounced momentum-dependent spectral weight at intersections with the identified Dirac-derived branches provides direct spectroscopic evidence for their participation in c-f hybridization. Complementary measurements on independently cleaved samples and an effective hybridization model connect these branches to the Kondo heavy-quasiparticle spectrum. The combined results support preservation of nonsymmorphic Dirac-band connectivity under Kondo renormalization, showing how symmetry-constrained conduction states become constituents of correlated heavy quasiparticles.

articles.title: Multifractality in sputtered crystalline and amorphous transition metal nitride thin films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we present evidence for multifractal growth in Titanium and Niobium nitride thin films on different substrates. Self-similar multifractal structures such as dendrites and multi-branched snowflake-like structures are reported. The fractal dimensions are controlled by a combination of processing parameters and conditions at the film-substrate interface. Significantly, fractal growth is observed not only in crystalline films on crystalline and amorphous substrates but also on amorphous films on crystalline substrates. The 2D Multifractal Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (2D MFDFA) carried out on the scanning electron micrographs, clearly reveals the multifractal nature of the nitride thin films. The statistical moments were varied between -5 to +5. The Hausdorff dimensions for the TiN films are in the range of 1.65 to 1.79 while it is 1.64 to 1.74 for the NbN thin films. It is proposed that the observed multifractality is due to a competition between morphological instabilities and Diffusion-Limited Aggregation

articles.title: Extended No-Go Theorem and Its Verification in Spin-Selective Transport through Chiral Cyclodextrin Assemblies
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical two-terminal single-channel no-go theorem relies on time-reversal symmetry (TRS) and scattering-matrix unitarity. In open systems, omitted channels or environment leakage break unitarity, so TRS and the symplectic reciprocity symmetry TRS(dagger) are no longer equivalent, invalidating the classical premises. We prove that if the two-terminal single-channel scattering matrix satisfies TRS(dagger) plus central inversion symmetry, transmission remains no spin selectivity; this result provides an important complement to the classical no-go theorem in nonunitary regime. When these conditions are violated or the single-channel constraint is lifted, spin-selective transport occurs. In charge transport through devices based on chiral (γ)-cyclodextrin molecular assemblies, we verify separately the classical no-go theorem in unitary case and its supplementary version together with its multichannel corollary in nonunitary case: when the conditions for the corresponding no-go theorem hold, the chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) of the assembly disappears, whereas when they are violated, CISS emerges. These results extend the no-go theorem to nonunitary scattering systems and establish an effective theoretical framework for studying CISS in real molecular assemblies.

articles.title: Thouless pumping and Haldane-model topology in a driven extended SSH chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thouless pumping provides a powerful route for probing Chern topology through quantized motion in one-dimensional lattices. We investigate such a topological pump in an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model with tunable next-nearest-neighbor hoppings. A graphical representation in Bloch space is used to construct pumping schemes. In this framework, the Bloch vector traces a closed loop that evolves in time. The Chern number of the synthetic band is then determined by the motion of this loop. Quantum pumping phenomena are demonstrated for a filled band and for a bosonic wave packet driven by Bloch oscillations. We further show that the Haldane model can be mapped to the driven extended SSH chain by replacing a quasimomentum by the pumping time. The quantized charge pump indicates that the Chern number of a two-dimensional model can be read out from a one-dimensional pumping protocol, offering an accessible route for detecting higher-dimensional topology, such as in photonic and cold-atom platforms.

articles.title: Pinching an elastic potato chip
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thin shells deform by transmitting stress across their surface, yet how a shell of general shape carries a localized load remains unclear. Combining experiments, simulations, and theory on pinched saddle-shaped elastic shells, we show that the asymptotic lines, curves of zero normal curvature, dictate both deformation and stiffness. Isometry turns the shell mid-surface into a medium obeying a wave equation in space. Material points lit by the pinch are lifted, while those in its shadow sink. Finite thickness blurs the lit--shadow boundary, and the same rule maps where a clamped shell is rigid. Our findings indicate that light and shadow offer a unified framework for understanding mechanical stress propagation along shell structures.

articles.title: Dynamic Scaling and Aging in Hydrodynamic Coarsening of Vapor Bubbles in a Lennard-Jones Fluid
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the coarsening and aging dynamics of vapor bubbles during liquid-vapor phase separation in a three-dimensional single-component Lennard-Jones fluid using large-scale molecular dynamics simulations. Following a temperature quench from a homogeneous high-temperature state into the two-phase coexistence region, vapor bubbles nucleate and grow in the liquid background. The characteristic bubble size follows a power-law growth, ell(t)sim t^α, with a growth exponent α simeq 2/3, characteristic of inertial hydrodynamic coarsening. We also investigate the two-time autocorrelation function Cₐg(t,t_w) which follows waiting-time dependent relaxation, revealing aging. Furthermore, data at different waiting times collapse onto a scaling function when plotted as a function of the length ratio ell(t)/ell(t_w), demonstrating dynamical scaling during aging. The corresponding scaling function exhibits an algebraic decay with an exponent λ simeq 3. Interestingly, bubble and droplet growth exhibit distinctly different domain-growth and aging exponents despite both being disconnected morphologies.

articles.title: This Is Water: Relative Humidity as a Hidden Parameter in the Self-Assembly of CdSe Nanoplatelets into Threads
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When nanocrystals order into large-scale assemblies, interparticle coupling can give rise to new properties. In the case of semi-conducting nanoplatelets (NPL), stacking them orderly into threads yields highly efficient, ultrafast Förster Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET) over distances of hundreds of nanometers. Producing such assemblies reliably and reproducibly therefore matters. Yet, the mechanism by which dispersed NPL form stacked threads under evaporative self-assembly remains unclear. Here, we show that the relative humidity (RH) under which the NPL dispersion evaporation occurs is a critical, and so far overlooked, experimental parameter. Using a humidity-controlled chamber, we find that micrometer-long NPL stacks form only when evaporation occurs at RH > 50% rather than under dry conditions and when free oleic acid is present in the dispersion. Because such values lie within typical laboratory conditions, humidity is an easily overlooked parameter. We discuss how adventitious water may modify colloidal forces between NPL, through changes in solvent polarity, depletion, capillary or solvation interactions. Our experiments demonstrate that relative humidity is a key parameter for nanoparticle self-assembly and, more broadly, point to colloidal interactions at the nanoscale.

articles.title: Strong Collective Dynamics Hidden behind a Nearly Free Single-Particle Spectrum
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10636v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Single-particle spectroscopy has long served as a criterion for the strength of electronic correlations: strong collective motion is expected to shift and broaden spectral peaks and to renormalize the dispersion. Here we show that this correspondence can fail on the same microscopic orbital. The mechanism relies on local interference between two resonant side orbitals: one suppresses low-energy real transitions into the interacting environment, while the other suppresses spectral-weight backflow to the source orbital; virtual mixing nevertheless transfers the environmental spin polarization to the source. We prove a rigorous relative spectral bound that is uniform in environment size and interaction strength and holds for arbitrary stationary states; the protection becomes stronger as the relative frequency resolution improves. In a fully quantum two-cell device, a collective mode softens by 60%, whereas the particle intensity at the free peak changes by only 3.6 parts per million. Quantum Monte Carlo shows that the transferred spin response grows with spatial correlations and is quantitatively predicted by the free-band polarization. These results recast the meaning of a simple particle spectrum and provide a design principle for quantum probes that combine predictable particle spectra with strong collective sensitivity.

articles.title: Sub-Thouless energy scale in interface-dominated unconventional superconductor junctions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive the conductance in unconventional superconductor - normal metal - normal metal junctions, taking into account the resistance between the normal metals. We show that applying Tanaka--Nazarov boundary conditions at both superconductor and normal metal interfaces reveals a new characteristic low-energy scale which is sub-Thouless in the experimentally relevant strong-interface regime. This scale governs, among other quantities, the curvature of the local density of states (LDOS) and the width of conductance dips near the zero-bias conductance peak in triplet superconductor junctions, thereby replacing the Thouless energy as the dominant low-energy parameter. We derive universal s-wave proximitized diffusive metal expressions for the zero-bias LDOS and differential conductance which solely depend on the interface and bulk resistances, independent of the superconducting gap and Thouless energy scale. This framework provides a possible origin of the anomalous low-bias conductance features observed in unconventional superconductors, offering a refined mechanism for interpreting interface and correlated electron physics in experimental hybrid junctions.

articles.title: Scalable MoS2/Si Photodiode Arrays from Roll-to-Roll Mechanical Exfoliation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a scalable, all-dry route to MoS2/Si photodiodes based on high-throughput roll-to-roll mechanical exfoliation. The method yields dense films of large-lateral-size MoS2 nanosheets and enables the formation of heterojunctions that operate in the photovoltaic regime when transferred onto locally etched Si regions. Individual devices show robust, fast photoresponses and broadband wavelength sensitivity. We further implemented a linear pixel array demonstrating position sensing capability and a 4x4 array as a proof-of-concept imaging sensor. These results indicate that roll-to-roll mechanical exfoliation can overcome common limitations of solution-processed films to enable low-cost, self-powered optoelectronic detectors for sensing and imaging applications.

articles.title: A new approach to measuring both the steady flow curve and the planar extensional viscosity of complex fluids using exponential shear
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the protocol known as Exponential Shear (ES), first proposed by Doshi and Dealy in 1986. This is a transient strong flow that can be readily imposed in the laboratory using commercial strain-controlled (separate motor and transducer) rheometers which accurately measure both the (exponentially) time-varying torque and normal force exerted by the sample. Numerous studies over the years have proposed competing definitions of an appropriate material function for reporting data obtained from the exponentially time-varying imposed deformation. We revisit this unresolved challenge and carefully reconsider the exponential material kinematics involved and the proper definition of the corresponding material functions. We show that by understanding the time-varying eigenvalues and eigenvectors of both the shearing kinematics and the evolving state of stress in the sample it is, in fact, possible to use an exponential shear test to quantitatively map out both the full flow curve (of shear viscosity vs. shear rate) and the steady planar extensional viscosity curve as a function of deformation rate. These findings are supported by numerical simulations of a number of nonlinear viscoelastic constitutive models, asymptotic analysis, as well as experiments with several polymeric liquids.

articles.title: Deintercalation Equilibria Control the Composition, Structure, and Electronic Quality in the Synthesis of 2M-WS₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alkali-metal intercalation-deintercalation (AMID) enables access to metastable layered materials such as 2M-WS₂. Mechanistic studies of AMID have focused on intercalation; how deintercalation proceeds and influences crystal properties is comparatively poorly understood. Here, we assess 34 deintercalation treatments of 2M-KₓWS₂ and find that K⁺ removal proceeds through coupled redox and ion-exchange equilibria, whose positions set the composition, structure, and electronic quality of the products. Across a series of neat solvents, K⁺ deintercalation amount increased with solvent polarity and was driven to near-completion upon addition of nonoxidizing crown ether chelators, regardless of solvent polarity. Spontaneous reintercalation occurred when 2M-WS₂ was placed in dilute aqueous solutions of the strong base KOH but not the neutral salt KCl. These results suggest that the extent of deintercalation is governed by the stability of K⁺ in solution, rather than oxidant strength alone, consistent with a reaction under thermodynamic control. Treatments that bias the deintercalation equilibrium most strongly toward the products while avoiding deleterious side reactions produce the highest quality 2M-WS₂. A six-hour treatment with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ gave the highest average residual resistivity ratio (overlineRRR). Residual K⁺, quantified by ICP-MS, was found in all treated samples and appeared to impose an upper bound on overlineRRR. Treatments yielding crystals with overlineRRR below this bound did not always afford 2M-WS₂; we observed two new structures in bleach-treated samples and signatures of alternative phases under other conditions. This work demonstrates that deintercalation is not merely a processing step in AMID but a mechanistically rich reaction that might be rationally tuned to improve and control metastable materials.

articles.title: Superconductivity and Polar Metallicity in Atomically Thin Nitride Superlattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.10976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of polar and superconducting materials in the atomically thin limit typically results in a competition that suppresses the superconducting order. Here, we challenge this conventional view by employing first-principles calculations to investigate 1:1 superlattices composed of alternating atomically thin layers of TiN/AlN and δ-NbN/AlN. Contrary to the expectation that dense insulating barriers would quench superconductivity, we find that the polar interface can coexist with a superconducting state. We observe that the transition temperature (Tc) of TiN is enhanced by nearly 2 K over its bulk value, while δ-NbN maintains a relatively high Tc exceeding 20 K. We demonstrate that this resilience arises from the formation of a polar metal, where the strong internal electric fields of the AlN layers are partially screened by a charge redistribution within the nitride layers. This screening mechanism, along with the geometric confinement, creates a quasi-two-dimensional electronic environment, establishing these superlattices as a novel platform for exploring the coexistence of structural inversion-symmetry breaking and superconductivity in the two-dimensional limit.

articles.title: Efficient Plane-to-Point Energy Transfer from Supramolecular Excitonic Systems to Molecular Acceptors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collective excitonic interactions in supramolecular assemblies offer opportunities for efficient light harvesting and directed energy transport. Here, we demonstrate efficient energy transfer from two-dimensional silica-encapsulated TDBC J-aggregate sheets to covalently attached ATTO 590 molecular acceptors. Silica encapsulation preserves the J-aggregate excitonic properties while enabling acceptor functionalization at a defined separation from the donor plane. Steady-state donor quenching and acceptor sensitization yield energy-transfer efficiencies of 75-81% in solution, while time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal donor lifetime shortening. We develop a generalized Forster resonance energy-transfer model for an extended planar donor coupled to localized molecular acceptors, predicting an inverse fourth-power dependence of the transfer rate on donor-acceptor separation. Using experimental spectroscopic data and estimated structural parameters, the model predicts an energy-transfer rate of 4.77 x 10¹⁰ s⁻¹, approximately ten times faster than the intrinsic donor decay rate, corresponding to a theoretical energy-transfer efficiency of approximately 91%. These findings provide a framework for developing hybrid excitonic architectures for light harvesting.

articles.title: Effect of Correlation on the Pressure-Induced Insulator to Metal Transition in Complex Spin-Orbit Coupled Double Perovskite La₂CoIr₁₋ₓTiₓO₆
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the effect of electron correlation (U) and hydrostatic pressure on the electronic properties of double perovskites La₂CoIr₁₋ₓTiₓO₆ for x = 0, 0.5, and 1, using first-principles electronic structure calculations within density functional theory (DFT). At ambient pressure, we systematically vary the electron correlation, i.e., on-site Coulomb interaction to study its effect on band gap and structural parameters. Increasing the value of U enhances the band gap of all three compositions while producing only a slight variation in structural parameters. The effect of hydrostatic pressure is also studied for the same compositions. The estimated band gap values at ambient pressure closes at approximately 39, 42, and 53 GPa for x = 0 (for U_Co = 5 eV and U_Ir = 2 eV), 0.5 (for U_Co = 5 eV and U_Ir = 2 eV), and 1 (for U_Co = 4 eV), respectively, indicating pressure-induced insulator-to-metal transitions. These results show that electron correlation stabilises the insulating state, whereas hydrostatic pressure favours the metallic state by closing the band gap. These findings highlight the tunability of correlated oxides through electron correlations and pressure, offering insights for materials design.

articles.title: Theory of spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy with topological insulator tips
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological insulators have enabled a new class of spin-sensitive scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) probes based on helical boundary states. However, how these probes generate a net spin-polarized tunneling current remains unclear. We present a theory of spin-polarized STM with topological insulator tips and show that asymmetric tunneling-contact geometry and spin dephasing enable helical boundary states to generate a spin-polarized tunneling current. Within the standard Landauer-Büttiker formalism, we demonstrate this mechanism for a quantum spin Hall (QSH) insulator tip: asymmetric contacts make the two counter-propagating helical edge states, which carry opposite spins, traverse path lengths that differ by Δ L, and spin dephasing induces backscattering that reduces the conductance more strongly for the longer path. For a representative asymmetric contact and weak spin dephasing, the QSH tip exhibits a tunneling spin polarization of Pₛ=-17.2% under positive bias, whose magnitude can reach 50% for larger Δ L, and which remains robust against Rashba spin-orbit coupling. Crucially, this polarization, dominated by helical edge transport rather than by bulk states, naturally reverses sign with the bias polarity owing to spin-momentum locking. Our findings are consistent with recent STM experiments using topological tips.

articles.title: Parametrizations of the solutions of Love equations and their momenta
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11268v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Love equation is a paradigmatic example of a Fredholm integral equation of great interest in mathematics and physics, where its applications range from electrostatic problems to exactly solvable models for one-dimensional systems. In this work we propose a method to approximate the normalized solutions of Love equations of the first and second kind via a parametrization obtained by Hermite interpolation at Chebyshev nodes. Following the same approach, we also obtain approximations for the second, fourth and sixth momenta of the solution of the Love equations. We focus in particular on one-dimensional quantum gases described by the Lieb-Liniger and the Gaudin-Yang models. For these models, the solutions of Love equations correspond to the normalized densities of pseudorapidities. We show that remarkably accurate results can be obtained using the Hermite-Chebyshev interpolation with a number of points as low as 17+2. In the case of the Lieb-Liniger model, we also propose a very accurate closed-form estimate of the dimensionless ground state energy valid for all values of the dimensionless interaction parameter incorporating known results for small and large couplings supplemented by the Hermite-Chebyshev interpolation for intermediate couplings. As an application of this result, we compute the dimensionless local two-particle correlation function and the black soliton solutions of the Lieb-Liniger model.

articles.title: Strain Controlled Hydrogen Interstitial Site Preference and Hydride Phase Suppression in Epitaxial Vanadium
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding hydrogen behavior in transition metals is crucial for energy storage and sensing technologies. Here we combine density functional theory (DFT) calculations with in-situ electrical measurements to reveal how epitaxial strain governs hydrogen interstitial site selection and phase stability in vanadium. Our calculations demonstrate a robust thermodynamic preference for tetrahedral (T) over octahedral (O) sites, with the energy difference modulated by lattice anisotropy through strain-tunable H 1s-V 3d orbital hybridization. Experimentally, epitaxial V films on MgO(001) exhibit a critical thickness-dependent crossover: 50 nm films show characteristic first-order alpha-beta hydride transitions, while 10 nm films display continuous solid-solution behavior with complete transition suppression. This crossover is governed by the progressive relaxation of epitaxial strain with increasing film thickness: the 10 nm films retain strong coherent strain that flattens the free-energy landscape and suppresses hydride nucleation, whereas the 50 nm films approach the strain-relaxed bulk limit where long-range elastic interactions restore first-order phase behavior. Finite-size truncation of elastic fields and interfacial electronic reconstruction further reinforce this dimensional crossover. Our work establishes a unified framework connecting atomic-scale orbital physics to mesoscopic phase thermodynamics, providing design principles for strain-engineered metal-hydride systems.

articles.title: sdos: spectral densities of large sparse Hermitian and generalized eigenproblems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: sdos is an open Python package that computes the density of states (DOS) and related spectral quantities of very large sparse Hermitian matrices A, and of generalized problems A psi = lambda B psi, from Chebyshev moments estimated with random vectors. The density is reconstructed by the kernel polynomial method (KPM, the default) or by maximum entropy (Maxent); the same interface gives band energies, Fermi levels, local and projected densities, harmonic thermodynamics, exact HOMO-LUMO gaps and eigenpairs in a spectral window. Interfaces cover electronic (empirical tight-binding, DFTB, SIESTA) and vibrational (matrix-free LAMMPS Hessians) problems. I checked most ingredients against dense diagonalization or an independent code; the exceptions are listed in Sec. V. On a workstation (4 threads, 19 GB) the DOS of an 884,736-atom amorphous silicon model (a 6³ tiling of a 4096-atom cell; 3.5 million orbitals; the orthogonal empirical tight-binding model of Kwon et al.) takes 71 s (M=100, R=2, no exact moments; 383 s with the default exact moments), and a matrix-free 2,097,152-atom crystal 10 min in 1.8 GB. A 17³ replica of a 216-atom amorphous cell (1,061,208 atoms) agrees with exact Bloch spectra: electronic DOS in 229 s, matrix-free ACE vibrational DOS in 2.2 h on one GPU. Shift-invert, incomplete-Cholesky setup, exact moments of high order and Maxent at high moment counts do not scale. The underlying methods are due to Silver, Roder, Kress, Voter, Drabold, Sankey and collaborators; the Introduction states what is added.

articles.title: Visualizing d-wave pairing symmetry at the atomic scale in a cuprate high-Tc superconductor by Josephson tunneling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconducting pairing symmetry provides crucial insight into the microscopic mechanisms of Cooper pairing. However, probing the local manifestations of sign-changing superconducting order parameters remains experimentally challenging. Here, we investigate the superconducting condensate in optimally doped (OPT) Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O10+δ (Bi-2223) using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM), equipped with an s-wave superconducting tip. Measurements at ultra-low temperatures reveal a pronounced modulation of the Josephson tunneling signal at different locations inside the crystallographic unit cell. A distinct Josephson tunneling signal is detected above O sites in the underlying CuO2 plane, whereas the signal nearly vanishes above the Cu-plaquette diagonals, including Cu sites and plaquette centers. This unique intra-unit-cell spatial pattern agrees with the theoretical prediction for the symmetry-dependent cancellation of Josephson tunneling between an s-wave superconducting tip and a d-wave superconducting sample. Our findings provide atomic-scale, real-space evidence for d-wave pairing symmetry in OPT high-Tc Bi-2223 and establish SJTM as a powerful approach for investigating the pairing symmetry of unconventional superconductors.

articles.title: Ergotropy as distance from equilibrium
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the ergotropy (a.k.a available energy) of a thermally isolated system is the 1-Wasserstein distance between two energy probability density functions. Specifically, between the energy profile of the system state, and the energy profile of its associated passive state. We prove this for both classical and quantum systems, and illustrate it with examples. Our result formalises the intuition that ergotropy is a quantifier of distance from equilibrium

articles.title: Momentum-dependent phonon effects on spin-fluctuation d-wave pairing in bulk La₆Ni₅O₁₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the effect of electron-phonon coupling on spin-fluctuation-mediated pairing in bulk La₆Ni₅O₁₂. A five-layer Hubbard model treated within the random-phase approximation yields a leading dₓ^₂₋y^₂ pairing state. Two phenomenological couplings motivated by oxygen breathing modes favor s-wave pairing when considered alone, while their attractive scattering between opposite-sign regions of the spin-fluctuation-induced gap suppresses d-wave pairing. Electronic charge screening strongly reduces this suppression. Comparing the s- and d-wave pairing strengths with and without screening shows that screening shifts their boundary in favor of d-wave pairing. Momentum-resolved projections locate the reduction of the unfavorable scattering processes. At the representative electronic interaction, d-wave pairing remains dominant.

articles.title: Coherent Control of High-Order Lightwave Currents in Gate-Tunable Bilayer Graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The sub-cycle acceleration of charge carriers in an electronic circuit by tailored terahertz (THz) electric-field waveforms, rather than conventional pulsed bias voltages, opens a transformative frontier for lightwave electronics operating far beyond the scaling limits of gigahertz electronic technologies. Yet gate-tunable coherent control of multi-order and non-perturbative currents has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate lightwave control over the amplitude, phase flips, and zero-crossings of THz field-driven high-order currents by utilizing phase-locked pairs of single-cycle THz fields in a dual-gated bilayer graphene (BLG) device. By leveraging the in-situ tuning of both bandgap and charge doping, we reveal extreme THz photocurrent rectification and sub-THz-cycle current generation that are governed by a strong field-driven crossover from interband multi-photon coherence to intraband lightwave acceleration, whose competition provides an exceptional sensitivity to the THz-pulse pair drive. Our interferometric nonlinear THz photocurrent spectroscopy of sub-cycle electronic excitations accesses and controls non-perturbative, multi-quantum photocurrents, which manifest as an extreme-order THz frequency comb. Quantum-kinetic simulations map these lightwave-controlled electron trajectories, revealing that sub-THz-cycle ballistic transport underpins gate- and THz-field-driven functionality enabled by electrostatic doping and bandgap tuning within the atomically thin device architecture. The demonstrated on-demand coherent control of nonperturbative photocurrent transport regimes can be extended to a broad range of atomically thin device architectures, opening new avenues for gate- and field-programmable logic, memory, and quantum simulators in which electronic pathways are steered on sub-cycle, petahertz timescales and atomic length scales.

articles.title: Hydrogen Thermodiffusion in Tungsten: Trapped Hydrogen Distorts Heat of Transport Estimation from Total Concentration Profiles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate hydrogen diffusion in tungsten under thermal gradients in the presence of trapping sites using multiscale simulations. Using molecular dynamics simulations, we find that the heat of transport, which quantifies the coupling between temperature gradients and hydrogen transport, for hydrogen in tungsten is positive (thermophobic) at lower temperatures but changes sign near 1000 K. We investigate the origin of the heat of transport and find that harmonic transition state theory with elastic thermal-expansion corrections is insufficient to explain the observed behaviour, consistent with either a breakdown of local thermodynamic equilibrium or non-negligible anharmonic contributions. We further extend previous studies of hydrogen thermodiffusion by including the effect of trapping sites in both simulations and analytical models. We show that when trapped hydrogen accounts for a significant fraction of the total hydrogen concentration, the heat of transport inferred from measurements of the total concentration is dominated by the temperature dependence of the trapped hydrogen population and no longer reflects the gradient in the mobile hydrogen concentration. Consequently, experimentally measured heats of transport cannot in general be used directly in continuum-scale models that explicitly account for trapping and detrapping. In such models, the heat of transport should be based on mobile hydrogen concentrations only to avoid incorporating trapping effects twice.

articles.title: Computing Classical Partition Functions via Cycle-Space Sampling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.11850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a method for computing thermodynamic properties of classical spin systems by reformulating the partition function as a sum over even subgraphs of the interaction graph. Starting from the high-temperature expansion, we show that the expansion coefficients are determined by the weight distribution of the null space of the binary incidence matrix over F₂, and that this statement holds verbatim for multi-spin interactions once the graph is replaced by a hypergraph. We introduce a Monte Carlo scheme based on the 1/t Wang-Landau algorithm that performs a random walk directly in this null space. Because the weight distribution is temperature independent, a single estimate yields the zero-field partition function, and the thermodynamic quantities obtained from its temperature derivatives, at arbitrary temperature. We validate the approach against exact finite-size results on the two-dimensional triangular-lattice Ising model, apply it to the three- and four-dimensional hypercubic Ising models where no exact solution is available, and to the two- and three-dimensional Baxter-Wu models, whose three-spin interactions place them outside the reach of Pfaffian methods. For the two-body models we compare against conventional Wang-Landau sampling in energy space; for the Baxter-Wu models we validate against exact enumeration at the smallest size in each dimension.

articles.title: Connate Topological Superconductivity and Vortex-Position-Controlled Majorana Modes in the Intergrowth Superconductor Th₂Mo₂Ir₂Si₄C
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.12080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recently synthesized intergrowth compound Th₂Mo₂Ir₂Si₄C is an experimentally established bulk superconductor whose topological electronic structure remains unexplored.
