The total cross sections show low-energy resonance features, with the strongest functional dependence around the broad peak near 0.8--1.0 eV. A sharper, higher-energy structure is also observed below 2 eV, shifting from 1.74 to 1.82 eV depending on the functional. Differential cross sections show modest functional sensitivity, with more noticeable angular differences at 7.5 and 10 eV. These results show that the DFT functional and basis set affect the target properties, with the resulting target description influencing low-energy electron-scattering observables of NO. The comparison supports ωB97X-D3/aug-cc-pVTZ geometry optimisation followed by aug-cc-pVQZ target-property calculations as a practical protocol for R-matrix modelling of NO.

articles.title: Emergent Non-Equilibrium Emission Profiles via Luminescent Angle Restriction for Photovoltaic Energy Conversion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.20783v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The detailed-balance method determines photovoltaic conversion efficiencies by relating non-equilibrium converter operation to an equilibrium reference state. Conventionally, the angular and spectral radiative channels are assumed to be defined by the equilibrium absorptivity and emissivity, with the photon chemical potential setting their occupation. The spatial distribution of emission must also be considered when radiative energy is redistributed within a complex nanophotonic converter architecture. Here we analyze this redistribution with a proposed luminescent angle restrictor, in which a flat-plate photovoltaic absorber is coupled to an overlayer with vertically aligned nanorods. The nanorod layer is nearly transparent to near-normal sunlight, while oblique photovoltaic luminescence can be absorbed, re-emitted, and partially returned to the absorber. To calculate the operating emission profile, we develop a Markov-chain transport model with an absorbing-chain formulation that enforces microscopic reversibility for local optical transitions while determining the spatially distributed steady-state emission rates. The model recovers the flat-plate detailed-balance limit and predicts voltage-dependent external emission profiles from the coupled architecture. Under idealized conditions, this non-equilibrium angular redistribution increases conversion efficiency relative to the conventional flat-plate reference. We further evaluate nanorod photoluminescence quantum yield, angular restriction, orientational disorder, and Auger recombination to identify practical constraints on the proposed architecture. These results show how detailed-balance limits for photovoltaic structures can depend on internal radiative energy redistribution and the resulting non-equilibrium emission profile, beyond what can be inferred from the macroscopic equilibrium optical response alone.

articles.title: Full 3D Maxwell solver for Inertial Electrostatic Confinement devices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.22253v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Results of a full 3D electromagnetic plasma fusion simulator are presented. It will enable investigations into the influence of structured electromagnetic potentials, anomalous magnetic moments, or charge cluster structures on the fusion yield. The simulator calculates fusion yields similar to those found in real world fusors. In addition, the ion energy and density are accurately simulated. Given that the ion properties arise from a full Maxwell solver there is ample evidence that this part of the simulation is accurate. Concluded with a recommendation for continued research.

articles.title: The NewMag crystal-field code for f-element systems: Implementation for extended active spaces, second-order correlated energies, and generalisation to fn configurations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.37541v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report a massive update of the NewMag program, which enables to extract Stevens crystal-field parameters (CFPs) after relativistic and multiconfigurational calculations are performed. The code can now post-treat ORCA and OpenMolcas outputs that contain state-average complete active space self-consistend field (SA-CASSCF) calculations with minimal or extended active spaces, second-order NEVPT2 or CASPT2 calculations, and spin-orbit configuration interaction (SOCI) calculations. Stevens parameters are extracted following the original Stevens convention with the so-called "extended" parameters. Rotation invariant indicators are also computed, after applying a correction of the parameter values to ensure normalization, following Rudowicz. At the SOCI level, the spin-orbit coupling (SOC) constant is also extracted within a spherical approximation of the SOC operator. For all the reference calculation levels, the model spectrum is reconstructed, allowing a direct assessment of its quality. The reported implementation is successfully applicable to f-element systems with a non-void, non-half-filled/empty or non-full f shell, that is for fⁿ configurations with n != 0, != 7 and != 14. Similarities and differences with the SINGLE_ANISO and AILFT codes are discussed. With selected examples, we showcase the interest of determining CFPs in f-element systems to understand their magnetic and optical properties in general, and more specifically the added value of NewMag. Finally, application of this approach to d-element systems is discussed, to reveal when it readily and successfully applies and when it may fail in reproducing satisfactorily the ab initio energies.

articles.title: Implementation and verification of a new free boundary module for Resistive Wall Modes simulations with the nonlinear 3D full MHD code SpeCyl
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13428v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Self-consistent numerical simulations of free boundary instabilities, such as resistive wall modes (RWMs) and external kink modes, require special attention given their relevance on the path towards magnetic fusion based nuclear reactors. In this work, a new implementation and a verification benchmark are presented for the nonlinear three-dimensional (3D) full magneto-hydrodynamics (MHD) code SpeCyl, which self-consistently combines a free flow 3D treatment for the edge plasma velocity with double resistive wall thin shell magnetic boundary conditions, capable of capturing the essential features of common setups in experimental devices. Two coaxial resistive shells surround the plasma. Vacuum conditions are assumed between and outside the resistive shells, whose relative positions and time constants can be varied on purpose. The implementation is extensively verified against Shafranov's analytic theory, valid for a circular cross section large aspect ratio tokamak and assuming a flat current profile. The correctness of newly implemented Boundary Conditions (BCs) is confirmed by the good agreement obtained for the linear growth rates of (m=2,n=1) RWM and external kink, over a wide range of wall positions, resistive shell time constants, and for different initial reference equilibria. The (m=2,n=1) RWM growth rates are also benchmarked against previous different RWMs modelling and successful validation studies for RFX-mod tokamak plasmas. The new BCs make SpeCyl a flexible and robust tool to investigate free boundary MHD modes in large aspect ratio magnetic confinement configurations, such as those achieved with the RFX-mod machine and expected in RFX-mod2.

articles.title: Quantum trajectory perspective of atom-field interaction in attosecond time scale
articles.abstract: arXiv:physics/0607110v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Here the ionization and high harmonic generation in Hydrogen and Helium by using quantum (hydrodynamic) trajectories is analyzed theoretically. The quantum trajectories allow a self-contained treatment of the electron exchange and correlation effects without introducing ad hoc potentials into the Schrodinger equation. Our approach predicts the correct high harmonic spectra and the attosecond pulses generated by the Helium atom beyond the single active electron approximation. It can be used to study complex multi-electron systems and their interaction with laser field of both high and low intensity.

articles.title: Time-dependent quantum Monte Carlo: preparation of the ground state
articles.abstract: arXiv:physics/0611196v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) Helium atoms using a new time-dependent quantum Monte Carlo (TDQMC) method. The TDQMC method employs random walkers, with a separate guiding wave attached to each walker. The ground state is calculated by a self-consistent solution of complex-time Schroedinger equations for the guiding waves and of equations for the velocity fields of the walkers. Our results show that the many-body wavefunction and the ground state energy of the model atoms are very close to those predicted by the standard diffusion quantum Monte Carlo method. The obtained ground state can further be used to examine correlated time-dependent processes which include, for example, interaction of atoms and molecules with external electromagnetic fields.

articles.title: Global Magnetohydrodynamic Simulations of Monster Shocks in Neutron Star Magnetospheres
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.21290v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Waves launched from the neutron star surface or inner magnetosphere propagate through the magnetosphere as small perturbations, but can grow relative to the background magnetic field and steepen into ``monster shocks'' -- ultra-relativistic magnetized shocks which can power high-energy emission. Such shocks can develop around isolated magnetars, merging binaries, and collapsing neutron stars. They occur in magnetically dominated plasma and are described by relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). We present global relativistic MHD simulations of monster shocks in unperturbed and perturbed (``wrinkled'') backgrounds with a global dipolar geometry. Our simulations confirm analytical predictions for equatorial shocks and provide new insight into the behavior of oblique shocks off the equator. Simulations where the shock is formed through Alfvén mode to fast mode conversion are also presented, demonstrating the generic nature of the monster shock mechanism. We explore how the presence of additional modes in the magnetosphere modifies the shock behavior. Modes of comparable amplitude can fragment the shock front, substantially reduce the magnetization, produce localized enhancements in the Lorentz factor relative to an unperturbed dipole background, and intermittently generate additional shocks along a line of sight.

articles.title: Operational bounds and diagnostics for coherence in energy transfer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.09748v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Excitation energy transfer in light-harvesting aggregates is highly efficient, yet whether quantum coherence plays an operational role in transport remains debated. A central challenge is that coherence is usually inferred from spectroscopic signatures, whereas transport performance is assessed through specific observables and depends on both the open system dynamics and the initial state preparation. Here we develop a resource theoretic approach that quantifies the maximum change that initial site-basis coherence can induce in a chosen readout under fixed reduced dynamics. The central quantity is the resource impact functional, which yields state independent, readout specific bounds on coherence-induced changes in signals and transport figures of merit. We apply the framework to two models. For a donor-acceptor dimer, we analyse coherence sensitivity across coupling and bath-timescale regimes and bound trapping efficiency and average transfer time in terms of the impact functional. For a multi-site chain with terminal trapping, we derive rigorous criteria that distinguish population placement from sensitivity to initial state site-basis coherence. These include upper bounds on the largest advantage over incoherent preparations, necessary delocalization requirements for achieving a prescribed improvement, and a simple pairwise sufficient condition that can be checked from local information. For quasi-local reduced dynamics, we further obtain a Lieb-Robinson-type bound that constrains when coherence prepared in a distant region can influence a localized readout at finite times. Together, these results provide operational diagnostics and rigorous bounds for benchmarking coherence effects and for identifying regimes in which they are necessarily negligible or potentially relevant in excitonic transport models.

articles.title: Kinetic magnetohydrodynamics and Landau fluid closure in relativity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.05058v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Diffuse accretion flows near a supermassive black hole are fundamentally weakly collisional. In such weakly collisional plasmas, the ion and electron distribution functions can deviate significantly from thermal equilibrium, and particle kinetic effects can influence large-scale fluid motion by driving pressure anisotropy, heat conduction, and plasma instabilities. Modeling these plasma effects in highly relativistic flows could be important for interpreting horizon-scale observations of black hole images. In this paper, we present a theoretical framework for understanding weakly collisional plasmas in general relativity by deriving the relativistic drift kinetic equations from the Vlasov-Maxwell equations. We present the evolution equations for the moments of the gyroaveraged distribution function and introduce a new analytic Landau fluid closure to capture anisotropic heat flow in relativistic plasmas. Unlike standard (collisional) general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics or extended magnetohydrodynamics, our model does not rely on strong collisions to enforce thermal equilibrium and consistently incorporates Landau damping in a fluid closure. The model introduced in this work provides a complementary approach to fully kinetic simulations in understanding weakly collisional effects in low-luminosity relativistic black hole accretion disks.

articles.title: Kerr Quasinormal Modes without Variable Separation: A Two-Dimensional Hyperboloidal Teukolsky Solver with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.19774v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to solve the gravitational quasinormal-mode (QNM) eigenvalue problem for Kerr spacetime directly in the two-dimensional hyperboloidal formulation of the Teukolsky equation. This formulation does not require separation of variables and thus retains the coupled radial--angular structure. Such a scheme provides a prototype for calculating the QNMs of beyond-Kerr black holes for which the perturbation equations are non-separable. Sequences with increasing angular momentum are constructed, reaching close to the extremal limit. We focus on the fundamental modes (ell,m,n)=(2,0,0), (2,1,0), (2,2,0), (3,3,0) and (4,4,0), together with the first two overtones (2,2,1) and (2,2,2). After training, the frequency at every spin is refined by solving the discretized equation for it, so that it depends much less on where the stochastic training happens to stop. Comparison with continued-fraction values shows that every reported real and imaginary frequency component of the production network remains below 0.23% error, with a median deviation of 2×10⁻⁴%. For the fundamental modes, both components agree within about 10⁻³% up to a/M=0.97, and the real parts within 5×10⁻⁴% at every spin. Sub-percent accuracy is maintained in the near-extremal regime, where the damping rate becomes small and the modes are longest-lived; there the damping errors grow, and the largest, 0.23%, belongs to the (2,2,1) overtone. The results establish a non-spectral numerical route to multidimensional black-hole perturbation eigenproblems which does not match the substantially higher precision of dedicated Kerr solvers but offers greater flexibility and requires less analytical pre-processing. The proposed approach is designed to be applicable to other backgrounds whose perturbation equations do not separate.

articles.title: Seifert type magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.08519v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains whose magnetic lines define an (m,n) Seifert fibration for arbitrary coprime integers m,n.

articles.title: Embedding Consistent Recurrent Neural Networks in Finite Element Simulations for Path-Dependent Damage Prediction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Capturing sheet-metal localisation physics with a trained surrogate inside a finite element (FEM) solver requires the surrogate to deliver consistent predictions irrespective of the solver's strain-increment count, which is difficult to control in non-linear explicit codes. We address this by re-implementing a trained recurrent neural network (RNN) damage criterion in Fortran and embed it as a live, increment-by-increment fracture criterion inside an Abaqus/Explicit user material subroutine (VUMAT), advancing the network state alongside the solver. Two architectures are compared: a SimpleRNN and the proposed Consistent RNN (ConsRNN), whose transition function is designed so that predictions converge as the strain path is refined rather than drifting with the increment count. Both are trained on bilinear strain paths and evaluated under varying temporal discretisations and nonlinear histories. SimpleRNN predictions drift as the increment count increases, which disqualifies it for embedding; ConsRNN converges under refinement, at a substantial fixed-resolution accuracy cost relative to SimpleRNN on multilinear paths. Deployed at structural scale, the embedded ConsRNN surrogate governs element deletion in a clamped steel plate and reaches the same peak force and peak displacement as an established two-parameter fracture criterion. This pre-peak agreement is expected by construction, since no element is deleted before the peak and the two runs therefore share an identical constitutive path; the responses diverge only on the post-peak softening branch. The results establish discretisation consistency as the decisive property for embedding recurrent surrogates in explicit FEM solvers, and report the first embedding of a customised, non-standard-transition recurrent cell at structural scale.

articles.title: Adaptive Depth Aggregation in Graph Transformers for Long-Range Graph Reasoning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08500v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Graph Transformers improve long-range node-to-node communication through global or structure-aware interactions. However, improving cross-node communication does not determine how computations produced at different depths should be combined. Standard residual streams accumulate successive computations with fixed unit coefficients shared across nodes. This fixed aggregation is a residual-interface constraint: once intermediate contributions have been produced, the interface cannot explicitly reweight them by node. We hypothesize that this constraint can create a depth-wise aggregation mismatch when the relative utility of these intermediate contributions varies across nodes and structural contexts. To study this hypothesis, we formalize Graph Transformer residual computation as a causal node-wise history of graph-propagation and feed-forward network (FFN) contributions, making depth aggregation an explicit interface choice. We realize node-adaptive aggregation over this history with Attention Residuals (AttnRes) while preserving the backbone's graph-propagation and auxiliary-state machinery. Block AttnRes reduces the routing cost of long histories relative to Full AttnRes by pooling consecutive contributions. We instantiate the interface in GPS and GRIT and evaluate it on all five ECHO tasks. Both variants achieve lower mean absolute error (MAE) than their independently tuned backbones on every task, and at least one obtains the lowest mean among all compared methods in each task. Routing-only donor-swap interventions support the mismatch hypothesis, while additional ablations examine the key design choices. Together, these results support node-adaptive depth aggregation as a useful complement to cross-node communication in long-range graph reasoning.

articles.title: Emergent Low-Dimensional Topological Dynamics Dictate Generalization and Escape Mechanics in Billion-Parameter Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The remarkable generalization of modern over-parameterized neural networks defies classical statistical learning bounds. Here we establish that optimization trajectories in billion-parameter models do not sample the ambient dimension R^N homogeneously; instead, they are dynamically constrained to a low-dimensional execution submanifold Mₑₓₑc (with empirically observed effective dimension dₑff le 12). By equipping the parameter space with a regularized Hessian metric gᵢⱼ = nablaᵢ nablaⱼ L + ϵ δᵢⱼ and analyzing stochastic Langevin diffusion on loss sublevel sets, we derive a rigorous Topological Generalization Bound grounded in projected subspace persistent homology. Furthermore, by linking Morse index transitions to Betti number annihilation (β₁ → 0), we formulate an exact mathematical mechanism for exponential escape from strict saddles under anisotropic noise. We validate our framework across 80+ architectures (ResNets, Vision Transformers, and 7B LLMs). To bridge theoretical topology with computational feasibility, we resolve the curse of dimensionality by computing projected persistent homology proxies via randomized Lanczos iterations restricted strictly within active Hessian subspaces. Building upon this mathematical foundation, we introduce Topological-Adaptive Optimization (Top-SGD and Top-AdamW)---a family of wrapper algorithms that dynamically modulate learning rates using active curvature signatures. Extensive benchmarks demonstrate a 14.1% reduction in total wall-clock training time on ImageNet with all computational and memory overheads fully accounted for. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/imslab-research/Topological-SGD.

articles.title: Minimum-Sufficient Knowledge and Computation for Wind Energy Predictive Analysis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resource-constrained cyber-physical decision systems often apply fixed sensing, knowledge, and computational pipelines despite state-dependent information needs. We introduce Minimum-Sufficient Knowledge and Computation (MSKC), a resource-aware computing principle: select the least-costly route meeting decision-risk and deployment constraints, escalating only when cheaper routes are insufficient. As proof of concept, we isolate adaptive knowledge routing, the decision underlying Knowledge-Guided Machine Learning (KGML), which conventionally injects external knowledge unconditionally rather than only where needed. We instantiate this for wind ramp-event predictive analysis, an edge-oriented decision-support task, evaluating local, relational, and physics-informed routes with a state-aware gate on publicly available real data from two wind farms. We establish conditions for feasibility preservation, cost dominance, and strict expected savings over always-on routing. At a 35.9% relational-knowledge injection rate, adaptive routing is statistically indistinguishable from always-on injection on the reported metrics while reducing knowledge calls by 64%, supporting sustainable, Green-IT-aligned deployment. These results support MSKC's premise that uniformly maximal intelligence is unnecessary. This offers intelligent data analysis for big data streams: the analysis itself decides, per state, how much knowledge and computation the data warrant.

articles.title: PINNeval: A Comprehensive Evaluation Standard for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) literature has produced a rapidly expanding catalogue of methods. We divide a PINN training pipeline systematically into four components and observe that many existing benchmarks study these components in isolation. These components are domain-importance adaptation, loss balancing, neural network architecture, and optimization scheme. Moreover, the studies set the surrounding and not considered components of the pipeline to a minimal default that is no longer representative of current best practice approaches. Conclusions drawn under such conditions may not transfer to competitive pipelines. In this work, we propose a new evaluation protocol that (1) treats the four components as an integrated system; (2) crucially requires competitive implementations of the components not under investigation; (3) specifies the metrics and reporting format; and (4) is accompanied by structured documentation that ensures the traceability of evaluations across studies. Based on this comprehensive protocol, we release PINNpipe, an innovative JAX package containing 18 different methods from the current literature as well as nine efficiently implemented benchmark problems. Using PINNpipe, we illustrate our evaluation protocol in relation to established benchmark studies and report results that challenge common assumptions.

articles.title: TopoSHAP: Shapley for Explainable and Efficient Topological Deep Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08789v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological deep learning (TDL) extends learning on graphs, such as molecules or social networks, to higher-order structures, such as rings in a molecule or groups in a social network. Explaining which of these structures drive a model's predictions, and which architectural components matter most for its performance, remains challenging. We introduce TopoSHAP, an efficient and general explanation framework that addresses both questions across topological domains and model architectures. TopoSHAP-cell assigns Shapley values to topological data cells and extracts compact explanations. These explanations match or outperform graph-based counterparts on GraphXAI benchmark data while running up to 112× faster. They also reveal advantageous topological feature design, leading to measured improvements in explanation recovery and predictive accuracy. On the architecture side, TopoSHAP-neighbor explains how neighborhoods contribute to model performance, and turns these evaluations into a backward-elimination search that identifies smaller, competitive architectures early in training. This is up to 11.3× cheaper than traditional TDL training sweeps.

articles.title: Global Solar Siting from Geospatial Embeddings
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Global solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity is rapidly growing, helping decrease our emissions and dependence on fossil fuels. However, optimally siting a solar plant remains challenging, requiring anticipation of geographical, urban, and infrastructure needs. Current methods rely on multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) using hand-picked geophysical layers and solar-resource products, however these strategies are not geographically transferable and do not capture the practical requirements of solar sites. We use geospatial embeddings, dense vectors representing geophysical properties of a location, to analyse 38,591 existing solar sites and the land they were built on to learn the latent solar suitability signal. We assess a set of linear and non-linear models and select a soft-voting ensemble of a random forest and a multilayer perceptron (RF+MLP ensemble), chosen for accuracy and large scale deployability. Validated against future installations in thirteen countries, the ensemble separates existing solar sites from random land with a median ROC-AUC of 0.90. Compared with published MCDA strategies, the ensemble increases ROC-AUC by 0.06-0.30 in every country. The ranking also concentrates real deployment: the most-suitable 20% of land holds 84% of estimated generation (annual energy yield) and 67% of installed capacity (potential power output). After applying standard siting constraints, 5.6% of global land (9.8% if cropland is permitted) remains highly suited to solar. The global 10 m resolution solar suitability dataset and code can be found here: https://github.com/Abdullahr29/Global-Solar-Siting.

articles.title: SSF-Net: A Spatial-Spectral Fusion Network for Accurate PDE Operator Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning methods for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) significantly improve computational efficiency over traditional numerical solvers such as finite element method (FEM). However, PDE dynamics inherently span both local and global dynamics: disturbances propagate and decay gradually through the domain, while global coupling effects can influence the whole system simultaneously. Capturing both types of dynamics with a low complexity model remains a key challenge. To address this, we propose the Spatial-Spectral Fusion Network (SSF-Net), built around a dual-branch Spatial-Spectral Fusion (SSF) block comprising a spatial branch and a spectral branch. The spatial branch employs a multi-directional Mamba, which mitigates its inherent causal, single-direction scanning bias and capture local interactions with reduced directional bias at linear complexity. The spectral branch leverages a Fourier transform with a block-diagonal MLP to efficiently capture global spectral features with reduced parameter count and complexity. The SSF block is embedded in a multiresolution convolutional encoder-decoder, which extracts multi-scale features. We evaluate SSF-Net on a comprehensive PDE benchmark spanning multiple task types and assess its long-horizon stability. Compared with attention-based and convolution-based baselines, SSF-Net achieves lower prediction error with fewer parameters while retaining near-linear asymptotic complexity in the number of spatial tokens.

articles.title: Calibrated Uncertainty Quantification on TDC ADMET: What Can Be Resolved Across 22 Datasets?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) models often rely on small, heterogeneous datasets, yet their predictions may determine which compounds proceed to experimental testing. Useful evaluations must therefore assess both predictive performance and the quality of reported probabilities or intervals. We ask which common uncertainty-quantification methods perform best on the 22 Therapeutics Data Commons (TDC) ADMET datasets and what this benchmark can resolve. We compare eleven calibrated pipelines using nested five-fold cross-validation across ten chemical partitions and five model seeds. Ensemble Monte Carlo (MC) dropout has the best average rank for TDC performance, Brier score, and 90% interval score. For TDC performance, however, it is not separated from the other ensemble pipelines; for Brier and interval score, LightGBM is also not ruled out as best. LightGBM wins more individual datasets than any other method for TDC performance and Brier score, but performs poorly on several endpoints. Smaller evaluations can identify a different leader and often fail to recover the broader comparison. These results make LightGBM and an ensemble neural model complementary baselines. Comparative claims should be checked across multiple chemical partitions using statistical analyses matched to the question being asked.

articles.title: One Run Is Not Enough: A Monte Carlo Protocol for Evaluating LLM Reliability on Data Science Tasks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for automating data science workflows. Benchmarks such as DataSciBench (2026) and StatQA (2024) have advanced the evaluation of their capabilities across data science and statistical tasks. Assessing their reliability requires examining both the quality of their responses and their consistency across repeated runs, task types, and difficulty levels. With this aim, we introduce DS-QA, a benchmark comprising 100 data science and statistics questions drawn from UK university courses, spanning 16 datasets and three difficulty levels. We develop a three-layer evaluation framework that combines general response properties (runtime, verbosity and text similarity), coarse-grained metrics (accuracy, code executability and completeness), and task-specific metrics. We evaluate OpenAI models using a Monte Carlo protocol with 100 repeated runs. The results reveal substantial variability in responses to data visualisation and supervised learning tasks, particularly at medium and hard difficulty levels, highlighting the importance of evaluating consistency alongside response quality. We also find that an increase of 0.1 in the word verbosity ratio corresponds to an increase of about 0.013 in the token verbosity ratio.

articles.title: Beyond the Lower-Star Filtration: Alternative Filtration Methods for Persistent Homology
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08833v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the lower-star filtration (LSF), simplices are assigned filtration values according to the maximum-vertex rule, with each simplex entering the filtration when its highest-valued vertex appears. A limitation of this construction is that some higher-dimensional simplices may enter simultaneously with their boundary faces, causing certain topological features to be filled immediately upon formation and thus not appear in the resulting persistence diagram. To address this limitation, we propose three alternative filtration methods: the (ε)-lower-star filtration (ELSF), the (Lₚ) filtration (LpF), and the softmax filtration (SMF). {ELSF introduces a dimension-dependent delay to the maximum-vertex rule,} allowing higher-dimensional simplices to enter the filtration after their boundary faces, whereas {LpF and SMF use aggregation functions that depend on all vertex values rather} than solely on their maximum. By modifying how filtration values are assigned, these methods allow simplices to enter the filtration more progressively, so that topological features such as loops and voids may persist over longer filtration intervals rather than being filled immediately. Consequently, the resulting persistence diagrams may include persistence features that are not observed under LSF, potentially providing useful information for distinguishing data populations. Experimental results on simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed filtration methods are computationally efficient and can provide greater sensitivity to structural differences in the data than LSF.

articles.title: Task-Contribution Dynamics of Adam in Physics-Informed Neural Networks: Slow-Manifold Analysis and Gradient Modulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08910v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often suffer from imbalanced optimization of competing loss components, particularly when approximating solutions with high-frequency or multiscale features. Although existing balancing strategies have proven effective in alleviating this difficulty, the mechanisms governing the evolution of individual task contributions to Adam's parameter updates remain insufficiently understood. We introduce task-wise indicators to characterize this evolution and identify three distinct training regimes: smooth variation, intermittent spikes, and persistent oscillations. Focusing on the early smooth regime, we combine discrete-time analysis with a continuous-time singular perturbation framework under the full-batch setting and the parameter regime (1-β₂)/(1-β₁)ll1. A first-order approximation of the locally attracting slow manifold reveals two factors governing the step-to-step redistribution of task contributions: curvature-related alignment disparities and differences in the coordinatewise distributions of preconditioned task gradients. Both factors involve Adam's shared second-moment estimate. Inspired by AdaTask, we propose Gradient-Modulated Adam (GMAdam), which modulates incoming task gradients using task-specific second-moment estimates. Numerical experiments on high-frequency Poisson and wave equations, the Allen-Cahn equation, and two-dimensional lid-driven cavity flow (Re=100,400) demonstrate consistent improvements in predictive accuracy over AdaTask at comparable computational cost.

articles.title: Equidistribution of Solution Gradients in Physics-Informed Neural Networks via Coordinate Transformations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09053v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) often struggle to approximate solutions with sharp gradients due to optimization difficulties and spectral bias. Motivated by the principle of gradient equidistribution from the stretching approach in grid generation, which redistributes solution gradients to reduce functional complexity, we propose Coordinate Transformation PINNs (CTPINNs), which incorporate learnable coordinate transformations to map the physical domain into a computational domain where the physical solutions become approximately affine, making them easier for neural networks to learn. We propose two constructions of the transformation: an explicit construction based on Majorants and an implicit construction based on invertable neural networks. Experimentally, the explicit construction can improve accuracy for PDEs with available explicit coordinate transformations, and the implicit construction can be combined with other advanced PINN models as an efficient plug-in module to improve performance across a range of challenging PDE benchmarks.

articles.title: CoMoFlow: Controllable Protein Conformational Ensemble Generation via Explicit Collective-Mode Modeling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09548v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Protein conformational ensemble generation aims to efficiently characterize the structural variations accessible to a protein beyond a single static structure. Recent flow-based methods efficiently generate conformational ensembles, but they model coordinated structural variation implicitly, which can limit ensemble fidelity and hinder direct control. To address this limitation, we propose CoMoFlow, a controllable framework for generating protein backbone conformational ensembles by explicitly modeling collective variation. CoMoFlow constructs protein-specific collective modes from the equilibrium structure, learns the distribution of their coefficients across the molecular dynamics (MD) ensemble, and uses sampled collective variations to guide SE(3) flow matching through feature conditioning and prior recentering. Experiments on ATLAS and de novo proteins show that CoMoFlow improves reconstruction of MD conformational distributions and coordinated structural variation relative to strong flow-based baselines, while enabling direct control over targeted conformational changes.

articles.title: Action-BED: Task-Driven Bayesian Experimental Design with Singly Intractable Objectives
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.23662v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bayesian experimental design (BED) has traditionally been based on maximising expected uncertainty reductions from prior to posterior. A major shortfall of this approach is that it leads to doubly intractable objectives that are difficult to optimise, while customising them to particular downstream tasks of interest can also be difficult. Following first principles decision theory, we demonstrate that BED can alternatively be formulated in terms of an expected future loss (EFL) on downstream actions, providing a simple and naturally task-driven framework. Critically, we then show that all such EFLs can be rearranged into singly intractable objectives that can be jointly optimised with respect to both the design policy and a downstream action policy using stochastic gradients, an approach we refer to as ACTION-BED. This formulation further sidesteps the need for any explicit posterior or marginal likelihood estimation and is naturally implicit, requiring only the ability to sample from the joint model over model parameters and data, and evaluate the downstream loss function. It thus allows design policies to be learned more effectively, efficiently, and simply than existing methods, while providing easy customisation to different downstream tasks and losses.

articles.title: PhyCAD: Physics-Aware Text-to-CAD Generation via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language-driven computer-aided design (CAD) generation enables the creation of editable parametric models from text, yet geometric correctness alone does not ensure physical feasibility. We present PhyCAD, a framework for physics-aware Text-to-CAD generation that trains language models to produce executable CadQuery programs under geometric and physical constraints. To support this setting, we construct a Text-to-CAD dataset that links parametric CAD models with geometric specifications, loading conditions, and physical constraints. We further develop an automated CAD--CAE verifier that combines program execution, geometric checks, and finite element analysis to provide feedback for model training. A key learning challenge is to prioritize joint satisfaction of geometric and physical constraints while retaining informative feedback on partial progress. A flat aggregation of heterogeneous rewards can obscure this priority, allowing improvements in individual criteria to compensate for unmet design requirements. We therefore introduce a Hierarchical Balanced Advantage for Group Relative Policy Optimization, grouping candidates into levels according to their verification status and combining between-level progress with objective-wise peer ranking within each level. This formulation preserves cross-level priority in the training signal while providing fine-grained feedback for satisfying constraints and improving feasible designs. Experiments across multiple language models show that PhyCAD consistently improves joint geometric and physical constraint satisfaction. These results demonstrate the value of verifiable engineering feedback for advancing language-driven CAD generation beyond geometric reconstruction toward physics-aware design.

articles.title: MIRA: Mitigating Pole Geometry Bias in Recurrent Language Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the Transformer's recurrent successors --- such as selective state-space models (SSMs), Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV), and Retentive Network (RetNet) --- can be characterized as infinite-impulse-response (IIR) systems. The zero--pole geometries of these IIR systems characterize the temporal modes they can represent. However, to trade parallelism, the algebraic structures of the parameterizations of these recurrent systems often give rise to poles constrained to the real axis, thereby inducing an architectural bias in their recurrent dynamics. To unify these recurrent architectures and eliminate their pole geometry bias, inspired by the lattice--ladder realization of general IIR systems, we present textscMira (Modal IIR Recurrent Architecture), a unified family of linear-time recurrent architectures for building large language models (LLMs) with a highly parallel algebraic structure. Each textscMira block realizes a higher-order IIR system that represents temporal modes from token streams through a lattice--ladder structure, followed by a feed-forward network (FFN). This realization enables the model to represent the temporal modes associated with both real and complex-conjugate poles. We pretrain textscMira-S, a 12-layer small-scale LLM with 0.14B parameters composed entirely of textscMira blocks. Throughout the pretraining, textscMira-S achieves lower perplexity than strong recurrent baselines, exhibits stronger context-window generalization beyond the training length, and attains higher throughput with a dedicated CUDA kernel.

articles.title: LEMMO: A Large Electromagnetic Model leveraging Pretrained LLMs for Million-Sample Signal Understanding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models have expanded beyond text to vision, audio, and other modalities, but understanding raw electromagnetic (EM) signals remains challenging. Wideband recordings can contain millions of samples, whereas existing waveform-based EM models are primarily evaluated on short in-phase and quadrature (IQ) segments, leaving long-recording understanding and detailed description insufficiently explored. We introduce LEMMO, a large EM model for instruction-driven recognition and description of long raw IQ recordings. LEMMO combines a linear-attention EM encoder with anti-aliased temporal resampling to process up to eight million complex samples. Its EM-text interaction module conditions learnable queries on instructions before retrieving signal evidence. Compact queries support recognition, while structured queries with auxiliary factual supervision organize scene-level properties, signal attributes, and cross-signal relationships for detailed description. We also construct and release a unified 1.38-TB corpus of real-world and synthetic EM signals, including LEMMO-ShortQA and LEMMO-LongDesc. Compared with MERLIN-LoRA, LEMMO improves mean EM-Bench perception accuracy by 15.77 %, mean strategy-generation ROUGE-L F1 by 4.38 points, and mean LEMMO-ShortQA accuracy by 14.31 %. It also improves categorical and numerical fact F1 on both LEMMO-LongDesc tasks while preserving its language backbone's MMLU performance. Our code and datasets are available at https://github.com/N1rv4n4/LEMMO and https://huggingface.co/datasets/DaftJun/RFLAS, respectively.

articles.title: A Physics-Informed Learning Framework for Linking Microscopic Surface Degradation to Bolted Joint Functional Behavior
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Returned products in circular engineering often have heterogeneous degradation histories, making remaining function difficult to assess. For bolted joints, corrosion alters surface morphology, contact, friction, preload retention, and mechanical response. This paper presents a physics-informed multimodal framework for linking microscopic and camera-based degradation observations to functional indicators of corroded bolted joints. The workflow defines the corrosion failure mode, generates synchronized inspection and functional-response records, preprocesses image, roughness, exposure, and joint descriptors, aligns microscopy and camera observations through similarity learning, and constructs a calibrated corrosion-severity field. Partial differential equation (PDE) discovery is applied to this field to identify candidate effective mesoscale laws rather than complete electrochemical mechanisms. The corrosion-evolution model is coupled to a separate functional model, with friction coefficient as the primary target and preload loss included when clamp-force data are available. The contribution is a reproducible pathway for physically constrained assessment of degraded bolted-joint behavior.

articles.title: MorphSched: Workload-Aware Adaptive Scheduler Generation for Linux
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08509v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern Linux scheduling increasingly requires workload-specific policies to meet the dynamic performance needs of heterogeneous applications. The recent sched_ext framework enables custom BPF schedulers, but building practical policies still requires coordinating Rust user-space control logic, BPF scheduling callbacks, generated user-kernel interfaces, and strict eBPF verifier constraints. This paper presents MorphSched, an LLM-driven system for synthesizing complete Rust+BPF sched_ext schedulers. MorphSched profiles target workloads under Linux EEVDF to construct dynamic, workload-specific optimization objectives, and uses a scaffold-constrained generation pipeline to translate scheduling intent into deployable scheduler implementations. To improve synthesis reliability, MorphSched separates implementation repair from strategy search: verifier, build, and runtime failures are handled through a DAG-structured repair process, while performance feedback is accumulated in an evolutionary memory pool to refine high-level scheduling strategies across iterations. We evaluate MorphSched across 120 machine/workload/interferer configurations on a real Linux kernel. The generated schedulers compile, pass eBPF verification, load successfully, and remain stable throughout our benchmark runs without manual edits to generated scheduler source code. Across these configurations, MorphSched improves the primary foreground metric over EEVDF by 26.5% on average and up to 87.3%. In selected comparisons, the generated schedulers are also competitive with representative hand-written sched_ext schedulers. These results show that scaffold-constrained, system-grounded LLM generation can be a practical tool for exploring workload-specific Linux scheduling policies.

articles.title: Evaluation of passive radio sounding of icy moons based on a radar equation
articles.abstract: Passive radar sounding is one of the ways to observe surfaces and subsurfaces of planetary objects through reflection of natural radio emissions. Using observations of Radio and Plasma Investigations (RPWI) aboard Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (JUICE), we have a plan to apply this technique to observe Jovian auroral radiation reflected on icy moons. For feasibility studies, we derived an expanded radar equation for planetary radio waves reflected on the moon’s surface, including the loss due to the moon’s spherical shape and scattering by surface roughness. Using this equation, we estimated the power and polarization characteristics of reflected radio emissions in two cases; terrestrial auroral kilometric radiation (AKR) reflected on the lunar surface and Jovian Hectometric radiation (HOM) reflected on the Ganymede surface. We showed the quantitative feasibility of the observation capability and potential of polarization measurements for detecting the permittivity of a surface. Additionally, we compared the estimation of the lunar case with a real case of AKR reflection observed using Lunar Radar Sounder (LRS) aboard Kaguya. The observed power ratio of reflected AKR to incident one was 2–5%, estimated from the interference fringe in the observed frequency-time diagram. This observed value agreed with the estimation from our radar equation.

articles.title: A 14,400-Year Sediment and Pollen Record of Lake Erie Limnological Response to Lake Level, Lake Connectivity, and Climate
articles.abstract: Lake Erie, the southernmost of the Laurentian Great Lakes, experienced major changes in climate, hydrology, and basin configuration from Late Glacial through Holocene time. We present a new ~ 14.4-thousand-year (~ 14.4 ka) sediment record for a central basin core constrained by radiocarbon and paleomagnetic secular variation ages, with pollen stratigraphy independently verifying the age model where radiocarbon ages are reversed. Five phases characterize the record: 1) low inorganic carbon (IC) from ~ 14.4–11.5 cal ka BP; 2) increasing IC after 11.5 cal ka BP, followed by pollen changes across an unconformity spanning 10.0–8.1 cal ka BP; 3) relatively high IC from 8.1 cal ka BP until 4) three stepwise decreases in IC and an increase in organic carbon (OC) between 5.3–3.5 cal ka BP; and 5) near zero IC from 3.5 cal ka BP to Present, with OC and pollen changes after ~ 2.3 cal ka BP. Comparison with a second central-basin core and lake level reconstructions indicates that climate, hydrologic connectivity, and lake level influenced sedimentary carbonate accumulation and contributed to the formation of an unconformity, a shift in the depocenter, and a mass slide.

articles.title: Electronic Bands and Altermagnetic State Modulation in a Se-Rich In₂Se₄/Cr₂SeO Heterostructure
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures provide a versatile platform for engineering electronic properties through interfacial charge redistribution and orbital hybridization. In this work, a Se-rich-designated In₂Se₄/Cr₂SeO vdW heterostructure is proposed and investigated using density functional theory. The In₂Se₄ layer serves as an electronically active interface in which the enhanced selenium sublattice provides Se-p states capable of interacting with the Cr-3d-derived states of an altermagnetic Cr₂SeO. A 1×1×1 In₂Se₄ monolayer and a strained (tensile in x and compressive in y) 1×2×1 Cr₂SeO cell were used to construct a supercell. The structural stability of the heterostructure is first evaluated through relaxation. The electronic properties are then characterized using spin-resolved band structures, projected density of states, orbital-resolved electronic states, and spatial charge density. The calculations reveal that interlayer coupling substantially modifies the electronic states near the Fermi level while retaining the characteristic spin-dependent structure of the Cr₂SeO layer. Overall, the heterostructure exhibits momentum-dependent semi-metallic/semiconducting behavior with strongly spin-selective local gaps. Se displacement in the In₂Se₄ monolayer acts as a symmetry and electrostatic control parameter that modifies the spin channels differently at different k-points. The resulting momentum-selective modification of Cr-derived states demonstrates the potential of Se-rich chalcogenide interfaces for tailoring the electronic structure of two-dimensional altermagnets. These findings suggest this heterostructure as a promising platform for investigating interfacial spin-dependent phenomena, provide insight into low-dimensional magnetic materials, and provide a theoretical foundation for nanoscale spintronic applications.

articles.title: Synthesis of Nb(V) Based MOFs with Benzene-1,3,5-Tricarboxylate As a Catalyst For The Catalytic Transfer Hydrogenation of Furfural to 1,5- Pentanediol: Preliminary Studies
articles.abstract: The conversion of biomass into high value-added chemicals has attracted considerable attention as a promising strategy for the development of sustainable energy and materials. Among various biomass-derived platform molecules, furfural is considered a potential feedstock for production of 1,5-Pentanediol via catalytic transfer hydrogenation (CTH). This study investigated the preliminary studies of effects of the synthetic method of Nb-based MOF under solvothermal condition (with and without the presence of modulator) on the physicochemical properties of the materials and catalytic performance toward CTH reaction of furfural to 1,5-Pentanediol. Nb-BTC based MOF were successfully synthesized using NbCl5 as the metal precursor and benzene-1,3,5-tricarboxylate (BTC) as the organic linker. The synthesized materials were characterized by Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR), X-ray Diffraction (XRD), Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy-Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (FESEM-EDX), Surface Area Analyzer (SAA), and Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA). The catalytic performance of Nb-BTC based MOF was evaluated in the physicochemical properties of the material. The catalytic performance of Nb-BTC based MOF was evaluated in the CTH of furfural using isopropanol as the hydrogenation donor in a batch reactor at 120°C and 5 bar of N2 pressure for 4 hours. The catalytic evaluation revealed that the Nb-BTC synthesized via solvothermal with modulator exhibited superior catalytic activity, promoting the selective conversion of furfural toward the formation of 1,5-pentanediol up to 68%. The findings demonstrate that the incorporation of a modulator plays a crucial role in tailoring the catalytic activity of Nb-BTC based MOF catalyst.

articles.title: Chiral-angle-selected spin splitting and spin-polarized conduction in nanotubes rolled from d-wave altermagnets
articles.abstract: Altermagnets combine compensated collinear magnetic order withmomentum-dependent spin splitting, promising spin-polarized currentswithout stray fields. In two-dimensional (2D) d-wave altermagnets,however, this splitting changes sign between orthogonal directions andvanishes along nodal ones, so the spin polarization of a current dependson its direction relative to the crystal axes, and exploiting it requirescurrents aligned with specific crystallographic directions. Here we showthat rolling a d-wave altermagnet into a nanotube fixes this directionstructurally: although rolling removes the parent C4Tsymmetry, the inherited splitting survives through zone folding as aselection rule set by the chiral angle. Tight-binding, symmetry, andfirst-principles analyses of symmetric and Janus nanotubes show thatantinodal nanotubes are spin split, whereas the nodal nanotube remainsexactly spin degenerate owing to a surviving mirror symmetry combinedwith spin reversal. In V2O nanotubes, the ballistic transmissionpolarization decreases from 39% for the antinodal nanotube to zerofor the nodal one at comparable total transmission. Our results identifynanotubes rolled from altermagnets as geometry-selected spin channels fornanoscale spintronics.

articles.title: Ringdown and greybody signatures of rational regular black holes in non-polynomial gravity
articles.abstract: Dated: September 25, 2026) We study the quasinormal mode spectrum and wave-scattering properties of the four-dimensional rational regular black hole recently obtained in non-polynomial (quasi-topological) gravity. Using third-order WKB together with two independent cross-checks a Frobenius–Riccati shooting method and a time-domain evolution we compute the fundamental scalar, electromagnetic, and ax-ial gravitational-type quasinormal frequencies, validating our approach against known Schwarzschild results. We find that as the geometry approaches extremality, its dimensionless ringing frequency is systematically suppressed relative to the Schwarzschild value, a direct and quantifiable imprint of the non-polynomial regularization that we trace, via the photon-sphere correspondence, to the response of the effective potential near the horizon. A Fisher-matrix estimate indicates that this suppression could in principle be resolved by a space-based detector such as LISA for a sufficiently massive and nearby source. We further compute, for the first time, the axial gravitational-type ringdown spectrum of this geometry using the Regge–Wheeler master equation, while noting that a full stability analysis of the underlying gravity theory remains an open problem requiring the linearized field equations of the modified action. Finally, we examine the greybody transmission factors across spins s = 0, 1, 2 and show that they follow the same systematic ordering and near-extremal enhancement as the ringing-frequency suppression, pointing to a common physical origin. Together, these results give one of the first quantitative characterizations of the observational signatures and the remaining open theoretical questions of a regular black hole in modified gravity.

articles.title: Automated cross-layer metamodeling for secure digital twins: attack detectability by construction
articles.abstract: This paper presents an automated model-driven engineering approach for constructing secure digital twins of cyber-physical systems. The core contribution is a cross-layer metamodel that represents physical assets, information flows, AI analytics, optimization services and cyber threats as typed, interrelated software artifacts within one conformance-checked structure. A conforming model is instantiated as an executable digital twin, so security rules can access not only measured values but also information-layer properties such as packet sequence, timestamp and integrity metadata. The approach is evaluated through a smart-grid digital twin with photovoltaic generation, battery storage, residential demand and electric-vehicle charging, using eleven years of ERA5-Land data (2015--2025). The executable services combine multi-horizon neural forecasting, linear-programming dispatch and cross-layer anomaly detection. Forecasting achieves 6.8--10.6% normalized RMSE and the dispatch reaches a 45% renewable fraction. Under staged false-data-injection, denial-of-service and replay attacks, the value-only detector attains 0.92 ROC-AUC but detects no replay attacks, whereas the metamodel-enabled information-integrity check raises replay detection to 100% and recovers about 81% of the attack-induced operating cost. The results show that explicit cross-layer software models can make classes of cyber manipulation detectable by construction that remain invisible to value-space monitoring alone.

articles.title: Characterizing Severe Geomagnetic Storms and Their Magnetospheric Drivers in Solar Cycle 23 & 24
articles.abstract: This study presents a systematic statistical analysis of the interplanetary drivers of severe geomagnetic storms (Dst ≤ -150 nT) over Solar Cycles 23 and 24. Utilizing OMNI plasma and magnetic field data, we investigate the relationship between storm intensity, key solar wind parameters (IMF B, Bz, Vsw, Nsw, Tsw), and solar activity proxies (SSN, F10.7). Our analysis confirms that all severe storms were unequivocally associated with prolonged intervals of southward IMF-Bz, affirming magnetic reconnection as the primary trigger mechanism. We find that the majority of events (~ 75%) are driven by four distinct structures: magnetic clouds (MC) and sheath fields (Sh) are the most prevalent, each responsible for 30.4% of storms, followed by combined sheath-MC structures (Sh + MC, 17.4%) and non-cloud ICMEs (17.4%). The occurrence and dominance of these drivers exhibit a strong solar cycle dependence: sheath fields and MCs prevail during the rising phase, sheath dominance peaks at solar maximum, while MCs, sheaths, and corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are the main drivers in the declining phase. Correlation analysis reveals a dominant control exerted by the peak parameters of the Interplanetary Magnetic Field (IMF), specifically the total magnetic field magnitude (B peak, CC = 0.65) and its crucial north-south component (Bz peak, CC = 0.60). These strong positive correlations highlight the direct and immediate influence of the IMF structure on storm severity. Moderate and weak relationships were observed with other solar wind parameters, including temperature (CC = -0.50) and density (CC = -0.19). Crucially, despite their fundamental role in the space environment, proxies for overall solar activity, such as the F10.7 radio flux (CC = -0.36) and sunspot number R (CC = -0.23), exhibit significantly weaker correlations with Dst peak. In stark contrast, however, geomagnetic activity indices like Kp (CC = -0.70) and Ap (CC = -0.74) show a strong negative correlation, reflecting their nature as results of the same storm phenomenon rather than its direct cause. Collectively, these findings underscore that while solar activity modulates the frequency of space weather events, the inherent physical properties of the interplanetary structures, especially the intensity and duration of southward Bz, are the most direct and potent determinants of severe geomagnetic storm intensity.

articles.title: Quantum utility routing in continuous-variable QKD networks with trusted and untrusted relays
articles.abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) networks require routing strategies that account simultaneously for secret key generation, relay trust and finite network resources. We introduce Quantum Utility Routing (QUR), a weighted routing framework for networks combining trusted point-to-point links with untrusted CV Bell measurement relays. Transition level composable finite size secret key rates (SKRs) are incorporated directly into the route search, allowing QUR to balance bottleneck SKR against route geometry and resource use. We consider graph optimized QUR (QURgo) and a fixed weight implementation (QURfw) that uses machine learning to avoid repeated graph specific weight optimization, and benchmark both against A* and Max-Min routing. At the default network configuration, QURgo and QURfw improve the mean path SKR relative to A* while requiring substantially fewer network resources than Max-Min. The framework also maintains secure connectivity over a broad range of trusted node availability by exploiting untrusted infrastructure as measurement relays. These results demonstrate that routing in CV-QKD networks can be treated as a configurable trade off between cryptographic performance and network resource consumption.

articles.title: Cutting force component in dry rough milling of AZ91D magnesium alloy using tools with different helix angles
articles.abstract: The study investigates the normal to the feed force component of the total cutting force in dry rough end down-milling of AZ91D magnesium alloy. The overall goal of this work is to investigate the dependence of this cutting force component on the milling parameters (particularly high cutting speeds – high-speed milling). An interesting aspect of this study pertains to the impact of end mill geometry (e.g. different helix angles) on machining effects. The study also involves capturing and analyzing the component’s signal in the time domain first, and then assessing its dynamics in the frequency domain. In addition to that, the following are determined: maximum, peak-to-peak and root mean square values, along with composite multiscale entropy (CMSE) and outliers or extreme values in box plots. Also, an analysis is performed using recurrence plots, in order to assess the periodicity and continuity of the plot diagonals. Results show a clear relationship between the final CMSE value and the applied cutting speed and depth of cut. FFT analysis revealed that the signal recorded - particularly at high cutting speeds - is characterized by a significantly lower number of harmonics. The reduced complexity of the frequency spectrum indicates a potentially lower susceptibility to self-excited vibrations.

articles.title: Boundary-Guided U-Transformer for Automatic Stratigraphic Correlation from Multichannel Well Logs
articles.abstract: Fine-scale stratigraphic correlation supports reservoir characterization, but manual interpretation is time-consuming and may vary among interpreters. This study proposes a Boundary-Guided U-Transformer (BG-UT) for automatic stratigraphic correlation from multichannel well logs. The method formulates correlation as a one-dimensional semantic segmentation task along the depth direction. A U-shaped convolutional encoder–decoder with skip connections is combined with a Transformer bottleneck incorporating relative positional bias, enabling the network to integrate local well-log response patterns with information from a broader depth interval. Auxiliary branches for stratigraphic top/base regression and boundary detection are jointly optimized with the classification task, providing complementary supervision for interval geometry and interface positions. During inference, sequence-constrained Viterbi decoding combines classification scores with transition preferences based on the expected vertical succession, encouraging stratigraphically coherent label sequences. The decoded labels are then converted into contiguous stratigraphic intervals and top/base-depth tables. On 60 validation wells, BG-UT achieves an average accuracy of 82.09% and a macro F1-score of 84.89%, exceeding SegNet and Encoder Transformer by 4.46 and 2.71 percentage points in average accuracy, respectively. The proposed method effectively improves boundary localization stability, reduces the influence of local abnormal log responses and stratigraphic thickness variations, and provides a reliable intelligent approach for fine-scale stratigraphic correlation and subsequent reservoir modeling under complex reservoir conditions.

articles.title: Groundwater Detection Using Geophysical Methods in Different Overburden Types in the Karst Region of Southwest China
articles.abstract: The overburden has a decisive influence on geophysical groundwater detection. (1) Exposed type area: The soluble rock aquifer is directly exposed at the surface. For conventional direct current (DC) electrical methods, this layer exhibits high resistivity, which hinders the application of the DC resistivity method. Non-ground-contact geophysical methods such as ground-penetrating radar (GPR) and transient electromagnetic (TEM) methods are often used for groundwater detection in such areas. (2) Covered type area: The soluble rock aquifer is overlain by clay, sand, gravel, and other materials, which forms an electrical layer with resistivity ranging from tens to hundreds of Ω·m. When the overburden thickness is less than 30 m, the conventional resistivity method is suitable for groundwater detection; when the overburden thickness exceeds 30 m, methods such as audio-frequency magnetotellurics (AMT), controlled-source audio-frequency magnetotellurics (CSAMT), or TEM are recommended. (3) Buried type area: The soluble rock is overlain by clastic rocks, which generally have resistivity ranging from tens to hundreds of Ω·m. For relatively intact, slightly weathered basalt, the resistivity can be on the order of n×103–n×104 Ω·m. When the groundwater level is shallow, electromagnetic methods are preferable. When the groundwater level is deep, the conventional resistivity method can be used within the target detection depth range. However, under confined site conditions and with deep target bodies, methods such as AMT, CSAMT, or TEM should be used for groundwater detection. Other methods may be integrated when geophysical anomalies are ambiguous or multiple interpretations are available to ensure comprehensive interpretation.

articles.title: Whole-Electrolyte Design Enables Concentrated Two-Electron Storage of Viologens
articles.abstract: Accessing the second reduction of viologens can double their charge-storage capacity, but at high concentrations the doubly reduced species associate into poorly soluble assemblies. Efforts to address this have focused on covalent modification of the redox active molecule. Here we show that the surrounding electrolyte can instead be designed to regulate this association. Charge-matched aromatic ions, PhSO3− and PhN(Me)3+, suppress capacity loss while leaving viologen redox potentials largely unchanged. Structural screening reveals that this function requires charge compatibility with the viologen, an aromatic framework and an appropriate counter anion. DFT calculations and diffusion measurements indicate that PhN(Me)3+ can interpose between reduced viologens and weaken their direct association, whereas NaCl stabilizes compact assemblies. Using this approach, an existing viologen supports reversible two-electron storage at 1.0 M, delivering a maximum capacity of 39.3 Ah L−1 over 100 cycles. These results establish the electrolyte as an active design parameter for controlling molecular association in concentrated multielectron redox chemistry.

articles.title: Syntheses, characterization, spectral properties, and catalytic activity of azo amido complexes of copper(II)
articles.abstract: A potentially terdentate ligands 1N-(N,N-diethylaminoethyl)-2-arylazoaniline HL, [where HL = ArN=NC6H4N(H)C2H4N(C2H5)2; Ar = C6H5 (for HL1, 3a) or p-MeC6H4 (for HL2, 3b) or p-ClC6H4 (for HL3, 3c)] have been used, in its deprotonated form, to prepare a copper(II) complexes which has been structurally characterized. The ligands (L̶ ) afford a mononuclear complex Cu(L)Cl (4). In complex (4), (L̶ ) binds to the copper(II) center in a terdentate (N,N,N) fashion. The CuIIN(azo)N/(amido)N//(amine) and Cl coordination environment is severely distorted from ideal square planar geometry. The Cu-N(amido) bond length is shortest and Cu-N(amine) bond length is larger. The distorted phenyl ring adjacent to the six-membered azo-amido chelate ring consist four longer and two shorter bonds indicates the delocalization. The delocalization of negative charge of the anionic ligands that formed in situ from the precursor (L̶ ) due to dissociation of an amino proton. The emission property of copper(II) complexes was examined in dichloromethane solvent. Cyclic voltammetry of 4c complex shows a Cu(II)–Cu(I) oxidation at 0.68 V vs. SCE, followed by an oxidation of the coordinated ligand 3c at 1.01 V vs. SCE. Two reductions of the coordinated 1N-(N,N-diethylaminoethyl)-2-arylazoaniline ligand 3c are observed – 1.14 V and – 0.65 V vs. SCE. The catalytic activity of complex 4a has been investigated in the oxidation of benzyl alcohol by using H2O2 as oxidant. The effects of two influential parameters in catalytic reactions, amount of catalyst and temperature have been studied to obtain the optimum condition.

articles.title: Hierarchical Fe₃O₄@Ni-MOF on Nickel Foam for Enhanced Electrochemical Water Splitting and Supercapacitor Performance
articles.abstract: The hierarchical Fe₃O₄@Ni-MOF composite was successfully fabricated directly on nickel foam and systematically characterized to confirm its crystal structure, morphology, chemical composition, porosity, and thermal stability. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis was employed to identify the crystalline phases and verify the successful formation of the Fe₃O₄ and Ni-MOF components, while scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) revealed the hierarchical morphology, surface features, and nanoscale structural characteristics of the composite. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy was used to identify the characteristic functional groups and chemical bonding interactions within the composite. Furthermore, Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) analysis was conducted to evaluate the specific surface area and pore characteristics, while thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) was performed to assess thermal stability and decomposition behavior. The resulting Fe₃O₄@Ni-MOF/NF electrode exhibited enhanced electrochemical performance for water splitting, achieving HER and OER overpotentials of 120 mV and 250 mV, respectively, at 10 mA cm⁻², together with Tafel slopes of 94 and 109 mV dec⁻¹. In supercapacitor measurements, the electrode delivered a specific capacitance of 531 F g⁻¹ at 0.5 A g ¹ and retained 77.6% of its initial capacitance after 8000 cycles. The improved electrochemical behavior is attributed to the synergistic interaction between Fe₃O₄ and Ni-MOF, the hierarchical porous architecture, and the highly conductive three-dimensional nickel foam substrate, which collectively promote efficient electron transport, electrolyte accessibility, and rapid ion diffusion. Furthermore, the electrode's practical water-splitting capability was demonstrated using a two-electrode electrolytic cell powered by a DC power supply. The assembled cell exhibited an overall cell voltage (Ecell) of only 1.73 V at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻², confirming the feasibility of the Fe₃O₄@Ni-MOF/NF electrode for real-time electrochemical water-splitting applications. These results highlight the potential of the hierarchical Fe₃O₄@Ni-MOF/NF architecture as a multifunctional platform for efficient hydrogen production and electrochemical energy storage.

articles.title: Simultaneous transformation of lignocellulosic components using acidic deep eutectic solvents: From action mechanism to scale extraction
articles.abstract: Achieving the balanced valorization of lignocellulosic components is essential for improving atom economy and sustainability in biorefinery, yet remains challenging. Herein, a green and scalable strategy was developed for the synergistic conversion of lignocellulosic biomass to polyphenoliclignin and lignocellulosic nanofibers (LCNFs) using customized acidic deep eutectic solvents (DESs). The acidity and hydrogen-bonding capability of the designed DESs were regulated by altering the hydrogen bond donors, including formic, acetic, lactic, and oxalic acids. Kamlet-Taft solvatochromic analysis and DFT calculations showed that the oxalic acid‑based DES (OD) had the strongest hydrogen‑bonding ability ( = 3.340) and acidity ( = 1.882). This efficiently disrupted the hydrogen-bonding network and selectively cleaved lignin ether bonds and glycosidic bonds in amorphous cellulose. Consequently, LCNFs with a high crystallinity index (CrI) of 83% and an average diameter of 7.64 nm were obtained. Simultaneously, high-quality lignin (ODL) was produced with a yield of 63.3%, phenolic hydroxyl content of 11%, nearly 100% purity, and a low molecular weight of 2038 Da. Structural characterization revealed that ODL exhibited substantially reduced and linkages, with guaiacyl (G) and syringyl (S) units accounting for 54.5% and 44.3%, respectively, demonstrating the selective cleavage and structural regulation of lignin by acidic DESs. Furthermore, the DES system was successfully scaled up to a processing capacity of 100 kg lignocellulose per day. This work provides a scalable and mechanistically informed platform for the integrated production of high-purity lignin and LCNFs from lignocellulosic biomass.

articles.title: Extraction and storage stability of anthocyanin rich Ixora coccinea flower extract using carbonated water
articles.abstract: Ixora coccinea flowers are a potential source of natural pigments, but the use of carbonated water for their extraction and subsequent stability of the resulting extract require further evaluation. This study investigated carbonated water as an extraction medium and assessed the resulting crude flower extract using spectrophotometric measurements. Monomeric Anthocyanin Content (MAC) was determined by the pH differential method, while the absorbance at 520 nm and browning index (BI) were used to monitor changes in color-related responses. Carbonated water, distilled water, and acidified ethanol were compared under the extraction conditions specified in the study. The effects of flower-to-solvent ratio and post-harvest withering were also examined. Storage conditions were evaluated with respect to light and temperature, and response surface methodology was applied to investigate the effects of flower mass and storage temperature on MAC and BI. Under the tested conditions, dark and refrigerated storage were associated with better retention of the measured responses. The model-derived operating conditions and their experimental validation are reported after verification of the model structure and calculations. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the use of carbonated water in extracting Ixora coccinea flower pigments and identify processing and storage variables for further investigation in food-colorant development.

articles.title: Additive Manufacturing of Hydrogel-Polymer Combinations for Applications in Smart Reactors
articles.abstract: The increasing use of renewable raw materials with fluctuating properties creates a need for process equipment that can adapt to changing operating conditions. As components of smart reactors, self-adaptive structures could respond to reaction conditions such as temperature, pressure drop, or pH to maintain selectivity and yield within a desired range.
