This approach allows for the reconstruction of high-fidelity molecular fingerprints that resolve complex vibrational relaxation pathways and weak structural dynamics, previously hidden within the background and noise, providing a pathway for new high-sensitivity and time-resolved studies of complex chemical structures.

articles.title: Quantifying the importance of equation of state and transport property compatibility in supercritical fluids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-fidelity simulation of supercritical flows requires accurate values of thermodynamic properties including the density (rho), specific heat cp, enthalpy h, and entropy s as well as transport properties such as the viscosity (eta) and thermal conductivity (lambda) as functions of the temperature T and pressure P. In simulations of mixtures, such as supercritical carbon dioxide (sCO2) with contaminants, a generalized equation of state (EoS) is often used, leading to errors in rho(T,P) when compared to results from correlations developed specifically for individual species. Similarly, generalized correlations for eta and lambda are often used, with a corresponding decrease in accuracy. However, a second source of error is introduced in calculations of transport properties. These correlations are created and computed as functions of T and rho instead of as functions of T and P. Because of this, when eta(T,rho )and lambda(T,rho) are calculated, errors in rho(T,P) propagate through the calculation. This work creates a procedure for tracking both errors caused by using a generalized correlation for eta(T,rho) and lambda(T,rho), and for tracking the errors caused by using a generalized correlation for rho(T,P) in these calculations. The viscosity and thermal conductivity of supercritical CO2, N2, andCH4 are used as examples to demonstrate how to separate the errors due to the generalized property correlations and the errors due to the generalized EoS. Both sources of error are largest near the critical temperature Tc. These errors are large enough to impact both the numeric stability and the accuracy of simulations.

articles.title: Classical control of quantum-state relaxation in confined molecular hydrogen
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum-state conversion between the ortho and para nuclear-spin states of H₂ is forbidden in the isolated molecule but these states can become connected through interactions with a surrounding environment. How that same environment governs the dynamics of the newly connected states remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate this problem using H₂ confined in crystalline molecular solids, where the host environment selectively enables conversion between a pair of otherwise disconnected ortho-H₂ and para-H₂ states. Rotationally resolved infrared spectroscopy directly determines the state-specific conversion dynamics in crystalline CO₂ and N₂O at 10 K, revealing that increasing H₂ concentration suppresses nuclear-spin conversion by nearly an order of magnitude, reaching complete suppression by 20% H₂ loading. Molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations identify two complementary origins of this concentration dependence: changes in the thermally populated phonon modes available to mediate relaxation, and strain-driven H₂ clustering that progressively removes molecules from the host crystal field responsible for enabling conversion. The resulting picture connects a classical collective response of the host to microscopic quantum-state dynamics: H₂ loading generates strain that reorganizes the local molecular environment, thereby modifying both the phonon bath and the molecular coupling to that bath. These results establish a multiscale mechanism by which condensed-phase environments can govern the connectivity and dynamics of an effective two-level system.

articles.title: Enforcing Symmetries on Pre-trained ML Models for Physics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08992v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-hoc group averaging (or test-time augmentation) is a simple way to impose symmetry on a trained predictor without changing its architecture or retraining it. For finite and compact groups, averaging over a normalized Haar measure on the group gives the Reynolds operator: a canonical projection onto invariant or equivariant predictors with known non-increasing risk guarantees under certain assumptions. This paper provides numerical experiments on physics emulation models that demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach in this setting. We then extend this framework to non-compact group symmetries. For non-compact groups, the Haar measure cannot be normalized, so group averaging cannot be defined in the same way. We replace it with three alternatives: the Weyl unitary trick (which requires complexifying the space and extending the predictor), a data-dependent orthogonal projection (which involves a non-trivial optimization on the space of invariant or equivariant functions), and a frame averaging approach (which involves mapping each point to a set of orbit representatives). We illustrate the constructions theoretically and empirically on the unit-rescaling group and the Lorentz group. Our results show that in the non-compact case, the Weyl trick and frame averaging do not provide a consistent improvement over the baseline, except where the test data is out-of-distribution (an orders-of-magnitude improvement in this case) and, for the Weyl trick, in low-data regimes. The orthogonal projection can provide improvements in-distribution and out-of-distribution. We also observe that models trained directly on invariant features matched or beat the projection of an unconstrained one. We conclude that post-hoc symmetrization extends to non-compact groups, but it does not consistently outperform training a symmetric model.

articles.title: Shaping Frequency-Bin Biphoton Correlations via Programmable Optical Frequency Combs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09713v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Programmable shaping of photon-pair spectral correlations is important for frequency-bin quantum information processing. However, achieving this control remains challenging in nonlinear optical systems without reliable forward models. Here, we demonstrate model-free, hardware-in-the-loop shaping of the measured joint spectral intensity of a cascaded photon-pair source driven by a programmable optical frequency comb. A blockwise simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation controller optimizes up to 22 pump, signal, and idler parameters. Each iteration requires only two accepted hardware evaluations, independent of the parameter count. The controller converges to diverse target patterns on 3×3, 4×4, and 5×5 frequency-bin grids. The optimized distributions achieve Pearson correlations between 0.66 and 0.98 and classical overlap fidelities between 0.32 and 0.62. Cross-target similarity analysis confirms that the optimized patterns remain target-specific. Source characterization yields a maximum coincidence-to-accidental ratio of approximately 585. Accuracy is limited by pump-phase transfer, parasitic nonlinear background, waveshaper constraints, amplitude-only filtering, and measurement noise. Joint spectral intensity contains no spectral-phase information. Therefore, the results demonstrate control of measured frequency-bin populations and correlations, not complete reconstruction of the two-photon state. Phase-sensitive characterization is required to verify inter-bin coherence and quantify the entanglement dimensionality of the output state. Our results establish direct measurement feedback as a practical approach to reconfigurable frequency-bin correlation engineering when an accurate end-to-end model is unavailable.

articles.title: Universal photonic synthetic temporal-mode converter for heterogeneous quantum interconnects
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a synthetic temporal-mode converter (STC) that combines programmable waveform matching with denser time multiplexing for heterogeneous quantum interconnects. Programmable couplers and optical delays reshape known single-photon temporal waveforms through coherent interference between time bins. Conversion to a common single-bin mode concentrates amplitudes from N bins in lceillog₂Nrceil mixing stages, simultaneously improving temporal indistinguishability and freeing channel time. Simulations yield mode overlaps above 99.9% for exponential and Gaussian inputs. For N=256 and 0.5,dB loss per stage, STC gives a 45.6-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate than temporal gating at equal mode overlap for two exponential inputs. Relative to long pulses, the shortened temporal matched mode can support an approximately 41-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate when the available time-multiplexing capacity is fully utilized.

articles.title: Discrete time crystals and heteroclinic switching in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09841v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the mechanisms underlying the emergence of discrete time crystals in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers. Our analysis is based on a Haus master equation generalized to retain carrier memory between round-trips. We perform a detailed bifurcation analysis that reveals a well-defined hierarchy of subharmonic states, illustrating how pulses may suppress their neighbors when the modulation runs faster than the pulse round-trip frequency. To identify the underlying mechanism, we derive effective equations of motion that couple the pulse energies, their positions relative to the modulation transmission maxima, and the local time-dependent gain. These reveal that transitions between time-crystalline states occur via transcritical global bifurcations, opening a regime of heteroclinic winnerless competition between symmetry-degenerate configurations.

articles.title: Correlated non-perturbative electron dynamics with quantum trajectories
articles.abstract: arXiv:physics/0605103v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An approach to electron correlation effects in atoms that uses quantum trajectories is presented. A comparison with the exact quantum mechanical results for 1D Helium atom shows that the major features of the correlated ground state distribution and of the strong field ionization dynamics are reproduced with quantum trajectories. The intra-atomic resonant transitions are described accurately by a trajectory ensemble. The present approach reduces significantly the computational time and it can be used for both bound and ionizing electrons.

articles.title: Operational impact of quantum resources in chemical dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.06833v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Quantum coherence and other non-classical features are widely discussed in chemical dynamics, yet it remains difficult to quantify when such resources are operationally relevant for a given process and observable. While quantum resource theories provide a comprehensive framework for comparing free and resourceful settings, existing approaches typically rely on resource monotones or on performance bounds under free operations, and do not directly quantify the maximal influence a chosen resource can exert on a fixed chemical dynamics. Here, we introduce task specific, process level quantifiers that upper bound the largest change a quantum resource can induce in a target figure of merit. Central is a resource impact functional C_M(Λ), defined by comparing a state with its paired resource-free counterpart under the same quantum channel Λ, which admits an operational interpretation in binary hypothesis testing. We derive variation and time bounds that constrain how rapidly a resource can modify a target signal, providing resource-aware analogues of quantum speed limits. Moreover, we show that open system dynamics can be decomposed into free and resourceful components such that only the resourceful component contributes to C_M(Λ), thereby isolating the parts of a generator responsible for resource-induced changes in the observable. We illustrate the framework exemplary for energy transfer in a donor-acceptor dimer in two analytically solvable regimes. Our results provide a general toolbox for diagnosing and benchmarking quantum resource effects in molecular processes.

articles.title: Spurious zero-dispersion continua in full (2,q)-positivity: A linear hierarchy-depth lower bound from an exactly solvable counting operator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.09698v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Variational two-particle reduced-density-matrix methods impose hierarchies of semidefinite constraints. We ask whether a fixed level of such a hierarchy can recover even an elementary many-fermion spectrum, using the dispersion test, in which a value is accepted as an eigenvalue when the minimized dispersion vanishes. We study an exactly solvable operator that counts fermions in one half of the spin orbitals. It is a sum of commuting occupation numbers, so its spectral problem is classical, a Boolean occupation-number problem with integer spectrum, and the obstruction found here is not a genuinely quantum one. We determine the complete set of accepted values at every level of the full hierarchy of particle-hole semidefinite constraints. Besides the integers, this set contains an entire interval of noninteger values unless the hierarchy level grows linearly with the particle number, and we give the exact threshold. The proof constructs explicit q-positive reduced density matrices, diagonal in the occupation basis, by continuing the occupation probabilities of a fixed-particle-number state to a noninteger particle number. The fermionic content is that classical semidefinite constraints on occupation correlations, with nonnegative occupation-pattern probabilities, imply positivity of every particle-hole block, so the noncommuting fermionic conditions remove no false value. A converse argument shows that no other false eigenvalues occur. The limitation is specific to the hierarchy: two-body inequalities that encode the integer spectrum would remove every false value but are not generated at a fixed level. By Erdahl's duality theorem, whose hypotheses we check at fixed particle number, the result applies equally to the full (2,q)-positivity conditions of the constructive solution of the N-representability problem.

articles.title: Geometry-Aware Score-Repellent Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08909v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The recently proposed Score-Repellent Monte Carlo (SRMC) method improves MCMC sampling by tilting the target density π in R^d with the factor exp(-α,θₙ^top s(x)), where the score function s(x) = nablaₓ log π(x), and θₙ is the score average from past samples. However, a single scalar repellence strength αge0 cannot handle both the steep and the flat directions in anisotropic energy landscapes at once. We introduce emphGeometry-Aware SRMC (GA-SRMC), which generalizes the Euclidean alignment to θ^top M s(x) for any symmetric positive-definite matrix M. A stochastic-approximation central limit theorem under a trace constraint on M identifies the trace-normalized inverse Fisher Mᵣₘ ₒₚₜpropto S⁻¹ as the unique minimizer of the worst-direction covariance bound, elevating the Fisher information S=Cov_π(s,s) from a proposal-side preconditioner (e.g., FisherMALA, natural gradient) to the bound-optimal repulsion-side matrix, with a single online estimate widehat Sₙ serving both roles at no additional computational cost. The full-Fisher online metric Mₙ converges almost surely to Mᵣₘ ₒₚₜ and satisfies a CLT, providing a theoretical guarantee for the online implementation of the GA-SRMC framework. On an 8-target simulation spanning the condition number κin[1.3,100] and dimension din[2,785], GA-SRMC dominates SRMC in ESS by boldsymbol4.3× on anisotropic Gaussian (κ=100) and boldsymbol6.8× on MNIST under the MALA baseline, by boldsymbol16--32% on three well-conditioned logistic-regression posteriors, and by up to boldsymbol+48% under FisherMALA; gains peak on the most anisotropic targets, and posterior-mean MSE is lower than with SRMC in all 16 full-Fisher implementations.

articles.title: Calibrated concept profiles: making the reading of a model's neurons a measurement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09196v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interpretability has largely moved from reading a model's neurons directly to reading a second model trained on the first: a probe, a sparse autoencoder, a crosscoder. The move answered real faults -- mixed meanings, thresholds without a unit, readings that did not transfer from one study to the next -- but gave up what a direct reading alone provides: nothing trained in between, the neurons themselves named, and a reading that can be repeated and compared. Here the direct reading is made a measurement. A neuron's activation varies with the prompt, so its reading is a distribution over a population of stimuli. We declare that population: every factor around a target construct is drawn at its rate in a reference corpus and logged. From the declared distribution we generate a battery of prompts, and draw it twice. From the battery we compute the calibrated concept profile, one number per neuron, stated in units of the neuron's own spread on ordinary input; the two draws give every number a noise unit. Before the profile is read, a fixed set of checks licenses the battery on the model, and the smallest change the profile can resolve across training checkpoints is measured. Realised for Python on OpenCoder-1.5B and followed across checkpoints spanning two trillion training tokens, the profile gives what the alternatives do not report: a unit on every number, a chance level for every comparison, and which neurons carry a construct at every checkpoint. The battery, the code and the data behind every result are released.

articles.title: BEiTScore++: Reference-free Image Captioning Evaluation with BEiT-3 and Conformalized Quantile Regression
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09505v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reliable uncertainty estimation is important for deploying evaluation metrics in real-world settings, where both input ambiguity and domain shifts are common. In this work, we propose an uncertainty-aware extension of the BEiTScore image captioning metric, producing conformally calibrated confidence intervals alongside alignment scores. Our approach models predictive distributions over human judgments, enabling both accurate scoring and principled uncertainty quantification in a single forward pass. We evaluate our BEiTScore++ metric across multiple benchmarks with human-annotated ratings, showing that it preserves the ranking correlation of BEiTScore, while producing intervals whose width tracks the prediction error more closely than Monte Carlo dropout on most benchmarks. The estimated uncertainty also grows under image degradation and on out-of-domain artwork images, making BEiTScore++ a practical tool for uncertainty-aware evaluation of image-caption alignment.

articles.title: Pdb or Not to Be: Comparing Debugging Interfaces With PassX@k
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactive debuggers are indispensable to human software development, yet coding agents overwhelmingly rely on edit-execute-observe loops, using common bash tools, test scripts, and print statements to debug via repeated shell commands. Stepping through a debugger provides live access to runtime state, which may enable different problem-solving capabilities. However, prior work typically introduces the debugger as an additional tool or through a new subagent, making its individual contribution difficult to isolate from the associated scaffold changes. To address this, we compare a debugger-only agent against a bash-only agent on all 500 SWE-bench Verified instances, holding the rest of the scaffold fixed. We evaluate both architectures on two models, GPT-OSS-120B and Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B, with three independent runs per architecture × model configuration. Crucially, to distinguish interface specialization from expanded coverage under repeated sampling, we introduce pass_X@k, a cross-agent pass@k that provides an unbiased estimator of the probability that at least one of k agents is successful. Although the bash and debugger agents solve partially disjoint subsets of the benchmark in any single pair of runs, our pass_X@2 estimator reveals that this is largely due to run-to-run variance rather than tool complementarity. Across both models, we find that two bash rollouts outperform the combination of one bash and one debugger rollout. Our findings highlight the importance of accounting for stochastic variance in evaluating agent and tool diversity, and we hope that pass_X@k will serve as a useful framework for the community.

articles.title: I Think, Therefore I Attack: Evaluating Thought Injection Attacks on Reasoning Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) are one of the key components of current agentic systems. LRMs augment their output with an explicit chain-of-thought reasoning stage, introducing a new attack surface for thought injection, in which untrusted text resembling the model's own deliberation is fed back to the model. We present a two-part study of this attack, performed against the prevailing large, production class open-weight models (e.g., GLM-5.3, MiniMax-M2.5, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). We first evaluate the effectiveness of static thought-injection prompts under different styles as well as tagged and untagged conditions and find that the effects of thinking tags and payload styles are all properties of the specific target model. In the second study, we exploit this model-specificity in a containerized agentic cyber range, using indirect injection prompts styled in the form of the target model's own reasoning traces to achieve attack success rates (ASR) up to 50% on operational objectives such as reverse-shell exfiltration and repository backdooring. We also find that the same malicious objective in standard prompt injection user voice never succeeds, and thinking tags suppress the agent's tendency to disclose the injection. Our results show that imitating a reasoning model's own thought style is effective for this style of attack, and that tag stripping is an unreliable defense.

articles.title: PreForceVision: Physics-Guided Optical Estimation of Bolt Preload from Bolt-Head Deformation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bolt preload is a decisive functional quantity in bolted joints because it determines whether external loads are transmitted primarily through frictional clamping or directly through the bolt. Existing preload measurement techniques, including strain-gauge bolts, force washers, ultrasonic methods, and bolt-length measurements, are effective in certain applications but require additional hardware, coupling, calibration, or joint modifications. This limits their scalability for large numbers of standard fasteners and motivates a non-contact optical approach. This paper proposes PreForceVision, a physics-guided optical framework for estimating bolt preload from preload-induced surface deformation of the bolt-head front face. The method treats preload estimation as an inverse deformation-to-force problem, where deformation of the optically accessible bolt-head surface is extracted from reference-loaded image pairs and related to the internal preload state. Preliminary results for an M16 strength class 8.8 bolt show an approximately SI12micrometer simulated head-face depression at SI90kilonewton, strain-gauge measurements of comparable magnitude, and an optical 3D measured central depression of approximately SIrange1020micrometer. The contribution is a physics-guided optical methodology combining controlled image-pair acquisition, DIC- or optical-flow-based deformation extraction, multimodal validation, and uncertainty-aware regression for rough preload estimation under controlled conditions.

articles.title: FoundaRF: A Physics-Informed Foundation Model Framework for Radio-Frequency Passive Components
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Designing RF/mmWave passive components is a time-consuming process that relies heavily on expert knowledge and iterative EM simulations. Although recent ML surrogate models have shown great promise in accelerating passive design, they remain task-specific and lack generalization. This paper presents FoundaRF, a foundation model framework that unifies passive layout modeling across diverse layout structures and technologies. It combines a self-supervised encoder with adaptive layout processing and physics-aware decoders to enable few-shot transfer. Experiments across four semiconductor technologies show strong generalization to unseen structures, outperforming baselines with up to a 3.3x reduction in prediction error, reducing labeled-data requirements by up to fourfold, and substantially shortening design turnaround. FoundaRF establishes a scalable and data-efficient solution for RF/mmWave passive design automation.

articles.title: Artificial Shoppers and Attention Competition
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.09399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how AI shopping interfaces affect price competition, platform profit, and consumer welfare. A platform hosts two of three products of different quality. Without AI, consumers compare the hosted pair under salience distortion and overweight whichever attribute, price or quality, stands out. Under assistance, an AI assistant recommends the two products with the highest true utility, leaving consumers to make the same distorted comparison. Under delegation, an AI agent selects the best product, subject to purchase approval. Both modes access all products and know consumers' preferences; firms price strategically. First, assistance can soften competition despite expanded product access. The middle-quality firm may forgo low-valuation consumers because attracting them requires cutting the price paid by higher-valuation consumers as well. Relative to no AI with the same assortment, assistance lowers both hosted prices under the high- and low-quality pair but can raise both under the high- and middle-quality pair. Second, we identify an alignment paradox: some consumers can become worse off than without AI even though their best option remains recommended and becomes cheaper. Salience can induce a switch to a lower-quality product whose quality loss exceeds the saving relative to the original purchase. The assistant ranks products accurately but does not optimize the shortlist for consumers' realized welfare. Third, assistance can raise both platform profit and aggregate consumer surplus with the high- and middle-quality pair; delegation can do so with the high- and low-quality pair. Fourth, among AI designs, the platform weakly prefers delegation with the high- and middle-quality pair wherever all compared pricing equilibria exist. Yet this preferred design can yield lower platform profit and aggregate consumer surplus than the no-AI optimum.

articles.title: Continental-Scale Groundwater Storage Dynamics and Climate Variability Across Africa (2003–2025): Regional Divergence and Hydro-Climatic Regime Shifts
articles.abstract: Groundwater is Africa’s most important buffer against climate variability, yet its regional and continental response to climatic and anthropogenic drivers remains poorly quantified. The study integrates Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment satellite gravimetry, Global Land Data Assimilation System land-surface model output, and surface water storage estimates in a mass-balance framework to derive the groundwater storage anomalies (GWSA), recharge, and discharge across Africa since 2003 on a common 0.25° regular grid, and to assess the GWSA response to precipitation, temperature, and ENSO to characterize its climate sensitivity. Results show that GWSA ranges from − 30.60 mm (North Africa) to 96.56 mm (West Africa) at an overall trend of 3.84 mm yr⁻¹ (precipitation 0.10 mm yr⁻¹). A formal structural break test identified a hydrodynamic shift in July 2020, with the GWAS trend rising from 2.59 to 5.74 mm yr⁻¹, coinciding with the onset of the 2020–2023 “triple-dip” La Niña. Recharge-to-precipitation ratio ranging from 11.0% to 21.5%, with regional GWSA trends of -0.78, 5.27, 5.12, 6.04, and 4.67 mm yr⁻¹ trend of GWSA for North, West, Middle, East, and South Africa, respectively. This recovery continues even during the 2020–2022 Horn of Africa drought, underscoring GWSA’s value as an indicator of climate and human influence, and the importance of regional variation for future water security assessments.

articles.title: Precoordination-directed synthesis of high-entropy perovskite colloidal nanocrystals
articles.abstract: Perovskite nanocrystals (PNCs) are solution-processable quantum materials with defect tolerance, tunable electronic structures and strong light-matter interactions, enabling applications in optoelectronics and photocatalysis. Integrating high-entropy configurations into PNCs unlocks a vast chemical space for multicomponent synergy and functional expansion beyond conventional stoichiometry. However, their synthesis has been fundamentally constrained by mismatched multi-precursor kinetics and a trade-off between entropic stabilization and enthalpic phase segregation. Here we report a precoordination-directed strategy for the colloidal synthesis of high-entropy vacancy-ordered double perovskite nanocrystals with high phase purity, near-equimolar stoichiometry and elemental homogeneity. We show that the participation of excess chloride energetically encourages the formation of well-defined metal-halide octahedral units in the precursor, thereby promoting the topological conversion to a high-entropy double-perovskite phase after hot-injection. The elemental synergy of high-entropy PNCs renders them versatile catalysts, delivering ~ 14-fold improvement in photocatalytic coupling of benzyl alcohol to hydrobenzoin, ~ 17-fold in oxidative coupling of methane to ethane, and ~ 35-fold in oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde, relative to their low-entropy analogues.

articles.title: Coal Phase-Down and Cross-Fuel Risk in Peninsular Malaysia: System-Level Trade-Offs among Thermal Retention, Co-Firing and Renewable-Storage Deployment
articles.abstract: Coal phase-down can lower power-sector emissions while shifting fuel-security exposure from coal to natural gas. This study quantifies that cross-fuel risk in Peninsular Malaysia using full-year hourly modelling in EnergyPLAN 16.22, MATLAB-based scenario automation and a controlled counterfactual that holds the wider national pathway constant while varying the treatment of an anonymised 1,600 MW Study Thermal Asset. The 2025 demand scale is externally checked against the Energy Commission’s recorded system peak, with a difference of 0.076%. Four cases are evaluated for 2030, 2035 and 2040: managed phase-down (PD), temporary retention (RET), retention with co-firing (RET-CF), and renewable-plus-storage deployment comprising 3,200 MW of solar PV and a 1,600 MW/6.4 GWh four-hour battery system (RE-ST). Relative to PD, RET reduces system natural-gas requirements by 9.35–12.45 TWh/yr but increases operational CO₂ emissions by 1.35–1.79 Mt/yr. A fuel-substitution ratio of 0.999–1.001 indicates near one-for-one coal-for-gas substitution on an input-energy basis. RET-CF preserves the gas reduction while moderating the emissions penalty. RE-ST changes the substitution mechanism more fundamentally, reducing both coal and gas use and lowering operational CO₂ emissions by 1.65–3.00 Mt/yr. It also lowers modelled annual system cost by USD 393–405 million under the adopted solar and battery cost assumptions. A 120-case sensitivity programme distinguishes the physical robustness of these effects from exposure to gas, carbon and substitute-fuel prices and retained-capacity availability. The results show that coal phase-down does not automatically reduce total fossil-fuel exposure: its resilience and decarbonisation outcomes depend on the portfolio that replaces the withdrawn coal contribution.

articles.title: Silent convergence failures in SCAPS-1D: unphysical open-circuit voltages and unflagged anomalies in temperature-dependent Perovskite Solar Cell simulations
articles.abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) based on inorganic charge transport layers are attracting increasing attention for their thermal stability and low fabrication cost, yet the temperature-dependent behavior of carrier extraction in these devices remains incompletely understood. Here we show that numerical simulations using SCAPS-1D can fail silently: temperature sweeps of CuI/MAPbI3/ETL and Spiro-OMeTAD/MAPbI3/ETL architectures, performed across three electron transport layers (SnO2, TiO2, ZnO) and two absorber thicknesses (100 nm and 500 nm) over the range 250–350 K, reveal two distinct convergence failure modes, neither of which is reliably flagged by the solver. In one, open-circuit voltage (Voc) and fill factor (FF) become unresolvable while a seemingly ordinary short-circuit current density (Jsc) is still returned. In the other - observed exclusively in Spiro-OMeTAD-based configurations - the solver returns a Voc that exceeds the thermodynamic ceiling Eg/q by up to 2.9×, with no indication that the output is physically impossible. Three candidate mechanisms for the first failure mode - Debye length confinement breakdown, conduction band offset inversion, and extrinsic-to-intrinsic carrier transition - were analytically ruled out. We demonstrate instead that it is caused by thermally activated divergence of the series resistance Rs at the ETL/perovskite interface: Rs increases by two to four orders of magnitude at anomaly onset, following Arrhenius behavior (R² = 0.88–0.99) with activation energies of 0.59–0.87 eV consistent with thermionic emission across the conduction band spike ΔEc. Both failure modes are ETL/HTL-specific and perovskite thickness-independent - identical patterns at 100 nm and 500 nm confirm an interfacial rather than bulk origin. While this study covers a limited set of architectures, the central implication is general: convergence anomalies in temperature-dependent SCAPS-1D simulations do not always announce themselves, and physically invalid or incomplete results may have gone unnoticed in prior work. These results provide a physically grounded framework for identifying such failures and establish ETL conduction band alignment and HTL identity as key design parameters governing extraction stability and Voc validity, respectively.

articles.title: Impact of Wall Roughness on the spontaneous ignition of pressurized hydrogen released into a tube
articles.abstract: While significant advancements have been made in understanding the spontaneous ignition of pressurized hydrogen during accidental releases, the aerodynamic effects of tube surface conditions remain critically underexplored. This paper presents a numerical investigation into the effects of equivalent sand-grain wall roughness (Ra) on the ignition mechanisms, shock wave propagation, and non-premixed flame evolution of pressurized hydrogen releases. Utilizing Large Eddy Simulation (LES) coupled with a mixture averaged transport model and an Improved Partially Stirred Reactor (PaSR) combustion model, the study evaluates the transient dynamics across absolutely smooth (Ra = 0 mm) and varying rough (Ra = 0.1, 0.5, 1.0 mm) tube boundary conditions. The analysis demonstrates that wall roughness significantly suppresses the radial expansion and central coalescence of the flame front, ultimately leading to the dissipation of the central reaction zone at high roughness scales. Conversely, roughness-induced localized vortices drastically intensify boundary layer combustion. Furthermore, wall roughness introduces a non-linear suppression of leading shock wave velocities and elevates the critical burst pressure threshold required for spontaneous ignition from 3.2 MPa to 3.5 MPa, driven by intense near-wall momentum and thermal dissipation. The findings provide critical theoretical foundations for the quantitative risk assessment of hydrogen infrastructure and inform future iterations of tube safety standards.

articles.title: Experimental Study of Mixed Convection and Thermal Radiation Heat Transfer in Horizontal Rectangular Ducts with Different Heating Orientations
articles.abstract: The current experimental work examines the combined effects of mixed convection and surface radiation on heating a horizontal rectangular duct from three distinct bottom orientations: CS1 (bottom), CS2 (top), and CS3 (side). The rectangular duct section consists of one heated isothermal wall, and the remaining walls are maintained under adiabatic conditions. The effects of Reynolds number, heat flow, surface emissivity, and heating orientation on the heated-wall temperature and total Nusselt number for convective and radiative heat transfer were systematically assessed. The findings show that forced-convection effects are strengthened as the Reynolds number increases from 978 to 1956, thereby significantly lowering the heated-wall temperature. The wall temperature increases, and the convective Nusselt number decreases by 5–13% as the applied heat flux increases from 644 to 1659 W/m². Among the three heating orientations, CS1 demonstrates the highest heat-transfer performance, followed by CS2 and CS3, respectively. Increasing the surface emissivity from 0.05 to 0.85 reduces the average wall temperature by approximately 15–16% and enhances the convective Nusselt number by 21–35%. The radiative Nusselt number rises significantly, indicating that surface radiation plays a major role in the total heat-transfer process. Stable thermal behaviour along the duct is shown by the axial profiles of the heat-transfer parameters being comparatively uniform. Overall, the results show that bottom heating (CS1) in conjunction with a high-emissivity surface offers the best heat-transfer performance and can be used successfully for heat dissipation and passive thermal management applications.

articles.title: Low plasma trimethylamine N-oxide is associated with vitamin D deficiency: toward a U-shaped TMAO–health hypothesis
articles.abstract: Background & aims: Trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a gut microbiota-derived metabolite, has been studied predominantly in relation to adverse outcomes at high concentrations, whereas the health relevance of low circulating TMAO remains largely unexplored. Because fatty fish provides both preformed TMAO and vitamin D, we postulated that plasma TMAO is positively associated with circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D]. Methods: We cross-sectionally analyzed 621 adults undergoing health examinations (median age 52.0 years; 52.7% men), using multivariable linear regression of serum 25(OH)D on plasma TMAO (per 1-SD logTMAO; quartiles), restricted cubic splines for dose–response, and likelihood ratio tests for BMI effect modification. Results: Median TMAO was 170.3 ng/mL (IQR 116.1–247.1); mean 25(OH)D was 22.1 ± 11.7 ng/mL. Adjusted for age, sex, BMI, and season, each 1-SD higher logTMAO was associated with 2.18 ng/mL higher 25(OH)D (95% CI 1.29–3.07), and Q4 vs Q1 differed by 4.56 ng/mL (2.05–7.07; both P < 0.001); across TMAO percentile bands, mean 25(OH)D rose from 20.1 to 29.8 ng/mL and deficiency prevalence fell from 60.3% to 33.9%. The association was nonlinear (P for nonlinearity = 0.018) and modified by BMI (P for interaction = 0.018): positive in normal-weight and overweight participants but attenuated, with a reversed point estimate, in obesity. It remained positive after excluding participants with obesity, high-leverage observations, and renal impairment. Conclusions: In Chinese adults, lower plasma TMAO was associated with lower circulating 25(OH)D, with BMI-dependent effect modification. Together with the established harms of high TMAO concentrations, these findings motivate a U-shaped TMAO–health hypothesis that awaits prospective confirmation.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Endoscopic Third Ventriculostomy Compared with Ventriculoperitoneal Shunting in Pediatric Post-Inflammatory Hydrocephalus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
articles.abstract: Background Ventriculoperitoneal shunting (VPS) remains the standard treatment for pediatric post-inflammatory hydrocephalus because it provides reliable cerebrospinal fluid diversion, but it is associated with infection, treatment failure, repeated revisions, and lifelong device dependency. Endoscopic third ventriculostomy (ETV) offers a shunt-independent alternative that may reduce long-term device-related complications, although its comparative efficacy and safety remain uncertain.Methods Nine databases were searched from inception to 28 February 2026 under a registered PROSPERO protocol (CRD420261382819). Random-effects models were used for direct comparative meta-analyses, with supplementary single-arm syntheses to estimate pooled procedure-specific event rates.Results Of 3,995 records identified and 2,092 screened after deduplication, 22 studies comprising 13,778 children were included. In comparative analyses, ETV and VPS showed no statistically significant difference in treatment success (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.73–1.31), mortality (RR 1.24, 95% CI 0.68–2.28), or overall complications (RR 2.09, 95% CI 0.17–25.27). In single-arm analyses, the pooled success rate was 51% for ETV and 63% for VPS. The pooled mortality rate was 7% for ETV and 4% for VPS. Revision rates were 45% and 39%, respectively, while overall complication rates were 25% for ETV and 26% for VPS. Infection rates were 8% for ETV and 13% for VPS.Conclusions Current evidence does not show a clear superiority of ETV or VPS for pediatric post-inflammatory hydrocephalus. ETV may show numerically lower infection and mortality, but this should be interpreted cautiously given marked heterogeneity and limited head-to-head data.

articles.title: Integrated artificial photosynthesis and microbial bioprocessing systems for solar biofuel and bioproduct production
articles.abstract: Coupling abiotic solar capture with microbial biosynthesis integrated artificial photosynthesis–microbial bioprocessing (IAP-MB) could convert sunlight, water and CO2 into fuels and polymers at areal efficiencies well above those of crops, which typically remain below 1%. Here we critically review three architectures decoupled photovoltaic–electrolysis/fermentation (A), electrode-attached biofilms (B) and photosensitised cells (C) and combine the literature with transparent screening calculations. A cascade analysis bounds the solar-to-chemical efficiency of Architecture A at 4.0–10.9% (base case 7.2%) and identifies electrolysis and bioconversion as the main leverage points. Substrate-inhibited uptake kinetics (Andrews model) imply an unstable operating branch above the optimum carrier concentration (9.8 mM for the constants used), so unmanaged supply–demand mismatch causes runaway accumulation; in simulation, a PI controller with back-calculation anti-windup reduced the peak formate concentration from 207 to 48 mM relative to an unprotected PI loop. Using the authors’ preliminary plant model (10,000 t PHB yr− 1), recomputed levelised costs are US2.19 kg− 1 (A) and US3.23 kg− 1 (B), dominated by discount rate and operating cost, and photoelectrode lifetimes near one year add roughly US0.8 kg− 1 to B. Stoichiometrically consistent life-cycle accounting shows that the climate benefit of PHB routes hinges on the biogenic carbon credit (2.04 kg CO2 per kg PHB): burdens alone are 1.80 (A) and 3.10 (B) kg CO2-eq kg− 1, versus 1.98 for polypropylene. A research roadmap and reporting recommendations close to the paper.

articles.title: Comparative morphology of the labium and external efferent system in the Janeirona clade (Hemiptera: Pentatomidae: Ochlerini)
articles.abstract: The labium and the external scent efferent system (ESES) are important characters in Heteroptera systematics. This study provides a comparative morphological analysis of these structures in genera within the Janeirona clade of Ochlerini (Pentatomidae: Discocephalinae), characterized by a subdivision in labiomere II. Using light and scanning electron microscopy (SEM), 15 species were investigated, including five outgroups. Results confirm that the subdivision in labiomere II is a functional intercalary segment, exhibiting articulation and intrinsic musculature. Two distinct morphological types of intercalary segments were identified: a dilated type with a wide range of motion, and a flat, short and less mobile type. Regarding the ESES, the clade shares an elliptical, ventrolaterally oriented ostiole and a spout-shaped peritreme. Detailed SEM imaging further revealed specialized scale-like microsculptures on the peritremal surface and complex spiracular filter systems. These findings provide the first high-resolution characterization of the labial intercalary segment and significantly expand the morphological data available for the tribe Ochlerini. This study offers relevant insights for future taxonomic and phylogenetic research aimed at refining the classification of Pentatomidae. Introduction The suborder Heteroptera is distinguished from other insect groups by the combination of the external scent efferent system (ESES), and the labium forming an elongated, segmented tube (Grazia et al. 2015; Schuh and Weirauch 2020). The labium is highly conserved within the Heteroptera infraorders, varying mostly in the number of segments (labiomeres); most families have four labiomeres, but three are seen in Reduviidae (Weirauch 2008). In contrast, the ESES morphology is highly variable between and within groups of Heteroptera, being useful for delimiting characters for phylogenetic inference and for taxonomic identification in different levels (Kment and Vilímová 2010; Barão et al. 2017; Weiler et al. 2017; Schuh and Weirauch 2020; Genevcius et al. 2021). The ESES plays an important role in the chemical communication of true bugs, being indispensable for their defense against predators. The system is composed by paired metathoracic scent glands, in the adults, which release repellent secretions (allomones) through specialized cuticular structures such as the ostiole, peritreme and the evaporatorium. The ostiole is the opening for the draining of the secretions of metathoracic scent glands; the peritreme consists of a cuticular expansion or excavation adjacent to the ostiole of the thoracic gland, responsible for conducting secretions to the evaporatorium, which is composed by cuticular mycoid microsculpture present on the meso- and metapleural surface, responsible for spreading and containing the secretion in a delimited pleural area (protecting the insect of the secretion toxicity) and helping volatilization (Staddon 1979, 1986; Aldrich 1988; Kment et al. 2012; Weber et al. 2017). Although studies of the ESES microsculpture under scanning electron microscopy (SEM) dates from the 1960s (for a review see Kment and Vilímová 2010), it was only recently that SEM techniques began to be employed in systematized comparative studies of groups within Pentatomoidea and Pentatomidae. In the seminal work by Kment and Vilímová (2010) the ESES in Pentatomoidea was characterized in detail, and standardized terminology was proposed. They distinguished six types of peritreme in the superfamily: auricle, spout, groove, ruga, disc and lobes; and highlighted the different parts composing the mushroom bodies of the evaporatorium: cap, stem, bridges, alveoli and trabeculae. This work served as a basis for studies in Pentatomidae (Carpocorini) (Barão et al. 2017), Aphylidae (Kment et al. 2012) and Scutelleridae (Weiler et al. 2017), however, the ESES fine morphology of many other groups remain unstudied. The labium has been considered of taxonomic value in Pentatomidae, frequently used in keys and diagnoses to genera and species (e.g., Rolston and McDonald 1979; Grazia et al. 2015; Rider et al. 2018; Schuh and Weirauch 2020), being highly variable in length in most subfamilies. However, in the Janeirona Distant, 1911 clade (sensu Sampaio and Campos 2023) of Discocephalinae, the proximal portion of labiomere II presents what previous authors have named as “pseudo-segment" (Kormilev 1949, 1955, 1956), “pseudo-base” (Ruckes 1958), or "intercalary segment” (Rolston 1992), what suggest different interpretations of the morphology and functionality of the structure. Discocephalinae is one of the 10 subfamilies of Pentatomidae, consisting of a Neotropical group with more than 300 species and 77 genera divided in two tribes, Discocephalini and Ochlerini (Grazia et al. 2015; Rider et al., 2018); in the latter belongs the Janeirona clade composed by Adoxoplatys Breddin, 1903, Neoadoxoplatys Kormilev, 1956, and Paropsocolis Sampaio and Campos, 2023 (Sampaio and Campos 2023). In this study we investigate the morphology of the labium and ESES of the genera in the Janeirona clade, following a comparative approach with species of other pentatomid genera.

articles.title: Influence of laser beam shaping on process stability, build rate, and microstructure in laser powder bed fusion of AlSi10Mg.
articles.abstract: Laser beam shaping offers promising opportunities to stabilize the laser powder bed fusion (L-PBF) process and improve manufacturing performance. However, most previous studies have focused on shaped beams with spot diameters above 0.2 mm, substantially larger than those conventionally used in L-PBF (< 0.1 mm). Here, we investigate annular and near-top-hat beam profiles with dimensions close to the conventional range for processing AlSi10Mg, using a Gaussian beam as the reference across different optical arrangements with an interlaboratory approach. At moderate laser powers (300–500 W), beam shaping widens the viable power–scan speed (P, V) processing window by delaying the onset of keyhole formation. Compared with the Gaussian beam, the shaped profiles produce shallower and wider melt pools, characterized by higher width-to-depth ratios, while also improving the surface quality of the fabricated parts, as evidenced by lower average roughness (Sa). Microstructural analysis reveals slightly stronger crystallographic textures for the near-top-hat and annular profiles, whereas the average grain size remains essentially unchanged. Consistently, no clear difference in tensile strength is observed between specimens produced using the near-top-hat and Gaussian profiles. At higher laser power (700 W), the annular beam enables stable processing at scan speeds up to 2.6 m s− 1, yielding build rates of approximately 20 mm³ s− 1, about twice those achieved with the Gaussian profile. This productivity gain is attributed to the more stable laser–matter interaction resulting from the lower peak irradiance of the annular intensity distribution. Although the shaped beams generate more spatter, this does not adversely affect the surface roughness of the fabricated parts. These results show that small-sized top-hat, annular, and core/ring beams provide an effective means of extending the stable processing range of L-PBF while improving surface quality and enabling substantially higher build rates.

articles.title: Hyperspectral Imaging for Subsurface Mineral Characterization: Integrated Application with FLEX Log and XRD in Devonian Ouabed reservoirs - Algeria
articles.abstract: Clay minerals pose significant challenges in hydrocarbon reservoirs, especially during drilling and production, where clay swelling and migration, particularly from smectite, kaolinite, and illite, can lead to severe operational problems such as stuck pipe and restricted production flow. Several techniques have been used to detect and characterize clay types in subsurface formations, including logging tools and X-ray Diffraction (XRD), but these methods differ in precision, processing time, and operational complexity. In the Devonian Ouabed reservoirs in Algeria, previous studies have revealed high clay contents with variable mineralogical compositions, which have caused numerous drilling and production difficulties. To identify appropriate solutions for these clay-related issues, two core samples from Wells A and B were analyzed using the FLEX logging tool, XRD, and, for the first time in Algeria, a hyperspectral camera system for clay determination. Results show distinct mineralogical profiles among the three methods. In Well A, hyperspectral imaging measured 11% kaolinite and 7% illite, aligning with XRD data that indicated a predominantly kaolinitic composition (65%). Conversely, Well B exhibited 15% kaolinite, 9% illite, and 32% mica based on hyperspectral imaging. Overall, this comparative study shows that hyperspectral imaging delivers rapid, high-resolution clay identification and becomes highly effective when integrated with XRD and logging data.

articles.title: CFD assessment of non-premixed turbulent methane flame with reduced chemical kinetics
articles.abstract: Pollutant predictions in turbulent diffusion flames depend on how mixing, chemistry and their coupling are modelled. Using the Brookes–Moss experiments as reference, this study assesses how the Reynolds-averaged Navier–Stokes (RANS) turbulence closure, the chemical-kinetic scheme and the turbulence intensity of the air co-flow affect the computed structure, nitric oxide (NO) and soot of an enclosed methane jet flame at a Reynolds number of 5000. Steady axisymmetric simulations used the eddy-dissipation model, thermal and prompt NO post-processing and the Moss–Brookes soot model. The measured mixture fraction and the fast-chemistry limit were combined to bound the predicted fuel mass fraction. Of the closures tested (k–ε, k–ω and a Reynolds-stress model, RSM), the RSM lowered the mean absolute percentage error of the centreline temperature from 30.1% to 15.9%. Replacing the one-step scheme by a 16-step augmented reduced mechanism lowered the fuel-decay error from 56.6% to 9.5%, a larger gain than that obtained by changing the closure. Raising the co-flow turbulence intensity from 20% to 80% reduced the peak NO from 183 to 168 ppm (− 8.4%) and the peak soot volume fraction by 43%. Centreline soot levels agreed with the measurements within 7%, although the radial soot extent was under-predicted.

articles.title: Monolithic gain–storage separation in low-noise supercavity lasers
articles.abstract: Vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers offer low power and wafer-scale integration, but their short cavities confine optical gain and photon storage to the same active region, limiting photon lifetime and spectral coherence. Here we propose a monolithic surface-emitting supercavity laser that functionally decouples optical gain from photon storage by coupling an active cavity to multiple passive storage cavities. Controlled intercavity coupling is achieved through precise engineering of the reflection, transmission, and phase matching of the connecting DBR mirrors. By tailoring the supermode profile and coherently redistributing its optical field among the active and passive cavities, we demonstrate a monolithic surface-emitting supercavity laser with an enlarged effective photon-storage volume and reduced noise. The coupled cavities yield a quality factor of 22,499 and a cold-cavity photon lifetime of 20.1 ps, while the supercavity laser retains low-threshold single-mode operation, a Lorentzian linewidth of 0.41 MHz, a frequency-noise floor of 2.0 × 105 Hz2 Hz⁻¹ and a high-frequency relative-intensity-noise floor near − 145 dBc Hz⁻¹ without external feedback. When the laser is locked to a Cs reference, the atomic-clock testbed reaches an Allan deviation of 8.7 × 10⁻13 at 8,192 s. This architecture establishes gain–storage separation as a scalable route to coherent surface emitters.

articles.title: Comparative study on microwave-assisted co-pyrolysis of tissue paper and polyethylene: Effects of zeolite, metal oxide, and carbon-based additives on syngas production
articles.abstract: Microwave-assisted pyrolysis for syngas production represents a promising technology for the resource utilization of solid waste. Due to the selective heating nature of microwaves, the introduction of microwave absorbers or catalysts is a prevalent strategy to enhance the process. This study investigated the effects of 3 representative categories of microwave absorbers/catalysts—zeolites (HZSM-5), metal oxides (CaO), and carbon-based materials (biochar)—on gas evolution and product characteristics during the co-pyrolysis of tissue paper and polyethylene (PE). The results indicated that HZSM-5 exhibited the most pronounced catalytic performance, notably intensifying the synergistic interaction between the feedstocks. CaO functioned effectively as both a CO₂ sorbent and a microwave absorber, while biochar significantly improved the heating rate and temperature throughout the reaction stage. The optimal loading for all 3 additives was determined to be 20 wt.%. The effect of the additives in promoting gas production followed the order: HZSM-5 > CaO > biochar. Specifically, with the addition of 20% HZSM-5, the gas yield and volume increased from 26.1% and 247 mL/g to 48.5% and 465 mL/g, respectively.

articles.title: Interfacial Regulation of Ruthenium Oxide-Modified CeVO4 Catalysts for the Catalytic Oxidation of Ammonia
articles.abstract: The selective catalytic oxidation of ammonia (NH3-SCO) to nitrogen (N2) is an effective strategy for controlling NH3 slip emissions from selective catalytic reduction (SCR) systems. This study reports the synthesis of CeVO4 by microwave-assisted deposition-precipitation and the preparation of RuOx-modified CeVO4 catalysts (xRu/CeVO4, x = 0-3 wt%) via wet impregnation, along with a systematic evaluation of the influence of RuOx loading on the NH3-SCO reaction performance. The results demonstrated that the incorporation of RuOx significantly enhanced the low-temperature catalytic activity of the pristine CeVO4 catalyst. The 2Ru/CeVO4 catalyst exhibited the best overall activity, achieving complete NH3 conversion at 240 ℃, whereas the pristine CeVO4 reached only 98.5% NH3 conversion even at 320 ℃. Comprehensive characterization by XRD, TEM, NH3-TPD, H2-TPR, XPS, and in situ DRIFTs revealed that the improved performance originates from strong metal-support interactions (SMSI) between RuOx and the CeVO4 support. At the optimal loading, the introduction of Ru increased the surface chemisorbed oxygen (Oα) content and the number and strength of acid sites. The Ru-O-V and Ru-O-Ce interfacial architectures substantially accelerated low‑temperature NH3 oxidation; however, the strong oxidizing ability of RuOx lowered the N2 selectivity of all the Ru-containing samples with respect to the pristine support and made it decrease further with temperature, which reveals an intrinsic activity-N2 selectivity trade-off. These findings provide mechanistic insight into the role of RuOx in CeVO4-based NH3-SCO catalysts and offer rational guidance for the development of high-performance NH3 abatement materials.

articles.title: Phantom Hand: Research on Dual-Arm Robotic Fine Teleoperation Based on VR Immersive Interaction and Adaptive Shared Control
articles.abstract: Operations in chemical accident sites, nuclear facilities, and other hazardous environments may expose personnel to toxic substances, radiation, high temperatures, or unstable structures. Teleoperation offers a way to keep the operator at a safe distance, but controlling two robotic arms naturally remains difficult because multiple joints, grippers, and viewing directions must be coordinated at the same time. This study develops Phantom Hand, a dual-arm robotic teleoperation system that combines wearable inertial sensing with virtual reality interaction. Five IMUs worn on the chest, upper arms, and forearms capture the operator’s upper-body motion. The reconstructed arm movements are mapped to the two robotic arms, while a VR headset controls the remote camera and two handheld controllers operate the grippers. Several practical problems arise when human motion is transferred directly to the robot. The five IMUs share one RS-485 bus and are read sequentially, so their measurements are aligned using timestamps and short-term quaternion extrapolation. Natural-pose calibration and a chest-centered reference frame are used to reduce mounting errors and the influence of torso rotation. Swing–twist decomposition is then applied to separate coupled shoulder and forearm rotations. The control system also checks data validity, joint limits, command velocity, and communication status. Valid commands follow the operator’s motion, whereas unsafe or incomplete commands are constrained or held. Experiments showed that the average sampling-time span across the five IMUs was 112.43 ms. After calibration, spatial compensation, and temporal alignment were applied, the mean motion crosstalk decreased from 18.7% to 5.4%, while static jitter decreased from 0.684° to 0.241°. The robot also completed a grasping-and-transfer sequence under combined arm, gripper, and visual control. These results show that the proposed system can support natural and fine-grained dual-arm teleoperation using relatively low-cost sensing and interaction hardware.

articles.title: Universal Criticality of Entropy Production in Chemical Reaction Networks
articles.abstract: Author(s): Kyota Tamano and Keiji Saito In homogeneous reversible chemical reactions, a prototypical nonequilibrium phenomenon, entropy-production fluctuations represent a sharper probe of nonequilibrium criticality than entropy-production response to variations in the chemical species concentrations. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 207101] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026

articles.title: Elastic, anelastic, and dielectric relaxations associated with the sequence of ferroelastic and isosymmetric phase transitions in the formamidinium lead halide perovskite CH(NH₂)₂PbBr₃
articles.abstract: Author(s): Dexin Yang, Yulin Peng, and Michael A. Carpenter Here, the authors combine resonant ultrasound spectroscopy (RUS), thermal and dielectric measurements, and strain analysis to reveal a rich sequence of ferroelastic and isosymmetric structural instabilities associated with octahedral tilting and the orientational ordering and dynamics of FA + cations in formamidinium lead bromide (FAPbBr 3 ). Acoustic loss reveals mobile ferroelastic domain walls and their sensitivity to thermal history, while the possibility of local polarity within these walls remains an open question. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 274106] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026

articles.title: Quantum dynamics via score matching on Bohmian trajectories
articles.abstract: Author(s): Lei Wang Bohmian mechanics describes quantum motion as deterministic trajectories steered by the score — the gradient of the log-density. Here, a neural network learns that score on the very trajectories it drives, turning the Schrödinger equation into a self-consistent normalizing flow. This approach opens real-time quantum dynamics to modern generative modeling. [APS Open Sci. 1, 000209] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026

articles.title: Pressure-driven metal-semiconductor-metal transition in Ca₂N: Localization and hybridization of interstitial electrons
articles.abstract: Author(s): Yiwei Liang, Biao Wan, and Huiyang Gou Here, the authors show that compression drives an anomalous metal–semiconductor–metal transition in the electride Ca 2 N. Initial compression localizes the extended interstitial anionic electrons, opening a band gap. Further compression induces rehybridization between the localized interstitial states and Ca d orbitals, restoring metallicity. These findings provide a unified framework linking interstitial electron behavior to electronic phase transitions in electrides. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 274105] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026

articles.title: Gapped and gapless quantum spin liquids on the ruby lattice
articles.abstract: Author(s): Atanu Maity, Rhine Samajdar, and Yasir Iqbal Quantum spin liquids can preserve exactly the same symmetries while harboring fundamentally different patterns of fractionalization. Here, the authors uncover a landscape of gapped and gapless U ( 1 ) and ℤ 2 spin liquids on the ruby lattice, a frustrated geometry realized in programmable Rydberg atom arrays. Distinctive fingerprints in their excitation spectra and spin correlations offer a practical route to telling these elusive states apart in numerical studies and experiments. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 274412] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026

articles.title: Fluctuation-induced supersolidity at the superfluid-solid interface
articles.abstract: Author(s): Baptiste Coquinot, Ragheed Alhyder, Alberto Cappellaro, and Mikhail Lemeshko Supersolidity, the coexistence of superfluidity and crystalline order, typically requires carefully tuned interactions. Here, the authors propose an alternative route: coupling a superfluid to phonons at a smooth solid interface. They show that this coupling can spontaneously induce a periodic density modulation while preserving superfluidity. The mechanism applies to both superfluid helium and Bose-Einstein condensates, and offers a route to engineering hybrid systems combining interfacial supersolidity with bulk superfluidity. [Phys. Rev. B 114, L260503] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026

articles.title: Identification of nonradiative recombination channels in Ga₀.₂Al₀.₈N-AlN wells with deep ultraviolet emission at 215 nm
articles.abstract: Author(s): Alexandra Ibanez, Sunanda Mitra, Sylvia Hagedorn, Wilfried Desrat, Pierre Valvin, Guillaume Cassabois, Julien Brault, and Bernard Gil To help overcome the efficiency limits of 215 nm deep-ultraviolet emitters, researchers have mapped the exact non-radiative recombination channels in Ga0.2Al0.8N-AlN quantum wells. They reveal that structural defects, exciton dissociation, and carrier escape all play distinct, quantifiable roles in thermal quenching. [APS Open Sci. 1, 000210] Published Mon Nov 09, 2026

articles.title: Polarization competition and relaxation rotation in chiral doped ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal
articles.abstract: Since the discovery of ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals (FNLCs), these materials have attracted considerable attention owing to their inherent spontaneous polarization and rapid electric field response characteristics. Recent studies on chiral ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (CFNLC) also indicate that CFNLC has great application potential in fast electro-optical switching and phase modulation. In this study, two new FNLC topological structures were observed in different temperature ranges of CFNLC samples. With the decrease of temperature (138–210 °C), a cross-shaped structure was observed in CFNLC, which was very similar to the conformation observed in cholesteric liquid crystal. Upon further cooling (104–138 °C), the interplay between chiral elasticity and spontaneous polarization leads to the formation of cross-shaped multidomain structures. When a weak alternating current electric field is applied, driven by the cooperative competition among chiral twisting force, spontaneous polarization, and external electric field, the single domain molecular director rotates reversibly and continuously and spontaneously returns to the initial equilibrium state after removing the electric field (relaxation rotation). Afterward, the relaxation rotation behavior of CFNLC was simulated by establishing a model, and the results were in good agreement with our experimental results. Based on the mechanism of relaxation rotation, it is anticipated to realize an optical modulator with superior low driving voltage and high modulation speed. These findings suggest that CFNLC may serve as low-voltage electro-optical platforms for tunable polarization modulation and switching.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Onsager–Dupuis theory, old and new
articles.abstract: The first theory that coupled electrostatics to structural polarization has been the Onsager–Dupuis theory for ice. The basic concepts that these authors developed were rapidly transferred to water as the usual solvent in liquid electrolytes. Subsequently, the Onsager–Dupuis approach has been forgotten and reinvented several times. In this short contribution, I discuss a simplified version of the structural polarization theory that I have formulated with Rudi Podgornik. I show that a phenomenological fourth-order equation for the electrostatic potential follows strictly from the Onsager–Dupuis theory. Furthermore, I derive generalizations of the Grahame equation for a set of different boundary conditions for a charged and polarizable electrode bounding a structured solvent, paving the way for the application of the general theory to experimentally realizable systems.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Polarizability of poly(ethylene oxide) enhances cooperative coupling between Li + and segmental motion
articles.abstract: Ion transport in polymer-based electrolytes is governed by coupled ion–polymer dynamics, yet the role of polymer polarizability remains unresolved. While molecular dynamics simulations have provided insights into the transport mechanism, simulation studies have often neglected explicit polarizability due to a high computational cost, especially for polymeric systems that require long time trajectories to estimate the transport properties. In this study, we consider lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF 6 ) in poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO) melts and perform all-atom molecular dynamics simulations using the APPLE&P force field. We turn on and off the polarization term in the APPLE&P Hamiltonian as a perturbation test and investigate the effects of the polarization term systematically. We find that the polarization term of PEO chains makes the Li + ion bind strongly to the oxygen atoms of the PEO chains. Such strong binding of the Li + ion to oxygen atoms slows down the hopping of the Li + ion between neighboring oxygen atoms of the PEO chains but facilitates the cooperative motion of the Li + ion with particular PEO chain segments at intermediate time scales. The enhanced cooperativity plays a key role in the ion conductivity and the self-diffusion of the Li + ions in PEO melts.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Nonzero-temperature vibronic spectra of polyatomic molecules from a zero-temperature classical trajectory
articles.abstract: By combining coherence thermofield dynamics with the single-Hessian approximation, we enable simulations of low- to medium-resolution vibronic spectra of weakly anharmonic systems at nonzero temperatures, at negligible additional cost relative to zero-temperature calculations. Single-Hessian coherence thermofield Gaussian wavepacket dynamics is exact in any harmonic potential, provided that the reference Hessian is that of the final surface. When applied to Morse systems of increasing anharmonicity and varying temperature, this method successfully captures excited-state anharmonicity and key temperature-dependent spectral features, including hot bands and broadening. By combining the method with on-the-fly ab initio dynamics, we demonstrate its utility by computing the absorption spectra of naphthalene, aminocoumarin C450, and phenyl radical, and the photoelectron spectrum of SeO2−. Within the ab initio single-Hessian approximation, after the zero-temperature spectrum is obtained at the cost of classical molecular dynamics (on the order of hours to days), all nonzero-temperature spectra are computed in seconds.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Partially reactive force field for the UiO-66 metal–organic framework
articles.abstract: UiO-66 is the most widely studied metal–organic framework, on account of its structural tunability given by its capacity of sustaining high amounts of point defects in its structure. Its synthesis mechanism is largely unknown, with only a few works mostly focused on the formation of the Zr-oxide cluster. In this work, a partially reactive force field to model UiO-66, nb-UiO-FF, is introduced. This force field incorporates node–ligand reactivity via a Morse potential and the introduction of dummy atoms to reproduce the anisotropic charge distribution of the Zr atoms in the node. nb-UiO-FF reproduces structural features of both UiO-66 and its isoreticular analog UiO-67 as well as framework stability with or without defects, activated or filled with N,N-dimethylformamide or ethanol. Defect generation and node–ligand binding energies are comparable with density functional theory values. The force field is further employed within a molecular dynamics scheme to study the early stages of solvothermal node–ligand binding. Species with structures corresponding to motifs present in UiO-66 are observed, along with other metastable species. This force field enables studying the self-assembly of UiO-66, as well as the formation of its point defects.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Conformation of microhydrated ethylimidazole isomers explored by microwave spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Chirped-pulse Fourier transform microwave spectroscopy (2.0–18.5 GHz) has been employed to determine the molecular structures of isolated N -ethylimidazole and 2-ethylimidazole and to investigate the structure and intermolecular interactions within N -ethylimidazole⋯H 2 O, 2-ethylimidazole⋯H 2 O, and N -ethylimidazole⋯(H 2 O) 2 . All species probed were isolated in the cold environment of a gas sample undergoing supersonic expansion prior to recording of their pure rotational spectra. Density functional theory calculations were performed to aid spectral assignments and provide further information. Consistent with the results of the density functional theory calculations, N -ethylimidazole was observed to adopt a C 1 geometry when isolated and also when subsumed into N -ethylimidazole⋯H 2 O and N -ethylimidazole⋯(H 2 O) 2 . The isolated 2-ethylimidazole molecule was observed to be C s but adopts a C 1 geometry within 2-ethylimidazole⋯H 2 O. Re-orientation of the ethyl group within 2-ethylimidazole is governed by a shallow potential energy surface. Spectroscopic parameters that include rotational constants ( A 0 , B 0 , and C 0 ), centrifugal distortion constants ( D J , D JK , and d 1 ), and nuclear quadrupole coupling constants of nitrogen nuclei have been determined by fitting parameters in a model Hamiltonian to observed transition frequencies. Precise values of intermolecular bond lengths and angles have been determined by fitting to experimentally determined moments of inertia for a range of isotopologues. All of the hydrates observed during the present work contain a primary hydrogen bond between O–H and the pyridinic nitrogen atom of the imidazole ring and also a weaker hydrogen bond between an O atom of H 2 O and the substituent group on the C2 atom of the imidazole ring.
