We prove an exact reduction: the minimum one-way classical communication for perfect success equals the logarithm of the ternary-cube covering number, equivalently the total domination number of the categorical power (:K₃×:ⁿ):

articles.title: Sustained macroscopic coherence in a superradiant diamond maser under ambient conditions
articles.abstract: Superradiant laser or maser provides a route to sustain macroscopic coherence of many photons and a large ensemble of emitters. Its realization, however, is mostly in gaseous atomic systems, where the number of emitters is relatively small. Solids can accommodate a large number of emitters, but the complex environments can rapidly break the macroscopic coherence and therefore stringent conditions like extremely low temperature are usually required. Here we realize a superradiant diamond maser under ambient conditions, in which optical pumping sustains long-lived coherence among about 10¹⁴ nitrogen-vacancy centre spins with coherence time (2.1 ms) much longer than the spin dephasing time (5.7 us) and the cavity photon lifetime (0.66 us). Continuous-wave emission reaches an output power of -52.3 dBm, corresponding to an intracavity occupation of approximately 10⁹ microwave photons.By tuning the pump and cavity conditions, we observe continuous-wave masing, periodic amplitude modulation and sequences of superradiant bursts, which are attributed, correspondingly, to macroscopic spin coherence synchronized at a fixed frequency, a synchronized limit cycle with a frequency comb, and unsynchronized superradiant transients. This work establishes a new platform for exploring macroscopic quantum coherence, with potential applications in quantum metrology and bright quantum light sources.

articles.title: Role Partitioned Swarm Intelligence for Resilient UAV Coordination in Contested Electromagnetic Environments: A Soccer Field Swarm Formation Framework
articles.abstract: Autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms must coordinate asset protection, threat interception, and collision avoidance even when electronic warfare degrades inter-agent communication. This paper presents Role-Partitioned Swarm Intelligence (RPSI) and its Soccer Field Swarm Formation (SFSF) implementation, which organise agents into Defender, Midfielder, and Forward roles for asset shielding, interception and relay, and outer-layer engagement. The proposed architecture combines rigid-body dynamics on SE(3), Covariance Intersection (CI) for distributed estimation, role-conditioned artificial potential fields, a decentralised High-Order Control Barrier Function (HO-CBF) quadratic-program safety filter, and a communication-health-triggered resilience mode that freezes role assignments and continues with local sensing. A dwell-time-constrained switched-system analysis is provided under stated feasibility and bounded-switching assumptions. In the PX4-based Software-in-the-Loop (SITL) evaluation, RPSI-SFSF achieved 92.7% asset-protection effectiveness (APE) under nominal communication, compared with 86.1% for distributed model predictive control, and 79.8% versus 57.6% under the C5 condition with 0% packet availability. In the 120-run reduced-order packet-drop experiment, RPSI exceeded the homogeneous controller by 8.75, 3.75, and 23.75 percentage points at 100%, 50%, and 0% target-state update packet delivery, respectively. Across-run standard deviations ranged from 10.26 to 20.32 points, and some runs at 100% and 50% delivery fell below the 5.0 m design threshold.

articles.title: AI-Based Particle Size Distribution Prediction from 3D Packed-Particle Tomographic Volumes: A Comparative Study with classical Watershed Segmentation
articles.abstract: Abstract Determining the Particle Size Distribution (PSD) of granular media and powder compacts is vital across condensed matter physics, geological sciences, and materials engineering. While X-ray computed tomography (µCT) captures granular microstructure non-destructively, traditional quantitative PSD estimation relies on classical morphological segmentation (binarization, distance transform, and watershed flooding), which is computationally intensive and sensitive to contact-neck ambiguities. In this work, we investigate whether a compact 3D Convolutional Neural Network (Compact3DCNN, 300,900 parameters) can predict normalized 20-bin PSD histograms directly from unsegmented 3D grayscale volumes without intermediate particle instance extraction. Using a synthetic dataset of 60 independent non-overlapping polydisperse packed-sphere volumes (48<sup>3</sup> voxels) with exact analytic PSD ground truth, we benchmark the CNN against a classical 3D Euclidean distance-transform watershed baseline on an untouched, held-out test split (N = 10, 40 train / 10 validation / 10 test). On this low-to-moderate packing regime (15%–25%), the classical watershed baseline achieved superior accuracy, attaining a mean Earth Mover’s Distance (EMD) of 0.0974 ± 0.0261 voxels compared to 0.3428 ± 0.0949 voxels for the CNN (paired 95% bootstrap CI: [+0.1837, +0.3156] voxels). Measured runtime was 1.19 ± 0.27 ms per volume for the CNN on an NVIDIA RTX 3050 Laptop GPU versus 33.71 ± 7.50 ms for the watershed pipeline on an Intel CPU; however, we emphasize that this reflects disparate computing architectures rather than a controlled hardware comparison. Furthermore, comparison against an empirical training-set-mean baseline (0.6206 ± 0.2440 vx EMD on validation) confirms that the CNN learns volume-specific morphological features (0.3970 ± 0.1335 vx, a 36.0% error reduction). A controlled validation experiment evaluating direct 1D Wasserstein-1 loss training yielded substantially higher error (1.1382 ± 0.4907 vx EMD) than the primary Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence configuration, illustrating optimization challenges in cumulative L1 histogram penalties. Our findings characterize the accuracy-throughput profile in direct volumetric PSD regression and delineate key open challenges for dense granular systems.

articles.title: Collective Modes in Neural Nets and their Dissipative Dynamics
articles.abstract: Walter Freeman’s mesoscopic neurodynamics placed a fundamental problemat the center of brain science, i.e. how local neural activity gives rise to coherentorganization at the scale of whole populations. Here we explore this problemby means of a finite dissipative neural field model. Starting from an initiallyunbiased lattice of interacting complex SU(2) doublets, a transient externalinput drives the network toward a stable macroscopic order. After the inputis removed, the neural field continues to reorganize spontaneously aroundthe established order, while coordinated fluctuations and spatial patternsemerge across distant regions of the lattice. These features provide finite-sizesignatures of the same organizing principles that, in Quantum Field Theory, areassociated with spontaneous symmetry breaking and collective modes. Importantly, theyappear in a finite system, without requiring the thermodynamic limit. Suchfinite neural fields therefore offer not only a bridge between local dynamicsand collective organization, but also a computational tool for developing andtesting new hypotheses about brain function.

articles.title: A 3D-Printed Neural Probe with Geometry-Defined Lithography-Free Metallization and Parylene Encapsulation
articles.abstract: Two-photon polymerization enables neural probes with complex three-dimensional geometries, but selectively metallizing and insulating these structures remains challenging. We present a geometry-defined fabrication process that combines trench-guided metallization with vapor-deposited Parylene-C encapsulation and lithography-free electrode exposure. Re-entrant trenches guide line-of-sight Ti/Au evaporation to form electrically separated interconnects connected to electrode sites and contact pads. A conformal Parylene-C coating then seals the high-aspect-ratio trenches over the interconnects, and a timed, maskless O₂ plasma etch-back followed by SF₆/O₂ plasma treatment exposes the electrodes and pads while retaining insulation over the recessed interconnects. We fabricated a prototype comprising a 2 mm-long shank with four mushroom-shaped electrodes, each 15 µm in diameter. Scanning electron microscopy showed metal deposition at the trench bottoms, Parylene-C coverage, and selective electrode exposure after plasma processing. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy in phosphate-buffered saline showed an impedance magnitude of approximately 1 MΩ at 1 kHz before and after insertion into 0.6% agarose gel. The probe reached a 2 mm insertion depth without observed buckling or fracture. These results demonstrate a fabrication proof of concept for 3D-printed neural probes using geometry-defined metallization and selective Parylene encapsulation, providing a potential route toward scalable fabrication of 3D-printed bioelectronic microsystems

articles.title: Development and Performance Evaluation of an Eco-Friendly Cutting Fluid using Aloe Vera for Sustainable Turning Operations
articles.abstract: An aloe vera-based cutting fluid was developed and tested as an eco-friendly alternative to petroleum-based fluids for  turning mild steel. Conventional water-soluble cutting fluids cool and lubricate effectively, but most do not biodegrade  and have been linked to skin and respiratory problems in machine operators. Fresh aloe vera gel was extracted,  blended, filtered, and mixed with water at a 30:70 ratio to produce the experimental fluid, then tested against a  conventional water-soluble oil emulsion (15% oil, 85% water) under identical turning conditions with a tungsten coated carbide tool. Twenty-seven trials were run per fluid across a three-level, three-factor (3³) design varying cutting  speed, feed rate, and depth of cut. Each trial recorded cutting temperature, chip thickness, and the chip reduction  coefficient (ζ); flank wear was tracked separately under a toolmaker’s microscope. Minitab handled factorial  regression, response surface methodology, and analysis of variance. The aloe vera fluid outperformed the conventional  fluid on every response measured: cutting temperature fell by 10.9%, chip thickness by roughly 7%, and ζ by about  3.7%, with the advantage held across the full tested range. Flank wear accumulated roughly 33% more slowly under  aloe vera. Twelve regression models, factorial and response-surface, fitted the data well for temperature and chip  thickness (R² above 91%) and moderately for ζ (R² 65–73%). These results point to aloe vera-based cutting fluid as a  viable, biodegradable, low-cost substitute for petroleum-based fluids in turning, worth testing across a broader range  of cutting speeds, feeds, and workpiece materials before drawing firmer conclusions.

articles.title: A Wearable Non-Visual Guidance System with an Inspectable Spatial-Cue Core
articles.abstract: Wearable assistance for blind and low-vision users must convert egocentric perception into interpretable action cues. This paper presents a three-node guidance system comprising smart glasses, an RK3588 edge unit, and a four-motor wristband. RGB-D/stereo perception, YOLO11s detection, metric depth estimation, and 3D back-projection produce task-specific spatial relations. An upstream cue core validates task intent, entity, mode, relation, and state before transmitting vector packets over BLE; the wristband applies roll compensation and renders directional haptic feedback. Placement-level relative-vector errors are 1.13 ± 0.38, 1.66 ± 0.47, and 1.76 ± 0.30 cm at nominal 30, 50, and 70 cm placements (n = 15 per distance). Grasping succeeds in 37/40 trials under a 60 s timeout. A supplementary study report compares smart glasses and a white cane in 100 participants, including 50 blind and 50 low-vision participants, using a counterbalanced mixed design and collision counts as the primary outcome. In the blind group, mean collision counts are 4.46 with glasses and 12.54 with the cane; the report gives t(49) = 30.92, p < 0.001, and Cohen’s d = 4.37. In the low-vision group, the mean paired difference is 0.14 collisions, with a reported 90% confidence interval of [−0.01, 0.29], meeting the specified ±1.5-collision equivalence criterion. The reported age-adjusted group-by-device interaction is significant (F (1, 97) = 412.5, p < 0.001), supporting visual-status-dependent benefit. By integrating performance indicators and behavioral outcomes, this multidimensional framework provides a practical tool for evaluating wearable assistive systems, supports safer and more effective autonomous assistance, and contributes to broader human–machine interaction research.

articles.title: Cycle-Scale Forecasting of Galactic Cosmic Ray Intensity: A Skill Assessment and The Role of Recurrent Solar Wind Structure
articles.abstract: Long-term forecasting of Galactic Cosmic Ray (GCR) intensity is conventionally assessed by how closely a model reproduces the observed record rather than by whether it outperforms a naive alternative. Using monthly Oulu and Moscow neutron monitor data for 1976 to 2025, together with heliospheric current sheet (HCS) tilt, Interplanetary Magnetic Field (IMF) magnitude, solar wind speed and the aa geomagnetic index, we evaluate cycle-scale Cosmic Ray Intensity (CRI) forecasting against a persistence benchmark under strict rolling-origin validation. Here all smoothed predictors constructed causally so that no information from after the forecast issue time enters any forecast. A conventional regression on CRI level, evaluated at matched forecast horizons, attains out-of-sample correlations as high as 0.91 yet fails to beat persistence at every horizon. It acquires a systematic bias of approximately − 4% when extrapolated from the calibration period into a later heliospheric state characterised by weaker IMF. Reformulating the target as the change in CRI over the forecast horizon largely removes this bias. The point-estimate skill is negative at six months, where persistence is difficult to beat, and turns positive from twelve months onward, reaching 0.36 at twenty-four months. All 95% bootstrap intervals nevertheless include zero and Diebold-Mariano tests do not reject equal predictive accuracy with persistence. A 27-day recurrence index derived from the aa index, hitherto known as a descriptive correlate of cosmic ray flux, contributes negligible aggregate skill at twelve months despite being individually significant there, and raises the aggregate point-estimate skill at eighteen and twenty-four months, with a standardised coefficient rising monotonically with lead time from 0.09 to 1.20. The orthogonal component of the index, after removal of the variance shared with the mean-field predictors, retains most of that contribution. No statistically robust incremental forecast skill from aggregate transient injection was detected, on either the Richardson and Cane near-Earth Interplanetary Coronal Mass Ejection (ICME) list or the CDAW SOHO/LASCO catalogue, under an acceptance criterion fixed in advance. Calibrating the neutron monitor network against AMS-02 daily proton fluxes accepts seven of twenty-two station and detector combinations and yields median response rigidities from 10 to 72 GV, with Thule, Oulu and Moscow degenerate near 10 GV despite cutoffs differing by a factor of eight, and with atmospheric depth rather than cutoff governing the response. Forecast skill is highest and most variable among monitors near 10 GV, falls to a lower level near 19 GV, and falls essentially to zero at 72 GV, consistent with useful cycle-scale skill being concentrated below approximately 20 GV. Nested cross-validation confirms that adaptive choice of the predictor specification yields no improvement over the fixed model, while retaining the recurrence index in every training fold at the longer horizons. No skill score attains significance at 95%. For the present validation design the estimated detectability threshold is about 0.4, and the observed 0.36 falls just below it, so the results do not provide sufficient evidence to reject the persistence benchmark. We conclude that the results provide suggestive evidence that recurrent solar wind organisation contains information beyond the mean interplanetary field at horizons of eighteen to twenty-four months, that no comparable evidence is found for aggregate transient injection, and that the available record is too short to establish differences of this magnitude at conventional confidence.

articles.title: Paired but out of step: Why electron pairing alone is not enough for room-temperature superconductivity
articles.abstract: Levitating trains, ultra-efficient energy storage, and quantum computers: superconductivity could unlock a wealth of possibilities for the future. New research led by scientists from Utrecht, Leiden, and Munich has now shed light on one of the key requirements for achieving superconductivity at room temperature. Their findings, published in Science, bring scientists a step closer to understanding how this might be achieved.

articles.title: How palm orientation shapes spin characteristics in volleyball jump serves
articles.abstract: A new biomechanical study has uncovered how elite volleyball players control ball spin during jump serves, offering fresh scientific insight into one of the sport's most decisive offensive skills.

articles.title: Physicist develops detector capable of counting photons for quantum computing
articles.abstract: Detecting a single photon is a challenge in itself. But what if you also want to know exactly how many photons arrive at a particular point at the same time? Physicist Erik Baalbergen is working on light detectors that can do just that. They form a key building block for the optical quantum computer of the future.

articles.title: Coupling of structural preordering and density fluctuation: A unified picture of nucleation in metallic glasses
articles.abstract: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Volume 123, Issue 45, November 2026. SignificanceHow do crystal nuclei emerge in disordered materials: through structural preordering or density fluctuation? Combining large-scale atomistic simulations and in situ synchrotron X-ray experiments, we find that both processes develop ...
authors: Tianding XuXiaodong WangQingping CaoShao-Qing DingSuya LiuKe YangDongxian ZhangYao YangJian-Zhong JiangaInternational Center for New-Structured Materials
State Key Laboratory of Silicon Materials

articles.title: Stability and Relaxation of Electron-Phonon Systems at Strong Coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the kinetic properties of Migdal-Eliashberg theory (MET) for electron-phonon interactions at strong coupling. Previously, the system was found to be dynamically unstable at large couplings within a Markovian quantum Boltzmann approximation. Using the quasiclassical Kadanoff-Baym equation, we show that this instability is absent when non-Markovian effects are taken into account. We also analyze the long-time relaxation dynamics at strong-couplin, and find a clear imprint of the non-Markovian nature of the dynamics: in an intermediate temperature range between the Debye frequency and the coupling strength, the relaxation rate becomes linear in temperature with Planckian slope, while the leading relaxation mode acquires a large imaginary component, producing strongly oscillatory decay. Our results imply that any instability which preempts superconductivity must arise from effects beyond MET, such as phonon softening or polaronic effects at finite electronic bandwidth. This shows that the characteristic phonon frequency is not a fundamental bound on T_c, and leaves open a route to higher T_c in multi-orbital electron-phonon systems.

articles.title: PFAS-induced modulation of vesicle diffusiophoresis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) partition into biological membranes and alter their properties is central for elucidating PFAS toxicity. Here, we experimentally investigate how the partitioning of anionic PFAS affects the surface charge of phospholipid vesicles and consequently, their electrokinetically driven vesicle motion, in particular diffusiophoresis. We find that PFAS partitioning enhances vesicle diffusiophoresis, consistent with a model combining the Nernst-Planck and Langmuir adsorption equations. Desorption experiments, together with quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring (QCM-D), further reveal that substantial lipid loss occurs during PFAS partitioning. We attribute this loss to lipophobic interactions between the fluorocarbon chains of PFAS and the alkyl chains of lipids. Our findings provide new mechanistic insights into how PFAS may disrupt biological systems.

articles.title: Nonequilibrium Spin-Glass Order in a Long-Range Quantum Ising Glass and Its Sensitivity to Noise
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study spin-glass order after a transverse-field quench in a long-range quantum Ising glass. The diagonal-ensemble Edwards-Anderson order coincides at the no-quench and zero-field endpoints, yet in between cold shells overshoot it and hot shells undershoot it. This stems from a competition in correlation space between the rigidity of populated eigenstates and the spread of their pair patterns. Under weak longitudinal dephasing the zero-field endpoint is exactly pinned while the characteristic finite-quench response fades, giving a self-referenced noise probe for quantum spin simulators.

articles.title: Flexoelectric Switching of Lock-and-Key Topological Bits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological defects in nematic liquid crystals are high-energy sites of reduced order. We show that a point defect can be stabilized in pillbox-shaped pores. The pore shape promotes lock-and-key docking similar to that observed for colloidal particles. The defect docks in one lobe or the other, displaying bistability. Furthermore, the defect moves like a charged object in an external electric field. An in-plane field drives the defect from one lobe to the opposite lobe, where it remains once the field is removed. The velocity is linear in field strength and reverses with polarity, consistent with flexoelectric coupling. Within the pore, the nematic around the defect carries a positive bulk bound charge density, compensated by negative space charge in the rest of the fluid and on the bounding surfaces. The external field breaks the mirror symmetry of the pore and drives the defect motion. Defect displacement increases the component of the net dipole in the domain along the field. Antagonistic curvature in peanut-shaped pores repels the defect, allowing pore geometry to set distinct switching thresholds. The defects, while not topologically required, are long lived, so information can be stored in their position, allowing them to serve as topological bits. Arrays of topological bits store and rewrite binary information in defect positions, offering a route to reconfigurable, field-addressable soft materials.

articles.title: Electrically tunable superconducting dimensionality in stripe-ordered monolayer MoTe₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dimensionality governs the stability of collective quantum states, including whether Cooper pairs can establish the phase coherence required for superconductivity. In solids, however, electronic dimensionality is usually encoded in the crystal structure and is difficult to control reversibly. Here we show evidence that monolayer 1Tprⁱme-MoTe₂ develops a stripe charge-density wave that reorganizes its low-energy electronic states into quasi-one-dimensional channels. Raman spectroscopy and scanning tunneling microscopy identify the stripe order, whereas directional transport and tunneling spectroscopy reveal superconducting correlations confined to the stripe direction and insulating behavior perpendicular to it. Electrostatic doping weakens the transverse insulating response and drives the system into phase-coherent two-dimensional superconductivity. These results show that stripe charge order can reconfigure superconducting dimensionality and make it electrically tunable within a single crystalline layer.

articles.title: PolyGPT: A Decoder-Only Transformer for Polymer Electrolyte Design
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07438v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing polymer electrolytes requires control over both material properties and chemical structure. Here, we present PolyGPT, a Transformer with 38.3 million parameters that generates polymer repeat units from optional property targets, requests to include or exclude a specified chemical feature, and an electrolyte-domain condition. Using the model selected by validation loss, we compared unconditional generation with requests for electrolyte-associated structures, a low glass-transition temperature (Tg), or both. Unconditional and electrolyte-only generation achieved structural validity of 99.46% and 99.59%, respectively. However, electrolyte conditioning increased repetition: uniqueness among valid outputs fell from 99.99% to 51.74%. At a Tg target of 246.11 K, we compared generation with and without electrolyte conditioning, and adding the electrolyte condition slightly reduced the predictor-estimated mean absolute error from 26.97 to 26.07 K, but the fraction of all attempts yielding distinct valid polymers within 50 K of the target fell from 82.35% to 32.31%. When we also required absence from the training catalog, these yields were 59.90% and 19.71%, respectively. The lower yield persisted with a tighter 25 K tolerance. Domain conditioning also weakened control of inclusion requests: the mean fraction of attempts producing valid polymers containing the requested chemical feature fell from 94.27% to 31.27%. Across nine checkpoints, earlier models sometimes produced more distinct, catalog-unseen polymers meeting the Tg target: 10,000 checkpoint model with electrolyte conditioning and 30,000 checkpoint model without it. Together, these results show why property error alone is insufficient for evaluating conditional polymer generation. It must be considered alongside repetition, training-catalog novelty, and whether combined design requests are satisfied.

articles.title: Percolation of discorectangles oriented predominantly along two mutually perpendicular directions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07484v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The percolation of finite-thickness elongated objects---discorectangles (stadiums)---oriented predominantly along two mutually perpendicular directions is studied, extending recent results for zero-thickness sticks. The angular distribution is the ``Maltese cross'' parametrized by α. Based on the known analytic expression for the excluded area of a discorectangle pair, the percolation threshold is estimated by the eigenvalue method. The discorectangle connectivity matrix is represented as the stick matrix plus a rank-1 term determined by the constant part of the excluded area, C=4lw+π w², which gives the approximate relations λₘₐₓDRapproxλₘₐₓstⁱck+C and n_cDRapprox n_cstⁱck/(1+C n_cstⁱck). Finite thickness shifts the absolute thresholds and affects the first normalization, whereas the second normalization, written through maximum eigenvalues, cancels the additive geometric contribution and preserves only the orientational dependence, explaining the universality of the normalized curves. Monte Carlo simulations of unit-length discorectangles with aspect ratios 8, 16, and 32, various domain sizes, periodic boundary conditions, and union--find scaling analysis confirm the theoretical predictions.

articles.title: Ultrafast Moiré Exciton Dynamics Revealed by Two-Dimensional Coherent Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moiré superlattices of van der Waals heterostructures confine excitons into discrete energy levels in finite-sized samples, yet their internal relaxation pathways remain obscured by inhomogeneous broadening. Here, using two-dimensional coherent spectroscopy (2DCS), we directly resolve seven discrete energy levels of the moiré-confined intralayer WS₂ A exciton in an hBN-encapsulated WS₂/WSe₂ heterostructure, corresponding to a confinement depth of 57.02 meV. By tracking the population of these levels over picosecond delays, we uncover a two-stage thermalization process: an effective exciton temperature drops from 171.8 to 99.3 K within 1.2 ps through rapid intra-manifold population redistribution, followed by a slower recovery toward quasi-equilibrium mediated by exciton--environment interactions. Kullback--Leibler divergence analysis confirms the progressive transition from a non-equilibrium to a Boltzmann-distributed population. Our results establish state-resolved access to moiré exciton dynamics and provide a foundation for exploring nonequilibrium many-body phenomena in moiré quantum materials.

articles.title: Initial heat-current decay versus thermal transport at a three-body resonance in a one-dimensional Fermi gas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically study kinetic relaxation and heat transport in a dilute one-dimensional spinless Fermi gas near a three-body resonance. The full vacuum amplitude of a finite-range interaction enters the linearized Boltzmann collision operator. The resonance position that maximizes the initial heat-current decay rate lies above the one that minimizes the integrated relaxation time. At higher resonance energies, coupling among momentum moments transfers heat-current weight to a slow mode. A faster initial decay can therefore coexist with slower subsequent relaxation and a larger low-frequency heat response. The dissipative responses at two resonance positions reverse their ordering at least twice as frequency increases. Bounds on the full collision operator confirm both reversals. A fourth-moment distortion exhibits the same separation of relaxation scales and provides a probe through the momentum distribution.

articles.title: Reduced Glass Transition Temperature with Preserved Super-Arrhenius Dynamics in Nanoconfined Glass-Forming Nematic
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The molecular dynamics and glass-forming behavior of 4-cyano-3-fluorophenyl 4-butylbenzoate (4CFPB) liquid crystal was investigated by broadband dielectric spectroscopy in anodic aluminum oxide cylindrical nanopores of 35 and 73 nm diameter. The primary α-relaxation was analyzed using the Vogel-Fulcher-Tammann (VFT) and Mauro-Yue-Ellison-Gupta-Allan (MYEGA) models. Confinement reduces the glass transition temperature from 217 K in bulk to 208-210 K, while preserving the super-Arrhenius character of the α-relaxation and a fragility index of approximately 60. Unlike in previously studied 6 and 8 nm pores, the secondary β-relaxation remains detectable, with possible intramolecular contributions examined by density functional theory calculations. Next to the pore-size-dependent changes in molecular dynamics and glass transition temperature, cold crystallization is not observed. These findings highlight the distinct effects of geometrical confinement on molecular relaxation, glass formation, and crystallization kinetics.

articles.title: Signature of charge-3e tunneling in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cooper pairing is a fundamental aspect of superconductivity and results in charge transport with a basic unit of 2e (e is the electron charge). This basic unit can manifest itself as the denominator in the formula for Shapiro steps of ac Josephson effect-nhf/(2e), where h is the Planck constant, f is the ac frequency and n is an integer. Violation of this standard formula may suggest unconventional physics, such as nhf/4e for charge-4e superconductivity. Here, we report discovery of a new sequence of nhf/3e in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions. The microwave frequency/power, temperature, and current annealing dependences of this exotic sequence consistently point to hf/3e as the unit for Shapiro steps, indicating a Josephson tunneling process involving a trio of electrons (3e). This bunching of an odd number of charges distinguishes itself from well-established superconducting processes, which are carried by composite bosons made of an even number of charges. The unusual observations highlight the important interplay between competing charge orders in twisted bilayer systems.

articles.title: Masked diffusion as random sequential adsorption: an exactly solvable model for parallel decoding
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Masked diffusion models generate text by reversing a stochastic masking process. Unlike autoregressive LLMs, which generate text one token at a time, they can reveal many tokens in parallel, at the price of an error, since tokens revealed together are drawn independently. We show that this trade-off maps onto the statistical physics of driven many-particle systems. (i) For any data, the error of parallel generation is the entropy production of the generation process relative to the reversed masking process. (ii) For Markov data, generation is a random sequential adsorption process with labelled gaps, which we solve exactly for any number of steps. (iii) For many steps, the error becomes the dissipation of a slowly driven system: the unmasking schedule plays the role of the driving protocol, the number of steps that of its duration, and the error is set by a thermodynamic metric that we obtain in closed form from the mutual information between tokens. Optimal schedules are geodesics of this metric. The exact solution shows how correlations in the text shape both the error and the quality of the output. The longer the correlations, the more the error concentrates at the start of generation. Schedules that start with small steps then gain more, both in path error and in perplexity, and need fewer steps to reach their asymptotic behaviour.

articles.title: Pressure-Induced Phase Transition and Superconducting Properties of LiPdH₂: A First-Principles Study
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a detailed first-principles investigation of the superconducting hydride LiPdH₂, focusing on the competition between its tetragonal P4/mmm and rhombohedral Rbar3m phases. Our results reveal a pressure-induced phase transition near 220 GPa, where Rbar3m overtakes P4/mmm in thermodynamic stability. The Rbar3m phase is predicted to be superconducting, with Tᵣₘ c values of up to 46 K in the harmonic approximation and 28 K at the anharmonic level. In contrast, although the P4/mmm phase is stable up to 200 GPa, it maintains a more rigid electronic character with weaker hydrogen involvement, resulting in lower superconducting performance. Ionic quantum and anharmonic effects play a decisive role in stabilizing P4/mmm and shaping its superconducting properties, whereas these effects diminish rapidly with pressure. These findings highlight the interplay between structural stability, hydrogen orbital activity, and quantum effect in optimizing the superconductivity of hydrogen-based superconductors.

articles.title: Zero-Point Renormalization Reshapes the Shift Current: The Role of Electron-Phonon Coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shift current (SC) drives the bulk photovoltaic effect, holding promise for near-instantaneous, low-dissipation photodetection and energy conversion. The current understanding of SC relies primarily on a single-particle picture, in which the SC is determined purely by band dispersion. While many-body effects from directly excited quasiparticles, such as excitons, magnons and phonons, have been explored, the renormalization of electronic states by quantum virtual-phonon coupling --- inherent in essentially all solids and particularly decisive for transport --- remains unaddressed. Here, using first-principles calculations, we identify this missing channel --- band-renormalized shift current (BRSC) --- in monolayer MoS2. We find that the zero-point renormalization alone, without any polarization-carrying photoexcited phonons and with barely any alteration of the band dispersion, dramatically reshapes the SC spectrum: emergent low-energy peaks arise from phonon-assisted optical transitions between momentum-distinct states, with a pronounced redshift of higher-energy features. A mere 1.0% strain sharply tunes the BRSC, whereas raising the temperature enhances it. Our findings overturn the band-structure-only paradigm, establishing electron-phonon coupling as an indispensable ingredient for nonlinear photocurrent and opening a strain-thermal route for engineering next-generation optoelectronic responses.

articles.title: Heat Transport Mechanisms in MOF-5
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We find that MOF-5 supports both long-lived phonons and linker vibrations whose split spectra signal a breakdown of the phonon quasiparticle approximation. Combining mode-projected molecular dynamics spectra with spectral Wigner heat transport, we resolve two contrasting transport channels: low-frequency particle-like phonon propagation decreases strongly from 200 to 500 K, whereas wave-like phonon coherence remains nearly constant and supplies about half the intrinsic conductivity at 500 K. A phenomenological extrinsic scattering model provides a plausible explanation for the discrepancy between calculated and measured conductivities in terms of both its magnitude and temperature dependence. We also identify signatures of phonon quasiparticle breakdown in the linker vibrations of ZIF-8 and HKUST-1, indicating that this feature extends to other metal-organic frameworks.

articles.title: Microscopic Origin and Josephson Signatures of d-Wave Superconductivity in Monolayer FeSe
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monolayer FeSe on SrTiO₃ exhibits high-temperature superconductivity with an electron-only Fermi surface, raising fundamental questions about its unconventional pairing mechanism. Motivated by recent Josephson scanning tunneling microscopy evidence for nodeless d-wave superconductivity, we investigate the microscopic role of the Fe dₓy orbital using an experimentally constrained multiorbital theory. A tight-binding model fitted to quasiparticle interference and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveals substantial dₓy character near the Fermi level and dominant nearest-neighbor hopping, in contrast to the conventional kinetic-frustration picture of iron-based superconductors. Both itinerant spin-fluctuation calculations and strong-coupling exchange approaches favor a robust d-wave pairing state, whose interband pairing components allow a fully gapped quasiparticle spectrum. We further establish a symmetry-based selection rule for spatial Josephson tunneling, revealing characteristic bond-centered maxima and mirror-enforced interference zeros that distinguish d-wave pairing from competing s-wave states. These symmetry-enforced nodal lines survive near Fe-site impurities, while a pronounced contrast between the d- and s-wave Josephson patterns persists around vortices despite the loss of mirror protection. Our results connect the unconventional dₓy electronic structure to nodeless d-wave superconductivity and demonstrate the power of spatial Josephson interference for resolving pairing symmetry in multiorbital superconductors.

articles.title: First-order condensation and meniscus pinning in finite open wedges
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study first-order condensation in finite open wedges using classical density functional theory (DFT) and compare the resulting microscopic phase behaviour with recent macroscopic predictions. Two geometries are considered: a symmetric wedge formed by two identical inclined walls and an asymmetric wedge formed by a vertical and an inclined wall. The DFT calculations confirm the two condensed morphologies predicted for the symmetric wedge and the three morphologies predicted for the asymmetric wedge and their emergence depending on the wedge size, opening angle, and wall contact angle. Under partial-wetting conditions, the microscopic phase boundaries are in nearly perfect quantitative agreement with the macroscopic predictions, including reentrant changes between pinned and depinned meniscus configurations and the appearance of the semi-double-pinned state in the asymmetric wedge. Under complete-wetting conditions, the DFT phase diagrams retain the topology predicted by the macroscopic theory, but the single-pinned region is systematically enlarged. This shift is attributed to adsorbed liquid films, which reduce the effective width available to the gas and thereby increase the effective aspect ratio of the confinement.

articles.title: Coherent phase slips in coupled rings: from weak to strong interactions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the coherent transfer of circulation between two weakly coupled lattice rings of ultracold bosons, in which a persistent current initially prepared in one ring oscillates back and forth between the rings without net transfer of particles. Combining Bose--Hubbard simulations with their Gross--Pitaevskii and quantum phase model limits, we show that similar current oscillations arise from two distinct microscopic mechanisms. At weak interactions, particles in each occupied momentum mode tunnel independently between the rings, leading to a transfer time inversely proportional to the inter-ring tunnelling, extensive particle-number fluctuations and entanglement distributed over many Schmidt components; this mode-exchange dynamics is suppressed by self-trapping as the interactions increase. At stronger interactions and large filling, in the phase-dominated regime, circulation is instead transferred through a second-order collective process between many-body persistent-current states, with a transfer time scaling as the inverse square of the inter-ring tunnelling in the weak-link limit. Number fluctuations then remain of order one instead of growing with the particle number, and within each number sector the system evolves into coherent superpositions of two many-body configurations, distinguished by which ring carries the circulation. The entanglement accessible under number-conserving operations therefore reaches up to approximately one bit. We propose a quench protocol to prepare the initial state and estimate transfer times within reach of current ring-lattice experiments, identifying coupled rings as a platform to study coherent quantum phase slips and to manipulate persistent-current states.

articles.title: Hydrodynamic interaction in Lattice Fokker Planck for dilute polymer dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the BGK-type kinetic model for polymer dumbbells and its lattice Boltzmann implementation by incorporating hydrodynamic interaction (HI) effects to accurately recover the slow-variable dynamics governed by the Smoluchowski equation. Unlike Brownian dynamics approaches, which demand the computationally expensive evaluation of the square root of the configuration-dependent diffusion tensor at every time step, this kinetic method is straightforward to implement and avoids such overhead entirely. Consequently, it achieves a significant reduction in computational cost. We validate the model in steady and transient shear flows, demonstrating its ability to capture the distinct signatures of hydrodynamic interactions on bulk rheological properties.

articles.title: Dynamical Keldysh model for colored noise and finite relaxation rate
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Keldysh model describes quantum dots subjected to Gaussian noise with infinite correlation time. For multi-component noise coupled through non-commuting matrices, the spectrum exhibits a pseudogap. We solve the model for coloured noise with any correlation time, 1/ γ. Finite memory leads to the pseudogap being filled, its peaks merging and the line narrowing.

articles.title: Dynamical effects induced by synthetic SU(1,1) gauge fields
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08447v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compact gauge fields are powerful tools for controlling quantum dynamics and topological phases of matter. Non-compact gauge fields are particularly relevant for open systems, where particles or energy are exchanged with the environment. Here, we investigate the wavepacket and entanglement dynamics induced by an SU(1,1) gauge field. The wavepacket undergoes non-Abelian non-compact Bloch oscillations, in which the spectrum of an auxiliary one-dimensional quantum problem determines the transition between stable oscillations and unstable amplification. In the unstable adiabatic regime, the wavepacket probes an SU(1,1) topological defect, and its amplification is determined solely by a hyperbolic solid angle in Minkowski space. Threading an SU(1,1) gauge field through a bosonic tight-binding model yields the bosonic Kitaev model, whose volume or super-volume entanglement scaling is governed by the stability of the gauge field. We further propose an experimental realization of an SU(1,1) gauge field in a spinor condensate. Our results can be generalized to other non-compact groups and higher dimensions, providing a geometric framework for entanglement control, selective amplification, and engineering energy transfer.

articles.title: Flat-band systems: A platform to realize the moments of Quantum Metric
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08479v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum metric is a fundamental geometric property of Bloch bands that governs a wide range of physical phenomena, yet experimentally accessing it remains challenging. We show that the momentum-space variation of the quantum metric can be probed through the real-space dynamics of a Gaussian wave packet prepared in an isolated flat band. Following the application of a weak constant force, we demonstrate analytically that the leading order change in the wave-packet variance is linear in time and contains a contribution proportional to the wave-packet averaged gradient of the quantum-metric trace. This geometric contribution remains finite despite the absence of band dispersion. We illustrate the effect using a gapped Lieb lattice with an exactly flat middle band and vanishing Berry curvature, allowing the quantum-metric contribution to the spreading to be isolated. The numerical results agree with the analytical prediction and confirm the quantum-metric contribution to the wave-packet spreading. The required lattice preparation, tunable hopping amplitudes, applied force, and density measurements are compatible with established ultracold-atom techniques, providing a possible platform for observing the predicted response. Our results establish wave-packet spreading as a dynamical probe of quantum geometry in flat-band systems.

articles.title: Multipartite Entanglement, TQFT Partition Functions and PL Bordism
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a previous work we conjectured that the multi-invariants of the ground state of a gapped (d-1)+1-dimensional system, labeled by bipartite (d+1)-edge-colored graphs encoding closed oriented d-manifolds M, compute the partition functions Z(M) of the low energy topological quantum field theory (TQFT), up to non-universal factors determined by the local structure of the triangulation. In this paper we determine which combinations of partition functions can be isolated from the non-universal factors. The answer is governed by oriented bordism. If M is null-bordant, Z(M) is obtained from an explicit, state-independent finite family of multi-invariants, up to a power of Z(S^d) which is fixed to be Z(S^d)χ⁽M⁾/² for even d and can be removed for odd d. Conversely, the obstruction is measured by a quotient of the group of "residues" of colored graphs which receives a surjective map from the oriented bordism group, with kernel precisely the torsion subgroup as far as smooth manifolds are concerned. In d=4 the obstruction is the signature: Z(M)/Z(S⁴)χ⁽M⁾/² can be extracted if and only if σ(M)=0. This is due to the fact that the first Pontryagin class p₁ has a local expression and thus eⁱθσ⁽M⁾=efracⁱ³θⁱⁿt_M p₁ cannot be separated from the non-universal factors. Torsion invariants, in contrast, are not obstructed: for the ground state of the 4+1-dimensional invertible phase with partition function (-1)ⁱⁿt w₂w₃ we compute the multi-invariants exactly, and two graphs with identical local data, encoding the Dold manifold and CP²× S¹, give opposite signs.

articles.title: Threshold-Free Symmetry-Enriched Topological Quantum Memory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07017v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that non-Abelian symmetry enrichment can protect a toric code memory against incoherent electric noise at any bond error probability pin[0,1]. For a toric code on the honeycomb lattice coupled to Sp(N) rotors, with electric anyons carrying the fundamental representation, we construct an efficient minimum-weight decoder whose logical error probability decays exponentially with system size for Nge40, a conservative sufficient bound. The same decoder also rules out strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking in the fundamental channel of Sp(N) under the corresponding local decoherence in two dimensions. The construction extends to other symmetries, including SU(N).

articles.title: Single-shot ground-state preparation via strongly coupled baths
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07021v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Preparing ground and thermal states of quantum many-body systems is a central task in quantum simulation. Dissipative protocols have emerged as a promising solution for both near-term and fault-tolerant hardware, but most constructions rely on weak system-bath coupling, leading to slow cooling. Here, we construct cooling protocols at strong system-bath coupling, and demonstrate accurate state preparation within even a single cooling cycle. Our protocols combine dynamically ramped ancilla energy levels with time-dependent couplings to optimize the trade-off between cooling error and physical time. For a general class of free-fermion systems, we reduce the dynamics exactly to a two-level scattering problem: ground-state cooling becomes a control problem of maximizing resonant excitation transfer while suppressing non-adiabatic heating. We then construct a family of ``Möbius-Ingham'' protocols, which reach optimal error scaling for gapless spectra and almost-exponential suppression of the leading heating error for gapped spectra, as a function of the cycle period. In our free-fermion benchmarks, Möbius-Ingham cooling lies on the Pareto frontier between steady-state error and cooling time among the controls tested. We further demonstrate its effectiveness in interacting Ising and t-V chains and the two-dimensional Fermi-Hubbard model. Finally, we extend our construction to Gibbs state preparation, showing how free-fermion thermal states can be prepared in a single cycle.

articles.title: 1/N corrections to langle TJJrangle and langle TTTrangle in the critical O(N) vector and Gross--Neveu--Yukawa models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07394v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the subleading corrections in the 1/N expansion of the three-point functions langle TJJrangle and langle TTTrangle in the three-dimensional critical O(N) vector and Gross--Neveu--Yukawa models. We determine the coefficients of the two parity-even conformal structures and the corresponding conformal collider parameters. The calculation uses an expansion of momentum-space Feynman diagrams in a soft external momentum, together with the contact terms required by background gauge and metric sources. The sums of the structure coefficients reproduce the known current and stress-tensor two-point normalizations. We also compute these coefficients independently using the metric and mixed metric--gauge derivatives of the sphere free energy. Extrapolating the large N results to the O(2) vector model yields reasonably good agreement with recent numerical bootstrap bounds. At N=2, our γ and t₄ predictions lie within the joint bootstrap region under weaker spectral assumptions; their deviations from the more restrictive interval midpoints are only 3.28% and 4.44%, respectively. We discuss the implications for energy flux, high-frequency conductivity, and shear response near quantum criticality.

articles.title: Higher-order topological quantum battery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07401v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A quantum battery is a next-generation energy-storage device that exploits genuinely quantum properties such as superposition and coherence. We propose a second-order topological quantum battery coupled to a photonic crystal described by the breathing-Kagome model, where optical loss is present on all lattice sites while nonlinear gains are introduced selectively at the output sites. Under these realistic non-Hermitian conditions, the system exhibits a clear topological phase transition manifested in both the ergotropy and the charging power. Remarkably, perfect work extraction is realized in the topological phase, where the maximum value of the ergotropy is quantized and acts as a good topological-phase indicator. The triangular geometry coherently distributes energy into two quantum batteries, where mirror-symmetry-protected phase synchronization gives rise to collective energy storage.

articles.title: Exact and Near-Exact Inverse Renormalization Group with Constrained Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.07641v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish conditions for exactness of the inverse renormalization group via constrained Markov processes, a class of Monte Carlo simulations which sample the degrees of freedom within a block on a fine lattice under the constraint that they remain consistent with the corresponding degree of freedom on the coarse lattice according to a forward renormalization group transformation. We show analytically, for an arbitrary transformation, that constrained Markov processes correspond to an exact inversion of the renormalization group at the fixed point action, and to a near-exact inversion in the vicinity of the fixed point. We then optimize renormalization group transformations directly on inversely renormalized configurations to effectively map the action onto itself and ensure computational stability in the generation of configurations for high-dimensional systems. Starting from a set of uncorrelated configurations for the three-dimensional φ⁴ quantum field theory at lattice volume V=16³, we invert the renormalization group with constrained Monte Carlo to construct a set of uncorrelated, near-equilibrium configurations for V=128³ and extract two critical exponents of the system. The inversion exhibits no critical slowing down, with dynamic critical exponent z=0.03(2).

articles.title: Accessing Fractional Wilson Lines from U(1) Monodromy Defects on the Fuzzy Sphere
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wilson lines are gauge-invariant probes of charge screening and deconfinement, which can detect the response of quantum critical matter to an external charge, but their universal information at strongly-coupled critical points remains hard to access. Here we investigate a continuous family of U(1) monodromy defects of the three-dimensional O(2) Wilson--Fisher conformal field theory, which is dual to fractional Wilson lines in the critical noncompact Abelian Higgs model with one unit-charged scalar. We realize this continuous family of defects within the fuzzy-sphere framework by threading a fractional Aharonov--Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We observe the emergence of charged operators carrying fractional transverse spins, as a characteristic signature of the imposed monodromy. The appearance of displacement operator at its protected dimension supports the conformal nature of this defect line. Crucially, we resolve no relevant symmetry-preserving defect scalar, and identify charge-one monopole operators as relevant symmetry-breaking deformations. Assuming the duality, these results provide non-perturbative evidence that fractional Wilson lines of the critical Abelian Higgs model are stable conformal lines.

articles.title: Disorder-blind Mpemba acceleration of quantum state preparation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08424v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using the strong Mpemba effect to accelerate relaxation by initial-state design requires suppressing the slowest mode, which typically needs prior knowledge of the system. However, in disordered systems, this mode is sample-dependent, so a fixed preparation generally retains a slow-mode overlap. We show that a ``blind'' preparation, designed from the clean chain without knowledge of the disorder realisation or its distribution, can start farther from stationarity yet overtake a reference in typical samples of a dephased disordered XX chain. It requires only the chain geometry and the particle number. At strong dephasing, the density dynamics maps to a resistor chain, and an exact inverse-generator identity links the residual overlap to the spatial resistance profile. We find two distinct thresholds: a finite mean resistance suffices for diffusion, but the residual overlap decays as L⁻¹/² with chain length L only when the resistance variance is finite; rare weak links slow this decay. We predict the fraction of samples in which the blind preparation wins, which is an ensemble-level measure of its reliability. Finite-size calculations support both scaling regimes with interactions at strong dephasing. We give preparation circuits and a density readout for the residual overlap.

articles.title: Defect Anomalies at a Distance
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08476v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Surface defects carry Weyl and gravitational anomalies that generalize the central charges of two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs) and characterize the anomalous response of gapless surface modes to background geometry. These anomalies usually appear as contact terms on the defect. We explain how they are encoded at a distance, in scheme-independent integrated bulk stress-tensor correlators. We derive sum rules for them in terms of defect operator data, establish a lower bound on the boundary Weyl anomaly in three-dimensional CFTs, and illustrate our results with explicit examples.

articles.title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.08488v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We provide an explicit scheme to realize a quantum memory in any 2D non-chiral topological order. For this, we construct syndrome extraction circuits based on the Turaev-Viro path integral as well as a classical algorithm for decoding on the fly. We prove that our scheme has a threshold under a local stochastic circuit-level noise model and discuss how to generalize it to implement topological logical gates.

articles.title: Symmetry-guided catalogue of chiral phonon materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2506.13721v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chiral phonons---circularly polarized lattice vibrations with angular momentum---have become a key frontier in quantum materials. They offer ways to control heat and information through their coupling to electronic spin, orbital, and valley degrees of freedom. We present a symmetry-based framework that classifies phonon chirality across all crystallographic space groups. Our approach, built on symmetry representations of phonon angular momentum in reciprocal space, identifies three phononic material classes, namely, crystals with no chirality, chiral crystals with conventional s-wave helicity, and a group of achiral crystals hosting exotic higher-order helicities such as d, g, and i waves. Through high-throughput computation, we shortlist the most promising material candidates for experimental investigation. These results are compiled into the open-access Chiral Phonon Materials Database, which enables screening for materials with the desired chiral phonon properties. Our work establishes both the theoretical framework and the material platform required to exploit the properties of chiral phonons for next-generation thermal management and quantum technologies.

articles.title: Evolution from intralayer to interlayer superconductivity in a bilayer t-J-Jbₒₜ ladder
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.07545v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the bilayer cuprate superconductors and nickelate superconductor La₃Ni₂O₇, we investigate the evolution from intralayer to interlayer superconductivity in finite-width bilayer t-J-Jbₒₜ ladders, where t is the in-plane electron hopping, J is the in-plane spin interaction, and Jbₒₜ is the inter-plane spin interaction. By means of the density matrix renormalization group calculations, we map out the quantum phase diagram of the bilayer two-leg ladders by tuning Jbₒₜ in a large doping range δ = 1/8 - 1/2. We find that a large Jbₒₜ can always drive an interlayer superconductivity by coupling the two layers in both the Luther-Emery liquid and Luttinger liquid states. By coupling two Luther-Emery liquid states, the in-plane superconductivity evolves to inter-plane superconductivity either through an intermediate charge density wave (CDW) phase or directly, depending on doping ratio. This emergent CDW phase, which exists over a finite doping range, appears to develop from the CDW state of the two-leg ladder at δ = 1/4. By coupling two Luttinger liquids, the in-plane Luttinger liquids show a transition to the inter-plane superconducting phase at large Jbₒₜ, as reported in previous literature. Interestingly, in the intermediate Jbₒₜ regime we find that while the in-plane Luttinger-liquid features remain stable, the inter-plane superconductivity can develop an enhanced quasi-long-range order with the power exponent Kzzᵣₘ SC sim 1. At last, we show that the interlayer superconductivity is also stable by coupling the bilayer three-leg t-J ladders by a strong Jbₒₜ interaction, from both the Luther-Emery liquid and Luttinger-liquid states.

articles.title: Gate-tunable Josephson parametric amplifiers based on semiconductor nanowires
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.00305v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Superconductor-semiconductor hybrid materials have been extensively used for experiments on electrically tunable quantum devices. Notably, Josephson junctions utilizing nanowire weak links have enabled a number of new gate-tunable qubits, including gatemons, Andreev level qubits and spin qubits. Conversely, superconducting parametric amplifiers based on Josephson junctions have not yet been implemented using nanowires, even though such nearly quantum limited amplifiers are key elements in experiments on quantum circuits. Here we present Josephson parametric amplifiers based on arrays of parallel InAs nanowires that feature a large critical current as required for linear amplification. The resonance frequency of the devices is gate-tunable by almost 1 GHz, with a gain exceeding 20 dB in multiple frequencies and markedly improved noise performance compared to a low-temperature commercial amplifier. This platform enables on-chip integration of gate-tunable qubits with nearly quantum limited amplifiers using the same hybrid materials and on any substrate.

articles.title: Bond-resolved STM with density-based methods
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.11929v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bond-resolved scanning tunneling microscopy (BRSTM) provides intramolecular contrast with CO-functionalized tips, but its interpretation requires a description of both probe relaxation and orbital-dependent tunneling. We introduce a simulation framework that combines the Full-Density-Based Model (FDBM) for CO-tip relaxation with Chen's derivative rules applied directly to real-space density-functional-theory (DFT) wave functions. We test the method against a series of constant-height BRSTM images of perylene-3,4,9,10-tetracarboxylic dianhydride (PTCDA) on Ag(111), acquired in 10~pm tip-height increments, and published data for 1,5,9-trioxo-13-azatriangulene (TOAT) on Cu(111). The simulations reproduce the principal intramolecular contrast features and their evolution with tip height. The comparison identifies distinct roles for the substrate: it modifies the partially occupied molecular states and probe--sample forces in PTCDA/Ag(111), while its influence on the TOAT/Cu(111) contrast remains relevant even without substantial changes in molecular-orbital occupation. Our framework thus provides a practical and accurate route to interpreting BRSTM images that incorporates, from a single DFT calculation, the separate contributions of electronic structure and CO-tip relaxation.

articles.title: The generic Mott transition in the sine-Gordon model through an embedded worm algorithm
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.20901v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The generic Mott transition in one-dimensional quantum systems can be described by the sine-Gordon model with a tilt via bosonization. Because the configuration space of the sine-Gordon model separates into distinct topological sectors, standard local Monte Carlo schemes are limited to very small system sizes. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the smooth worm (SmoWo) Monte Carlo algorithm which enlarges the configuration space to allow smooth transitions between topological sectors. The method combines worm updates with event-chain Monte Carlo moves. We explicitly prove its validity and quantify its performance. Thanks to the substantial acceleration achieved by the SmoWo algorithm, we are able to simulate large system sizes, providing a precise picture of the different phases and critical behaviour of the sine-Gordon model.

articles.title: Kelvin-Helmholtz and counter-superflow instabilities driven by differential effective rotation in a three-component Bose-Einstein condensate
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.19207v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Interfacial hydrodynamic instabilities in multicomponent superfluids provide a versatile platform to explore nonequilibrium quantum dynamics beyond classical fluid analogues. We study dynamical interfacial instabilities in a quasi-two-dimensional three-component Bose-Einstein condensate confined in a harmonic trap, where differential effective rotation between neighboring components is generated through selective phase imprinting. A component with an imprinted vorticity lⱼ acquires an azimuthal phase winding φⱼ = lⱼθ, producing a superfluid velocity v_θ(rⱼ) = lⱼhbar/mrⱼ at interface radius rⱼ and an effective angular velocity Ωⱼeff = lⱼhbar/mrⱼ². The differential effective rotation ΔΩⱼeff = Ωⱼeff - Ωⱼ₊₁eff between neighboring components constitutes the sole driver of interfacial shear and the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability (KHI). Three instability regimes are examined: KHI in the strongly immiscible limit, counter-superflow instability in the partially miscible regime, and a parameter window where both mechanisms coexist. A hydrodynamic pressure-balance model is derived, showing that the KHI onset condition depends only on ΔΩⱼeff. Time-dependent Gross-Pitaevskii simulations and a Bogoliubov-de Gennes analysis identify the dominant unstable modes, whose spatial structures are consistent with the observed density modulations. The dominant azimuthal mode is set by a competition between shear-driven destabilization and surface-tension stabilization, confirmed by numerical simulations with different imprinted vorticities. The results show that a three-component condensate with two tunable interfaces provides a controlled platform for studying multicomponent quantum hydrodynamics, with instability dynamics significantly richer than those of binary mixtures.

articles.title: High-pressure elastic properties of GeO2 polymorphs up to 120 GPa
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.09469v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We systematically investigated the phase stability, pressure dependence of the elastic properties, and elastic anisotropy of four GeO2 polymorphs: rutile-, CaCl2-, alpha-PbO2-, and pyrite-type phases using theoretical calculations based on density functional theory. The elastic constants were calculated at regular pressure intervals within the stability fields of each phase, as determined by static enthalpy calculations. We further employed a strain-coupled Landau free-energy expansion to describe the pressure evolution of the elastic response associated with the rutile- to CaCl2-type transition and elucidate the origin of the elastic softening near the transition. The rutile- to CaCl2-type phase transition is consistent with a Landau-type second-order transition. As the transition is approached, elastic softening develops in the rutile-type phase, resulting in anomalous pressure dependence of the bulk and shear moduli. The calculated elastic-wave anisotropy increases markedly near the transition, primarily due to the rapid reduction in shear-wave velocity, reaching a maximum of approximately 190% at 20 GPa. Following the transition, the anisotropy decreases sharply in the CaCl2-type phase and exhibits discontinuity at the CaCl2-type/alpha-PbO2-type phase boundary. The higher-pressure alpha-PbO2- and pyrite-type phases exhibit comparatively weak pressure dependence of anisotropy, with small discontinuities at their respective phase boundaries. The pyrite-type phase has the lowest anisotropy with AP = 4% and AS = 12% at 120 GPa, consistent with its high-symmetry cubic structure and nearly isotropic elastic-wave propagation.

articles.title: Inclined surfaces bias bacterial swarming expansion and edge organization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.01281v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bacterial swarming is the collective expansion of dense populations of motile cells across hydrated soft surfaces, yet gravity is usually treated as a fixed background condition in standard horizontal assays. We used surface inclination to examine how agar-surface orientation relative to gravity affects the expansion of Enterobacter sp. SM3 swarms. At macroscopic scales, we found that colony expansion depended non-monotonically on inclination, with the strongest spreading at intermediate inclinations and weaker expansion under shallow or near-inverted conditions. Paired up-facing acute and down-facing obtuse configurations with the same tilt magnitude showed different expansion responses, suggesting that swarm expansion depended on both tilt magnitude and which side of the agar surface faced upward relative to gravity. Inclination also produced downhill-biased colony morphologies. For microscopic scales, particle image velocimetry (PIV) analysis showed generally lower mean activity under inclination than in the flat references, with a non-monotonic angular response. The downhill tip showed slower motion, shorter spatial correlations and smaller vortex cores than the upper region. To interpret the macroscopic trends, we extended a two-phase thin-film model by introducing an effective gravity coupling projected normal and tangential to the agar surface. Simulations suggest that the surface-tangential component mainly drives lateral redistribution, whereas the surface-normal component modifies film pressure and helps distinguish up-facing from down-facing configurations.

articles.title: The Puzzle of the Replica Transition at Ising Criticality
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.13802v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Critical quantum ground states exhibit universal properties governed by conformal field theories (CFTs), yet some of these universal signatures remain poorly understood even for the paradigmatic Ising chain in 1+1d at its quantum critical point. In particular, numerical studies have long identified universal contributions to its ground-state measurement statistics, but their origin remains unexplained. Replica methods offer a natural framework to study such post-measurement statistics, with the replica limit Q→ 1 describing the physical Born-averaged ensemble. Here we show that, for the monitored critical Ising chain, the replicated post-measurement ensemble of states itself undergoes a phase transition precisely at the physically relevant replica limit Q → 1, preventing standard replica treatments. We use boundary conformal field theory (BCFT) methods to explain the underlying mechanism of this transition. Our methods yield a perturbative analytic calculation of the universal O(1) constant in the Shannon entropy of the measurement record, previously known only numerically. We also apply our tools to study measurement-averaged spin correlators, providing a unified description of the universal properties of measurement outcomes and post-measurement states.

articles.title: Principles of Quantum Communication Theory: A Modern Approach
articles.abstract: arXiv:2011.04672v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This is a preliminary version of a book in progress on the theory of quantum communication. We adopt an information-theoretic perspective throughout and give a comprehensive account of fundamental results in quantum communication theory from the past decade (and earlier), with an emphasis on the modern one-shot-to-asymptotic approach that underlies much of today's state-of-the-art research in this field. In Part I, we cover mathematical preliminaries and provide a detailed study of quantum mechanics from an information-theoretic perspective. We also provide an extensive and thorough review of quantum entropies, and we devote an entire chapter to the study of entanglement measures. Equipped with these essential tools, in Part II we study classical communication (with and without entanglement assistance), entanglement distillation, quantum communication, secret key distillation, and private communication. In Part III, we cover the latest developments in feedback-assisted communication tasks, such as quantum and classical feedback-assisted communication, LOCC-assisted quantum communication, and secret key agreement.

articles.title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qubit Quantum Processors: Simulating Fermions, Bosons, and Gauge Fields
articles.abstract: arXiv:2409.03747v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Key to solving many societally-relevant problems in materials science, quantum chemistry and nuclear physics is understanding their fundamental microscopic quantum behaviour. All of these problems can be phrased as fermionic (e.g. electrons) and bosonic particles (e.g. lattice vibrations, photons) interacting with each other. However, solving these systems of strongly-interacting fermions and bosons is out of reach for classical computers and also non-error-corrected qubit-only quantum computers. In this paper, we introduce a hybrid qubit and bosonic-oscillator quantum-simulation framework, which is so efficient that it could simulate some of these strongly-correlated problems even without error correction. Specifically, we leverage the available universal bosonic gate set with O(1) operations per gate as a function of the bosonic cutoff. This enables our framework to provide exact decompositions of higher-order fermion-boson interactions, including notoriously challenging terms such as (2+1)D gauge theories. We show how to compile dynamics, ancilla-free partial error detection, non-local observable measurement, and ground state energy estimation using both qubit-boson variational quantum eigensolvers and quantum signal processing. We introduce a "post-qubit quantum advantage" experiment which is both out of reach of near-term qubit-only quantum computers and classical computers. We develop a new qubit-based algorithm for simulating a beamsplitter which scales as almost-linear with boson number cutoff Nmax, asymptotically outperforming previously-known qubit methods. Our framework can be used in superconducting, as well as trapped-ion and neutral-atom hardware. This work establishes digital hybrid qubit-boson quantum simulation as a promising and advantageous method for solving the many challenging strongly correlated fermion-boson models of relevance to science and technology.

articles.title: Fractional Quantum Hall States: Infinite Matrix Product Representation and its Implications
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.12165v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a novel matrix product representation of the Laughlin and related fractional quantum Hall wavefunctions based on a rigorous version of the correlators of a chiral quantum field theory. This representation enables the quantitative control of the coefficients of the Laughlin wavefunction times an arbitrary monomial symmetric polynomial when expanded in a Slater determinant or permanent basis. It renders the properties, such as factorization and the renewal structure, inherent in such fractional quantum Hall wavefunctions transparent. We prove bounds on the correlators of the chiral quantum field theory and utilize this representation to demonstrate the exponential decay of connected correlations and a gap in the entanglement spectrum on a thin cylinder.

articles.title: Lee-Yang theorem for fermions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.23942v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Lee-Yang theorems are a powerful tool for studying many-body systems, with applications ranging from analyzing phase transitions to proving the efficiency of certain classical and quantum algorithms. In this work, we prove a Lee-Yang zero-freeness theorem for the partition function of a broad class of interacting fermion models, implying the existence of a provably efficient quantum algorithm for estimating their ground-state energies. This class includes several well-known models such as the attractive Hubbard model, repulsive Hubbard model on bipartite graphs, and the interacting Hofstadter model. Our results also rigorously establish the nonexistence of phase transitions in these models in the presence of a nonzero local external field.

articles.title: Nonperturbative optomechanics with thin, weakly reflective intracavity dielectrics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15749v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Levitated dielectric sensors are often treated as perturbative probes of a pre-existing optical field. We show that this picture fails for a novel sensor geometry: a dielectric plate whose transverse extent captures the full optical mode. Even an optically thin sensor with modest refractive index can heavily restructure the intracavity fields, effectively partitioning a cavity into two subcavities with substantial cross-coupling and producing new optical resonances and trapping sites with properties which deviate from the standard intuition. Conventional perturbative expressions for the cavity frequency shift and optomechanical coupling depart from the exact solution at thicknesses as small as simλ/(10n). Furthermore, cavity locking decreases the coupling and increases the trap stiffness by orders of magnitude, and the coupled subcavity structure permits appreciable optical cooling at zero detuning, a distinct behavior unique to this nonperturbative regime.
