The central thesis is that machine learning should not be treated merely as an offline data-analysis tool; rather, when constrained by physical insight and embedded in robust data infrastructure, it can support real-time diagnostics, surrogate modeling, anomaly detection, experimental optimization, and progressively autonomous discovery workflows.

articles.title: Chromatic Calorimetry -- A Novel Approach to Validate Energy Resolution and Particle Discrimination
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.09511v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Chromatic calorimetry (CCAL) analyses particle detection by utilizing scintillators with distinct emission wavelengths to measure the longitudinal energy deposition of particle showers in high-energy physics, improving particle identification (PID) and energy resolution. By stacking scintillators in order of decreasing emission wavelength, CCAL enables layer-specific energy measurements, analyzed via amplitude fractions (fᵢ = Aᵢ / sumⱼ Aⱼ) and center of gravity (langle zcₒg rangle = sumᵢ zᵢ Eᵢ / sumᵢ Eᵢ). This thesis presents results from two CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) experiments conducted in 2023 and 2024, complemented by GEANT4 simulations of a quantum dot (QD)-based CCAL design, to validate its potential for future colliders such as the Future Circular Collider (FCC).

articles.title: Negative quasiprobabilities redistribute (and complex ones reduce) the information in unabsorbed photons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.00740v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Negative Kirkwood--Dirac quasiprobabilities are credited with the quantum advantage of interaction-free measurement and postselected metrology. We test that claim on the task interaction-free measurement was designed for: learning about a sample while it absorbs as little light as possible. The quasiprobability distribution of path and output gives the linear response to a weak sample: its real part responds to absorption, its imaginary part to a phase. For a pure single photon passing once through any interferometer, the Fisher information about transmittance per absorbed photon is the direct-transmission value minus a sum of squared imaginary parts: no interferometer or readout beats direct transmission. Negativity only concentrates information in weakly lit outputs. These imaginary parts depend on the output basis, not the sample, so an optimal basis with all terms real always exists. A single photon beats direct transmission only through a phase response, which for an optical line needs a thick or inhomogeneously broadened sample, or through many passes when absorptions go uncounted, as a critically coupled resonator shows. For detecting a weak absorber, negativity gives a single-shot advantage that does not accumulate over repeated trials. The advantage that accumulates comes from outputs dark without the object, and needs no negativity.

articles.title: Message-passing graph persistence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Message-passing graph neural networks (GNNs) are limited in expressive power by the one-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman test. Persistent homology (PH) provides topological descriptors that can complement GNN representations, but existing approaches typically compute persistence separately from the representation learning process. In this paper, we introduce Message-Passing Graph Persistence (MGP), a family of topological descriptors that incorporates message passing into graph filtrations. At each filtration step, node embeddings are updated using the current subgraph and associated with persistence events. These embeddings also determine the representatives of connected components during persistence computation. We prove that MGP is invariant under graph isomorphism and that it is strictly more expressive than the PH-based descriptors it extends. We evaluate MGP on an expressivity benchmark and on several graph classification and regression datasets. Experiments show that MGP outperforms other PH-based descriptors on most of these datasets.

articles.title: Quantifying Trait-State Hierarchy in EEG Foundation Model and Signal Processing Embeddings
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) measures brain activity through recording electrical potentials of the scalp. EEG recordings capture two distinct sets of characteristics in the signal: (1) emphTraits -- information that remains relatively constant over the course of a recording session, such as subject identity, age, and sex; (2) emphStates -- signatures that encode responses to external stimuli, including visual, auditory, and motor information. There is limited understanding of how different EEG modeling features (signal processing and foundation models) encode state and trait characteristics. In this work, we quantify state- and trait-level features captured by EEG embeddings using a hierarchy metric and kNN purity on Brain-Computer Interface dataset trials, and find that a majority of EEG features form a macro-trait hierarchy (embeddings form trait-level clusters with micro-states within). Our linear probe results indicate that this hierarchy structure leads to suboptimal state distinguishability, negatively impacting BCI performance of EEG foundation models. To mitigate this, we explore normalization techniques that reduce trait-specific information in embeddings and provide a sim 10% improvement in balanced accuracy for state classification. Additionally, we observe that when fine-tuning models for downstream state decoding, embedding spaces transform from macro-trait to macro-state hierarchies, which in turn lead to better state decoding.

articles.title: Autonomy and Coordination in Intelligent Manufacturing: A Recursive Autonomous Agent Framework
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intelligent production requires systems to make decisions and organize work according to production goals and operating conditions. It also requires continuous adjustment through feedback. This paper analyzes intelligence in human production organizations from a complex adaptive systems (CAS) perspective. The analysis identifies two coupled mechanisms: individual autonomy and collective coordination. Individual autonomy enables actors to form local decisions using available information. Collective coordination aligns these decisions with shared goals and joint constraints. Learning and adaptation improve both mechanisms over time. A production-system model formalizes how local decision rules and coordination jointly form system decisions. On this basis, we propose the Recursive Autonomous Agent (RAA) framework, which combines goal-driven autonomous agents with a recursive organizational structure. Goal contracts define local objectives and operating boundaries, while capability contracts support the selection and composition of production units. Common interfaces allow coordinated groups to participate as units in larger organizations, connecting equipment, production lines, and factories. RAA thus provides an engineering approach to next-generation intelligent manufacturing, translating the requirements of intelligence, openness, and system-wide integration into mechanisms for autonomous and coordinated production.

articles.title: From Handcrafted to Generative: RLVR-Optimized Icon Generation for Alexa+
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alexa+ devices with screens display animated icons during conversations to visually reinforce what is being said. The original set of these icons was hand-drawn by designers one at a time, a process that produces polished results but is time-consuming and cannot scale to the range of topics encountered in open-ended conversation. We describe an automated pipeline, deployed in production, that generates these vectorised animated icons from a text description alone and surfaces relevant animations to customers based on their ongoing conversation. The pipeline decomposes icon creation into a sequence of stages (image generation, semantic decomposition, vectorisation, styling, and animation). Its quality is determined at the very first of these, image generation, on which every downstream stage depends. We therefore focus on improving this first and most critical stage. Because the icons are rendered on small display canvases under strict design guidelines, generations are often unsuitable for production. Supervised fine-tuning is not viable, as no dataset of line-art icons exists under these constraints. Instead, we design objective verifiers that automatically flag generations violating the design guidelines, and use them to fine-tune a flow matching image generation model via reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR). The fine-tuned model raises the pass rate from 15.7% to 58.7% (3.7x) under a VLM judge that is independent of the reward model. Both the trained model and the verifier are deployed in the production pipeline, where the verifier also serves as the automated quality gate before final design review.

articles.title: CARM: Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking for Reliable Scientific Super-Resolution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) can reconstruct fine-scale Earth-observation fields from coarse observations, but reconstruction accuracy alone does not provide a calibrated rule for identifying reliable spatial regions. Conformal Mask Calibration (CMC), built on conformal risk control, converts a spatial uncertainty score into a trust mask and controls the expected worst-case local distortion under exchangeability. However, its fixed threshold can become miscalibrated in Earth-observation streams affected by seasonality and episodic events. We propose CARM (Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking), a statistical framework for adaptive spatial risk control under temporal distribution shift. CARM maintains experts with heterogeneous update rates and aggregates their threshold proposals online using an asymmetric surrogate loss, balancing rapid adaptation to distribution changes against stability during relatively stationary periods. All updates are causal and use only mature feedback available after a fixed delay, allowing CARM to operate with any SR model that provides a spatial uncertainty score. We prove that the time-averaged mask-conditioned risk converges to at most α at an O(1/T) rate, without distributional assumptions and for any choice of aggregation weights across experts. On a daily South China Sea chlorophyll-a SR stream, CARM reduces the empirical violation rate from 43.49% to 9.38% and the moving-average exceedance frequency from 47.29% to 1.22% at α=0.10, while retaining a non-trivial trusted region. Experiments on ERA5 wind and OSTIA sea-surface temperature further show consistent relative improvements across multiple SR backbones.

articles.title: Unsupervised Neural Operators for Rotating Relativistic Stars: High-Fidelity Equation of State Inference and Pulsar Spin Evolution at Scale
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Observed populations of rotating neutron stars~(NSs) with millisecond-order periods are powerful probes of fundamental physics. Mass-radius measurements inform poorly constrained properties of degenerate nuclear matter, whereas high-fidelity population synthesis connects unknowns in NS formation and binary evolution to large radio-timing surveys. However, repeated structure calculations are prohibitive due to the computational cost of solving the highly coupled partial differential equations of axisymmetric general relativistic hydrostatic equilibrium that govern rotating NS interiors. Non-rotating calculations or approximate rotational corrections can bias equation of state inference and limit the fidelity of population synthesis in tracing the evolutionary history of progenitors and propagating equation of state uncertainties. In this Letter, we develop physics-informed neural operators that can solve the axisymmetric problem with high accuracy and negligible computational cost. Our solvers are trained in a fully unsupervised setting, with the training objective informed solely by the partial differential equations, and achieve a 10³× speed-up with negligible accuracy loss. These solvers enable scalable EoS inference that self-consistently accounts for rotation and repeated stellar-structure calculations during binary evolution, making spin predictions that account for rotational structure and EoS uncertainties computationally accessible to population synthesis.

articles.title: Learning When Human Decisions Matter: Executor-Relative Consultation Value for LLM Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05814v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models increasingly automate complex tasks, but human decision capacity does not scale with their capabilities. In many applications, humans remain essential for providing private context, authority, or judgments unavailable to the agent. We formulate human decision capacity allocation: given multiple consultation opportunities and a limited budget, at which decisions should an LLM agent consult a human? The central challenge is estimating consultation value, which is executor-dependent because the same human input may benefit different downstream agents differently. We introduce Consultation Value Distillation (CVD), which estimates consultation values offline using Monte Carlo executor rollouts and distills these values into lightweight predictors for budgeted allocation, requiring no rollout-based value estimation at deployment. Across five batch and three sequential settings with two frontier executors, CVD improves allocation through joint and continuation-aware value learning, while independent consultation values remain competitive in several settings. CVD also broadly outperforms direct prompting and Value of Information where applicable, remains robust with substantially less rollout supervision, and enables nearly lossless approximate allocation at low search cost.

articles.title: Noise-regularized training of quantum circuit Born machines under a finite shot budget
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06630v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum circuit Born machines (QCBMs) can learn distributions that are hard to sample from classically, but their value depends on generalizing from finite training data. Here, we study how hardware noise affects this generalization. We show that, for any noise process, the generalization gap of a QCBM trained with the maximum mean discrepancy is bounded by the complexity of the distributions the noisy model can reach. Scrambled local Pauli noise contracts this complexity but biases the model towards the uniform distribution, so residual noise acts as a regularizer whose optimal strength can be intermediate. We propose GENIE, a framework that realizes a chosen noise level with capped error mitigation and selects it during training from held-out data within a fixed execution budget, with provably bounded regret. In simulations on synthetic and census data, GENIE stays close to the best of four noise-control strategies, whereas every fixed noise level falls short in many settings.

articles.title: Order selection rules and interband geometry in dissipative nonlinear transport
articles.abstract: Rate-independent nonlinear transport probes quantum geometry, although its coefficients can also containcontributions determined solely by the dispersion and depend on the dissipative steady state. Here we establisha parity selection structure across response orders in a controlled open system: a Bloch Hamiltonian coupled toa uniform wide-band fermionic bath. Taking the dc limit before weak coupling at fixed positive temperature, weprove that the rate-independent coefficient, or finite part, vanishes at every odd order for a smooth periodic scalarband, irrespective of spatial symmetry, whereas finite terms remain allowed at even orders. Closed interband pathscan supply the phase absent from scalar vertices and lift this restriction. For separated bands, a nonzero finitepart at odd orders therefore requires virtual interband processes, even when only one band crosses the chemicalpotential. We derive the full transverse third-order finite part for two bands in closed form. In a tilted Chern model,competing geometric terms reverse the sign of the curvature–metric contribution alone, while comparison with tworelaxation-time prescriptions resolves the dependence on the description of the steady state. Within the samebath model, subleading longitudinal terms combine with nonlinear poles to shift the asymptotic conductivity scalingintercept away from the microscopic finite part. The resulting framework connects a selection rule and its interbandmechanism to the calculation and extraction of rate-independent nonlinear transport.

articles.title: Bad metallicity in the semi-quantum regime of the Hubbard model
articles.abstract: Bad metals exhibit approximately T-linear dc resistivity beyond the Ioffe--Regel limit. That this behavior occurs in systems with radically different ground states suggests it is a generic manifestation of strong local correlations. We test this hypothesis in the infinite-U Hubbard model with small hole densities using exact diagonalization to compute thermodynamic and transport properties of finite clusters. Upon cooling, we find an intermediate temperature range, an electronic analogue of the ``semi-quantum regime'' of liquid helium, in which quantum effects produce a roughly T-independent compressibility, yet the resistivity is T-linear and exceeds the Ioffe--Regel limit. Entry into this regime is accompanied by the formation of quasi-local ferromagnetic ``spin cages'' around doped holes, regions that facilitate local quantum motion embedded in a fluctuating spin background, analogous to the transient crystalline cages thought to control incoherent transport in semi-quantum liquid helium. Remarkably, despite the simplicity of the model, the bad metal behavior found here resembles that seen in various material platforms.

articles.title: Authenticated delivery of BB84-keyed messages through lossy image channels using hardware-derived keys
articles.abstract: Pipelines that key image-based information hiding with quantum key distribution (QKD) assume the stego image arrives bit-exact, and keys from noisy quantum hardware are unusable without reconciliation. This work addresses both. BB84 runs on IBM’s ibm fez are reconciled with Cascade, confirmed by hashing and compressed by Toeplitz privacy amplification; at 4096 qubits every run yields 1,110–1,237 secure bits, identical for both parties, at a quantum bit error rate of at most 0.98%. The keys protect messages with authenticated encryption, Reed– Solomon coding and key-driven embedding in discrete cosine transform (DCT) or wavelet domains. A pre-registered evaluation on 300 images shows that a key-driven least-significant-bit reference scheme, representative of lossless-channel designs, recovers 0 messages after JPEG recompression, while coded DCT embedding delivers at least 99% of messages at every quality tested; restricted post hoc to images above 40 dB peak signal-to-noise ratio, it carries 0.218 bits per pixel at quality 95 and 0.005 at quality 50. A hardware-keyed message decrypts and verifies after JPEG quality 50. This robustness costs detectability: at the smallest payload tested, a simple learned detector separates the robust variants from covers with an area under the curve of at least 0.797, against 0.517 for the reference scheme. The keys characterize hardware noise rather than deployable secrecy, and the security estimate is asymptotic.

articles.title: Verified Bounds on the Charging Gain From Reactive Power at Battery-Buffered Electric Vehicle Fast-Charging Stations
articles.abstract: A battery that supports a fast-charging station has to be recharged through the same feeder, and its converter can supply reactive power while it charges. This paper quantifies how much additional charging that reactive capability admits and how firmly the estimate can be stated. For each control policy, an AC-feasible operating point is paired with an upper bound from an outer linear approximation of the branch-flow relaxation; the dual bound is evaluated in rational arithmetic. A fixed command is then checked over a continuous box of load and source-voltage uncertainty with an invariant voltage enclosure. Four balanced feeders (16, 33, 69, and 141 buses) and controlled changes of R/X ratio, upstream short-circuit level, connectivity, and head-branch rating separate voltage, thermal, and converter limits. At the representative 33-bus location, reactive dispatch raises admissible charging from 250.57 kW to 469.35 kW, and the optimization bracket that remains is 1.1×10− 4 kW. A Volt-VAR curve tuned for the same state inside the IEEE 1547 Category B setting ranges reaches the same value, so the 124.52-kW shortfall of the default curve is a setting effect. A tuned curve frozen across load levels loses 5.60 kW at the held-out state. In a public 33-bus case, reactive support relieves a binding head-branch limit while the local voltage stays inside the default dead band. All 3340 reported operating points were re-solved with MATPOWER and OpenDSS: voltage magnitudes agree within 7.6×10–10 p.u., and no admitted point violates a network limit.

articles.title: Old Corrugated Containerboard (OCC) Bleaching for Tissue Application: Metal Ion Removal Pretreatments and Hydrogen Peroxide-Based Delignification
articles.abstract: This study investigates the oxidative bleaching of Old corrugated containerboard (OCC) using alkaline hydrogen peroxide to improve pulp brightness and evaluate its suitability for hygiene tissue applications. As conventional recycled fiber supplies decline, OCC represents a promising alternative recovered fiber source. Metal-ion control pretreatments, including ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) and diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid (DTPA) chelation, acid washing, and flotation deinking, were evaluated to remove Fe, Cu, and Mn, which catalyze peroxide decomposition through Fenton-type reactions. Two OCC sources from the southern United States and Colombia were compared to assess the effect of furnish origin on bleachability. The U.S. OCC exhibited higher lignin content (Kappa 89 vs. 61.8), longer fibers (1.7 vs. 0.9 mm), and lower ash content (2.1% vs. 10.1%) than the Colombian OCC. Metal-ion removal improved peroxide stability, resulting in brightness gains of up to 17 ISO points and Kappa reductions of up to 36 points. Bleached OCC was evaluated alone and in blends containing 5–20% commercial bleached recycled fiber pulp (RFP). Although OCC reduced blend brightness, it improved softness, bulk, and compressibility without significant losses in tensile strength, demonstrating its potential as an alternative recycled fiber for tissue manufacturing.

articles.title: TraceRIFT: Reference-preserving ensemble selection for discrete fracture networks from incomplete traces
articles.abstract: Incomplete surface traces admit multiple three-dimensional discrete fracture networks with different intensity, size, connectivity and orientation. Reducing these candidates to a small ensemble can discard useful alternatives even when the generated pool contains them. We introduce TraceRIFT, a framework that separates candidate-support loss from retrieval regret and treats ensemble selection as predictive scenario coverage. Candidate-support loss measures the pool's minimum attainable error; retrieval regret measures the additional error introduced by shortlist construction. Set quality is evaluated through the closest retained network, linking ensemble reduction to retention of plausible geological alternatives. Coverage in an eight-attribute space values each network by its contribution beyond a prescribed core of the baseline Reference ranking. TraceRIFT preserves that core while permitting at most two additions beyond the original Reference top ten. Enumerated-greedy optimization of the submodular objective gives a ((3/4)) approximation guarantee for the finite-scenario proposal before an independent predictive check. On 3,276 held-out simulated parent networks, all selectors retain ten networks from identical query-specific 64-member pools. Under fragmented or missing-surface observations, TraceRIFT reduces mean retrieval regret by 22.68% relative to Reference, from 0.0903 to 0.0698. The paired gain is 0.0205, with a 95% parent-clustered interval of 0.0183--0.0227. Mean regret is also 9.60% lower than rank-based maximal marginal relevance (MMR) and 10.70% lower than predictive MMR under the same constraints. TraceRIFT also lowers regret relative to target-consistency-only and observable-discrepancy References. Workflow deployment and predictive transfer are also assessed using 480 catalogue-derived virtual queries from Wadi Birk.

articles.title: Application of Magnetic Susceptibility and Heavy-Metal Concentrations to Assess Soil Pollution Around Savannah Sugar Company, Numan, Adamawa State, Nigeria
articles.abstract: Agro-industrial activities may contribute to heavy-metal accumulation in surrounding soils, creating potential ecological and human-health risks. This study assessed soil pollution around the Savannah Sugar Company (SSC), Numan, Adamawa State, Nigeria, using magnetic susceptibility, X-ray fluorescence (XRF), scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM–EDS), pollution indices, multivariate statistics and human-health risk assessment. A total of 200 soil samples comprising topsoil, farmland-reference, vertical-profile and lateral-transect samples were analysed for low- and high-frequency magnetic susceptibility (χLF and χHF), while 30 selected samples were analysed by XRF for eleven elements. Topsoil χLF ranged from 21 to 1,473 × 10⁻⁸ m³ kg⁻¹, while lateral-transect χLF ranged from 24 to 486 × 10⁻⁸ m³ kg⁻¹, indicating marked spatial magnetic variability. Pb, Co, Cu and Ni showed substantial enrichment, with Pb reaching 1,350 mg kg⁻¹. The Pollution Load Index exceeded unity in all analysed samples (mean = 4.83), while the Potential Ecological Risk Index ranged from 199.9 to 547.5 (mean = 349.3), with 60% of samples classified as considerable risk. Pearson correlation analysis (n = 29) showed significant positive relationships between χLF and Fe (r = 0.584, p < 0.01), Mn (r = 0.558, p < 0.01) and Ti (r = 0.427, p < 0.05), indicating that magnetic susceptibility may provide a useful preliminary screening indicator of Fe-, Mn- and Ti-associated enrichment. Multivariate and SEM–EDS analyses indicated mixed geogenic/pedogenic and anthropogenic influences. Human-health assessment showed that the adult Hazard Index remained below unity, whereas the child Hazard Index exceeded unity, driven mainly by chromium. The findings demonstrate substantial multi-metal contamination around the SSC and support combining magnetic screening with direct geochemical analysis for environmental monitoring.

articles.title: A carefully timed pair of light pulses can amplify the motion of atomic layers in a quantum material
articles.abstract: The principle "Work smarter, not harder!" apparently also applies to controlling quantum materials with light. Many of their fascinating properties depend on how the atoms are arranged in the crystal. Ultrashort laser pulses can be used to alter these structures in a targeted way—the light first excites electrons, whose changed energy and dynamics exert forces on the atomic nuclei and can thereby set the atoms in motion. Such processes unfold within femtoseconds, a millionth of a billionth of a second.

articles.title: A new superinductor created within a silicon integrated circuit
articles.abstract: A recent study published in Nature Electronics and carried out by researchers from nanoGUNE's Quantum Hardware research group, Quantum Motion, London Center for Nanotechnology, Imperial College London and the University of Cambridge introduces a new superinductor created within a silicon integrated circuit fabricated in a commercial complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) process.

articles.title: Classification and Signatures of Dissipative Quantum Hall-Superconductor Junctions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) edges with proximity-induced superconductivity can host parafermionic zero modes (PZMs), making them a promising platform for topological quantum computing. Recent experiments [Gül et al., Phys. Rev. X 12, 021057 (2022)] measured the edge conductance from crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) between counter-propagating FQH edges separated by a narrow superconductor. The observed conductance was small and non-quantized, with two distinct behaviors: some states show temperature-independent conductance, while others show conductance that grows as temperature decreases. We explain these results by dissipation to sub-gap modes in the superconductor and present a phase diagram for the FQH-superconductor junction. We show that for Jain states, temperature-independent non-quantized conductance occurs only in the presence of an integer mode (such as at filling ν=1±frac1m, with odd m≥3) strongly coupled to the dissipative channel. The predicted temperature trends qualitatively agree with the experiment, which shows temperature-independent conductance for ν=2/3 and integer states, but not for ν=1/3 and ν=2/5. We propose comparing ν=4/3 and 2/3 to test the predicted influence of the relative chirality of integer and fractional modes.

articles.title: Low cross-plane thermal conductivity of κ-Ga₂O₃ thin films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The thermal conductivities of (001) κ-Ga₂O₃ thin films deposited on c-plane sapphire substrates were measured with frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR). The thermal conductivity increases from 1.83 ⁺⁰.¹⁹₋₀.₁₈ W/m·K to 2.26 ⁺⁰.³⁵₋₀.₄₀ W/m·K as the thicknesses increase from 159 nm to 689 nm. This weak thickness dependence indicates that the majority of the intrinsic phonon mean free paths are smaller than the range of investigated film thicknesses. First-principles-based calculations that include phonon-phonon and phonon-boundary scattering capture this size-dependent behavior and support our experimental observation. Temperature-dependent measurements of a 689 nm film from 293 to 400 K show a decrease in thermal conductivity with increasing temperature due to enhanced phonon-phonon scattering. A weaker temperature dependence is observed in a 159 nm film where phonon-boundary scattering becomes more prominent. At comparable film thicknesses, our measured κ-Ga₂O₃ films exhibit lower values of cross-plane thermal conductivity than the other experimentally measured Ga₂O₃ polymorphs. Our experimental observations are supported by prior predictions, which suggest that the low thermal conductivity of κ-Ga₂O₃ results from its complex crystal structure, which leads to increased anharmonicity and lower phonon group velocities relative to other polymorphs. Thermal management strategies, such as integration with high-thermal-conductivity substrates, may thus be required to mitigate self-heating for κ-Ga₂O₃-based electronic devices.

articles.title: Medial Model of Elastic Curve Contacts, from Clasps to Knits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Materials constructed from interlocking and tangled fibers are challenging to model and understand due in part to the complex interplay between fiber shape and contact mechanics. Much of our intuition about contact mechanics comes from the Hertzian description, which is based on interactions between convex bodies. However, fibers often form clasp shapes, which involve saddle-shaped contact surfaces; the ability for two interacting bodies to conform to each other along a saddle surface confounds many existing mechanical contact models. Following an observation that contact surfaces between fibers tend to look like minimal, constant mean-curvature surfaces, we seek to test this hypothesis and provide a direct link to geometric modeling methods. To do this, we leverage the medial axis transformation, which generalizes the notion of a Voronoi tessellation to generating curves and surfaces. Through computational studies on an orthogonal clasp and a simple knit structure, we find that the medial axis transformation provides a reasonable model for contact surfaces between identical curves. We also show that a generalization of the medial axis transformation based on radical Voronoi tessellations can be used to well-approximate contact surfaces between non-identical curves. We apply this ``radical axis transform'' to curves of different radii and demonstrate a trend for surfaces to adopt finite mean curvature. Our results may point the way towards more sophisticated geometric methods for modeling tangles.

articles.title: Topological localization in unentangled random braids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2015, P. Serna, G. Bunin, and A. Nahum numerically investigated fluctuations in a bunch of unentangled random threads. They showed that fluctuations of an individual thread in a braid are qualitatively different from those of a thread embedded in a medium of fixed parallel lines. In particular, Serna et al. observed a logarithmic increase in the average transverse span, left<|x_N|right>, of a thread with polymer length, N. This behavior highlights the collective nature of topological interactions, in which each polymer fluctuates and constrains the motion of the others. Studying this problem both numerically and analytically, we propose the following interpretation: the logarithmic regime is transient, and sufficiently long polymers exhibit topological localization, where left<|x_N|right> approaches a finite limit at N→infty. Unlike localization induced by quenched external disorder, this phenomenon arises solely from collective topological constraints. We study braids within a locally free approximation and support the localization by analytical investigation of Brownian bridges on the asymptotic Cayley graph of a locally free group. We further conjecture that topologically induced localization emerges as a phase transition: for a small number of threads, n sim 2div 5, the span, left<|x_N|right>, grows algebraically, with the usual scaling left<|x_N|right>sim N¹/⁴ at Ngg 1; by contrast, for sufficiently large n, each thread in a long braid (Ngg 1) asymptotically localizes, approaching left<|x_N|right>sim const.
authors: Pieter Hendrik Willem Van Der Hoek

articles.title: Shock-driven Jetting at HMX Crystal Surface Asperities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shock-induced jetting and recompression are plausible mechanisms for hot spot formation in energetic materials, but remain poorly understood. To this end, we apply all-atom nonreactive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of a shock-loaded sinusoidal surface asperity in the crystalline explosive HMX (octahydro-1,3,5,7-tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocine) to quantify the roles of shock strength, asperity geometry, system size, and crystallographic orientation in determining the jetting response. Our simulations span a shock pressure interval of approx4-47 GPa, which captures responses in both detonation initiation and steady-state detonation regimes. We find that shock strength and asperity curvature exert strong influence on jet velocity, temperature, and morphology, while feature size and crystallographic orientation play more modest roles. Jet morphology correlates strongly with the HMX ambient-pressure phase diagram and the narrow temperature range associated with its liquid phase. Coherent jets form when focusing and dissipation are sufficient to drive local temperatures above the melting point, while formation of molecular plumes is seemingly connected to jet temperatures exceeding the liquid-vapor transition temperature. Formation of plumes is unlike the jetting responses seen in metals, which typically exhibit liquid phases that are stable over wider temperature intervals. This work proposes a simple hypothesis for the connection between jet morphology and ambient-pressure phase diagrams that can be readily tested in other explosives and metals. It also provides a foundation for ongoing nonreactive and reactive MD simulations of jet impact and recompression to quantify the role played by jets in forming hot spots in HMX-based explosives.

articles.title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded β-Ga₂O₃/SiC Heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, β-Ga₂O₃/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. A nanoscale crystalline Si interlayer is designed and fabricated by wafer bonding to bridge the mismatched phonon states of β-Ga₂O₃ and SiC. Spatially resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations show that this Si layer opens new channels for phonon transport across the interface. The engineered interface raises the interfacial thermal conductance to 165 MW m⁻² K⁻¹ -- the highest value yet reported for β-Ga₂O₃/SiC interfaces. These results offer an effective way to manage heat in β-Ga₂O₃ devices and point to a general approach for building phonon-bridging interfaces that improve heat dissipation in heterogeneous systems.

articles.title: Analytic two-body density-matrix spectrum of the Fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The two-body density matrix (TBDM) of a quantum many-body system provides information about particle correlations, e.g., pairing. In this work, we derive the complete spectrum of the TBDM of the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas using its exact ground-state wavefunction in second quantization. We obtain analytical expressions for all eigenvalues and eigenvectors for an arbitrary number of particles and identify two different types of eigenstates: collective states, formed by superpositions of paired momentum modes, and single-determinant states. We provide a physical interpretation of this structure, explaining the origin of the different eigenstates and their degeneracies. We further derive an asymptotic expansion for the largest eigenvalue, improving on previous estimates and analytically confirming its linear scaling with the particle number, thereby indicating off-diagonal long-range order. For the high-index collective states, we obtain simpler expressions for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors, showing that the eigenvalues decay as n⁻⁴ and that the eigenvectors become independent of the number of particles. Finally, we discuss the connection between the collective states and an effective description in terms of composite bosons, whose spectral properties suggest a behavior consistent with Tan's contact for interacting bosonic systems.

articles.title: Core Reactivity in Cs-Ba-O ternary system under pressure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High pressure can activate Cs 5p core electrons for covalent bonding. In this study, we investigate the Cs-Ba-O system at 150 and 250 GPa using first-principles structure searches. CsBa₃O₈ and CsBaO₄ both lie on the static-lattice convex hull at 250~GPa and exhibit mild Cs 5p-O 2p bonding while retaining O₂ units with intermediate superoxide-peroxide character. Cs₂BaO₃ shows substantially stronger bonding but remains metastable with respect to CsO and BaO. A 1:1 Cs₂O-BaO₂ mixture provides a solid starting composition for investigating this chemistry, with core-reactive CsO among the predicted products at 250~GPa. Calculated Cs L₃-edge x-ray absorption near-edge spectra and powder diffraction patterns provide electronic and structural signatures to guide identification of the predicted phases in diamond anvil cell experiments.

articles.title: An All-Atom Model of the Resorcinol-Formaldehyde Aerogel Skeleton from DFT and Molecular Dynamics: Validation and Iron Incorporation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resorcinol-formaldehyde (RF) aerogels are lightweight, ultra-porous thermal superinsulators whose complex amorphous structure has not yet been described at the all-atom level. Here, we build an all-atom model of the RF aerogel skeleton by combining density functional theory (DFT) and classical molecular dynamics (MD), validate it against experimental infrared and density measurements, and use it to study the incorporation of iron dopants. The RF base unit was optimized with Gaussian, DMol³ and SIESTA, and its calculated infrared spectrum agreed with experiment. Comparing classical force fields with DFT for branched systems of two to four base units (140-278 atoms) led to the choice of COMPASS II. A 15,012-atom system of 54 branched RF units, not cross-linked to each other, aggregated into a single cluster in the canonical (NVT) ensemble and reached an equilibrium density of 1.296 g.cm⁻³ in the isobaric-isothermal (NPT) ensemble, in agreement with the experimental skeletal density (1.3 g.cm⁻³). Then, 5 wt% iron (109 atoms) was added to the equilibrated structure: during 1 ns of NPT simulation, the fraction of iron atoms embedded in the skeleton rose from 63% to 71%, and the Fe-C radial distribution function peaked at 3 Å. The model thus provides an experimentally supported starting point for screening fillers and dopants in RF gels, with prospective application to their thermoelectric functionalization, which we have previously demonstrated experimentally with basalt and PANOX fibres. Future extensions could address skeleton properties relevant to thermal insulation and the pyrolysis of RF gels into carbon and metal-doped carbon aerogels.

articles.title: Kardar--Parisi--Zhang density hydrodynamics in a coherent XXZ--ASEP Lindbladian
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coherent interactions can generate quantum correlations without changing a stationary density current. Whether that current still determines long-wavelength transport is a dynamical question. We study an XXZ chain with asymmetric Lindblad hopping, whose stationary current has the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) form although its populations do not evolve autonomously. The current curvature and static susceptibility fix the leading Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) length and amplitude without a fitted length or amplitude conversion factor. The density-visible Liouvillian spectrum, real-space spreading, and Fourier relaxation support KPZ scaling at the finite coherent couplings studied. Central and intermediate stationary density correlations are consistent with the Prähofer--Spohn profile at this microscopic scale, with resolved finite-time corrections. Reservoir-matched classical references quantify boundary effects, while symmetric hopping recovers diffusion and reduced asymmetry produces the expected crossover. These results connect an exact nonlinear current to the observed long-wavelength KPZ transport of the physical density in an interacting open quantum chain away from the isotropic Heisenberg point.

articles.title: Complex Martensitic Microstructures in rm Ti₇₆rm Nb₂₂rm Al₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze the unusual microstructure resulting from the cubic to orthorhombic phase transformation in the shape-memory alloy rm Ti₇₆rm Nb₂₂rm Al₂. This seems to represent an approximate experimental realization of a deformation having a finite number of incompatible deformation gradients, which has been known to exist only as a theoretical possibility. Because the middle eigenvalue γ of the transformation strain is very close to 1, the phase transformation in this alloy takes place via nucleation of exact austenite-martensite interfaces rather than, as usual for other alloys, by classical austenite-martensite interfaces separating the austenite from a finely-twinned laminate of martensite. According to the moving mask approximation of Della Porta this leads to the question whether a microstructure can be formed from the set H of the twelve matrices mathbf Vᵢ on the martensite energy wells that are rank-one connected to the identity, even though these matrices are mutually incompatible. We show that when γ=1 and the transformation is volume preserving, such a microstructure is possible that does not deform the grain boundary. This is a consequence of H forming a degenerate T₁₂ configuration in the sense of Kirchheim. In fact there are such microstructures supported on just 8 of the 12 matrices in H. However there is no deformation satisfying the same boundary condition whose gradient belongs to H almost everywhere. An additional prediction, confirmed experimentally, is that the macroscopic deformation gradient equals the identity everywhere. We also analyse the approximate compatibility of the mathbf Vᵢ. Although mutually incompatible, they are nearly compatible, with some pairs much more nearly compatible than others, these pairs corresponding to interfaces that are more frequently observed.

articles.title: First-principles study of the formation of Group-IV--vacancy color centers in diamond
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06671v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: XV (X is Si, Ge, Sn, or Pb, and V is the carbon vacancy) color centers are promising platforms for quantum computing and quantum information science due to their favorable optical and spin properties. They are commonly fabricated by ion implantation, which inevitably introduces vacancies and carbon self-interstitials (Cᵢ) into the lattice. However, the microscopic formation mechanism remains unclear, limiting the yield and stability of XV centers. Here, first-principles calculations are conducted to systematically investigate the roles of V and Cᵢ in XV formation. We find that XV formation is energetically favorable, with large binding energies and low diffusion barriers. Nevertheless, XV readily captures Cᵢ to form substitutional defect Xₛ, or captures an additional V to form the complex XV₂. Charge transition levels show that oppositely charged reactants never meet in these reactions, and that Coulomb repulsion blocks them only when both reactants carry charges of the same sign, which for the capture of Cᵢ requires strongly n- or p-type conditions. These competing defect reactions destabilize the split-vacancy configuration and could account for the low formation yield of XV centers, so that they appear at concentrations well below those expected from the implanted dose. Our results elucidate the microscopic origin of this intrinsic instability and suggest that Fermi-level control may suppress defect conversions and stabilize the split-vacancy configuration.

articles.title: Majorana-like Josephson branch structure in one-dimensional transport of cold atoms
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study phase-controlled transport through a one-dimensional channel of attractively interacting fermions connecting two three-dimensional BCS reservoirs. The competition between channel phase stiffness and pair tunnelling at the two contacts results in the emergence of two 4π-periodic families of stationary states, characterised by symmetric or asymmetric phase drops at the boundaries. Advancing the reservoir phase difference by 2π exchanges these families so that the equilibrium energy remains 2π periodic, while the 4π  periodicity might be attained in a diabatic regime. This structure admits a formal description in terms of two boundary Majorana operators, combining into a nonlocal fermion mode. Renormalization-group analysis shows that quantum fluctuations and phase slips are suppressed in the zero-temperature thermodynamic limit, preserving the branch crossings. The predicted branch exchange, metastable currents, and sweep-rate-dependent switching provide experimentally testable signatures of Majorana-like Josephson branch physics in a gapless interacting channel.

articles.title: Hall-Density Collapse as Direct Evidence for Percolative Conduction Onset in Monolayer MoS₂ Transistors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The origin of the apparent metal-insulator transition in two-dimensional electron systems remains debated. Using temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on industry-relevant MoS₂ monolayer FETs with amorphous HfO₂ dielectrics, we establish classical percolation as the underlying mechanism. We report two complementary signatures of disorder-driven conduction onset: a temperature-independent Hall-density collapse as a function of absolute gate voltage and a vanishing activation energy at a characteristic carrier density nc, identified as the percolation threshold. These findings identify dielectric-interface disorder, rather than channel quality alone, as the key parameter governing device turn-on. The extracted activation barriers reach values substantially exceeding room-temperature thermal energies, indicating that disorder-driven conduction onset remains relevant well beyond cryogenic transport.
authors: C. J. L. de la Rosa

articles.title: How much data does a memory kernel need? Measurement requirements for fractional models of battery and corrosion degradation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05426v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How much data does a memory kernel need before a fit is meaningful? For a distributed-order model, the answer is about 3.1 decades of observation, more than standard battery-degradation tests provide. Battery capacity fade and corrosion-film growth depend on their history, so they are often modelled using general fractional calculus (GFC), where memory is described by an arbitrary Sonine kernel rather than a single power law. We tested this using two mechanistic models without fractional operators and de Levie's porous-electrode model, whose high-frequency order is exactly 0.5; our estimator recovered 0.500. A single aging curve can recover an effective order, alpha, to within 5% noise using a weak formulation, while separating the tempered parameters (alpha, lambda) requires several Arrhenius conditions, with errors improving from (0.25, 0.43) with one condition to (0.04, 0.07) with four. A distributed-order memory needs 3.1 decades of data to be resolved to 90%; below that, a two-order memory can collapse into one intermediate order that fits the data better than the true spectrum. For saturating passivation, however, a general kernel improves the fit substantially, raising R2 from 0.862 to 0.998. Across 20 cells from two public datasets, observation windows span only 1.23 to 2.24 decades, making the 3.1-decade result a practical design rule: it defines what must be measured before fitting a memory kernel, not only what cannot be fitted.

articles.title: Toward a Quantum Information Foundation for Neutron Scattering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neutron scattering is a central probe of quantum materials, yet what quantum information can, in principle, be extracted from a scattering experiment remains unclear. Here we formulate neutron scattering as a quantum measurement, with the scattering amplitudes acting as Kraus operators on the material state. This provides a unified description of conventional intensity, coherent scattering, interferometric measurements, and entanglement witnesses, including those based on quantum Fisher information. We then ask how far this connection can be extended to nonlinear properties of a quantum state. For two independently prepared samples, we derive the general structure of probe-mediated measurement probabilities and show that, for spin-projection-conserving dynamics, low-order scattering cannot resolve certain many-body coherences required to determine purity. Conversely, an idealized single-spin protocol shows how probe-mediated exchange can access purity when the appropriate two-copy operation is realized. Our results establish a quantum-information description of neutron scattering and delineate the information accessible through conventional and interferometric measurements.

articles.title: Zero noise extrapolation of transport coefficients
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05481v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: NISQ devices routinely estimate properties of the noiseless system from measurements at varying noise strengths γ. These zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) schemes fail to estimate transport coefficients of conserved quantities when the noise violates the associated conservation laws. We show how to extrapolate measurements in noisy, one-dimensional, non-integrable spin chains to obtain the spin transport coefficients governing linear response in the zero-noise limit. As the wavevector of the Fourier mode of a conserved quantity goes to zero, its decay rate vanishes. The coefficient of the leading momentum dependence defines a transport coefficient in the noiseless system, and an analogous effective coefficient in the noisy one. Naive ZNE implicitly assumes that this effective coefficient is analytic in γ as γ→ 0. Our main result is that universal non-linear corrections to hydrodynamics can produce non-analytic dependence on γ. In particular, we argue that the effective spin diffusion coefficient of a dissipative Heisenberg chain and the effective subdiffusion coefficient of a dipole-conserving fracton approach their noiseless value as γ¹/². We benchmark these analytical predictions numerically.

articles.title: Krylov meets Fock: Complementary lenses on quantum dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05495v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum dynamics in Krylov space can be represented by a particle hopping on a chain whose sites are the Krylov basis vectors. The goal of this work is to extend this idea to the Fock basis, which in turn allows the description of a generic dynamics in terms of a more general, possibly higher-dimensional lattice. This construction has been dubbed the Fock state lattice (FSL), since its sites are identified with Fock states. To analyze the dynamics on the FSL we introduce various measures of the spread of a state, comparing them among themselves and with their Krylov counterparts. We apply our analysis to two models of light-matter interaction studied in quantum optics: the multi-mode Jaynes-Cummings and the Dicke models. We find that, whenever the FSL is not a chain, the corresponding dynamics provides insights complementary to the Krylov space analysis and, in some instances, greater analytical control. For example, we obtain analytical results for the FSL spread measures of the Dicke model in the thermodynamic limit and determine that their scaling in time detects the superradiant phase transition.

articles.title: Dynamical Signatures of Selective Gap Closing in Multi-Dimensional Monotone Quasiperiodic Operators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We translate the spectral gap-closing criterion for multi-dimensional monotone quasiperiodic Schrödinger operators into a concrete dynamical protocol and verify it by large-scale numerics. For a non-principal label we construct a sampling function whose leading eigenfunction weight at the origin vanishes; a local bump then drives the residual weight through zero. The height of a weighted oscillatory time average of the origin-to-localization-center correlator exhibits a deep minimum precisely at the closing, while the site-control label remains featureless and orders of magnitude larger. The signature is robust and maps directly onto superconducting-circuit and photonic platforms.

articles.title: Spatial Cost of Recovering a Fusion Qubit in a Critical Spin Chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06215v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vanishing-error recovery of a fusion qubit from a fixed-sector ground doublet of four Kramers--Wannier defects in a critical Ising chain requires at least the shorter three-defect span of physical spins to leading order. Across arbitrary preselected spin sets and unrestricted joint decoding, this bound holds when the thermodynamic limit precedes large spacings at fixed positive ratios. An exact interval decoder attains it. Collective records of both logical axes in the complement force successful near-minimal supports to concentrate in density on a leading-order shortest interval.

articles.title: Directional Control of Chiral Polymer Emission Dissymmetry by Plasmonic Metasurfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06400v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Circularly polarized (CP) emission is central to next-generation photonic and optoelectronic technologies, yet simultaneously controlling its directionality, intensity, and handedness remains a major challenge. Advances in molecular and materials design have enabled strong chiral light-matter interactions and large dissymmetry between opposite CP states. However, conventional thin-film architectures provide limited control over the angular distribution of CP emission and often exhibit strongly angle-dependent chiral emission. Metasurfaces, on the other hand, offer powerful control over emission directionality and polarization, but have predominantly been explored with intrinsically achiral emitters. For the first time, we integrate organic chiral polymer thin films with planar chiral plasmonic metasurfaces to enhance chiral light-matter interactions while controlling the directionality and angular dependence of chiral emission. Using angle-resolved Stokes Fourier polarimetry, we show that metasurface coupling produces directional emission, near-normal dissymmetry factors exceeding 0.7, and, remarkably, direction-dependent reversal of the emission handedness at fixed molecular stereochemistry.

articles.title: Fluctuating Hydrodynamics of Quantum Fluids from the Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Starting from the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation (NFPE), we establish the fluctuating hydrodynamics for quantum fluids. We also investigate the corresponding stochastic thermodynamics and derive the associated fluctuation theorems. We then apply this framework to both fermionic and bosonic systems. For the ideal Fermi gas, we study the electrical conduction and reveal a resistance proportional to the product of temperature and the density of states at the Fermi surface. For bosonic fluids, we analyze the relaxation time characterizing the critical slowing down phenomenon and identify three distinct scaling behaviors corresponding to the non-interacting, repulsive interaction, and attractive interaction regimes. Overall, this work provides a experimentally verifiable phenomenological description for the dynamics of quantum fluids and demonstrates the applicability of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation in characterizing such systems.

articles.title: Cryogenic suppression of correlated loss in Rydberg atom arrays
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06613v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Blackbody radiation (BBR) poses a central challenge for quantum science with Rydberg atoms. By driving transitions to nearby opposite-parity states, BBR shortens Rydberg lifetimes and has long been suspected to trigger "avalanche" events known to cause correlated atom loss. Here, we suppress avalanche decay and establish BBR as its dominant trigger using a Rydberg atom array that operates either cryogenically or at room temperature. A 45~K radiation shield reduces ambient BBR, extending Rydberg nS lifetimes for n ranging from 50 to 75. BBR-induced decay rates are suppressed by 30%-50%, corresponding to an effective blackbody temperature Tᵣₘ ₑffapprox190~K. This enables controlled comparisons of Rydberg-dressed atom arrays operating in different BBR environments. Arrays of up to 70 atoms demonstrate cryogenically suppressed avalanche rates, tracking the suppression in BBR-induced decay, for both n=50 and n=60 dressing. A parameter-free rate model agrees with the measured avalanche rates after accounting for frequency-dependent cryogenic shielding, photoionization-triggered avalanches, laser phase noise, BBR decay channels, and Rydberg interaction effects. We demonstrate a quantitative description of avalanche decay and show that improved BBR shielding should further suppress correlated loss to the T_eff=45~K achievable in the current apparatus. Our results establish a route to mitigating correlated errors that otherwise impede fault-tolerant operation in neutral-atom quantum processors.

articles.title: Photonic and Electronic Interaction of TMD-Hybridized ZnO Nanowire Lasers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06740v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Semiconductor nanowire lasers are promising on-chip coherent light sources for photonic integrated circuits, but integration inevitably places them in contact with other materials, thereby changing their properties upon hybridization. In this study, we examine the photonic and electronic coupling between single ZnO nanowire lasers and TMDs. Using deterministic nanomanipulation, we first hybridized the same nanowire first with a WS₂ monolayer and then with a MoS₂ monolayer. The respective lasing threshold rises, the emission is strongly quenched at high pump power densities, and the mode envelope blueshifts. Upon hybridization with bilayer, trilayer, and bulk MoS₂, lasing is fully suppressed. Finite-Difference Eigenmode simulations show that the TMD absorbs part of the evanescent field. Because this absorption is wavelength dependent, it also removes modes from the low-energy flank of the envelope, which accounts for small difference between the two monolayers, while the blueshift itself follows the increase of the carrier density at threshold. Density functional theory calculations that include the interface dipole predict a type-I alignment at the ideal ZnO(10bar10)/TMD interface, which turns into type~II for a moderately reduced dipole, as expected for hydroxylated facets in air. In both cases, holes are transferred from the nanowire into the TMD and removed from the gain medium. Evanescent absorption and hole transfer thus jointly suppress lasing, and both must be accounted for when integrating nanowire lasers with 2D materials.

articles.title: Odd Capillarity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06882v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Capillarity governs interfacial relaxation and hydrodynamic motion in binary fluids through parity-even mechanical stresses. Here, we introduce emphodd capillarity, a parity-breaking interfacial mechanical response, by incorporating a symmetric, nonvariational, parity-odd capillary stress into the Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes (CHNS) equations. This stress generates forces along interfaces, transverse to ordinary capillary forces, and performs mechanical work that is not balanced by changes in the composition free energy. Direct numerical simulations reveal that odd capillarity arrests domain coarsening while sustaining turbulent fluid motion without a conventional inertial energy cascade, as energy injection is predominantly balanced by viscous dissipation. In asymmetric mixtures, odd capillarity driven deformation and breakup interrupt droplet growth, producing dynamically arrested emulsions with composition hyperuniformity and suppressed large-scale vorticity fluctuations. These findings establish odd capillarity as a distinct interfacial mechanism for controlling phase separation and sustaining nonequilibrium fluid motion.

articles.title: d-wave superconductivity in quintuple-layer bulk superconductor La₆Ni₅O₁₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.22212v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The recent realization of bulk superconductivity in the quintuple-layer nickelate La₆Ni₅O₁₂ opens new opportunities to probe the pairing symmetry of the reduced Ruddlesden--Popper (RP) nickelate family. Using an effective five-layer Hubbard model and variational Monte Carlo calculations, we find that a spin-singlet dₓ^₂₋y^₂-wave state is energetically favored, while extended s-wave pairing is strongly suppressed. Based on the optimized superconducting state, we further calculate several experimentally accessible observables. The tunneling density of states exhibits a characteristic V-shaped low-energy spectrum, the superfluid density shows a linear low-temperature depletion, the Knight shift decreases below T_c, and the spin-lattice relaxation rate follows 1/T₁Tpropto T², together providing consistent signatures of a clean nodal superconductor. Extending the same framework to related reduced RP nickelates, we find a robust d-wave tendency in infinite-layer LaNiO₂, while trilayer La₄Ni₃O₈ at its nominal filling lies close to the boundary between d-wave superconductivity and a non-superconducting state. These results establish bulk La₆Ni₅O₁₂ as a promising platform for determining the pairing symmetry of nickelate superconductors and suggest a common dₓ^₂₋y^₂-wave pairing tendency across the reduced RP nickelate family.

articles.title: Approaching the Landauer Bound without Slowing Down
articles.abstract: arXiv:2407.03096v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Finite-time memory erasure is conventionally understood to incur an additional energy cost beyond the Landauer bound. Whether this bound can be approached without taking the infinite-time limit remains open. Based on a quantum speed limit, we identify coherence between degenerate states as a resource that allows the Landauer bound to be approached at a finite operation time. For both the 2N-state and collective spin models, we show that the minimum dissipated heat and the heat generated by continuous protocols approach the Landauer bound at finite operation times, with the corresponding finite-time penalty scaling inversely with system size. We further validate these theoretical predictions numerically for systems coupled to the Ohmic bosonic heat bath with various driving protocols. Our results reveal that operation time is a substitutable resource for approaching the fundamental thermodynamic bound of information erasure.

articles.title: Energy-filtered readout preserves gap-enhanced sensing in interacting quantum dots
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.04063v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A small excitation gap makes a quantum dot a sensitive probe of a weak electric field, but the charge detector reading it can also excite it. We calculate how much of this enhancement survives continuous readout for two interacting electrons tuned through a confinement-driven crossover in a gate-defined dot. The probe is a few-level system read by a weakly coupled linear detector, with second-order transition rates and information from the mean detector current, for gaps up to a few hundred microelectronvolts, couplings up to 50 μeV and temperatures up to 100 mK. The outcome depends on the energy structure of the detector, not only its noise. A quantum point contact measures more strongly at higher bias but, once the bias energy exceeds the gap, also excites the probe; when this back-action dominates the relaxation of the probe, the optimised information rate grows only as the inverse of the gap. A sensor quantum dot with a narrow level instead reaches full strength at a bias below the gap, where a non-interacting detector cannot excite it at zero temperature. This energy-filtered readout keeps the inverse-square gap dependence of the quantum Fisher information down to gaps comparable to the level width of the detector or ten times the thermal energy. At the tested operating points, higher probe states change the sensitivities by up to 6% and the exponents by up to 0.06; coherence corrections to the populations and transduced signal are negligible, and any gain from the full detector record is unresolved within 1-2% numerical uncertainty. Under the same conditions the interacting pair gives about three times the information rate of a single electron with the same gap and detector, for contact and Coulomb-type interactions alike. The different gap dependences and optimal biases of the two detectors can be tested by bias and gate sweeps on charge-sensed double dots.

articles.title: Holographic dark energy through Kruglov entropy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a holographic dark energy model built on the new entropy proposed by Kruglov, S_K=SBH/(1+γ SBH²), with the Granda--Oliveros infrared cutoff L⁻²=α H²+βdot H in a flat universe. The Kruglov entropy is smaller than the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy and has a maximum value. We obtain the energy density of the model, the differential equation for the dark energy density parameter, and the expressions for the equation of state parameter, the deceleration parameter and the squared sound speed. At early times the model behaves like the usual Granda--Oliveros holographic dark energy, and the dark energy follows the background with a constant fraction. At late times the Kruglov correction gives a stable de Sitter future when α>1, with the final Hubble rate fixed by the entropy parameter. The model gives a matter era followed by a dark energy era, with a transition from deceleration to acceleration near zapprox0.66. For larger values of the entropy parameter the equation of state can cross the phantom divide; for the parameters allowed by the data this happens only in the future, if at all. We constrain the model with 31 cosmic chronometer points, Pantheon+ supernovae and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation data, together with a big bang nucleosynthesis condition, using a Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis. We find H₀=68.0±1.6 km,s⁻¹,Mpc⁻¹, α=1.19⁺⁰.¹⁰₋₀.₀₈, β=0.61⁺⁰.⁰⁶₋₀.₀₅ and the 95% upper limit tilde b=b/H₀⁴<0.24 on the dimensionless Kruglov parameter (for a matter-era dark energy fraction below 0.3), which gives γ<4.9×10⁻²⁴⁶. The present equation of state is wD₀=-0.83±0.03. The model fits the data slightly better than ΛCDM (Δχ²=-4.5) and is equally good by the Akaike criterion, while the Bayesian criterion and the Bayesian evidence prefer ΛCDM.

articles.title: A closed-form design rule for photonic hopfions of arbitrary order
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05595v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topological textures of light are robust against perturbation and are emerging as carriers of information and probes of light-matter interaction. The most intricate of them, the photonic hopfion, in which the loops of different polarization states are linked, has so far been assembled from chosen superpositions of laser modes, with weights set by hand or found by numerical optimization. Here we replace this search with a design rule. Two scalar beams, an optical vortex of order ell and a field with n dark rings, propagate in closed form, and their phases on one plane are the two masks of a metasurface that controls two orthogonal polarizations. Although a beam, unlike the closed spaces of topology, extends to infinity, we prove that it is a hopfion of order nell whenever three algebraic conditions on the ring coefficients and the vortex order hold, and that the polarization loops of every state that the far field does not reach then link exactly nell times; each condition guards against one way in which the topology can escape. The order is thus chosen on paper and the device follows directly, without optimization. In scalar simulation, one terahertz metasurface geometry produces hopfions up to order nine, and a full-wave simulation of the complete first-order device preserves its topology. The rule applies to any platform that shapes the phases of two orthogonal polarizations.

articles.title: On the role of grazing atmospheric particles in hypersonic boundary-layer receptivity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The role of small atmospheric particulates in the initiation of the laminar-turbulent transition is investigated for the HIFLIER vehicle during Mach 6 ascent condition. High-fidelity simulations are used to examine the disturbance wavepackets generated by particles following either grazing trajectories through the boundary layer or trajectories that lead to impact and rebound at the cone surface. Grazing particles that penetrate less than halfway through the boundary layer are found to generate wavepackets with amplitudes comparable to those produced by wall-impinging particles. To identify the receptivity mechanisms responsible for this behaviour, a multiple-scales asymptotic formulation is developed that accounts for the extended streamwise region over which a particle interacts with the boundary layer. The analysis shows that a grazing particle can generate a strong disturbance response when crossing the critical layer, where the streamwise-momentum component of the adjoint mode is largest and the boundary layer is most receptive. Thus, direct surface impact is not required for atmospheric particulates to excite dynamically significant instability waves. Root-mean-square disturbance estimates for submicron grazing particles predict transition-onset locations close to those measured in flight, suggesting they may have contributed significantly to the onset of transition on HIFLIER at the trajectory condition considered.

articles.title: Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy with entangled photons and visible-light detection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. Quantum infrared spectroscopy avoids these constraints: harnessing quantum interference between the generation processes of frequency-entangled photon pairs, it reads out the infrared response of a sample by detecting only the visible partner photon, for which efficient detectors exist. To date, it has been limited to steady-state measurements. Here we demonstrate its ultrafast, time-resolved form with a picosecond visible pump pulse and a silicon detector. Each visible pulse generates photon pairs within a picosecond window; the infrared photon of a pair probes the excited sample at a set delay after excitation, and the transient response is read out from the count rate of its visible partner. We resolve picosecond carrier dynamics in a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror near 1529 nm with a picowatt-level probe, unaffected by thermal background and by sample IR photoluminescence 50 times stronger than the probe. The approach is applicable to the mid-infrared, fingerprint region, where infrared detection is hardest, and to the terahertz region.

articles.title: High-transformer-ratio plasma-based afterburner for extending X-ray free-electron laser photon energies to gtrsim50 keV
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bright coherent X-rays in the gtrsim50 keV range are highly desirable for applications in materials science, high-energy-density physics, and nuclear physics, but are difficult to obtain from present X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) facilities. Plasma-based afterburners offer a compact route to increasing the electron-beam energy, yet high transformer ratio (TR) operation is vulnerable to hosing instability, which can severely degrade the witness beam quality. We propose using a transversely elliptical driver beam to excite an elliptical nonlinear plasma wake with an axially varying focusing gradient, thereby suppressing the witness beam hosing through betatron decoherence. Three-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations show that, for a 3 kA driver and a 2.35 kA witness beam with an rms length of 4 μm and a beam separation of 94 μm (TR approx 3), this scheme can accelerate an 8 GeV witness beam to sim30 GeV while nearly half of the electrons meet the XFEL requirements. Start-to-end simulations show that the resulting beam can drive gtrsim50 keV XFEL radiation with peak powers of sim10 GW and durations of sim10 fs, even when quantum diffusion is included, offering a compact route to extend existing XFEL facilities to higher photon energies.

articles.title: Estimation of Very High Energy Electron (VHEE) beam parameters using an in-air screen
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Very high energy electron (VHEE) beams offer several promising properties for radiotherapy. Accurate beam delivery requires a beam model that accounts for scattering along the beam propagation path. This work develops and validates a beam model incorporating Multiple Coulomb Scattering (MCS) to estimate beam parameters. MCS is incorporated as an additive term to the covariance matrix transformation for a drift space, allowing conventional quadrupole scans to estimate beam parameters in the presence of a downstream scatterer. The scattering correction factor is fitted to Monte Carlo (MC) simulations for a range of materials and thicknesses. The model is then validated by recovering the initial beam parameters from simulated quadrupole scans of a realistic beamline. Finally, the method is applied to in-air screen measurements at the Pulsed Energetic Electrons for Research (PEER) end station of the Australian Synchrotron. After fitting the correction factors, the mean and standard deviation of the estimation errors for the final emittance, diameter, divergence, and mean kinetic energy were (-0.06 ± 3.17)%, (0.15 ± 0.66)%, (0.18 ± 2.18)%, and (-0.03 ± 0.06)%, respectively. Simulated quadrupole scans successfully recovered the initial beam parameters, with errors of at most 13%. PEER measurements yielded emittance estimates ranging from 0.238 to 1.753~mm,mrad across scans, which were within the expected range. Following an initial quadrupole scan, the method allows the in-air beam size to be estimated for other quadrupole configurations. Further work is required to improve the consistency and reliability of the experimental estimates.

articles.title: The two-loop Lamb shift: the final missing contribution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The last significant unknown contribution to the two-loop Lamb shift, namely the electron self-energy with vacuum-polarization insertion into the photon line, is determined including higher-order effects in the parameter α Z, with α being the fine-structure constant and Z the nuclear charge number. Our calculation improves the accuracy of theoretical predictions for energy levels and transition energies in heavy hydrogen-like and lithium-like ions by up to one order of magnitude, enabling more stringent comparisons between theory and available experimental results.
