These results pave the way for more precise tests of quantum electrodynamics in the strong-field regime, as well as for accurate determinations of nuclear charge radii.

articles.title: Single-sided lens terahertz flat-top beam shaping in the Fresnel region
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, a novel, to our knowledge, analytical approach is introduced for the design of a single-sided plano-convex lens (PCL) capable of terahertz (THz) flat-top beam shaping in the Fresnel region. The lens profile, derived from geometrical optics principles, integrates collimating and beam-shaping functions into a single optical surface, thereby simplifying fabrication. The efficiency of the method is demonstrated by designing two PCLs that convert a divergent Gaussian beam from a monochromatic THz source (at 100 and 200 GHz) into flat-top beams with target radii of 400 and 500 mm at distances of 3 and 4 m, respectively. The resulting fields, evaluated through analytical, integral equation, and finite element techniques, are shown to be comparable to those produced by a conventional double-sided concave-convex lens. Furthermore, the sensitivity of the design to frequency and alignment variations is investigated, confirming the robustness of this single-curvature approach for integration into practical THz imaging systems.

articles.title: Millimeter-Wave Gaussian-to-Flat-Top Beam Shaping Using a Single-Curvature Lens: A Novel Approach
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a novel method for converting the divergent Gaussian intensity distribution of a millimeter-wave source into a uniform (flat-top) distribution using a single curved surface. The proposed method combines the surface profile of a collimator with that of a beam shaper. To validate the method, the profile of a single-sided (plano-convex) lens is derived and placed 52 mm in front of a conical horn antenna operating at 100 GHz. The lens transforms the Gaussian radiation of the horn, with an incident beam radius of 11.9 mm, into a uniform beam with a radius of 400 mm at a distance of 3 m. The lens surface profile is optimized using a full-wave-simulation-based procedure, and the resulting output beam is compared with that of a previously designed double-sided (concave-convex) lens. Simulation results show that, within the desired field of view, the optimized single-sided lens produces a flat-top intensity distribution with satisfactory ripple and roll-off. Finally, the sensitivity of the optimized lens to frequency variation is investigated. The proposed lens is suitable for generating uniform illumination in active stand-off millimeter-wave imaging systems.

articles.title: Temporary gas turbines powering a US AI data center created a cross-state air pollution hotspot
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06115v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data centers increasingly use on-site gas turbines that regulators can treat as temporary. Two satellites show the fleet powering SpaceXAI's Colossus 2 raised local nitrogen dioxide columns by about half as it expanded, the most anomalous increase among 656 urban locations nationwide since 2020. Mississippi authorized the fleet, but two-thirds of the hotspot's 116,000 mostly Black residents live in Tennessee, and the hotspot contains no regulatory nitrogen dioxide monitor. The fleet causes an estimated four premature deaths yearly, valued at 49 million, over 80% outside Mississippi and nearly all from units without selective catalytic reduction. On new turbines, this control's benefits exceed costs over the service life, but not over temporary stays or for in-state damages alone. Standards following the equipment could recover these benefits.

articles.title: Colloidal 2D WS2 nanosheets exhibiting high-purity single photon emission
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The search for quantum emitters, delivering single photons "on demand" at cryogenic and elevated temperatures for photonic technologies is ever progressing. For example, micrometer-sized WS2 monolayers exhibit single photon emission by elaborated local defect or strain engineering. Here, we show that wet-chemically synthesised monolayered two-dimensional (2D) WS2 nano sheets (NSs) with lateral sizes of 14 (+/- 6 nm) readily emit single photons from exciton recombination without the need for substrate-induced patterning, strain/defect engineering or spectral filtering. Single particle spectroscopy of 70 individual NSs shows photoluminescence from excitons (2.02 eV), trios (1.94 eV) and defect-localized states (1.85 eV) with fast emission (t1<0.2 ns, t2=3.2 ns), allowing highly frequent excitation cycles. Pulsed at 80 MHz, colloidal WS2 NSs exhibit limited spectral diffusion, no blinking and distinct photon antibunching (g2(0)=0.07 at 5 K), thereby tackling challenges of established colloidal quantum dot systems (blinking, longer emission cycles), while retaining high single photon purity as key quality of deterministic quantum emitters.

articles.title: Spatial structure of surface plasmon resonance under narrow-beam illumination and its implications for sensing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The reflection of light on a surface plasmon resonance structure can be understood as the interference between the direct Fresnel reflection and the light radiated back by the plasmon as it propagates along the metal film. When the beam waist is only an order of magnitude larger than the surface plasmon propagation length, these two contributions separate spatially, and their destructive interference localizes into a dark fringe within the reflected beam. We develop an analytical model of this effect, design a realistic setup based on off-the-shelf components to observe it, and simulate the complete experiment, from illumination to detection, with an open-source framework. In the regime where the interference is maximized, the spatial structure of the reflected beam becomes extremely sensitive to the outer medium. This allows us to define an observable more than an order of magnitude more sensitive than amplitude-based measurements, and we expect a comparable improvement in resolution.

articles.title: Finite-time mixing and reaction in packed bed reactors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate mixing dynamics in porous media at finite times, using pore-scale lattice-Boltzmann simulations combined with Lagrangian particle tracking. We compute fluid deformation in randomly packed beds based on the moving Protean frame approach introduced by Lester 2018. From the extracted Lagrangian kinematics, we construct a mixing model based on lamellar aggregation that well predicts the Eulerian scalar fields obtained from simulations. Our results reveal an early time mixing regime dominated by shear-driven fluid deformation, where solute mixing arises from the random overlap of diffusive concentration elements. In this regime, mixing proceeds slowly and follows a temporal decay of concentration variance, σ_c² sim Pe⁻α/⁽²α⁺¹⁾ t⁻¹/², where Pe is the Peclet number and α the exponent characterizing shear deformation. This dynamic arises when the Peclet number is small relative to the ratio between the exponential-mixing and shear-deformation timescales. This analysis also demonstrates that shear-induced mixing govern the homogenization of early-stage reactions at the fluid-solid interface in finite-size random packed beds, typically operating at moderate Peclet numbers Pe =O(10²).

articles.title: Evanescent-Depth-Engineered High-Q topological Cavities for Strong Photon-Exciton Coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Due to the inherent scattering in topological edge states, the topological resonant cavity (TRC) formed by their interference exhibits a relatively low quality factor (Q). To address this issue, we propose the mechanism of engineering the transverse evanescent depth of edge states to achieve high-Q in irregular shaped TRCs, which further enables strong photon-exciton coupling at the single-quantum level. By adjusting the intra- and inter-cell coupling strengths in the pseudo-spin topological photonic crystal, the transverse evanescent depth of edge states is greatly reduced, thereby suppressing the scattering of TRCs. Consequently, the Q of various shaped TRCs with 2 ~ 3 um size is up to 10⁵ ~ 10⁶ in the visible, so that the strong photon-exciton coupling is achieved. The high-Q topological cavities hold promising application in integrated lasers, sensors, cavity quantum electrodynamics, and quantum photonics.

articles.title: A coupled lattice Boltzmann model for pore-scale mushy-layer dynamics with application to sea ice
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A pore-scale lattice Boltzmann model is developed for reactive transport in phase-changing porous media, coupling solute transport in the liquid with conjugate heat transfer across the solid and liquid phases. Two methodological developments are introduced: a novel link-based Volume-of-Pixel formulation for direction-dependent interface motion, and a generalized Robin boundary treatment for solute redistribution at moving interfaces. The phase-change formulation is validated against thermal benchmarks, while the Robin treatment is assessed through literature test cases, exhibiting convergence rates between first and second order. The coupled model is then applied to a local pore-scale segment of a sea ice brine channel in a purely diffusive regime. The simulations recover the expected ideal mushy-layer behaviour under appropriate scale separation. At sea-ice-relevant concentration ratios, thermal perturbations produce relatively large variations in brine salinity, causing freezing rather than melting to reshape the pore geometry in a non-uniform way. The resulting framework provides a pore-scale numerical tool for resolving coupled temperature, solute redistribution, and phase-boundary dynamics in mushy layers.

articles.title: A Finite Element Model for Fluid--Poroelastic Structure Interaction with Dissipative Interface
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper extends our prior work on interface conditions between two poroelastic domains to the case when a poroelastic domain interacts with a pure fluid. The porous medium is assumed to be deformable and modeled following mixture theory. When not in a mixture, each constituent of the porous domain is assumed to be incompressible. An arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian formulation is developed for both the fluid and porous domains. The fluid velocity and pressure fields are allowed to be discontinuous across the pure fluid/porous domain interface. A globally continuous displacement field is defined to represent both the deformation of the solid skeleton of the poroelastic medium and the mesh motion in the pure fluid domain. As an interface condition, the continuity of the normal component of the filtration velocity is enforced via a Lagrange multiplier. The mixture momentum jump condition is implemented so as to transfer the traction from the fluid side to the porous domain. A dissipative behavior is attributed to the interface, and the jump condition for the fluid momentum, derived from Hamilton's principle, incorporates this prescribed behavior. The model implementation is verified using the method of manufactured solutions, and a sample problem is solved to compare an inert interface with a fully dissipative one. The results show satisfactory convergence rates, while the proposed model successfully reproduces the analytical solution of a benchmark problem using conventional jump conditions. Furthermore, the findings highlight the significant influence of the selected interface model on the behavior of the system.

articles.title: Open-shell Configuration State Functions as trial states for phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The accurate description of open-shell states in molecular systems poses challenges for approximate electronic structure methods. One emerging approach is to variationally optimize the orbitals of a single user-selected Configuration State Function (CSF), i.e., a linear combination of Slater determinants that is constructed as an eigenstate of the total spin operator. In this work we explore the use of these orbital-optimized single CSFs as trial wavefunctions in phaseless auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (ph-AFQMC), a stochastic method that recovers electron correlation by evolving an initial state in imaginary time, subject to a constraint imposed by the trial state. We investigate the symmetric stretch of H-He-H, a series of small p-block compounds with diradicaloid singlet states, twisted ethene conformers, and a bimetallic iron-sulfur complex. We find that accurate energetics are obtained for states dominated by open-shell character, and that for certain atoms and diatomics the accuracy can be significantly improved when the trial is made to also preserve the relevant angular momentum symmetries. Furthermore, our study reveals that the open-shell CSF trial is suboptimal when the target electronic state reflects a significant mixture of ionic and covalent character, e.g., at shorter bond lengths in H-He-H and for the superexchange-stabilized ground state of [2Fe-2S]²⁺. Our findings suggest that ph-AFQMC using CSF trial states is a promising method for many (but not all) strongly correlated molecular states, especially given its relatively low computational cost, and that it provides a reasonable non-perturbative way to recover some of the dynamic correlation that is otherwise missing in the CSF.

articles.title: Search for the 229Pa Parity Doublet via Internal-Conversion Spectroscopy at FRIB
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05494v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The radioisotope ²²⁹Pa is predicted to possess a nearly degenerate ground-state parity doublet. Previous γ-ray and conversion-electron spectroscopy suggests a splitting of Δ E = (60± 50)~eV, although the doublet's existence remains unconfirmed. Such a small splitting would give ²²⁹Pa an exceptionally large enhancement of symmetry-violating nuclear properties. However, the splitting, and with it the sensitivity of ²²⁹Pa to CP-violating physics, remains uncertain by orders of magnitude. We propose an experiment to measure this splitting with sub-eV precision within a few days of measurement time by using delayed-coincidence internal-conversion spectroscopy of ²²⁹Pa ions produced by the electron-capture decay of ²²⁹U⁺ ions stored in a Penning trap at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB). This measurement would provide the key nuclear-structure input needed to establish ²²⁹Pa as a leading candidate for next-generation atomic and molecular electric-dipole-moment (EDM) experiments.

articles.title: Collectively pumped superradiant laser with coherence scaling beyond the standard quantum limit
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05976v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For more than half a century, the standard quantum limit (SQL) was thought to limit the laser coherence mathfrakC -- the number of photons emitted from the laser into the beam in one coherence time -- to a scaling Θ(μ²), where μ is the mean number of optical-frequency excitations stored inside the laser. However, recently it has been shown [Baker et al., Nat. Phys. 17, 179 (2021)] that the Heisenberg limit -- an achievable ultimate limit set by quantum mechanics for the task of producing a beam with the standard properties of a laser beam -- is mathfrakC=Θ(μ⁴), a quadratic enhancement. So far, proposals to demonstrate beyond-SQL scaling of mathfrakC have been limited to circuit QED, at microwave frequencies (i.e., a maser). Here, we introduce a class of generalized far-above-threshold (FAT) laser models, obtained by replacing the ordinary bosonic lowering operator hata by a general lowering operator hatL in the superoperators appearing in the master equation that governs the FAT laser dynamics. We then show that an optical-frequency superradiant laser in the bad-cavity limit, with feedback-controlled collective pumping, realizes one such model, in which hatL is identified with the collective superradiant lowering operator hatJ. This model can surpass the SQL scaling, with the coherence exhibiting a scaling as large as mathfrakC= Θ(μ⁸/³) in the optimal parameter regime. Here, in the bad-cavity limit, μapprox N/2, where N is the number of superradiant atoms.

articles.title: Perturbation-Based Reconstruction of Depth-Resolved OCT Attenuation without Requiring a Fully Decayed Signal Tail
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05983v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Depth-resolved attenuation in optical coherence tomography (OCT) can provide quantitative optical contrast beyond structural imaging. However, conventional reconstruction methods can be biased when the OCT signal does not fully decay within the imaging range or when the distal signal tail is dominated by noise or residual reflections from distal sample or support interfaces. Here, we present a perturbation-based Beer-Lambert framework that combines a zeroth-order exponential estimate with a first-order correction, reducing reliance on the unreliable distal signal tail below the current depth. Numerical A-line simulations, Monte Carlo modeling, multilayer silicone-dye-TiO2 phantoms, and ex vivo bovine retina experiments were used to evaluate the method under finite-depth and heterogeneous imaging conditions. The numerical A-line tests showed reduced depth-dependent error against prescribed attenuation profiles; the Monte Carlo comparisons showed less distal drift relative to model-defined benchmarks, while the phantom profiles were compared with separately acquired single-layer OCT calibration values. In a Monte Carlo component test that withheld vessel-mask and vessel-boundary information from reconstruction and used that information only for post hoc evaluation, the first-order correction recovered 61% of the segmentation-informed target vessel contrast and reduced vessel ROI mean absolute error by 65% relative to the fixed zeroth-order baseline. These results suggest that perturbation-based reconstruction may provide a practical approach for depth-resolved reconstruction of effective OCT attenuation when the fully decayed A-line condition is not satisfied.

articles.title: A generic framework for extending Miles' approach to wind-wave interactions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2504.09369v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Understanding the energy transfer from wind to waves is an important but complex topic, typically based on phenomenology, on heavy numerics, or on technically challenging analysis, carried out on a case by case basis. Here we show that the approach by Miles, initially proposed for a still and infinitely deep ocean of inviscid water, is in fact generic: it can easily be adapted, as we demonstrate directly from the mathematical structure of the arguments put forward by Miles. We establish simple transformations, which infer wave growth rates in complex hydrodynamic situations directly from those in Miles' conditions, without any adjustable parameters. The corresponding conversion factors are determined from the hydrodynamic water pressure produced by a propagating surface wave, and can be determined without requiring to further analyse wind and air flow. Alternatively, the dispersion relation (in the absence of air andt hus wind) may be used as a starting point. We reproduce a variety of results for different hydrodynamic situations to show how such generalisations can be achieved with surprisingly simple calculations and without any additional numerical effort, which should make the approach interesting for real-life applications.

articles.title: Comparing the dynamics of idealized squall lines between NWP and LES models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2506.19435v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mesoscale convective systems, such as squall lines, produce large amounts of rainfall but remain challenging to forecast. We intercompare two atmospheric models, namely ICON (ICOsahedral Non-hydrostatic) and MicroHH, to investigate how a simulated squall line depends on the model formulation. ICON is a Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) model, which traditionally aims for accurate weather forecasts, whereas MicroHH is typically used to study physical processes with Large-Eddy Simulations (LES). These different purposes resulted in different designs, mainly because ICON solves the compressible equations on a triangular grid, while MicroHH solves the anelastic equations on a regular grid. With increasing computer power, the applications of these models converge, raising the question of whether the model results also converge. We investigated an idealized squall line with the same case setup in both models, including grid spacing, domain size, boundary conditions, and microphysics scheme. The models simulate the same squall-line structure and circulation pattern. Furthermore, the mean vertical wind and upward mass and humidity fluxes differ less than 5% averaged over the cloud layer at 500 m grid spacing. In contrast, ICON produces less surface precipitation than MicroHH and has higher maximum vertical velocities across grid spacings. At 500 m grid spacing, inter model differences are controlled by the advection scheme and the formulation of moist thermodynamics while differences in the turbulent formulation are less relevant. The quantitative differences between the models across grid spacings highlight that the details of model physics and numerics are at least as important as the grid spacing.

articles.title: Model-Adaptive Simulation of Hierarchical Shallow Water Moment Equations in One Dimension
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.25351v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Shallow free surface flows are often characterized by both subdomains that require high modeling complexity and subdomains that can be sufficiently accurately modeled with low modeling complexity. Moreover, these subdomains may change in time as the water flows through the domain. This motivates the need for space and time adaptivity in the simulation of shallow free surface flows. In this paper, we develop the first adaptive simulations using the recently developed Shallow Water Moment Equations, which are an extension of the standard Shallow Water Equations that allow for vertically changing velocity profiles by including additional variables and equations. The model-specific modeling complexity of a shallow water moment model is determined by its order. The higher the order of the model, the more variables and equations are included in the model. Shallow water moment models are ideally suited for adaptivity because they are hierarchical such that low-order models and high-order models share the same structure. To enable adaptive simulations, we propose two approaches for the coupling of the varying-order shallow water moment equations at their boundary interfaces. The first approach dynamically updates padded state variables but cannot be written in conservative form, while the second approach uses fixed padded state variable values of zero and reduces to conservative form for conservative moment equations. The switching procedure between high-order models and low-order models is based on a new set of model error estimators, originating from a decomposition of the high-order models. Numerical results of a dam break and of the collision of a dam-break wave with a smooth wave for different friction parameter values yield accurate results, while achieving speedups up to 40 percent compared to a non-adaptive model with fixed modeling complexity.

articles.title: Brilliance for adaptive computational research in accelerator physics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.15615v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Computational research requires repeated decisions about models, calculations and the interpretation of results. We introduce Brilliance, an agent that combines large language models, reusable physics expertise and numerical simulation to construct and revise investigations in accelerator physics. Starting from a detailed expert-specified request, Brilliance develops an ideal storage-ring lattice meeting the specified emittance ceiling and sampled nonlinear-acceptance criteria after revising optics that fail particle-tracking tests. Further scientist-guided exploration produces a candidate with a natural emittance of 6.51 pm rad and millimeter-scale transverse acceptance, while exposing unresolved momentum-acceptance limitations. Using measured responses from the High Energy Photon Source, Brilliance also performs offline optics calibration consistent with an independent specialist analysis. An expert-module ablation examines how reusable domain knowledge influences research choices and outcomes. Here, we demonstrate a practical route to scientist-agent collaboration in sustained numerical research.

articles.title: Pump-scheme dependence of few-emitter lasers: exact multilevel correlations and photon statistics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01205v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Few-emitter laser models usually replace the excitation cycle of the gain medium by a single Markovian pump jump of a two-level emitter. We test this replacement with the cavity and laser-transition parameters held fixed and the two-level pump rate fitted to the same mean photon number, using an exact damping-basis continued-fraction solution of the cavity--emitter master equation for N identical d-level emitters with arbitrary independent incoherent transitions and one cavity-coupled transition, in the known reduced space of level populations and lasing coherences. First, a pump-quantum filtration shows that the inter-emitter coherence of Λ and ladder media starts at second rather than first order in the pump; we evaluate its leading coefficient from the exact finite-system series and map the recycling rate at which its sign changes. Second, at matched photon number, rate-limited steps in the pump cycle push the long-time output-counting Fano factor of two and three emitters well below one: for two emitters it reaches 0.66 at a mean cavity occupation of 0.3 and is still 0.74 at an occupation of one, where g⁽²⁾(0) is within 3% of unity, because the anticorrelation sits at delays of about half a cavity lifetime rather than at zero delay. For two and three emitters the fitted two-level model gets both statistics wrong and places the output above the shot-noise level. Against independent single-emitter lasers at the same output, the common cavity erodes rather than enhances this single-emitter effect.

articles.title: Generative Modeling for Cascading Extremes via Autoregressive Transformers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extreme events often occur sequentially, from earthquake-tsunami cascades to successive extreme losses in financial markets. We introduce an extremal token representation that encodes multivariate observations as a categorical sequence. A quiet token records the absence of threshold exceedances; otherwise, the token identifies the exceeding component with the largest marginal probability-scale score. The representation is invariant to componentwise strictly increasing transformations. It preserves the identity and temporal ordering of dominant exceedances but discards their magnitudes and the identities of nondominant simultaneous exceedances. A decoder-only transformer estimates the history-dependent next-token kernel on this representation, and recursive sampling generates future token sequences from the induced joint predictive law. We amortize our generative model by pretraining across simulated process families with varying parameters and dependence persistence. Next-token predictions are evaluated against exact conditional probabilities for held-out categorical processes and particle filter references for heavy-tailed vector autoregressive processes. Applied to ten-second returns for five semiconductor stocks, the pretrained model supports zero-shot transfer, while a few epochs of adaptation improve agreement between observed and generated token frequencies and transition patterns. These results support task-specific tokenization and simulation-based pretraining for modeling which dimensions dominate multivariate extremes.

articles.title: Who May Overrule the Agent? Evidence-Gated Authority in LLM Review Institutions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent language-model systems often add a reviewer to improve an upstream agent's decision. Yet a reviewer can both repair errors and replace decisions that were already correct. We study this as a problem of institutional jurisdiction: conditional on the same proposal, task information, model, and review output, when is the reviewer authorized to make its recommendation binding? We compare broad override authority with an evidence gate that permits replacement only after the reviewer produces a mechanically valid record of a binding-constraint violation and a compliant repair. Across two locally run open-weight models, 96 spatial-policy tasks, and a 96-task portfolio-transfer benchmark, the gate sharply reduces corruption of correct proposals while retaining most repairs of violations. The directions of this tradeoff are partly implied by the rule; its magnitude depends on reviewer transitions and upstream proposal states. A prospective validation then gives the reviewer an explicit choice to retain, replace, or escalate. This eliminates correct-proposal corruption for Qwen, but Mistral still replaces all 48 correct proposals; Qwen also declines every welfare-only repair that Mistral frequently attempts. Thus interface design changes reviewer behavior but is not a model-independent safeguard. The result is not that restricted review is universally better. It is that reviewer competence, action interface, and binding jurisdiction jointly determine both the correction domain and the corruption surface.

articles.title: Verified but Vacuous: Three Failure Surfaces of LLM-Driven Verified Code Generation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: What should ``verified'' mean when evaluating LLM-generated code? Many existing pipelines report a single verification number. We argue this collapses three distinct properties measured in a conditional audit sequence: verifier acceptance (Surface A), emph{syntactic specification binding (Surface B: does the proof obligation bind to the spec?), and emphsemantic specification fidelity (Surface C: does the spec capture the informal requirement?). Two empirical demonstrations show the surfaces separate. textbf{First (A ≠ B), via Li@Opus (a same-model reproduction of citetli2025dafny's Dafny-as-intermediate-representation (IR) pipeline under Claude Opus 4.7) on three Python benchmarks}: it reaches 99.1% verifier acceptance on HumanEval while only 1.9% carry a certificate binding to a spec-defined predicate or function. Second (B ≠ C), via VCG on two Rust benchmarks: we use VCG (which is our own in-house Dafny-as-intermediate pipeline) on Rust because the Rust target lets us enforce fully-verifiable output (every component ships as a Dafny certificate, ensures-binding gate passing by construction). Even inside that construction, 11.48% (MBPP-Rust) and 14.82% (VeriContest LC slice) of structurally-verified samples still fail hidden tests. On the LC slice of VeriContest, VCG's reported End2End rate is 7.79% (535/6870). The cited external rates are 5.51% (GPT-5.5) and 1.88% (single-shot Opus 4.7). These give descriptive differences of 2.3 percentage points and 4.14×, respectively; task-budget, repair and harness differences prevent a matched-performance claim.

articles.title: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The performance of large language model (LLM) agents depends on both the underlying model and the harness that governs interaction with tools and the environment. Yet harness design remains largely manual, and automating it requires navigating an open-ended search space through costly end-to-end evaluations. We introduce HarnessFlow, a framework for optimizing complete executable harnesses under a limited candidate-evaluation budget, with the model and task environment held fixed. HarnessFlow organizes candidates and their evaluation histories in a refinement tree, using a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS)-based policy to balance exploitation and exploration. A coding agent refines selected harnesses using archived code, execution feedback, and a library of reusable harness mechanisms. With 15 refinement attempts per benchmark, HarnessFlow achieves the highest mean test scores among the compared methods on six benchmarks spanning agentic tasks, coding, and web interaction. The optimized harnesses achieve an average score of 69.48%, outperforming the initial harnesses and Meta-Harness by 10.89 and 3.95 percentage points, respectively, while incurring lower average per-task execution costs than hand-engineered baselines. These results suggest that structured harness search offers a promising route toward automating the design of capable and efficient LLM agents.

articles.title: DyPSI: Dynamic Physics Sensing via Joint Field and Sensor-Trajectory Generation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06280v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics sensing in evolving environments requires reconstructing dense spatiotemporal fields from sparse observations while adapting where future observations should be collected. Existing reconstruction and sensor-placement methods have made substantial progress, but they typically rely on static sensing assumptions: they either use a single layout across all frames or optimize placements independently at each frame, which limits their ability to produce temporally coherent sensing trajectories. We introduce DyPSI, a dynamic physics sensing framework that formulates this problem as the joint generation of future fields and sensor trajectories conditioned on historical observations. DyPSI lifts discrete sensor coordinates into continuous Sensor Position Fields, encodes fields and sensing configurations with a shared Functional Tucker representation, and trains a joint diffusion model to generate future fields and sensing trajectories simultaneously in the resulting latent space. A Gaussian-process temporal kernel correlates the perturbation injected during diffusion training, biasing the denoiser toward temporally smooth recoveries, and we further provide an analysis linking the EDM training objective to a sequence-aggregated A-optimality criterion and a kernel-induced bound on discrete trajectory variation. Experiments on turbulent flow, GLORYS12 sea-surface temperature, and 3D car aerodynamics show that DyPSI consistently outperforms static and frame-wise placement strategies, with substantial error reduction under tight sensor budgets. The code is available at https://github.com/mengqi132/DyPSI.

articles.title: AI-Driven SaaS Platform Integration: AI Express for Unified Generative AI Services with Pay-As-You-Go Credit Systems and Scalable Microservice Architecture
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05389v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI is currently fragmented, with separate subscriptions required for text generation, image synthesis, and code assistance, leading to high costs and workflow disruptions. AI Express is a SaaS platform that consolidates these capabilities into a unified pay-as-you-go service. The platform provides a range of AI tools, including a Core Code Reviewer that evaluates GitHub repositories, a Text-to-Website generator that converts text into fully functional websites, script generation, grammar checking, data analysis, and watermark removal, all accessible through a single interface without requiring technical expertise.

articles.title: When File Ingestion Misleads Language Models: Measuring and Mitigating Divergences in Office Documents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05806v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Office documents are now routinely uploaded to large language models (LLMs) for processing. However, an LLM does not always see what a human sees, because it typically reads the text that an extractor produces from the document's underlying Office Open XML (OOXML) files. Depending on the implementation, extractors differ in which OOXML parts they read and how they interpret them, so their output can differ from what Office applications display. For example, by slightly shifting the positions of text boxes on a slide, an adversary can swap the order in which the model reads them while the slide looks unchanged. We show that this extraction divergence is an attack surface for LLM applications. In this work, we first measure what an adversary can exploit by analyzing the widely used extractors that LLM applications rely on. By combining static source code analysis with dynamic analysis, we identify 19 OOXML channels where extractors read content a human cannot see and 12 where they drop content a human can. We also find that widely used extractors ignore display formatting and reading order, so even visible content reaches the model in a different form. Building on these findings, we construct five attacks that lead the model to interpret a document differently from a human reviewer, without injecting any instruction. We test the attacks on four major chat assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Microsoft 365 Copilot) and four coding agents (Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity, and GitHub Copilot CLI), and every one of them is misled by at least one attack. Finally, we propose Prism, a lightweight defense that reconstructs the human view from the OOXML specification before passing the text to the model. Prism also generalizes to unseen attack payloads.

articles.title: ArcRAG: Agentic Compositional Retrieval over Knowledge Graphs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06481v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG) answers questions by retrieving over a knowledge graph built from a corpus. Yet retrieval strategies are designed around the structure their own construction pipeline produces, and whether they survive a change of construction is rarely tested. We study this cross-construction portability: whether one retrieval procedure, with no construction-specific schema, relation names, or retuning, stays effective when the graph is built differently. We introduce ArcRAG, which induces a query-local graph interface at inference time (the node labels, relation descriptors, and property keys reachable from the entities a question names), plans multi-hop traversals against it, and executes and repairs them as Cypher. We build each of the MuSiQue, HotpotQA, and TriviaQA corpora as a schema-guided graph (typed nodes, a closed relation set, source provenance) and as an open-information-extraction graph (untyped nodes, free-text relations), with the retriever's configuration fixed across them. We compare against a construction-agnostic Direct-Cypher agent, ablate each stage across retry and pass budgets on both graph families, and compare with results reported for prior GraphRAG systems, most of which design retrieval together with their own graph construction. Across the two constructions, we find that retrieval need not be co-designed with the graph: query-time interface induction keeps a construction-agnostic retriever effective when the construction changes, although construction still shapes absolute accuracy.

articles.title: AgentTrustCI: Build-Time Policy, Grounding, and Trajectory Tests for Java LLM Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.06674v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Infrastructure security does not establish whether an LLM agent selected an allowed tool, grounded its answer in tool output, or followed a required workflow. AgentTrustCI is a Java/JUnit 5 framework that expresses these application-layer expectations as policy, grounding, and trajectory checks over recorded traces. A deterministic replay implementation supports repeatable build-time tests; a judge interface provides an extension point for optional semantic evaluation. On 55 synthetic cases spanning seven enterprise domains, the full pipeline correctly classifies all 30 injected faults and 25 passing controls, including ten non-trivial controls, and misses none of 12 designated critical cases. Each single-layer configuration correctly classifies 35 cases because the corpus deliberately isolates ten faults per layer. A grounded answer obtained through a disallowed sequence illustrates the additional coverage of trajectory checks. Repeated measurements quantify validator execution separately from process startup and reporting. These results establish coverage of the authored regression suite, not production accuracy. We describe a production-trace validation protocol, optional LLM-judge integration, and maintenance of expectations as workflows evolve. The contribution is a practical pattern for expressing behavioral contracts within an existing Java release pipeline.

articles.title: Task-Dependent Prefrontal Cortex Activation During Balance–Cognitive Dual Tasks in Ice Hockey Players: Evidence From Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: This study compared prefrontal activation in ice hockey players and non-athlete adults during balance and cognitive dual-task conditions and examined its relationship with balance performance. Seventeen male ice hockey players and 17 age-matched healthy controls completed five randomized tasks: static and dynamic balance single tasks, a cognitive single task, and static and dynamic balance–cognitive dual tasks. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy measured prefrontal oxygenated hemoglobin (HbO), while balance indices and cognitive performance were recorded. Repeated-measures analysis of variance and Pearson correlations were conducted. Players showed superior balance performance across balance tasks (P < 0.05), whereas cognitive performance did not differ (P > 0.05). A significant group × task interaction was found for left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex HbO changes (F = 5.303, P = 0.002, q = 0.022, η²p = 0.142). Compared with controls, players showed greater HbO changes during the static dual task but lower changes during the dynamic dual task. During the dynamic dual task, DLPFC-L HbO changes correlated positively with balance indices in players (r = 0.721, P = 0.001) and controls (r = 0.674, P = 0.003). Ice hockey players may achieve better balance through task-dependent, efficient prefrontal resource allocation.

articles.title: Forced transition as a design and robustness variable for the lifting surfaces of solar stratospheric platforms
articles.abstract: Forcing boundary-layer transition is the standard remedy for the laminar separation bubble that dominates the drag of low-Reynolds lifting surfaces, and on a solar stratospheric platform it is normally discussed for the wing. Here the forced-transition location is treated as an explicit design variable inside a coupled environment–sizing–mission closure, the trip is charged for its own excrescence drag, and the result is resolved by component. Section polars for five low-Reynolds airfoils are generated over chord Reynolds numbers (:3×:10⁴le:Recle:10⁶) with the transition location and the amplification factor (:ncᵣᵢₜ) as free axes; the trip height is sized from the roughness Reynolds number criterion. Three results follow. First, charging the trip for its own drag moves the profitability threshold from (:Recapprox:3.5×:10⁵) to (:approx:2.0×:10⁵). Second, the platform straddles that threshold: the wing, at (:Rec=1.97×:10⁵), loses from a trip at every height considered, while the empennage, at (:1.08×:10⁵), gains throughout — tripping both surfaces costs 1.8% in gross mass, the empennage alone saves 4.6%, the wing alone costs 6.6%. Third, the benefit grows as the disturbance environment quiets, from 1.5% at (:ncᵣᵢₜ=7) to 8.7% at (:ncᵣᵢₜ=13), so transition control is worth most precisely where transition prediction is least verifiable; against wind-tunnel data, tripping reduces the sensitivity of predicted drag to the amplification factor eighteen-fold. The design rule is therefore component-wise, not chordwise: trip the surfaces below the bubble threshold and leave those above it clean.

articles.title: Comparative effect of dietary full-fat or defatted Hermetia illucens larvae on growth and fatty acid profiles of juvenile Oncorhynchus mykiss
articles.abstract: Although black soldier fly (BSF) larvae meal (BSFL) has been a promising alternative ingredient, limited information is available on full-fat BSF larvae meal (FBSF), which may offer cost-savings in aquafeed. This study evaluated the effects of FBSF compared with defatted BSF larvae meal (DBSF) as fishmeal substitutes on the growth performance and biochemical responses of juvenile rainbow trout. A control diet contained fishmeal at 360 g/kg diet, and four experimental diets replaced fishmeal with FBSF or DBSF at 36 or 108 g/kg diet (designated as FBSF10, FBSF30, DBSF10, and DBSF30, respectively). Following an 8-week feeding trial, only FBSF30 resulted in reduced growth and an increased feed conversion ratio compared to the control. Proximate compositions of carcass and viscera were unaffected. Tissue fatty acid profiles mirrored dietary composition; polyunsaturated fatty acids (including C20:5n-3 and C22:6n-3) decreased with higher BSFL inclusion, whereas saturated fatty acids increased, with C12:0 levels significantly elevated in the FBSF30 group. Principal component analysis associated FBSF30 strongly with saturated fatty acid vectors (C12:0 and C14:0), demonstrating that high FBSF inclusion markedly shifts tissue lipid composition toward saturation. Serum cortisol, glutathione peroxidase, superoxide dismutase, lysozyme, and immunoglobulin M levels were unaffected across treatments. Overall, up to 30% DBSF and 10% FBSF can replace fishmeal in juvenile rainbow trout diets without compromising growth or physiological health. While FBSF offers economic advantages, inclusion levels must be optimized to prevent growth impairment and lipid alterations.

articles.title: Retrieval of wheat biophysical parameters using hybrid polarimetric SAR decompositions from RISAT-1 data
articles.abstract: Accurate estimation of crop biophysical parameters such as biomass and phenological stage is critical for large-scale agricultural monitoring. Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), particularly in hybrid polarimetric mode, offers enhanced capability for vegetation characterization under all-weather conditions. This study investigates the retrieval of wheat biophysical parameters using hybrid polarimetric decomposition techniques applied to RISAT-1 C-band SAR data acquired during the 2015–2016 rabi season over Junagadh district, Gujarat, India. Ground-based measurements, including crop biomass and age, were collected in synchronization with satellite overpasses. Stokes parameter-based decompositions, m-δ and m-χ, were implemented alongside Raney decomposition to examine their sensitivity to biomass, crop growth progression, and maturity. Additionally, the Radar Vegetation Index and Alpha Angle were derived from C2 and pseudo-C3 matrices to assess their correlation with ground-truth parameters. Results indicate that the m-δ decomposition provides the most consistent response, with odd-bounce components decreasing and diffuse scattering increasing as biomass and crop age progress. Radar Vegetation Index values ranged from 0.27 to 0.52, while Alpha Angle values indicated a transition from surface to volume scattering with crop development. The diffuse component of the m-δ decomposition showed the strongest correlation with field-measured biomass, outperforming both m-χ and Raney methods. The study confirms the effectiveness of hybrid polarimetric SAR for estimating crop biophysical parameters and presents a transferable decomposition framework for operational crop monitoring. The findings are directly applicable to national and global agricultural monitoring programmes and provide methodological benchmarks for hybrid SAR missions, including RISAT-1A/1B and NISAR.

articles.title: A leptomeningeal-astrocyte co-culture model reveals that cell communication informs barrier function and gene expression at the human pial-glial membrane
articles.abstract: The pial-glial membrane is a specialised interface which maintains separation between the brain parenchyma and cerebrospinal fluid, limiting immune cell entry into the brain. This structure is comprised of two dominant cell types, leptomeningeal cells and astrocytes, separated by a shared basement membrane. Despite its importance, there are few in vitro models which examine this brain border. This study comprehensively examines a leptomeningeal-astrocyte co-culture model through transcriptomic profiling, functional barrier assessment, and protein expression. Co‑culture generates distinct, interaction-mode-dependent transcriptional states. Functional barrier assessment reveal that astrocytes are essential modulators of leptomeningeal cell barrier functions, significantly increasing transendothelial resistance while maintaining physiological permeability. Protein validation highlights challenges in identifying leptomeningeal markers in vitro, with all markers detected in adult human meningeal tissue including BMP5 and NGFR. Collectively, these findings establish a foundational model for dissecting pial-glial interactions, defining the global transcriptional reprogramming elicited by co-culture, and advancing mechanistic understanding of barrier function.

articles.title: Preclinical Evaluation of CuraVue ® : A Novel Dual-Action Antimicrobial Silicone Adhesive Securement Dressing
articles.abstract: Background Catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSIs) are among the most important challenges facing health care workers, leading to morbidity and mortality all over the world. CuraVue® is an antimicrobial adhesive securement dressing loaded with Chlorhexidine and Silver that is designed to offer sustained broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity over 7 days, thus proving it to be an efficient dressing at vascular access and device insertion sites, allowing reduction of the incidence of CRBSIs. Results Seven antimicrobial studies were carried out to assess CuraVue® antimicrobial activity, namely Disc Diffusion Testing (CLSI M02), Quantitative Contact-kill Test (ISO 22196), Quantitative Time-kill Test over 7 Days (Modified ISO 22196), Minimum Inhibitory Concentration (MIC) Detection, Static Coupon Biofilm Assay (ASTM E3435), assessment of Chlorhexidine and Silver Spatial Uniformity Distribution, and In Vivo Evaluation of Antimicrobial Efficacy in a Rat Skin Abrasion Colonization Model. Disc diffusion testing showed measurable zones of inhibition against all tested strains. The ISO 22196 contact-kill assay showed ≥ 99.99% reduction against all tested organisms, with exceptional activity against P. aeruginosa (R = 6.00). The 7-day time-kill assay gave mean R values ≥ 4.0 for S. aureus, E. coli, and P. aeruginosa, with no significant decline over time (linear regression, p > 0.05). MIC testing showed bacterial inhibition. The biofilm assay demonstrated strong antibiofilm activity (> 99% inhibition against the three tested strains). Spatial uniformity testing confirmed consistent antimicrobial activity across all regions of the dressing. An ISO-certified testing laboratory validated CuraVue® antimicrobial activity, showing > 5.22 log and > 5.12 log reductions against E. coli and S. aureus, respectively, confirming its strong, sustained antimicrobial efficacy. In the rat skin abrasion colonization model, CuraVue® significantly reduced bacterial burden compared to the negative control. Conclusions CuraVue® demonstrated broad-spectrum and sustained antimicrobial activity throughout the 7 day wear period supported by antibiofilm formation activity and localized microbial suppression on skin surface as proven in an in vivo animal model. These results indicate that CuraVue® should be considered as an effective antimicrobial protective dressing for vascular access and device insertion sites.

articles.title: Analog/RF performance of Hexagonal Gate All Around Nanosheet FET with Spacer Engineering
articles.abstract: The analog/RF performance of gate-all-around nanosheet field-effect transistor (GAA NSFET) with spacer dielectric engineering is investigated using three-dimensional TCAD tool. The analog/RF figures of merit of the GAA NSFET, including the intrinsic gain, transconductance generation factor, unity-current gain frequency (f_T), transconductance-frequency product (TFP), gain-frequency product (GFP), and gain-transconductance-frequency product (GTFP), are evaluated for different single layer spacers and dual layer spacers. Employing single-layer SiO₂ spacer as the reference baseline, which inherently exhibit favourable RF metrics with f_T of 540.19 GHz, TFP of 5,120 GHz/V, GFP of 32 THz, GTFP = 137 THz/V, and intrinsic voltage gain of 59.3 V/V owing to low dielectric permittivity and consequent parasitic capacitance minimization, this work demonstrates that strategic dual-layer heterostructure implementation enables application domain specific performance optimization transcending single-dielectric limitations. For RF and analog-centric applications, the proposed GAA NSFET with SiO₂+Si₃N₄ dual-spacer architecture manifests unprecedented enhancements: 31.25 % TFP elevation to 6720 GHz/V, 29.38 % GFP amplification to 4.14×10⁴ GHz, 19.71 % GTFP augmentation to 1.64×10⁵ GHz/V, and 7.55 % f_T improvement to 580.96 GHz, compared to single-layer SiO₂. This performance superiority emanates from synergistic exploitation of the outer low-k SiO₂ layer for fringing capacitance suppression and the inner moderate-k Si₃N₄ layer for enhanced gate-channel electrostatic coupling, yielding optimized transconductance-to-capacitance ratios.

articles.title: Joint Field Characterisation of Onboard Perception, Mapping and Manipulation on a Sub-13 kg Rocker-Bogie Rover
articles.abstract: This paper reports the joint outdoor characterisation of detection, mapping, local re-planning and grasping running concurrently on one 4 GB embedded graphics processing unit module aboard a 12.982 kg six-wheel rocker-bogie rover, and the power it draws. Platforms of this class are characterised one subsystem at a time. The high-level stack runs as Robot Operating System 2 (ROS 2) nodes. On a held-out split of 250 annotated outdoor frames spanning overcast and direct sunlight, a half-precision single shot multibox detector on a MobileNetV2 backbone reached 89.4% mean average precision at 0.5 intersection over union while the vehicle sustained 14.5 frames per second with mapping, planning and telemetry resident. Planar light detection and ranging inertial mapping over a bounded 10 m by 10 m grass plot returned 11.2 cm positional root mean square error, with 220 ms local re-planning latency, bounding safe ground speed near 0.34 m s −1. Thirty autonomous pick-and-place trials on a 12 cm cylindrical target succeeded 23 times: 76.7%, Wilson 95% interval 0.59–0.88. Mean terminal draw under mixed duty was 38.5 W, exceeding the duty-weighted prediction from three isolated states by 16.3 W and giving about 5.3 h of derived endurance. Perception , mapping, manipulation and terminal power were measured together on one sub-13 kg field platform, and the shortfall shows that a budget built from isolated subsystem states underestimates what this autonomy actually draws.

articles.title: Experimental Characterization of Early Colonization Kinetics of Rhizobium meliloti on Alfalfa (Medicago sativa) roots
articles.abstract: Aims The establishment of nitrogen-fixing symbiosis between Sinorhizobium meliloti (syn. Rhizobium meliloti) and alfalfa (Medicago sativa) depends on early bacterial colonization of root surfaces. This study experimentally evaluated the kinetics of early bacterial attachment, desorption and persistence on axenic alfalfa seedlings using the wild-type strain S. meliloti 41.Methods Colonization dynamics were assessed under different inoculum densities (10⁴–10⁶ cells mL⁻¹) and sequential washing conditions in phosphate buffer (0.05 M, pH 7.0), including continuous exposure and mechanical agitation (ten cycles), to distinguish weakly retained cells from firmly attached populations. Root-associated and released bacteria were quantified as colony-forming units (CFU) on MR agar, and functional symbiosis was verified by transferring washed seedlings to nitrogen-free Jensen's medium to monitor nodulation.Results Colonization followed a biphasic pattern, with a rapid association phase (0–2 h) followed by stabilization (3–5 h). Bacterial retention increased with inoculum density (R² = 0.8587), the highest density (10⁶ cells mL⁻¹) producing the greatest colonization efficiency. Sequential washing and mechanical agitation showed that approximately 93.6% of initially retained bacteria were weakly bound and readily removed, whereas a smaller resistant subpopulation remained stably attached. Longer incubation and higher plant density promoted bacterial persistence and root-surface recolonization.Conclusions Early root colonization by S. meliloti is a dynamic, time- and density-dependent process involving an initial reversible retention phase followed by the establishment of a stable, nodulation-competent bacterial population, providing the biological foundation for subsequent symbiotic development.

articles.title: Towards strength-ductility synergy in bimodal-grained 7075Al matrix composites reinforced with high-content n-SiC by regulating coarse-grained components
articles.abstract: Owing to the inherent strength–ductility trade-off and complex changes in precipitation behavior, the design of 7xxxAl composites with high n-SiC content has long been a formidable challenge. Here, we fabricated a bimodal n‑SiC/7075Al composite in powder metallurgy route and investigated the role of coarse-grained (CG) microstructures in mechanical responses. The spatially alternate arrangement of ultrafine-grained (UFG) zones with high-content (10 wt%) n‑SiC and CG zones without n‑SiC delivers superior mechanical properties: yield strength (YS) of 538.4 MPa, ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of 662.0 MPa, elongation (El) of 5.7% and a strain hardening exponent of 0.078. Compared with 7075Al, the suppressed intragranular nanoprecipitates by dispersive n-SiC/Al interfaces facilitate the hetero-deformation-induced (HDI) stress as dominant strengthening contribution rather than Orowan mechanism. The improved ductility is attributed to the synergy of both intrinsic and extrinsic toughening mechanisms. The former origins from the enhanced HDI strain hardening capacity by means of strain gradients and nanoprecipitates; while the latter derives from the delocalized nucleation and growth of microcracks.

articles.title: Effect-Engineered Hardening in KNL–NTS via CuO Acceptor Doping: A Doping-Window Map for Resonant Applications
articles.abstract: Lead-free KNL–NTS piezoceramics exhibit competitive electromechanical properties, but their performance may deteriorate under resonant operating conditions. Here, CuO incorporation was investigated as a strategy to balance mechanical quality factor and piezoelectric activity. CuO promoted mechanical hardening, with (Qm) reaching a maximum at a nominal CuO content of x = 0.5 mol% and decreasing moderately at (x = 1.0) mol%, likely because of increasing structural and microstructural heterogeneity. This evolution is consistent with restricted domain-wall motion associated with Cu-related defect pinning, although this mechanism was not directly established in the present samples. Among the investigated compositions, (x = 0.25) mol% provided the most favourable balance between reduced mechanical losses and retained electromechanical activity. Structural, dielectric, and resonance measurements, together with finite-element modelling, showed that this composition produced a higher resonant displacement than undoped KNL–NTS under identical electrical excitation. These results demonstrate that controlled CuO incorporation is a practical strategy for tailoring the resonant performance of lead-free piezoceramics.

articles.title: Improved Water/Polar Liquid Separation Performance of Graphene Oxide Membranes by Increasing the Starting Dispersion Concentration
articles.abstract: Graphene oxide membranes (GOMs) are promising materials for separating water from polar organic liquids, but their separation performance depends strongly on membrane architecture and fabrication conditions. Three free-standing GOMs were prepared from the same starting graphene oxide dispersion at two concentrations: 2 mg mL⁻¹ (isotropic) and 10 mg mL⁻¹ (liquid-crystalline). The orientation of graphene oxide layers within the membranes was examined using spin-probe technique. For one membrane prepared from the concentrated dispersion, the nitroxide spin probe H2 was added before filtration; for the other two membranes, the probe was introduced after membrane formation. Lamellar orientation was evaluated by SEM image analysis. The second-rank lamellar order parameters were similar for all three membranes (T2 = 0.86–0.92), whereas the layer order parameters were lower (P2 = 0.49–0.62) and differed between membranes prepared from isotropic and liquid-crystalline dispersions. Water-vapor permeance was comparable across all membranes, at approximately 0.046–0.052 mol m⁻² s⁻¹ bar⁻¹. In contrast, ethanol- and acetonitrile-vapor permeances decreased by a factor of approximately 4 and 2.5, respectively, for membranes prepared from the concentrated dispersion. Consequently, their water/ethanol selectivity increased from 12 for the isotropic-dispersion membrane to 36–43 for the membranes prepared from the concentrated dispersion, while water/acetonitrile selectivity increased from 9 to 21. These results show that increasing the starting dispersion concentration can substantially improve transport selectivity while maintaining similar water permeance. The two membranes prepared from the concentrated dispersion showed similar permeance and selectivity.

articles.title: Geotechnical Characterisation of Subgrade and Sub-Base Materials for Road Pavement Design in Kasese District, Western Uganda
articles.abstract: Abstract Pre-design and construction geotechnical assessment of subgrade and sub-base materials was carried out for optimal pavement performance and sustainability in Kasese District, Western Uganda. The method involved boring 30 trial holes, sampling, and geotechnical testing. Soil profile indicates a top organic clay layer (OL/OH) from surface to 0.45 m, a silty clay layer (CL/CI) to 1.2 m, and a poorly graded sand with gravel layer (SP/GP) to 2.0 m. Subgrades classify as USCS CL-CI, AASHTO A-2-6, A-2-7, and A-7-6, with 62% rated as poor to fair and 38% good to excellent due to high seasonal moisture from nearby Rwenzori Mountains and Nyamwamba River floods. Clay activity ranges from 0.9 to 38.7, expansivity from 5.2 to 62.4, indicating presence of sensitive and expansive clays. 48-hour soaked CBR varies from 5% to 32%, surface modulus (Eₛ) from 55 MPa to 150 MPa. Sub-base fills have moisture content 14-22%, liquid limit 22-35%, plastic limit 12–20%, plasticity index 8-14, composed of 32% fines and 68% sands; AASHTO A-2-6 rated excellent to good. Soaked CBR of sub-base ranges 18-42% with 12-58% strength reduction upon soaking. Resilient modulus varies from 200-500 MN/m². Recommended pavement thickness is 350-400 mm based on CBR and group index, with coarse granular sub-bases recommended for moisture egress to improve effective stress.

articles.title: Event-Triggered Practical Predefined-Time Fault-Tolerant Synchronization of Second-Order Chaotic Systems
articles.abstract: This study addresses the synchronization problem of second-order chaotic systems subject to parameter uncertainties, external disturbances, and actuator faults, and proposes a predefined-time nonsingular terminal sliding mode control (NTSMC) strategy. A nonsingular terminal sliding surface is designed so that the convergence time can be prescribed in advance. A time-varying barrier-function-based adaptive gain is developed to increase the robust gain as the sliding variable approaches the barrier boundary. The proposed strategy does not require prior knowledge of the disturbance upper bound, thereby avoiding control-gain overestimation associated with conventional fixed-gain or adaptive-gain approaches. In addition, a periodic event-triggering mechanism (ETM) is designed to transmit a new command only when the deviation of the nominal compensation command from its held value exceeds a threshold, thereby reducing the communication burden. The stability of the closed-loop system is established using Lyapunov theory. Finally, several simulation experiments demonstrate the feasibility and superior performance of the proposed scheme.

articles.title: Enhancement of photocurrent in NdCoO 3 via the plasmonic effect of silver microparticles
articles.abstract: Rare earth cobalt perovskites of formula ReCoO3 are an important group of materials that have applications in many emerging technologies such as energy storage devices, photocatalysis, gas sensors, and many more. An effective strategy for improving their physical and physicochemical properties has been the formation of metal-semiconductor heterojunctions. In this work, the effect of adding silver microparticles (Ag (µPs)) to NdCoO3 on its photodetection properties was investigated. For the preparation of NdCoO3 and Ag/NdCoO3, the microwave-assisted combustion method was used, which provides a fast, inexpensive and efficient route to synthesize them, without subsequent high temperature calcination. The photoconductive properties in UV light were evaluated through photocurrent (Iph) measurements, at room temperature, on thick films made with the as-prepared materials. The results revealed an increase of at least one order of magnitude in the variation of Iph (ΔIph) in Ag/NdCoO3, compared with the single-phase material. This was attributed to the plasmonic effect produced by the homogeneous distribution of Ag (µPs) in the perovskite. Polarization curves confirmed the quantitative detection of this radiation. For near-infrared radiation (NIR), no significant response was obtained for NdCoO3; however, reliable results were registered in Ag/NdCoO3. Based on the results, it was possible to conclude that the introduction of non-agglomerated Ag (µPs) into cobalt-based perovskites represents a suitable method for improving their photosensing properties.

articles.title: Bio‑Stabilized Copper Nanoclusters Enable Highly Selective Aerobic Alcohol Oxidation in Water
articles.abstract: Water‑soluble bovine serum albumin‑stabilized copper nanoclusters (BSA–Cu NCs) were synthesized and fully characterized by FT‑IR, UV–Vis, TEM, XPS, photoluminescence spectroscopy, ICP, and TGA. The ultrasmall nanoclusters (1.7 ± 0.5 nm), predominantly containing Cu⁰ species, exhibited high structural stability and strong ligand‑to‑metal charge transfer features. The BSA–Cu NCs demonstrated excellent catalytic performance in the aerobic oxidation of a wide range of primary and secondary alcohols under mild conditions (25°C, water, air or O₂), affording the corresponding carbonyl compounds with > 99% selectivity. Studies on optimization showed that catalyst loading, oxygen flow rate, and isobutyraldehyde as a cocatalyst are all important for getting quantitative conversions in a short amount of time. Spectroscopic analyses and radical-trapping experiments substantiate a Cu(II)/Cu(I) redox-mediated radical pathway, while dismissing the generation of peroxo or superoxo copper species. The catalyst kept working over many cycles with very little damage to its structure. Compared with previously reported copper‑based systems, the BSA–Cu NCs offer a sustainable, efficient, and environmentally benign platform for aerobic alcohol oxidation in aqueous media.

articles.title: Mathematical Framework for Dynamic Downside-Minimizing Portfolio with Exotic Option Overlay
articles.abstract: This study develops and evaluates a dynamic downside-minimizing portfolio through five stages. Starting with a 4-asset universe of equity, bonds, gold, and a volatility instrument, the portfolio is expanded to 13 and then 21 assets while incorporating mean-semivariance optimization, Asian arithmetic-average puts, American puts valued with Longstaff–Schwartz Least-Squares Monte Carlo, covered calls, momentum tilts, and regime-aware rebalancing. The final stage targets a 15% expected return. Portfolio performance is evaluated using correlated Geometric Brownian Motion with 20,000 Monte Carlo paths over a one-year horizon. The four-asset semivariance-optimized portfolio has a Sortino ratio of 2.04 and a maximum simulated loss of −23.7%, compared with 1.20 and −45.9% for SPY. Adding Asian and American puts increases the Sortino ratio to 2.26 and reduces maximum simulated loss to −8.8%. The 13-asset buy-and-hold portfolio reaches a mean Sortino ratio of 5.81. Among the rebalancing strategies tested, calendar rebalancing produced the highest mean Sortino ratio of 9.62. The 21-asset portfolio with a 15% return target has a Sortino ratio of 4.06 and maximum simulated loss of −28.8%; the full option overlay reduces the latter to −9.1%. These results characterize the tradeoffs among diversification, downside protection, return targets, and adaptive rebalancing within the simulated framework.

articles.title: Seismic Performance of Reinforced-Concrete Beam-Column Joints With Conventional Steel and Hybrid Shape-Memory-Alloy/Fiber- Reinforced-Polymer Reinforcement: A Critical Review
articles.abstract: Background Reinforced-concrete (RC) beam-column joints are critical regions in moment-resisting frames because they must transfer large cyclic moments, shear forces, and axial forces while maintaining anchorage integrity and structural continuity during earthquakes. Conventional steel-reinforced joints can provide substantial strength and hysteretic energy dissipation when properly detailed, but severe cyclic loading may produce reinforcement yielding, bond deterioration, joint shear damage, corrosion-related durability problems, and permanent residual deformation.  Purpose—This review critically evaluates conventional reinforcement, shape-memory-alloy (SMA) reinforcement, fiber-reinforced-polymer (FRP) systems, and emerging SMA+FRP hybrid concepts for improving the seismic performance and resilience of RC beam-column joints. Coverage Particular emphasis is placed on literature published from 2023 to 16 August 2026, supplemented by landmark earlier studies required to establish joint mechanics, SMA constitutive behaviour, FRP strengthening principles, and the origin of hybrid SMA-FRP concepts.  Findings—The literature indicates that SMA reinforcement is particularly effective for self-centering and residual-deformation control, whereas FRP systems are attractive for corrosion resistance, joint shear strengthening, confinement, and minimally invasive rehabilitation. However, SMA systems can provide narrower hysteresis than yielding steel, while FRP performance is strongly controlled by bond, anchorage, fiber orientation, substrate condition, and brittle failure. Hybridization offers a rational means of combining restoring capability with strength, confinement, durability, and energy-dissipation mechanisms.  Research gap—Direct, recent, full-scale experimental validation of true SMA+FRP RC beam-column joints remains sparse, particularly under bidirectional loading, variable axial force, slab participation, temperature effects, aftershocks, and multi-hazard exposure.  Conclusion—SMA+FRP hybrid joints represent a promising resilience-oriented structural concept, but standardized detailing, validated nonlinear models, probabilistic performance assessment, life-cycle evaluation, and code-ready design procedures are required before routine engineering implementation.

articles.title: Ab initio -based intermolecular potential for normal hydrogen, orthohydrogen, and parahydrogen: Prediction of thermodynamic behavior
articles.abstract: An ab initio -based intermolecular potential is reported for normal hydrogen, orthohydrogen, and parahydrogen. Molecular simulations for thermodynamic properties and calculations of the second virial coefficients demonstrate very good agreement with reference values for both the nuclear spin isomers of hydrogen. The thermodynamic behavior studied includes vapor–liquid equilibria, energy, enthalpy, heat capacities, isochoric pressure coefficient, isobaric thermal expansion coefficient, isothermal compressibility, Joule–Thomson coefficient, and speed of sound. The simulations extend from low (cryogenic) to ambient temperatures and pressures of up to 100 MPa. Quantum effects have an important influence on the behavior of these properties, which, in some cases, are not limited to the intermolecular potential contribution to the energy. That is, the enthalpy, heat capacities, Joule–Thomson coefficient, and speed of sound are also significantly affected by quantum effects on the kinetic energy. The simulation values may be more reliable than existing reference data in some instances. This is particularly the case for the thermodynamic properties of orthohydrogen that cannot be measured directly.

articles.title: Fractional viscoelasticity in transient unentangled polymer networks
articles.abstract: Stress relaxation in transient polymer networks often shows extended power-law behavior, G ( t ) ∼ t − β , where the exponent β frequently departs from the value 1/2 predicted by the sticky Rouse model and its variants. We introduce the fractional inhomogeneous Rouse model (FIRM), which uses a generalized Langevin equation driven by fractional Gaussian noise of exponent α , while retaining heterogeneous bead friction to represent sticky cross-links. Thus, FIRM unifies subdiffusive sticker dynamics and chain heterogeneity within a single framework. We show that the relaxation modulus G ( t ) can be represented as a linear combination of the squares of Mittag–Leffler functions. For homogeneous chains, it recovers two power-law regimes, t − α /2 and t −2 α , on either side of the Rouse relaxation time. Fitting FIRM to stress relaxation data for an imine-based polystyrene vitrimer shows that α < 1 captures the shape of G ( t ) over finite observation windows. FIRM accommodates both Arrhenius and non-Arrhenius temperature dependences in the effective activation energy. We derive expressions for dynamic properties, such as mean-squared displacement and dielectric response, and outline how generalized memory kernels extend the framework to real materials. Together, these results suggest novel ways in which data from rheology, dielectric spectroscopy, scattering, and other experimental methods may be incorporated into a molecular model.

articles.title: Interaction embedding via factorized linear models for multi-element machine learning interatomic potentials
articles.abstract: Linear machine-learning interatomic potentials, such as the Ultra-Fast Force Field (UF3), deliver near-density functional theory accuracy at low computational cost. Their number of parameters, however, grows combinatorially with the number of chemical species, limiting their use on multi-element systems. We address this scaling problem with pseudo-interaction UF3 (PI-UF3), a factorized linear model in which the Z ( k ) real k -body potentials are expressed as linear combinations of a small number P ( k ) ≪ Z ( k ) of shared pseudo-interactions. Learned element embeddings are standard in nonlinear potentials; inside a linear model, the embedding becomes a rank constraint on the coefficient matrix of each body order, and the resulting bilinear problem is trained with alternating least squares, where each block update is one closed-form linear solve. We benchmark PI-UF3 on a five-element refractory high-entropy alloy (HEA) and a subset of MD22, training on forces, with restarts and cross-validation. On the chemically homogeneous HEA, compression acts as implicit regularization: with three-body terms included, PI-UF3’s test force root-mean-squared error drops below the unfactorized UF3 baseline with 3% of the baseline’s parameters on the predefined split and 7% on every cross-validation fold, and the maximally compressed model recovers a chemically meaningful ordering of homonuclear interaction strengths consistent with experimental bulk melting temperatures. On the chemically heterogeneous MD22 subset, where UF3 is not expressive enough to overfit, PI-UF3 approaches the baseline from above and reaches parity with it at about two thirds of the parameter count. Compression thus regularizes only where the unfactorized model overfits, while a parameter reduction is available in both regimes.

articles.title: Quantum critical behavior in chains of hindered dipolar planar rotors
articles.abstract: We study the ground-state properties of linear chains of dipolar planar rotors hindered by a sixfold on-site potential, a model motivated by water molecules confined in the hexagonal cavities of beryl. Using density matrix renormalization group calculations, we locate the quantum phase transition between the disordered and ferroelectrically ordered phases using the von Neumann entanglement entropy and the Binder ratio of the polarization. A sweep of the sixfold pinning strength shows that increasing hindrance shifts the critical dipolar coupling g c to smaller values. These results suggest that crystal-field hindrance can promote, rather than suppress, dipolar ordering. This work has implications for ferroelectricity and quantum-device tuning in confined molecular rotors.
