articles.title: In-situ azimuthal sample rotation within a horizontal-field cryomagnet for small-angle neutron scattering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an in-situ azimuthal rotation stage for small-angle neutron scattering measurements. The stage provides an azimuthal rotation range of 315^circ about the stage normal. At the reference sample-stick orientation, the stage normal is parallel to the incident neutron beam, so that the sample rotates in the plane perpendicular to the beam. Combined with a sample stick rotation about a second, orthogonal axis, the stage provides control of the magnetic-field direction relative to the crystal axes, while the field remains fixed in the laboratory frame. For a 5 mm diameter incident beam, sample-stick rotations of approximately ±315^circ are accessible with negligible additional attenuation from the holder. The commercial rotator is specified for operation between 1 and 373 K and in magnetic fields up to 35 T, making the stage nominally compatible with the full temperature (1.8 to 320 K) and field (0 to 6.8 T) ranges of the used cryomagnet. As a working example, we characterize its performance on a spherical single crystal of MnSi between 20 and 35 K and in fields up to 183 mT, observing local sample heating during operation of sim20 mK per 5^circ step. We illustrate the design considerations behind the holder construction, with specific notes for mounting spherical samples, and discuss the resulting performance and limitations.

articles.title: Counterexample-driven autonomous research with application to excess radiated energy in a Z-pinch
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03721v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent breakthroughs in artificial-intelligence-assisted mathematics show that open-ended machine search can outperform human mathematicians, yet transferring this paradigm to physics requires refactoring the research workflow. We introduce Simjecture, an open-source framework in which language-model agents pursue human-defined physical conjectures. The framework tackles two central challenges in this transfer: first, because physics is empirical and no model is final, it structures inquiry around counterexample-driven falsification and prospective hypothesis repair; second, because physical theories must interact with the real world, it uses computational physics as an executable testbed while separating the qualification of numerical instruments from scientific claim review so solvers and diagnostics can be adapted within a recorded investigation. We apply the framework in an 82.6 h investigation to tackle the long-standing problem of radiated energy exceeding the imploding-shell kinetic energy in a Z-pinch. The investigation reveals competing effects of energy conversion, retention, and release timing. Stronger coherent helical deformation increases resistive conversion while reducing radiation and increasing retained energy. A broader trailing-plasma profile delays the later radiation maximum and recovers much of its early bolometric deficit, with a spectral response that changes during the pulse. These results provide new insight into energy conversion in high-energy-density plasma physics and demonstrate a new paradigm for physics research.

articles.title: Physics-Informed Identification of Tensegrity Prestress across Taut-Slack Transitions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04007v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Prestress governs the stability, stiffness, and dynamic behavior of tensegrity structures, but it is not directly observable from sparse structural measurements, and it may decrease during service life. Under strong excitation, the cables may slacken and the dynamics become nonsmooth. Existing identification methods are limited to the taut regime, and physics-informed networks for tensegrities solve only the forward problem of predicting the response from known member parameters. This study formulates the inverse problem. Neural networks are trained on the equation-of-motion residual in constrained Cartesian coordinates, where the mass matrix is constant and the force densities enter linearly. The force densities, damping, and axial stiffness are trainable parameters, and the tension-only cable law is kept. A Fisher-information analysis shows, before inversion, which member parameters a record can determine. The method is tested on simulated planar tensegrity frames with up to five modules and a three-dimensional prism, and on measured records of a biomimetic leg and a full-scale tensegrity simplex. On the one-module frame, the identifiable force densities are recovered within 1.5% from noisy accelerations at half the free coordinates, on records with and without taut-slack transitions. Records with transitions determine members that taut records leave undetermined. On the five-module frame, a 16-cable two-span bridge, the median force-density error rises moderately, to 4.2%. On measured records, an identified spring stiffness is within 0.1% of its independently measured value on average, and the identified simplex prestress at 13 levels agrees with its cable force transducers to 2.9% root-mean-square.

articles.title: Broken-Symmetry Reference States for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization with Near-DMRG Accuracy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) accuracy remains limited for strongly correlated systems like iron-sulfur clusters. This accuracy heavily depends on the mean-field reference state, which determines the sampling ansatz and configuration-recovery target. We extend the qcsc-prefect workflow to support a broken-symmetry unrestricted Hartree-Fock (BS-UHF) starting point, derived from atom-localized antiferromagnetic initial guesses. For the [Fe₄S₄(SCH₃)₄]²⁻ cubane (54 electrons, 36 orbitals, 72 data qubits; 88 total qubits), this lowers the mean-field reference by approx 534 mHa relative to the Restricted Hartree-Fock (RHF) solution (-327.0809 vs. -326.5474 Ha). Combined with deep multi-step configuration recovery on ROQUO GPU nodes at subspace dimension d = 3 × 10¹⁰, we reach E = -327.235076 Ha. This is 4.3 mHa above the finite-D = 4000 DMRG value (-327.2393952 Ha) and sim 512-517 mHa below a previous same-active-space RHF-reference SQD calculation. Extrapolating to the d → infty limit via a Gaussian-in-log d fitting ansatz gives an asymptotic estimate E_infty = -327.244468 Ha ± 1.05 mHa, just 0.33 mHa above our discarded-weight-extrapolated DMRG estimate (ED→ᵢₙfₜy = -327.244797 Ha ± 0.46 mHa), well within their combined 1σ uncertainty. We characterize the determinant-subspace composition driving convergence, show matching validation on [Fe₂S₂(SCH₃)₄]²⁻, and report multi-HPC execution on Fugaku, Miyabi-G, and ROQUO. We conclude that reference-state preparation, rather than subspace size alone, is a key driver of SQD energy accuracy under strong electronic correlation.

articles.title: A New Bound on Light-by-Light Scattering in the Low-Energy Regime
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04531v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The superposition principle at the heart of optics states that electromagnetic fields do not interact in vacuum. This principle is not universal, instead electromagnetic fields couple weakly via quantum vacuum fluctuations. Striking consequences are light-by-light scattering and vacuum birefringence. Experimental results from colliding X-ray free-electron and optical high-intensity lasers combined with dark-field detection and polarimetry for background suppression are reported. This approach yields the most stringent bound for light-by-light scattering in the low-energy regime achieved to date -- improving upon previous experimental limits by ten orders of magnitude -- and paves the way for precision measurements.

articles.title: Temporal stretching of single-photon pulses by intra-cavity frequency conversion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spectral bandwidth and frequency mismatch between quantum light emitters and quantum components is a common problem in the realization of hybrid quantum information networks. Here we propose a simultaneous solution to both of these problems by using a free-space cavity with an embedded nonlinear crystal that, through frequency conversion, facilitates perfect coupling into a cavity mode. The slow leakage of the cavity effectively stretches the photon pulse, resulting in a much longer photon pulse at a different wavelength. We show that the amount of stretching is strictly limited by the finesse and length of the cavity. Including realistic internal losses in the cavity, we show that it is possible to stretch a photon by at least two orders of magnitude with high efficiency. The proposed setup can thus constitute a valuable addition to the toolbox of quantum information technologies.

articles.title: Small-Scale Dynamo for Full Spectrum of Hydrodynamic Turbulence in Kazantsev Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.01718v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A method is proposed for computing coefficients in the Kazantsev equation of small-scale dynamo for the full spectrum of hydromagnetic turbulence comprising the inertial range together with the range of viscous dissipation. The dynamo equation with so-defined coefficients is solved numerically for magnetic (Rm) and hydrodynamic (Re) Reynolds numbers from 10² to 10⁸. The threshold value rm Rm_c for onset of dynamo increases initially with Re but then saturates at a constant value of rm Rm_c simeq 300 for rm Re≥ 10⁵. In the case of small Prandtl number Pm = Rm/Re << 1, the field growth rate is also small and depends logarithmically on Rm. In this case, the magnetic energy spectrum peaks around the scale of Ohmic dissipation, which decreases with increasing Pm. The decrease stops at the scale of viscous dissipation while the growth rate increases sharply when Pm approaches the value of one. The increase in the growth rate proceeds to rm Pm > 1 but slows down and then saturates at a value somewhat below the inverse lifetime of most short-living eddies. An explanation of the results is proposed.

articles.title: Positron Emission Tomography with quantum-entangled Compton events: first imaging results at clinically relevant activities
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.25804v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In Positron Emission Tomography, a potential, yet unutilized enhancement, may come from exploiting the quantum entanglement of the annihilation quanta, inscribed in the correlation of their polarizations. To investigate this, we built a PET demonstrator capable of measuring polarization correlations of annihilation quanta by their Compton scattering, based on single-layer scintillator polarimeters. We present a detailed study of the imaging of two ⁶⁸Ge line sources, 45 MBq each, to extract the spatial resolution and assess image quality. The results show that a spatial resolution of 2.5±0.1 mm is obtained using single-pixel events, while resolutions obtained with polarization-correlated Compton events range from 3.6±0.3 mm to 4.9±0.3 mm, depending on data selection criteria. We also found that the polarization-correlated Compton events exhibit up to 20% higher average signal to random background ratio compared to the single-pixel events. We also present the first imaging of the NEMA NU-4 phantom filled with a ⁶⁸Ga solution of 378 MBq initial activity, successfully combining polarization-correlated events with conventional single-pixel event selection. Based on the extracted spatial resolution, signal-to-background, signal-to-noise, contrast, and contrast-to-noise ratio, we estimate that up to 10% sensitivity increase may be attained by exploiting the polarization-correlated events, while preserving a high image quality.

articles.title: Spectral taxonomy for quartic systems: fundamental clock, parity, and continuum
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.07731v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A symmetric quartic potential is a physics model with expansive applications, ranging from broadband energy harvesters, quantum tunneling in molecules and the early universe, to torque-free spacecraft rotation. Its rich dynamics have been traditionally classified into regimes and expressed as disjointed time-domain solutions. Here we build a taxonomy for this broad class of motions and discover that their regimes exhibit a symmetrical spectral structure: they share a fundamental clock, obey parity selection, and dissolve into the separatrix through a discrete-to-continuum transition. Applied to the famous Dzhanibekov effect where a rotating body periodically undergoes rapid 180-degree flips in its attitude, the taxonomy reveals its spectral anatomy. The three principal-axis rotations share a common clock while occupying distinct parity channels, with stable-axis branches exchanging DC bias across the separatrix. We discuss a case study where the three spectral pillars: clock, parity, and continuum, survive the Wick rotation from real-time into imaginary-time kinematics.

articles.title: Emergence in Network Systems is Bounded by Boundary-Crossing Paths
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.38037v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Emergence, features of a whole that no part shows alone, is central to complex systems but rarely measured so as to locate its source. Viewing a system structurally, as a network of interacting parts, we evaluate emergence as what observing the coupled whole reveals beyond, or erases from, the combined observations of the parts. For observations that build what they see route by route, we show that every emergent feature is produced by its own route across the interface between parts, a route that traces it to the components and interactions responsible. We show the number of all such boundary-crossing paths bounds the total emergence discrepancy, and equals the emergence of measures that count routes. The bound is computed locally around the interface, validated through network examples, and in a nervous system the routes show that interneurons relay most of the emergence. Our work associates emergence with path structure in the network system that can be anticipated, attributed, and engineered.

articles.title: Advances in the Vacuum Magnetic Birefringence measurement using a pulsed Foil Coil
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.06043v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, in the framework of the it Biréfringence Magnétique du Vide (BMV) experiment, we present our current apparatus in detail and we discuss its critical points. We also report the results obtained using specially designed pulsed coils called Foil Coils. Our novel measurement of the vacuum linear magnetic birefringence constant is KVMB < 1.7 · 10⁻²¹~T⁻² at a confidence level of 68%, which is an improvement with respect to our previous 2014 measurement.

articles.title: Mechanisms governing photon-pair generation and emission directionality in quantum metasurfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.26303v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Metasurfaces are emerging as a promising platform for photon-pair generation through spontaneous parametric down-conversion, thanks to their compactness, integrability, and intrinsic multifunctionality, which enables the engineering of complex quantum states. However, their full potential remains only partially exploited because the physical mechanisms governing key properties of the generated photon pairs, such as generation efficiency and emission directionality, are not yet fully understood. As a result, metasurface designs and experimental configurations are often optimized through trial-and-error procedures. Here, we theoretically investigate the main mechanisms that control photon-pair generation and detection by studying how different pump configurations and measurement geometries affect the generation efficiency, emission directionality, and collection efficiency of the emitted photon pairs. This framework allows us to interpret existing experimental results and to provide general guidelines for the design of metasurfaces and the choice of experimental configurations in future experiments. Finally, we show that substrate thickness and multilayer configurations represent additional degrees of freedom for quantum metasurface design and can be engineered to enhance the generation efficiency and control the emission directionality, providing a new route for the optimization of photon-pair sources based on metasurfaces.

articles.title: Seeing Why: Exact Evidence Maps for Quantum and Optical Image Classifiers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01993v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When an image classifier decides, we can usually only estimate why. For quantum and all-optical classifiers that act linearly on amplitude-encoded pictures up to the measurement, with no trained classical network before or after them, each class's Born probability above its no-information share, P_g - b_g, splits exactly into contributions of the encoded amplitudes, shown as Born evidence maps (BEM) over the picture. The split itself follows from known results on quadratic forms: with the transmitted light held fixed, it is what Integrated Gradients from a zero baseline and the Shapley value give. What we add is a way to measure it on the hardware that classifies, from class probabilities on a quantum chip or from camera frames on a lens bench, with no gradient circuit and no light sent backwards; a g× g map takes 1 + 2g² runs. Deleting the 5% of pixels with the highest evidence drops accuracy from 73% to 9%, as occlusion does with 1,024 extra runs per picture, whereas gradient saliency removes much less. The classifiers share one architecture, a Fourier-plane mask followed by a brickwall circuit on qubits or by phase plates on a lens bench, read by a fixed Born headroom readout with no trained parameter; centring each picture on its own mean lets dark features count as much as bright ones. In simulation, four phase plates at a single wavelength reach 72.3% on Caltech-10 colour photographs. On IBM's ibm_kingston, with the mask applied before approximate loading, 300 test pictures were classified at 37.7% against 10% by chance (56.3% in exact simulation), and 2×2 maps of ten correctly classified pictures, one per class chosen by a stated rule, measured on the chip, agreed with the exact ones (r = 0.77). The maps also revealed a shortcut in the data; as the trim that removed it was chosen on test pictures, the Caltech-10 results are exploratory.

articles.title: Ermakov--Based embeddings as a parameter-free layer for physics-informed neural networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients force a neural solver to spend capacity on a scale that the equation already determines. We show that a single classical object, the Ermakov-Pinney scale function ρ, can be written into the input layer of a physics-informed neural network as a parameter-free embedding. One construction covers three problem families through the two signs of the Pinney constant c: linear diffusion (c=-1, ωequiv0), diffusion in a time-dependent confining trap (c=-1, ω≠0), and the quantum oscillator with time-dependent frequency (c=+1). An exact moment identity gives ρ in closed form from the initial data alone, so no auxiliary network or knowledge of the solution is needed. Our central finding is comparative: each family requires a different component of the construction and has a different honest control. In family I, the diffusive-time reparametrisation alone reproduces most of the gain, so that family is a poor test of the idea and shows why an ablation is mandatory. In family II no time reparametrisation exists, the control degrades accuracy, and the amplitude prefactor becomes essential (40.8x). In family III the adiabatic approximation also fails, and the quadratic phase factor is what matters (5.7x). The method does not help when the reduced solution does not converge to a fixed point: its extrapolation advantage then disappears. The reduction itself is the classical scaling-variable change of the self-similar-asymptotics literature; what is new is the moment identity that makes it architectural for time-dependent coefficients, and the comparative anatomy above.

articles.title: ModelBlaster: Closing the Performance Gap through Learning-Augmented Agents Across Models, Kernels and Hardware Backends
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimizing accelerator code across hardware architectures is difficult. ML compilers search predefined spaces of schedules and micro-kernels, while LLM-guided optimization can explore alternative algorithms, operator decompositions, and hardware-specific techniques. However, existing LLM agents typically target a single programming interface, toolchain, or accelerator family, focus on kernel-level optimization without model-level transforms, and offer limited reuse of experience across hardware targets. We present ModelBlaster, a Memory-Augmented In-Context Reinforcement Learning (MAIC-RL) framework for optimizing data-parallel kernels and whole models across heterogeneous SIMD and SIMT accelerators. Its mutable policy is a persistent knowledge base updated at inference time by Actor-Critic Textual Gradient Descent (AC-TGD). The knowledge base maps performance states to actions, outcomes, and constraints, enabling experience reuse across kernels, models, and hardware targets. A model-level optimizer uses kernel-level knowledge to inform whole-model decisions. The same optimization loop and knowledge schema support CUDA on NVIDIA GPUs, OpenCL on Qualcomm GPUs, and RVV intrinsics on RISC-V vector cores, with only lowering and measurement layers specific to each target. Compared with PyTorch, ModelBlaster achieves geometric-mean speedups of 1.85x, 5.58x, and 5.18x on KernelBench Levels 1, 2, and 3, and 1.69x on SOL-ExecBench Levels 1 and 2 on a B200 GPU. On Qualcomm Adreno GPUs, it achieves 5.8x over the vendor SDK and 1.7x over Apache TVM; on RISC-V vector cores, it achieves 2.7x over ExecuTorch with XNNPACK across 70 KernelBench problems.

articles.title: Ground-Wing: A Parametric 3D Wing-in-Ground-Effect Dataset for Benchmarking Neural Surrogate Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a CFD dataset of a highly parametrized 3D wing operating in ground effect, designed for benchmarking neural surrogate models for aerodynamic prediction, using a wing shape and flow conditions typically encountered in motorsport applications. The dataset comprises 770 RANS simulations of 194 unique wing configurations, sampled across 27 airfoil profile variants and 4 distances from the ground, spanning variations in wing sweep, chord, taper, angle of attack, and tip twist. Six neural network architectures representing distinct paradigms --- convolutional (DoMINO), graph-based (X-MeshGraphNet), transformer-based (AB-UPT, GeoTransolver, GAOT), and JEPA-based (AeroJEPA) --- are evaluated on their ability to predict surface pressure coefficient and wall shear stress distributions, from which integral drag and lift coefficients are recovered. The dataset is intended to be used as a challenging benchmark for surrogate CFD models, due to the uniqueness of the ground effect being absent from other wing and airfoil datasets.

articles.title: Self-Privileged Fine-Tuning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is a key component of language model post-training, enabling effective task adaptation and serving as an important foundation for subsequent reinforcement learning. Recent methods seek to improve SFT by introducing token-level weights into the training objective, where these weights are typically derived from a model's output distribution at each token position. To better understand how such weighting schemes affect SFT, we analyze their optimization objectives and theoretically characterize the target distributions they induce. Our analysis shows that dynamic weighting methods, such as Dynamic Fine-Tuning (DFT), induce a heavily sharpened distribution, whereas static weighting methods fit a target distribution proportional to the product of the data distribution and a frozen prior. These findings suggest that static weighting provides a more stable training target, while its effectiveness critically depends on the quality of the prior distribution. Building on this observation, we propose Self-Privileged Fine-Tuning (SPFT), which uses a frozen copy of the initial model conditioned on privileged information (such as ground truth for mathematical questions) as a prior to provide guidance for token-level weighting during fine-tuning. Through a Bayesian decomposition, we further show that SPFT reweights the standard static prior according to how informative each target token is for predicting the ground-truth outcome, thereby assigning larger weights to more predictive tokens. Experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation show that SPFT improves over standard SFT and other baselines across the main settings.

articles.title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing Detection with Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work investigates the application of Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks to the binary classification of sleep-disordered breathing events in time-series data, aiming to distinguish between apneic and normal breathing episodes. A variational classical--quantum architecture is proposed and evaluated against classical Recurrent Neural Network models. Experiments were conducted on multiple real-world datasets with varying levels of complexity to assess the strengths and limitations of the quantum approach. In the comparative analysis, both classical and quantum models showed comparable performance. The quantum model achieved superior performance on the smallest dataset, while yielding slightly weaker results in the most complex setting. However, the quantum approach exhibited notable strengths, such as competitive performance despite a drastically reduced parameter count and low-qubit regime, as well as good generalization capabilities. These results suggest that, despite current hardware and algorithmic limitations, variational quantum recurrent models represent a promising alternative for time-series classification as Quantum Computing technologies continue to mature.

articles.title: Cool Graphs: Active Property Search Towards Quantum Nano-Refrigerators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanodevices that absorb energy from their thermal environment can act as quantum refrigerators. Finding suitable configurations, however, is a needle-in-a-haystack problem: the many-body state space scales exponentially with the size of the device, where each candidate configuration requires an expensive quantum-chemical computation. We introduce a search framework that couples a Graph Variational Autoencoder (GVAE) with an uncertainty-driven Active Learning (AL) loop to efficiently identify energy-absorbing configurations in electronic junctions with a 2D "working material" to be optimized. The GVAE maps physical parameters - site energies, coupling matrices, temperature - into a smooth latent space that distinguishes cooling from dissipative parameter regimes, achieving a classification discriminability of 0.920 ± 0.004 on held-out configurations and 0.895 ± 0.010 on unseen extrapolation topologies. An AL pipeline based on Monte Carlo dropout then targets the decision boundary, iteratively selecting the candidates where the model is least certain for simulation. Over 32 AL cycles, the uncertainty-driven strategy discovers energy absorbing systems at rates consistently exceeding the random baseline across all tested topologies (where only 1.9-8.4% of configurations exhibit the desired property), providing a data-efficient pathway for navigating a combinatorically large design space. The learned latent space organizes configurations along physically interpretable axes, that correlate with underlying microscopic model parameters. This hints at the existence of "cooling coordinates" - low-dimensional, physically interpretable quantities separating cooling from non-cooling regimes. Our framework, thus, paves a new way towards effective cooling of nanoscale electronic information processing devices, to reduce the environmental footprint of high performance computing.

articles.title: Auditing Multi-Proxy Explanations of Web User Preferences: Identification Boundaries and Abstention
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web systems infer user preferences from behavior, ratings, text, and LLM-generated profiles, yet explaining a proxy may reveal its measurement process rather than the preference of interest. We develop an audit framework distinguishing point identification, partial identification, and abstention relative to an explicit reference distribution. Under feature-dependent, arbitrarily signed proxy bias, a strict majority of uncontaminated proxy attributions lets the coordinatewise median recover latent-attribution support and direction and, with externally justified positive scales, magnitude. We prove this threshold sharp using response-valid indistinguishable worlds, characterize sharp minimax error and exact compatible-target sets under approximate cleanliness and scale uncertainty, and propagate clean-proxy attribution error. A frozen known-truth benchmark spans two response families, four proxy counts, all contamination counts, three bias strengths, and eleven methods, with a focal comparison confirmed on twenty unseen seeds. Under correct budgets, a direct attribution-tensor audit achieved 100% coverage, 95.40%-97.05% active-driver sign decisions, and no false signs. In a temporally separated Amazon study, median aggregation reduced comparator-relative conditional sign error for all four targets; six of eight prespecified target-metric contrasts had Bonferroni intervals excluding zero. A controlled real-covariate perturbation favored the median on the prespecified focal metric for all four targets. Compatible sets showed that the current proxy configuration rarely licensed strict-sign conclusions. Weak comparator calibration limits the Amazon evidence to fitted-surface alignment rather than latent-preference recovery.

articles.title: Empirical Bayes Flow Matching for Continuous Cryo-EM Heterogeneity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address the problem of learning generative priors over high-dimensional latent variables from indirect, noisy observations, with a focus on continuous heterogeneity in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). In this setting, 3D atomic structures x in R³Nₐ are never directly observed and must be inferred from 2D projection images y generated by a complex, non-linear forward operator. We propose Empirical Bayes Flow Matching (EB-FM), a method that learns a flow matching prior p_θ(x) directly from observations using a Monte Carlo stochastic approximation Expectation-Maximization framework. EB-FM alternates between an E-step that performs approximate posterior sampling from p_θ(x mid y) via guided flow-based generation while maintaining persistent latent estimates through stochastic approximation, and an M-step that updates the flow model using these stabilized latent variables as training targets. This approach eliminates the need for pretraining on clean data and naturally accommodates non-linear forward models. We validate our method on controlled inverse problems using two-moons and MNIST data, and demonstrate its effectiveness on simulated cryo-EM data with known poses, showing that EB-FM can recover continuous distributions of protein conformations directly in atomic-coordinate space.

articles.title: NovoCRF: Globally Normalized De Novo Peptide Sequencing on a Prefix-Mass Lattice
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: De novo peptide sequencing has moved from dynamic programming over hand-designed or generative scores to large transformers that learn the task end to end. We present NovoCRF, a conditional random field (CRF) whose states are prefix masses, so that its paths are exactly the peptides within +/-0.06 Da of the precursor mass. A small network scores each edge from physics-derived ion-match features and is trained with its scores globally normalized over all mass-feasible peptides. To our knowledge, NovoCRF is the first de novo method trained with exact normalization over all mass-feasible peptides. Our software has three modules, each with exactly one job: a precursor mass finder recovers the accurate precursor mass from MS1, the CRF finds the peptides that fit the precursor mass by exact k-best decoding, and two BiGRU rerankers add sequence context and internal-fragment evidence. The model has 310k parameters and trains in about 17 GPU-hours. On seven held-out data-dependent acquisition datasets published in 2026 (126,262 labeled spectra), NovoCRF's mean peptide recall is 42.4%, against 39.1% for Casanovo v5 with five beams, and its amino-acid recall 64.0% against 53.1%, at 1,746 spectra/s on 18 CPU threads, 55x Casanovo's throughput on a GPU. Split by fragment evidence, NovoCRF leads on labels with up to three peptide bonds without a b or y ion, and Casanovo only beyond. NovoCRF can also search modifications it was never trained on at their exact mass: it finds 32.1% of the hydroxyproline peptides of a lion bone sample.

articles.title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We attempt to alleviate failure modes of classical physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in scenarios of topological pathologies corresponding to punctures, holes, poles, and voids by introducing de Rham cohomological augmentations, or Hodge-de Rham PINNs. Vanilla PINNs often encounter pitfalls in hole-based settings due to discontinuous interfaces, nonzero closed path integration, path dependence, correspondence to exact forms via the exterior derivative, etc., therefore we absolve traditional failures via parameterizing a 1-form by the Hodge-Morrey-Friedrichs (HMF) decomposition for manifolds with boundary, drawing a connection to de Rham cohomology such as through the HMF isomorphism theorem. 1-forms can act as representations of scalar-valued PDE solutions through integral operator mappings. We propose performing a PINN-based loss on the parameterized 1-form through an associated PDE, which subsequently solves the potential-based PINN problem and moreover remedies the failures of vanilla PINNs via the Sobolev-regular operator under a Fréchet differentiation interconnection. The operator relationship often has a nontrivial closed-form and often requires integration or a case-by-case analysis, which we address thoroughly in our experiments. When an integrability condition is not met on our losses, we can equip exhaustion functions to train the networks. We demonstrate our methods on the Aharonov-Bohm effect, which, to our understanding, is largely nonexistent in PINN literature. We develop theoretical guarantees of our methods and demonstrate our pathological safeguards on a broad selection of topologically-adverse problems, including scenarios of inexact forms, and those of nontrivial harmonics and coexact terms.

articles.title: HyVox: Rethinking Low-Power Voice Intelligence towards Neuromorphic-von Neumann Edge Computing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03735v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present HyVox, a hybrid neuromorphic--von Neumann system for low-energy open-set speaker identification under tight energy budgets. HyVox splits the workload at the speaker embedding. A neuromorphic processor embeds the speech with sparse, event-driven computation, and a von Neumann microcontroller holds the speaker gallery and makes every decision: it scores queries by cosine similarity, rejects unknown speakers, and enrolls new users by writing a prototype, with no weight update. On the neuromorphic processor, a hierarchical temporal abstraction (HTA) SNN backbone learns a synaptic time constant per leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron, allocating 832 neurons across fast, medium, and slow timescales. A 32-neuron spiking embedding extractor (SEE), pretrained on episodes that each enroll new speakers and reject outsiders, turns the backbone output into an embedding for speakers unseen in training; its 32 spike counts are the only interface between the two processors. To fit the chip's synapse and integer budgets, we compress the backbone 6.5x to 29.0k synapses, train it for integer bit-shift dynamics, and fine-tune it with chip-accurate spiking training (CAST). CAST trains through a differentiable replica of the chip's integer neuron update, derived from its cycle-accurate simulator, so that gradient descent optimizes the exact weights and thresholds the chip runs; it doubles the top-1 accuracy of the mapped backbone on unseen speakers. On 20 Common Voice households of unseen speakers, HyVox reaches 99.6% top-1 and 5.5% rejection EER with 2 members and 94.9% and 13.2% with 20, and the network deployed on the neuromorphic chip matches its trained model. Each inference on a 3-s window takes 0.96 s and 1.63 mJ of dynamic energy, 42% lower latency than the fastest embedded ANN baseline and 13.5x less dynamic and 5.8x less total energy than the most energy-efficient one.

articles.title: Learning Almost Complex and Complex Structures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03872v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the numerical constructions of almost complex and complex structures on spheres and products of spheres up to real dimension six. Our general set-up parametrises almost complex structures via a global matrix field in an ambient Euclidean space, compressed by the tangent projector. The projector's algebraic residual measures the almost complex condition, while its Nijenhuis tensor is evaluated in the intrinsic norm of the round product metric. Polynomial features and neural networks are trained without prescribed targets to perform general searches for these structures. The almost complex search passes numerical admissibility checks on all nine examples that admit such structures and rejects S⁴, where a topological obstruction is known. A matrix correction then enforces the almost complex identity, subject to a novel uniform admissibility condition. For integrability, a free polynomial representation with Levenberg-Marquardt optimisation learns the complex structures on S²× S², S³× S¹, S³× S³ and S⁵× S¹, with the largest Nijenhuis norms found by adversarial search all below 10⁻⁹. These general searches were unsuccessful on S⁶, S⁴× S² and S⁴× T². Therefore, for these three cases direct numerical reconstructions were built in torus-fibred coordinates. They are integrable by construction, satisfy their compatibility conditions to better than 10⁻¹¹, and corroborate the recent constructions on S⁶ and S⁴× S².

articles.title: ScrambleMark: Zero-Query Watermark-Agnostic Black-Box Evasion of Modern Speech Watermarking
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04122v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Speech watermarking is becoming a key defense for digital copyright and content authentication. Existing attacks treat evasion as a removal problem: they erase the watermark, relying on detector access or on speech data that is hard to collect, such as paired clean-watermarked or clean target speaker speech. Commercial platforms are moving to close off these assumptions. TrustedAudio, for instance, restricts detection to authenticated users and denies meaningful detection feedback to unauthorized parties. Adversaries thus cannot tell whether a sample is watermarked or which watermark it carries, nor reliably remove it without degrading speech quality. In this work, we show that evading a speech watermark does not require erasing it: detection relies on the structural consistency of the embedded pattern, and disrupting this consistency is enough to defeat it. Building on this observation, we identify harmonic structure as an effective attack surface, as perturbing it breaks watermark consistency while preserving perceptual quality. We therefore propose ScrambleMark, a zero-query, watermark-agnostic, black-box attack that evades detection through harmonic scrambling. ScrambleMark combines a deterministic engine for discovering transferable harmonic perturbations with a generative model that learns randomized scrambling patterns, avoiding reliance on fixed attack rules. Across three commercial platforms (Google SynthID, Resemble AI, and TrustedAudio), ScrambleMark is the only attack to both evade detection and keep speech natural, achieving nearly 97% evasion and a 4.2/5 human rating, far above the 1.1 to 1.7 of prior attacks. Beyond evasion, ScrambleMark withstands adaptive recovery designed to reverse it, evidence that structural evasion is hard to mitigate in practice.

articles.title: UniFlow: Unified Multi-Scale Flow Matching for Time Series Generation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-world time series exhibit complex dynamics across multiple temporal resolutions, yet effectively incorporating multi-scale information into generative modeling remains challenging without increasing generative complexity. We propose UniFlow, a unified framework that integrates multi-scale representation learning with efficient non-autoregressive generation through a shared-semantic discrete interface. Specifically, a multi-scale tokenizer employs shared-index voting to consolidate complementary temporal information into a single public-ID sequence, while scale-specific codebooks preserve the information required for reconstruction. Building on this unified representation, we develop geometry-aware categorical flow matching, which initializes transport from learned low-rank anchors and generates public identities non-autoregressively. This design captures multi-scale temporal structure without requiring multiple generative token streams or sequential token decoding. Experiments across four benchmarks and both short- and long-term settings demonstrate improved generative fidelity, strong cross-scale consistency, and substantial inference speedups over representative autoregressive and diffusion-based baselines. Code is available at https://github.com/William-Liwei/uniflow

articles.title: Score-Based Modeling of Effective Langevin Dynamics with State-Dependent Mobility
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.23952v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a previous work [L. T. Giorgini, Phys. Rev. E 114, L012102 (2026)], we introduced stochastic reduced-order models that reproduce by construction the stationary density and short-time correlations of the observed variables, using a constant mobility matrix and the score, the gradient of the logarithm of this density. Here we generalize the framework to state-dependent mobilities, calibrated so that the model also reproduces the finite-lag correlation functions of chosen target observables. The calibration uses exact finite-lag forms of the generalized fluctuation-dissipation theorem, which express time derivatives of lagged correlations as averages over observed pairs of states and are linear in the mobility. When the mobility is expanded on a basis of known fields, its coefficients follow from a least-squares problem involving only the stationary score, and the observables and basis are selected by data-driven diagnostics. Otherwise, a neural-network mobility is calibrated through the conditional score of the finite-time transition density. We validate the approach analytically on a Cox-Ingersoll-Ross process and numerically on a two-dimensional nonequilibrium diffusion with multiplicative noise and a 36-dimensional soft-spin Landau-Lifshitz chain. Both methods reproduce the stationary statistics and the target correlations accurately. Because the identities can be integrated between consecutive lags, so that no time derivatives need to be estimated, the recovered drift and diffusion are much less sensitive to coarse sampling than Kramers-Moyal estimates, which require short sampling intervals. Calibration requires no simulation of the model and applies to high-dimensional systems.

articles.title: Controlling Action-Head Co-Adaptation to VLM Representation Anisotropy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern learning systems increasingly combine pretrained models with downstream heads. Despite the growing importance of such modular designs, how the downstream model co-adapts to the geometry of pretrained representations remains relatively underexplored. We study this problem through vision-language-action models (VLAs), where a pretrained vision-language model (VLM) conditions an action model for control. We find that the action model progressively concentrates its sensitivity on high-variance dimensions of the VLM outputs. Through controlled experiments across different backbone-head models, we further show that counteracting this sensitivity concentration can be beneficial under representation--task mismatch settings. Motivated by these observations, we introduce emphAdaptive Interface Equalizer (AdaIE), a parameter-free mechanism that reweights pretrained representations according to the evolving downstream sensitivity during training. AdaIE improves VLA success rates on simulation benchmarks, with gains of up to +5.28 percentage points (pp) on RoboCasa-GR1 and +1.68 pp on RoboTwin 2.0, and achieves an average gain of +19 pp across five real-world manipulation tasks. It further generalizes to diffusion policies and world models, improving downstream performance in both settings. Our results highlight interface co-adaptation as an important optimization problem when coupling pretrained representations with downstream models.

articles.title: Benchmarking Unsupervised Jamming Detection in 5G Open RAN
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radio Frequency (RF) jamming threatens fifth-generation (5G) networks. Open Radio Access Network (Open RAN) telemetry enables jamming detection without dedicated spectrum monitoring equipment, but labeled attack data are rarely available across deployments, motivating unsupervised detectors. Comparing such detectors across algorithmic families, however, remains difficult without ground-truth labels. This paper benchmarks statistical and reconstruction-based unsupervised jamming detectors using a symmetric evaluation interface that combines detection confidence and temporal interval coherence into a detector-independent composite score. We compare a Statistical Ensemble Method (SEM) detector against Vanilla, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Variational Autoencoder (VAE) baselines on Key Performance Indicator (KPI) telemetry from ten heterogeneous 5G environments with fixed and variable jamming bursts and dynamic jammer gains. Under leave-one-out (LOO) evaluation, SEM achieves a mean composite score of 0.906, compared with 0.688 for the best autoencoder (AE) per fold. Ground-truth validation yields a mean F1-score of 0.918 for SEM, compared with 0.521 for the best AE variant. The composite ranks SEM first in all environments, consistent with F1 rankings. However, in both within-trace and cross-trace evaluation, it fails for detectors that flag far fewer samples than the jamming prevalence, indicating that rankings are reliable only when detection rate matches the expected prevalence.

articles.title: ValQID: Learning the Net Value of Semantic Query Groups for Web Device Identification
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web interfaces are widely used to access network services and manage networked devices. Identifying the vendors and types of devices behind Web interfaces is a critical step in asset inventory, security management, and risk assessment. Device identity cues are dispersed across page text, configuration fields, and management functions, and interpreting them often requires linking related Web objects. Responses and objects require different amounts of semantic analysis, so exhaustively processing all candidate content can introduce unnecessary computation. We present ValQID, which uses a relation graph to combine dispersed device identity cues, evaluates semantic questions efficiently with DSEJEV, and accounts for complementarity among semantic questions when estimating computation value. Based on the current identification state, ValQID weighs each question group's expected identification benefit against its execution cost and adaptively allocates computation to identify device vendors and types. Evaluation on real Web response data shows that ValQID achieves relative gains of up to 47.1% in joint macro-F1 and up to 82.1% in macro-F1 for low-frequency vendors over a state-of-the-art method. DSEJEV speeds up semantic processing by up to 8.58 times compared with general-purpose language models.

articles.title: Catalyzing Interactive HTML Generation Capabilities via High-Fidelity Reinforcement Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating HTML from natural-language specifications is an important application of code large language models (LLMs). Despite producing renderable pages, current models often fail to ensure functionality and visual quality during actual interaction. Existing methods typically target task-specific webpage supervision, leaving demanding interactive artifact optimization underexplored. Using mini-games as a challenging testbed, we expose limitations in interaction experience, reward signal, and credit assignment fidelity that are obscured by shallow webpage interactions. We introduce WebCatalyst, a browser-interaction reinforcement learning framework with three complementary components: a game-level GUI assessor for sustained interaction and evaluation, Visual Anchor for mitigating VLM reward hacking, and Action-Trace Credit for grounding token-level credit assignment in runtime execution traces. Trained on fewer than 1K requests, predominantly for games, WebCatalyst raises the Cookie-Bench Mini Games score from 68.8 to 75.3 and also the WebGen-Bench accuracy from 48.8 to 56.9 on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, outperforming Claude Opus 4.7 in average rank across evaluated metrics. Further analysis shows that Visual Anchor prevents aesthetic degradation, while runtime-grounded credit assignment accelerates functional improvement. Together, our results show that improving feedback fidelity is the key to substantially advancing interactive HTML generation.

articles.title: Physics-Informed Functional Tucker Method with RKHS Factors for Sparse Spatiotemporal Reconstruction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03717v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reconstructing physical dynamics from fixed sparse sensors and missing frames is a fundamental challenge in scientific research. Sparsity leaves large regions of the field unconstrained, making the inverse problem ill-posed: a model may fit the observed sensors while producing inaccurate off-sensor structures or unreliable predictions between support frames. To this end, we propose PhysFTM---a physics-informed functional Tucker model that parameterizes the Tucker mode factors in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs) and incorporates PDE constraints through finite-difference residuals evaluated at off-sensor collocation points. These residuals provide additional physical information in regions without direct observational supervision. PhysFTM first reconstructs continuous spatial fields at support frames via an alternating minimization scheme, optimizing the Tucker core tensor and the RKHS-based factors separately. To enable missing-frame reconstruction, PhysFTM constructs a continuous trajectory in Tucker-core space, which is decoded by the learned spatial RKHS-FTM representation to recover the full spatiotemporal field. Experiments on Allen--Cahn, Navier--Stokes, three-dimensional Heat equations, and a three-dimensional gridded Copernicus ocean reanalysis demonstrate accurate 2D/3D reconstruction under two missing-frame protocols. Code is available at https://github.com/liusirzzz/PhysFTM.

articles.title: Spectral Quantum Memory for Implicit Neural Representations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04574v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) model signals as continuous functions from coordinates to values, but their performance depends strongly on how spectral capacity is allocated. Yet most Quantum INR (QINR) architectures treat spectral components as independent outputs of separate quantum blocks. We introduce the Spectral Quantum Memory Model (SQMM), a memory coupled quantum INR in which sequential hybrid data reuploading layers (bands) communicate through a shared coherent quantum memory register. Each band reads the memory, computes on its own coordinate upload, and writes part of its state back, so later bands can build on the computation of earlier ones. When memory read and write layers are input independent, we prove that the memory state forms an operator valued Fourier series whose support is contained in the Minkowski sum of the initial memory spectrum and the local band spectra. Downstream bands then condition their Fourier coefficients on the spectral content stored by earlier bands, and the memory coupling creates no new primitive frequencies. This theory motivates a spectral memory alignment loss that encourages memory to encode the spectrum expressed by the deployed prefix of the model. Across audio and image reconstruction benchmarks, SQMM improves over compact QINR and INR baselines.

articles.title: Disturbance storm time index coupling with solar wind/IMF parameters
articles.abstract: Understanding the complex coupling between the interplanetary magnetic field (IMF), solar wind dynamics and geomagnetic activity remains a cornerstone of space weather research. While the broader relationships are well-acknowledged, quantifying the precise, time-dependent impacts of specific heliospheric drivers on the Disturbance Storm Time (Dst) index requires deeper investigation. This study systematically analyzes the interactions between the Dst index and a comprehensive suite of solar wind and IMF parameters-including velocity (vsw), density (nsw), dynamic pressure (Psw), convective electric field (Esw) and magnetic field components (Bx, By, Bz, Btotal), alongside the ap and AE indices-using high-resolution data from 2010 to 2018. Employing a robust framework of Time-Shifted Cross-Correlation (TSCC), Cross Wavelet Transform (XWT) and Wavelet Transform Coherence (WTC), we map both the transient lags and localized periodicities of these interactions. TSCC analysis reveals a distinct zero-day lag response, characterized by strong negative correlations for vsw, ap, AE, Esw, Btotal and Psw against the Dst index, contrasted by positive correlations with Bz, nsw and the vswBz coupling term. Furthermore, XWT and WTC analyses identify high common-power regions and phase-locked coherence dominated by a ∼28-day solar rotation periodicity across the driving parameters. These findings refine our understanding of solar-terrestrial energy transfer mechanisms and offer critical constraints for empirical geomagnetic storm forecasting models.

articles.title: Effect of higher NOx emissions tax rates on carbon efficiency: Quasi-natural experiment based on China's NOx emissions tax rate reform
articles.abstract: This study employs a quasi-natural experiment with a difference-in-differences (DID) approach to estimate the impact of China’s nitrous oxide (NOx) emissions tax reform on carbon efficiency (CE), defining the reform as the adoption of rates above the national minimum to precisely capture regional heterogeneity. Results reveal that the NOx emissions tax rate reform significantly accelerates sample cities’ CE progress and has beneficial spatial spillover effects, driving CE improvement in surrounding areas. The reform exhibits more pronounced CE enhancement effects in eastern China and cities with a larger share of secondary industry. Furthermore, the reform effectively synergizes with policy measures such as clean energy promotion, air pollution prevention and control plans, and the Low-Carbon City pilot policy, yielding more positive outcomes. The NOx emissions tax rate reform enhances CE through promoting green technological innovation and curbing industrial agglomeration in pilot regions. Furthermore, synergistic NOx and carbon dioxide (CO2) reduction is the most comprehensive and primary channel for promoting CE progress through NOx emissions tax rate reform. The findings reveal the ancillary influence of NOx emissions tax on CO2 reduction and their potential as an interim instrument before China enacts a carbon tax, offering a practical, efficiency-aligned mitigation pathway.

articles.title: Learning Across Wells: A Robust Framework for Lithology Classification and Prediction
articles.abstract: Automated lithology classification from wireline logs plays a crucial role in enhancing subsurface characterization, reservoir delineation, and completion design efficiency. This paper develops two widely used supervised machine-learning classifiers, Random Forest (RF) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), for predicting multi-well lithology. The evaluation uses four standard wireline logs: gamma ray (GR), bulk density (RHOB), corrected sonic transit time (DTCORR), and effective porosity (PHIE), collected from four North Sea wells (F02-01, F03-02, F03-04, and F06-01). Four lithology classes Shale, Sandstone, Tight Sand, and Carbonate were used to conduct the evaluation of the models, which were conducted without core-calibrated ground truth or fixed petrophysical cut-offs. The assessment involved blind-well testing and Leave-One-Well-Out (LOWO) cross-validation. Hyperparameters were improved through the application of stratified five-fold cross-validation. In the blind F06-01 well, Random Forest (RF) demonstrated an accuracy of 100.0% (weighted F1 = 1.000), in contrast to KNN's accuracy of 98.45%. Additionally, LOWO validation produced mean accuracies of 99.58% for RF and 97.10% for KNN. GR, RHOB, and PHIE were the primary features of significance, while DTCORR had a negligible contribution. The models reached a consensus on 98.4% of blind-well samples, with RF accurately addressing all discrepancies. Even without feature scaling, Random Forest's full, feature-randomized ensemble structure surpasses the distance-based KNN classifier in inter-well log variability robustness. We address the limitations of rule-based labeling without core data, review machine learning research for lithology and facies classification, and propose resistivity logs, ensemble boosting, and core-calibrated labels for future research.

articles.title: Plasmonic anchoring boosts mechanoluminescence via mechano–electro–optical cascade
articles.abstract: Localized surface plasmon resonance has been extensively exploited to enhance photoluminescence and electroluminescence, yet its application to mechanoluminescence remains unrealized due to the metal-induced quenching-enhancement trade-off and irreversible interfacial delamination under cyclic strain. Here we report the first plasmonically enhanced ML elastomer via an in-situ reduction strategy that anchors ~ 70 nm Au nanoparticles directly onto ZnS:Cu phosphors through covalent Au–S bonds within a PDMS matrix. This interfacial architecture simultaneously passivates sulfur-vacancy quenching centers and confines the LSPR near-field within the carrier-detrapping zone, accelerating radiative recombination via the Purcell effect. Concurrently, the covalent Au–S dipole establishes an “electronic lock” that temporally gates carrier release, mitigating non-radiative losses. Au incorporation alone boosts ML brightness (~ 6-fold) and mechano–optical sensitivity (~ 5.5-fold). When integrated with Al2O3 stress concentrators, a synergistic mechano–electro–opticall cascade achieves ~ 9-fold enhancement at 20 wt% phosphor loading, with exceptional cyclic stability (2.78% fluctuation over 600 cycles). This platform circumvents the long-standing quenching-durability dilemma, enabling self-powered strain mapping, wearable stress monitoring, and intuitive human-machine interfaces. Our work establishes a generalizable interfacial design paradigm for plasmon-enhanced mechanophotonic devices.

articles.title: Advanced Functional Thin Films via Nebulizer Spray Pyrolysis: Synthesis, Structure, and Applications
articles.abstract: Nebulizer-assisted spray pyrolysis (NSP) is a solution-mediated route for producing functional thin films through controlled aerosol generation, droplet transport, solvent evaporation and thermally activated precursor conversion at a heated substrate. Its appeal lies in the relative simplicity of the apparatus, flexibility in precursor chemistry and potential for coating extended substrate areas. Nevertheless, film formation is governed by coupled phenomena—including droplet-size distribution, solvent volatility, precursor speciation, substrate temperature, aerosol residence time and post-deposition treatment—that determine phase constitution, morphology, defect populations and functional response. This review examines NSP as a materials-engineering platform, with particular attention to oxide semiconductors such as ZnO and Al-doped ZnO (AZO), and to spray-pyrolysed chalcogenide absorbers such as Cu₂ZnSnS₄ (CZTS). Published work on solvent-dependent ZnO deposition and AZO coatings is considered alongside the author’s contributions to ZnO, CZTS, ZnTe and magnesium phthalocyanine (MgPc) thin-film research. A necessary distinction is maintained between materials demonstrated by nebulizer/spray pyrolysis and comparative systems prepared by physical vapour deposition: the cited ZnTe and MgPc studies used vacuum or thermal evaporation and are therefore discussed as complementary examples of structure–property engineering, not as NSP demonstrations. The review develops a unified process–composition–structure–defect–property framework, evaluates characterization strategies and identifies research priorities in precursor design, reproducibility, phase verification, scale-up and application-specific optimization.

articles.title: Task-Evoked Metabolic Balance and Intrinsic Network Organization Relate to Processing Speed
articles.abstract: Processing speed is a core component of cognition that declines with aging and is impaired across neurological and psychiatric disorders. We combined functional proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy at 7 T with resting-state functional MRI to examine neurochemical and functional correlates of processing speed in 26 young and eight older adults. During a symbol–digit matching task, lactate showed a significant age-by-condition interaction, with a larger stimulation-related increase in older adults. Glutamate showed no significant group-level modulation, although its time course suggested a delayed response in older adults. The glutamate-to-lactate ratio decreased during stimulation in older adults, with an apparent rise during subsequent control periods, suggesting a possible temporal offset between the metabolite responses. Across participants, larger task-evoked lactate changes were associated with slower processing, whereas glutamate responses were heterogeneous and nonsignificant at the group level. Older adults also showed lower intrinsic functional coherence in the dorsal medial anterior cingulate cortex and executive and attention networks. Exploratory analyses linked greater coherence to better processing speed and smaller lactate responses. Together, these findings link individual differences in processing speed to both task-evoked neuroenergetic responses and intrinsic functional organization. The greater lactate recruitment observed with aging and poorer cognitive performance may reflect increased reliance on non-oxidative metabolism or compensatory metabolic engagement to meet cognitive demands. These results highlight fMRS as a complementary approach for characterizing the metabolic mechanisms underlying individual differences in cognition and cognitive aging.

articles.title: CFD-informed machine learning for surface-temperature mapping of side-cooled 4680 lithium-ion cells under thermal uncertainty
articles.abstract: Large-format 4680 lithium-ion cells present a thermal-monitoring challenge because surface measurements do not fully describe the temperature field and key heat-transfer properties remain uncertain. This study combines a validated three-dimensional steady thermal model with machine learning to reconstruct the external can-surface temperature field of a side-cooled 4680 cell. Seventy-five CFD cases were generated by varying radial jelly-roll conductivity from 0.90 to 2.00 W m− 1 K− 1 and equivalent interface thickness from 0.40 to 0.60 mm at a fixed 6.0 W heat input and 25°C cooling boundary. Temperatures from 25 surface locations produced 1,875 spatial samples. The CFD model reproduced three published validation temperatures within 0.196°C, and the two finest meshes differed by less than 0.01%. CNN-LSTM and SVM yielded similar held-out point-level performance, with R² values of 0.981 and 0.980 and RMSE values of 0.238 and 0.245°C, respectively; MLP was less accurate. Feature perturbation identified axial position as the dominant predictor, followed by x-position and radial conductivity. The resulting surrogate reproduces the simulated can-surface temperature field within the investigated steady-state parameter range and provides a computationally inexpensive basis for thermal-sensitivity analysis.

articles.title: An Extended Multi-Source WEPI Framework for Mapping Wind Erosion Potential, Hotspots, and Priority Zones in Lorestan Province, Iran
articles.abstract: Wind erosion is a major driver of land degradation in dryland and seasonally exposed landscapes, yet its spatiotemporal dynamics remain insufficiently quantified in many mountainous semi-arid regions. This study developed an extended multi-source Wind Erosion Potential Index (WEPI) to assess wind erosion susceptibility in Lorestan Province, western Iran, during 2016–2025. The proposed framework integrated 120 monthly observations at 1000 m spatial resolution by combining vegetation protection loss, bare soil exposure, soil moisture dryness, land surface temperature, wind force, precipitation dryness, soil erodibility, topographic susceptibility, and land-cover exposure. The results revealed persistent moderate-to-high wind erosion potential, with annual mean WEPI ranging from 0.584 in 2020 to 0.605 in 2021 and a long-term mean of approximately 0.592. Approximately 95.31% of valid pixels were classified as moderate or higher risk, while summer exhibited the highest seasonal erosion potential, with a mean WEPI of 0.633. Component contribution analysis showed that bare soil exposure and vegetation protection loss together accounted for nearly 45.8% of the total WEPI. Spatial analyses identified 12,804 statistically significant hotspot pixels and 17,366 persistent high-risk pixels, indicating that chronic erosion susceptibility was more extensive than areas exhibiting significant temporal increases. The proposed framework provides a robust, reproducible, and transferable approach for identifying priority areas for wind erosion monitoring, land degradation assessment, and sustainable land management in semi-arid environments.

articles.title: An Insert-Compatible Magnetic Actuation Platform for Dynamic Air–Liquid Interface Culture of Human Alveolar Epithelial Cells
articles.abstract: Static air–liquid interface (ALI) culture reproduces apical air exposure but not breathing-associated deformation. We developed an insert-compatible magnetic actuator that cyclically deforms a porous polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)-supported human alveolar epithelial culture while the culture plate remains lidded and free of pneumatic tubing or mechanical linkages entering the culture chamber. A polyamide-coated NdFeB magnet resting on collagen I was driven by an electromagnet beneath the plate. Short-term screening showed that coating prevented the marked MTT/LDH toxicity of an uncoated magnet. The selected 12 V, 0.2 Hz condition, operated with auxiliary convective cooling, maintained culture medium near 37°C and produced approximately 2.5 mm central displacement; geometry-based analysis estimated an annular mean strain of 7–16%. Human pulmonary alveolar epithelial cells (HPAEpiCs) were matured at ALI for 7 days and then cultured for 72 h under dynamic, static-ALI, or submerged conditions. Dynamic ALI showed higher apparent transepithelial electrical resistance than static ALI at 72 h (1780 ± 140 vs. 1634 ± 120 Ω·cm²; n = 9; p = 0.0304). At the matched 72 h endpoint, dynamic ALI also expressed the AT1-associated marker AQP5 4.3-fold higher than static ALI (p < 0.001), and whole-mount immunofluorescence confirmed retention of concurrent AT1- and AT2-associated features. The platform provides a compact route to add breathing-like mechanical input to an insert-based alveolar ALI workflow while preserving conventional barrier and molecular readouts.

articles.title: Toward Intelligent Thermal Fluids: AI-Driven Design of Zeta-Engineered Nanofluids and Self-Organized Thermal Transport Networks
articles.abstract: The development of next-generation nanofluids requires a shift from empirical formulation approaches toward data-driven design strategies that simultaneously optimize thermal conductivity, dynamic viscosity, stability, and system-level performance. This perspective highlights the emerging convergence of artificial intelligence (AI), zeta-potential (ZP) engineering, and advanced nanomaterials for the design of intelligent thermal fluids. Particular emphasis is placed on ZP-engineered nanofluids, in which electrostatic interactions are deliberately tailored to control nanoparticle dispersion, stability, and the formation of self-organized thermal transport networks. While interconnected nanoparticle networks can enhance thermal transport, excessive network connectivity, especially in high-aspect-ratio nanomaterials such as carbon nanotubes and graphene derivatives, may increase the dynamic viscosity and hydraulic resistance. Therefore, optimal nanofluid design requires balancing competing thermophysical and operational objectives under application-specific conditions. An AI-driven framework integrating machine learning, physics-informed machine learning, explainable AI, active learning, and multi-objective optimization is presented to accelerate nanofluid discovery and optimization. A representative case study of ZP-engineered iron oxide-carbon nanotube-graphene oxide nanofluids demonstrates the use of data-driven modeling, feature-importance analysis, SHAP interpretation, and Pareto optimization. The integration of AI-guided optimization with ZP-controlled network engineering provides a promising pathway toward intelligent thermal fluids and autonomous materials discovery for advanced thermal management systems.

articles.title: A “Three Birds with One Stone” Strategy for the Pretreatment of Swine Wastewater Using Modified Attapulgite: Purification Mechanisms of Crystallization–Coagulation–Adsorption
articles.abstract: This study developed a novel attapulgite-based coagulant (ATPC) to address the high turbidity, high organic content, and high NH4+ concentration of swine wastewater. ATPC was synthesized from natural attapulgite (palygorskite) (ATP) through a synergistic modification strategy that combined high-temperature calcination, sulfuric acid leaching, and alkali-induced polymerization. The optimal preparation conditions were determined as follows: calcination temperature of 600°C, sulfuric acid concentration of 25%, solid–liquid ratio of 1:5, and polymerization pH of 3. Under these conditions, ATPC achieved a turbidity removal efficiency of 98.8% for swine wastewater. Compared with conventional polyaluminum chloride (PAC), ATPC formed denser flocs that settled considerably faster. Coupling ATPC with magnesium salts induced struvite crystallization and increased the NH4+ removal efficiency from less than 10% to approximately 50%. At the optimal aging time of 12 h, the functional component accounted for 48.8% of [Fe(III) + Al(III)]T. The zeta potential trend indicates that charge neutralization is the primary mechanism of ATPC, in which high-valent cations are essential for destabilizing colloids, while the insoluble particles strengthen the floc structure and promote sedimentation through bridging effects. The as-prepared ATPC is an eco-friendly natural mineral coagulant with promising prospects for the advanced treatment of swine wastewater.

articles.title: Testing Einstein's laws from the bottom of the Mediterranean Sea
articles.abstract: Are the laws of physics truly the same everywhere in the universe? This fundamental principle, known as Lorentz invariance, lies at the heart of Einstein's theory of relativity. Yet some theories that seek to reconcile gravity with quantum physics suggest that it might not always hold. To investigate this possibility, researchers from the international KM3NeT collaboration analyzed 5,828 atmospheric neutrino candidate events detected by KM3NeT/ORCA, a neutrino telescope located deep in the Mediterranean Sea.

articles.title: Finding the fingerprints of noisy distributions in random quantum systems
articles.abstract: Imagine shuffling a deck of cards where some of the cards are fading just because of the way they interact with the external environment as you shuffle them. Your job is to figure out the interplay between the shuffling, or "imposed randomness," due to the way you shuffle your cards and how that relates to the fading as cards are exposed to the external environment.

articles.title: Light-matter hybrids form supersolid quantum state at room temperature
articles.abstract: Researchers from the Faculty of Physics at the University of Warsaw, the Military University of Technology (Poland), IBM Research Zurich and the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) have observed a new quantum state of matter known as a supersolid in an exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensate. Remarkably, the phenomenon occurs not at temperatures close to absolute zero, but at room temperature. The results have been published in Science Advances.

articles.title: A laser can draw superconductivity at the nanoscale
articles.abstract: Researchers from ICMAB-CSIC, the Politecnico di Milano and Université de Liège have adapted a direct laser writing technique that allows them to "draw" superconducting properties in a material. The result is a new way to locally program the behavior of a superconductor, tuning it from a fully superconducting state to an insulating one with extraordinary precision.

articles.title: A single measurement makes quantum bits more reliable
articles.abstract: Researchers at the University of Regensburg and their international partners have found a way to significantly reduce errors in quantum bits. In an experiment, they demonstrated that a single additional measurement before a series of quantum operations can cut the error rate by more than half. The results have been published in Applied Physics Reviews.

articles.title: Current-Confined Formation of a Buried Ge/Si Free Surface for Defect Filtering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lattice-mismatched heteroepitaxy is limited by misfit dislocations, threading defects, and residual strain generated at buried interfaces. Here, we show that current-confined electrochemistry transforms the Ge/Si heterointerface into a laterally continuous nanometric free surface while preserving the Ge epilayer. A low-doped Ge layer on a conductive p-type Si substrate redirects anodization current toward the misfit-dislocation-rich interface. Numerical modelling including charge-transfer kinetics shows that this confinement arises from hole-limited charge transfer and, together with electrochemical calibration, defines a process window that combines interfacial current confinement with controlled Si porosification. STEM reveals an approximately 15 Ang separation, while EDX shows localized interfacial oxygen enrichment. After soft annealing, geometric phase analysis and plan-view TEM show a modified strain-relaxation pathway and strongly suppressed threading-dislocation emergence. Raman spectroscopy indicates a reduction in residual tensile strain from approximately 0.10 % to 0.05 %, whereas spreading resistance profiling confirms preservation of the Ge carrier profile. Current-confined electrochemistry therefore provides a controllable post-epitaxial route for buried-interface decoupling, defect filtering, and strain control in lattice-mismatched semiconductor heterostructures.

articles.title: Agentic inverse design of spatially programmed materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatially programmed functional materials, from functionally graded alloys and metamaterials to quantum superlattices, use their spatial structure to tailor physical properties. However, translating a desired spatial structure into a practical fabrication recipe remains challenging due to the complex relationship between processing conditions and resulting material structures. Here we show that a large language model (LLM) agent can inverse-design such fabrication recipes by using a physics-based simulator of ion-matter interactions as a tool. Given an arbitrary depth profile of implanted ions or vacancies, the agent selects the ion species, energies, incident angles, and target material layers; writes, runs, and interprets simulations; and iteratively refines the recipe until the simulated profile matches the target, with minimal human input. Our work demonstrates physics-guided agentic inverse design as a practical approach to making the spatial structure of materials a programmable variable, opening new opportunities to explore emergent physical phenomena and functional phases of matter.

articles.title: Thermal Phase Transition of Three Dimensional Orthogonal Metals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orthogonal metals provide a paradigmatic example of strongly entangled metallic states whose transport and thermodynamic properties resemble those of conventional Fermi liquids, while their single-electron excitations remain fundamentally distinct. Despite considerable interest in their unusual ground-state properties, orthogonal metals in three spatial dimensions and their finite-temperature behavior remain relatively unexplored. Here, we investigate a three-dimensional orthogonal metal and characterize the thermodynamic and spectroscopic signatures associated with its finite-temperature phase transition. Starting from a simple model of fermions coupled to spin degrees of freedom, we perturbatively demonstrate that the thermal transition known to occur in the purely bosonic limit persists in the presence of coupling to a gapless Fermi surface. We then examine physical observables that change prominently between the coherent and orthogonal-metal regimes.
