Discretization uses Strang splitting, combining an order-parameter-weighted discrete unified gas kinetic scheme for the transport substep with a positivity-preserving update of the interfacial source. Benchmarks over planar and curved, stationary and moving boundaries reproduce rarefaction-dependent velocity slip and wall heat transfer, absorption-driven flow, and feedback between gas forces and solid translation and rotation. In final simulations, the order parameter evolves by a Cahn--Hilliard equation with degenerate mobility, and thin-film growth exhibits distinct surface profiles at different vapor incidence angles. By connecting implicit geometry to molecular surface exchange, DIKM provides a basis for coupling rarefied gas dynamics to solid motion and material evolution.

articles.title: On flow unsteadiness in strongly separated high-speed ramp flows using kinetic and data-driven methods
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The gas dynamics of high speed flows over several compression-expansion ramp geometries with large separation regions were investigated using a particle kinetic approach and data driven methods. These large separation regions allow study of the role of scaled angle predicted by triple deck theory on recirculation strength, separation size, and appearance of secondary recirculation regions, all of which lead to flow unsteadiness. Examining four different free stream conditions for the same geometry using the direct simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) approach, we show that the stability of single recirculation in the separation region is more sensitive to wall temperature and free stream velocity than physical ramp angle. Stability in this context refers to appearance of secondary separation regions. In addition, configurations with similar types of recirculation regions from literature considered, we find that general trends regarding unsteadiness, such as appearance of secondary recirculation regions, mostly hold; however, the flows are too complex to be characterized by only scaled angle. Thus, stochastic flowfields generated by DSMC were investigated using data driven methods, namely spectral proper orthogonal decomposition and dynamic mode decomposition. We found that both methods yield similar frequency components and mode shapes for spatio-temporal coherent structures of unsteady DSMC flows. With the help of these structures, the main mechanisms of unsteadiness were identified as oscillations of the reattachment shock, Kelvin-Helmholtz like instability of the shear layer, and c-shaped mode of the separation bubble. This is the first time SPOD has been applied to a DSMC generated flowfield and compared with DMD.

articles.title: Generalized Lorentz Framework for Active Semiconductor Quantum Surface Plasmonics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanostructured semiconductors provide an actively tunable platform for light-matter interactions across a broad spectral range. As feature sizes shrink to the deep nanoscale (~10 nm scale), nonclassical carrier dynamics and surface plasmonic responses become prominent, creating substantial challenges for a rigorous and efficient theoretical treatment. Here we develop a generalized Lorentz framework for quantum surface plasmonics in nanostructured semiconductors with arbitrary energymomentum dispersion relations. The framework enables efficient quantitative treatment of carrier nonlocality, carrier surface accumulation and depletion, and nonlocal damping in three-dimensional semiconductor nanostructures, under electrical tuning and across a wide range of doping densities. Building on this framework, we further establish a rigorous quasinormal-mode analysis that provides transparent physical insight into complex surface plasmonic responses of multiscale semiconductor structures. We demonstrate electrically controlled deep-nanoscale carrier accumulation and depletion in a semiconductor nanoantenna, leading to pronounced plasmonic-response modulation that can be interpreted in terms of eigenmode shifts, creation, and annihilation. By quantifying and linking complex nonclassical carrier dynamics with plasmonic eigenmodes, our work establishes a comprehensive quantitative framework for active semiconductor quantum surface plasmonics and will foster the convergence of electronics and photonics at the deep nanoscale.

articles.title: Analog signal processing, storage, and demultiplexing via in-materia wave-based computing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ability of mechanical systems to perform basic computations has gained traction in recent years, providing a robust supplement to digital computing in off-grid, low-power, and extreme environments where electronics are inaccessible or risk failure. However, prior work has focused on Boolean logic applied via bistable structures, snap-through mechanisms, or origami lattices. Digital signal processing (DSP) underpins a wide range of computational tasks, providing the foundation for information encoding, manipulation, and analysis. In contrast to conventional DSP approaches, we present a new paradigm for analog information processing, where an elastic substrate houses a spatial wave-based platform for mechanical signal manipulation in the temporal domain. The proposed metasurface-based system exploits temperature-dependent phase transitions of shape memory alloys (SMAs) to realize key signal-processing functionalities, including gating, retention, and programmable delay of impinging mechanical loads. In doing so, we address a new set of challenges by manipulating transient mechanical waves through dispersive and lossy media. Building on this capability, we introduce the concept of mechanical wave-based memory, in which a locally resonant metamaterial's dispersion characteristics are actively reconfigured to achieve programmable delays while preserving spatial waveform integrity, and demonstrate its utility in the context of input shaping and frequency demultiplexing of superimposed waves. More broadly, the modular and scalable nature of the demonstrated framework paves the way for advanced mechanical computing architectures, enabling higher-order operations such as signal classification, parallel processing, and reservoir computing through the controlled sequencing and temporal alignment of mechanical signals.

articles.title: Pump quantization changes optimal measurements for quantum sensing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03943v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard analyses of quantum phase sensing often neglect the overhead of generating squeezed-light by treating the pump as an undepleted classical resource. Realistically, the pump is a quantum object that undergoes significant depletion and entangles with the produced squeezed light, raising the question of how the crossover from a classical to a quantum pump limits the quantum advantage in sensing. Contrary to prior analyses, we show that quantum advantage persists despite pump quantization, but depends critically on the nonlinear (χ⁽²⁾) source dynamics. In particular, we demonstrate that Heisenberg scaling emerges in the regime of strong pump depletion, rather than maximum signal squeezing. At maximum squeezing, the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for interferometric sensing of an unknown phase scales as N³/², where N is the pump photon number, surpassing the shot-noise limit but establishing that squeezing itself is insufficient to attain Heisenberg scaling of N². At maximal pump depletion, where the signal flux is maximized, the QFI scales as N². In this regime, standard photon counting is suboptimal, while a joint nonlinear measurement of the entire pump-signal system is shown to achieve Heisenberg scaling. Our work shows that pump quantization changes both the optimal operating point and the measurement strategies required to preserve a realistic quantum advantage in phase estimation and, more broadly, many-body quantum dynamics.

articles.title: High-order compact ALE gas-kinetic scheme on three-dimensional unstructured meshes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05095v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, a compact high-order gas-kinetic scheme (HGKS) is developed for compressible arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) computations on three-dimensional unstructured meshes. To achieve high-order spatial accuracy, a large number of matrix inversions are required for spatial reconstruction. In ALE computations, the mesh moves and the geometric information must be recalculated at each time step, which reduces computational efficiency. To improve efficiency, a memory-reduction reconstruction strategy is employed to construct a quadratic polynomial on unstructured meshes. By differentiating the candidate polynomial, the quadratic terms are obtained by the least-squares method using the average gradient values of the cell itself and its neighboring cells. The linear terms of the polynomial are also determined by the least-squares method. On three-dimensional unstructured meshes, a 3×3 coefficient matrix must be stored, and four least-squares procedures are required to construct a quadratic polynomial. To suppress numerical oscillations in flows with discontinuities, generalized essentially non-oscillatory (GENO) reconstruction and a gradient compression factor are adopted. To accelerate the computation, a multi-GPU accelerated code is implemented using Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) and Message Passing Interface (MPI). The current scheme is fully explicit, and the acceleration framework can be developed based on cell-level parallelism. Numerical examples are presented to evaluate the accuracy and robustness of the scheme, including flows with strong discontinuities, pitching wings, and helicopter rotors. Numerical results confirm the excellent performance of the compact ALE scheme on unstructured meshes.

articles.title: Remap for ALE Hydrodynamics via Direct Interpolation and Constraint Optimization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.05327v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work presents an optimization-based remap approach for arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) hydrodynamics that preserves sharp features and physical bounds while conserving global quantities such as volume, mass, momentum, and total energy. Achieving these properties is the main challenge in remap methods. The presented approach is well-suited for high-order finite element (FE) discretizations and ALE methods that allow for large, purely Lagrangian displacements between successive remeshing and remapping steps. Recent advances in parallel, GPU-capable interpolation routines enable the initial transfer of all fields via direct physical-space interpolation, avoiding computationally costly and diffusive pseudo-transient PDE-based advection. The interpolation produces bounded fields with minimal numerical diffusion. However, it may violate the desired conservation of global properties. Thus, a subsequent optimization step restores conservation while preserving physical bounds. The presented method provides minimally diffusive remapping of finite element fields of arbitrary order. Moreover, it directly remaps quantities defined at integration points, eliminating the need for projection onto finite element spaces. The approach also mitigates typical challenges associated with synchronizing primal variables and conserved quantities in advection-based remap methods. The proposed optimization-based remap method is evaluated using standard two- and three-dimensional remap benchmarks and full ALE hydrodynamics simulations.

articles.title: Analytic Model of Trans-axial Sensitivity in Cylindrical PET Systems Based on Solid Angle
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.13118v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In positron emission tomography (PET), a clear theoretical model describing how system sensitivity varies as a source is moved trans-axially within the field of view (FOV) is lacking. The current understanding and practical intuition often suggest that sensitivity is maximum at the center of the FOV, an assumption reflected in standardized protocols. In this work, we derive an analytic model for the trans-axial-plane sensitivity distribution in a cylindrical PET scanner based on solid angle. The model, formulated as a function of trans-axial offset from the center, is validated through both Monte Carlo simulations and physical experiments on a representative system. We find that the derived theoretical distribution is essentially consistent with simulation and experimental results, revealing a non-intuitive feature: sensitivity increases with trans-axial offset, peaks at the edge of the FOV, and drops off sharply beyond it. This study provides the first closed-form model of trans-axial geometric sensitivity in cylindrical PET scanners, offering a vital benchmark for isolating detector technology improvements and revealing a non-intuitive, offset-dependent sensitivity profile that enables new protocol optimization strategies.

articles.title: Design of a radio-frequency photoinjector for generating relativistic vortex electron beams
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.00732v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the design and an analysis of the classical and quantum beam dynamics for an S-band radio-frequency (RF) photoinjector dedicated to the generation of relativistic vortex electron beams carrying a quantized orbital angular momentum (OAM). The field-map-based tracking simulations were performed in the ultra-low bunch charge regime (Q = 0.63 pC), where space-charge effects are strongly suppressed. We demonstrate that optimizing the injection phase and solenoidal focusing preserves the intrinsic thermal limit of the photoemission source, yielding a stable, emittance-compensated beam with a final kinetic energy of 4.9 MeV and a normalized transverse emittance of 56,π,mumcdotmrad. Furthermore, our quantum-mechanical analysis of single-electron Laguerre-Gaussian wave packets inside the designed accelerating fields reveals that rapid energy gain suppresses transverse quantum spreading by nearly three orders of magnitude compared to free-space propagation. This suppression protects the characteristic OAM-dependent spatial structure of the wave packet. These results establish the beam-dynamics operating regime and vacuum conditions required for subsequent experiments on the generation and transport of relativistic vortex electron beams.

articles.title: Roadmap to Quantum Aesthetics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.08363v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum mechanics occupies a central position in contemporary science while remaining largely inaccessible to direct sensory experience. This paper proposes a roadmap to quantum aesthetics that examines how quantum concepts become aesthetic phenomena through artistic mediation rather than direct representation. Two complementary and orthogonal approaches are articulated. The first, a pioneering top-down approach, employs text-prompt-based generative AI to probe quantum aesthetics as a collective cultural construct embedded in large-scale training data. By systematically modulating the linguistic weight of the term "quantum," generative models are used as experimental environments to reveal how quantum imaginaries circulate within contemporary visual culture. The second, a bottom-up approach, derives aesthetic form directly from quantum-mechanical structures through the visualization of quantum-generated data, exemplified here by hydrogen atomic orbitals calculated from the Schrödinger equation. These approaches are framed not as competing methods but as intersecting paths within a navigable field of artistic research. They position quantum aesthetics as an emergent field of artistic research shaped by cultural imagination, computational mediation, and physical law, opening new directions for artistic practice and pedagogy at the intersection of art, data, artificial intelligence and quantum science.

articles.title: Hydrogen and Lithium Isotope Analysis via Optical Spectroscopy of Laser-Produced Plasmas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.13554v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate detection and quantification of light-element isotopes, particularly hydrogen (H) and lithium (Li), are essential across chemistry, materials science, geology, nuclear energy, forensics, and defense applications. Their isotopic compositions provide insight into fuel cycles, materials degradation, mass transport, and environmental processes. Hydrogen and Li isotopes are especially relevant in nuclear environments because neutron-induced reactions directly connect their isotopic inventories. Despite their importance, analysis of these light isotopes remains challenging due to their low atomic mass, high mobility, and, in some cases, radiological constraints. While some existing analytical techniques can detect and measure H and/or Li, they typically require extensive sample preparation, laboratory-based instrumentation, or extended analysis times that preclude real-time monitoring capabilities. To address these limitations, optical spectroscopy of laser-produced plasmas offers a promising solution, enabling field-deployable, standoff sensing of isotopic signatures with real-time analysis capability and no sample preparation requirement. This Topical Review summarizes fundamentals and recent advances in H and Li isotopic analysis using optical spectroscopy, with emphasis on laser-produced plasmas generated by laser ablation of solid targets. Key concepts relevant to isotope-resolved optical measurements are introduced, including isotope shifts, fine and hyperfine structure, and line-broadening mechanisms. Progress in optical emission, laser induced fluorescence, and absorption spectroscopy is reviewed for H and Li isotopes.

articles.title: When can buoyancy be neglected in simulations of crystallization fouling? Evidence from a confluence flow cell
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.07305v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Predicting crystallization fouling remains difficult because it couples supersaturation, nucleation, crystal growth, transport, and adhesion. Separating these processes requires model systems in which they can be independently controlled. One such system is the confluence flow cell, where two incompatible brines mix and generate supersaturation at their interface. The mixing pattern is often predicted using constant-density simulations because density differences between the brines are typically only a few percent or less. We investigate whether this assumption holds when calcium chloride and sodium sulfate react to form gypsum. A constant-density simulation predicts deposition on the channel floor along the centreline. Experimentally, however, gypsum forms bands on both side walls, with deposition moving upstream as flow rate decreases. Dye experiments spanning density differences of 0.14 to 2.1 %, three channel heights, and 32 flow rates show that the distance required for the dyed stream to reach the opposite wall is governed by the bulk Richardson number, Ri=g'H/U², following L/H = 3.31,Ri⁻⁰.⁶⁶ over four decades in Ri (R²=0.89). When the stream densities are matched, the dyed stream typically no longer reaches the opposite wall, and a reacting experiment shows gypsum deposition on the floor, consistent with the constant-density simulation. A small density difference alone is therefore insufficient to neglect buoyancy; the Richardson number must also be small. At the low flow rates typical of confluence flow cells, this condition is often not met. Because Ri depends only on density difference, channel height, and flow velocity, we recommend evaluating it before applying constant-density models of mixing, reaction, or fouling.

articles.title: A Square-Root Barrier to Quantum Gate Speed under Linear Coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.19280v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Faster quantum gates can reduce the decoherence accumulated during a computation, but in superconducting processors, speeding up gates often involves stronger microwave pulses, which can increase leakage, off-resonant excitation, stray-field errors, and crosstalk. This creates a central energy--speed--error tradeoff: can quantum state engineering make a gate faster without paying proportionally more drive energy? We address this question by treating the driving pulse as a quantum bosonic field rather than a classical waveform. For a finite-dimensional system coupled linearly to that field, we prove that gate transition rates at fixed trace distance between the initial and final system states grow at most as the square root of the pulse energy, under pulse-uniformity conditions, without assuming an upper bound on the coupling strength. The bound permits arbitrary pulse states, including squeezed and non-Gaussian states, as well as drive--system entanglement and back action; coherent Gaussian pulses attain its energy exponent. Thus squeezing or other state engineering alone cannot replace the square-root energy law of a conventional linear drive by the linear scaling allowed by general quantum speed limits. Achieving that improvement requires changing the interaction class, in addition to using a suitable nonclassical pulse, thereby identifying interaction nonlinearity as an essential resource for relaxing the practical gate-speed error tradeoff.

articles.title: Efficient detection of spectral cluster states
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.09745v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multimode entangled states of light are key resources for high-dimensional photonic quantum technologies, particularly for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum information processing. Exploiting their full capabilities requires detection strategies that can efficiently and simultaneously access a large number of modes and their quantum correlations. Multimode optical parametric amplification (MOPA) provides a promising approach by amplifying multiple quadratures prior to detection, rendering the measurement robust against subsequent optical losses while enabling broadband operation. Here, we demonstrate the spectral multimode capability of MOPA by simultaneously characterizing a broadband 60-node dual-rail continuous-variable cluster state. We reconstruct the cluster-state nullifiers across the spectral modes and observe nearly uniform squeezing of up to -6.9 dB, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the highest level reported for pulsed spectrally multimode squeezed light. Furthermore, by evaluating the van Loock-Furusawa criterion across all relevant bipartitions, we verify genuine multipartite entanglement throughout the 60-node state. These results establish MOPA as a promising platform for scalable high-dimensional quantum information processing in the spectral domain.

articles.title: Stress-Testing the Robustness of LLM-Based Causal Inference
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Why do some of the world's most powerful Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems still struggle to reason about cause and effect? Causal discovery, the ability to discern the underlying drivers of a system, is fundamental to scientific inquiry and has traditionally relied on structured data and statistical methods. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have been explored as an alternative paradigm for causal inference, leveraging their broad knowledge and reasoning capabilities. Yet, despite their linguistic fluency, LLMs often rely on surface-level pattern recognition rather than genuine causal logic. While it is known that LLMs stumble in this domain, we lack a precise map of where, why, and how significantly these failures occur. In this paper, we propose a systematic stress-test framework across six critical dimensions: model scale, causal graph complexity, prompting strategy, metadata quality, data quality, and sensitivity to uncertainty. Our findings reveal a significant "optimism bias" in LLMs; models consistently overestimate causal links, leading to low precision across the board. Furthermore, we demonstrate that traditional evaluation metrics can be deceptive: while reasoning-heavy models lead in performance, the highest scores often occur when uncertainty in inference is overlooked. Once uncertainty is integrated into the evaluation, performance drops, providing a more honest reflection of causal reliability. We also find that, while scaling model size improves outcomes, these gains are fragile; performance degrades sharply as the quality of metadata decreases. This work serves as a practical guide to the blind spots of LLMs, offering a clear-eyed assessment of when these tools can be integrated into a causal discovery pipeline and when they are likely to lead researchers astray.

articles.title: Hardware-Aware Design and Layout Selection in Quantum Reservoir Computing for Insurance Claims Forecasting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03891v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) processes temporal information through quantum dynamics, but it remains unclear whether small QRC models can forecast real data competitively with classical models and whether their predictions survive the transfer from ideal simulation to noisy hardware. We address both questions for a six-qubit gate-based reservoir that forecasts next-day motor-insurance claim counts. Five reservoir candidates were selected and frozen using hardware-native interaction graphs, Trotterized Ising dynamics, memory and measurement-robustness criteria, circuit cost, and calibrated-noise screening. On 232 held-out test days, the ideal candidates reached root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of 5.66-6.12 claims/day, compared with 5.36 for ridge regression. For four of the five, the difference from ridge was not significant under a 95% block bootstrap, and their accuracy was comparable with classical recurrent and reservoir baselines. On the 156-qubit IBM Kingston processor, we ran 63 evaluations in 21 paired rounds, comparing hardware-aware, random-native, and Qiskit optimization level 1 layouts. Hardware-aware placement gave lower RMSE than Qiskit in every round, with a maximum transfer distortion of 7.59 claims/day (11.84 for Qiskit), and avoided the severe transfer failures seen for some random layouts. Most of the hardware distortion appeared as a systematic forecast shift, which a short hardware probe on training inputs detected before the test runs. Longer replay windows raised circuit cost without a consistent gain in forecasting accuracy or hardware transfer. Small QRC models can thus reach competitive accuracy on this task, and hardware-aware layout selection makes their transfer to IBM Kingston more consistent.

articles.title: Training LLM Agents to Automate LLM Post-Training with RSI-Dojo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) aims to enable AI systems to autonomously build and improve AI systems themselves, including models, harnesses, and underlying infrastructure. Within this broader agenda, a central capability is enabling agents to train and improve base models. However, existing studies on automated model training primarily focused on workflow- or harness-level optimizations, rather than internalizing the ability to conduct post-training into the model itself. Developing this capability requires executable model training environments that can produce high-quality trajectories demonstrating how to select data, train models, diagnose failures, and iteratively improve results. In this paper, we introduce RSI-Dojo, a collection of executable model training environments designed to teach LLM agents to conduct post-training. To construct RSI-Dojo, we develop RSI-Craft, an automatic pipeline that converts human research artifacts into executable model training environments. RSI-Craft automatically collects research papers from top venues, instantiates datasets and metrics into a unified interface, and reproduces evaluation dependencies. It then filters tasks by data size, execution reliability, and discriminability, yielding RSI-Dojo with 281 seed model training tasks. Building on RSI-Dojo, we employ a trajectory collection method with an improved harness to collect high-quality model-training trajectories from frontier models, then retain examples through rubric-based and outcome-based filtering. We fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on these trajectories. The resulting RSI-Dojo-9B and RSI-Dojo-35B-A3B improve over their base models by 8.74 and 16.87 PostTrainBench points, respectively. RSI-Dojo-35B-A3B reaches 29.95 on PostTrainBench and 53.29 on PostTrainBench-Lite, matching the performance of frontier models such as GLM-5.2 and GPT 5.5.

articles.title: Human-to-Robot Transfer via Bridging Representation and Action Space in VLAs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies provide a strong starting point for deployment, but adapting them to a target robot and environment still requires costly embodiment-specific demonstrations. Human demonstrations are far easier to collect, yet directly leveraging them is challenging due to the substantial human-robot embodiment gap, particularly when the underlying VLA has been pretrained primarily on robot data. We introduce H2RB (Human-To-Robot Bridge), a human-robot co-training framework for adapting pretrained VLA policies from unpaired human and robot demonstrations. H2RB bridges the embodiment gap at both interfaces: geometry-anchored alignment grounds human and robot observations in a compatible representation, while a decoupled-decoder tokenizer shares action latents without forcing both domains through a single action mapping. This design allows human demonstrations to provide useful behavioral supervision while retaining the rich visual, semantic, and control priors of the pretrained VLA. Across real-world tasks, H2RB substantially improves object transfer performance from 8.0 to 51.8 and enables skill transfer to score 62.7, in settings where co-train baselines totally fail to transfer human-demonstrated skills. The benefit also persists under object-placement shifts, improving out-of-distribution transfer from 6.0 to 45.3. H2RB suggests a way for human demonstrations to serve as a scalable supervision source for adapting pretrained robotic policies, reducing the dependence on costly target-robot data collection.

articles.title: Goal-Driven Autonomous Optical Experimentation via a Self-Recursive Hardware-Software Harness
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose goal-driven self-recursive optical research in which agents use physical evidence to revise the hardware, software, models, and protocols used to pursue a scientific goal. The framework can be instantiated with different stimulus systems and measurement devices. We formalize its updates and derive a relation between physical attainability, command access, and model approximation error. We demonstrate the concept in an optical see-through color-matching case study using an iPad, RayNeo X3 glasses, and a TOP 300 probe coupled to a CAS140D spectroradiometer, both from Instrument Systems. A revised glasses application adds USB-controlled RGB holds and frame acknowledgements, keeping model-generated colors displayed during spectral acquisition. The interface passes 12 live control checks. Spectral feedback reduces one target color difference from 19.756 to 1.211 ΔE₇₆^*; all five targets improve in a separate comparison. These measurements demonstrate the concept in one configuration. The resulting software and protocols remain available for subsequent investigations.

articles.title: Kierston & KierstonBench: Simulation of Allentown, PA and Evaluation of Language Models in Crime Investigation and Surveillance Tasks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04785v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are candidates for collecting and analyzing records in criminal investigations and mass surveillance. Their capability and accuracy in this work cannot currently be measured. Real deployments lack the ground truth needed to score a model's conclusions, and no benchmark evaluates these capabilities in a simulated environment. We present Kierston, a city-scale simulation engine, and KierstonBench, a benchmark that tests these capabilities against known simulated events. Kierston models approximately 125,000 residents of Allentown, Pennsylvania, generating their daily activities and the telecommunications, financial, administrative and license-plate records that surveillance and investigative systems collect about them. These records derive from a common behavioral timeline and are distributed across sources representing separate providers. Models investigate through a restricted records interface, linking observations across sources without access to the underlying simulation. The benchmark comprises 32 task families covering record linkage, routine reconstruction, incident investigation and assessment of deceptive accounts. In an evaluation of sixteen language models, most could not perform records investigation and submitted identifications the records did not support. A small number of frontier models solved most of the tasks and abstained when evidence was insufficient. In some cases these models still fell for common deceptions and assumptions, and none replaced an investigator.

articles.title: ScamWorld: An Interactive Environment for Evaluating Web Agents Against Online Fraud
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents increasingly browse, shop, and manage accounts on behalf of their users. Prior work has shown that they can be misled by adversarial content, including prompt injections and deceptive interfaces. Beyond such attacks, agents operating on the open web also encounter online fraud designed to deceive humans, including fraudulent online stores, fake investment platforms, and advance-fee schemes. How web agents respond to such fraud during task execution remains underexplored, in part because scam websites are short-lived, making systematic evaluation difficult. To address this gap, we introduce ScamWorld, an interactive environment that reconstructs reported scam websites across diverse scenarios, fraud mechanisms, and languages. Each reconstructed website reproduces documented fraud mechanisms, making relevant signs of fraud observable before the agent's final action and enabling controlled, repeatable evaluation. Through an extensive study of web agents powered by six frontier LLMs, we find that baseline deception rates range from 11% to 35% across models. Agents proceed more readily with payments than with requests for credentials or wallet information. A closer analysis of agent trajectories shows that some agents acknowledge suspicious conditions yet proceed, at times treating the user's instructions as authorisation to accept additional terms imposed by the website. ScamWorld provides a reusable testbed for systematically evaluating and stress-testing web agents against real-world online fraud.

articles.title: NepTTS-Bench: Native-Speaker Benchmarking and NepaliMOS for Nepali Text-to-Speech
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03718v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nepali TTS has reached a point where multiple systems are available, but there is no shared evaluation to compare them. NepTTS-Bench was created to address what existing automated and manual evaluation systems lack for Nepali TTS. A controlled benchmark with phonological grounding which contains 205 sentences (77 minimal pairs targeting aspiration, retroflex/dental contrasts, nasalization, gemination, and schwa deletion) which is rated by 180 speakers. There are 6,962 ratings for 10 TTS configurations and two human references. Along with this 7 ASR systems were evaluated for round-trip CER. SCOREQ was also run as an automated baseline. The key finding is that automated evaluation like SCOREQ prefers proprietary systems like ElevenLabs but native listeners prefer Piper. This is contributed by the fact that most of the systems not properly tuned for Nepali tend to show Hindi phonological behaviour and our minimal pairs are designed to surface such contrasts. We also present NepaliMOS predictor which is fine tuned on collected ratings. NepaliMOS achieves system-level rho = 0.90 on the dense panel but drops to utterance-level rho = 0.43 under leave-one-system-out evaluation. This is statistically significant and confirms that NepaliMOS captures genuine signal but cross-provider transfer is limited. A human calibration is recommended for new systems for which we release a Python evaluation package for practitioners to run the benchmark against new systems.

articles.title: RoboScope Kit: Unified Interfaces for Fast and Scalable Embodied-AI Evaluation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03850v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulation benchmarks are the standard way to compare robot policies, but each benchmark brings its own evaluator, observation layout, and action convention, and evaluation is slow: 500 RoboTwin Easy episodes with one simulator and one model on one GPU take 359.7 minutes. Profiling the official StarVLA evaluator shows that simulation occupies CPU cores while the GPU averages 14.3% utilization. RoboScope Kit wraps each model once in a Python class called a Policy, and each benchmark once in an adapter around the benchmark's own evaluator, so the benchmark's rules and scoring stay unchanged. Scheduling runs simulator workers and Policy replicas as separate pools, sizes both from measured probes, and shards work deterministically across GPU instances; runtime optimization renders only the observations an action-chunk Policy reads. Adapters cover six benchmark families. On LIBERO-Long with a StarVLA checkpoint on one 48 GiB RTX 4090, the concurrency search selects twelve simulator workers sharing three Policy replicas, which evaluate 500 episodes 4.45× faster than the official StarVLA evaluation with equivalent success rates, 2.78× faster than RLinf, and 1.52× faster than vla-eval at its tuned configuration. With CUDA MPS, which lets the replicas run their kernels concurrently, the search selects sixteen workers sharing four replicas, 6.16× faster than StarVLA, 3.85× faster than RLinf, and 2.10× faster than vla-eval. On RoboTwin Easy, four GPUs with chunk-boundary observation complete the 500 episodes in 14.4 minutes, 25.04× faster than the single-GPU baseline, with identical success outcomes and terminal steps.

articles.title: ProteoCraft: Protein Design as Proposal-Verification Search
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Protein-protein interactions underpin nearly all biological processes. Yet, designing proteins with desired interactions remains challenging due to the structural complexity governing molecular recognition. This study views protein design as a search optimization problem over a combinatorial sequence space under expensive structural evaluation. Toward this goal, we introduce a novel tree-based search framework, ProteoCraft, that employs approximate structural gradients from diffusion-based structure predictors as effective proposal policies to specify where the search should explore. Complete no-gradient inference of folding models separately assigns values to the resulting sequences, determining what is good. ProteoCraft allocates this verification budget through a coarse-to-fine paradigm: multi-site edits first explore distinct sequence basins, then verified promising states undergo strict single-site refinement. Across fourteen de novo binder-design settings spanning eight target proteins, five immune-relevant TCR-facing targets, and four localized CDR redesign tasks, ProteoCraft improves design quality and high-confidence yield. These improvements persist under independent AF2-IG and Rosetta-based interface evaluation. Prospective experimental validation further yielded an 82.9% binding hit rate for PD-L1 miniproteins, with a best measured KD of 0.879 nM, and confirmed binding of designed IFNAR2 VHH. Our code is available at https://github.com/smiles724/ProteoCraft_v1.

articles.title: CloakFEM: Agentic FEM Code Generation for Red-Teaming Computational Resource Exhaustion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04356v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Finite element method (FEM) solvers are foundational to scientific and engineering simulation, yet their susceptibility to emphefficiency attacks remains largely unexplored. An adversary can craft syntactically valid and runnable FEM programs that complete successfully while forcing excessive computational work, enabling computational denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. Finding such inputs is challenging because FEM programs occupy a vast, structured space constrained by numerical, geometric, and constitutive requirements. We introduce CloakFEM, a domain-guided LLM-agent framework for automatically generating runnable adversarial FEM programs that amplify solver computation. CloakFEM combines LLM-guided search with an FEM-specific intermediate representation and a deterministic validity gate that enforces runnable constraints. Across three FEM stacks, 17 problem classes, and 1,068 seeds, CloakFEM discovers adversarial inputs that substantially amplify solver work while remaining valid and solvable. In the most extreme case, solver iterations increase from 43 to 247,367, a (5,752.72×) amplification. CloakFEM outperforms five generic black-box baselines and retains an advantage over evolutionary search under a controlled bounded action space. Cross-solver analysis further reveals both problem-intrinsic and solver-specific sources of vulnerability. Our results uncover an underexplored efficiency-attack surface in FEM solvers and show that runnable FEM programs can serve as adversarial inputs.

articles.title: Understanding Backdoor Attacks in Scene Graph Generation via Global Context Pathway
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04379v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scene Graph Generation (SGG) produces structured scene representations, yet its training-time backdoor risk remains unexplored. Unlike classification, SGG exposes a pair-level attack surface that enables selective corruption of relations involving a designated object category. However, because SGG largely relies on localized evidence, globally placed triggers may face difficulty in manipulating such predictions. Recent SGG architectures increasingly incorporate global context to improve scene modeling, which may in turn facilitate such attacks. In this paper, we systematically study this backdoor risk and investigate the role of the global context pathway in backdoor behavior. Concretely, we first instantiate this attack with an effective method, and propose a three-axis evaluation protocol to characterize backdoor behavior. Experiments on Visual Genome with representative open-vocabulary and closed-set SGG models demonstrate the effectiveness of the attack. Mechanistic analyses reveal that the explicit global context pathway serves as a major carrier of the backdoor effect across the evaluated SGG models. In particular, replacing the poisoned global context representation with its clean counterpart during inference sharply suppresses the attack, yielding 100% and 97% reductions in attack success for the OvSGTR family and RelationFormer, respectively. Moreover, training-time interventions in the OvSGTR family show that suppressing trigger signals in this pathway either reduces attack success or substantially degrades utility. Together, these findings suggest that explicit global context designs may pose a backdoor risk in SGG architectures.

articles.title: τ-Rec-Books: A Disclosure-Controlled Benchmark for Requirement Elicitation in Agentic Recommender Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.04459v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While conversational recommendation systems provide a more natural user interface, they face the challenge of progressively discovering a user's needs before they can recommend an item that satisfies them. To evaluate the ability of AI agents at this elicitation process, we introduce τ-Rec-Books, a benchmark that holds each user request fixed while varying only when the user reveals their requirements: all at the start (volunteer), one at the start and the rest when asked (mixed), or some never (hidden). A hidden requirement can be found only by proposing books and inferring it from the user's accept or reject verdicts. We generate 450 tasks over a catalog of 20,000 books from Wikidata, develop a rule-based simulated user to answer the agent, and score recommendations against catalog metadata without an LLM judge. Across four agents and two search interfaces, success rates fall for every agent and interface, on average from 0.975 (volunteer) to 0.756 (mixed) and 0.283 (hidden). Mixed tasks fail mainly because agents do not ask, and when told to ask, every agent reaches at least 0.931. On hidden tasks, most failures come from agents recommending a book they never proposed to the user. When told to propose first, agents only match a simple baseline that proposes popular books, and stay well below one that uses rejection to rule out possible requirements. We release the catalog pipeline, task generator, simulated user, validators, reference agents, and all agent traces at https://github.com/nbharaths/tau-rec/tree/main/data/tracks/books-wikidata-v2.

articles.title: Comparison of phosphate adsorption on kaolinite, illite and montmorillonite by surface complexation modelling
articles.abstract: Kaolinite, montmorillonite, and illite are representative silicate minerals that play important roles in controlling the fate and mobility of phosphorus in soils. In this study, phosphate adsorption on these minerals was described using two surface complexation models, namely the Constant Capacitance Model (CCM) and the Triple Layer Model (TLM). The determination of surface site densities and surface complexation constants was evaluated and compared. Compared with the CCM, the TLM provided a better description of phosphate adsorption envelopes under different ionic strength conditions. In the TLM, the optimized equilibrium constants for the AlHPO₄⁻, SiOH₂⁺–PO₄³⁻, and AlPO₄²⁻ surface complexes were 24.53, 18.60, and 17.44 for kaolinite, 23.68, 17.83, and 17.56 for montmorillonite, and 23.09, 19.51, and 17.23 for illite, respectively. After normalization to mineral mass, the maximum phosphate adsorption capacities were 3.81×10− 6, 6.23×10− 6, and 1.88×10− 6 mol/g for kaolinite, montmorillonite, and illite at same initial concentration 8.40×10− 5 mol/L, respectively, indicating that montmorillonite exhibited the highest adsorption capacity, whereas kaolinite and illite reached approximately 61.1% and 30.1% of that of montmorillonite, respectively. ATR-FTIR spectra showed characteristic phosphate bands at 650, 960, 1027, and 1100 cm-1, corresponding to the ν₄, ν₁, and ν₃ vibrational modes of phosphate. The spectroscopic results indicated that phosphate was adsorbed in similar surface species on all three minerals. Adsorption-envelope similarity analysis revealed that kaolinite and illite exhibited more comparable phosphate adsorption behaviors, whereas montmorillonite showed distinctly different adsorption characteristics. These findings highlight the importance of identifying and quantifying clay mineral compositions in soils and contribute to the development of consistent and realistic protocols for modelling ion adsorption reactions on soil minerals and soils.

articles.title: Can Hydroxyapatite Micro-Parts Be Mass-Produced by Vat Photopolymerization? Geometry Is Necessary, But Not Sufficient
articles.abstract: Mass production of discrete, sub-millimetre hydroxyapatite parts — called for as shape-engineered reinforcement in composites — is undocumented for ceramic vat photopolymerization, well established at centimetre scale. We report the fabrication and post-processing of hydroxyapatite cubes (1 mm design) and tetrapods (0.876 × 0.767 × 0.656 mm). Green parts released spontaneously from the build foil after 72 h at 40°C, eliminating mechanical deplatforming with no measurable dimensional change. Co-sintering required no separation medium, with parts in mutual contact remaining free-flowing. Corner rounding of 23–34% was already present in the green state, identifying it as a printing artefact rather than a sintering effect. Most consequentially, two batches from the same feedstock, furnace and thermal schedule reached 94.9%TD (tetrapods) and 79.9%TD (cubes); the tetrapod value sits within the supplier’s own stated range for this material (94–97%TD) while the cube value sits clearly below it. X-ray diffraction excluded phase composition as an explanation, confirming single-phase hydroxyapatite. The tetrapod encloses 77 times less material than the cube; since binder removal is diffusion-limited, the cube requires of order 35 times the debinding time. An independent, geometry-dependent exposure artefact reported here confirms that at sub-millimetre scale, process parameters are geometry-specific rather than size-specific, and that the ratio of enclosed volume to free surface — not nominal part dimension — is the governing quantity. Geometry-matched parameters are therefore necessary for mass production at this scale, but not sufficient alone: throughput economics and the absence of batch-level quality control remain separate barriers.

articles.title: HV-Bus-Assisted Flyback Converter With Only One Additional Active Switch for Leakage- Energy Recycling and Full-Range Soft Switching
articles.abstract: This paper proposes an HV-bus-assisted flyback converter (HBAFC) for systems with a common-ground HVDC bus and battery. The HBAFC is supplied directly from the battery and, with only one auxiliary diode connected to the existing HVDC bus, can recycle transformer leakage energy and clamp the main-switch voltage. Replacing the diode with an actively controlled switch establishes the reverse current in the leakage inductance required for ZVS turn-on of the main switch over the full operating range. Since the HBAFC does not depend on the power stage or switching operation of the existing bidirectional converter between the HVDC bus and battery, it operates independently and supports modular expansion to different output voltage and power ratings. The operating principles, steady-state characteristics, device stresses, and ZVS condition are analyzed and discussed in detail. Three 200-W HBAFC modules with 12-, 24-, and 48-V outputs have been built and experimentally tested. The results confirm independent operation, leakage-energy recycling, and main-switch ZVS turn-on. In the active-switch version, the full-load efficiencies of the 12-, 24-, and 48-V modules are 89.6%, 94.2%, and 96.1%, respectively.

articles.title: Investigation into the removal of persistent organic pollutants from soil using infrared thermal desorption apparatus
articles.abstract: The rapid accumulation of electronic waste has led to severe soil contamination with persistent organic pollutants (POPs), particularly polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs), posing significant environmental and health risks. Consequently, this study developed and evaluated a vacuum-infrared thermal desorption system for the efficient remediation of POPs-contaminated soil. A comprehensive investigation was conducted to determine the critical operating factors governing the desorption process. The results identified temperature, pressure, and residence time as the dominant factors affecting POPs removal, whereas moisture content and particle size exhibited minimal influence. Furthermore, a second-order polynomial prediction model for POPs removal was established using response surface methodology based on a box-behnken design, achieving an R2 of 0.9921. It is noteworthy that the synergistic interaction between high temperature (400°C) and low pressure (100 Pa) significantly enhanced the contaminant removal rate of POPs to levels exceeding 90%. Moreover, an increase in heating rates substantially accelerated the removal of POPs independent of system pressure, progressing from a rapid initial spike to a subsequent phase of steady enhancement. Throughout this process, PBDEs consistently exhibited higher removal efficiencies than PCBs due to their lower thermal decomposition thresholds. In conclusion, these findings not only validate the feasibility of the integrated vacuum-infrared technology but also provide crucial theoretical guidance and technical support for the energy-efficient remediation of POPs-contaminated soil.

articles.title: Moment-Condition Contamination and Pseudo-True Values of Difference-GMM and System-GMM under Persistent AR(1) Measurement Error
articles.abstract: This paper studies Difference-GMM and System-GMM estimation of the autoregressive parameter of a dynamic panel when the dependent variable is observed with persistent AR(1) measurement error. Our contribution is a closed-form derivation of how the error contaminates the moment conditions of both estimators. For the lag-s lagged-level instrument of the differenced equation the contamination is (φ-1)(φ-ρ)φs⁻²σₑ², and for the lag-s lagged-difference instrument of the level equation it is (1-φ)(φ-ρ)φs⁻¹σₑ², where ρ is the autoregressive parameter and φ and σₑ² are the persistence and variance of the error. Both vanish when the error is exactly as persistent as the latent process, because the composite disturbance then collapses to serially uncorrelated noise, and, except at the shallowest lag, when the error is serially independent. We also derive the pseudo-true value of each estimator: for a single instrument it is a weighted average of ρ and φ, with the weight on φ equal to the noise share of the differenced variance at that instrument's lag. A Monte Carlo study shows that the derived expressions reproduce the simulated biases, that the bias does not vanish as the cross-section or the panel length grows, that the two estimators are biased by almost the same amount under classical error, and that dropping the shallowest instruments removes most of the classical-error bias but not the bias caused by persistent error.

articles.title: Technical Performance and Probabilistic Energy Yield Assessment of a 620 MWp Bifacial Grid-Connected Photovoltaic Power Plant in an Area Located in the Eastern Part of the Absheron Peninsula of Azerbaijan
articles.abstract: This study audits the energy balance, geometric inputs, performance indicators and exceedance-yield calculation of a 620 MWp DC / 477.5 MWac bifacial photovoltaic plant proposed for the eastern Absheron Peninsula. The source is a single PVsyst V8.0.12 simulation (VC1, 23 June 2025), rather than measured plant operation. Simulated first-year grid-injected energy is 886.81 GWh (1,430 kWh/kWp), with conventional PR of 89.95% and reported bifacial PR of 83.89%. Under an explicitly assumed normal distribution and illustrative 4.39% combined relative standard deviation, conditional P90 and P95 estimates are approximately 837.0 and 822.8 GWh. The review distinguishes active module width from shed width, tests the internal arithmetic of the exceedance estimates, and identifies the input evidence needed before the forecast can support investment decisions. Independent weather validation, manufacturer-specific uncertainty evidence and confirmation of as-built electrical design remain outstanding.

articles.title: Falls, fractures, lean mass and age with GLP-1receptor agonists and tirzepatide: meta-analysis of 162 placebo-controlled trials andage-subgroup data for adults aged 75 years orolder
articles.abstract: Background. Weight loss with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) and tirzepatide includes loss of lean mass, raising concern about falls and fractures in older adults. Whether harm increases with participant age, and whether benefit persists at 75 years or older, has not been examined systematically.Methods. We extracted serious adverse events coded as "Fall", any fracture, and hip/femur fracture from all placebo-controlled, parallel-group randomised trials of GLP-1 RAs or tirzepatide in adults (treatment ≥ 12 weeks) with results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov (searched 31 October 2026), and searched PubMed (1 November 2026) for placebo-controlled trials reporting lean mass by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Risk ratios (RR) and mean differences (MD) were pooled by random-effects models (REML, Hartung-Knapp), and effect modification by trial mean age was tested by meta-regression. Post hoc, we extracted results by participant age from FDA review documents and published subgroup analyses, and pooled placebo-controlled trials reporting 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) and bone-turnover markers.Results. In 162 trials (83,571 participants on GLP-1 RA or tirzepatide, 62,962 on placebo; trial mean ages up to 74 years), serious falls (k = 30; RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.77–1.07), any serious fracture (k = 76; RR 0.90, 0.80–1.01) and hip/femur fracture (k = 22; RR 1.04, 0.80–1.36) were not increased, and meta-regression showed no association with trial mean age (falls: RR per 10 years 0.92, 0.55–1.54; p = 0.75). Lean mass fell by 2.76 kg more than with placebo (9 trials, mean age 29–53 years; −3.78 to − 1.74), and by 4.12 kg in the four semaglutide or tirzepatide trials. Within SELECT (semaglutide 2.4 mg, n = 17,604), the fracture RR rose across age bands from 0.47 (0.25–0.91) at < 55 years to 1.30 (0.75–2.26) at ≥ 75 years (ratio per band 1.44, 1.11–1.87; p = 0.006); at ≥ 75 years, hip and pelvis fractures occurred in 17/703 vs 4/663 participants (RR 4.01, 1.36–11.85). At about 75 years or older (subgroups ≥ 70 to ≥ 75 years) in type 2 diabetes, HbA1c was lowered by 0.6–0.7 percentage points and the pooled hazard ratio for major adverse cardiovascular events was 0.80 (0.61–1.06); any serious adverse event was not more frequent with treatment in SELECT, LEADER or STEP-HFpEF. 6MWD improved by 15.2 m (8.6–21.9; k = 6). No placebo-controlled trial reported grip strength, gait speed or the Short Physical Performance Battery.Conclusions. Across trials, GLP-1 RAs and tirzepatide reduced lean mass without increasing serious falls or fractures, with no evidence that trial mean age modified this. Within the largest trial, however, the fracture RR increased with participant age, and hip and pelvis fractures were more frequent with semaglutide at 75 years or older. In adults with type 2 diabetes aged about 75 years or older, HbA1c is lowered and cardiovascular estimates point in the same direction as in younger adults without reaching significance. Trials in this age group that measure efficacy together with fat mass, lean mass, muscle strength, physical function and fractures are needed.

articles.title: Decoupled geogenic and faecal hazards in shallow coastal groundwater: evidence and a screening framework from the lower Indus Delta, Pakistan
articles.abstract: Shallow hand pumps supply drinking water to millions of people in low-lying deltas worldwide, where groundwater is exposed to geogenic salinisation and faecal contamination. Because these hazards are usually assessed together, it remains unclear whether they share a pathway and, therefore, which interventions are needed. In the lower Indus Delta (Pakistan), we analysed 93 hand pumps for 16 physicochemical variables, total coliforms and Escherichia coli, and combined hydrochemical diagnostics, a seawater mixing index (SMI), multivariate statistics, entropy-weighted and weighted-arithmetic water quality indices (EWQI, WA-WQI) and deterministic and Monte Carlo health-risk models. TDS exceeded 1000 mg/L in 58.1% of wells. A single salinity factor (65.9% of variance) integrated evaporation, cation exchange (slope −0.95, R² = 0.97) and limited marine mixing (SMI > 1 in 23.7%). E. coli occurred in 23.7% of wells, was independent of salinity (OR = 0.83, p = 0.81), was predicted only by turbidity (OR = 4.18 per log₁₀ NTU; AUC = 0.82) and, unlike salinity, was not spatially clustered, indicating wellhead ingress. WA-WQI assigned 66% of its weight to F⁻ and turbidity and agreed poorly with EWQI (weighted κ = 0.20). Child hazard index exceeded 1 with 46.1% probability, driven by F⁻, and drinking water supplied up to 122% of the WHO daily sodium limit. A well-by-well typology showed that only 26.9% of wells were safe, 8.6% needed only wellhead repair and 64.6% required treatment or a new source. The framework uses only routine monitoring data and is transferable to other salinising coastal deltas.

articles.title: Boosting Multifunctional Composites Thermal Conductivity via Nanometallic Interfacial Low-Frequency Phonon Resonance
articles.abstract: Modulation of inter-filler heat transfer governs the overall heat-dissipation performance of thermally conductive composites for electronics. Unlike covalent/non-covalent bond interfaces constructed using organic modifiers and inorganic secondary fillers, nanometallic bond-free interfacial structures built under mild conditions also promote interfacial thermal conduction while delivering multifunctionality. However, the related interfacial heat transfer behaviors and enhancement mechanisms remain poorly understood. Herein, guided by density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations, we demonstrate that introducing conductive TCNQ at the graphene (Gra)-silver (Ag) interface strengthens low-frequency phonon (LFP) resonance via the resulting electron-phonon coupling (EPC) effect. Electron transfer between TCNQ and Ag optimizes the EPC effect, further activating LFP resonance across Gra and Ag surfaces to facilitate phonon transport between Gra layers. To corroborate these predictions, polybenzoxazole (PBO) nanofibers (PNFs)-based composites (GTAgx/PNFs) with TCNQ-modified graphene nanosheets (GNS)/Ag nanowires (AgNWs) composite fillers are fabricated via pressure-driven self-assembly. GTAg30/PNFs exhibits an in-plane thermal conductivity of 28.8 W m‑1 K‑1 and EMI shielding effectiveness of 61.0 dB, alongside outstanding Joule heating and mechanical properties. Validated by practical cooling tests on operating electronic devices and mitigation of vehicle heat-soaking injury, this simulation-assisted low thermal resistance interface design offers a promising route toward developing high-performance multifunctional thermal management materials.

articles.title: Inducible Nitric Oxide Synthase (NOS2) is Required for Oligodendrocyte Lineage Progression and Remyelination in Murine β-Coronavirus-Induced Neuroinflammation
articles.abstract: Background Multiple sclerosis (MS) and post-viral demyelinating encephalomyelitis are characterized by chronic central nervous system (CNS) inflammation, myelin sheath destruction, and impaired tissue repair. While inducible nitric oxide synthase (NOS2) is traditionally viewed as a cytotoxic mediator in acute neuroinflammation, its temporal role, from myelin loss to the long-term endogenous remyelination phase, has remained controversial and poorly defined. Using a murine β-coronavirus (MHV-RSA59) model of neuroinflammation, we investigated the requirement for NOS2 during the myelin loss and repair phase (days 30 to 60 post-infection).Method Age-matched C57BL/6 wild-type (WT) and NOS2-/-mice were intracranially inoculated with 10,000 PFU of RSA59. Animals were euthanized at defined time points (day 30 and day 60 post-infection) to harvest the tissue samples. Luxal Fast Blue (LFB) staining, immunofluorescence (IF), immunoblotting, immunohistochemistry, and flow cytometry were performed on the RSA59-infected brain and spinal cord samples of NOS2-/- and WT mice.Results Our recent findings revealed that NOS2-/- mice, compared to WT mice, showed persistent demyelinating plaques, reduced myelin restoration, as indicated by the expression of myelin-forming proteins, and a diminution of oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) and mature oligodendrocytes during the remyelination phase. This delayed regenerative process in the absence of NOS2 was associated with prolonged activation of CNS-resident microglia and an infiltrated myeloid cell population, which may lead to a dysregulated inflammatory environment in the CNS. Mechanistically, loss of NOS2 led to more phagocytic activity in CNS-resident microglia and infiltrating myeloid cells. Our findings establish that NOS2-derived signals are essential for clearing inflammatory debris and transitioning myeloid cells from a pro-inflammatory state toward a pro-regenerative phenotype, thereby creating a permissive microenvironment for myelin repair.Conclusion This study elucidates how NOS2 regulates the balance between pathological damage and tissue repair. Also, our current research highlights NOS2 not merely as a marker of inflammation, but as a crucial protective factor required for effective myelin regeneration in virus-induced neuroinflammatory demyelination.

articles.title: Episodic atmospheric transport reshapes cross-administrative methane attribution from Shanxi coal basins to Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei
articles.abstract: Methane mitigation is planned within administrative boundaries, but atmospheric transport redistributes methane across jurisdictions. Here we show that the methane-column response to Shanxi coal-mine emissions over the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei megacity region is episodically amplified, while a key terrain gate is persistently undersampled by TROPOMI. A 4.5-year TROPOMI record, supported by independent Xianghe TCCON observations, demonstrates that the associated atmospheric organization and receptor relationships recur significantly beyond the originally simulated summer, including after excluding the entire 2022 calendar year. Controlled WRF-GHG experiments show that observation-constrained refinement of the Shanxi inventory increases mean downwind methane column mass by 15.2×103 tons relative to EDGAR, equivalent to 5.1% of the monthly regional emission benchmark (EBE), and that this response is amplified 3.36-fold under strong southwesterly flow. Valid TROPOMI retrievals cover only 0.13% of the gate-grid days, versus 8.6% regionally, with matched methane-carbon monoxide diagnostics linking the deficit to terrain-dependent screening. These findings reframe cross-boundary methane attribution as an episode resolved source-gate-receptor problem, linking source representation, atmospheric state, and observational coverage. Effective verification therefore requires coordinated source, pathway and receptor observations across the coupled airshed.

articles.title: Correlated timing errors and terrain dependent uncertainty in synthetic slope microseismic localisation
articles.abstract: Surface microseismic arrays can support monitoring of subsurface fracture activity, but increasing receiver density does not necessarily improve the reliability of reported locations. We present a reproducible synthetic benchmark that evaluates terrain coordinates, velocity calibration and timing correlation together. Six surface geometries share a 34.5 m horizontal envelope, with 16–576 receivers assigned to four timing groups. An independently implemented two-layer ray solver generates arrivals for 200 paired test events; a separate set of 12 known sources calibrates layer velocities. Generalised least squares is compared with diagonal weighting, homogeneous propagation and flattened receiver coordinates. At 64 receivers and a 0.15 ms array-shared clock standard deviation, covariance-aware inversion gives 90th-percentile location errors of 0.78–0.82 m and empirical 95% ellipsoid coverage of 96.5–97.5%. Diagonal weighting gives errors of 2.06–2.12 m and coverage of 33.0–34.5%. With 576 receivers, diagonal coverage falls to 3.5–4.0%, whereas propagating calibration uncertainty improves covariance-aware coverage to 94.0–96.0%. Additional waveform tests use unknown event times, noise-only detection calibration and automatic arrival picking. These tests expose sensitivity to coherent transients and reference contamination. A weak lateral slowness anomaly also produces severe undercoverage despite modest location errors. The results identify conditional accuracy and uncertainty-calibration requirements for slope-array design, without establishing field performance or an early-warning threshold.

articles.title: Warming and iron steepen ocean particle spectra without enhancing carbon export
articles.abstract: Particle size structure sets how much of the carbon fixed at the ocean surface reaches depth. Two communities disagree about the sign of that link. Size-resolved ecosystem models expect steeper spectra — proportionally more small particles — to raise the export efficiency of primary production. We assemble 8,479 global UVP5 particle size-spectrum profiles (137 cruises, 75°S–81°N), co-locate them with Bio-ORACLE v3 environmental layers and match them to three global particle-export compilations and monthly satellite primary-production fields. Warming steepens the mesoplankton spectrum (−0.28 per SD of sea-surface temperature, P = 1.4 × 10−8, 56% of the shared variance). Iron-rich waters are steeper too (−0.21 per SD, P = 0.0013). Oxygen contributes no independent effect. The iron axis replicates against in situ GEOTRACES measurements. Against the model prediction, steeper spectra track lower export in two independent tests: e-ratio rebuilt on satellite NPP (+0.073 per SD, n = 6,539, P = 2.5 × 10−5) and POC/²³⁴Th ratios (+0.065 per SD, n = 3,680, P = 1.1 × 10−19). The signal the models describe is real, and it peaks in the micro-particle segment. Projected to the 2050s under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5, the median POC/²³⁴Th change is +1.9%, with declines beyond 15% in 14% of grid cells, concentrated in the North Atlantic subpolar gyre. The observational side of the dispute wins. Warming does not lower export everywhere. It lowers it in identifiable places, and those places can be mapped.

articles.title: Lewis acidity-triggered active reconstruction sustains industrial-scale CO2-to-Formate conversion beyond 1500 h
articles.abstract: The electrochemical upgrading of CO2 remains hindered by its unsatisfied durability to meet industrial requests, which is in part due to the passive reconstruction of catalyst during dynamic operation. Prior research primarily focuses on suppressing such reconstruction with modest improvement in durability. Herein, we innovatively propose an active reconstruction (AR) strategy that employs Lewis acid, as a seed, to trigger rapid reconstruction, thereby enabling on-demand reconfiguration into dynamically stable rich-low-coordination sites through in-situ regeneration of defect sites for industrial-scale CO2-to-formate electrolysis. Combined experimental and theoretical results reveal a linear-like tailoring relationship between Lewis acidity and reconstruction kinetics, allowing precise control of unsaturated-coordinated sites to achieve high activity and enhancing the metal-oxygen bond order to improve intrinsic stability, which applies to various catalysts. Meanwhile, low-coordinated sites also optimize the interfacial H2O/CO2 microenvironment via enhancing *CO2·- intermediates adsorption and regulating 2H (2-coordinated Hydrogen-bonded) interfacial water ratio. The optimized AR-ITO (active-reconstruction In1.8Sn0.2O3/In9Sn) catalyst delivers a high FEformate of 91% at 1 A cm-2 and achieves an unprecedented durability of up to 1500 h at 300 mA cm-2 (1.5 A) with the maintained FEformate of 92% in MEA electrolyzer. Our findings highlight the superiority of a controlled activated reconstruction strategy for industrial CO2RR applications.

articles.title: Novel Observing Strategies Testbed: A Lightweight, Collaborative Platform for Prototyping Earth Observing Missions
articles.abstract: Distributed space mission concept development increasingly relies on collaborative, software-based testbeds, yet established distributed simulation standards and mission-operations frameworks impose overhead disproportionate to early-stage prototyping. Operating the first version of the Novel Observing Strategies Testbed exposed five systemic limitations---identity and authorization, reliable and persistent messaging, session resilience, schema governance, and coordinated scenario time control---that hindered long-duration, multi-institutional use. We evolved the testbed across two further versions to address them: Version 2 hardened the identity, messaging, session, and schema layers, and Version 3 added coordinated scenario time control through programmatic freeze, resume, and time-scale orchestration, while keeping the platform lightweight, cloud-native, and standards-aligned. Two independent Snow Observing Strategy campaigns, spanning 577 scenario days and closing the loop with an external land-surface model, validated the evolved architecture at technology readiness level 6. The campaigns delivered zero message loss, automated session recovery, sub-second coordinated freezes, and event-driven resume that eliminated idle waiting, and they coordinated a multi-sensor observation-selection workflow toward improving snow water equivalent estimation. The testbed thereby offers an accessible, standards-aligned platform for evaluating novel observing strategies before costly development, generalizable well beyond the snow domain.

articles.title: Fire disturbance drives depth-dependent soil organic carbon loss and recovery in a cold temperate forest: interactions with land-use transitions and stand structure
articles.abstract: Background Wildfire is a primary disturbance controlling soil organic carbon density (SOCD) in cold temperate forests. However, depth-dependent fire effects are rarely evaluated together with land-use transitions and forest stand structure within a single process framework, limiting fire–carbon management in northern forests.Methods In Yakeshi City, western Greater Khingan Mountains, China, we integrated fire records (2000–2023), multi-temporal land use/cover data, 91 soil profiles (0–100 cm), remote-sensing stand classification, and plot surveys. Fire intensity × recovery-time effects were tested using two-way ANOVA. Carbon-loss rates were compared across fire intensities and frequencies. Land-use transition effects on 0–30 cm SOCD and stand-structure controls were quantified using ANOVA and generalized linear models (GLMs).Results Fire was the strongest near-surface carbon-loss process. Fire intensity, recovery time, and their interaction significantly affected stratified SOCD (P < 0.05). Severe fires caused the largest losses, mainly in 0–40 cm soils. One year after fire, 0–100 cm SOCD declined by approximately 27.5%; after 5 and 10 years it recovered to approximately 87.2% and 94.9% of pre-fire levels, yet severe-burn sites remained approximately 8.7% below unburned references after a decade. Single-fire 0–100 cm loss rates ranged from 13.8% to 41.3% and increased with intensity; sites burned ≥ 3 times lost approximately 35.7%. Forest-to-cropland, forest-to-grassland, and forest-to-unused-land transitions reduced 0–30 cm SOCD by 34.8%, 22.7%, and 17.4%, whereas cropland-to-forest conversion increased SOCD by 12.8%. Larix gmelinii had the highest 0–100 cm SOCD (4.21 kg m⁻²), followed by Pinus sylvestris var. mongolica (3.83 kg m⁻²). GLMs showed that dominant species, stand density, and canopy closure significantly regulated SOCD; a 10% increase in canopy closure was associated with + 1.09 kg m⁻² in 0–100 cm SOCD.Conclusions In this cold temperate forest landscape, fire attributes shape the depth and persistence of SOCD loss and recovery, while land-use transitions and stand structure modify carbon baselines and within-forest retention. Reducing high-severity short-interval reburns, limiting forest conversion, and maintaining structurally stable coniferous stands are process-consistent priorities for soil carbon conservation, within the constraints of the chronosequence sample.

articles.abstract: Author(s): Sang-Wook Cheong, Lei Han, and Fei-Ting Huang Kinetomagnetism describes magnetization, or related pseudovector responses, induced by linear momentum k or symmetry-equivalent external stimuli.
