Over a window of about one large-eddy turnover time, the UNet and the transformer reach relative velocity errors of 0.018 to 0.053 and keep the current sheets, the enstrophy, the current density and the energy spectra of the simulation; which of the two is the more accurate depends on the Reynolds number, the UNet leading at 3000 and 6000 and the transformer at 1000. Applied with the same backbones and training procedure to two public benchmarks, the models reach the lowest error reported to date on the isotropic turbulence set of FactFormer, 39% below the best published model. On the compressible MHD set of The Well, their rollout errors are a third to a half below those of the best of The Well's baselines. They also match a 1.3 B-parameter pretrained foundation model in its rollout windows, with 20-62 times fewer parameters. The code, the configuration of every model, the evaluation scripts and the data generator with the seed of every simulation will be released upon publication.

articles.title: InformedXRD: Reproducible Benchmarks and Physics-Informed Evaluation for Powder Diffraction Symmetry Classification
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning for powder diffraction (PXRD) symmetry classification is being trained at scale, yet the field lacks a common evaluation standard: papers report results on different subsets of experimental archives, with different target taxonomies, preprocessing, and metrics, and published models are rarely released in a form that permits rescoring. We present InformedXRD, an evaluation framework with three parts: (i) a machine-readable mapping from 230 space groups to 99 extinction groups, the finest classes powder diffraction can identify from systematic absences alone; (ii) a benchmark-construction method whose inclusion rules are specified as code and reproduce from a frozen snapshot, instantiated as RRUFF-473, RRUFF-325, and, as a small example, opXRD-98; (iii) a reporting protocol with prior-only frequency baselines, a label-permutation test, a hierarchy-aware error metric on the condensed translationengleiche subgroup graph, and stratified evaluation. We build on the mapping, RRUFF benchmarks, subgroup graph, and four ViT checkpoints released in our earlier work (Baggett et al., 2026). Using these checkpoints, a 1D residual CNN, and six architectures trained under the XRDBench recipe (Cao et al., 2025), we show that evaluation design changes what conclusions are justified: paired tests point in different directions at Top-1 and Top-5; paired Top-k tests do not separate the three leading XRDBench models, while hierarchy-aware analysis describes error distance and direction across all six; an input-blind frequency predictor matches the models on aggregate Top-k, yet a label-permutation test still detects pattern-specific evidence; and stratified analysis exposes a label-entropy confound that aggregate accuracy hides. All mapping tables, benchmark code, scripts, and checkpoints are released as shared infrastructure for PXRD-ML evaluation.

articles.title: Sonny-ENS: demystifying machine-learning ensemble weather forecasting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every weather forecast is uncertain, and decisions from flood warnings to energy trading depend on how well that uncertainty is quantified. Machine-learning (ML) ensembles now quantify it better than the best physics-based ensemble, yet two things about them remain opaque: whether their skill requires hundreds to thousands of accelerator-days of training, and how a network with a simple source of randomness produces a spread that follows the flow. Here we introduce Sonny-ENS, an ensemble of three 68.9-million-parameter networks with Monte Carlo dropout, trained on the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in 2.7 A40 GPU-days. On 2022, it has a lower CRPS than the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts ensemble (ENS) on 96% of 570 targets and an 8.3% lower mean CRPS at lead times of 1-10 days. It outperforms the operational GenCast on 69% of the targets, and a 51-member, 15-day forecast takes 69 s on one GPU. Ablations identify the ingredients of this skill, and a Kolmogorov-Arnold sparse autoencoder shows that dropout injects uncertainty mainly in the tropics, whereas the spread grows where the atmosphere is baroclinically unstable (spatial correlation 0.91 with the Eady growth rate). Skillful probabilistic weather forecasts are therefore within reach of a single GPU server.

articles.title: Physics-Informed One-Step Generation on Long-short flow maps
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-informed generative models should produce samples that are both data-aligned and physically valid, yet existing methods are often iterative and too slow for practical use. Achieving this with a one-step flow-map model is difficult because both data-distribution and physics-constraint learning are enforced only indirectly through surrogate objectives, making their joint learning fragile for long-range flow maps. We propose Physics-Informed Long-Short Flow Maps with Direct Guidance (LSFM-DG), which makes direct target computation feasible by decomposing one-step generation into a long flow map for global evolution and a near-terminal short flow map with computable closed-form solutions and physics potentials. As the short flow map shrinks to zero, it provides both direct distributional and physical targets for learning the long flow map. This yields a unified one-step flow-map model that removes Jensen's gap, improves training stability, and achieves stronger data fidelity and physical consistency without distillation.

articles.title: Wave Physics as Representation: Tensor-Structured Neural Reconstruction for Ocean Acoustic Fields
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reconstructing three-dimensional (3D) complex ocean acoustic fields from sparse measurements is challenging due to highly oscillatory wave structures and restricted sensing patterns/routes. Learning-based approaches fall into two categories. First, purely data-driven models can learn complex field patterns, but do not explicitly exploit wave physics that may enhance interpretability and reduce training costs. Second, physics-informed methods impose a specified physical equation as a reconstruction constraint, but often require environment-dependent parameters that are difficult to acquire. As a result, practical 3D acoustic field reconstruction that is both physically grounded and robust to uncertain environmental information remains largely unexplored. This work takes an alternative route: instead of solving a fully specified wave equation, it extracts a structured representation from wave physics and learns its components from data. From the Helmholtz equation and normal mode propagation, we derive a structured spatial-angular tensor representation, termed the S/c representation. Under a low-rank specialization, it takes the form of a rank-(L,L,1) block-term tensor decomposition, which connects structured sampling patterns/routes used in ocean sensing to sufficient conditions for field recovery. Building on this tensor representation, we propose TIDAL, a neural reconstructor that uses the S/c representation as an inductive bias for structured decoding and aligns information aggregation with the sampling geometry. The neural learner removes the need for known model parameters required by conventional physics-based recovery methods. Experiments across three structured sampling geometries show that TIDAL achieves the best reconstruction performance and fastest inference among baselines, with benefits from the physics-derived representation under limited data and model capacity.

articles.title: A sensor-driven physics-informed neural network for real-time occupant-centric space heating control
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional space heating systems typically rely on single or sparse fixed-point temperature measurements, overlooking non-uniform indoor temperature distributions, transient thermal dynamics, and occupant-specific comfort requirements. This study explores an occupant-centric control strategy that aims to maintain the desired temperature around the occupant location. Spatially and temporally varying temperature fields, together with occupant mobility, make real-time local temperature estimation challenging. To address this challenge, we propose a control-oriented Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) model for indoor temperature-field prediction. Conventional PINNs rely on explicit time inputs and assume consistent temporal patterns across samples, which limits adaptability under variable initial conditions and heating sequences. The proposed model infers temporal dynamics implicitly from spatial coordinates and limited sensor measurements, improving robustness to changes in initial conditions and external disturbances. The method was validated across nine horizontal sensing planes in three controlled room-scale configurations. Against a validated COMSOL Multiphysics simulation, the PINN predicted the evaluated temperature fields with a maximum relative error below 1.85% across validation cases. These predictions supported an occupant-centric space heating control scheme. Compared with COMSOL-based offline control, the PINN-based system achieved an average prediction error of around 0.67%, and its rapid inference supports real-time occupant-centric control implementation. This work represents a move away from reliance on fixed-point temperature measurements in space heating control to an occupant-centric control strategy informed by real-time environmental feedback.

articles.title: Robust EEG-based Emotion Recognition from Coarse Trial-level Labels under Intra-trial Affective Variability
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01731v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: EEG-based emotion recognition has become an active research area in brain-computer interfaces. However, fine-grained affective annotation is costly, so most datasets provide only a global label for each long EEG trial. For practical emotion recognition, trials are commonly divided into short temporal windows, with the global label propagated to all windows for training. This practice treats trial-level emotion as temporally uniform, although affective responses may fluctuate within a trial. Consequently, windows that weakly reflect or deviate from the global emotional state may receive unreliable labels, posing a key challenge to robust EEG-based emotion recognition. To address this challenge, we propose VARY, a variability-aware robust learning framework for EEG-based emotion recognition from coarse trial-level labels. VARY incorporates a Two-stage Sample Selection (TSS) strategy to identify EEG windows with reliable emotional labels, and introduces MixAug, a data augmentation method tailored for EEG to improve model robustness under limited and unreliable supervision. We comprehensively evaluate VARY under the setting of label-noise learning on two public datasets, using three network architectures and multiple label-noise settings. Our method demonstrates superior performance, achieving a maximum accuracy gain of 11.54% on the DREAMER dataset and 5.39% on the SEED dataset compared with the best-performing baseline, highlighting the effectiveness of VARY in learning from unreliable trial-level labels under intra-trial affective variability.

articles.title: ReCoG: Relative Node Contexts for Multi-Domain Graph Pre-training
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The success of foundation models in language and vision has motivated Graph Foundation Models (GFMs), which learn transferable knowledge through multi-domain graph pre-training. Existing methods advance GFMs through feature unification and structural learning, and in doing so they rely on the raw graph structure to organize node contexts. However, we observe that removing a large proportion of edges from source graphs during pre-training improves cross-domain transfer accuracy across four representative methods. Our theoretical analysis identifies the raw graph structure as a source of conflict in cross-graph model sharing. We therefore advocate defining node contexts using criteria consistent across graphs. Achieving this requires (1) constructing node contexts consistently across graphs without a shared positional structure, such as the token order of text or the pixel grid of images, and (2) retaining the structural and neighborhood information of the original graphs. To this end, we introduce Relative Contexts for Graphs (ReCoG) for multi-domain graph pre-training. Specifically, we first construct attribute contexts to provide a comparison rule independent of the raw graph structure. Furthermore, we construct structural contexts based on common neighbors and semantic contexts based on neighborhood attribute summaries to retain the topological and neighborhood information of the original graphs. Since all graphs share these construction rules, we pre-train a single graph encoder by reconstructing node attributes over these contexts, without domain-specific modules. We conduct extensive experiments on 18 target datasets, which demonstrate the effectiveness of ReCoG. In particular, ReCoG exceeds the strongest baseline by 7.61 percentage points in mean 1-shot cross-domain node classification accuracy and by 4.47 points in cross-type transfer to heterophilous graphs.

articles.title: Fragility Is Not Reducible to Hardness: Conditional Causal Difficulty for LLMs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models show large and seemingly arbitrary performance drops when a task is rewritten in ways that leave its requirements untouched. We recast task difficulty as a causal quantity: the treatment effect of meaning-preserving perturbations on a model. A meaning-preserving rewrite can only be observed to hurt a task the model can already solve, so we place the estimand on the principal stratum where the degradation occurs: the conditional causal difficulty (CCD), the probability that a randomly drawn twin breaks a solvable task. Because harder tasks tend to be more phrasing-sensitive, complexity enters as an effect modifier rather than a confounder, and we residualize it out to obtain complexity-residualized difficulty (CRD); zero for a task exactly as fragile as its complexity predicts, positive for anomalously fragile ones. Current benchmarks do not supply the data CCD requires, so we introduce GlassGSM and GlassMATH, augmenting GSM8K and MATH with twins built from perturbation families, raising fragility on GlassGSM by approx 12× over GSM-IC-style distractors on the same problems (3.7%→44.9%) while keeping the answer key unchanged. Our predictor Frail learns the per-perturbation break probability and reaches 0.613±0.023 of the suite reliability ceiling on GlassGSM and 0.557±0.023 on GlassMATH, against 0.171/0.401 for a surface-feature baseline and 0.444/0.463 for supervised baselines such as VAP3, and, at a 5% curation budget on GlassGSM, doubles random recall of fragile items, matching an oracle ranking. Additionally, cross-fitted residualization leaves CRD uncorrelated with the declared proxy in practice. Code is available at https://github.com/upwork/Conditional_Causal_Difficulty_for_LLMs

articles.title: Large Geometry Models Are Priors For Fast Physics Pretraining
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language and vision models became data-efficient by pretraining on plentiful unlabelled data; physical field models have such data, over ten million 3D shapes, but geometry pretraining designs its targets rather than deriving them from the physics. Euler-Lagrange geometry pretraining derives them: for attached flow, a shape enters the flow's Euler-Lagrange equation only through coefficients that distance and normal line (the normal up to sign) fix to first order. Their reconstruction error therefore bounds what a representation loses about any field, and fine-tuning on costly simulations need only assemble the global field. We realise it in AREALS, a masked surface autoencoder whose areal tokens carry position, normal and area, pretrained self-supervised and sign-free on 61,822 raw meshes. Because the operating condition enters only through the far field, sensors can supply it: AREALS completes a hidden field in one forward pass without condition labels. It matches the accuracy of the same architecture trained from scratch with half the simulations on DrivAerML and DrivAerNet++ and about a quarter on WindsorML. On DoubleDelta wings, 20 sensors give 3.9× and 4.0× lower field and force error than GABI, a Bayesian inversion method with a learned prior, and beyond the training angles pretraining halves the error.

articles.title: HQNN-CL: Regime-Aware Hybrid Quantum Neural Network with Continual Learning for Financial Forecasting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Financial time-series forecasting is still difficult owing to the non-stationary nature of the market, regime changes, and catastrophic forgetting, which makes conventional deep learning models hard to adapt in the long term. To achieve uncertainty-aware robust financial forecasting in the face of changing market conditions, this study proposes a Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network with Continual Learning (HQNN-CL). The proposed framework combines Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM) based regime detection, BiLSTM temporal encoding, adaptive-depth parameterized quantum circuits, Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), experience replay, and probabilistic forecasting in a single architecture. The framework was tested on four real-time stock datasets: Microsoft, Systems Limited, Teradata and Tata Consultancy Services, and compared with seven state-of-the-art forecasting models, including recurrent and Transformer-based models. The experimental results show that HQNN-CL has outperformed other methods on the Systems Limited (RMSE = 3.0149) and Teradata (RMSE = 0.8909) datasets and is within 0.32% and 0.40% of the best baseline method for Microsoft and Tata Consultancy Services, respectively. The proposed framework also generates well-calibrated probabilistic forecasts within the range of 89.5% to 96.5% empirical coverage rate, has zero catastrophic forgetting (BWT = 0.0000) for all sequential learning tasks, and consistently shows positive forward transfer. Ablation and statistical significance analyses also validate the performance of adaptive quantum feature learning and continual adaptation under heterogeneous market conditions, regime-wise.

articles.title: Mesh2Shell Neural Operator for Inverse Shape Optimization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-driven design seeks high-performing geometries, which need not conform to a learned shape category. Parametric and latent-space approaches facilitate surrogate-based optimization, but restrict deformations to prescribed shape families or learned decoders. We introduce the Mesh-to-Shell Neural Operator (M2S-NO) as the mesh-to-shell component of a category-agnostic inverse shape optimization framework. We separate the explicit mesh used for design from the volumetric representation used for physics prediction. M2S-NO maps oriented surface samples to a surface-centered shell representation, such as TruncatedSDF or HeatSDF. A separate problem-specific PDE neural operator (PDE-NO) maps this representation to physical fields. Objective gradients update mesh vertices through both operators, without a latent shape decoder. Preconditioning and remeshing support free-form deformation, while fixed interfaces are controlled directly on the mesh. Optional shell-space proposals enable topology changes. We evaluate geometric matching, jet-engine brackets, and neutron moderators, with independent FEM and OpenMC evaluation. Relative to the best training designs, M2S-NO reduces maximum bracket displacement by 14.3% and increases neutron-sensor current by 13.8%. Optimization also succeeds from an out-of-distribution bracket initialization, demonstrating the framework's geometric flexibility.

articles.title: Beyond Unit-Circle Eigenvalues: Invariant Bases for Stable State Space Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diagonal state space models process long sequences at linear cost, yet the same transition is applied at every step of a rollout, so an unconstrained recurrence holds no quantity fixed and the state decays or grows without bound. Current designs constrain one quantity, and preserving one does not guarantee preservation of the others, so a model can hold its norm to machine precision while momentum drifts by hundreds of percent. We claim that the conserved quantities of a diagonal recurrence are layered, that each layer requires a strictly stronger condition on the operator, and that a unit-modulus spectrum reaches only the outermost. Acting on the claim, we enforce the conditions required for every layer by construction. The generator of the Kronecker-Cayley transition (KC) is a graph Laplacian over object subspaces, H=Lotimes Iₘ, advanced by a Cayley transform, and the step stays diagonal at O(N³+N²m) cost. The conserved set is exactly a 2m²-dimensional family of quadratic forms, held at every parameter value, so the quantities and the dynamics the construction reaches are fixed before training. On four conservation benchmarks, KC holds total mass at or near the reference floor while every diagonal baseline loses it by orders of magnitude. We further compare against mass correction and find that two correctors fail once the underlying prediction diverges, which shows that assembly rather than correction is necessary for a guarantee that holds across the rollout. A free modal basis trained under a conservation penalty conserves only by freezing its spectrum, whereas the assembled operator conserves with every mode but one free to rotate. Beyond these benchmarks, KC holds the linear momentum of three N-body systems and, at the operator level, the conserved quantity in molecular dynamics, chemical kinetics, pharmacokinetics and power-grid swing dynamics.

articles.title: Adaptive Optimizers Can Get a Policy Ranking Wrong: Momentum, Dependent Data, and a Two-Run Remedy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operators choosing among decision rules, such as when a battery charges or where an idle taxi goes, rank them by estimated long-run value. A standard estimator, linear temporal-difference (TD) learning, fits values from one stream of correlated observations. Large fits often use an adaptive optimizer, such as adaptive moment estimation (Adam), with fixed averaging rates. We show that these rates can change what is estimated, not just how fast: the same observations drive the updates and the optimizer's step-size scaling, moving the fit away from the intended TD value. The shift differs across rules, so it need not cancel in a comparison, and more data only makes a wrong ranking look more certain. Our remedy refits the same data at a second averaging rate that halves the effective gain, the number to which the leading shift is proportional. Twice the new fit minus the original removes that shift. In New York taxi and battery models calibrated to real data, common optimizer settings leave the selected rule unchanged but order close rules wrongly and misstate its value. Our remedy corrects nearly every wrong ordering, with one extra fit when the shift is moderate and two when it is larger.

articles.title: Mutual Information Estimation via Triangular Transport Maps: Finite Sample Guarantees and Sample Allocation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00471v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study finite sample guarantees for transport based mutual information estimation. Mutual information can be estimated by first learning the conditional and marginal densities and then evaluating their log-density ratio by Monte Carlo. Given training samples, we use triangular transport maps to learn these densities and then compute the mutual information estimate on an independent batch of evaluation samples. For conditional density estimation using triangular transport maps, we establish non-asymptotic guarantees over realizable Hölder classes by viewing the conditional density as an ordinary density with respect to the product of the law of the conditioning variable and Lebesgue measure. This allows standard density estimation techniques to be applied directly to the conditional density estimation. These results yield finite sample guarantees for the resulting mutual information estimator and characterize how a fixed sample budget should be allocated between training and evaluation in order to minimize the mean squared error. Numerical experiments support the predicted training and evaluation error rates and illustrate the resulting sample allocation tradeoff.

articles.title: Conditioning Gaussian Processes on Almost Anything
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.21041v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gaussian processes (GPs) offer a principled probabilistic model over functions, but exact inference is restricted to the linear-Gaussian regime. We establish an explicit equivalence between GPs and a class of linear diffusion models, recasting predictive sampling as an ODE with closed-form Gaussian dynamics and a likelihood-dependent guidance term that admits a simple Monte Carlo approximation. In the linear-Gaussian setting, we recover standard GP conditioning exactly; beyond conjugacy, the same machinery handles any conditioning statement admitting point-wise likelihood evaluation - including non-linear physics, and, for the first time, natural language via large language models. Whitening isolates the irreducible non-Gaussian dynamics, minimising Wasserstein-2 transport cost and eliminating numerical stiffness. The result is a general-purpose GP inference scheme requiring no bespoke derivations. Together, these results provide a general mechanism for incorporating the full richness of real-world knowledge as conditioning information, opening a new frontier for the probabilistic modelling of real-world problems.

articles.title: Statistical Machine Learning for Astronomy -- A Textbook
articles.abstract: arXiv:2506.12230v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This textbook gives a systematic treatment of statistical machine learning for astronomical research, based on Bayesian inference. It shows how modern data analysis techniques connect to classical statistical methods and follow from familiar statistical principles. The Bayesian perspective, used throughout, gives priority to uncertainty quantification and statistical rigor, which scientific inference in astronomy needs. The textbook progresses from probability theory and Bayesian inference through supervised learning, including linear regression with measurement uncertainties, logistic regression and classification. Unsupervised learning topics cover Principal Component Analysis and clustering methods. We then introduce sampling and Markov Chain Monte Carlo, followed by Gaussian Processes as probabilistic nonparametric methods and neural networks in the broader statistical context. Our theory-focused approach derives each method from first principles with complete mathematical development and then shows its astronomical applications. We put statistical insight first and explain why algorithms work, when they are appropriate, and how they connect to broader statistical principles. From a solid grounding in classical methods and their theory, the treatment leads to modern techniques such as neural networks. With this grounding, readers can apply the methods to astronomical research with proper attention to assumptions, limits and uncertainty propagation, as large astronomical surveys require. The 22 companion tutorials apply the methods to astronomical data in Jupyter notebooks.

articles.title: Efficient NPN Classification for Large Functions using Graph Neural Network
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two Boolean functions are considered NPN equivalent if one can be transformed into the other by negating inputs, permuting inputs, or negating the output. Efficient NPN classification is valuable in fields such as logic synthesis, quantum computing, and information theory. However, exact NPN classification demands exhaustive enumeration of all possible input permutations and negations. Its complexity grows exponentially, making it impractical for larger functions with more inputs. In this paper, we introduce the first learning-based formulation for NPN classification by recasting it as NPN action prediction. Our method represents Boolean functions as AND-Inverter Graphs (AIGs) and applies a bidirectional heterogeneous graph neural network to predict input negations, output negation, and input permutations. To mitigate the non-canonicity of logic networks, we further introduce graph rewriting techniques that reduce structural ambiguity and recover useful symmetries before prediction. Experimental results show that NPN action prediction is learnable, that the resulting canonicalization quality improves over heuristic baselines, and that on practical benchmarks our method approaches exact methods on tractable cases while scaling to functions with up to 16 inputs.

articles.title: TopoQuant: Topological Framework to Characterize Behavioral Shifts in Quantized Large Language Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00631v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces the com putational cost of large language models (LLMs), but it can introduce internal structural and behavioral changes that are not captured by traditional metrics such as accuracy and per plexity. We present TopoQuant, a topological framework that uses topological data analysis (TDA) to quantify structural drift in self-attention weights and relate it to behavioral changes in quantized LLMs. Across four LLM families and multiple quantization levels, we show that topological drift remains stable at moderate compression levels but increases sharply below 4 bit precision, closely tracking declines in attention agreement. Our results reveal a strong relationship between topological drift and attention agreement, indicating that structural changes in model parameters closely reflect behavioral degradation under quantization. We further demonstrate that topological features can accurately predict attention consistency using lightweight machine learning models, achieving R2 scores of up to 0.85. Predicting attention agreement enables efficient assessment of be havioral consistency in quantized LLMs, allowing quantization induced degradation to be detected without running expensive downstream tasks. The results indicate that topological drift pro vides an efficient early-warning signal for quantization-induced degradation and can help identify safe compression limits without extensive downstream evaluation.

articles.title: Evidence-grounded large language models guide perovskite solar cell design and optimization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00633v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using large language models to interpret experimental evidence, design discriminating experiments and formulate well-supported mechanistic explanations remains a central challenge in materials research. Here we establish PSM-Bench, an 800-question benchmark developed by perovskite researchers to evaluate scientific reasoning in perovskite photovoltaics. We also introduce OpenPerov, an expert-informed language-model framework that learns from expert-calibrated evidence records reconstructed from 4,532 articles; these records link experimental strategies, controls and observations to mechanistic interpretations. Structured-evidence adaptation outperformed conventional question-answer training, and OpenPerov Flash ranked first among 13 closed-book systems. OpenPerov Pro raised Scientific Mastery further, from 87.6 to 89.1, by revising selected passages with retrieved evidence. On questions derived from subsequent studies, both models also outscored expert-authored answers. In an experimental test of self-assembled monolayer design, OpenPerov selected a K analogue that outperformed the Na analogue preferred by experts. Devices incorporating the selected contact reached a power conversion efficiency of 27.05% and retained 96.74% of their steady-state reference efficiency after 1,000 h of dark thermal ageing at 85 ^circC. These results show that reconstructed scientific reasoning provides an effective basis for building domain models that interpret experiments and inform materials design.

articles.title: Geometric Morphology Learning: Empowering Foundation Models from Structure to Spacetime Intelligence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geometry is the very form that connects space, time, and matter, serving as the fundamental fabric of the physical world, from continuous fields to discrete structures. Despite its importance, deep learning is inherently blind to geometry. Riemannian geometry stands as a well-established mathematical foundation for studying geometry, yet it remains largely incompatible with deep learning architectures. To bridge this gap, we establish a new learning framework--Geometric Morphology Learning--that learns geometric or topological structures, shapes or conformations for representation learning, reasoning and action modeling. Moving beyond early attempts limited to specific geometric priors, this theory centers on modeling the intrinsic geometry of objects and learning from such geometric or topological knowledge. Specifically, we construct a neural bundle, a unified scaffolding linking local and global structures, and formulate differentiable operators, including connection and curvature, thereby enabling the study of geometry with advanced geometric concepts such as holonomy and cohomology. Consequently, Geometric Morphology Learning opens new horizons in foundation models, reasoning and planning, graph modeling, physical simulation, PDE systems, and dynamics, marking a fundamental shift toward instilling systematic geometry in artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent decisions depend on empirical relationships that deployment observations reveal and task descriptions alone may leave unresolved. We introduce Decoupled Predictive Decision Making (DPDM), an architecture that formulates heterogeneous agent decisions as conditional prediction with a shared pretrained learner. Language models provide semantic representations of current and historical records, while a general-purpose conditional predictor predicts task-defined targets from the represented evidence. Pretraining supplies reusable inference capability; deployment evidence instantiates problem-specific predictions without updating either model's neural parameters. Tool judgments, candidate preferences, and reasoning assessments share an evidence-and-query interface, with predictions mapped to choices by a decision rule. This architecture establishes complementary sources of agent capability: semantic knowledge acquired through language pretraining and empirical inference acquired through structured-data pretraining. A single frozen LimiX-2 predictor serves all five task categories. With Qwen3.5-27B as the semantic encoder, DPDM raises mean accuracy across 50 benchmarks from 78.80% with few-shot prompting to 84.92% under their respective evaluated history budgets, and reaches 82.33% with identical histories and queries. On ToolPRMBench's BFCL and ToolSandbox tasks, absolute accuracy gains are 34.26% and 28.87%, respectively, at the methods' respective evaluated history budgets. Accuracy improves as history grows. With identical imbalanced histories, mean balanced accuracy improves by an absolute 14.51% across five reasoning-step assessment tasks and four encoders. DPDM makes learning from experience an independently improvable foundation-model capability, creating a shared route for advances in conditional prediction to improve decisions across agent tasks.

articles.title: Reap: Uncovering Monte Carlo proof search with a lightweight model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Reap, an open framework for learning and analyzing formal proof search in Lean4. Reap implements policy-value-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search directly in Lean, sharing proof-state transitions, AND-OR search, and replay verification between inference and training rollouts. Structured action logs expose how neural predictions and tactic execution interact during search. Using this framework, we train Reaper-1, a 1.7B-parameter policy-value model, through continued pre-training, supervised tactic learning, and iterative search-based reinforcement learning. Using a separate premise selector, the final system solves 79.9% of miniF2F-test at pass@32, establishing state-of-the-art performance among open provers of comparable size while remaining competitive with substantially larger models. Beyond improved solve rates, our results suggest that RL strengthens the prover's ability to organize proofs around useful intermediate results, favoring substantial advances over repeated local adjustments. This more directed proof construction is accompanied by increasingly elaborate tactic programs: fewer explicit search decisions are needed, while more work is performed within each decision. The resulting trade-off between search effort and tactic execution cost provides insight into how learning changes the prover's problem-solving strategy.

articles.title: DRL-Based Adaptive Routing for Energy-Efficient and Reliable Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks
articles.abstract: The amount of energy lost in underwater wireless sensor networks is greatly influenced by the choice of relay: a node that is frequently chosen might end up with an empty battery, and a weak acoustic link can cause retransmissions to be needed. Routing has to take into account both the conservation of relay energy and the need to make progress, ensure timely forwarding, and keep a viable next node available. The present study focuses on developing an Adaptive Routing method based on Deep Reinforcement Learning for energy efficient and reliable Underwater Wireless Sensor Networks. Prior to carrying out each transmission, the current node deletes from consideration any of its neighbors, that have insufficient residual energy, poor link quality, or fail to make any positive contribution to depth advancement towards the surface sink. The DRL policy then assesses the remaining possible relays according to their residual energy, SNR, depth advancement, forwarding delay, and void risk. Feedback on delivery updates the action values, and both link failures and voids are penalized. Testing in NS-3, using Aqua-Sim included nine baseline protocols and five different deployment scenarios. In a number of repeated trials involving 100 nodes each, the proposed approach obtained a mean PDR of 93.26%, a mean residual energy of 87.732%, and a mean delay of 0.982 s. ADRP-DQL achieved a PDR of 85.70% and a delay of 1.162 s, while Dynamic DRL maintained 81.029% residual energy. The proposed method was able to keep the network running for 662.6 rounds, as opposed to 625 rounds for Dynamic DRL. When adaptive reward balancing was not used, the network lifetime dropped to 560 rounds.

articles.title: Exemption Without Exposure: Formally Verified Conditional Privacy-Preserving Authentication with Secure-Ranging Binding for Authorised Armed Carriers in AI Weapon Surveillance
articles.abstract: Automated weapon detectors treat every visible firearm as a threat, yet plain-clothes soldiers, police officers and licensed guards lawfully carry weapons on the roads where kidnappers operate. Exempting them keeps false alarms manageable, but an exemption is also an attack surface: a stolen, relayed or wrongly attributed credential can silence an alert about a genuine threat. This paper presents conditional privacy-preserving authentication (CPPA) for authorised armed carriers in artificial intelligence surveillance. Carriers present short-lived pseudonymous role credentials through a challenge-response exchange, so the verifier learns a role but not an identity, while an oversight authority can resolve a pseudonym only under lawful order. Ultra-wideband secure ranging binds the credential to the vehicle the camera flagged, and a three-outcome policy ensures that no weapon detection is silently discarded. The protocol is verified in the Tamarin prover: unforgeability, injective agreement, identity secrecy and unlinkability hold, and weakening any of four design elements yields an attack. A reference implementation verifies a 225-byte presentation in a median of 253,unboldmathupmus on one 2.1~GHz virtual processor. Monte Carlo simulation shows a binding error of unboldmath6.7×10⁻⁴ for side-by-side vehicles with 0.1~m ranging and 0.5~m camera localisation, against 0.08 with 1~m ranging and localisation. In a representative scenario, binding lowers the probability that a threat is silently exempted from 0.21 to the credential compromise rate of 0.01. A closed-form analysis of multi-agent threat verification shows that half of its accuracy gain is lost once agent errors correlate at about 0.4.

articles.title: Site Response Characterization Investigation of Kathmandu Valley by HVSR Ambient Noise Analysis
articles.abstract: Microtremor measurements for the seismic microzonation of the Kathmandu Valley were conducted at 75 stations spread across a 500 m × 500 m grid in the current study. The amplification factor (Ap) and predominant frequency (Fp) of the surface soils are estimated using the Horizontal-to-Vertical Spectral Ratio (HVSR) approach. The findings indicate that Fp ranges from 0.7 to 5.45 Hz and Ap spans from 1.0 to 6.2 Hz throughout the valley. Higher frequencies are found on the basin borders and in the southern regions where shallower stiff deposits predominate, whereas lower frequencies are found in the northern regions with thick lacustrine sediments. The soil classification revealed 1.3% very soft, 24% soft, and 74.67% stiff soils based on the fp. Bhaktapur (B-21) and Lalitpur (L-24), two highly populated locations with a fragile building stock, were found to have significant amplification sites, suggesting a high potential for soil-structure resonance. The stable zones below 1.5 Hz showed low amplification, while Bhaktapur (4.39 Hz) and Lalitpur (5.45 Hz) showed the highest amplification, suggesting potential liquefaction or slope instability risks that need to be verified by geotechnical data and shear-wave velocity profiling. By facilitating neighborhood-level hazard assessments and offering helpful data to architects, engineers, and urban planners, the 500 m grid spacing greatly increased the microzonation resolution. Despite its limitations, such as the inability to completely quantify soil dynamics, the absence of two or three-dimensional basin modeling, and ambient noise interference, the HVSR approach is a reasonable starting point for valley-wide microzonation. To validate risk zones and improve engineering applications for seismic hazard assessment and catastrophe mitigation, future research should include these findings with MASW surveys, borehole Vs30 data, and numerical basin response models. The findings show that macro-scale danger maps often oversimplify the highly varied soil in the Kathmandu Valley.

articles.title: Predictive Equilibrium–Flux Framework for Zn(II) Extraction and Stripping with Cyanex 272
articles.abstract: The design and scale-up of hydrometallurgical solvent extraction circuits require quantitative understanding of both equilibrium partitioning and intrinsic stripping kinetics. Although Zn(II) extraction by Cyanex 272 (bis(2,4,4-trimethylpentyl)phosphinic acid) is well documented, hydrodynamics-independent kinetic descriptions of stripping remain unavailable. This work addresses this gap by developing a predictive equilibrium–flux framework for the Zn(II)/Cyanex 272/kerosene/H2SO4 system. Equilibrium studies confirm a cation-exchange mechanism (Zn²⁺ + 2HA ⇌ ZnA2 + 2H⁺) with second-order pH dependence and exothermic thermodynamics (ΔH = −6.9 to −21.4 kJ mol⁻¹). Sulfuric acid achieves >95% stripping efficiency at ≥0.50 M. The core contribution is the first quantitative flux-based kinetic analysis using the single-drop technique, yielding first-order dependence on [H⁺] and [Zn]org, positive sulfate order (0.4), and negative half-order inhibition by free extractant ([H₂A₂]⁻⁰·⁵). The apparent activation energy Eₐ = 41.1 kJ mol⁻¹ and activation entropy ΔS‡ = −85 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (first report) confirm reaction-influenced interfacial control with an associative mechanism. The integrated design equation Fb = k.[Zn]¹·⁰org.[H⁺]¹·⁰.[SO₄²⁻]⁰·⁴.[H₂A₂]⁻⁰·⁵.e (−Eₐ/RT), with k = 3.34 × 10⁻⁷ kmol m⁻² s⁻¹ and R² = 0.986 (n = 32). The model is validated by leave-one-out cross-validation (R² = 0.978, error = 7.2%) and independent literature data (error = 8.3%). Dimensionless analysis yields Da = 0.42 and Ha = 0.68, confirming a mixed reaction–diffusion regime. Sobol sensitivity analysis identifies [H⁺] as dominant (Si = 0.42), while Monte Carlo simulation quantifies prediction uncertainty at ±10.8%. A proof-of-concept Random Forest model achieved a testing R² of 0.981 and MAPE of 5.8%, with feature importance confirming [H⁺] dominance (0.86). Techno-economic analysis for a 50,000 t/year plant yields an IRR of 28.5% and a payback period of 2.3 years, with 15–20% lower H2SO4 consumption. Life cycle assessment demonstrates a 42% reduction in global warming potential. The validated framework enables direct scale-up to industrial circuits, delivering 0.5–1.5 million annual savings.

articles.title: Transpolar Drift and Atlantic inflow shape microbial biogeography and metabolic processes across the central Arctic Ocean
articles.abstract: The Arctic Ocean is changing rapidly. Sea-ice loss, advancing Atlantification and terrigenous inputs create contrasting ecoregions, yet their underlying microbial processes remain unresolved. Here, we combine high-resolution oceanographic observations and multi-omics data from the North Pole to the Svalbard shelf to determine how the shift from terrigenous influence to Atlantic-dominated waters shapes microbial biogeography, community assembly and metabolic processes. We demonstrate distinct, lifestyle-specific differences in microbial communities across four hydrographic regimes, with particle-attached communities showing a predominantly stochastic distribution while free-living communities were more regime-dependent. In the terrigenous-influenced Amundsen Basin, particle-attached microbial communities drive degradation of recalcitrant terrigenous organic matter with enrichment in denitrification, suggesting potential net nitrogen loss. Moving into Atlantic-dominated waters in the Nansen Basin during late summer, free-living communities increasingly rely on mixotrophic scavenging, trace gas oxidation and marine organic matter cycling as waters become progressively more nutrient-depleted. Surface-driven photoheterotrophy prevails in the warmest, ice-free waters. Comparative genomics across the Arctic Ocean further demonstrates highly connected yet regionally adapted microbial communities governed by these distinct hydrographic regimes. These results offer a mechanistic view of how microbial metabolic processes may restructure as the region becomes seasonally ice-free, Atlantification intensifies, and terrigenous inputs increase, thereby reshaping biogeochemical cycling across the Arctic Ocean.

articles.title: Sensor placement study for estimation of Reynolds number in flow past a circular cylinder using an Inverse Physics-Informed Neural Network
articles.abstract: Determining an unknown flow parameter from a limited number of experimental measurement data is an essential requirement for many engineering problems. Inverse physics-informed neural network (I-PINN) provide a mesh-free way unlike the usual adjoint- or conjugategradient-based methods by adding the unknown parameter as a trainable one along with other weights of the neural network during the training phase. In this paper, we study the effective sensor placement for a flow past a circular cylinder to recover the Reynolds number (𝑅𝑒) of the flow. We consider five zones in the flow independently and try to recover the 𝑅𝑒 from synthetic data obtained from the validated forward PINN. In the first of three sweeps, the near-, mid-, and far-wake zones recover 𝑅𝑒 to within 9.9–21.6% error whereas the shear-layer zone stays in a tighter 28.2–31.7% error band. The upstream zone which samples the near uniform free stream values comes out to be the ineffective almost every time at 46.3–54.1%. The two repeat sweeps shift these errors, but the wake zones stay the most accurate in all three. We also see that more sensors do not translate into better accuracy in any zone, which implies that sensor location matters more than sensor count for recovering 𝑅𝑒.

articles.title: Bioaccessibility and Toxicity of Particle-Bound Metals and Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons: Sources, Respiratory Fate, Mechanisms, and Risk Assessment
articles.abstract: Particulate matter (PM) mass is widely used to estimate health risk, yet particles with similar mass concentrations can produce very different biological effects. Toxicity depends on source, size, atmospheric aging, chemical speciation, and the mixture of compounds carried on particle surfaces. This critical narrative review examines particle-bound metals and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), following their pathway from respiratory deposition and bioaccessibility to oxidative stress and toxicity. Metal release varies with element, source, particle size, extraction conditions, and solid-to-liquid ratio, while acidic lysosomal environments often increase dissolution compared with near-neutral extracellular fluids. PAH release is shaped by hydrophobicity, binding to soot, surfactants, proteins, and changes in the respiratory environment during inflammation. Once released, or when particles are taken up by cells, these constituents may contribute to oxidative stress, antioxidant depletion, inflammation, genotoxicity, and vascular injury. Poorly soluble particles can still remain biologically active even when only a small fraction of their chemical content is released. Interactions between metals and organic compounds may be synergistic or antagonistic, further complicating interpretation of complex PM mixtures. Differences in simulated lung fluids, dosimetry, speciation, and biological validation also limit comparisons across studies. We therefore propose a tiered framework integrating PM mass, source, size, speciation, compartment-specific bioaccessibility, oxidative potential, and delivered-dose toxicology. Bioaccessibility should complement, rather than replace, whole-particle testing. Greater consistency and attention to real-world mixtures may improve source prioritization and health-risk interpretation.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Prediction and Optimization of Methylene Blue Adsorption onto Albizia lebbeck Bio-adsorbent Using Ensemble Machine Learning
articles.abstract: This study investigates the adsorption of methylene blue (MB)from aqueous solution using a bio-adsorbent prepared from Albizialebbeck pods and evaluates the predictive performance of ensemble machine learning models for modeling the adsorption process. The bio-adsorbent was characterized using pH PZC , Fourier Transform Infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray Diffraction (XRD),and Scanning Electron Microscopy with Energy Dispersive Spectroscopy (SEM–EDS). Characterization revealed a porous, carbon-rich, predominantly amorphous structure with abundant oxygen-containing functional groups favourable for dye adsorption. The effects of solution pH, contact time, adsorbent dosage, and initial dye concentration were systematically investigated through batch adsorption experiments. Equilibrium and kinetic data were analysed using Langmuir, Freundlich, and Temkin isotherm models, as well as pseudo-first-order, pseudo-second-order, and intraparticle diffusion kinetic models. The Langmuir isotherm provided the best equilibrium fit, yielding a maximum monolayer adsorptioncapacityof424.24mgg − 1 , while the pseudo-second-order model best described the adsorption kinetics. Furthermore, ensemble machine learning models—Random Forest (RF) and eXtreme Gradient Boosting(XGBoost)—were developed and optimized to predict adsorption performance. The optimized RF model achieved an R 2 value of 0.98876 for MB removal efficiency, while XGBoost attained an R 2 of0.99953 for adsorption capacity prediction. These findings demonstrate that Albizia lebbeck bio-adsorbent is a highly efficient, eco-friendly material for MB removal, and that ensemble learning provides a robust and accurate framework for predicting and optimizing adsorption processes in wastewater treatment.

articles.title: Generation of Supertoroidal Pulses with Controlled Topologies
articles.abstract: Toroidal electromagnetic excitations have been recognized as the third fundamental excitations besides classic electric and magnetic dipoles, offering great promise for next-generation information carriers. However, a big step ahead blocking the practical implementation remains the deterministic generation and control of the full family from toroidal to supertoroidal pulses with tailored topological orders. Here, we experimentally demonstrate supertoroidal pulse generation by both passive and active spatiotemporal metasurfaces. We also observe and manipulate their nontrivial properties—including fractal-like singularities, deep-subwavelength skyrmions, nondiffracting propagation, and space–time superoscillations—which were previously predicted but unrealized. These findings complete a missing chapter of supertoroidal electrodynamics and open immediate horizons for ultra-capacity robust communications and exotic light-matter interactions.

articles.title: Generative design for additive manufacturing through data-free optimization-derived neural weight subspaces
articles.abstract: Generative design (GD) enables exploration of diverse shape variants that exhibit trade-offs among competing design objectives related to part manufacturability and performance, offering a transformational approach towards automated part design for advanced additive manufacturing (AM). However, existing GD methods often derive design diversity either from large datasets of existing designs or through topological modifications, limiting their applicability to data-scarce engineering problems, particularly for complex parts where manufacturability and preservation of topology and geometric features are critical. In this work, we present a training-free generative design framework that leverages the optimisation trajectory of a single neural field-based shape optimisation to represent and explore neural field variants within a low-dimensional neural weight subspace. Our design space exploration is realised through a Langevin diffusion-inspired stochastic process with energy-conditioned guidance, enabling the generation of constraint-satisfying shape variants that provide distinct objective trade-offs. The framework generalises across geometrically and topologically diverse complex parts, including freeform geometries with intricate surface features and non-trivial topology. We validate the method through simulations and physical additive manufacturing experiments, demonstrating support-free 3D printing of the generated shape variants and establishing a data-free route towards manufacturability-aware generative design for complex parts.

articles.title: Polypropylene imine dendrimer/carbon nanotube as an impressive adsorbent for cadmium, copper and lead elimination from wastewater: Isotherms, kinetics and thermodynamic
articles.abstract: Herein, highly ordered and branched polymeric polypropylene imine dendrimer-carbon nanotube-composite (denoted as PPI/MWCNT) was synthesized and characterized using XPS, FTIR, RAMAN, SEM, TEM, TGA, and Zeta potential analyses. The synthesized nanocomposite was used to eliminate Cd2+, Cu2+, and Pb2+ from industrial effluent. The efficacies of pH, adsorbate concentration, time, and dosage in the removal process were assayed. Optimum conditions for the elimination efficiencies of Cd2+, Cu2+, and Pb2+ were dosage: 0.06 g/L; adsorbate concentration: 100 mg/L; and adsorption time: 20 min, and pH: 7). The utmost adsorption capacities of Cd2+, Cu2+, and Pb2+ were 1620, 1590, and 1460 mg/g, respectively, which are fitted with the isotherm and kinetic equilibrium data to the Langmuir model and the pseudo-second-order, respectively. Desorption of the Cd2+, Cu2+, and Pb2+ ions from the surface of PPI/MWCNT was best carried out with removal efficiency of 84%, 87%, and 92%. Therefore, PPI/MWCNT possesses a considerable capacity for eliminating metal ions from industrial wastewater and reusability after the desorption step.

articles.title: Estimating cotton leaf area index under shallow subsurface drip irrigation using TabPFN and UAV-based multisource remote sensing
articles.abstract: Leaf area index (LAI) is a key indicator of cotton canopy development and crop water status, yet its accurate estimation under shallow subsurface drip irrigation in arid regions remains challenging because spatial variability in soil moisture and salinity increases canopy heterogeneity. This study integrated UAV-based hyperspectral and RGB imagery with Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) to estimate cotton LAI under small-sample conditions. Spectral vegetation indices, colour indices, and texture features were extracted, and stable predictors were selected using recursive feature elimination with cross-validation. Stage-specific models for the squaring, flowering, boll-development, and boll-opening stages were developed from hyperspectral, RGB, and fused feature sets. TabPFN was compared with XGBoost, random forest, and support vector regression, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) quantified feature contributions. Across the 12 growth-stage–feature-set combinations, TabPFN performed best overall (mean R² = 0.781 ± 0.190). Multisource fusion was strongly stage dependent: relative to the best-performing single-source feature set, fusion increased R² by 1.2%, 7.1%, and 12.2% at squaring, flowering, and boll development, respectively, but performed slightly worse than hyperspectral features at boll opening. SHAP revealed clear stage-specific shifts in feature importance: texture dominated at squaring, photochemical indices were most influential at flowering and boll opening, and pigment-related and structural features jointly contributed at boll development. Field-scale LAI maps generated with the optimal models revealed pronounced spatial differences among irrigation treatments. Combining TabPFN with UAV-based multisource remote sensing can provide accurate and interpretable cotton LAI estimates under small-sample conditions, thereby supporting crop monitoring and precision irrigation in arid regions.

articles.title: Physics-Informed Explainable Machine Learning for Tight Sandstone Facies Prediction from Conventional Well Logs: A Blind-Well Comparative Study Krishna-Godavari Basin, INDIA
articles.abstract: Background Conventional hydrocarbon exploration worldwide with India as not exceptional is increasingly finding smaller, deeper and more marginal accumulations, the transition from "find another conventional field" to target "productivity from tight reservoirs" could become one of the most important exploration-development strategies over the next decade along with deepwater exploration. Tight sandstone reservoirs commonly exhibit complex lithological and petrophysical characteristics and require stimulation for production. Reliable identification of tight sandstone facies from conventional well logs is challenging. Although machine-learning techniques have increasingly been applied to automated lithofacies classification, most of the studies rely on random sample-wise validation, which may overestimate predictive performance because adjacent well-log samples are highly correlated. Furthermore, the incremental value of physically derived petrophysical, petro-elastic and geo-mechanical attributes over conventional log measurements remains insufficiently quantified. Objective This study develops an explainable machine-learning framework for four-class lithofacies classification of deep-seated syn-rift sediments of KG Basin comprising primarily Shale, Siltstone, Clean Sandstone and Tight Sandstone—and investigates whether computed petrophysical and petro-elastic attributes improve tight sandstone discrimination along with identification of zones which would require stimulation and well-to-well generalization. Methodology Three wells with interpreted lithofacies are used for model development and blind-well validation, while two additional wells are reserved for independent prediction. Three principal feature configurations are evaluated: (i) conventional well logs and (ii) conventional logs augmented with computed petrophysical, petro-elastic and geomechanicalattributes. Random Forest, Catboost, LGBM and XGBoost classifiers are evaluated using reciprocal well-wise validation with same prediction parameters. (iii) Model performance is assessed using accuracy, balanced accuracy, macro-F1 and class-specific precision, recall and F1 scores, with particular emphasis on Tight Sandstone classification. SHAP-based explainable AI is employed to identify the dominant geological and elastic attributes controlling model predictions. Prediction probabilities and model disagreement are used to characterize uncertainty. Expected contribution The study establishes whether physics-informed feature engineering provides measurable improvement in blind-well lithofacies prediction and determines which conventional and derived properties contribute most strongly to Tight Sandstone identification. The resulting workflow provides an interpretable framework for extending facies interpretation into wells lacking direct lithofacies information. Results The study shows that ensembles of machine-learning classifiers can accurately classify Shale, Siltstone, Clean Sandstone, and Tight Sandstone from conventional well logs, with physics-informed petro-elastic attributes significantly improving accuracy. Overall, using extended attributes increased mean accuracy by 14–16% and mean ROC-AUC by approximately 9% and resulted in ΔF1 of 0.1869 (30.86% improvement and 95% bootstrap CI: 0.1766–0.1966). For Tight Sandstone, the Random Forest classifier achieved a precision of 0.979, a recall of 0.996, and an F1-score of 0.987. The study used SHAP analysis to identify physically informed petrophysical and elastic attributes that contributed to the model’s predictions and used prediction probabilities and model agreement/disagreement to highlight uncertainty. The study recommends applying the well-log–petro-elastic–explainable ML framework for analyzing tight-sandstone deposits and using blind-well validation to assess the method’s transferability and avoid overestimated performance metrics.

articles.title: Participant Overlap and Apparent Accuracy in Behavioral Depression Classification
articles.abstract: Background Behavioral machine-learning studies can include several observations from each participant. When observations from the same person appear in both training and evaluation data, a classifier may recognize participant-specific characteristics instead of learning relationships that generalize to new people.Objective To quantify how participant overlap affects apparent classification accuracy under controlled conditions with and without a class-related signal.Methods Six simulation scenarios combined three levels of participant-specific variation with two levels of class-related signal. Each scenario contained 100 Monte Carlo replicates, each comprising 60 simulated participants, 10 observations per participant, and 10 features. A one-nearest-neighbor classifier was evaluated using five-fold record-wise and participant-wise cross-validation. Both approaches used 480 training observations and 120 evaluation observations per fold. Outcomes were pooled out-of-fold accuracy, the paired accuracy difference between evaluation approaches, and the frequency with which the record-wise classifier selected a neighbor from the same participant.Results Without class-related signal, increasing participant-specific variation raised mean record-wise accuracy from 49.88% to 94.81%. Corresponding participant-wise accuracy ranged from 49.90% to 51.27%. At the strongest participant-specific variation, the mean accuracy difference was 43.54 percentage points, with a Monte Carlo standard error of 0.41 percentage points. In that scenario, 89.81% of selected neighbors belonged to the same participant as the evaluated observation.Conclusions Under the simulated conditions, high record-wise accuracy occurred without a generalizable class-related signal. Evaluation intended to estimate performance in previously unseen people should preserve participant separation. These findings demonstrate an evaluation mechanism and do not establish depression-detection performance.

articles.title: Verifiable Deep Learning: Smart Contract--Enabled Model Integrity and Provenance on Distributed Ledgers
articles.abstract: Deep learning artifacts undergo long and mutable lifecycles in which datasets, preprocessing pipelines, checkpoints, evaluation configurations, and deployed versions may be controlled by different actors. Hash anchoring makes individual bytes tamper-evident but does not establish that a checkpoint was derived from authorized data or that its alleged computation actually occurred. We present ProofWeave, a provenance-coupled verification specification that treats model evolution as a typed, policy-constrained transition system. Each transition binds content commitments, authenticated parent references, version rules, and explicit evidence obligations; the proposed contract state machine admits only policy-valid transitions. We distinguish full computational proofs, conditioned on a sound external proving backend, from probabilistic committed-step audits with a finite-population detection bound. For transparent evaluation we implement a local integrity prototype, not a live blockchain or zero-knowledge proof service. Seven deterministic integrity fault types are assessed across three public datasets; four nested validators cover 2, 4, 6, and 7 of the nine broader threat classes discussed. To expose an essential security boundary, we additionally perform 105 real MLP training runs over seven random seeds and five controlled training-label corruption rates. Hash/signature microbenchmarks and Merkle trees of up to 65,536 leaves characterize local scaling. A controlled Monte Carlo audit study quantifies probabilistic detection under committed-step sampling, separately from the local measurements. The evidence supports preliminary provenance-check correctness and quantifies its limits; it does not establish on-chain costs or end-to-end verifiable neural training.

articles.title: Crosslinked-grafted-blended polybenzimidazole alkaline anion exchange membranes for water electrolysis
articles.abstract: Anion exchange membranes (AEMs), as the core material in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) for hydrogen production, play a pivotal role in enhancing electrolysis efficiency and extending the operational lifetime of electrolyzer. To improve the solubility and ionic conductivity of Poly[2,2′-(1,4-naphthalene)-5,5′-bibenzimidazole](NPBI)-based AEMs, methyl groups were grafted onto the pyrrole and pyridine nitrogen atoms of NPBI, and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) with different molar ratios was mixed with methyl grafted NPBI (MeNPBI) to prepare a grafted-blended PVA-MeNPBI AEM. By tuning the molar ratio of PVA-to-MeNPBI, the resulting membranes demonstrated significant improvements in ion exchange capacity, ionic conductivity, and elongation at break. Notably, the PVA-MeNPBI-4:1 membrane exhibited a hydroxide ion conductivity of 138.2 mS·cm⁻¹. The cationic crosslinker, 3-Hexyl spacers N,N-Dimethylpiperidinium cations (QDMP), was introduced into PVA-MeNPBI AEM via the Menshutkin reaction to produce QDMP-PVA-MeNPBI AEMs. The resulting membrane achieved a peak hydroxide ion conductivity of 150.3 mS·cm⁻¹, significantly surpassing that of the pristine MeNPBI membrane (91.3 mS·cm⁻¹) and 1.79 times higher than that of the commercial FAA-3 membrane (84.0 mS·cm⁻¹). This membrane exhibited a tensile strength of 57.1 MPa and an elongation at break of 63.4%, showing excellent mechanical stability. At 2.10V, the AEMWE with QDMP-PVA-MeNPBI membrane delivered a current density of 3.37 A·cm⁻², four times than that with the FAA-3 membrane (0.84 A·cm⁻²). After immersion in 1 M KOH at 80°C for 500 hours, the QDMP-PVA-MeNPBI membrane retained 92.4% of its initial conductivity. These results indicate that the QDMP-PVA-MeNPBI membrane exhibits excellent potential for application in AEMWE for hydrogen production.

articles.title: RepMOBO: Representation-Guided Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization for Pareto-Optimal MOF Discovery
articles.abstract: Screening metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) across chemical space by simulation or experiment is costly, while trade-offs among adsorption objectives hinder Pareto-optimal discovery. Material representation learning offers a promising route by encoding crystal structures into compact feature spaces. However, prior work has been confined to offline prediction, leaving unclear how representation choice shapes search behaviour and Pareto discovery in multi-objective Bayesian optimization. Here we propose RepMOBO, a representation-guided multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework, using multi-vapour MOF adsorption to examine how handcrafted physicochemical descriptors and pretrained structural embeddings shape low-budget Pareto discovery. At a 10% query budget, the hybrid-representation configuration yielded 4.5-fold more configuration-specific strict Pareto-front discoveries than the handcrafted-descriptor configuration. RepMOBO-prioritized candidates guided experimental screening, yielding synthesizable MOFs with target-dependent, state-of-the-art adsorption performance. These results reveal a prediction–discovery mismatch: strong offline prediction need not translate into efficient low-budget Pareto discovery. RepMOBO therefore elevates representation from static encoding to an active search variable and motivates transferable representation–surrogate–policy co-design for costly multi-objective discovery in numerically representable candidate spaces.

articles.title: Out-of-Plane Oscillating Electric Fields Unlock Low-Temperature Nonequilibrium Superionicity in Quasi-Two-Dimensional AgCrSe2
articles.abstract: Superionic conductors enable exceptionally fast ion transport and offer broad technological potential, but their highly conductive states are typically accessible only above the mobile-ion sublattice order–disorder transition temperature. Here, electric-field-responsive machine-learning molecular dynamics reveals a nonequilibrium route to superionic transport in quasi-two-dimensional AgCrSe2 under an out-of-plane oscillating electric field. At 300 K, far below the transition temperature near 475 K, the field activates fast in-plane Ag+ transport with an ionic conductivity reaching ∼1.7 S cm−1. This originates from field-driven dynamic disorder of Ag+ across two equivalent sub-lattices. The highly conductive, dynamically disordered state emerges when the driving half-period approaches the characteristic Ag-sublattice switching time, which shortens with increasing temperature and field amplitude. At strong fields, this timescale is consistent with field-assisted thermal activation, while weak-field deviations suggest additional dynamics. These results show timescale-matched periodic driving as a route to low-temperature nonequilibrium superionic transport.

articles.title: Tailoring Crystal Structure, Optical Band and Wettability of Green-Synthesized BiOI Nanoparticles via pH-Controlled Hydrothermal Method
articles.abstract: In this study, BiOI nanoparticles were synthesized through a green hydrothermal route using Murraya koenigii(curry leaf) extract, with the reaction pH systematically varied from 5 to 13. to investigate its influence on the structural, morphological, optical, surface-charge, and wettability characteristics. X-ray diffraction analysis showed that BiOI retained a tetragonal structure at pH 5–10, whereas a structural transformation toward an orthorhombic phase was observed under strongly alkaline conditions at pH 13. The crystallite size varies from 18.67±4.86 to 30.37±11.34 nm, accompanied by changes in crystallinity, lattice strain, and defect density. Scanning electron microscopy revealed a pronounced morphological evolution from cauliflower-like aggregates to hierarchical flower-like structures and subsequently to larger plate/rod-like features with increasing pH, indicating the influence of solution chemistry on crystal growth and aggregation. FTIR analysis identified characteristic vibrational features of Bi–O–I nanoparticle framework and surface functional groups. UV–Vis analysis revealed pH-dependent optical band gaps, with indirect values of 1.607 ± 0.005–2.202 ± 0.011 eV and direct values of 2.170 ± 0.012–2.523 ± 0.009 eV. The zeta potential became increasingly negative from −30.93 ± 1.61 to −40.83 ± 0.34 mV, while the water contact angle decreased from 53.57 ± 2.23° to 23.03 ± 2.29°, indicating systematic changes in surface charge and wettability. Thus, reaction pH provides an effective route to tune the structural, morphological, optical, and interfacial properties of BiOI-based materials, offering potential for photocatalytic, photo-electrochemical, optoelectronic, self-cleaning, and atmospheric water-harvesting applications.

articles.title: Parameterisation of NMC and LFP 4680 cells for electrochemical and thermal modelling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An electrochemical-thermal model of the 4680 cylindrical cell is presented: a Doyle-Fuller-Newman model of the electrode stack coupled to a two-node thermal balance of the roll and the can (a thermal DFN, TDFN), solved by an implicit finite-volume scheme. Two cells are parameterised from teardown geometry and open literature, with every value tagged by provenance: the Tesla NMC811/graphite tabless cell and the BYD FC4680 LiFePO4 multi-tab cell. The reaction heat is evaluated at the open-circuit potential of the particle-mean concentration, which restores the heat of mixing. Both sets are calibrated in the same way, with the test fixture identified from the measurement alone. Against the 1C and 2C charge test of Ank et al., the calibrated NMC set follows the mean can temperature within 0.52 and 1.46 K, with a contact heat of 0.94 mOhm matching the authors' estimate for their holder. For the LFP cell, 1C and 2C discharges to 2.0 V were measured on the authors' bench; the fixture conductance (0.337 W/K) follows from the energy balance and the heat capacity (277 J/K) from the cooling. With the end-of-lithiation drop of LiFePO4 restored in the cathode open-circuit potential, the calibrated set follows the can temperature within 0.44 K (1C) and 0.76 K (2C), reproduces the peaks and the relaxation after cut-off. What remains is what a single can node and a single representative particle do not describe: the axial gradient of the NMC can under contact heating, and a gradual decline of the LFP voltage before the knee at 2C, which points to the distribution of particle states in the electrode. The parameter sets (BPX, CSV) and the bench data are openly available.

articles.title: Organizational Learning in Materials Discovery Campaigns: Which Databases, Calculations, and Agent Teams Pay Off
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02571v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: More databases can make a materials campaign worse. Through an organizational lens, we trace each source's contribution. One band-gap campaign ranks seven anion families from archived measured gaps, one vote per source. In the first half of its budget, all seven pooled rank worse (rank agreement 0.737; 1 = measured order) than the best pool of three (0.851). As a stability check, choosing the pool on half the runs and testing on the rest kept the gap. Splitting Materials Project afterwards points to its transition-metal oxides and fluorides. Two databases from one pipeline add nothing over one, but pooling gives their shared ordering two votes. New calculations repay their cost early only when two or three campaigns reuse them. Flat language-model agent teams trailed a random-pick baseline (mean 0.876, sd 0.096, 20 searches). An adaptive Al-Mg-Si team, mostly interatomic potentials, was scored on unseen HSE06 calculations. In its first quarter of compute it found 49% of the ten lowest-formation-energy compounds, against at most 40% for fixed teams and 73% for MACE-MP-0 alone. Merging members whose orderings agreed carried most of its gain. This suggests pooling a few sources that fit the measurements, counting each pipeline once and charging for computation.

articles.title: Quantum 6j-symbols arising from a subfactor of finite index and finite depth and the zipper condition for 4-tensors in two-dimensional topological order
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02582v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study 3-tensors satisfying the ``zipper condition,'' which play an important role in tensor network approaches to two-dimensional topological order. In our previous work, we identified the 4-tensors appearing in these approaches with bi-unitary connections in the Jones theory of subfactors in operator algebras. These bi-unitary connections give rise to subfactors of finite index. We prove that, when the associated subfactor has finite depth, the 3-tensors satisfying the zipper condition correspond precisely to the quantum 6j-symbols, also known as F-symbols, of the unitary multi-fusion category arising from the subfactor. This realization of quantum 6j-symbols differs from their realization through a flat bi-unitary connection arising from the higher relative commutants of a subfactor.

articles.title: Derivation of Novel Isotropic Metamaterials at the Hashin Shtrikman Stiffness Limit Enabled by Physics Informed Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02622v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Current methods of deriving ultrastiff isotropic metamaterials require heuristics or topology optimization, which are highly inefficient and limited by human input. To circumvent this, Physics Informed Neural Networks are applied to analytical equations to systematically solve for plate orientations in closed cell lattices. Following a standardized procedure, the plate orientations were modelled and assembled into geometries resembling quasi random foams for validation via finite element simulations.
