Based on our extensive two- and three-dimensional simulations, we identify limitations of the existing conversion relations and propose improved closure expressions that enable more accurate determination of material's rheological properties. Furthermore, the three-dimensional flow structures and yielding patterns within the vane-in-cup fixtures are characterised.

articles.title: Nondestructive 3D Metrology of Through-Glass Via Geometry and Internal Wall Texture Using Holotomography
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Through-glass vias (TGVs) are increasingly important for semiconductor packaging, yet their internal geometry and wall texture remain difficult to characterize nondestructively. Here, we use holotomography (HT) to inspect the three-dimensional (3D) geometry and internal wall texture of intact, unfilled TGVs before metallization. HT reconstructs the refractive index (RI) distribution of the glass and via. Maps of RI and spatially filtered RI then localize the internal boundary. Geometric fitting quantifies via dimensions and taper, while spatial filtering separates slowly varying wall form from finer texture. The reconstructed surface supports volumetric visualization, dimensional measurements and spatial characterization of wall texture within one optical inspection workflow. These measurements reveal internal features inaccessible from surface views and provide quantitative descriptors to evaluate TGVs

articles.title: Bistability in the stalling behavior of thick, cambered airfoils under elevated freestream turbulence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aerodynamic performance of a thick, cambered FFA-W3-301 airfoil section near and beyond stall was examined under elevated freestream turbulence using time-resolved surface pressure measurements for chord-based Reynolds numbers from 125,000 to 275,000. Three passive turbulence grids were used to isolate the effects of turbulence intensity and integral length scale, and the results were compared with a clean inflow. The elevated turbulence largely had a positive effect on the mean performance of the airfoil section, eliminating premature flow separation and recovering lift and drag polars more representative of a higher effective Reynolds number; however, resolving the lift in time showed that the time-averaged polars concealed bistable switching. The time-averaged lift was an occupancy-weighted average of two states, and conventional mean and standard-deviation statistics misrepresented the true post-stall unsteady loads. Beyond the maximum-lift angle of attack, the lift alternated repeatedly between two distinct levels with no characteristic frequency. At the highest tested Reynolds number, the switching persisted over an angle-of-attack range of up to nine degrees, more than an order of magnitude wider than that reported for a thin, symmetric section in a low turbulence inflow. The lift levels of the two states were also found to be nearly independent of the inflow turbulence level, whereas the fraction of time spent in each differed between turbulence conditions. conditionally averaged surface pressure distributions and proper orthogonal decomposition of the surface pressure consistently showed that neither state is fully attached; the states correspond to two positions of a single separation front on the suction side, a switching accurately captured by a single pressure mode from the decomposition.

articles.title: Optical Detection of Coefficient of Thermal Expansion via Frequency Tracking at Cryogenic Temperatures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate characterization of the coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) in nanoscale thin films is critical for predicting residual stress and ensuring the reliability of modern micro-electromechanical systems and advanced semiconductor architectures. The primary limitation is that traditional methods depend on precise thickness measurements or are restricted to crystalline materials. In this work, we present an in-situ, non-destructive optical methodology to determine the CTE of suspended nanofilms by tracking the temperature-dependence of their vibrational frequency. This approach eliminates thickness measurements entirely and works for amorphous films where X-ray diffraction (XRD) fails. We experimentally validate this technique across a broad temperature range, evaluating membranes in their native microstructure state without requiring additional destructive patterning or complex sample preparation. This non-contact optical method achieves uncertainty below 5.3 * 10-8 K-1, substantially improving upon conventional thin-film CTE metrology.

articles.title: A spatial autocorrelation method for estimating Rayleigh-wave attenuation coefficients from microtremor array measurements
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The velocity and attenuation structures of near-surface soils play an important role in controlling earthquake ground motions. While numerous passive techniques have been developed for estimating velocity structure, practical methods for estimating attenuation from microtremor array measurements remain limited. We developed a spatial autocorrelation (SPAC) method for estimating Rayleigh-wave attenuation coefficients using an attenuation-aware formulation of the SPAC coefficient. A theoretical analysis of directional aliasing showed that attenuation estimation requires denser azimuthal sampling than conventional phase-velocity estimation, motivating the use of a regular heptagonal array. The method uses a two-stage procedure in which initial estimates of phase velocity and the attenuation coefficient are obtained using a first-order approximation and then refined by fitting the complex SPAC coefficient. Synthetic data analyses demonstrated that the proposed method can recover attenuation coefficients under ideal conditions and clarified how directional aliasing, record length and sensitivity to attenuation affect the estimates. Comparison with a beamforming-based method showed that the proposed method is less sensitive to wavefield directionality and can be applied at longer wavelengths relative to the array size. The method was further validated using microtremor-like waveforms generated by independent P--SV wave-propagation simulations. Finally, a preliminary application to field microtremor records yielded attenuation coefficients that were broadly consistent across array sizes and with values expected from existing empirical attenuation relationships. These results demonstrate the applicability of the proposed method to passive estimation of Rayleigh-wave attenuation.

articles.title: Finite-size scaling and cutoff functions of critical avalanches under cubic saturation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Power-law avalanche statistics characterize the branching bulk but leave open how finite systems terminate their largest events. Here we determine both the finite-size cutoff and the full crossover function connecting the branching regime to the large-event tail for an exchangeable absorbing event process motivated by Cauchy-stable recurrent dynamics. The Cauchy dynamical mean-field theory yields a linear-cubic low-activity drift, while a repeatable-event lift supplies absorbing branching fluctuations. Their competition at criticality generates a distinct finite-size edge controlled by cubic saturation. For avalanches initiated by a fixed microscopic seed, the rescaled edge measure connects the universal branching power law continuously to an exponential large-area tail. This full crossover admits an analytic spectral representation in terms of the boundary spectrum of a quartic Schrödinger operator on the half-line: high modes reconstruct the branching singularity, while the ground state fixes the far-tail decay. Exact finite-size calculations and Monte Carlo simulations confirm both the predicted cutoff behavior and the full spectral crossover.

articles.title: Coupled Soft-Clamped Polygon Resonators with Tunable Mechanical Coupling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coupler geometry controls both the frequency splitting and the dissipation of coupled polygon resonators. We develop a continuum model for two identical square-shaped resonators coupled by a shared tether and compare the analytical predictions with finite element simulations. The model relates the coupler length and width to the frequency splitting and dissipation dilution of the two coupled modes. In the short-coupler limit, k_cl_cll1, the symmetric-mode coupler undergoes nearly uniform rotation, and its torsional strain energy vanishes asymptotically. The remaining loss contributions arise from polygon-side bending and supporting-tether torsion. The reduced supporting-tether contribution allows the symmetric-mode dissipation dilution to exceed that of an isolated polygon with the same side and supporting-tether dimensions. The antisymmetric mode retains torsional strain in the coupler and has an additional loss contribution. We also derive an expression for Q· f in the short-coupler and short-tether limits, where Q is the mechanical quality factor and f is the resonance frequency. This expression gives the dependence of Q· f on tensile stress, film thickness, and supporting-tether geometry. For a coupler length of 100~mum and width of 2~mum, finite element calculations give a frequency splitting of 17.7~Hz and a symmetric-mode dilution factor approximately 13% above the analytical isolated-polygon value.

articles.title: Physics-Informed Surrogate for Sb2S3 Dispersion Trimming in Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A film-thickness error of 8 nm, within the tolerance of commercial thin-film lithium niobate wafers, shifts the group-velocity dispersion β₂ at 1550 nm by about 28 ps² km⁻¹. We study numerically whether a segmented, non-volatile phase-change cladding can correct this error after fabrication. In mode solves of 3012 geometries, Sb₂S₃ switches β₂ by a median of 181 ps² km⁻¹ at a 40 nm strip thickness with no material absorption under the adopted optical constants, whereas Sb₂Se₃ reaches a comparable contrast at a median modal loss of 5.6 dB cm⁻¹. Because phase adds along the guide, four independently switched binary segments reach a two-dimensional region of the (β₂,β₃) plane; eigenmode expansion supports this description at the junctions. Full-wave solves at 65 die geometries show that the segment states move with the die error, so the bit pattern is chosen from a per-die model: a spectral surrogate constrained by exact identities of the lossless Maxwell problem. Its accuracy within the training domain is similar to that of unconstrained baselines; it keeps β₂ and β₃ consistent, and its error at an unseen film thickness is 8.3 rather than 13.0 ps² km⁻¹. With a bare test ring and a second ring carrying a crystalline strip already on the mask, 96.8% of the dies are trimmed into ±25 ps² km⁻¹, scored on full-wave solutions. A thermal model gives a candidate write window for a 532 nm beam.

articles.title: Edge photocurrent distribution in luminescent solar concentrators: analytical treatment and solar cell arrangement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In luminescent solar concentrators (LSCs), the light flux along the edges is non-uniform, which causes current mismatch between series-connected edge solar cells. Here, the optical path distribution of photons arriving at an edge point was derived analytically for a rectangular LSC and generalized to convex polygons, with reabsorption and scattering included as a geometric series. The model agrees with Monte Carlo simulations and reproduces measured edge cell currents of a 60×60 cm² LSC within 2-3%. In a square LSC, the series mismatch reduces the current by 8-12% for four cells per edge. Rules for edge solar cell arrangement are formulated.

articles.title: A plug-and-play platform for self-aligning 3D-printed structures on optical fibers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two-photon polymerization 3D printing advances optical fibers into complex lab-on-fiber devices. However, widespread adoption remains bottlenecked by the inherent inefficiencies of sequential, direct-on-fiber printing. To address this, a custom-designed modular platform and a corresponding fiber-decoupled fabrication methodology on planar substrates are presented. This platform features a compliant, spring-like socket that enables passive self-alignment and reversible fiber insertion, paired with a customizable frontal device. The shift to fabrication on planar substrates enables parallel batch processing and allows the substrate to serve as a functional magazine for device mounting. To demonstrate this approach, modular platforms featuring a functional tip are printed, sharpened via post-process plasma etching, metallized, and equipped with an optical aperture using focused ion beam milling, while remaining on the planar substrate. Subsequently, these are used as exchangeable scanning probe microscopy tips mounted in situ within a scanning electron microscope. Simultaneous three-channel correlative imaging (atomic force microscopy topography, secondary electron, and cathodoluminescence) is used to validate the optomechanical stability of the design. Ultimately, by decoupling the delicate optical device's lifespan from the optical fiber, this architecture transforms lab-on-fiber tools into scalable, seamlessly replaceable consumables, offering a highly adaptable pathway for broader applications in photonics, sensing, and microscopy.

articles.title: Site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer for symmetry-constrained crystal generation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative models for crystal structure prediction (CSP) have expanded the search space for novel materials and improved screening efficiency. However, simultaneously generating stable and novel structures remains challenging because of the complex structural and physical constraints governing crystals. To address this challenge, we propose site-orbit masked twin-branch Transformer model (ST2M), a symmetry-guided discrete--continuous diffusion framework incorporating degree-of-freedom masks and conditioned on Wyckoff patterns. ST2M represents crystal structures as sequences of independent occupied Wyckoff orbits and employs a twin-branch Transformer to jointly denoise discrete and continuous variables. In our experiments, ST2M achieves a structural validity of 96.37%. For known patterns in dataset, 23.86% of generated structures simultaneously satisfy stability, uniqueness, and novelty criteria, representing a relative improvement of 68.15% over the best-performing baseline. First-principles calculations identify a total of 21 previously unreported stable structures among selected candidates with low predicted energies. These results demonstrate that ST2M can generate chemically viable crystal candidates under prescribed crystallographic constraints and generalize to unknown Wyckoff patterns, providing a practical route to accelerated materials discovery.

articles.title: Brillouin comb line amplifiers for optical atomic clocks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical atomic clocks outperform the microwave clocks at the heart of current timing and navigation infrastructure by orders-of-magnitude, and recent progress in on-chip integration provides the opportunity to widely deploy them. Conventionally, a narrow linewidth laser interrogates the atomic transition, and an optical frequency comb divides its stabilised frequency (hundreds of terahertz) down to a microwave that is electronically countable. The laser(s) impose a significant size, weight, power and cost penalty, which is a current barrier to low-cost, scalable, fully on-chip optical clocks. Here, we position the frequency comb as the central engine of the clock by using Brillouin-amplified comb lines for atomic spectroscopy, which eliminates the need for stable clock lasers. Amplified comb lines reach an ultra-low frequency noise floor of 6,Hz²/Hz at 30,kHz offset, an order-of-magnitude below a high-end commercial fibre laser. We realize a clock based on the 5S₁/₂→5D₅/₂ transition in ⁸⁷Rb with competitive fractional frequency stability of 2×10⁻¹³ at τ = 1,s, averaging to 9×10⁻¹⁵ at τ = 1000,s. Lastly, we demonstrate a photonic chip-integrated Brillouin amplifier with a record 62.9 dB gain and up to 40 dB transferred noise suppression when pumped with a simple, low-cost diode laser. This opens a new route to compact optical clocks and enables use of atomic transitions lacking low-noise lasers by broadening a comb to the required wavelength and amplifying single lines.

articles.title: Dynamics of a two-dimensional microswimmer near a slippery boundary
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Microswimmers near walls and interfaces can switch between qualitatively different modes of motion depending on the slip properties of the neighbouring boundaries. To study this theoretically, a two-dimensional point-singularity model of a microswimmer, which does not self-propel in unbounded fluid, is placed near a flat viscosity discontinuity between two fluids with viscosity ratio σ, and also near a partial-slip wall with Navier-slip length λ. Using complex-variable methods, the dynamical systems governing the swimmer motion are derived explicitly in both scenarios. Near the viscosity discontinuity, below a universal critical viscosity ratio σ_c=1/2, the swimmer is trapped at a fixed height with its stresslet axis normal to the boundary. When σ=σ_c it glides parallel to the boundary at a speed selected by its orientation, with a terminal speed determined by its initial state. For σ>σ_c it oscillates periodically in height and orientation while drifting along the boundary. The dynamics near a partial-slip wall depend on the ratio of the slip length to the length scale of the singularity and are similar in exhibiting an analogous transition at a critical slip length. It is found, however, that the dynamics near a viscosity discontinuity for σ above σ_c are richer than those near the partial-slip boundary, including the existence of a hydrodynamic bound state with zero net displacement over one period. Although the study is limited to two dimensions, these results show how a single boundary parameter organises qualitatively distinct modes of locomotion, in close analogy with slip-induced transitions reported for three-dimensional swimmers.

articles.title: Geometric Phase and Spinor Beam Dynamics of Paraxial Beams
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that treating a paraxially propagating electric field as a spinor provides a natural way to include geometric phase in beam propagation models. Importantly, by exploiting differences in the way geometric phase and dynamical phase accrue during propagation, we show that spatial variations in the former can have surprising and rather remarkable consequences for beam dynamics. As an example, we design a beam with a centroid that is predicted to follow a curved path through free space, a prediction we subsequently validate in experiment. The model presented herein does not contradict existing propagation models, but rather shows how to leverage the extra degree of freedom afforded by the spinor angle to make new predictions.

articles.title: Single-pass stochastic cooling for electron microscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific applications of free electrons, such as in electron microscopes and particle accelerators, are limited by the brightness of available electron sources. Accelerators can use phase space cooling to surpass these source limitations, whereas electron microscopes can only rely on particle filtering to increase beam coherence at the cost of reduced brightness. We show that strong electron-light coupling in nanophotonic structures makes it possible to achieve single-pass stochastic cooling inside an electron microscope for a lossless improvement of longitudinal emittance. This approach is laser-free and compatible with normal CW operation of electron microscopes. We derive a fully quantum mechanical model of stochastic cooling valid in the strong coupling regime, finding an analytic asymptotic formula for the optimal cooled energy spread σE_fsimeq0.88(hbarω)²/³σE_₀¹/³, with hbar ω the cooling photon energy and σE_₀ the initial energy spread. Numerical simulations confirm that the energy spread reduction is reflected in an increase in the purity of the electron's quantum state and a reduction of the longitudinal phase space area. Our work paves a path towards even brighter beams for electron microscopy, promising higher image quality, enhanced spectral resolution, and a route to reaching fundamental quantum limits on electron beam phase space area.

articles.title: Temperature-Independent Logarithmic Current Slope in Interdiffusion-Broadened Silicon pn Junction toward Low-Power Thermometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03593v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the development of cryogenic technologies such as quantum computing, there is an increasing need for low-power cryogenic thermometers that minimize self-heating. Here, we report an anomalous temperature-independent logarithmic current slope, d(ln J)/dV, in heavily doped silicon p⁺n⁺ junctions with significant dopant interdiffusion and highlight the advantages of our device as a low-power, cryogenic thermometer. Electrical characterizations from 2 to 420 K reveal that, at low forward bias, d(ln J)/dV remains nearly constant, which yields a voltage-temperature responsivity that is nearly independent of bias current. The observed transport cannot be fully understood with conventional diffusion or direct band-to-band tunneling. Instead, the results suggest the contribution of trap-assisted tunneling. These results establish interdiffusion-broadened silicon p⁺n⁺ junctions as a route to low-power temperature sensors while providing insight into carrier transport in heavily doped semiconductor junctions.

articles.title: Do Multimodal Models Decide Consistently on Equivalent Optical Spectra?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00428v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A spectrum can be given to a model as a table in nanometers or as a plot in photon energy, and the decision should not depend on which one it sees. When the data needed for an answer are missing, the model should say so. We test representation invariance and abstention on measured optical spectra of silicon metasurfaces (MOCLIP) and gold nanoparticles, with labels computed from the data. Each spectrum is shown as four tables (nm, μm, scientific notation, eV) and two plots (nm, eV), and partial spectra remove data inside or outside the queried range. We evaluate the decision models d3-nano and Jev 1.13, three GPT-6 Luna configurations and the Qwen3.5-2B base model. Changing only the representation moves accuracy by up to 41 percentage points within one model, mostly on photon-energy tables and plots. With the same evidence, asking in photon energy instead of wavelength helps some model-view pairs by 16-50 points and hurts others by up to 25. When the relevant extremum is removed, unadapted models rarely answer "undetermined". LoRA fine-tuning of d3-nano improves comparisons on the trained table formats, but much of its gain on unanswerable questions comes from a shortcut: it abstains whenever the input is truncated. Training with answerable truncations avoids the shortcut in all six seeds, with a 90-100 point gap between abstention after inside and outside cuts on held-out structures; with the same amount of extra original-task data, five of six seeds keep the shortcut. On gold spectra the two training sets perform similarly. Multimodal language models used for scientific decisions should be tested on equivalent representations and on missing evidence, not only on average accuracy. We release the tasks, per-response results and analysis code.

articles.title: Ultra-broadband quantum infrared spectroscopy extending to 20 textmum
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00561v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum infrared spectroscopy (QIRS), which exploits quantum interference between photon-pair generation processes, enables infrared spectroscopy using only visible and near-infrared (VNIR) light sources and detectors. Extending the spectral coverage of QIRS into the long-wavelength infrared region up to 20 textmum is crucial for the identification and characterization of a broad range of materials. However, implementing QIRS beyond 10 textmum has been challenging because the nonlinear materials used to date do not provide suitable photon-pair sources in this spectral region. Here, we design a wavelength-tunable photon-pair source based on a gallium selenide crystal and develop a QIRS system covering a broad spectral range from 8.6 to 20 textmum. Using this system, we measure the transmittance spectrum of a polystyrene film and observe characteristic absorption bands beyond 10 textmum relevant to identifying polystyrene and to probing local chain conformation. These results demonstrate that QIRS is capable of covering the entire molecular fingerprint region.

articles.title: Quantum algorithm for weakly correlated molecular electronic ground states with sub-quintic scaling in the system size
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00751v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weakly correlated electronic structures are predominant among molecules, and are routinely solved with heuristic classical methods such as the ``gold standard'' CCSD(T) coupled cluster model, incurring a formal time complexity O(n⁷) in the number of molecular orbitals and with no guarantee of energy error ε at or below chemical accuracy. In this work, a quantum algorithm is presented for ground state energy estimation of weakly correlated molecules using Trotterized time evolution, with an end-to-end quantum operations cost that scales as tildeO(n⁴.⁸/ε²) in the limit of high-order product formulae when run as a low-depth, shot-noise limited algorithm, or tildeO(n⁴.⁸ + n³.⁸/ε) when scaling the simulation time Tpropto 1/ε. The algorithm combines adiabatic state preparation using a smoothed Gevrey schedule with eigenstate filtering via quantum prolate diagonalization (QPD). Both steps of the algorithm rely on a size-independent spectral gap assumption, which is validated by numerical studies on alanine chains with up to 64 monomers. We benchmark the performance of our eigenstate filtering algorithm on a set of 28 molecules to compare our approach against prior phase estimation algorithms, finding that QPD achieves state-of-the-art cost tradeoffs for ε-accurate results. Physical quantum resource estimates are obtained for running Trotter step circuits with up to 40 spin-orbitals, providing a clear path for scaling up quantum simulation of chemistry on early fault-tolerant hardware.

articles.title: Inferring missing locations in human mobility data using memory effects
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Empirical datasets used to characterize human mobility are sparse in space and time, owing to technological factors such as coverage and battery, or to the erratic nature of online interactions. Missing data can bias the conclusions drawn from them, so filling the gaps in incomplete timelines is a key challenge in computational social science. Here, we propose a simple imputation method in which the informativeness of an observation decays with its bidirectional temporal distance from the missing entry, at a rate set by a single parameter per individual. On synthetic and real Twitter data, a power-law decay, selected by Bayesian model comparison, yields accurate imputations (macro-AUROC above 0.9 overall, and above 0.8 for the most mobile users) and matches a gap-aware continuous-time Markov chain, outperforming it among the most mobile users. The method is robust to moderate noise and generalizes across countries and European administrative regions.

articles.title: ReFrame: Silence-Aware Compute Reclamation for Full-Duplex Speech Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Full-duplex speech models execute dense model inference for every audio frame throughout a live interaction. This uniform framewise schedule creates sustained GPU load across dialogue states whose computation has strong, reusable temporal structure. ReFrame formulates full-duplex inference as a silence-aware computation problem. Mutual Silence Speculation (MSS) operates when both participants are silent: it evaluates multi-frame Temporal continuations, verifies text and hidden-state stability, and applies batched Mimi audio-token correction. Listening Frame Folding (LFF) operates while the user speaks and the agent listens: it processes already-arrived user frames through parallel Temporal execution and frame-batched audio-token generation while accepting only the verified prefix. Frame-Budget Reinvestment (FBR) assigns the released frame intervals to resumable external retrieval and language-model workers, then injects timely references through Moshi's conditioning interface. We instantiate ReFrame on five full-duplex models spanning Moshi-family, phase-structured, and flattened autoregressive generation. Across the complete 1,225-conversation FDBench, ReFrame reduces measured GPU execution time by 18.80-31.01% and retains 96.92-100% non-PAD text agreement on five different models. On HaluEval tests, FBR increases the number of correct generated spoken answers from 86 to 205 under the same auxiliary-service budget. ReFrame turns recurring dialogue structure into lower inference cost and higher end-to-end service capability.

articles.title: Diagonal Equivalence in State Space Models: Characterization, Retrieval Rank, and Selective Extensions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03101v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify real and complex state-space models (SSMs) with linear transitions, distinguishing fixed-basis diagonal equivalence from input-output equivalence and tracking coefficient-conditioning windows under coordinate changes. We characterize diagonal equivalence through commuting transition families whose members are diagonalizable over the chosen field. With time-shared token-local matrix maps, we identify this class's state-mediated kernels with unnormalized scalar-mode linear attention with multiplicative masks. Mamba 3's multiple-input, multiple-output (MIMO) construction lifts one value per local interface; SSD-MIMO routes independent values for local retrieval rank above one. HybridMamba combines Mamba 1's per-coordinate decay, Mamba 2-style heads and Mamba 3's complex rotations and two-endpoint writes, mixing real and rotating state blocks with different decay laws. They recover Mamba 1-3 single-input, single-output (SISO) configurations as exact special cases. On five large H100 bfloat16 workloads, our fused GPU kernels improve geometric-mean training time over official Mamba 1/3 in matched SISO recoveries, with Mamba 2 near parity at SSM-core scope. Memory tradeoffs depend on the baseline and metric: saved-for-backward versus peak allocation. In small-model multi-token recall experiments, both designs outperform Mamba 1-3 on the hardest tier; higher routing ranks perform best in gated or phase-diverse configurations. In single-seed language models with about 500M parameters, both improve on Mamba 1/2 in test loss at 2B tokens, but the routing gains do not translate into lower language-model loss. Our best configurations approach Mamba 3 SISO through 10B tokens while remaining behind it and Mamba 3 MIMO in language-model loss.

articles.title: MemU-Bench: Benchmarking GUI Agents on Long-Horizon User Interactions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing Graphical User Interface (GUI) benchmarks predominantly rely on precise and stateless user instructions. In everyday usage, however, instructions are often emphvague and history-dependent: users omit the exact details of their past operations because they no longer remember them, leaving the agent to recover the missing context from long and noisy interaction histories. To bridge this evaluation gap, we introduce MemU-Bench, a mobile benchmark of 118 vague tasks grounded in 29 long-horizon user trajectories, where agents must distill raw interaction streams into memory and retrieve the missing context on demand, with task outcomes verified against serialized application databases. Alongside Success Rate, we incorporate Interaction Efficiency (IE) and Success weighted by Path Length (SPL) to expose agents that succeed by exhaustively searching across different applications rather than by emphgenuinely recalling the history. Evaluations show that without user history, state-of-the-art systems struggle under such ambiguity: the best-performing Gemini-3.1-Pro achieves an SPL of only 16.4%, and end-to-end GUI agents fall below 5%. To address this, we further propose AppMem, a training-free framework that distills user history into a emphstructured, app-centric memory bank, tracks interrupted intents across application switches, and selectively retrieves relevant memories via target-app inference. AppMem raises the SPL of GPT-5.5 from 15.7% to 66.9% (+51.2%), outperforms a naive summary baseline by 9.3%, and delivers consistent gains across evaluated backbones.

articles.title: Taurus: LLM-in-the-Loop CT Annotation Matches Coding Agents at Half the Cost
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dense labels of the aorta in CT are slow to draw, and the public aortic CT datasets that could stand in for them each label different structures under their own conventions. Large language model (LLM) agents can now write code and read images. We asked whether such a model labels these scans better as a free-form agent that writes its own segmentation code, or inside a harness, where an automated pass labels the scan and the model reviews the result. We built a harness, Taurus, and compared it with free-form agents by blind label recovery: we withheld the human labels of six public datasets (939 volumes) and scored every approach against each dataset's own classes. In the first version of Taurus, the model's review raised the primary metric on only two of six datasets, by less than the noise between two reviews of the same case. A free-form agent running Claude Opus 5.5 scored higher on most datasets. Moving what the free-form agents did well into the automated pass then carried most of the gain on 38 held-out cases. The final version smooths the label surfaces with a fixed rule and checks for the large errors the automated pass tends to make, such as an aneurysm drawn to half its size. Each check that fires puts a multiple-choice question to the model, with candidate corrections drawn on the scan. It matched the surface smoothness of the human references, and in the primary metric we found no difference from the free-form Opus agent, at under half its cost, 1.22 against 2.71 per case. Most of what made Taurus competitive came from the harness and its automation rather than from the language model itself. Taurus shows that this kind of annotation can be automated, so that expert time can move from drawing labels to checking them.

articles.title: Decentralized Multi-Agent Coordination and Communication in Shared Codebases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents working in shared repositories may receive separate, independently-motivated requests from human developers, creating a setting that is multi-agent by necessity. When this scenario happens, their individual implementations may work separately but conflict when combined. To study this setting, we introduce ParallACT, a benchmark of orchestrator-free multi-agent coding tasks. ParallACT contains both complementary and contradictory tasks. In complementary tasks, each agent's task is separately useful and implementations must share an interface to be productively combined. In contradictory pairs, both agents' tasks require editing the same code in incompatible ways, and naively combining independent solutions fails to produce a useful implementation. We compare a single-agent oracle given the combined set of tasks against multi-agent settings that vary execution order, visibility, awareness of other agents, and access to a communication channel. We find that the oracle solves most tasks while parallel agents perform substantially worse. Their performance drop is notable for complementary tasks, and particularly sharp for contradictory tasks (e.g., from 62% to 16% for Claude Code with Claude Opus 4.8) where merged code typically satisfies only one specification, and the same gap appears in all six further configurations pairing two agent harnesses with three open-weight models. Simply telling an agent that a peer exists does not help significantly, and giving agents access to a communication channel recovers only a small part of the performance, at an additional token cost. ParallACT thus identifies and isolates a core challenge that will become more common as multi-agent coding by independent principals becomes standard, and provides a controlled test of which coordination strategies help, and at what cost.

articles.title: Swap, Replicate, Read the Mass: A Protocol for Auditing Demographic Bias in System One Decision Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: System One decision models replace text generation with typed, probability-scored answers and are entering production. Answers execute without a person in the loop, and no multi-model audit exists on established bias benchmarks. We provide that audit: three benchmarks: BBQ (all eleven categories), CrowS-Pairs, and SilverSpoon, adapted to the typed interface, twelve models plus a no-thinking ablation, and 1,638,000 decisions. Every order-sensitive item runs twice with options swapped; native typed models also swap labels; ten configurations repeat under extra seeds and batch 16. We find widespread stereotype alignment, order-dependent answers, and confidence that tracks instability rather than bias. In BBQ, 97 of 143 model-by-category scores are significant and 94 aligned, while the commercial reference abstains on 99.5% of ambiguous items, hiding aligned probability mass. Option swaps flip 0.0% to 72.6% of choices; typed scoring stays below 10% except Laya (22-33%), and untuned letter prompting reaches 73%. CrowS-Pairs preference spans 0.496 to 0.816, and boolean answers can be decided by position (1.00 versus 0.005). SilverSpoon judgments shift toward lower-SES labels in five of eight decision models, inherited from the 9B backbone or induced by tuning. Audits must permute options and reverse questions by default; order-invariant scoring should become a procurement requirement.

articles.title: Decision-Centric Research: A Calibrated Decision Model and Benchmark for Scientific Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.00774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific agents make consequential choices about evidence, next actions and research strategy, but choices embedded in generated text are difficult to evaluate independently. Decision-Centric Research (DCR) is introduced to make individual choices the common unit of supervision, prediction and evaluation through typed predictions over an explicit Research State. DCR defines 24 decision types, ten of which are instantiated in the Research Decision Benchmark (RD-Bench) of 2,000 rule-generated cases. The Decision-Centric Research Model (DCRM) shares a candidate-token readout across types to produce answers and option probabilities in one forward pass. Under a held-out research-domain split, a 0.6B DCRM (state-aware) achieves 89.4% Top-1 accuracy, compared with 27.8% for DCRM (question-only) trained with the same recipe and 36.4% for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. All 30 type-seed comparisons against DCRM (question-only) are significant after Holm correction. After held-out calibration, the resulting prediction sets contain a mean of 1.515 candidates at 97.1% empirical label coverage, reducing mean set size by 57.4% relative to DCRM (question-only) at similar coverage. These results establish a compact state-aware decision layer with accurate typed prediction and an inspectable uncertainty interface.

articles.title: I-PTC: Interactive Programmatic Tool Calling for Stateful Tool-Augmented Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly capable of writing and executing code, suggesting a natural paradigm for tool-augmented agents: expressing tool use as programs rather than isolated calls. Programmatic tool calling (PTC) captures this idea through loops, batching, abstraction, and structured computation, but existing PTC approaches are largely stateless, limiting their ability to reuse intermediate results and adapt over time. This is problematic for real-world tasks, where tool environments and problem-solving processes are inherently stateful. We therefore present I-PTC, an interactive framework that executes stateful PTC: models issue code snippets that call tools, maintain reusable state, and evolve the tool interface through API corrections. To evaluate the effectiveness of I-PTC and the general PTC setting, we introduce PTC-Bench, a benchmark of long-tail, production-style user requests whose difficulty comes from large initial environments, many dependent API interactions, extended planning, and recovery across follow-ups and transient failures. Experiments on PTC-Bench show that I-PTC improves performance on complex multi-step tasks with large tool sets while substantially reducing token consumption over conventional tool-calling baselines and the original PTC baseline, highlighting stateful programmatic tool calling as a promising direction for scalable tool-augmented agents.

articles.title: Delivered, Not Used: Evaluating Agent Memory at Its Point of Use
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Task success, retrieval quality, and cost do not show whether an LLM agent used a delivered memory or what followed from that use. We introduce MemUse, which evaluates memory at its point of use in recorded trajectories: each memory delivery is compared with what the agent could already see and followed through the agent's later actions and their consequences. An agentic judge rates each delivered entry's relevance, accuracy, novelty, influence, and observed effect; programmatic checks enforce complete reading of cited evidence, and fixed rules aggregate the ratings into verdicts linked to memory histories and delivery cost. On 8,000 SWE-bench Verified episodes from three memory systems, resolve rates stay within 0.4 percentage points of a no-memory baseline, yet MemUse shows that most delivered entries were irrelevant, most relevant entries went unused, and in two systems most deliveries restated content the agent could still see. It also surfaces effects that outcomes hide: 23.2% of episodes with beneficial memory use still failed, and 5 of 16 with harmful use still succeeded.

articles.title: Safety4DM: A Vision-Language Framework for Risk-Aware Dynamic Maps in Vehicle-Road-Cloud Collaborative Driving
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamic map (DM) is a core information infrastructure for vehicle-road-cloud (VRC) cooperative autonomous driving. It fuses perception data from multiple sources to overcome the inherent line-of-sight and field-of-view limits of single-vehicle perception. However, DM still falls short on driving safety in two ways. First, DM data specifications already define road conditions semantically, but no pipeline yet turns real-world road observations into fine-grained risk entities in the DM. Second, existing DM systems lack a natural language interface for driving risks. To close these gaps, we propose Safety4DM, a safety-oriented language system for VRC dynamic maps. We first build RoadRisk, a real-world road image dataset that covers four types of road conditions and four risk levels. On this dataset, we fine-tune a vision-language model (VLM) for road safety risk perception. The model outputs structured risk representations that the DM can ingest directly. We then introduce a Safety-aware Step-wise Prompting (SafeStep) mechanism as the natural language query interface of the DM. SafeStep answers queries accurately and also generates actionable driving advice. To build and evaluate this interface, we develop SafeVRC-Sim, a VRC cooperative simulation framework, and SafeDM-QA, a safety question-answering benchmark. Experiments show that even the compact Qwen3-VL-4B reaches 89.83% accuracy on risk perception after fine-tuning. SafeStep also plugs easily into multiple LLM families. With medium and large models (20B and above) from five families, it achieves over 93% natural language query accuracy in every case, which shows strong generalization.

articles.title: Parallelism-Aligned Pruning and Round-Aware Context Reuse for On-Device Multimodal Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-device multimodal agents are limited by two deployment mismatches: pretrained attention structures may not divide evenly across the compute cores of an edge accelerator, causing irregular partitions; and standard prefix caching keeps historical visual tokens in the persistent KV cache, whose capacity grows with the number of rounds. We present PARC, which combines parallelism-aligned structured pruning with lifetime-aware KV-cache reorganization. At the model level, it uses first-order Taylor importance and grouped-query-attention-aware selection to make attention dimensions divisible by the target core count while preserving the query-to-key/value ratio and head dimension. At runtime, it separates the system prompt, persistent text history, and transient visual observations by lifetime, updating text history during tool execution so that historical images leave the persistent cache and more interaction rounds fit a fixed budget. On 2,062 GUI actions, the incremental interface shows no accuracy regression, and task-aware recovery training restores 98.7% of the action-type accuracy gap and the coordinate hit rate to the original level. Under seven-core deployment, hardware-aligned pruning reduces vision-encoder latency by 11.4%, improves decoding throughput by 23.8%, and lowers per-heap high-water memory by 12.7%; a parameter-matched control confirms that the speedup stems mainly from core alignment rather than parameter reduction.

articles.title: Creating Hybrid Interactive Narrative Systems with LLM: From Formal Description to Evaluation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.02807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactive narratives let users shape a story while an Experience Manager (EM) keeps it coherent, balancing player freedom against authorial control. Large Language Models now enable a new generation of hybrid EMs, which combine run-time generation from free-text input with symbolic narrative control. However, their heterogeneity makes them hard to compare: A manager's behaviour is generally tied to the unique and specific scenario in which it operates, and much of its decision-making takes place outside of any explicit and verifiable structure. We address this with an LLM-based narrative platform whose managers are interchangeable modules operating over a shared symbolic world model of facts, operations, and goals. Because every applied operation carries explicit preconditions and effects, each session can be analysed as a plan through a common state-transition representation and evaluated, independently of how the manager works internally, with shared indicators of four properties: player agency, EM controllability, author intent, and robustness. We implement three contrasting managers, based respectively on open generation, Monte Carlo repair, and autonomous characters, and compare them through functional analysis on an interactive Little Red Riding Hood scenario. The results show that no manager dominates on every property, giving authors and EM designers a concrete basis to select a manager according to their priorities.

articles.title: Towards a Trustworthy and Governable Internet of Agentics: An Architectural Perspective on Protocols, Systems, and Services
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model applications are increasingly being organized as tool-using and multi-agent workflows rather than as isolated chat interfaces. This perspective paper examines the architectural problem that follows from that shift: agents may reason, invoke tools, and delegate work, but dependable deployment still requires interoperability across frameworks, runtimes, data boundaries, and organizational control domains. We study this problem through the lens of the emphInternet of Agentics (IoA), an emerging service-computing view in which heterogeneous agents are treated as governable service participants rather than only as stand-alone model endpoints. The paper organizes the landscape as a three-layer progression: from today's fragmented agent ecosystem, to interoperable agents, and ultimately to trustworthy and governable autonomy. First, it examines the protocol stack centered on the Agentic AI Foundation, including MCP for agent--tool interaction; A2A for agent--agent coordination; AGENTS.md and Skills-style procedural manifests; and discovery, transport, and trust mechanisms such as AGNTCY and SLIM. Second, it reviews the systems abstractions that make agents deployable as service components, including logical agent architectures, orchestration patterns, gateways, registries, runtime control loops, and hardware-aware inference infrastructure. Third, it situates these developments within services computing, arguing that agentic systems reinterpret classical concerns from SOA and microservices---discovery, composition, governance, pricing, and trust---at the level of cognitive capabilities rather than deterministic functions.

articles.title: Auto-Research Agent on MSA Organization to Improve Protein-Protein Complex Structure Prediction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.03183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Protein-complex structure prediction with AlphaFold 3 depends on MSA content, depth, and cross-chain pairing. Current pipelines apply uniform recipes, typically maximizing depth and pairing by species, yet even whether cross-chain pairing helps AF3 remains contested. We show that the value of both depth and pairing is strongly target-dependent, so no single recipe is optimal across interfaces. We introduce an autonomous agent that treats a frozen AF3 as a black-box experimental instrument. For each target, the agent formulates biological hypotheses, analyzes and reorganizes the MSA, and iteratively refines sequence selection and pairing using predictor label-free signals alone. On 1,015 protein--protein interfaces from three benchmarks released after AF3's training cutoff, the agent improves overall interface DockQ over AF3's default pipeline and fixed MSA recipes on every benchmark, while using on average 60% fewer MSA sequences than the default. Gains are largest for inter-species heteromers, where species-based pairing is unreliable: mean DockQ increases from 0.465 to 0.612 on FoldBench and from 0.482 to 0.562 on HD439. The improvements arise from both sequence construction and pairing policy, including deliberate non-pairing.These results recast MSA design as a target-specific problem and show that an autonomous agent can adapt it at test time through biological reasoning and self-directed, confidence-guided experimentation.

articles.title: Feasibility of modulating taste perception using subthreshold electrical stimulation
articles.abstract: Subthreshold electrical noise can enhance sensory processing via stochastic resonance; however, its effect on taste remains unclear. This study investigated whether subthreshold white-noise electrical stimulation, applied to the skin surface along the mandibular margin, modulates taste perception. Young, healthy adults participated in psychophysical experiments using sodium chloride solutions for salty tastes and sucrose solutions for sweet tastes. For each taste, participants evaluated salty or sweet samples under randomized no-stimulation and stimulation conditions at 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8 times their sensory threshold using a nine-point taste intensity scale. The minimum perceptible concentrations were determined based on taste evaluation values. Additionally, stimulation to no-stimulation ratios were calculated as normalized minimum concentrations. For saltiness, the minimum concentration was significantly lower with stimulation under the 0.8 times condition than with no-stimulation (median, 0.15% vs. 0.20%; Holm-adjusted p = 0.012), and normalized minimum concentrations differed across stimulation intensities ( p = 0.004). No significant effects were observed for sweetness at any stimulation intensity. Additionally, exploratory within-participant selection of the best-performing intensity was conducted separately for saltiness and sweetness, which yielded descriptively low minimum concentrations. These findings suggest feasibility of modulating taste perception with subthreshold electrical noise, particularly for saltiness, with no significant enhancement for sweetness.

articles.title: Closed-Form Storage Stability, Induction Delay, and Thermal- Feedback Criticality of Melt-Gated Autocatalytic Cure
articles.abstract: We derive closed-form results for a lumped model of a cure triggered by the melting of an encapsulated catalyst, and test each against the full equations. At constant temperature the gated cure equals the ungated cure evaluated on the cumulative amount of catalyst released, so the gate delay grows with conversion and approaches the release time constant only late in the cure. The storage conversion of a Gaussian population of capsules follows from the fraction of capsules that are open, which bounds the spread of melting temperatures to within 3% of the full equations. For a fully released catalyst, the thermal balance at fixed conversion has a critical value of the product of the reduced exothermicity and the ratio of thermal to reaction time, given in closed form (1.96 for reaction order 3/2); integrated thresholds approach it for fast heat loss, and Arrhenius kinetics raise it by about exp(1/Ar), with Ar the reduced activation energy (within 5% on the tested grid). In a continuous-flow reactor with ungated kinetics, two folds of the steady-state curve do not imply two stable states: the upper branch can lose stability at a Hopf-type point before its fold. The window of two stable states is computed on an Arrhenius temperature path (24 K here), while sweep loops through that point depend on noise. All parameters are illustrative; no experimental data are used.

articles.title: Quantum-Assisted Recommender Algorithms for Financial Asset Recommendation: Theoretical Bounds and Empircal Validation
articles.abstract: We present a unified, practical pipeline for a quantum-assisted financial recommender system. Investor similarity graphs are constructed from high-dimensional profiles, compressed via normalized Laplacian spectral embedding, and optimized using the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) on GPU-based quantum simulators (cuQuantum, Cirq-GPU, Cirq with IonQ simulation). We consolidate theoretical derivations (QUBO/Ising mapping, spectral compression correctness, QAOA parameter optimization) and implementation details (feature selection, Nyström extension, QAOA parameter optimization). The key contribution is a unified theoretical framework that directly connects QAOA optimization to classification performance, eliminating disjoint post-processing steps. We provide complete, rigorous proofs of all error bounds, including a variance bound for QAOA concentration, an explicit treatment of the degree-matrix discrepancy, unbalanced misclassification, effective VC dimension, and the QAOA approximation ratio. Two explicit caveats are documented: (i) the overcomplete feature regime is rank-deficient, with generalization controlled solely by the downstream bottleneck and dropout; and (ii) the unconstrained PAC bound is vacuous for target accuracies above roughly (15%), which formally motivates the Laplacian-constrained effective VC dimension. Results show that spectral compression enables tractable quantum optimization for mid-sized problems and that Cirq-GPU offers a favorable speed-accuracy trade-off. We discuss deployment considerations for financial institutions, including explainability, compliance, and workflows under the likely hybrid classical-quantum architecture. Mathematics Subject Classification (2020) 68Q12 · 81P68 · 91G10 · 68T05 · 90C27

articles.title: Analytical and Interlaboratory Evaluation of an Adapted Procedure for 210Pb Determination by Alpha Spectrometry in Mangrove Sediments
articles.abstract: An adapted procedure for indirect ²¹⁰Pb determination through ²¹⁰Po alpha spectrometry in mangrove sediments was evaluated for analytical performance and interlaboratory comparability, including the influence of analytical differences on CF–CS-derived sediment accumulation rates. Analytical performance was assessed using blanks, minimum detectable activity, ²⁰⁹Po recovery, and IAEA-412 reference material. Comparison of 46 sediment sections between LABTOX-UES and IAEA-MEL showed statistical compatibility for 80.4% of paired results. York regression indicated a slope compatible with unity but a significantly negative intercept, precluding complete analytical equivalence. Nevertheless, surface mass and sediment accumulation rates showed no significant interlaboratory differences, supporting the procedure under the evaluated conditions.

articles.title: Experimental Synthesis, Characterization, and Numerical Device Simulation of Hydrazinium–Methylammonium Mixed Lead Bromide Perovskites for Solar Cell Applications
articles.abstract: Mixed-cation lead bromide perovskite thin films and powders with composition HA(1−x)MAxPbBr3 (x = 0.0, 0.20, 0.40) were synthesised via solution-processed spin-coating and comprehensively characterised to elucidate the role of methylammonium (MA+) incorporation in hydrazinium (HA+) lead bromide perovskites. XRD analysis revealed a progressive hexagonal-to-tetragonal phase transition with increasing MA+ content, accompanied by crystallite size reduction from 86.68 ± 5.99 nm to 61.26 ± 11.59 nm and concurrent increases in dislocation density and microstrain. SEM confirmed morphological evolution from agglomerated nanoparti cles (88.61 ± 23.43 nm) in pristine HAPbBr3 to a refined homogeneous nanostructure (72.41 ± 16.40 nm) in HA0.6MA0.4PbBr3, while EDX confirmed stoichiometric compositions and successful A-site cation mixing. FTIR and Raman spectroscopy verified co incorporation of both cations within the intact PbBr4− 6 octahedral framework. UV–Vis spectrophotometry revealed direct bandgaps of 2.9565, 2.9339, and 2.3075 eV for x = 0, 0.20, and 0.40, respectively, demonstrating continuous bandgap tunability via a two-stage mechanism of chemical A-site perturbation and phase-transition-driven bandgap collapse. Urbach energy decreased monotonically from 0.2112 to 0.1902 eV, indicating progressive band-edge quality improvement. Hall effect measurements showed carrier mobility increasing from 71.86 to 143.2 cm2 V−1 s−1 and conductivity from 1.078×10−5 to 2.278×10−5 Ω−1 cm−1 for HA0.6MA0.4PbBr3. Using experimentally determined parameters, seventeen solar-cell architectures (SC1–SC17) were evaluated by SCAPS-1D simu lation, employing HAPbBr3 and HA0.8MA0.2PbBr3 as electron transport layers and HA0.6MA0.4PbBr3 as the absorber layer. The highest PCE of 32.18% was achieved by Cs2InSbCl6-based devices (SC3 and SC8) with NiO hole transport layers, while HA0.6MA0.4PbBr3 single-absorber cells (SC11–SC13) attained the highest fill factors (>82%) among all architectures. Temperature (300–420 K) and back-contact work function (4.8–6.0 eV) analyses confirmed the thermal robustness and contact tolerance of the devices, establishing HA(1−x)MAxPbBr3 as a promising candidate for next-generation tandem photovoltaic applications.

articles.title: Rational Design and Synthesis of Porous Organic Polymers for Targeted Adsorptive Separation of Model Organic Pollutants
articles.abstract: Porous organic polymers (POPs) are promising adsorbents for organic contaminants, but their powdery form hinders recovery and practical deployment. Here, an imine- and aromatic-rich porous organic polymer (TFB/2-AP POP) was synthesized from 1,3,5-triformylbenzene and o-aminophenol by a solvothermal route, with an optimized monomer mass ratio of 4:3. The resulting POP powder showed a BPA adsorption capacity of 215.49 mg∙g− 1. To overcome the handling and recycling limitations of the powder, natural loofah sponge and cellulose sponge were evaluated as macroscopic supports, and an easily recoverable POP@cellulose sponge (POP@CS) monolith was fabricated by ultrasound-assisted loading. POP particles were uniformly distributed on the cellulose sponge skeleton while the interconnected channels were retained. Under neutral conditions, POP@CS achieved an equilibrium adsorption capacity of 171.18 mg∙g− 1 and removed more than 98% of BPA within 6 h at an adsorbent dosage of 0.4 g∙L− 1. The composite maintained strong adsorption over pH 3–11 and reached a maximum capacity of 227.15 mg∙g− 1 at pH 9. Adsorption followed the pseudo-second-order kinetic model and the Freundlich isotherm model. Common coexisting ions caused less than a 25% decrease in BPA removal, and more than 88% of the initial removal performance was retained after five adsorption–desorption cycles. Mechanistic analysis indicated synergistic contributions from π–π electron donor–acceptor interactions, hydrogen bonding, electrostatic attraction, and hierarchical-channel-enhanced mass transfer. This work provides a simple strategy for transforming high-performance POP powders into recyclable monolithic adsorbents for practical removal of phenolic organic pollutants from water.

articles.title: Finite-Key Security Analysis of MP-QKD under Trojan-horse Attacks
articles.abstract: Trojan-horse attack (THA) pose a serious threat to the practical security of quantum key distribution by leaking source-encoding information through back-reflected probe light. Although mode-pairing QKD (MP-QKD) can overcome the conventional rate–distance limit, its finite-key security under THA has not been systematically investigated. In this work, we develop a unified framework for analyzing the finite-key security of decoy-state MP-QKD with source-side leakage. Based on the reference-state method and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, we introduce a leakage parameter to quantify the deviation between practical emitted states and ideal reference states, and derive statistical constraints that enable valid decoy-state parameter estimation. We further obtain an explicit and computable finite-key secret-key-rate formula by incorporating statistical fluctuation analysis. Numerical simulations show that both side-channel leakage and finite-size effects reduce the achievable secret-key rate and maximum secure transmission distance, while the degradation becomes less significant for weak leakage or a sufficiently large number of transmitted pulses. These results provide a rigorous basis for evaluating and improving the practical security of MP-QKD systems against Trojan-horse attacks.

articles.title: Graphene Nanoribbon Sensors for Prosthetic Socket Wear-Time Monitoring: A Lambert W Function Framework
articles.abstract: Objective measurement of prosthetic socket use, encompassing wear time together with the pressures, strains, and microclimate at the limb--socket interface, would strengthen prosthetic rehabilitation research by complementing self-report measures, which are prone to recall error and social desirability bias. Existing thermal wear-time sensors face a fundamental limitation inside prosthetic sockets: the silicone liner worn over the residual limb attenuates body heat, and in the Limbkit study of 3D-printed sockets a validated commercial temperature microsensor consequently recorded zero wear time despite reported daily use of SIrange1115hour. Here we present a theoretical framework based on graphene nanoribbon (GNR) quantum sensors that addresses this limitation through the Lambert~W function branch-point enhancement mechanism, with sensitivity scaling as liner-attenuated differentials with millikelvin-scale noise-equivalent temperature differences, and that instrumenting the liner itself removes the thermal barrier entirely. A multi-modal architecture sensing temperature, pressure, strain, and humidity provides redundant wear classification and a route toward monitoring skin health at the interface.

articles.title: Mechanochemically covalently functionalized hexagonal boron nitride with proanthocyanidins for high-performance cellulose packaging toward fresh fruit preservation
articles.abstract: Pristine cellulose paper is a biodegradable packaging material, yet it fails to regulate the internal microenvironment of fruit packages, lacking adequate antioxidant activity and sufficient gas/moisture barrier performance. Although hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) and proanthocyanidins (PACI) can individually modify cellulose, PACI tends to self-aggregate in pulp and h-BN sheets stack severely, hindering uniform dispersion. We employ solvent-free mechanochemical ball-milling to graft PACI onto exfoliated few-layer h-BN, yielding h-BN-g-PACI hybrid fillers with a high grafting ratio of 66.7%. Comprehensive characterizations confirm the formation of stable B-O-C covalent linkages. The composite paper, fabricated via standard paper-making, with 40 wt% filler loading exhibits uniformly dispersed fillers, resulting in a tensile strength of 70 MPa (2.33 times that of pristine paper) and thermal conductivity of 1.954 W/m·K (6.76 times), alongside superior UV-shielding, surface hydrophobicity, and DPPH radical-scavenging activity. Moreover, the composite paper demonstrates improved resistance to moisture permeation. Ambient storage tests on cherry tomatoes reveal that the paper synergistically moderates temperature fluctuations, blocks moisture escape, and inhibits oxidative degradation, significantly reducing fruit weight loss, soluble solids accumulation, and mold growth. This scalable, eco-friendly fabrication approach offers a biodegradable multifunctional cellulose material as a promising alternative to petroleum-based plastic films for fresh fruit preservation.

articles.title: Conventional to Agroecological Vegetable Production: Five-Year Evidence on Productivity, Profitability, Variability and Whitefly Management under Smallholder Conditions in Southwest Ethiopia
articles.abstract: Smallholder vegetable production in Ethiopia often relies on synthetic inputs, while multi-year on-farm evidence on agroecological alternatives remains scarce. We evaluated a five-year (2021–2025) transition from conventional management (2021) to an agroecological package (2022–2025) on a multi-plot vegetable farm at the Eladale research site of Jimma University, southwest Ethiopia. From 2022 onward, synthetic fertilizers and insecticides were replaced with animal manure and garlic maceration, alongside crop diversification, rotation, and marigold companion planting in pepper and tomato plots. All eight crops showed significantly higher annual revenue under agroecological management than at baseline, whereas mean harvest increased in 30 of 32 comparisons (p < 0.0001). All crops profit margins increased, by up to about 18.5 percentage points. Since implied unit prices rose approximately three to five fold, these economic gains are nominal and partly price-driven. Monte Carlo simulation (1,000 iterations per crop) indicated wider revenue variability for pepper, carrot and garlic, than for beetroot and onion. Carrot had the highest fertilizer-use productivity (14.2 kg/kg), whereas garlic and pepper had the highest prices (170 and 85 ETB/kg). A composite stress index for conventional management was highest for tomato (0.62 units/kg) and pepper (0.37) and lowest for carrot (0.16). Whitefly was recorded in pepper and tomato in 2021, in 2022 only in tomato, and not in 2023–2025. The findings suggest association, rather than causation, as the agroecological practices were applied jointly without replication or untreated controls. The agroecological transition appears productive and viable, with crop selection weigh returns, risk and input efficiency.

articles.title: Landscape-Scale Assessment of Gully Erosion Distribution in the Tashkent Region, Uzbekistan: Elevation, Basin, and Anthropogenic Controls
articles.abstract: Gully erosion is a major but poorly documented driver of land degradation across the irrigated plains and foothill zones of Central Asia. This study presents the first comprehensive, landscape-scale inventory of gully erosion in the Tashkent region, Uzbekistan (14,995.7 km²), combining high-resolution imagery (Google Earth Pro) with GIS-based landscape mapping (ArcGIS) and field verification. Gullies were manually digitized and analyzed across 50 landscape units, four major river basins (Syrdarya, Chirchiq, Ohangaron, and Gijigen), and successive elevation zones. Gullies occupy 345.4 km² (2.30%) of the study area overall, yet reach 30–40% of surface area within individual landscape units, particularly in foothill zones between 300 and 600 m a.s.l. The Gijigen and Chirchiq basins account for the largest share of regional gully area (30.5% and 29.8%, respectively), while Gijigen shows the highest within-basin gully density (10.90%). The results indicate a significant relationship between gully prevalence and both elevation zonality and irrigation-related land use. These findings provide the first empirical baseline for basin-level erosion management in the Tashkent region and demonstrate that even landscapes of modest overall extent can host severe, spatially concentrated degradation, supporting targeted soil conservation planning in the irrigated foothill environments of Central Asia.

articles.title: Spatial non-stationary relationship between temperature and precipitation variation patterns and drought in the southwestern Caspian Sea
articles.abstract: One of the consequences of temperature and precipitation variation is drought, the continuation of which is accompanied by destructive environmental effects and depletes surface and groundwater resources. In this study, the most significant consequence of variation in temperature and precipitation—namely, drought—is examined and analyzed. To this end, the required data were first obtained from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) at a spatial resolution of 0.25° × 0.25° for a 44-year period (1980 to 2023). Subsequently, the trends in the SPI and RDI indices were determined using the Mann-Kendall trend test, and the Anselin Local Moran’s I (ALMI) statistic was employed to identify the type of their spatial patterns. In addition, ordinary least squares (OLS) regression was used to determine the relationship and harmony of the variables across Guilan Province. The results showed that the RDI index exhibited a negative, decreasing trend in the months of March, May, June, and August. Furthermore, the results of this analysis regarding the mean SPI index indicate a negative trend during the months of May, June, and August; it should also be noted that the intensity of both the RDI and SPI indices increased during the period. Given that average precipitation during the months of May, June, and August follows a decreasing trend, a corresponding decreasing trend in the drought indices has also become significant. In addition to a negative trend in the mean RDI index for the months of March, May, June, and August, a negative trend in the RDI index for all cells during these months was also confirmed. Furthermore, the results obtained from the MK trend test for the SPI index of the cells in August confirm a negative trend, which is consistent with the findings from the same test applied to the mean SPI index for August. In this regard, spatial analysis of the RDI and SPI drought index trend test indicates that the high-high (HH) and low-low (LL) cluster patterns have formed as separate zones in different parts of the province, from the plains to the mountains and from east to west, in March, May, June, and August. Also, a very good spatial relationship was obtained between SPI and precipitation in all months of the year (except October). Furthermore, the spatial relationship between the variables RDI and precipitation, as well as between RDI and SPI, was significant at the 0.05 level during certain months. Overall, it can be stated that non-random behavior governs the spatial patterns of the RDI and SPI indices as well as precipitation, and there is a notable spatial correspondence among them.

articles.title: A spin-crossover route to charge ordering in Fe4O5
articles.abstract: Charge order reflects a delicate balance between localization and itinerancy, yet the microscopic parameters that control this balance remain poorly understood. Here we identify spin crossover as a route to control charge order in mixed-valence Fe4O5. Using single-crystal X-ray diffraction and synchrotron Mössbauer source spectroscopy to 112 GPa at room temperature, we reveal three previously unreported charge-ordered phases associated with two site-selective spin crossovers. The first two phases are characterized by Fe-Fe dimers, whereas the highest-pressure phase hosts isolated planar bent Fe trimers, a motif not previously reported in iron oxides. All three charge-ordered phases are confined to mixed spin state regimes: charge order emerges as an octahedral Fe site enters spin crossover, persists while high-spin and low-spin states coexist on that site, and vanishes once the crossover is complete. Between the two spin crossovers, a charge-disordered phase in which high-spin and low-spin iron occupy different sites shows that spin-state heterogeneity within a single site is required for ordering. We propose that near spin-state degeneracy, enhanced charge-lattice coupling favours localization and stabilizes charge order. Our results establish spin crossover as an externally tunable route to stabilizing and controlling charge order in mixed-valence materials.

articles.title: Development of preparation method for Tc-99m labelled bamboo biomass radiotracer for its use in pyrolysis reactor
articles.abstract: The objective of this study is preparation of Tc-99m labelled bamboo biomass or bamboo shreds as radiotracer for its eventual use in measurements of flow dynamics in pyrolysis reactors. The bamboo shreds were chemically modified and radiolabeled using short lived radioisotope Tc-99m. The labeled bamboo shreds were characterized for analysis of morphology, crystallinity/amorphous nature, surface functionality and quantitative analysis of transfer of adsorbate using SEM, XRD, FTIR and neutron activation analysis (NAA), respectively. The radiolabeling experiments were performed at different pH of solution, temperature, different concentration of precursors and effect of reducing agent. The experimental condition was optimized for maximum transfer of Tc-99m as pertechnetate onto the shreds. Perrhenate as a non-radioactive analogue of pertechnetate was used as surrogate to investigate the adsorption kinetics as well as to characterize the adsorbed shreds. Freundlich model showed best fit with experimental result for describing the adsorption phenomena. Based on experimentally-determined value of enthalpy, the adsorption was found to be physisorption in nature.

articles.title: In-catalysts based on porous aromatic frameworks for the liquid-phase CO2 hydrogenation to methanol
articles.abstract: The catalytic hydrogenation of carbon dioxide into valuable petrochemical products and fuel components is a promising approach to its utilization. One of the most important products of this reaction is methanol, which is used both for the production of various chemicals and as an alternative fuel. Recently, In-based catalysts have emerged as promising systems for the hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol. However, the challenge of tuning the morphology of the active phase particles and selecting suitable supports and media for efficient catalytic performance remains a key issue. Herein, In-catalysts based on the porous aromatic framework PAF-20 and its aminated analogue PAF-20-NH2 were synthesized and tested in the liquid-phase hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol for the first time. The structure of the materials and catalysts was established using low temperature N2 adsorption, elemental analysis, FTIR spectroscopy, TEM and XPS. According to XPS data, a short reduction time facilitates the formation of oxygen vacancies in the structure of In-catalysts. The influence of reaction temperature, hydrogen pressure, indium content, and reaction media on the catalytic activity was systematically studied. In–PAF-20 demonstrated the highest methanol production rate of 435 mgMeOH gIn−1 h− 1 at 60 atm and 275°C, while in a subcritical ethanol In–PAF-20-NH2 exhibited methanol production rate of 507 mgMeOH gIn−1 h− 1. Both catalysts retained their activity over five reuse cycles.

articles.title: HMTS-YOLO: Detection of Weed Apex and Root/Stem-Base Treatment Regions for Precision Laser Weeding
articles.abstract: Under complex field backgrounds, weed apex and root treatment regions are readily affected by soil texture, surface cracks, target-scale variation, and morphological differences, resulting in missed detections, false detections, and bounding-box regression errors, particularly for small-scale and elongated targets. To improve dual-class treatment-region detection for field weeds, a dataset comprising 4,582 images and 13,421 bounding boxes was curated from existing field images and treatment-region annotations, and HMTS-YOLO (Hierarchical Morphology-aware Texture-Suppression YOLO) was developed using YOLOv8s as the baseline. The proposed model introduces STS-C2f, LDM-C2f, and DMA-SPPF at the P2, P3, and P5 feature levels, respectively. These modules improve feature representation across target scales and morphologies through shallow-layer soil-texture suppression, mid-level dual-morphology detail enhancement, and deep multi-scale context modeling. On the validation set, HMTS-YOLO achieved a Precision of 72.736%, Recall of 68.988%, mAP50 of 73.129%, and mAP50-95 of 35.177%, representing improvements of 3.619, 2.665, 4.341, and 4.514 percentage points, respectively, over the baseline. The model contains 11.572 M parameters and requires 69.157 GFLOPs. Class-wise evaluation showed that the mAP50-95 values for apex and root reached 42.212% and 28.142%, respectively, corresponding to gains of 4.969 and 4.059 percentage points over the baseline.
