These results demonstrate that feature-level mechanisms for texture suppression, morphology modeling, and contextual fusion can effectively improve the overall detection performance of apex and root treatment regions in complex field scenes.

articles.title: Planar low-overhead quantum memories with only nearest-neighbour gates
articles.abstract: High-performance quantum low-density parity-check codes promise substantial reductions in the overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computation, but most constructions require long-range connectivity or qubit shuttling, both of which are difficult to realise in superconducting architectures. Here we introduce a family of quantum low-density parity-check codes that, for the first time, combines planar open-boundary layouts, finite-size ad- vantages over surface codes, and syndrome extraction using only nearest-neighbour gates on a planar grid of qubits with either square or hexagonal connectivity. The resulting circuits achieve optimal constant-depth sta- biliser measurement, independent of code size, and naturally enable periodic leakage removal by exchanging the roles of check and data qubits between syndrome-extraction rounds. We find finite-size instances such as a [[323, 14, 15]] code, whose code-efficiency ratio is nearly an order of magnitude larger than that of rotated surface-code patches. At around 40 circuit qubits per logical qubit, the best directional tile-code layouts reduce the per-logical per-round logical error rate by a factor of 100 relative to rotated surface-code memories. These results show that the advantages of quantum low-density parity-check codes can survive compilation into strictly planar nearest-neighbour circuits, bringing low-overhead fault-tolerant memories closer to near-term hardware.

articles.title: Structural Housing Features, Exposure Context, and Wildfire Damage Severity in California's Wildland–Urban Interface
articles.abstract: California CAL FIRE Damage Inspection (DINS) records from fire-impacted areas (analytic N = 89,826; 298 incidents) do not support a simple “code materials always help” story once exposure context sits in the model. A pre-specified confirmatory set of nine literature terms, with Holm correction on those nine rather than on 56 kitchen-sink dummies, keeps tile roofing (odds ratio [OR] = 0.55), enclosed eaves (OR = 0.74), wood siding (OR = 0.57), local canopy, Wildfire Risk to Communities (WRC) Direct exposure (OR = 1.76), and recorded defense (OR = 0.62) after incident-clustered standard errors. Metal roofing is an honest null (OR = 1.08). Neighborhood density’s clustered interval (OR = 1.38, 0.99–1.92) is compatible with no effect to a large one and does not travel from South to North. Combustible siding destruction rises from 61% to 96% across density tertiles, while wood’s protective-direction association strengthens in dense neighborhoods. An extended-binary CatBoost ensemble is kept for those density-gated siding bends and two residual phenotypes—packed low-canopy survivors (n = 289, three fires) and sparse hardened losses (n = 379)—not as a second odds-ratio table. Weather enters as a three-variable principal component analysis (PCA) with elevation held out as a geographic control. Incident-held-out leave-one-fire-out quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) is ≈ 0.48; random-split QWK ≈ 0.73–0.77 is in-fire discrimination only. McFadden R² = 0.1738. Associations are post-inspection and under exposure context—not measured ember flux and not a retrofit prescription.

articles.title: Finite Element Analysis of Residual Stress in Cu-20Sn-10Ti Alloy Brazed Diamond
articles.abstract: The interfacial thermal stress in brazed diamond tools originates from the mismatch of thermal expansion coefficients among constituent materials; non-coordinated deformation induced by temperature-field variations leads to thermal-stress concentration. Interfacial residual compressive stress can enhance the holding force of the brazing filler on diamond grits, but excessively high interfacial residual stress may induce cracks and reduce the service life of diamond tools. To accurately characterize the interfacial stress distribution, this study takes single-layer diamond brazed with Cu-20Sn-10Ti filler alloy as the research object. A three-dimensional thermo-mechanical coupled finite element model comprising diamond, the Cu-Sn-Ti filler layer and a 45-steel substrate was established using ABAQUS, and the residual-stress distribution under different brazing temperatures (850–1050°C) and holding times (1–9 min) was systematically simulated. The results show that both brazing temperature and holding time exhibit a nonlinear trend of first decreasing and then increasing. At 950°C and 7 min the residual stress reaches minimum values of 417.3 MPa and 402.1 MPa (FEM), respectively, or 463 MPa (Raman measurement); 950°C / 7 min is thus identified as the optimal process window. Raman spectroscopy verifies the reliability of the finite element simulation: the measured and simulated values share the same trend, fully confirming the accuracy of the method. Grinding tests show that, under the 950°C/7 min process, diamond grits exhibit a moderate micro-fracture ratio, combining good self-sharpening ability with bond strength, and the tool achieves optimal wear resistance. This study provides a scientific basis for the control of residual stress and process optimization of brazed diamond tools.

articles.title: Optimally Weighted Constrained Shadow Tomography for Reduced Density Matrices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01079v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate measurement of reduced density matrices (RDMs) is central to quantum simulations of many-fermion systems, but the required measurement resources remain a significant challenge. Constrained shadow tomography (CST) combines randomized measurements with N-representability conditions to reconstruct physically valid RDMs from limited measurement data. Here we improve CST by orthogonalizing the measurement constraints and using the resulting singular values to determine the relative weight of each independent measurement direction according to how strongly it is sampled by the quantum computer. These optimally weighted constraints are incorporated into the semidefinite program through a least-squares objective implemented with a Schur-complement relaxation. We demonstrate the approach for hydrogen chains on a quantum simulator and for azobenzene on a quantum processor. In both cases, optimally weighted CST systematically improves the accuracy of the reconstructed 2-RDM without increasing the measurement budget, providing a more measurement-efficient approach to partial tomography for quantum simulations of correlated fermions.

articles.title: Programmable Droplets as Active Matter in a Reconfigurable Environment
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01277v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Exploring systems that bridge the gap between non living and living matter requires a reconfigurable environment coupled to synthetic systems capable of autonomous motion, adaptive behaviour and persistent dynamics. Self propelled droplets provide a minimal platform for such life like behaviour, but quantitative measures capturing both persistence and adaptability to enable closed loop reconfiguration remain lacking. Here we introduce an autonomous closed loop robotic platform to characterise and dynamically program the autonomous behaviour of multicomponent oil in water droplets. We explored two chemical composition spaces, with and without external pH perturbations, analysing droplet behaviour in real time and iteratively selecting formulations. To quantify this behaviour, we introduce two descriptors, persistence and diversity. Persistence is quantified by mapping temporal dynamics in a speed shape complexity space, where we identify a persistence domain that distinguishes active from inactive droplets. Diversity captures spontaneous or environmentally induced variation in motion and the propensity of droplets to reorient or adapt under perturbation. We show that persistence and diversity are constrained by a behavioural trade off: high persistence limits diversity, whereas high diversity reduces persistent activity. Our results provide a quantitative framework for navigating and programming life like behaviours in active droplets and show how closed-loop experimentation can uncover organising principles in complex active matter.

articles.title: Convergence of many-body truncations in the in-medium similarity renormalization group
articles.abstract: arXiv:2611.01458v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The in-medium similarity renormalization group (IMSRG) is a leading ab initio method for describing atomic nuclei. Most applications truncate the flowing operators at the normal-ordered two-body level, neglecting induced higher-body terms. Convergence with increasing operator rank remains poorly understood, particularly in strongly correlated systems. We systematically assess the many-body truncation hierarchy in the single-reference and multi-reference IMSRG, retaining normal-ordered operators through the four-body and three-body levels, respectively. Using an exactly solvable pairing-plus-particle-hole model, we quantify successive higher-body corrections over a broad range of interaction strengths, spanning weakly to strongly correlated regimes. The multi-reference formulation exhibits faster and more robust convergence than its single-reference counterpart, with the advantage becoming most pronounced at strong coupling. In this regime, higher-rank irreducible density matrices play an essential role in achieving convergence of the many-body expansion.

articles.title: Unlocking n-alk-1-ynes Conformers: Quantum "Trigger Finger" versus "Stiff Joint" Conformations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.02470v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Molecular conformation in n-alk-1-ynes (CnA) is conventionally simplified to an all-planar structure. We report a comprehensive quantum chemical analysis revealing two near-isoenergetic rotamers at the acetylenic terminus: planar (Cₛ) and skewed (C₁). The high, symmetric rotational energy barrier (approx 150,meV) arises from unique steric relief near the sp center coupled with electronic stabilization of C₁. This creates a unique kinetic profile: a Quantum ``Trigger Finger'' (α rotation) that enforces an approx 50%:,50% Cₛ/C₁ ensemble, sharply contrasting with the thermodynamically biased ``Stiff Joint'' (δ rotation) of the alkyl chain. This structural degeneracy necessitates ensemble averaging for spectroscopic data interpretation, while the slow interconversion permits kinetic trapping and intentional conformer enrichment during synthesis and molecular junction fabrication. Our work redefines the alkyne anchor, providing a blueprint for accurate interpretation of spectroscopic data and achieving conformational control in molecular electronics.

articles.title: Symmetry-Protected Topological Structures in Quantum Many-Body Scar Subspaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.11216v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate how symmetry-associated topological properties, originally defined for ground states, can be consistently extended to dynamically isolated subspaces of quantum many-body systems. Focusing on quantum many-body scars (QMBS), we show that a scar subspace is invariant under the relevant symmetries, and it can support well-defined topological properties inherited from an underlying symmetry-protected topological (SPT) ground state, even though individual scar states need not themselves be symmetric. We refer to such structures as SPT-like scar subspaces, emphasizing that the topological properties are defined at the level of the symmetry-invariant subspace rather than on a state-by-state basis. As a concrete example, we analyze the spin-1 Affleck--Kennedy--Lieb--Tasaki (AKLT) model, where a restricted spectrum-generating algebra (rSGA) generates a tower of QMBS on top of a nontrivial SPT ground state admitting a matrix product state (MPS) representation. We demonstrate that the resulting symmetry-invariant scar subspace inherits well-defined topological characteristics, encoded in bond-space symmetry representations, expectation values of symmetry-twist operators, and long-range string order in the dilute regime. We further show that these features persist in a broader class of models, including deformations and higher-spin generalizations that preserve the relevant symmetries and admit nontrivial SPT ground states with MPS representations. Our results provide a general framework in which symmetry-associated topological properties, while inherited from the ground state, are consistently realized at the level of symmetry-invariant nonthermal subspaces. This perspective clarifies how topological structures can be meaningfully defined beyond individual eigenstates.

articles.title: Non-invertible symmetries and mixed anomalies from equations of motion in (3+1)D twisted BF topological quantum field theories
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.01523v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a systematic study on the topological operators that generate invertible and non-invertible higher-form symmetries in left(3+1right)D twisted BF topological quantum field theories (TQFTs). We focus on the twisted BF theories with gauge group G=prodᵢ ZN_ᵢ and an awedge awedge b twist, where a's and b are 1-form and 2-form gauge fields, respectively. These theories realize non-Abelian (3+1)D TQFTs supporting Borromean-Rings braiding and describe three-dimensional non-Abelian topological orders in condensed matter. For G=(Z₂)³, a microscopic realization is given by the D₄ Kitaev quantum double model. Starting from the equations of motion (EoMs), we construct gauge invariant operators that are supported on closed submanifolds, hence are genuine topological operators. Some of them are associated with nontrivial Hilbert spaces which are the projective representation spaces of specific gauge subgroups, thus being non-invertible. The others are invertible topological operators with group-like fusion rules. The fusion rules of non-invertible topological operators correspond to the decomposition of the product of the projective representation spaces. We provide a field-theoretical algorithm to calculate the fusion rules. Besides, we identify an obstruction to retaining a non-invertible topological operator after gauging an invertible symmetry, and derive the constraints on pairs of non-invertible operators relevant to simultaneous gauging. Our results give a unified and practical approach for identifying and characterizing higher-form symmetries and mixed anomalies, which can be extended to more general TQFTs and topological orders.

articles.title: Electric Field Gradients in Multiconfigurational Embedded-Cluster Calculations of Solids
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.07098v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The electric field gradients (EFGs) at the (non-spherical) nucleus contribute to atomic and molecular hyperfine structure and govern Nuclear Electric field gradients (EFGs) at nuclei contribute to atomic hyperfine structure and govern Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance (NQR) and Mössbauer spectroscopy, providing a sensitive probe of local electronic structure and symmetry. EFGs can be obtained from electronic-structure calculations and inferred from spectroscopic measurements, linking theory and experiment. In this work, we use representative molecular and crystalline examples to examine selected factors that control calculated EFGs, with particular emphasis on multiconfigurational embedded-cluster calculations for solids. We analyze the sensitivity of EFGs to geometry and to computational choices including basis set, correlation treatment, and active-space construction. We also discuss differences in EFG tensor conventions adopted by commonly used quantum-chemistry codes and their implications for comparing computational results. Periodic calculations are used where appropriate as reference data for assessing the embedded-cluster description. Our results provide practical guidelines for the reliable computation and interpretation of EFGs as descriptors of the electronic structure and local chemical environment.

articles.title: Rationalizing defect formation energies in metals and semiconductors with semilocal density functionals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.05385v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The study of defects in materials is of utmost importance for technological applications and the design of new materials. In this work, we analyze the performance of density functional approximations on two prototypical sets of defective systems: monovacancies in eight fcc metals, and interstitials in the semiconductor Si-diamond. Specifically, we compute defect formation energies using the local density approximation, the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof generalized gradient approximation, the meta-generalized gradient approximations (meta-GGAs) strongly constrained and appropriately normed (SCAN), its regularized version (r2SCAN), the Lebeda-Aschebrock-Kummel (LAK) meta-GGA, and the Heyd-Scuseria-Ernzerhof screened hybrid functional. For metals, the local density approximation shows better performance compared to the other approximations, whereas for silicon, the meta-generalized gradient approximation Lebeda-Aschebrock-Kummel yields outstand- ing accuracy, surpassing the hybrid functional and approaching the results of more computationally demanding Quantum Monte Carlo methods. To rationalize the different performances, we study the semilocal ingredients rs, s and α in both the pristine and defective structures. We identify critical regions that indicate the observed trends of the defect formation energies and pave the way for improving density functional approximations.

articles.title: Imaging phase winding in topological superconductors with a fork-tip Josephson STM
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.38174v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The topological phase winding in a chiral superconductor remains challenging to access by conventional real-space probes. We propose a scheme to probe this winding with a fork-tip Josephson STM near an impurity, where two superconducting tips form an interferometer sensitive to phase differences between two positions. The phase winding remains accessible via the fork-tip critical current even if the relative phase between the fork-tip and sample fluctuates, establishing a route towards a local phase-sensitive STM probe of topological superconductivity. We numerically compute the interference pattern to demonstrate that the magnitude and phase of the order parameter can be reconstructed as a function of angle, providing a route towards resolving the longstanding open experimental problem of directly detecting phase winding in topological superconductors.

articles.title: Superconductivity in structurally complex σ-phase Re-X (X = V, Nb, Ta) and derived medium-entropy alloys
articles.abstract: Author(s): Pavan Kumar Meena and Tomasz Klimczuk The structurally complex tetragonal sigma (σ) phase provides a unique platform for investigating the interplay between chemical disorder, electronic structure, and superconductivity, particularly in Re-based alloys, in which unconventional superconductivity has been widely discussed. Here, the authors investigate superconductivity in σ-phase Re–X (X = V, Nb, and Ta) alloys, covering 3d, 4d, and 5d transition-metal substitutions, as well as in a derived medium-entropy alloy incorporating multiple transition metals. The narrow stability range of the σ phase highlights the sensitivity of its structural stabilization to chemical composition and valence electron concentration. Magnetization, electrical resistivity, and specific heat measurements establish bulk type-II superconductivity in all compounds. The electronic heat capacity is consistent with a fully gapped, weak-coupling BCS state. These findings highlight σ-phase Re-based alloys as model systems for exploring the roles of structural complexity, chemical disorder, and spin-orbit coupling in superconductivity. [Phys. Rev. Materials 10, 114802] Published Tue Nov 03, 2026

articles.abstract: Author(s): Kazumasa Ueno and Hiroaki Miura Quantum computing may help reduce computational costs of simulating large and nonlinear systems, but research into the use of quantum computers in atmospheric and oceanic sciences is still at an early stage. articles.title: Next generation of ultra-coarse-graining: Self-consistent inference of critical internal states
articles.abstract: Bottom-up coarse-graining systematically expands the length and effective timescales accessible to molecular dynamics simulations, but the information loss during coarse-graining can prevent an accurate incorporation of the multistate phenomena common in complex biomolecular dynamics. The Ultra-Coarse-Graining (UCG) method projects the influence of discrete “quantum-like” extended degrees of freedom, “internal states,” onto the coarse-grained (CG) mapped molecules, significantly extending the expressiveness of the CG model. The previous rapid-local-equilibrium (RLE) approximation in UCG depends on user-defined collective variables (CVs, e.g., local density) and does not incorporate correlations between internal states within and between CG molecules. We present Self-Consistent UCG (SC-UCG), an integrated methodology that utilizes the underlying UCG interactions directly for internal state designation, without designing collective variables in the CG ensemble. For simulations, the internal state probabilities are self-consistently determined via graph message-passing in simulation time. We also enhance the RLE Hamiltonian with the Bethe approximation plus AI-based inference to allow explicit internal state correlations between UCG beads. For forcefield training, we develop Multilayer Internal State Consistency, a machine-learning-based method derived from the relative entropy minimization principle that does not require iterative sampling of the intermediate forcefields. We then apply SC-UCG to a model tetramer system with a second-order symmetry-breaking phase transition from the supercritical racemic fluid into subcritical D-rich and L-rich fluids. We show that SC-UCG can capture collective switching events of internal UCG states in the subcritical region, and it exhibits temperature transferability by recapitulating the phase transition, even if trained from a single-temperature dataset.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Water–ice coexistence under nanoscale confinement revealed by magnetization-transfer NMR
articles.abstract: Low-temperature ice–liquid phase coexistence and nuclear magnetization exchange dynamics of water confined in the ordered mesoporous silica material KIT-5 were investigated by nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). The temporal evolution of the magnetization following the preparation of non-equilibrium spin states was measured over a range of temperatures to quantify magnetization exchange between the coexisting ice and liquid phases. The analysis of the NMR spectra yielded the phase fractions, spectral linewidths, and magnetization dynamics of both phases. The equilibrium phase fractions were used to determine the temperature dependence of the non-frozen layer thickness separating the silica surface from the ice core, which was found to be in good agreement with theoretical predictions. The magnetization exchange kinetics were quantitatively described by a diffusion model, yielding an effective diffusion coefficient in the order of 10 −16 m 2 /s for magnetization transport within the confined ice phase. Spin diffusion rates were estimated independently using several complementary approaches to assess the relative contributions of spin diffusion and molecular diffusion. While these estimates constrain the possible mechanisms of magnetization exchange, they do not permit an unambiguous separation of the spin diffusion and molecular diffusion contributions, suggesting that confinement-induced structural disorder may play an important role in magnetization transport in nanoconfined ice.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Tunable electron and spin transfer from ionized polythiophene oligomers encapsulated in cycling hydrocarbons: A combined DFT and EPR approach
articles.abstract: The structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of thiophene oligomer ions, which possess polarons excited on their main axis and are encapsulated within polyaromatic cyclic hydrocarbons, were investigated using density functional theory and electron paramagnetic resonance methods. Charge and spin densities, analyzed using Mulliken and Löwdin population analyses, reveal how cyclic rings locally affect the effective parameters of the dual organic π-systems. The energy gap of these composites depends on their structure and the reorientation of the polaron spin in a magnetic field and was identified as a key feature to tune electronic and magnetic properties. The appearance of equidistant peaks in population and energy dependencies was explained in terms of the concept of magic numbers, which are linked to symmetrical and conjugated clusters. Anisotropic hyperfine coupling and g -factor eigenvalues were shown to depend on the ionic charge and spin orientation in a magnetic field, as well as on the structural properties of the surrounding cyclic belt. Separate intermolecular transfer of electronic and spin clouds to the surrounding subsystem could potentially be used for independent control of the corresponding processes in all-organic molecular devices. This could provide a foundation for designing electronic and spintronic components with independently controlled charge and spin parameters.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Slowing down of carrier dynamics via temperature-controlled phase transition in two-dimensional ferroelectric CuInP 2 S 6
articles.abstract: The relaxation and recombination of photoexcited carriers directly determine the performance of optoelectronic devices and photocatalysts, and ferroelectric materials with spontaneous polarization may offer a unique route for modulating carrier lifetimes. Two-dimensional CuInP 2 S 6 (CIPS) exhibits ferroelectricity at room temperature. However, the mechanism by which the temperature-induced ferroelectric-to-paraelectric phase transition modulates the carrier dynamics in CIPS remains unclear. Herein, second-harmonic generation measurements are combined with broadband ultrafast spectroscopy to directly resolve temperature-induced phase transition in CIPS, clarifying how carrier dynamics evolve in the ferroelectric phase vs the paraelectric phase. Near the phase-transition region, the carrier lifetime exhibits a sudden and nearly twofold increase when transitioning from the paraelectric phase to the ferroelectric phase. By contrast, the carrier lifetime is only weakly affected by temperature outside this region. Electronic structure calculations and Raman spectroscopy indicate that the change in carrier lifetime is related not only to the intrinsic polarization field in the ferroelectric phase but is also closely associated with phase transition-induced modifications in the electron and phonon structures. The findings of this study provide a mechanistic basis for developing temperature-tunable and polarization-controlled behaviors for a broad range of light-related applications.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Atomic softness: The inherent empirical parameter calculated analytically for an atom-in-molecule by the conceptual DFT method
articles.abstract: By exploring our previously published gradient theorem [P. Ordon and L. Komorowski, in Chemical Reactivity: Volume 1: Theories and Principles , edited by S. Kaya, L. von Szentpaly, G. Serdaroglu, and L. Guo (Elsevier, 2023), Chap. 9], that provides a relationship of the gradient of the electron density function and the electric field with the softness kernel as the response function, we introduce the method for analytical calculation of the local softness as the trace of the electronic softness tensor and the global softness index of a molecule is obtained by its integration. The atomic contributions to the global softness have also been calculated analytically. These softness parameters for bonded atoms have been tested as the potential indicators of site reactivity in a collection of linear molecules. The analysis has been extended to the rational hypersoftness parameter dsr/dNv, the leading factor for calculations of the local hypersoftness s2r as well as the atomic contributions thereof.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: A new generation of effective core potentials: Selected heavy 5 d and 6 p elements
articles.abstract: We expand the correlation-consistent effective core potentials (ccECPs) library by developing semi-local pseudopotentials and matching basis sets for heavy elements from 5 d (Hf, Os, Hg) and 6 p (Tl, Po, At, Rn) blocks. To accurately capture scalar relativistic effects, spin–orbit coupling, and electron correlation effects, we implement a tiered core-valence partitioning strategy across three distinct resolutions. This includes a small 60-core (Hf, Os, Hg) that explicitly correlates subvalence shells, a large 78-core definition for the main-group elements that rigorously accounts for core polarization and relaxation effects in sparse valence environments, and an intermediate 68-core partition for Hg and Tl. This 68-core architecture represents a unique development in the ccECP library, optimizing the balance between accuracy and computational efficiency in a manner unexplored for lighter elements. Optimized against relativistic all-electron coupled-cluster theory with singles, doubles, and perturbative triples references, the ccECPs deliver outstanding atomic precision, achieving a global average atomic low-lying states deviation of just 0.045 eV. This accuracy translates directly to robust molecular transferability, systematically restricting dissociation energy discrepancies to under 0.03 eV and equilibrium bond lengths to within 0.005 Å. By enforcing a regularized, finite potential at the origin for enhanced numerical stability in stochastic quantum Monte Carlo methods, this library removes a critical methodological bottleneck for predictive many-body simulations of heavy-element systems and materials.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Probabilistic assessment of windblown sand hazard across a desert photovoltaic site using terrain-downscaled reanalysis winds
articles.abstract: Windblown sand hazard at desert photovoltaic (PV) sites is commonly assessed using coarse regional winds or local array scale experiments, leaving dune scale spatial variability poorly resolved. An hourly probabilistic framework was developed to resolve spatial variations in sand-drift potential. Dune morphology was derived from a digital elevation model, and hourly ERA5 winds for 2021–2023 were downscaled to 30 m using a conservation of mass solver. The downscaling method was independently validated and showed good agreement with field observations (r = 0.949). The downscaled winds were converted into hourly potential sand transport and aggregated into flux potential (FP) and other transport indicators. Uncertainty in threshold friction velocity and representative annual winds was propagated to PV subarray estimates through Monte Carlo simulation. Terrain downscaling produced acceleration over crests and upper slopes and deceleration in interdune and sheltered terrain. Dunes in more exposed surroundings exhibited higher overall FP, while local hotspots clustered near crests and upper windward slopes, where FP reached approximately three times the dune mean. High transport crest zones generally showed greater directional variability than lower leeward areas. Monte Carlo analysis broadened annual FP distributions without obscuring terrain-controlled spatial contrasts. The five activity classes remained clearly separated, with median FP decreasing from 71.88 m3 m− 1 yr− 1 in Class I to 60.40 m3 m− 1 yr− 1 in Class V, while the 5th percentile of Class I exceeded the 95th percentile of Class V. The framework supports targeted sand control planning in desert PV development.

articles.title: Scalable CVD Growth of Layered HfS2 Thin Films for Photodetector Applications
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation optoelectronic devices owing to their layer-dependent tunable band gaps and strong light–matter interactions. However, scalable growth of uniform, device-compatible HfS2 thin films with reliable photodetection performance remains challenging. In this work, scalable CVD-based layered HfS2 thin films were grown on Si/SiO2 (500 µm/300 nm) substrates using a three-zone chemical vapour deposition (CVD) process. Structural and chemical analyses using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) confirmed the formation of highly crystalline, c-axis-oriented, stoichiometric HfS2 layered thin films. The fabricated Al/HfS2/Al metal–semiconductor–metal (MSM) photodetectors exhibited a photocurrent density of approximately 6.20 × 10−4 Acm−2 at 5 V under 532 nm illumination with a power density of 0.25 W cm−2, compared with a dark current density of approximately 1.01 × 10−6 Acm−2, yielding a dark-to-light current ratio of 614 . The photodetector demonstrated a responsivity of approximately 0.61 mA W−1, an estimated shot-noise-limited specific detectivity of approximately ~1.1×109 Jones, and an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 0.14% at 5 V. The devices exhibited stable photoswitching over multiple illumination cycles, with rise and decay times of 160 ms and 310 ms, respectively, indicating a moderate yet reliable temporal response. These results show that scalable CVD-grown HfS2 films provide stable photoresponse and high detectivity, demonstrating their potential for optoelectronic photodetector applications.

articles.title: Water layers on ice submerged in antifreeze liquid: Nano-forcemetry
articles.abstract: Ice is an important material on Earth. However, despite the extensive research conducted on ice surfaces exposed to vacuum or vapor, studies of liquid–ice interfaces are limited. In this study, we used an atomic force microscope cooled to −10 °C to observe force–distance curves at the interfaces of ice and four antifreeze liquids: decane, octane, octanol, and saltwater (an aqueous solution of NaCl). The approach force curves recorded in decane and octane indicated the presence of liquid water layers on the ice wafers. Based on our accumulated knowledge of vacuum–ice interfaces, we hypothesized that the free OH groups on the ice exposed to the liquid alkanes would induce surface disordering of the ice and form a water layer. Force–distance curves observed in octanol and saltwater suggested that the ice wafers were directly exposed to these liquids without a water layer in between. The surface disordering of the ice may have been prevented in these liquids because they can form hydrogen bonds with the OH groups on the ice.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Combining exponential expansion theory with Bayesian inference for the analysis of inelastic scattering spectra
articles.abstract: Over the past decade, advances in inelastic x-ray and neutron scattering instrumentation have created a demand for probabilistically grounded data analysis. To address this, we proposed a Bayesian method that uses Monte Carlo techniques and a reversible jump routine to support the determination of the number of modes that contribute to the spectrum of density fluctuations S ( Q , ω ). So far, a similar approach has been applied to models that fail to satisfy the proper sum rules governing the moments of the distribution S ( Q , ω ), typically consisting of multiple damped harmonic oscillator modes, along with additional central peaks. We show that applying Bayesian inference to an exponential expansion theory-based model, which explicitly enforces the relevant sum rules, provides a rigorous and physically constrained framework for the analysis and interpretation of experimental spectra. In particular, this result enables analysis of the complex and relatively unstructured shape of terahertz inelastic spectra of disordered systems.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Tilt control of coverage heterogeneity for hard spherocylinders locked on a sphere
articles.abstract: We study hard spherocylinders on a sphere with axes rigidly locked to a tangential director field at fixed angle ω to the meridian, necessarily singular at the poles. Three lengths set the problem: the rod length ℓ , the diameter D , and the host radius R s . Monte Carlo simulations across 15 geometries and four coverages give two main results for the polar marginal, the azimuthal average of rod-center density. First, the tilt is a continuous handle on the width of the depleted region that packing induces around each singularity. Under meridian locking it is set principally by the rod length; turning the director toward the latitude contracts it substantially, the contraction being spent well before latitude locking. Second, how uniform the polar marginal can be made is limited by geometry, not tilt. The smallest variance on the sampled grid follows an empirical power law in ℓ 2 /( R s D ), which measures how far a straight rod’s ends stand off the curved surface in rod diameters, with an effective exponent between 1.10 and 1.31. Long rods on small hosts cannot be made uniform at any sampled tilt; the remedy is geometric, not orientational. The polar marginal is equator-heavy almost everywhere, inverting only at high coverage and tilt; meridian locking is the least uniform choice, and the variance-minimizing tilt usually lies in a sampled band from 31.7° to 55°. Both results describe the infinitely locked athermal ensemble.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Dilute-regime polymer thermophoresis from coil to globule via molecular dynamics simulations
articles.abstract: Particles (molecules, colloids, polymers, etc.) in solution migrate along a temperature gradient in a process called thermophoresis, thermodiffusion, or the Soret effect. Experiments have revealed many striking behaviors in dilute polymer solutions, including sign changes and extrema in the Soret coefficient S T as a function of solvent quality. We investigate the phenomenology of dilute-regime polymer thermophoresis using a minimal particle-based model that interpolates between a swollen coil and a compact globule, simulating various chain lengths. Our model exhibits sign changes in S T as a function of solvent quality, from thermophilic ( S T < 0) to thermophobic ( S T > 0) behavior, in both the good-solvent and poor-solvent regimes. To our knowledge, the latter has not been previously reported and occurs when increasing the monomer–monomer attraction. We correlate the increase/decrease of S T with that of the negative solvation entropy. Furthermore, our results highlight that the difference between the thermophoretic and drift velocities can be large, even for relatively large polymers approaching the long-polymer limit. We observe the counter-intuitive situation of a net drift against the direction of particle accumulation for portions of the good-, Θ-, and poor-solvent regimes.

articles.title: Pressure and temperature dependence of hydrogen-induced volume in fcc nickel hydride
articles.abstract: In transition-metal hydrides, hydrogen occupies interstitial sites in the metal lattice, resulting in significant volume expansion. The difference in unit-cell volume between the metal and its hydride is denoted as hydrogen-induced volume ( v H ), and this value has been determined for various metal hydrides. However, systematic investigations of its effects on thermoelastic properties under pressure ( P ) and temperature ( T ) are scarce, and the P – T -dependence of v H is poorly constrained. Here, we report the P – V – T relations of nickel hydride (H/Ni ∼ 1) with a face-centered cubic structure, which is frequently observed in 3 d transition metals and their hydrides. We collected x-ray diffraction data on nickel hydride at 7–16 GPa and 300–1000 K and determined its equations of state. We also conducted a melting experiment at 15 GPa and observed melting at 1450 K. The results show that nickel hydride is more compressible than pure Ni and exhibits a large thermal expansion, resulting in a negative dependence on pressure and a positive dependence on temperature of v H . This behavior originates from the reduction in bulk modulus and Debye temperature by hydrogenation, suggesting that interstitial H atoms weaken the Ni–Ni bonds through lattice expansion and possibly also through phonon softening, as evidenced by comparison at equivalent volumes.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Electrowetting: Contact angle saturation induced by non-local surface excess free energy
articles.abstract: Contact-angle saturation limits the high-voltage response of electrowetting-on-dielectric systems, but it is not captured by the classical Young–Lippmann relation. Here, we develop a composition-dependent interfacial energy-landscape model in which the liquid-covered and gas-covered parts of the substrate are described by adsorption-layer states with composition-dependent free energies and capacitive responses. The Young–Lippmann behavior is recovered at low voltage, while saturation emerges when the gas-covered adsorption layer becomes liquid-rich and the electrical contributions to the solid–liquid and solid–gas interfacial free energies decrease synchronously. The model provides analytical expressions for the onset voltage, saturation voltage, and saturated contact angle and separates the voltage scale from the terminal interfacial-energy contrast. Comparison with experimental data shows that the normalized electrowetting response is consistent with the proposed interfacial transition pathway. The resulting energy landscape can also contain metastable states, giving rise to path-dependent behavior during voltage withdrawal. Together, these results indicate that variations in the underlying interfacial parameters can regulate both the terminal wetting state and the overall electrowetting response.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Adsorption of patchy colloids on a patchy surface: A combined thermodynamic perturbation theory and Henderson–Abraham–Barker approach
articles.abstract: Reversible binding of ligands to their substrates is a common refrain in physics, chemistry, and other disciplines that features prominently in problems as diverse as the binding of proteins to membranes or passivating ligands depositing onto quantum dots. Here, we introduce a theoretical formalism to describe this phenomenon analytically with the help of very basic physical concepts. We assume that the ligands can be modeled as spherical particles that interact with each other via an attractive patch placed rigidly on their surface. The ligands are located above an infinite impenetrable surface with which they also interact via attractive patches. Therefore, the proposed model captures excluded volume of ligands, confinement in space, and adsorption to planes mediated by attractive forces—the three basic properties common to all complexation processes near surfaces. The Wertheim thermodynamic perturbation theory for associating fluids is extended to the proposed model utilizing the Henderson–Abraham–Barker-type approach. Analytical expressions are derived for the surface coverage as a function of various parameters such as temperature, ligand density, and others. Computer simulations are performed to test and confirm the accuracy of the theoretical predictions. Increasing ligand density is seen to enhance the surface coverage, while ligand–ligand interactions always lead to surface destabilization. Similarly, sticky patches on a surface in close proximity to each other negatively affect its ligand coverage. Our findings add new insight to the basic understanding of ligand–surface interactions, suggesting that the proposed model can be used as a powerful tool with which to design and analyze new surface-based materials.

articles.title: Vibrationally assisted dissociative ionization of H 2 + in orthogonal laser fields
articles.abstract: We present full-dimensional quantum simulations of H2+ dissociative ionization driven by strong orthogonal laser fields. We consider equal-frequency orthogonal components, which generate elliptical or circular polarization, depending on their relative phase and amplitude, as well as orthogonal 800 and 400 nm two-color fields. These two-dimensional fields strongly modify the fragmentation dynamics. Most notably, a secondary proton kinetic-energy-release (KER) peak at approximately 4–5 eV, generally negligible in height relative to the main peak in the single-color, linearly polarized reference, is strongly enhanced by the orthogonal fields studied here and becomes pronounced and comparable in height with the main peak. The yield of this peak can be coherently controlled by varying the relative carrier-envelope phase of the perpendicular field component. The perpendicular field also disrupts the clear electron–proton energy-sharing pattern observed in the main 3–3.5 eV dissociation channel, indicating more complex multichannel dynamics. Time-dependent state projections and calculations initiated from individual excited states attribute the additional peak to laser-induced vibrational excitation of H2+. The added high-KER yield provides a concrete microscopic mechanism that may contribute to the broader, flatter proton KER distribution observed experimentally under circular polarization, even when the secondary peak is not individually resolved. Furthermore, the perpendicular field rotates the fragment angular distributions, causing the most probable proton and electron emission directions to deviate substantially from the principal z axis. These findings demonstrate that the spatial and temporal geometry of orthogonal laser fields provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling ultrafast electron–nuclear dynamics.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Vibrational spectra and anharmonic coupling of the O–H stretch in 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline: Insights from constrained nuclear–electronic orbital theory
articles.abstract: Hydrogen bonds can exhibit pronounced nuclear quantum effects (NQEs) that strongly influence proton-transfer dynamics. 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline (HBQ) is a prototypical excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT) system with a strong intramolecular hydrogen bond, and its vibrational spectra and anharmonic mode couplings have recently attracted considerable interest. Here, we use constrained nuclear–electronic orbital density functional theory (CNEO-DFT) and molecular dynamics (CNEO-MD), which account for NQEs, particularly nuclear quantum delocalization effects, to investigate the O–H stretching vibration (νOH) of HBQ and its anharmonic coupling with other modes in the ground state. The νOH frequency calculated by CNEO-DFT agrees closely with the experiment, and CNEO-MD reproduces the characteristic finger-like structure of the infrared spectrum. Normal mode frequency shift analysis and CNEO-MD simulations with resonant νOH excitation consistently identify several low-frequency in-plane backbone bending modes that are strongly coupled to the νOH. Taken together, this work establishes a detailed understanding of the ground-state vibrational spectrum and νOH mode couplings in HBQ, providing a basis for further investigation of their roles in ESIPT dynamics.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Molecular rotor in copper borozene Cu 4 B 8 : A freely rotating σ-aromatic tetrahedral Cu 4 core atop a boron wheel
articles.abstract: We identify two-layered Cu 4 B 8 clusters featuring tetrahedral Cu 4 units anchored on B 8 boron wheels as global minima. A substantial charge transfer from Cu 4 to the B 8 wheel is observed, resulting in a charge distribution close to the idealized [Cu 4 2+ ] [B 8 2− ] electron-counting scheme. AdNDP analysis reveals two delocalized σ-electrons within the quasi-tetrahedral Cu 4 unit, identifying it as one of the simplest σ-aromatic motifs. The B 8 2− wheels exhibit dual (6π + 6σ) aromaticity, serving as boron analogs of benzene (“borozene”). Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics simulations show pronounced fluxionality, with nearly barrierless Cu 4 rotation (∼0.01 kcal/mol) enabled by an ultrasoft vibrational mode. The delocalized electronic structure of the B 8 wheel contributes to the facile Cu 4 rotation, while electrostatic and dative interactions stabilize the two-layer framework. These results identify electroneutral Cu 4 B 8 as a prototypical copper–borozene cluster combining aromatic stabilization and dynamic fluxionality, offering a promising model for molecular rotor.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Disorder-induced dark states line shape in pump-probe spectroscopy of polaritons
articles.abstract: The formation of hybrid light–matter states called polaritons provides a route to shape the photophysics and photochemistry of molecules. Accordingly, the dynamics of polaritons following photoexcitation is extensively studied. In particular, the role of the dark state manifold in such processes remains unclear. Here, we investigate the line shape of pump–probe spectra of polaritons emerging at the dark states energy under the influence of disorder. Previously, we already investigated the pump–probe line shapes of polaritons in a disorder-free model and identified distinct signatures of relaxation into dark states, thus providing an indirect probe of this relaxation. Since the transition dipole moment of dark states vanishes in a disorder-free model, they cannot be directly probed. However, dark states acquire small transition dipole moments as soon as disorder is explicitly included in the model, enabling them to be directly probed. In this work, we demonstrate that the inclusion of the relaxation to dark states and disorder leads to the evolution of the spectral shape at the dark states energy from a derivative-like into an absorptive line shape. Furthermore, we investigate the dependence of the line shape on the disorder strength and its asymptotic scaling for a large number of coupled molecules. Our results demonstrate that probing dark states can help to single out the polaritonic response from the total signal.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Reliable X-Ray diffraction linewidth analysis of metastable cubic GaN thin films using baseline-corrected nonlinear peak fitting
articles.abstract: Evaluating the crystalline quality of metastable cubic GaN (c-GaN) thin films requires reliable X-ray diffraction (XRD) linewidth analysis, which can be affected by defect-induced broadening and background contributions. This study systematically compares nonlinear fitting strategies for the c-GaN(200) reflection of films grown on GaP substrates by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition. Unconstrained pseudo-Voigt, fixed-mixing-parameter pseudo-Voigt, baseline-subtracted pseudo-Voigt, and baseline-corrected nonlinear Gaussian fitting were evaluated. Unconstrained pseudo-Voigt fitting artificially overestimated Lorentzian broadening due to background sensitivity, resulting in physically inconsistent linewidths. In contrast, baseline-corrected nonlinear Gaussian fitting provided the most stable and physically consistent full width at half maximum evolution. Using this approach, a systematic linewidth reduction from S1 to S4 was observed, consistent with increased crystallite size and reduced defect density. These results demonstrate the importance of rigorous baseline correction and profile selection for reliable structural analysis of semiconductor thin films.

articles.title: Supernatant from primary human gut microbiota fermentation as a modulator of intestinal barrier in in vitro models
articles.abstract: The human intestine harbours a complex microbial community that closely interacts with intestinal epithelial cells, the first line of host defence. Although several in vitro models have been developed to study host–microbiota interactions, direct co-culture of gut microbiota and mammalian cells remains technically challenging. Here, we evaluated an in vitro approach for testing human faecal fermentation supernatant on intestinal barrier function using differentiated Caco-2/HT29-MTX monolayers maintained in static cell culture inserts or a dynamic gut-chip model. Fermentation supernatant diluted in HBSS was applied for 4 h, and barrier function was assessed by transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) in static cultures and by Lucifer Yellow apparent permeability (Papp) in both models. Under the conditions tested, exposure to the fermentation supernatant did not compromise barrier integrity. Lucifer Yellow Papp was significantly lower in cell culture inserts (1.04×10⁻⁷±8.98×10⁻⁹ cm·s⁻¹) than in the dynamic gut-chip (7.96×10⁻⁷±1.82×10⁻⁷ cm·s⁻¹), highlighting differences in epithelial permeability between static and dynamic culture conditions. To enable prolonged exposure studies, different carrier conditions were evaluated. HBSS was unsuitable for 24 h incubation, resulting in reduced cell metabolic activity and TEER, whereas HBSS-HEPES maintained cell viability and barrier function. A TNF-α-induced barrier dysfunction was subsequently established, resulting in a 45% decrease in TEER and a 48% increase in Lucifer Yellow Papp compared with the healthy control. Treatment with fermentation supernatant diluted in HBSS-HEPES was associated with a reduction in the increased permeability, with Papp values becoming comparable to those of the healthy control condition. restored barrier integrity, demonstrating its capacity to repair impaired intestinal epithelial. Overall, this study establishes a practical in vitro framework for evaluating faecal fermentation-derived products using intestinal epithelial models representing both healthy and barrier-impaired conditions. The findings highlight the importance of selecting appropriate culture platforms, carrier conditions, and exposure periods when assessing the effects of complex microbiota-derived products on intestinal barrier function and provide a basis for the subsequent testing of fermentation samples in cell-based intestinal models.

articles.title: Thermochemical adsorption at high overpotentials limits molecular CO-to-methanol electroreduction
articles.title_zh: 高过电势下的热化学吸附限制了分子CO到甲醇的电还原
articles.abstract: Nature Chemistry, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02285-5 Applied potential controls charge-transfer kinetics, but thermochemical steps can limit electrocatalytic rates. Now it has been shown that CO-to-methanol conversion shifts from charge-transfer-limited kinetics to adsorption-limited kinetics as overpotential increases, establishing CO adsorption energy as a descriptor of the thermochemical constraint.
articles.abstract_zh: 施加的电位控制电荷转移动力学，但热化学步骤会限制电催化速率。现在已经表明，随着过电势的增加，CO 到甲醇的转化从电荷转移限制动力学转变为吸附限制动力学，从而建立 CO 吸附能作为热化学约束的描述符。

articles.abstract: Nature Chemistry, Published online: 02 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41557-026-02290-8 Electrochemical kinetics are shaped by both the thermodynamic driving force and interfacial polarization. articles.title: Faster-than-power-law decay of order parameter correlations in the two-dimensional RP² model: a rigorous result by vibe-proving
articles.title_zh: 二维 RP² 模型中序参数相关性的衰减速度快于幂律衰减：vibe 证明的严格结果
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41256v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the RP² model on the two-dimensional square lattice with nearest-neighbor interactions. It is obtained by replacing the spin in the standard classical Heisenberg model with a director, which does not distinguish two opposite directions. Unlike the standard classical Heisenberg model or the O(3) nonlinear sigma model, the RP² (and its cousin RP³) model allows point vortex defects classified by π₁(RP²)= Z₂ in two dimensions. It is tempting to expect the Z₂ vortices to induce a phase transition analogous to the well-established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in the O(2) model (XY model) in two dimensions. Indeed, the possibilities of a critical phase or a critical point with power-law correlations of the order parameter in the RP² and RP³ models have been discussed in the literature. However, the challenging nature of the problem has prevented a definitive conclusion on the phase diagram so far. In this paper, we report a rigorous mathematical proof by Artificial Intelligence (ChatGPT 6 Astra) that the absolute value of the two-point correlation function of order parameters at distance r in the RP² and RP³ models on the two-dimensional square lattice is bounded above by C_β exp(-c_β[log(2+r)]²) for any finite inverse temperature βge0, with positive constants C_β and c_β depending only on β. Namely, the correlation function decays faster than any power of r. The proof is formalized and verified in Lean; the formalization is publicly available at doi:10.5281/zenodo.23548847 . A heuristic argument based on a one-parameter effective theory ansatz at large distances combined with the rigorous correlation bound suggests (but does not prove) that the Z₂ vortices are always unbound at any nonzero temperature.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们考虑具有最近邻相互作用的二维方格上的 RP² 模型。它是通过用指向矢代替标准经典海森堡模型中的自旋而获得的，它不区分两个相反的方向。与标准经典海森堡模型或 O(3) 非线性 sigma 模型不同，RP²（及其同类 RP³）模型允许在二维中按 π₁(RP²)= Z2 分类点涡流缺陷。人们很容易认为 Z2 涡流会引发类似于二维 O(2) 模型（XY 模型）中成熟的 Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless 相变的相变。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们考虑具有最近邻相互作用的二维方格上的 RP² 模型。它是通过用指向矢代替标准经典海森堡模型中的自旋而获得的，它不区分两个相反的方向。与标准经典海森堡模型或 O(3) 非线性 sigma 模型不同，RP²（及其同类 RP³）模型允许在二维中按 π₁(RP²)= Z2 分类点涡流缺陷。人们很容易认为 Z2 涡流会引发类似于二维 O(2) 模型（XY 模型）中成熟的 Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless 相变的相变。事实上，文献中已经讨论了 RP² 和 RP³ 模型中阶次参数的幂律相关性的临界相或临界点的可能性。然而，到目前为止，该问题的挑战性性质阻碍了相图的明确结论。在本文中，我们报告了人工智能（ChatGPT 6 Astra）的严格数学证明，对于任何有限反温度 βge0，对于任何有限反温度 βge0，在二维方晶格上的 RP² 和 RP³ 模型中，距离 r 处的序参数的两点相关函数的绝对值由 C_β exp(-c_β[log(2+r)]²) 上界，其中正常数 C_β 和 c_β 仅取决于 β。即，相关函数的衰减速度比 r 的任何幂衰减得都快。证明在精益中被形式化和验证；正式化可在 doi:10.5281/zenodo.23548847 上公开获取。基于远距离单参数有效理论 ansatz 的启发式论证与严格相关界相结合表明（但未证明）Z2 涡旋在任何非零温度下始终不受约束。

articles.title: SKFitter: Symmetry resolved Slater Koster tight-binding models from first principles for s, p, d and f electrons, spin orbit coupling and magnetism
articles.title_zh: SKFitter：根据 s、p、d 和 f 电子、自旋轨道耦合和磁性的第一原理，对称性解析了 Slater Koster 紧束缚模型
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40729v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Constructing accurate and physically interpretable tight binding (TB) Hamiltonians from first principles calculations remains challenging, particularly for materials exhibiting complex orbital hybridization, spin orbit coupling (SOC), and magnetic order. SKFitter is an open-source Python framework for constructing and optimizing symmetry resolved Slater Koster TB models directly from density functional theory (DFT) calculations performed using Quantum ESPRESSO or VASP. The framework supports s to f orbitals, incorporates on site SOC and site resolved magnetic exchange interactions, and accommodates both orthogonal and nonorthogonal basis. A central feature is the symmetry resolved parameterization of orbital manifolds, which allows independent two centre hopping integrals between symmetry allowed orbital groups and across distinct neighbour shells. SKFitter also identifies missing orbital contributions and guide systematic basis set refinement and optimizes parameters through weights. The resulting Hamiltonian can be used to evaluate anomalous (AHC) and spin Hall conductivities (SHC), and topological invariants. We demonstrate the framework using eight representative materials spanning semimetals, semiconductors, transition metals, f-electron compounds, and magnetic systems. Symmetry resolved models achieve band energy errors of 9 to 41 meV within 1 eV of the Fermi level. The fitted Hamiltonians reproduce characteristic features of the SHC response of Pt, the SOC dependence of the AHC of Fe, and the momentum dependent altermagnetic spin splitting of MnTe without any altermagnet specific interaction. For EuMn2Bi2, projection guided orbital refinement reduces the near Fermi level fitting error from 120 to 32 meV. Together, these results establish SKFitter as a flexible and reproducible framework for developing symmetry consistent, physically interpretable TB models of complex materials.
articles.abstract_zh: 从第一原理计算构建准确且物理上可解释的紧束缚（TB）哈密顿量仍然具有挑战性，特别是对于表现出复杂轨道杂化、自旋轨道耦合（SOC）和磁序的材料。 SKFitter 是一个开源 Python 框架，用于直接根据使用 Quantum ESPRESSO 或 VASP 执行的密度泛函理论 (DFT) 计算构建和优化对称解析的 Slater Koster TB 模型。该框架支持 s 到 f 轨道，结合了现场 SOC 和现场解决的磁交换相互作用，并适应正交和非正交基础。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 从第一原理计算构建准确且物理上可解释的紧束缚（TB）哈密顿量仍然具有挑战性，特别是对于表现出复杂轨道杂化、自旋轨道耦合（SOC）和磁序的材料。 SKFitter 是一个开源 Python 框架，用于直接根据使用 Quantum ESPRESSO 或 VASP 执行的密度泛函理论 (DFT) 计算构建和优化对称解析的 Slater Koster TB 模型。该框架支持 s 到 f 轨道，结合了现场 SOC 和现场解决的磁交换相互作用，并适应正交和非正交基础。一个中心特征是轨道流形的对称解析参数化，它允许在对称允许的轨道组之间以及不同的相邻壳层之间进行独立的两个中心跳跃积分。 SKFitter 还可以识别缺失的轨道贡献并指导系统基组细化并通过权重优化参数。由此产生的哈密顿量可用于评估反常 (AHC) 和自旋霍尔电导率 (SHC) 以及拓扑不变量。我们使用半金属、半导体、过渡金属、f 电子化合物和磁性系统的八种代表性材料演示了该框架。对称解析模型在费米能级 1 eV 范围内实现了 9 至 41 meV 的带能误差。拟合的哈密顿量再现了 Pt 的 SHC 响应、Fe 的 AHC 的 SOC 依赖性以及 MnTe 的动量依赖性交变磁自旋分裂的特征，而没有任何交变磁体特定相互作用。对于 EuMn2Bi2，投影引导轨道细化将近费米能级拟合误差从 120 meV 降低至 32 meV。总之，这些结果将 SKFitter 确立为一个灵活且可重复的框架，用于开发复杂材料的对称一致、物理可解释的 TB 模型。

articles.title: Cavity-engineered ferroelectricity in SrTiO₃
articles.title_zh: SrTiO₃ 腔体工程铁电体
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interfacing quantum materials with photonic cavity architectures is at the vanguard of materials engineering. The structured electromagnetic fluctuations of a dark cavity environment can renormalize fundamental thermodynamical material properties and energy scales, holding promise to create a rich ecosystem of cavity-induced ground states and functionalities absent in the bare material. However, direct experimental demonstrations that cavity coupling can stabilize or enhance genuinely new phases of matter have remained scarce. In this work, we establish the presence of cavity-induced and cavity-enhanced ferroelectric phases in free-standing SrTiO₃ membranes coupled to dark THz-frequency photonic crystal cavities. Using THz spectroscopy, we observe ultrastrong coupling (USC) between the ferroelectric soft mode in SrTiO₃ and the cavity resonance. The structural response of SrTiO₃ to this USC is measured via second harmonic generation imaging, which reveals a substantial (greater than 400%) enhancement of signal in the cavity environment and a distinct modification of the crystalline symmetry, indicating the onset and enhancement of ferroelectricity. We interpret these observations as resulting from renormalized piezoelectric and flexoelectric couplings, which in turn arise from the cavity-modified dielectric environment. This interpretation is supported with microscopic modeling via DFT-based multi-scale dynamics simulations and by macroscopic Ginzburg-Landau theory. Altogether, our experimental and theoretical results firmly confirm that cavity engineering can indeed be used to create new ground states in materials and enhance existing ones. This work establishes a new paradigm for materials engineering with direct applications for quantum transduction, quantum sensing, and nonlinear integrated photonics.
articles.abstract_zh: 将量子材料与光子腔结构连接起来是材料工程的前沿。暗腔环境的结构化电磁涨落可以重新规范基本的热力学材料特性和能量尺度，有望创建一个丰富的生态系统，其中包含空腔诱导的基态和裸材料中不存在的功能。然而，空腔耦合可以稳定或增强真正的新物质相的直接实验证明仍然很少。在这项工作中，我们确定了与暗太赫兹频率光子晶体腔耦合的独立 SrTiO₃ 膜中存在空腔诱导和空腔增强铁电相。使用太赫兹光谱，我们观察到 SrTiO₃ 中的铁电软模式与腔谐振之间的超强耦合 (USC)。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 将量子材料与光子腔结构连接起来是材料工程的前沿。暗腔环境的结构化电磁涨落可以重新规范基本的热力学材料特性和能量尺度，有望创建一个丰富的生态系统，其中包含空腔诱导的基态和裸材料中不存在的功能。然而，空腔耦合可以稳定或增强真正的新物质相的直接实验证明仍然很少。在这项工作中，我们确定了与暗太赫兹频率光子晶体腔耦合的独立 SrTiO₃ 膜中存在空腔诱导和空腔增强铁电相。使用太赫兹光谱，我们观察到 SrTiO₃ 中的铁电软模式与腔谐振之间的超强耦合 (USC)。 SrTiO₃对此 USC 的结构响应是通过二次谐波生成成像测量的，这揭示了腔环境中信号的显着增强（大于 400%）以及晶体对称性的明显改变，表明铁电性的开始和增强。我们将这些观察结果解释为重正化压电和挠曲电耦合的结果，而这些耦合又是由腔体修改的介电环境产生的。这种解释得到了基于 DFT 的多尺度动力学模拟的微观建模和宏观金兹堡-朗道理论的支持。总而言之，我们的实验和理论结果坚定地证实，空腔工程确实可以用于在材料中创建新的基态并增强现有的基态。这项工作为材料工程建立了一个新的范式，可直接应用于量子转导、量子传感和非线性集成光子学。

articles.title: Moiré metals and continuum models beyond a single valley
articles.title_zh: 超越单谷的莫尔金属和连续介质模型
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive continuum models of moiré materials valid over the full monolayer Brillouin zone, as required for metals whose large Fermi surfaces are not confined to a single valley. To this end, we introduce an environment-resolved two-center approximation, in which each hopping amplitude depends not only on the distance between the orbitals it connects but also on its position within the moiré cell. Taking the local environment to be set by the disregistry of the two layers alone, these moiré couplings and their full set of harmonics can be learnt from commensurate bilayers at uniform stackings, without fitting. The method shows excellent agreement with ab initio band structures on moiré cells containing a few hundred atoms. Applied to twisted NbSe₂, it yields a continuum model in which moiré effects concentrate at the van Hove singularities, a single-particle starting point for studying moiré-tuned superconducting, charge-density-wave instabilities and their competition.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们推导出在整个单层布里渊区有效的莫尔材料的连续介质模型，这符合其大费米表面不限于单个谷的金属的要求。为此，我们引入了环境分辨的双中心近似，其中每个跳跃幅度不仅取决于其连接的轨道之间的距离，还取决于其在莫尔单元内的位置。考虑到局部环境仅由两层的不重合来设置，这些莫尔耦合及其全套谐波可以从均匀堆叠的相应双层中学习，无需拟合。该方法与包含数百个原子的莫尔晶胞上的从头算能带结构表现出极好的一致性。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们推导出在整个单层布里渊区有效的莫尔材料的连续介质模型，这符合其大费米表面不限于单个谷的金属的要求。为此，我们引入了环境分辨的双中心近似，其中每个跳跃幅度不仅取决于其连接的轨道之间的距离，还取决于其在莫尔单元内的位置。考虑到局部环境仅由两层的不重合来设置，这些莫尔耦合及其全套谐波可以从均匀堆叠的相应双层中学习，无需拟合。该方法与包含数百个原子的莫尔晶胞上的从头算能带结构表现出极好的一致性。应用于扭曲的 NbSe2 时，它产生了一个连续介质模型，其中莫尔效应集中在范霍夫奇点，这是研究莫尔调整超导、电荷密度波不稳定性及其竞争的单粒子起点。

articles.title: Gapless and Non-Equilibrium Topology in Blockaded Ladders
articles.title_zh: 封锁梯中的无间隙和非平衡拓扑
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a multi-leg PXYP model as a minimal setting to explore constraint-induced intertwinement between itinerant and internal degrees of freedom. We argue that the Rydberg-like blockade induces correlations in squeezed space, providing a unified mechanism for nontrivial string order both in and out of equilibrium. In a two-leg geometry, this leads to an intrinsically gapless topological ground state, which can terminate at a supersymmetric multicritical point. This mechanism also leads to the preservation of string order for parametrically long times after a quench, which we verify using tensor network simulations and a classical stochastic approximation to the dynamics. In a three-leg geometry, the blockade leads to an additional emergent U(1) symmetry, resulting in a multicomponent Luttinger liquid where both itinerant and internal degrees of freedom are critical. This family of models arises naturally in a range of quantum simulator platforms such as Rydberg tweezer arrays and dipolar atoms in optical lattices.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们提出了一个多腿 PXYP 模型作为探索流动自由度和内部自由度之间约束引起的交织的最小设置。我们认为，类似里德堡的封锁会在压缩空间中引起相关性，为处于平衡状态和非平衡状态的非平凡弦序提供统一的机制。在两腿几何中，这导致本质上无间隙的拓扑基态，其可以终止于超对称多临界点。这种机制还导致在淬灭后参数化地长时间保存弦序，我们使用张量网络模拟和动力学的经典随机近似来验证这一点。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们提出了一个多腿 PXYP 模型作为探索流动自由度和内部自由度之间约束引起的交织的最小设置。我们认为，类似里德堡的封锁会在压缩空间中引起相关性，为处于平衡状态和非平衡状态的非平凡弦序提供统一的机制。在两腿几何中，这导致本质上无间隙的拓扑基态，其可以终止于超对称多临界点。这种机制还导致在淬灭后参数化地长时间保存弦序，我们使用张量网络模拟和动力学的经典随机近似来验证这一点。在三腿几何结构中，封锁导致额外出现的 U(1) 对称性，从而产生多组分卢廷格液体，其中流动自由度和内部自由度都至关重要。这一系列模型自然出现在一系列量子模拟器平台中，例如里德伯镊子阵列和光学晶格中的偶极原子。

articles.title: Singlet-Triplet Transition of Rotating Moiré Atoms in a Magnetic Field
articles.title_zh: 磁场中旋转莫尔原子的单重态-三重态跃迁
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moiré superlattices can bind several electrons to each potential minimum, forming few-electron "moiré atoms." Using neural quantum states that obey magnetic periodic boundary conditions, include full Landau-level mixing, and treat both spin sectors, we map the ground state of two-electron moiré atoms in a superlattice as a function of moiré depth and magnetic field strength. At strong field each atom is a spin-triplet maximum-density droplet with canonical angular momentum langle L_zrangle=-1 and a persistent circulating current: the rotating counterpart of the "Wigner molecular crystal" recently imaged in moiré superlattices. Deepening the wells drives a singlet-triplet transition to non-rotating spin-singlet atoms whose only current is a weak diamagnetic counter-circulation. The transition moves to deeper wells as the field grows, so depth and field together open a window for the formation of rotors. This is the collective analog of the singlet-triplet transition of two-electron quantum dots. At the transition, the orbital magnetic moments of the atoms reverse sign as their spin polarization switches, a joint signature accessible to magnetometry. If the atoms are instead polarized by other means, such as magnetic proximity coupling, the rotors lock at weak field into a spontaneously ordered crystal of dimers in a pinwheel pattern.
articles.abstract_zh: 莫尔超晶格可以将多个电子结合到每个电势最小值，形成少电子“莫尔原子”。使用服从磁性周期性边界条件的神经量子态，包括完全朗道级混合，并处理两个自旋扇区，我们将超晶格中双电子莫尔原子的基态映射为莫尔深度和磁场强度的函数。在强场下，每个原子都是自旋三重态最大密度液滴，具有规范角动量 langle L_zrangle=-1 和持续循环电流：最近在莫尔超晶格中成像的“维格纳分子晶体”的旋转对应物。加深阱会驱动单重态-三重态转变为非旋转自旋单重态原子，其唯一的电流是弱的反磁性反循环。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 莫尔超晶格可以将多个电子结合到每个电势最小值，形成少电子“莫尔原子”。使用服从磁性周期性边界条件的神经量子态，包括完全朗道级混合，并处理两个自旋扇区，我们将超晶格中双电子莫尔原子的基态映射为莫尔深度和磁场强度的函数。在强场下，每个原子都是自旋三重态最大密度液滴，具有规范角动量 langle L_zrangle=-1 和持续循环电流：最近在莫尔超晶格中成像的“维格纳分子晶体”的旋转对应物。加深阱会驱动单重态-三重态转变为非旋转自旋单重态原子，其唯一的电流是弱的反磁性反循环。随着油田的增长，过渡会转移到更深的井，因此深度和油田共同为转子的形成打开了一个窗口。这是双电子量子点的单重态-三重态跃迁的集体模拟。在转变时，原子的轨道磁矩随着它们的自旋极化切换而反转，这是磁力测定法可获取的联合特征。如果原子通过其他方式（例如磁邻近耦合）极化，转子就会在弱场锁定成风车图案中自发有序的二聚体晶体。

articles.title: Anisotropic spin splitting in α-MnTe epilayers on InP(111)A and Si(111) substrates
articles.title_zh: InP(111)A 和 Si(111) 衬底上 α-MnTe 外延层的各向异性自旋分裂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: α-MnTe has emerged as a prototypical altermagnetic material, combining compensated antiferromagnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting. Here, we investigate the structural and electronic properties of epitaxial α-MnTe layers grown by molecular beam epitaxy on InP(111)A and Si(111) substrates. The crystalline and surface quality of the epilayers was characterised by reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and X-ray diffraction (XRD), confirming the formation of high-quality, single-phase films. The transport measurements were performed, confirming an antiferromagnetic transition and weak ferromagnetism. The electronic structure was studied using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). At 90 K, both samples exhibit relativistic anisotropic valence band splitting, which is substantially larger along the Γ-K direction, reaching approximately 300 meV, than along Γ-M, where values of about 150~meV are observed. The magnitude and momentum dependence of the splitting are very similar for α-MnTe grown on the two different substrates, indicating the robustness of the altermagnetic electronic structure with respect to the epitaxial environment.
articles.abstract_zh: α-MnTe 已成为一种典型的变磁材料，它将补偿反铁磁序与动量相关的自旋分裂相结合。在这里，我们研究了在 InP(111)A 和 Si(111) 衬底上通过分子束外延生长的外延 α-MnTe 层的结构和电子特性。通过反射高能电子衍射 (RHEED)、原子力显微镜 (AFM) 和 X 射线衍射 (XRD) 表征外延层的晶体和表面质量，证实形成了高质量的单相薄膜。进行了输运测量，证实了反铁磁转变和弱铁磁性。使用角分辨光电子能谱（ARPES）研究电子结构。
articles.abstract_zh_full: α-MnTe 已成为一种典型的变磁材料，它将补偿反铁磁序与动量相关的自旋分裂相结合。在这里，我们研究了在 InP(111)A 和 Si(111) 衬底上通过分子束外延生长的外延 α-MnTe 层的结构和电子特性。通过反射高能电子衍射 (RHEED)、原子力显微镜 (AFM) 和 X 射线衍射 (XRD) 表征外延层的晶体和表面质量，证实形成了高质量的单相薄膜。进行了输运测量，证实了反铁磁转变和弱铁磁性。使用角分辨光电子能谱（ARPES）研究电子结构。在 90 K 时，两个样品都表现出相对论各向异性价带分裂，沿 Γ-K 方向的价带分裂明显大于沿 Γ-M 方向的价带分裂，达到约 300 meV，观察到的值约为 150~meV。对于在两种不同衬底上生长的 α-MnTe，分裂的幅度和动量依赖性非常相似，表明交变磁电子结构相对于外延环境的鲁棒性。

articles.title: Quantum Monte-Carlo study of spin-valley ferromagnetism in rhombohedral graphene
articles.title_zh: 菱形石墨烯自旋谷铁磁性的量子蒙特卡罗研究
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent capacitance measurements in bilayer and trilayer rhombohedral graphene reported large magnetic entropy above the Curie temperature, suggesting the formation of fluctuating local moments. Further experimental support comes from scanning tunneling microscopy experiments in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, which directly visualized honeycomb electron-crystal order that strengthens upon heating before melting, related to the Pomeranchuk effect. Motivated by these experiments, we construct spin-valley local-moment Hamiltonians for the quarter-metal and half-metal phases. We extract their couplings from constrained Hartree-Fock calculations, and solve their finite-temperature thermodynamics with stochastic-series-expansion quantum Monte Carlo. For the quarter metal we find a continuous 2D-Ising transition at T_c approx 0.7 K, an order of magnitude smaller than the Hartree-Fock estimate (~30 K) and closer to the experimental scale of a few kelvin. For the half metal, we study the field-induced magnetization as a function of temperature with and without proximity-enhanced spin-orbit coupling. When spin-orbit coupling is negligible, intervalley Hund's coupling enhances the magnetic response. Strong spin-orbit coupling, as can be induced by a neighboring transition-metal dichalcogenide, gives rise to the standard spin-canted ground state at zero temperature. Upon heating, the in-plane polarization decreases more rapidly than the out-of-plane polarization. Surprisingly, despite the itinerant nature of the electrons, local-moment models with microscopically determined couplings appear to capture key finite-temperature magnetic properties of rhombohedral graphene without any fitting.
articles.abstract_zh: 最近双层和三层菱面体石墨烯的电容测量报告了高于居里温度的大磁熵，表明波动局部矩的形成。进一步的实验支持来自菱面体六层石墨烯的扫描隧道显微镜实验，该实验直接可视化了蜂窝状电子晶体顺序，该顺序在熔化前加热时增强，与波美兰丘克效应相关。受这些实验的启发，我们构建了四分之一金属和半金属相的自旋谷局部矩哈密顿量。我们从约束 Hartree-Fock 计算中提取它们的耦合，并使用随机级数展开量子蒙特卡罗求解它们的有限温度热力学。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 最近双层和三层菱面体石墨烯的电容测量报告了高于居里温度的大磁熵，表明波动局部矩的形成。进一步的实验支持来自菱面体六层石墨烯的扫描隧道显微镜实验，该实验直接可视化了蜂窝状电子晶体顺序，该顺序在熔化前加热时增强，与波美兰丘克效应相关。受这些实验的启发，我们构建了四分之一金属和半金属相的自旋谷局部矩哈密顿量。我们从约束 Hartree-Fock 计算中提取它们的耦合，并使用随机级数展开量子蒙特卡罗求解它们的有限温度热力学。对于四分之一金属，我们发现 T_c 处有一个连续的 2D-Ising 转变，约为 0.7 K，这个数量级比 Hartree-Fock 估计值 (~30 K) 小，并且更接近几个开尔文的实验尺度。对于半金属，我们研究了在有或没有邻近增强自旋轨道耦合的情况下场感应磁化强度与温度的函数关系。当自旋轨道耦合可以忽略不计时，间隔洪德耦合增强了磁响应。强自旋轨道耦合（可由邻近的过渡金属二硫族化物引起）在零温度下产生标准自旋倾斜基态。加热后，面内偏振比面外偏振下降得更快。令人惊讶的是，尽管电子具有巡回性质，但具有微观确定耦合的局部矩模型似乎无需任何拟合即可捕获菱面体石墨烯的关键有限温度磁特性。

articles.title: Intertwined ferromagnetic and altermagnetic orders in Cr-doped MnTe
articles.title_zh: Cr 掺杂 MnTe 中相互交织的铁磁和交磁序
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ferromagnetism and altermagnetism both break time-reversal symmetry, yet their distinct transformation properties under crystalline symmetries forbid direct bilinear coupling between their order parameters. Whether these two magnetic orders can remain thermodynamically distinct while strongly influencing one another remains an open question. Here we demonstrate the homogeneous coexistence of ferromagnetism and altermagnetism in Cr-doped MnTe. By tuning the ferromagnetic ordering temperature across the nearly unchanged Néel temperature with Cr doping, we uncover a striking interplay between the two orders: the ferromagnetic transition becomes a crossover when altermagnetism develops first, whereas the onset of altermagnetism strongly suppresses the out-of-plane ferromagnetic remanence when ferromagnetism develops first. Moreover, spin-orbit coupling enables symmetry-selective interactions through which the ferromagnetic moment controls the altermagnetic domain manifold, with its out-of-plane and in-plane components biasing the time-reversal (Z₂) and orientational (Z₃) sectors, respectively. Our results reveal how two symmetry-distinct magnetic orders can retain separate ordering tendencies while remaining strongly coupled, providing a route towards internal control of altermagnetic domain states.
articles.abstract_zh: 铁磁性和交变磁性都打破了时间反转对称性，但它们在晶体对称性下的独特变换特性禁止它们的有序参数之间的直接双线性耦合。这两种磁序是否能够在热力学上保持不同，同时强烈地相互影响仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。在这里，我们证明了 Cr 掺杂 MnTe 中铁磁性和交磁性的均匀共存。通过用 Cr 掺杂在几乎不变的尼尔温度上调整铁磁有序温度，我们发现了两个有序之间的惊人相互作用：当交变磁性首先发展时，铁磁转变变成交叉，而当铁磁性首先发展时，交变磁性的开始强烈抑制面外铁磁剩磁。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 铁磁性和交变磁性都打破了时间反转对称性，但它们在晶体对称性下的独特变换特性禁止它们的有序参数之间的直接双线性耦合。这两种磁序是否能够在热力学上保持不同，同时强烈地相互影响仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。在这里，我们证明了 Cr 掺杂 MnTe 中铁磁性和交磁性的均匀共存。通过用 Cr 掺杂在几乎不变的尼尔温度上调整铁磁有序温度，我们发现了两个有序之间的惊人相互作用：当交变磁性首先发展时，铁磁转变变成交叉，而当铁磁性首先发展时，交变磁性的开始强烈抑制面外铁磁剩磁。此外，自旋轨道耦合能够实现对称选择性相互作用，通过铁磁矩控制交变磁畴流形，其面外和面内分量分别偏置时间反转（Z2）和取向（Z3）扇区。我们的结果揭示了两个对称性不同的磁序如何在保持强耦合的同时保留单独的有序倾向，从而提供了一种实现交变磁畴状态的内部控制的途径。

articles.title: Triplon thermal Hall response in a honeycomb-lattice J₁-J₂ Heisenberg antiferromagnet with Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions
articles.title_zh: 蜂窝晶格 J₁-J2 海森堡反铁磁体中的三联热霍尔响应与 Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya 相互作用
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate triplon topology and the thermal Hall transport in a columnar valence-bond solid of a spin-1/2 honeycomb-lattice J₁-J₂ Heisenberg antiferromagnet. Inequivalent triangular sublattices, modeled by J₂^A≠ J₂^B, remove inversion symmetry at nearest-neighbor bond centers and allow in-plane Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interactions. We identify the two symmetry-allowed in-plane DM vector patterns and present detailed results for the pattern parallel to the bonds including an out-of-plane magnetic field. Within a harmonic bond-operator treatment, we determine the triplon bands, their Berry curvatures and Chern numbers, and the triplon thermal Hall conductivity. The DM interaction and magnetic field generate nonzero Berry curvatures, but the numerically integrated Chern number of every isolated triplon band vanishes. Nevertheless, the energy-dependent Bose weighting of positive and negative Berry-curvature regions produces a finite thermal Hall response at nonzero low temperatures. We delimit the dilute-triplon regime in which the harmonic transport calculation is expected to be reliable. These results show that a vanishing Chern number band does not directly constrain the triplon response of a valence-bond solid. We also comment on the effects on the columnar valence-bond solid phase of a DM interaction between next-nearest-neighbor spins characterized by an out-of-plane vector pattern.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们研究了自旋 1/2 蜂窝晶格 J₁-J2 海森堡反铁磁体的柱状价键固体中的三重子拓扑和热霍尔输运。由 J2^A≠ J2^B 建模的不等三角形亚晶格消除了最近邻键中心处的反演对称性，并允许面内 Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) 相互作用。我们识别了两种允许对称的面内 DM 矢量图案，并给出了与包含面外磁场的键平行的图案的详细结果。在谐波键算符处理中，我们确定了三重子能带、它们的贝里曲率和陈数，以及三重子热霍尔电导率。
