In conclusion, K. palustris shows potential for the sustainable production of carotenoids with a profile compatible with sarcinaxanthin using alternative agro-industrial substrates. Process scale-up and the photoprotective and antioxidant properties of the extract support the potential for further development of this bioprocess. These findings are particularly relevant to the cosmetic and biotechnology industries, where there is growing interest in natural pigments and bioactive compounds obtained through more sustainable production routes.

articles.title: Transformer-Based Models for Streaming Anomaly Detection in Solar Microgrids: A Systematic Review
articles.abstract: Background:Solar Photovoltaic (PV) microgrids operate in highly non‑stationary conditions, where irradiance, weather, and load variability cause frequent concept drift in streaming telemetry. Traditional anomaly detection models degrade under these dynamics. Objective: To systematically review Transformer-based models for streaming anomaly/fault detection in energy systems, emphasizing solar PV and microgrids and appraise evidence on (i) drift adaptation, (ii) edge deployment efficiency, and (iii) interpretability for operator use. Methods: We followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Records published between January 2023, and May 2026 were screened reflecting the recent emergence of Transformer-based anomaly detection research addressing streaming operation, concept drift, and edge deployment. Inclusion required a Transformer/attention-based architecture applied to anomaly/fault detection on time-series or operational telemetry, with rule-based removal of clearly irrelevant studies followed by manual validation. Results: A total of 2968 records were identified. After duplicate removal and screening, 113 studies were included in the final synthesis. Transformer-based architecture is widely reported across included studies but shows uneven application across domains. Photovoltaic systems account for most studies, while microgrid-specific applications remain limited. Reporting of drift adaptation, edge efficiency, and interpretability is inconsistent. Conclusions: Transformers show strong anomaly detection potential, yet gaps persist in drift-aware training, standardized edge metrics, and validated interpretability. We recommend lightweight attention mechanisms, integrated drift detectors, and operator-tested explanations to enable reliable PV microgrid deployment.

articles.title: Reliable Underground-to-Aboveground Communications with Magnetic Transmitters and Electric Receivers
articles.abstract: Unlike conventional electric- or magnetic-antenna transceiver systems, the magnetic transmitters and electric receivers (MTER) system jointly exploits the induction and radiation fields, providing a new solution to enable both deep underground transmission and long-range aboveground communication. However, the maximum reliable aboveground coverage achievable by MTER-enabled UG2AG communications has not yet been systematically studied, which is essential for guiding transmitter configuration and practical gateway deployment. In this paper, we develop a reliability-oriented framework to maximize the aboveground coverage of MTER-enabled UG2AG communication through transmitter configuration and operating-frequency design. Specifically, we first establish a reliable-coverage model that links the MTER link characteristics to the achievable aboveground communication range. Furthermore, we determine the transmitter configuration and operating frequency to maximize the reliable coverage under practical system constraints. Finally, we evaluate the proposed solution under different underground environments and validate the MTER link through a field experiment in an underground mine. The results show that transmitter configuration optimization can effectively extend the reliable aboveground coverage, and the optimal transmitter configuration is environment-dependent. In addition, the MTER link can support successful end-to-end data transmission in a realistic underground environment.

articles.title: Unveiling the Atmospheric Corrosion Behavior of Die-cast AZ91D Magnesium Alloy: From Mechanism to Laboratory-to-Field Test Correlation
articles.abstract: The application of Mg alloy components in automobiles enables significant weight reduction. However, the poor corrosion resistance of Mg alloys remains a critical impediment. Moreover, their corrosion mechanisms and modes are fundamentally different from those of conventional materials such as steel and aluminum. Currently, the automotive industry lacks well-established accelerated corrosion testing and evaluation methodologies specifically tailored for Mg alloys. In this study, the corrosion behavior of die-cast AZ91D Mg alloy was systematically investigated under three distinct exposure conditions, including marine atmosphere, proving ground vehicle corrosion test (PGVCT) and various laboratory corrosion environment. The corrosion performance was evaluated in terms of morphology, weight loss rate, and corrosion depth, based on which the atmospheric corrosion mechanism was elucidated and a laboratory-to-field corrosion test correlation was established for the magnesium alloy. This work provides a critical foundation for developing highly relevant accelerated corrosion test method for Mg alloys used in automotive applications.

articles.title: Preparation of Crosslinked Grafted Modified Anionic Starch-Based Flocculants and Their Dye Removal Performance
articles.abstract: This study addresses two critical limitations of conventional flocculants applied to textile dyeing and printing wastewater: their poor biodegradability and persistent toxic residues. It also tackles the suboptimal performance commonly observed with single-modified starch flocculants. To overcome these challenges, a novel cross-linked, graft-copolymerized anionic flocculant—termed CSPA—was synthesized using cassava starch (St) as the backbone polymer, acrylamide (AM) and sodium acrylate (AANa) as co-grafting monomers, N,N′-methylenebisacrylamide (MBA) as the cross-linker, and an ammonium persulfate/sodium bisulfite redox system as the initiator. The dye removal efficiency of a composite coagulant composed of CSPA and polyaluminium chloride (PAC) was evaluated under ambient conditions. Structural and compositional characteristics of CSPA were systematically elucidated via Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and solid-state ¹³C nuclear magnetic resonance (¹³C-NMR) spectroscopy. Using Disperse Red FB and Disperse Yellow RGFL as model dyes, the effects of key synthesis parameters—including the St-to-monomer mass ratio, AM-to-AANa molar ratio, MBA dosage (wt% relative to total reactants), initiator dosage (wt% relative to total reactants), and reaction temperature—on decolorization performance were rigorously investigated. Optimal flocculation performance was achieved at a St:AM:AANa molar ratio of 1:1:1, with MBA and initiator dosages of 0.2 wt% and 0.6 wt%, respectively (both calculated relative to total reactant mass), and a synthesis temperature of 70°C. Under these conditions, CSPA–PAC achieved removal efficiencies of 98.97% for Disperse Red(FB) and 99.56% for Disperse Yellow(RGFL). Moreover, the system demonstrated robust operational flexibility, maintaining > 90% decolorization across a broad CSPA dosage range (40–70 mg/L) and acidic-to-neutral pH range (pH 1–7).

articles.title: Benchmarking Modular Optimization Strategies for Parameterized Quantum Circuits
articles.abstract: Training parameterized quantum circuits requires balancing optimization progress with limited evaluation budgets and the statistical uncertainty of near-term quantum hardware. We present a modular benchmarking framework that separates quantum search-direction estimation from classical parameter-update rules, allowing their interactions and sensitivities to be examined independently. We evaluate a suite of gradient-based, stochastic, and derivative-free optimizers across combinatorial optimization using the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), supervised quantum machine learning using Iris classification and a quantum convolutional neural network (QCNN) for binary MNIST classification, and quantum chemistry using the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) for molecular hydrogen. By separating objective evaluations from sample-circuit costs under finite-shot simulation and physical execution on a 156-qubit processor, we compare optimizer behavior across workloads with different parameter counts and measurement requirements. Four selected simulator and hardware case studies report terminal and best observed objectives separately, alongside post-training classifier accuracies. The comparisons include selected MaxCut and hydrogen trajectories and illustrate workload-dependent objective changes and evaluation costs, while the simulator benchmark compares both peak and mean performance across three seeds. The hardware runs do not establish an optimizer ranking or isolate a causal effect of device noise.

articles.title: Non-equilibrium crystallisation of aqueous sol-gel-derived Bi₄Ti₃O₁₂ thin films using concentrated solar energy
articles.abstract: Controlling the crystallisation of sol-gel-derived oxide thin films remains one of the most critical challenges in chemical solution deposition, as the post-deposition thermal treatment largely determines phase formation, densification and microstructural development. This issue is particularly relevant for layered ferroelectric oxides such as Bi₄Ti₃O₁₂ (BiT), whose crystallisation under conventional thermal conditions often promotes exaggerated anisotropic grain growth and the formation of secondary phases associated with bismuth volatilisation. In this work, Bi₄Ti₃O₁₂ thin films were prepared by an aqueous sol-gel route combined with spin coating and subsequently crystallised using concentrated solar energy (CSE) as an alternative radiative annealing strategy. The use of an aqueous precursor chemistry avoids organic solvents, while the high radiative fluxes delivered by a Fresnel-lens-based solar concentrator provide access to thermal conditions far from equilibrium. The crystallisation behaviour and microstructural evolution of the films were systematically compared with those obtained by conventional hot-plate annealing. The results demonstrate that concentrated solar irradiation fundamentally modifies the crystallisation pathway of the sol-gel-derived films. Whereas excessive radiative input accelerates anisotropic grain growth and promotes pyrochlore formation, a narrow processing window centred around 400 °C and short dwell times enables complete phase formation, good densification and microstructural homogeneity while suppressing the equilibrium growth of plate-like grains. The study further reveals that the combination of rapid heating rates and strong thermal gradients allows the balance between crystallisation, densification and grain growth to be finely controlled. These findings demonstrate that concentrated solar energy represents a powerful processing tool for tailoring the crystallisation of sol-gel-derived oxide thin films under non-equilibrium conditions. Together with the significant reduction in processing temperature and thermal treatment time, this approach offers a sustainable and energy-efficient alternative for the thermal processing of functional oxide coatings.

articles.title: Explaining the “Missing Loss” Process in Earth’s Magnetosphere
articles.abstract: The dynamics of the Earth’s electron ring current are governed by a complex balance between transport , acceleration, and loss. Despite decades of modeling, a persistent discrepancy remains: physics-based simulations consistently overestimate electron fluxes by up to two orders of magnitude. The current theories fail to explain this "missing loss" process. Here, we demonstrate that no additional loss process is required to explain this apparent mismatch between theory and observations; rather, the discrepancy arises from neglecting the variability of the background plasma density. By coupling a time-dependent plasma density model with a ring current simulation, we show that density depletions modulate the plasma wave dispersion relation, enhancing electron precipitation by a factor of 100. This increase in loss rates explains the difference between theoretical predictions and satellite observations. Our results reveal that background plasma density, rather than wave intensity alone, is a primary driver of magnetospheric particle loss, providing a vivid example of how cold plasma density can influence the loss of particles that are up to 10,000 times more energetic than the cold plasma itself.

articles.title: Climate-Driven Performance Assessment and Loss Mechanisms of Utility- Scale Photovoltaic Systems
articles.abstract: Saudi Arabia possesses exceptionally high levels of solar irradiance, providing substantial potential for utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) deployment. However, the conversion of this solar resource into electricity is strongly influenced by site-specific climatic and environmental conditions, particularly elevated ambient temperatures, airborne dust and soiling, and coastal atmospheric conditions. This study presents a climate-driven comparative assessment of utility-scale PV systems across three representative climatic regions of Saudi Arabia: Qassim, representing an inland desert climate; Makkah, representing a hot-arid climate; and Jazan, representing a hot and humid coastal climate. A hybrid assessment framework is developed by integrating long-term satellite- and meteorological-data-derived climatic inputs from NASA POWER, Solargis, and Meteonorm with detailed PVsyst simulations based on representative utility-scale PV system configurations. Key performance measures, such as specific PV yield, performance ratio (PR), temperature-related losses, and soiling losses, are used to compare the systems. The findings show that increasing solar irradiation does not always result in proportionately higher PV energy generation since environmental losses and high module operating temperatures might significantly outweigh the advantages of the available solar resource. The annual specific PV yield varies from roughly 1650 to 2050 kWh/kWp throughout the locations under investigation, and the corresponding PR varies from 0.76 to 0.84, indicating the impact of site-specific loss mechanisms and climatic circumstances. Instead of depending just on solar-resource intensity, the comparison results emphasize the significance of including temperature-dependent module performance and environmental loss processes in PV yield evaluations. The work highlights the necessity of climate-aware optimization of PV deployment in high-irradiance desert and coastal locations and offers climate-specific insights for utility-scale PV system design and performance prediction.

articles.title: Optimal Sail Angles to Drive Circular Motion
articles.abstract: This study examines the optimisation of sail or airfoil angles to generate torque in circular motion, focussing on the interplay of lift and drag forces under constant wind conditions. Motivated by potential application to wind energy production and storage, the model considers a sail mounted on the surface of a rotating flywheel and identifies optimal sail orientations to maximise torque, highlighting dependence on the ratio of sail speed to wind speed. That is, when the sail travels slower than the wind speed, there are positions where the sail can utilise drag whilst travelling downwind; at higher speeds, this is not possible, and maximising lift whilst mitigating drag is crucial. We extend the model to a system with multiple evenly spaced sails, showing that increasing the sail count reduces torque variance, ensuring more stable energy production. Additionally, the analysis identifies a critical speed threshold above which the sails hinder rotation, acting only to decelerate the flywheel. Furthermore, sail placement can influence system performance, where the sail radius affects the torque generated and the optimal radius depends upon the rotational speed. These findings underscore the importance of precise control over sail parameters to enhance energy capture efficiency.

articles.title: MixFunn: A Neural Architecture for Differential Equations with Mixed Functions and Second-Order Interactions
articles.abstract: We introduce MixFunn, a neural network architecture designed for modeling solutions of differential equations. The proposed architecture combines two main components: (i) mixed-function neurons, which employ a set of predefined activation functions to enrich the functional representation, and (ii) second-order neurons, which explicitly incorporate interactions between different neurons. Together, these elements aim to increase representational flexibility while maintaining a compact model structure. We evaluate MixFunn on a set of differential equation problems, including the damped and forced harmonic oscillator, the one-dimensional viscous Burgers equation, and the quantum infinite square well. The results indicate that the proposed architecture can achieve accurate approximations using fewer parameters compared to standard multilayer perceptrons. Additionally, the structure of the network enables the extraction of analytical expressions that approximate the learned solutions, providing a degree of interpretability. These findings suggest that MixFunn offers a viable alternative for neural modeling of differential equations, particularly in settings where compact representations and interpretability are desirable.

articles.title: From Bulk Copper Samples to Functional DCB Test Boards: Process Transfer and Joint Characterization of Pressure-Less Nano-Silver Sintering
articles.abstract: Increasing operating temperatures in power electronic applications require joining technologies with improved thermal and mechanical stability compared with conventional Sn-based soldering. Silver sintering is a promising alternative, but many sintering processes still require elevated temperatures and external pressure. Pressure-less sintering using in-situ nano-silver precursor pastes offers a potential route for low-temperature joining without applied joining pressure. In this study, a pressure-less nano-Ag sintering process previously investigated on bulk copper samples was transferred to application-oriented direct copper bonding (DCB) test boards. A Cu-cube/DCB test structure was developed to enable four-terminal resistance measurement, die shear testing, metallographic analysis, and SEM characterization of the sintered joint region. The as-joined Cu-cube/DCB joints showed low electrical resistance and shear strength values mainly in the range of 70–80 MPa. Metallographic analysis revealed a continuous Ag-based bonding layer between the Cu-cube and the DCB substrate. SEM observations showed a porous sintered Ag microstructure with local non-uniformities, especially near the edge regions. Fracture surface analysis indicated predominantly cohesive fracture within the sintered Ag layer, with local interfacial contributions. Overall, the results demonstrate that precursor-based pressure-less nano-Ag sintering can be transferred from simplified bulk copper samples to functional DCB test boards. The Cu-cube/DCB configuration provides a suitable platform for electrical, microstructural, and mechanical assessment of pressure-less sintered Ag joints.

articles.title: BioGraphX-Sol: A Structure-Free, Fully Interpretable Protein Solubility Predictor Exceeds AlphaFold3-Based Methods and Reveals Nine Universal Cross-Species Determinants
articles.abstract: Protein solubility is a critical determinant of recombinant expression yield, yet current state-of-the-art predictors often rely on either AlphaFold3-predicted structures or large ensembles of protein language models, limiting accessibility and interpretability. We present BioGraphX-Sol, a sequence-only predictor that constructs biophysically grounded constraint graphs directly from amino acid sequences to extract 200 physicochemical features spanning graph topology, IDP and polymer physics, aggregation-hotspot geometry, and novel surface- and terminal-conditioned descriptors, without requiring 3D coordinates, multiple sequence alignments, or pretrained models. On the standard eSOL benchmark, the XGB+ESM post-hoc ensemble essentially matches ProtSATT in predictive performance (R² = 0.5451 vs.R² = 0.5450), despite training only 1.44M neural parameters and requiring no structure prediction. The physics-only XGBoost configuration (R² = 0.499, ROC--AUC = 0.873) exceeds FGNNSol (R² = 0.487, ROC--AUC = 0.867), which combines AlphaFold3-derived 3D coordinates with ESM-C embeddings and structural descriptors across roughly 1,831 input dimensions, showing that explicit 3D structure prediction is unnecessary when the relevant physicochemical information is correctly encoded. A post-hoc α sweep quantifies the physicochemical-to-evolutionary information balance at approximately 59%/41%, providing, to our knowledge, the first quantitative decomposition of information sources for protein solubility prediction. In zero-shot transfer to S.cerevisiae, the physics-only XGBoost achieves the highest ROC--AUC (0.8524) and PR--AUC (0.9246) among all evaluated methods. Permutation-importance analysis identifies nine universal solubility determinants exhibiting consistent directional effects across E.coli and S.cerevisiae (9/9 agreement). The physics-only configuration requires no GPU at inference and runs efficiently on standard CPU hardware, supporting the Green AI principle that compact, interpretable representations grounded in domain knowledge can provide a viable alternative to parameter scaling.

articles.title: Torque ripple suppression in switched reluctance motors using iterative learning control to optimize the torque sharing function
articles.abstract: Torque ripple caused by uneven torque transfer during phase commutation limits the low-speed steady-state performance of switched reluctance motors (SRMs). This paper proposes a control strategy that uses iterative learning control (ILC) to optimize the torque sharing function (TSF). Starting from a cosine TSF, the method uses the torque error recurring within each electrical cycle to update the TSF in the commutation region from one cycle to the next. The resulting reference torque distribution progressively approaches the actual electromagnetic torque response, thereby improving torque transfer between phases. An 8/6-pole SRM drive model is developed using ANSYS/Maxwell and MATLAB/Simulink to evaluate the proposed strategy. Compared with conventional TSF control, the proposed strategy reduces the torque ripple rate of the SRMs by 39.69%,38.86%, and 38.29% under low-speed steady-state operating conditions of 100 r/min, 200 r/min, and 400 r/min, respectively, demonstrating its effectiveness in suppressing torque ripple.

articles.title: Search-based agents outperform reinforcement learning in Dahal Jeet, a Nepaliimperfect-information card game
articles.abstract: Dahal Jeet is a four-player partnership card game played daily across the Terai- Madhesh region of Nepal, in which only the four tens score. Its objective is lexicographic rather than additive: a majority of tens decides most hands, trick count the rest. The game belongs to the documented Mendikot branch of the Court Piece family, matching Mendikot on 21 of 26 compared features, but the Nepali variant has no published rule description, and the indexed literature returns one paper on the entire family. We contribute a formal specification of the ruleset, drawn from the first author’s own play across seven districts, and a computational study built on it. 26 agents spanning hand-written heuristics, metaheuristic tuning, determinized search and seven learning families are compared across 325 pairings under duplicate-deal protocols with bootstrap intervals and family-wise error control. Search dominates: information-set Monte Carlo tree search leads and no learner reaches a tuned heuristic. An exact doubledummy solver shows search converts 0.923 of theoretically won endgames against 0.810 for the best heuristic. A minimal state encoding outperforms a rich handdesigned one, every deterministic heuristic is exploitable by a search that knows its policy, and the deal alone explains up to 0.391 of outcome variance.

articles.title: Classical finite-element solvers as differentiable graph programs on GPUs
articles.abstract: Conjugate heat transfer in turbomachinery, heat exchangers, and energy systems couples buoyant flow to the surrounding solid on complex geometries. The cost of simulating it is dominated by large sparse linear solves on CPUs. We recast a mixed finite element discretization on unstructured meshes, and its multigrid pressure solve, as sparse graph layers within an automatic differentiation framework. Nothing is trained: weights are entries of the assembled operator, and manufactured solutions recover theoretical convergence orders. Reverse-mode sensitivities match central finite differences; one gradient costs 5.6 forward solves with unrolling and 4.9 with implicit differentiation, nearly constant from one to 32 parameters. Implicit differentiation through every linear solve substantially reduces truncation-induced sensitivity error and makes memory independent of forward iteration count. Against three established solvers, no single code is fastest; the ranking depends on the regime, the size of the problem, and the accuracy demanded. With the discretization, mesh, time step, and tolerances held fixed, the same problem runs up to 181 times faster per step on one GPU than on 32 CPU cores, and the pressure solve alone runs 18.7 times faster. The graph representation depends on operator sparsity rather than the governing equations, providing a route to other assembled discretizations.

articles.title: Attractor computation in continuous-time digital networks
articles.abstract: Attractor dynamics underlie the collective computation of neural networks. Recurrent connections between biological neurons can give rise to stable states towards which network activity relaxes, allowing parallel operation without global coordination while preserving robustness. Implementing physical systems with reliable attractor dynamics is therefore important both for understanding biological intelligence and for developing bio-inspired computing systems. However, parallel physical evolution introduces dynamical challenges. Concurrent evolution of artificial neurons can support rapid collective relaxation, but can also prevent the network from settling. Here, we realise a continuous-time digital Hopfield neural network (CTD-HNN) that combines digitally programmable energy landscapes with state evolution in physical time. Across ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Ising models, associative memory tasks, and Max-Cut problems up to 1,000 vertices, we show that this system can be tuned to exhibit stable relaxation, persistent instability, or transient exploration of state space before convergence. By regulating feedback, activation and propagation delays, we control the intrinsic instability as a dynamical degree of freedom, thereby balancing exploration and convergence while preserving the task-defining interactions. This work combines the configurability and precision of digital hardware with continuous-time dynamics, establishing a programmable framework for attractor computation in which energy landscapes are digitally defined but physically explored.

articles.title: Leveraging Quantum Uncertainty for Modeling Financial Volatility via Quantum Reservoir Computing
articles.abstract: Financial markets exhibit complex non-linear dynamics, temporal dependencies, and stochastic volatility, posing enduring challenges for classical forecasting models. Quantum computing provides a fundamentally different computational paradigm, exploiting superposition, entanglement, and quantum interference to encode and process information in richer representational spaces. Here, we introduce the Entangled Quantum Coherent Reservoir Network (eQCRN) — a quantum reservoir computing framework that leverages quantum uncertainty to model financial uncertainty. eQCRN integrates multiple quantum reservoirs with distinct entanglement configurations, enabling coherent feature expansion and improved temporal correlation modeling beyond classical limits. To our knowledge, this represents one of the first systematic evaluations of entangled quantum reservoirs on real-world financial data. Experiments on 30 stocks across the NASDAQ, S&P 500, and FTSE indices show consistent performance improvements in volatile and non-linear markets, with eQCRN achieving 60.4% accuracy on high-volatility technology stocks versus 58.2% for the best classical models. This gain arises from representing market dynamics in quantum superposition states and capturing inter-temporal correlations via qubit entanglement. Ablation studies identify optimal configurations of 6--8 qubits and 10--12 reservoirs, balancing expressivity and noise resilience. These findings suggest that quantum reservoir computing can complement classical methods for modeling stochastic and non-stationary systems. While not yet a definitive demonstration of quantum advantage, the results indicate a promising pathway toward practical quantum-assisted learning for complex temporal-prediction tasks.

articles.title: NuTwin: A Zero-Trust, Confidential Cloud Architecture for Real-Time Nuclear Reactor Digital Twins Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
articles.abstract: Real-time telemetry diagnostics and predictive anomaly tracking in nuclear reactor cores present a fundamental computational dilemma: high-fidelity numerical neutronics and thermal-hydraulics solvers are too computationally prohibitive for sub-second edge evaluation, whereas conventional black-box deep learning architectures violate physical conservation bounds and lack operational determinism. Simultaneously, transmitting safetycritical nuclear operational data to public cloud infrastructure introduces acute cyber-physical security vectors that breach strict operational air-gaps. This paper introduces NuTwin, a zero-trust, confidential cloud architecture designed for real-time nuclear reactor core digital twins. NuTwin couples a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) surrogate model—constrained directly by point reactor kinetics equations (PRKE) with six delayed neutron precursor groups and coupled thermal-hydraulic reactivity feedback—with hardware-enforced cryptographic isolation. Live operational telemetry, simulated via Python Point Reactor Kinetics (PyRK), is streamed over unidirectional mutual TLS (X.509) connections into AWS IoT Core and processed exclusively inside an ephemeral, attestation-verified AWS Nitro Enclave via an internal virtual socket (vsock) channel devoid of persistent storage or external network interfaces. Experimental validation demonstrates that NuTwin bounds the physical residual loss below 1.4 × 10−4 , achieves sub-second inference latency (42.8 ms per step), and guarantees zero data-leakage surface under zero-trust operational constraints. Index Terms—Digital twins, physics-informed neural networks, confidential computing, AWS Nitro Enclaves, point reactor kinetics, nuclear cyber-physical security, real-time anomaly detection.

articles.title: Effects of Zn addition on the microstructure and corrosion behavior of as-extruded Mg–Al–Ca–Mn-based alloys
articles.abstract: The influence of Zn addition (0–0.6 wt.%) on the microstructure and the corrosion behavior of as-extruded Mg–1Al–0.3Ca–0.3Mn (wt.%) alloys was investigated by X-ray diffraction, optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy combined with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, immersion tests and electrochemical measurements in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution. All the as-extruded alloys consist of an α-Mg matrix and a small fraction of Al4Ca particles distributed along the grain boundaries; no Zn-bearing phase is detected over the composition range studied, so that Zn is retained in solid solution. Immersion tests show that a small Zn addition markedly improves the corrosion resistance: after 168 h the corrosion rate of the alloy containing 0.2 wt.% Zn is 4.77 × 10⁻⁴ g cm⁻² h⁻¹, which is only 14.3% of that of the Zn-free alloy. Potentiodynamic polarization confirms the same ranking, the corrosion potential shifting from −1.490 V to −1.440 V and the corrosion current density decreasing from 71.1 μA cm⁻² to 15.4 μA cm⁻². Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, however, ranks the four alloys differently. Because the grain-size sequence does not track the corrosion-rate sequence—the alloy with the finest grains does not exhibit the lowest corrosion rate—grain refinement alone cannot account for the observed improvement. The beneficial effect is instead attributed to Zn dissolved in the α-Mg matrix, which modifies the growth of the corrosion-product film and limits the area over which micro-galvanic coupling at the Al4Ca particles can operate; this effect is optimal at 0.2 wt.% Zn and is weakened when a higher Zn content coarsens the grains.

articles.title: A general, non-energetic formation route to carboxylic and fatty acids in the interstellar medium
articles.abstract: Carboxylic acids have been detected in the interstellar medium, and biologically relevant fatty acids have been identified on meteorites. However, their formation routes under interstellar conditions and possible delivery to planetary surfaces to act as molecular building blocks for the origin of life remain poorly understood. Here we demonstrate a general, non-energetic, condensed-phase formation route to carboxylic acids under astrophysical, low-temperature conditions, through the interaction of aldehydes and either O-atoms or hydroxyl radicals. This general acid formation route was investigated and confirmed experimentally through the use of infrared spectroscopy and mass spectrometry, and theoretically through the use of hybrid density functional theory and coupled cluster calculations. The finding of a non-energetic formation route from aldehydes to acids and the pathway to form biologically relevant fatty acids under interstellar conditions indicates that such molecules could form and subsequently be inherited into stellar systems, thus potentially contributing to the origin of life.

articles.title: Ultrathin kagome material opens a route to study unusual quantum states
articles.abstract: How atoms are arranged inside materials can influence the behavior of electrons and the resulting electronic states. Kagome lattices, repeating arrangements of atoms forming triangles that share corners (with hexagonal spaces between them), have been linked with the emergence of unusual electronic states.

articles.title: Co--dsorption of terrylene and tetrapentacontane on hexagonal boron nitride - towards a two-dimensional Shpolskii matrix
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organic molecular emitters are promising building blocks for quantum technologies, but their use at two-dimensional interfaces is limited by diffusion, aggregation, and photobleaching. We present work towards constructing an ultrathin two-dimensional Shpolskii-like host-guest matrix on hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) by co-depositing terrylene fluorophores with the long-chain tetrapentacontane in a solution-phase process. We demonstrate that this approach disperses terrylene in a roughly one-nanometer-thin alkane layer without detectable phase separation and allows tuning the emitter density from ensembles to isolated emitters showing characteristic blinking behavior consistent with single-molecule fluorescence. Time-lapse confocal microscopy, autocorrelation analysis, and fluorescence recovery after photobleaching show that suppressed diffusion and stable emitter positions can be achieved in several samples with a tetrapentacontane matrix. Encapsulation with hBN from the top side further improves photostability, with emitters demonstrating long lifetimes despite high photon doses. Successful co-adsorption of isolated emitters and alkane matrix is a milestone towards extending Shpolskii-type molecular isolation to hBN and provides a route towards stable, interface-integrated molecular qubits.

articles.title: Spectral properties of orthorhombic KSbOSiO₄ crystals: studies of infrared, visible and ultraviolet radiation absorption, Raman scattering, cathodoluminescence and photoluminescence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Crystals of orthorhombic KSbOSiO₄ (KSS) are often found to synthesize in glass of historical and artistic articles. For instance, these crystallites in the glass of turquoise Bohemian seed beads are known to play a significant role in the process of internal-stress driven corrosion of the glass causing deterioration and destruction of bead embroidered museum exhibits, especially articles made in the early 19th century. In art materials science, KSS has been known since the mid-2010s only for its destructive effects on historical glass objects, but as an optical material it has long been studied. KSS belongs to the group of compounds isomorphic to KTiOPO₄ (KTP) and, like other compounds from this group, has anomalies in dielectric constant. The article presents the results of a study of orthorhombic KSS crystals using a number of spectroscopic techniques. IR absorption and diffuse reflection spectra of KSS in the spectral range from 50 to 4000~cm⁻¹, its Raman spectrum, its absorption spectrum in the range from near infrared to ultraviolet as well as its cathodoluminescence and photoluminescence spectra are investigated. The constituent peaks of the spectral bands are analyzed and their properties are summarized in tables; the allowed direct and indirect band gaps of KSS are determined. The presented data are necessary both for the correct spectral analysis of historical and artistic glass and enamels, during the production of which this substance was sometimes synthesized in glass, and for a more in-depth study of crystals of the KTP group.

articles.title: Electron-electron interactions mediated by overdamped vibrations: Implications for chirality-induced spin selectivity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS), we investigate spin polarization during molecular electron transfer through a correlated bridge in the presence of a rapidly relaxing Peierls mode. By modulating both electronic hopping and spin--orbit coupling, the mode mediates two-body spin-spin interactions, including isotropic, anisotropic, and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya exchange. We derive these interactions using an exact Lang-Firsov transformation for a four-site chiral bridge. We then include fast vibrational relaxation in the joint electron--vibration master equation and derive the reduced electronic dynamics to second order in the vibronic coupling, retaining both coherent and dissipative contributions and the finite-time buildup of the vibrational response. We test our derivation by numerical simulations, finding spin polarization accumulated at the acceptor after unpolarized injection, with nonmonotonic dependence on damping and bridge filling. Within the postulated local-loss model, our results show that rapid vibrational relaxation does not preclude spin polarization through a correlated bridge and provide a framework for assessing vibration-mediated interactions and dissipative dynamics as ingredients of CISS in molecular electron transfer.

articles.title: Tunable Three-Body Interactions in Microwave-Shielded Polar Molecules
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that microwave shielding, which enables collisionally stable ultracold polar molecules, also leads to genuine nonadditive three-body interactions comparable to the shielding interaction itself. Their magnitude, sign, and geometrical dependence can be flexibly controlled through microwave parameters and orientation. Interaction strengths can reach the ten kilohertz-scale for ultrapolar molecules in typical optical lattices. The nonadditive three-body interactions can stabilize novel many-body phases, and should be accounted for in quantum simulation with microwave shielded molecules.

articles.title: 10 kV β-Ga₂O₃ Sub-Bandgap Triggered Impurity Photoconductive Semiconductor Switches (i-PCSSs): Lessons for Optimal Design
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: β-Ga₂O₃ photoconductive semiconductor switches (PCSSs) are attractive for high-voltage operation, but above-bandgap triggering requires deep-ultraviolet excitation. Here, we investigate a 650-um-thick, 0.01% Fe-doped β-Ga₂O₃ impurity PCSS with a 5-mm lateral gap under continuous-wave (CW) 808-nm sub-bandgap excitation at biases up to 10 kV ( 20 kV cm⁻¹). The device exhibited clear sub-bandgap photoconductive switching. As the optical power density increased from 0.64 to 3.18 W cm⁻², the ON-state current increased progressively while the ON-state resistance decreased, consistent with enhanced defect-assisted photocarrier generation. A higher applied bias further strengthened the switching response through enhanced field-assisted carrier transport. The ON/OFF ratio increases with optical power density but exhibits a nonmonotonic bias dependence, reaching approximately 15-16 near 5-7 kV. At 10 kV, increased OFF-state conduction and non-ideal transient behavior reduce the switching contrast. These results demonstrate near-infrared photoconductive switching but also highlight critical trade-offs in photoconductive thresholds for impurity states.

articles.title: Unifying dynamical electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions from first principles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electron-phonon interactions in materials with free carriers are dynamically screened by low-energy electronic excitations, yet first-principles calculations almost always treat this screening in the adiabatic approximation. A fully dynamical treatment of metals and doped semiconductors within time-dependent density functional perturbation theory (TDDFPT) is expensive and numerically delicate. Here, we introduce DFPT+A downfolding ("A" for active space), which starts from the static density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) response of a computationally convenient base system and adds the dynamical screening of a low-energy active space, described by Wannier functions. The required statically screened electron-electron interaction is computed using DFPT directly in the basis of Wannier-function pairs and truncated in a computationally efficient and systematically improvable way. The method handles entangled bands and accurately reproduces TDDFPT at a fraction of its cost. We use it to compute the total dynamical electron-electron interaction, including direct Coulomb and phonon-mediated interactions with dynamically screened electron-electron and electron-phonon couplings, all on equal footing. In hole-doped monolayer hBN, the hybridization of the carrier plasmon with the longitudinal optical phonon makes the low-energy retarded interaction nonmonotonic in the carrier density, an effect missed by the adiabatic approximation. In metallic monolayer TaS2, nonadiabatic effects are weak and occur only due to the intraband electron-hole continuum and the nesting of nearly parallel Fermi velocities. We also validate the widely used screened-screened approximation for the phonon spectral function. This work opens the way to first-principles studies of spectral functions, transport, and superconductivity with dynamically screened interactions.

articles.title: Anisotropic Boltzmann transport in a tight-binding superlattice: Exact results for power-law energy-dependent scattering
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a complete Boltzmann transport theory for the in-plane (σₓₓ) and out-of-plane (σzz) conductivities of an electronic superlattice consisting of a periodic stack of two-dimensional (2D) parabolic-band layers coupled along the superlattice axis by nearest-neighbor tunneling t, in the physically relevant regime tll E_F where the Fermi surface is an open, corrugated cylinder. Within the relaxation-time approximation with a power-law energy-dependent scattering time τ(E)propto Ep, we study the seven models p=0,±1,±3/2,±2 as functions of the 2D electron density n per layer and temperature T. For p=-2 (in plane) and ple -1 (out of plane), long-lived carriers at the miniband bottom can dominate transport at finite temperature. For p=-2, these carriers produce a pronounced peak in σzz(T) at Tsim E_F. We find that the temperature dependence of the anisotropic metallic dc conductivity can be highly counterintuitive depending on t, T, and p, with no generic increase or decrease with temperature. The Lorenz ratio is determined by the energy variance of the current-carrying electrons; the Wiedemann-Franz (WF) law is exact as T→0 for all models at fixed t, with anisotropic corrections at finite temperature. Band-edge carriers first enhance the interlayer Lorenz ratio up to several times its low-temperature value through thermal occupation of separated energy ranges within the same electron band and then suppress it at high temperature by energy filtering. Strong violations of the Wiedemann-Franz law can therefore arise from miniband structure and energy-dependent elastic scattering alone.

articles.title: Quantifying Blinking Suppression and Probing Its Mechanism in PPD-Treated Single Quantum Dots
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Colloidal semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are highly promising materials for various applications, yet photoluminescence intermittency (blinking) remains a key obstacle to their practical use. While recent advances have enabled partial or complete suppression of this effect, both the degree of suppression and the mechanism by which it occurs are often difficult to establish. In the present work we analyse the blinking suppression of single CdSe/ZnS QDs after treatment with p-phenylenediamine (PPD), recently discovered by Yang et al. We revisit the blinking mechanism in this system and show that it is governed predominantly by the trapping mechanism, rather than by Auger ionization as previously proposed. For data analysis we apply a threshold-free two-dimensional criterion recently proposed by Podshivaylov and Frantsuzov. The criterion is based on the relative quantum yield estimator langle hatQ rangle⁽s⁾ and the decay-rate fluctuation parameter hatξ. We found that PPD treatment significantly increases the relative quantum yield and leads to only a modest increase in hatξ, indicating that the dominant effect of PPD is to shift the distribution of the non-radiative recombination rate toward lower values, rather than to eliminate its fluctuations. We further suggest a number of possible mechanisms of PPD-induced suppression and propose critical experiments for their verification.

articles.title: Agentic Global Optimization of Site-Disordered Crystalline Materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Site-disordered crystals, in which several elements partially occupy the same atomic site, cannot be simulated atomistically without first resolving an explicit ordering, and the number of possible orderings grows combinatorially with supercell size. Because each candidate requires an expensive structural relaxation, locating the global-minimum ordering is a costly combinatorial search. Here, we present an agentic search in which a surrogate model, fitted to previously evaluated configurations, selects each subsequent candidate by balancing exploitation, uncertainty, and novelty. Four surrogates are implemented within a shared framework: an ExtraTrees ensemble, Bayesian ridge regression, sparse ARD regression, and an ALiEGNN-inspired graph ensemble. These are benchmarked against three traditional methods: random walk, Markov chain Monte Carlo, and a genetic algorithm across 14 test cases spanning 12 crystal structures, with exhaustively enumerated global minima as ground truth. The agentic surrogates reach the global minimum in 94% of runs, compared with 55% for the traditional methods, with a median 4.3-fold reduction in evaluations relative to the best traditional method. Bayesian ridge regression succeeds in all runs with the fewest evaluations. Applied to Na2/3FePO4, with coupled Na/vacancy configurational disorder and Fe2+/Fe3+ charge disorder, the framework recovers the experimentally reported ordering when charge states are encoded in the surrogate representation, demonstrating its extension to multi-sublattice disorder.

articles.title: An internal mode shifts the depinning threshold of dissociated dislocations without changing universality
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Driven elastic manifolds exhibit a depinning transition whose large-scale behavior is governed by a nonequilibrium critical fixed point. Real interfaces, however, often possess internal degrees of freedom, raising the question of whether such modes alter depinning universality or only nonuniversal properties of the transition. We address this question for a dissociated dislocation, whose two Shockley partials define a fluctuating stacking-fault width driven by correlated random-alloy stresses. Comparing exact thresholds on identical disorder realizations with the width either free or frozen, we find that width fluctuations leave the depinning universality class unchanged: the roughness exponent ζ and correlation-length exponent ν remain the same even when the width becomes strongly fluctuating and locally multistable. The threshold, however, shifts. The shift is governed by the elastic crossover length of the internal mode rather than by multistability, and can have either sign. An infinite-range mean-field treatment misses this mechanism. With the physical two-partial elastic kernel and disorder calibrated against measured strengths, width fluctuations raise the athermal critical resolved shear stress by 10-35% over that of a rigid dissociated dislocation. An internal mode can thus be irrelevant at the depinning fixed point while remaining quantitatively important for where the transition occurs.

articles.title: Strong-Field-Driven Non-Linear Vibronic Coupling in an Asymmetric Donor-Acceptor Oligomer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41462v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how nuclear motion couples to intramolecular charge transfer beyond the perturbative regime of light--matter interaction remains an open problem. We tackle this problem by investigating the electron-nuclear response of an acceptor-donor-acceptor oligomer with structural asymmetry due to the partial fluorination of an acceptor unit. Adopting real-time time-dependent density functional theory combined with Ehrenfest dynamics, we excite the systems with a resonant pulse of varying intensity, spanning the weak-, intermediate-, and strong-coupling regimes. When nuclei are clamped, field-driven charge preferentially flows from the donor to the fluorinated acceptor, with selectivity reduced upon increasing intensity. With moving ions, the early-time spatial response remains qualitatively unchanged, despite a distinct, spatially asymmetric charge redistribution. In the strong-field regime, nuclear motion preserves the preference for field-driven charge accumulation on the fluorinated acceptor, although the process takes approximately twice the time as in the fixed-nuclei scenario. Mode-resolved kinetic-energy analysis reveals that, with increasing field strength, the laser-induced nuclear response shifts from selected bond stretchings to collective low-frequency modes. These results provide a benchmark for assessing the interplay between vibronic dynamics and strong-field coupling in donor/acceptor oligomers.

articles.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. I. Clean surface properties
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to elucidate the properties of the polar surfaces of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors, i.e., metal- and nonmetal-terminated. The systems considered were clean wurtzite gallium nitride (i.e. (0001) and (000-1) GaN surfaces), zinc blende gallium phosphide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaP), gallium arsenide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaAs), and (111) and (-1-1-1) GaSb surfaces. The calculated data include the crystallographic structure and the electronic states of the termination atoms on both sides, i.e. their positions, energies, and occupations. All nonmetal-terminated surfaces exhibit no reconstruction, and their broken-bond states are located in the vicinity of the valence band maxima (VBM), pinning the Fermi level. The Ga-terminated surface exhibited (4 x 4) reconstruction related to the division of termination atoms into sp3 and sp2 hybridized in proportions of 6 to 10, based on charge redistribution according to the electron counting rule (ECR). Thus, the broken-bond state is separated into two sets, occupied and empty, with the Fermi level located between them in the vicinity of the conduction band minimum (CBM).

articles.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. II. Adsorption of nonmetal atoms (N, P, As, and Sb) on Ga-terminated surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the adsorption processes on Ga-terminated surfaces of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. The considered adsorbates are nonmetal species, i.e., nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, and antimony on wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e., GaN(0001) surfaces, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e., GaP(111), gallium arsenide, GaAs(111), and gallium antimonide, GaSb (111) surfaces. The cases investigated include single adsorbed nonmetal atoms and full coverage, i.e. theta=1 of these surfaces. The calculated results include the stable sites and the energies of the single adsorbed atoms: located at H3 sites at low coverage and in on-top positions at high coverage for GaP, GaAs and GaSb. At high nitrogen coverage, the N2 admolecules are formed, weakly attached to the surface. The calculated electronic properties of the single-adatom systems include the band diagrams of the slabs in real and momentum space, the energies of the quantum states. In addition, the overlaps of the quantum states of the nonmetal adatoms and the nearest topmost surface Ga atoms are given. The full coverage data include the atomic configurations and the bond energies of the adsorbed layers. The electronic properties include the above-mentioned data for single adatoms, together with additional properties related to interactions between adsorbed atoms. The evaporation stability analysis confirms that the adatoms stabilize the topmost Ga atoms against detachment because of the high energy barrier of DE > 3 eV which is further increased to DE > 4 eV by coverage located at H3 sites. Thus, growth simulations should employ unreconstructed Ga-terminated surfaces covered by nonmetal atoms located at on-top positions.

articles.title: Evaluating Instrument-Centered AI Agents for Table-Top Science Experiments
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable evaluation of AI agents for table-top science experiments has remained elusive because live instruments are hard to reset and share at scale, while instrument statefulness and safety constraints complicate evaluation. We introduce instrMCP and q-devBench, an evaluation stack for instrument-centered AI agents in table-top experiments. instrMCP connects coding agents to scientific instruments through the Model Context Protocol, serving as the instrument-access harness. q-devBench reconstructs 37 real experimental tasks from condensed-matter physics as virtual QCoDeS instruments covering quantum electronic transport, scanning probe imaging, and calibration workflows. q-devBench exposes reproducible failure modes in laboratory-agent systems while preserving realistic instrument-control workflows. Across a range of commercial coding-agent configurations, current systems already show substantial operational competence, satisfying 70-83% of measurement-related rubric criteria. The main bottleneck is scientific analysis, where performance falls to 28-46%. In an analysis-only ablation in which agents receive clean reference datasets without running the virtual measurement session, analysis performance improves substantially, closing roughly two thirds of the difference between the measurement and analysis scores. This suggests that much of the deficit arises from the measurement-session context, including tool-use overhead, longer context, measurement-planning decisions, and possible acquisition errors, while a residual scientific-reasoning gap remains. Together, instrMCP and q-devBench provide a practical sandbox for benchmarking, diagnosing, and improving laboratory AI harnesses, and establish a route from controlled virtual evaluation to future live-hardware validation.

articles.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. We further demonstrate that Fermi-sea layer polarization provides an additional degree of freedom for controlling many-body interactions. In particular, the presence of a Fermi sea induces hybridization between oppositely oriented dipolar polarons, whereas confining the Fermi sea to a single layer suppresses this hybridization and produces orientation-selective many-body dressing. Our findings establish an experimental platform for dipolar-polaron physics in which dipole orientation and Fermi-sea layer polarization jointly govern many-body interactions, opening a route towards electrically tunable interactions and dipolar-polaron-mediated attraction between itinerant electrons.

articles.title: Pair-Condensation Peak in Radio-Frequency Dimer-Projection Spectroscopy of a Unitary Fermi Gas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Radio-frequency dimer-projection spectroscopy has recently emerged as a powerful probe of strongly interacting Fermi gases, yet its frequency-resolved spectrum remains largely unexplored. Here we show that the spectrum exhibits two qualitatively distinct features: a broad quasiparticle continuum governed by fermionic pairing and a sharp pair-condensation peak arising from the coherent projection of condensed Cooper pairs onto the final-state dimer. To reveal this physics, we develop a point-dimer approximation that exploits the separation between the molecular and many-body length scales and expresses the radio-frequency response directly in terms of pair correlations in the initial many-body state. Within the BCS mean-field theory, we derive the frequency-dependent spectrum, identify the microscopic transfer processes underlying its structure, and show that the continuum possesses a threshold determined by the superfluid gap. Our theory establishes radio-frequency dimer-projection spectroscopy as a unified probe of short-range correlations, fermionic pairing, and long-range coherence in strongly interacting Fermi gases.

articles.title: Andreev-Enhanced Conductance in a Bilayer Graphene Quantum Point Contact
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41915v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum point contacts provide a platform for probing mode-dependent Andreev reflection. Here, we demonstrate Andreev-enhanced conductance in a gate-defined bilayer graphene quantum point contact coupled to a superconducting aluminum electrode. Electrostatic gating enables sequential mode occupation, verified by normal-state conductance quantization. In the superconducting state, the conductance is enhanced within the conductance plateaus, while the enhancement decreases between plateaus, consistent with the nonlinear transmission dependence of Andreev reflection. The enhancement yields effective transmission probabilities up to 0.9, and extends over a bias window of approximately 140 μV, which we associate with a proximity-induced superconducting gap, close to the gap of the aluminum film. For in-plane fields, the enhancement persists up to the critical field, and the bias window follows the spectral gap predicted by Abrikosov-Gor'kov theory. In contrast, perpendicular fields suppress the enhancement approximately linearly from zero field, deviating from homogeneous pair breaking and indicative of flux penetration.

articles.title: Anomalies of TQFTs coupled to parameter spaces and constraints on ground-state degeneracies
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.42007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anomalies of global symmetries can arise in long-range entangled quantum many-body systems and provide useful constraints on their dynamics. In this paper, we study anomalies of d-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs) coupled to parameter spaces and their implications for ground-state degeneracies. Specifically, we formulate anomalies as obstructions to constructing parametrized families of TQFTs. We discuss how the classification of these anomalies depends on the choice of topology on the universal U(1) (d-1)-form symmetry. In this framework, we use the projective ground-state bundle obtained by compactifying the TQFT on a spatial manifold to derive a general constraint relating its ground-state degeneracy N to its torsion anomaly ω, expressed as Nint_WωinZ for bundles W of spatial manifolds over closed surfaces. We apply this constraint to ground-state degeneracies of (2+1)-dimensional TQFTs with framing and 1-form symmetry anomalies and to obstructions to symmetry-preserving TQFTs. We also discuss implications for bordism generators and propose a conjecture on anomaly detection by manifolds fibered over surfaces.

articles.title: Charge Pumping Leptogenesis from the Symmetric Mass Generation Phase on a Four-Leg Ladder Lattice
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.42103v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantized charge pumping in quantum Hall systems is a bulk topological property, typically manifesting on gapless boundaries as spectral flow through chiral edge modes upon flux insertion. When the boundary is anomaly-free, it can be symmetrically gapped by symmetric mass generation (SMG) interactions. However, the effects on quantized charge pumping at an interacting gapped boundary are unclear. We address this using density-matrix renormalization group simulations of a four-leg ladder quasi-(2+1)d realization of the (1+1)d 3-4-5-0 lattice chiral fermion model with six-fermion interactions at one edge. We find gapless modes near the interacting edge for both weak and strong couplings, but the edge can be in a fully gapped SMG phase at intermediate coupling. We also identify spontaneous breaking of the model's Z₂ symmetry above a critical interaction strength. Across all three boundary phases, we find quantized charge pumping with the same pumped charge per flux quantum. The spatial distribution of the pumped charge varies between phases. Besides charge pumping, we study how a single injected fermion propagates under open boundary conditions. In the SMG phase, an interaction-induced flavor-mixing current develops at the endpoints of the gapped edge, which is absent in the weak- and strong-coupling limits. This current reveals a charge-redistribution mechanism unique to the SMG phase. Additionally, we propose an analogy between charge pumping in this model and a topological leptogenesis scenario in the (3+1)d Standard Model. The anomaly-free chiral U(1) symmetries of the 3-4-5-0 model play a role analogous to the baryon-minus-lepton symmetry of the Standard Model. In both settings, charge pumping can be associated with a continuous deformation along a classically defined but quantum-anomalous direction, while a discrete subgroup remains an exact quantum symmetry.

articles.title: Topological Quantum Error-Correcting Thresholds of a Symmetry-Enriched Toric Code
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37791v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the error thresholds of a new topological quantum error-correcting code under the independent bit-flip and phase-flip noisy channel. By mapping to classical spin-glass models, we find that if Pauli X and Z errors are equally probable, the threshold of vertex syndromes is improved by 30% compared to that of the toric code, while the threshold of plaquette syndromes is lowered. Both thresholds increase when the Z component is less likely than the X component, reaching 0.5 if the Z component is absent. An analytical proof justifies this special case of perfect correctability, and a disordered version of Peierls's argument establishes a lower bound for the vertex-syndrome threshold.

articles.title: Physics-Grounded Simulation Enables Zero-Shot Molecular and Reaction Analysis in Scanning Tunneling Microscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40666v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantitative identification of molecular products and reaction pathways from scanning tunneling microscopy images is difficult when labeled images are unavailable for a new chemical system. We develop a simulation-assisted framework for zero-shot analysis that requires only precursor information for a new target system, with no experimental images or annotations from that system used during model training. The framework couples two functional components: NanoSim generates physics-grounded synthetic images from predicted reaction products and sampled surface scenes, while NanoAnalysis translates molecular detections into product populations, spatial arrangements, and mechanistic interpretations. Applied to a representative on-surface reaction, the detector achieves a micro-averaged F1 score of 0.92 on experimental images. Analysis of the detected molecules reveals annealing-dependent population changes and reaction-site preferences consistent with experimental observations. Beyond this capability, its modular organization allows heterogeneous data from other systems to be used to improve each component independently, providing a scalable route for continued generalization.

articles.title: Guaranteed Slater Conditions for the Numerical Conformal Bootstrap: Fixing Instabilities in SDPB, Navigator Methods, and Skydiving
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40764v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The semidefinite programs (SDPs) of the numerical conformal bootstrap, and of S-matrix and quantum-mechanics bootstraps, are solved with primal-dual interior-point methods whose convergence guarantees rest on primal and dual Slater conditions: the existence of strictly feasible points on both sides of the duality. Many bootstrap SDPs violate these. The consequences range from slow convergence to inconclusive verdicts and the breakdown of the Skydive algorithm. We introduce "Slater tools", all acting within the PMP class accepted by SDPB. Diagnostics measure the Slater margins and, when a margin vanishes, extract the exposing certificate that identifies the degeneracy. Two independent cures follow. Transforms that provide rigorous bounds on the original SDP objective and that for the right parameter choices return the exact value. Facial reductions that use the exposing certificate to remove the degeneracies themselves. We reproduce, explain and resolve all known types of failures in a mixed-correlator 3d Ising setup. We show that the X-Slater condition (SDPB's primal) fails at every disallowed point in feasibility mode, holds in every navigator problem we tested, and can be guaranteed by one additional condition on the navigator function. We show that the folklore "instability remedy" of a twist gap works by removing degeneracies at the endpoints of the positivity conditions. These often stem from a mistake in factoring out the block prefactor but can also arise legitimately in channels that mix equal and unequal operator pairs. Finally we classify and remove all degeneracies of the published current-scalar bootstrap, among them one at x=infty, thus incurable by any gap assumption, caused by unequal polynomial degrees within one matrix block.

articles.title: Fock-space delocalization and its control in scarred-vs-ergodic dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40805v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum many-body scarred dynamics in Rydberg-atom arrays is characterized by revivals, in which the system repeatedly returns to its initial state despite its many-body complexity. But how extensively does the wave function explore the space of allowed configurations between revivals? We address this question by quantifying the fraction of configurations occupied during PXP dynamics initialized from the paradigmatic polarized and Néel states, which respectively exhibit thermalizing and scarred dynamics. Despite their striking revivals, dynamics from the Néel state spreads over exponentially many configurations, yet occupies a vanishing fraction of the full space in the thermodynamic limit. Dynamics from the polarized state, by contrast, occupies a finite fraction of the configuration space, close to anticoncentration and random-state statistics, although chiral symmetry limits this fraction to one third. A weak quasiperiodic field enables the polarized state to occupy half of the configuration space by lifting the constraint imposed by chiral symmetry. The Néel state, however, requires a stronger field to reach a comparable anticoncentrated regime. As the field increases further, the occupied fraction decreases for both initial states, revealing a nonmonotonic dependence of Fock-space delocalization on field strength without necessarily implying localization.

articles.title: Proof of the entropic c-theorem
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40874v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove an entropic c-theorem in two dimensions by constructing a c-function from the mutual information between spacelike separated wedges, defined through the relative entropy. The proof follows Casini and Huerta's, with strong subadditivity of entanglement entropy replaced by increasing differences of the mutual information, which we prove directly in the continuum from the split property and standard properties of relative entropy. The benefit of relative entropy is that every quantity we use is finite and no cutoff ever needs to be introduced. The assumptions of the theorem are only the standard axioms of algebraic quantum field theory, the split property with finite mutual information across a gap (both implied by modular p-nuclearity), and a finite ultraviolet bound on the resulting c-functions. We also note that, formally, the c-function is proportional to the minimal averaged null energy of a state that reproduces the vacuum correlations between the two wedges.

articles.title: Stress-enhanced diffusion in Yukawa crystals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-diffusion in crystallized Coulomb (Yukawa) plasmas proceeds by the thermally activated formation of vacancy-interstitial pairs and the migration of these defects through the lattice, commonly known as Frenkel pairs in the materials literature. Molecular dynamics has recently resolved an Eyring law for diffusion in unstrained crystals, which we generalize to deformed crystals in this work. We simulate sheared Yukawa crystals and show that a static elastic strain exponentially enhances diffusion due to the additional elastic energy stored in the region that participates in Frenkel pair formation relative to the unstrained crystal: D(ε)=D₀(Γ*)exp[V*σ/kᵣₘ BT], with σ=tfrac12με² the elastic energy density stored by the shear strain ε and V* the activation volume. We find a single activation volume Nᵣₘ ₐcₜ = nᵢV*simeq31 suffices for typical astrophysical screenings with a reduction at higher screening. This suggests Frenkel pair formation requires only a brief coordination of the nearest neighbors at a thermal maximum in oscillation. Stress-enhanced diffusion supplies a microphysical mechanism for creep in strained neutron star crusts and crystallizing white dwarf cores.

articles.title: Helper-assisted quantum sensing with low dressed-state leakage
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41404v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a two-qubit sensing protocol in which only a helper qubit is read out. Calibrated loading and unloading encode a transverse signal in the helper's phase, keep leakage out of a selected dressed-state band small, and return the sensor close to its idle ground state. We derive an information bound for a single sensor whose excitation stays below a prescribed budget, and simulate repeated operation with an uncertain coupling and finite-duration resets in a driven open-system model. At the tested settings, finite measurement records support estimation with infrequent resets. A helper flip at zero coupling, combined with a reversal of the coupling sign, suppresses a static helper offset shared across a record while retaining the signal, at a cost of about 27% of the no-offset information of a plain sequence of equal duration. Under slowly varying noise, averaging each cycle's likelihood over the correct noise law removes most of the added bias, and a wrong noise law can worsen the estimate. A selected directly read sensor with ideal controls and repeated nondemolition verification has the higher information rate. Any practical benefit of avoiding direct readout therefore requires a device-specific disturbance model.

articles.title: Root-of-unity limit of the Aₙ₋₁ lens elliptic gamma function solution of the star-star relation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41438v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the root-of-unity limit of the multi-component spin solution of the star-star relation whose Boltzmann weights are products of lens elliptic gamma functions, and whose spins take values in Rⁿ⁻¹×(Zᵣ)ⁿ⁻¹. When one of the elliptic nomes tends to a primitive 2rN-th root of unity, the quasi-classical expansion gives at leading order the classical star-star relation of the Bazhanov-Sergeev multi-spin model; at the next order, under the standard assumptions on the saddle points, a (ZᵣN)ⁿ⁻¹-state solution of the star-star relation, which depends on r and N only through rN. Real Zₙ-symmetric configurations of the continuous spins give elliptic mathfraksl(n) Kashiwara-Miwa type models labeled by n-torsion points. Extended to general primitive torsion points, these include the broken ZᵣN model of Quano and Fujii, for which the star-star relation follows from their Yang-Baxter equation when gcd(n,rN)=1. In the trigonometric limit the saddle point equations single out the spectral curve of the mathfraksl(n) chiral Potts model of Bazhanov, Kashaev, Mangazeev and Stroganov, and the Boltzmann weights become those of that model.

articles.title: Lifting the mixed to the pure: quantum phases of matter from canonical purification
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41926v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pure-state quantum phases are defined through finite-depth local unitary connections. This concept of phases has recently been generalized to mixed states in terms of locally reversible channels. In this work, we establish a fundamental relation between mixed-state phases and pure-state phases. We show that a locally reversible channel between mixed states can be lifted to a local isometry between their canonical purifications; thus, if two mixed states are in the same phase, then their canonical purifications are in the same pure-state phase. Furthermore, an explicit construction of the lifting isometry is given by ``half'' of the Petz recovery map, suggesting that the Petz recovery map emphwithout rotation is enough to connect mixed state phases. We illustrate our results with two examples: toric code under bit flip noise and Chern insulator under fermion number noise.

articles.title: Field-resolved observation and quantification of the instantaneous Kerr response in semiconductors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.42098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The optical Kerr effect, whereby the refractive index of a material changes with light intensity, underpins nonlinear photonics and emerging mid-infrared technologies. Accurate determination of the nonlinear refractive index is therefore essential, yet conventional intensity-based techniques infer the nonlinear phase shift indirectly from changes in beam propagation or optical spectra. Moreover, methods such as the z-scan cannot resolve the temporal evolution of the nonlinear response, making it difficult to distinguish instantaneous Kerr nonlinearities from delayed contributions, including free-carrier effects. Here, we investigate the nonlinear optical response of germanium at 5 mum using field-resolved degenerate pump-probe spectroscopy. By measuring the transmitted probe electric field as a function of pump-probe delay, we directly retrieve the pump-induced phase shift and its temporal evolution while retaining sensitivity to changes in absorption. We observe cross-phase modulation that follows the pump intensity envelope and vanishes when the pump and probe no longer overlap, consistent with an instantaneous Kerr response. The phase shift scales linearly with pump intensity, yielding a nonlinear refractive index of n₂=(0.87±0.16)×10⁻¹⁷ m²/W. Our results establish the instantaneous Kerr effect as the dominant contribution to the measured nonlinear phase shift under our experimental conditions and demonstrate field-resolved pump-probe spectroscopy as a direct, time-resolved method for determining the nonlinear refractive index and distinguishing instantaneous from delayed optical responses.

articles.title: Counting statistics and inference limits for reactions driven by latent ergodic dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2409.11433v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many natural phenomena--from chemical reactions to biological encounters and sensor detections--are described through counts of discrete events. Such events occur at random times when an underlying, often unobserved, dynamical system enters a reactive region of its phase space.
