Despite the ubiquity of these processes in nature, a general framework linking counting statistics to the properties of the underlying stochastic process is lacking. Most existing theories, including widely used mass-action models, neglect trajectory correlations and assume independent counts. We develop a theory that overcomes these limitations, deriving a general expression for the inter-count time distribution as a function of the spatiotemporal scales of the reactive region and the stochastic process. The counting statistics interpolate between a reaction-limited regime, where counts are effectively independent and follow Poisson statistics, and a diffusion-limited regime, where counts are strongly determined by the correlation structure of the latent stochastic process and exhibit systematic overdispersion relative to the Poissonian limit. This structure establishes fundamental constraints on what properties of the stochastic process can be inferred from measured event counts alone. We illustrate these constraints in two biophysical examples: an activity-monitoring assay for a small organism based on detector crossings and population size estimation from encounter counts, in which we recover and generalize classical sensing limits. Our framework thus provides a unified theoretical description of counting processes driven by latent diffusion dynamics, and quantifies how much information each process carries about the other.

articles.title: The effect of Nb and O on the martensitic transformation in the Ti-Nb-O alloys
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.05725v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This study examines the influence of niobium and oxygen on phase stability, crystal structure, and martensitic transformation pathways in Ti-Nb-O alloys. A series of Ti-(8-28)Nb-(0-3)O (at.%) alloys were prepared and solution-treated in the β-phase field. Microstructure and crystallography were characterized by X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, and reciprocal-space mapping. A 2D-XRD orientation simulation approach was applied to distinguish all 12 crystallographically equivalent α" martensitic variants originating from a single prior β grain, enabling detailed diffraction analysis. This method further allowed quantitative evaluation of the atomic shuffle parameter y, describing the β→α" transformation. The results demonstrate that Nb primarily governs α" martensite evolution. Increasing Nb stabilizes the β phase and shifts the α" structure toward higher symmetry, as reflected by systematic changes in lattice parameters and increasing shuffle parameter y, indicating suppression of transformation toward the hexagonal α' phase. Oxygen, in contrast, modifies transformation pathways. At lower Nb contents, it suppresses the ω phase formation and promotes β→α" transformation, while at higher Nb levels it inhibits long-range martensitic transformation, resulting in retained β or competing ω phase. These effects are attributed to local lattice distortions induced by interstitial oxygen.

articles.title: What do the fundamental constants of physics tell us about life?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.09892v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the 1970s, the renowned physicist Victor Weisskopf famously developed a research program to qualitatively explain properties of matter in terms of the fundamental constants of physics. But there was one type of matter prominently missing from Weisskopf's analysis: life. Here, we develop Weisskopf-style arguments demonstrating how the fundamental constants of physics can be used to understand the properties of living systems. By combining biophysical arguments and dimensional analysis, we show that vital properties of chemical self-replicators, such as growth yield, minimum doubling time, and minimum power consumption in dormancy, can be quantitatively estimated using fundamental physical constants. The calculations highlight how the laws of physics constrain chemistry-based life on Earth, and if it exists, elsewhere in our universe.

articles.title: Informational and algebraic renormalization group
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.30362v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Renormalization group (RG) is a core concept from statistical mechanics to quantum field theory, yet its schemes differ widely across literature. We formulate Wilsonian RG for generic, including finite-dimensional, quantum systems as a quantum channel combining coarse graining with isometric rescaling, whose Kraus representation yields pure conditional trajectories for pure inputs and recovers mixed-state flows upon averaging. We then develop an algebraic extension without assuming tensor-product factorization: the retained low-energy algebra is constructed from the one-particle spectrum, and coarse graining is a conditional expectation onto it. Identifying the channel's Cesàro mean with a resource-destroying map onto fixed states establishes a resource theory of RG and yields a relative-entropy monotone without variational optimization. For thermal states in the zero-temperature limit, the resulting Bogoliubov--Kubo--Mori metric per unit spacetime volume is proportional to the Zamolodchikov metric, directly relating the resource density to c-cᵣₘ IR near a two-dimensional IR fixed point. We also introduce the relative entropy of coarse graining to measure discarded UV information, prove its monotonicity along successive coarse grainings, and evaluate it holographically in global AdS₃.

articles.title: Resonance and Transition-Channel Competition in Cavity-Assisted Floquet-State Stabilization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39169v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Static coupling to a dissipative cavity has been proposed as a route to autonomously stabilize Floquet eigenstates. The cavity provides an energy-selective relaxation channel: when its photon energy matches a quasienergy difference modulo drive quanta, it mediates transitions between Floquet states, followed by irreversible photon loss. Here, we show that at intermediate driving frequencies, this resonance condition alone is not sufficient for stabilization. Instead, the steady state is controlled by the interplay between resonance selection and the cavity-induced transition strengths between Floquet states, which can either cooperate or compete. This interplay leads to successful stabilization, mixed steady states despite resonance, and complete breakdown near Floquet-zone hybridization. We further show that the same mechanism extends to multilevel spin-S systems, providing a general framework for understanding when static dissipation can reliably stabilize driven quantum states.

articles.title: Accurate structural identification for layered composite structures, through a wave and finite element scheme
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40689v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present for the first time an approach for identifying the geometric and material characteristics of layered composite structures through an inverse wave and finite element approach. More specifically, this Non-Destructive Evaluation (NDE) approach is able to recover the thickness, density, as well as all independent mechanical characteristics such as the tensile and shear moduli for each layer of the composite structure under investigation. This is achieved through multi-frequency single shot measurements. It is emphasized that the success of the approach is independent of the employed excitation frequency regime, meaning that both structural dynamics and ultrasound frequency spectra can be employed. It is demonstrated that more efficient convergence of the identification process is attained closer to the bending-to-shear transition range of the layered structure. Since a full FE description is employed for the periodic composite, the presented approach is able to account for structures of arbitrary complexity. The procedure is applied to a sandwich panel with composite facesheets and results are compared with two wave-based characterization techniques: the Inhomogeneous Wave Correlation method and the Transition Frequency Characterization method. Numerical simulations and experimental results are presented to verify the robustness of the proposed method.

articles.title: Benchmarking One-Dimensional Quantum Lattice Boltzmann Methods on Quantum Hardware
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methods encounter significant computational bottlenecks in large systems and at high Reynolds number flows due to the rapid increase in degrees of freedom, even on flagship supercomputers. As quantum computers emerge, the Quantum Lattice Boltzmann Method (QLBM) has been proposed as a quantum-native alternative for solving fluid dynamics problems. However, until recently, nearly all studies have relied on classical quantum simulators rather than real quantum hardware. This study presents a benchmark of a one-dimensional QLBM implementation executed on three different IBM Quantum hardware. We design and test a quantum circuit for the advection-diffusion equation using amplitude encoding, a Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK)-type collision operator, and a streaming step with periodic boundary conditions. Our numerical experiments evaluate transpiled two-qubit gate count, total circuit depth, runtime, and accuracy metrics including maximum absolute error (L_infty norm) and root-mean-square error (RMSE). We find that the present collision and streaming operators dominate the overall cost and become the primary scalability bottleneck on current hardware. To mitigate the prohibitive cost of full quantum state tomography on hardware-based benchmarking exercises, we introduce a sampler-based measurement strategy that reconstructs macroscopic density fields directly from computational-basis measurements. This approach substantially reduces measurement overhead while preserving the expected advection-diffusion dynamics on hardware. These results provide a quantitative assessment of QLBM performance in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) regime and identify the principal algorithmic and experimental limitations that must be addressed for QLBM to become viable for fluid dynamics.

articles.title: An analytical framework for wave-coherent airflow over fast surface waves
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical theories attribute wind-wave momentum transfer to a critical layer, where the mean wind speed equals the wave phase speed. For waves that travel faster than the near-surface wind, this layer may lie outside the wave boundary layer or be absent altogether. We develop an analytical description of the wave-coherent airflow in this regime for a prescribed mean wind, using a Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin--Jeffreys (WKBJ) approximation to the viscous Orr--Sommerfeld equation in wave-following coordinates. The solution combines an outer Rayleigh mode, which carries the dominant wave-coherent motion, with a thin viscous Stokes layer that supplies the phase shift producing the pressure form stress. At leading order, the form stress scales with the inverse square root of the wave Reynolds number, with a coefficient set by an integral of the outer response, and transfers momentum from the waves to the air. For an exponential mean profile, the WKBJ approximation gives closed-form expressions for the wave-coherent response. To accommodate the rapid near-surface variation of realistic wall-bounded profiles, we develop a long-wave expansion near the surface and match it to the outer WKBJ mode (LW--WKBJ). For wall-modelled simulations, whose first resolved level lies above the viscous sublayer, we replace the molecular viscosity in the Stokes layer with a constant-stress effective viscosity. Using mean profiles from direct numerical simulations and wave-phase-resolved large-eddy simulations, the LW--WKBJ framework closely reproduces the dominant wave-coherent velocity and pressure obtained from numerical solutions and available simulation data. The predicted form-stress coefficients also agree well with the available LES estimates.

articles.title: Physical Mechanisms of Light-Induced Molecular Fragmentation in the Long-Wavelength Regime
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Strong near-infrared (NIR) laser fields ionize polyatomic molecules through tunneling and multiphoton processes, while subsequent molecular fragmentation can be driven by electron rescattering and field-induced nonadiabatic excitation of the molecular ion. How these competing mechanisms deposit energy into molecular ions and determine fragmentation branching remains unresolved. By combining wavelength- and ellipticity-dependent intensity-difference mass spectrometry of methanol with time-dependent Schrödinger equation (TDSE) and semiclassical Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that, in the tunneling-to-intermediate regime (γ lesssim 1), molecular fragmentation is governed by the interplay of electron recollision and field-driven nonadiabatic excitation, revealing competing physical mechanisms relevant to polyatomic molecules more broadly. Ellipticity-dependent measurements demonstrate that these mechanisms can be experimentally distinguished for individual cationic fragments. Channels requiring high internal energies exhibit the strong ellipticity-dependent suppression characteristic of rescattering-driven processes, while lower-energy channels are comparatively less sensitive. Although small-fragment yields decrease substantially with increasing wavelength, their relative distributions remain largely unchanged, indicating that the underlying fragmentation pathways are preserved and that the suppression primarily reflects reduced probabilities of electron recollision and nonadiabatic excitations at longer wavelengths.

articles.title: A Large Eddy Simulation Study of Turbine Pitch Motion Effects on Power Generation in Fully Developed Floating Wind Turbine Arrays
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactions between floating wind turbines and the marine atmospheric boundary layer affect turbine wakes and power output. This study examines the impact of turbine representations and platform pitching motion on power predictions for aligned floating wind turbine arrays. Large-eddy simulations (LES) are performed for a fully developed wind turbine array boundary layer with periodic streamwise and spanwise boundary conditions and moving surface drag (MOSD) at the bottom surface. A proposed power-curve-aware extension of the conventional actuator disk model (PCADM) is compared with the traditional constant coefficient actuator disk model (CCADM), which is valid in principle only during Region 2 operation. Harmonic pitching motion matched to a representative ocean wave frequency is prescribed for IEA 15MW turbines mounted on the UMaine VolturnUS-S platform. Results demonstrate that the CCADM produces unphysical power overshoot when relative velocities induced by harmonic pitching periodically exceed rated speed, while the PCADM eliminates these unrealistic excursions from the actual turbine operating range. Various wind-wave conditions and relative pitching motions for an aligned farm with PCADM turbines are analyzed, including in-phase, opposite-phase, and incommensurate-phase row-to-row relative turbine motion. Results reveal that, depending on operational regions, turbine pitching motion can either increase or decrease mean turbine power output. Among the relative phases considered, in-phase motions produce larger fluctuations at the farm scale due to stronger turbine-turbine correlations. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for turbine motion and associated changes in operational regions when modeling turbine and wind farm power production in LES of offshore floating wind farms using actuator disk representations.

articles.title: Non-contact temperature sensing and optical scatter in cryogenically-cooled crystalline silicon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cryogenic crystalline silicon is a promising optical material for next generation gravitational-wave detectors due to its low mechanical loss (a driver of thermal noise), high thermal conductivity and zero coefficient of thermal expansion at 123 K. In this paper, we report on the design and results of an experiment to measure the temperature of a flat-flat uncoated crystalline silicon sample using a non-contact sensing method relying on interference (optical fringes) made from reflections between the front and back surfaces. We also propose a scheme for implementation of this technique for cryogenic test masses in future gravitational-wave detectors such as Einstein Telescope and LIGO Voyager. Additionally, we characterize the optical scattering of the sample in vacuum at cryogenic temperatures by using a high-sensitivity infrared camera. We measured relatively constant scatter with an average bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) of (4.43±0.2)× 10⁻³,mathrmsr⁻¹ at a scattering angle of θₛ = 7.5^circ over the (cold-plate) temperature range of 123-294 K and saw no evidence for growth of cryogenic molecular layers (ice) on the sample in our current setup.

articles.title: Shielding design and construction for the XINGZHI cold neutron triple-axis spectrometer: integrating velocity selector, S-bender polarizer, and neutron guide
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The optimized design and construction of shielding for the velocity selector, S-bender polarizer, and neutron guide in the XINGZHI cold neutron triple-axis spectrometer have been successfully completed. The challenge of limited space available for XINGZHI has been met by a compact shielding structure, developed through Monte Carlo simulations and realized by purpose-built mechanical design, thus leaving more floor space for the spectrometer. An innovative lead-antimony alloy ensures rigidity for self-support, while optimized tolerances for gaps between mating blocks meet safety, machinability, and mounting requirements. Additionally, a long-distance alignment method has been implemented, facilitating the alternating installation of the neutron guide and shielding system. After six years of operation, this structure has been verified to meet radiation safety standards while maximizing available space, marking a significant advancement in neutron instrumentation in China and offering valuable methodologies for future development.

articles.title: Feature-preserving interface reconstruction using piecewise circles and cusps
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a geometric interface reconstruction method for Volume-of-Fluid (VOF) simulations that captures both curved interfaces and sharp features using only volume fraction data. We represent interfaces with linear facets, circular arcs, and corner facets formed by two lines or arcs joined within a single cell. We first propagate local orientation constraints through a graph and merge cells to resolve ambiguities, treating topological consistency as a first-class constraint. An optional conservative refinement improves C⁰ continuity while preserving local volume constraints. Users can independently enable circular facets, corner facets, cell merging, and continuity refinement to balance accuracy and computational cost. In its simplest configuration, our method provides a fast local line-fitting scheme competitive with state-of-the-art PLIC methods. On standard static benchmarks, the full configuration reconstructs identifiable lines, circles, and sufficiently resolved corners to numerical precision on coarse, perturbed Cartesian meshes. On varying-curvature interfaces, it achieves third-order convergence in facet-gap error and approximately first-order convergence in curvature error. These results demonstrate global volume conservation and accurate reconstruction of curved and corner features.

articles.title: Dual-rate optical frequency comb based on a cylindrical microresonator with a nanoscale radius variation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We theoretically find that a cylindrical microresonator with nanoscale radius variation can be a source of coherent microcombs with two repetition rates, independently controlled by the device geometry. This phenomenon arises from the formation of two-dimensional axial-azimuthal dissipative Kerr solitons (2D DKS), which we discovered through numerical simulations of the nonlinearly coupled Lugiato-Lefever equations with realistic microresonator device parameters. We demonstrate that, despite the variation in the dispersion characteristics of azimuthal modes at different axial numbers, the spontaneous synchronization mechanism leads to a unified soliton repetition rate. We consider near-parabolic variations in the radius of a cylindrical resonator, compatible with the surface nanoscale axial photonics (SNAP) platform. In our example, we generate 2D DKS with an azimuthal rate of approximately 329 GHz and an axial rate of 6 GHz, which can be adjusted on demand by selecting the appropriate resonator geometry, thereby promising compact sources of frequency combs operating simultaneously across different frequency scales.

articles.title: Streptavidin-Biotin Binding is Intrinsically Non-Cooperative, but Experimental Artefacts Can Induce Apparent Positive Cooperativity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The biotin-streptavidin interaction is a key component of nanobiotechnology, yet the nature of its cooperativity remains a debated question. Here, we introduce a label-free spectroscopy approach based on confocal UV autofluorescence microscopy to probe the binding cooperativity of this high-affinity system. By leveraging the intrinsic autofluorescence of tryptophan residues, we avoid artefacts associated with extrinsic fluorescent labels, enabling precise measurements of fully biotin-saturated streptavidin across a wide range of molar ratios. Our experimental results, supported by Monte Carlo simulations, provide conclusive evidence for the absence of cooperativity. However, we show that false signs of apparent positive cooperativity can emerge from local concentration inhomogeneities occurring when rapid reaction kinetics outpace mixing. By establishing the non-cooperative nature of biotin-streptavidin binding and identifying the key conditions to avoid cooperativity artefacts, these insights resolve a longstanding debate and offer critical implications for streptavidin-based biotechnological applications.

articles.title: Non-Hermitian Spectral Topology Shaped by Memory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Non-Hermitian spectral topology has transformed our understanding of bulk--boundary correspondence in open systems, yet its exploration has largely remained within the Markovian regime of instantaneous coupling. Here, we reveal how memory shapes non-Hermitian spectral topology by extending coupling asymmetry from space to time. Spatiotemporal nonreciprocity and memory-induced spectral multivaluedness give rise to nontrivial spectral topology on multi-sheeted Riemann surfaces, governed by both spatial connectivity and interaction history. Coherent interference among long-range memory channels can induce anomalous spectral winding and skin localization opposite to the dominant-coupling direction. Moreover, asymmetric retardation alone can generate non-Hermitian spectral topology and skin accumulation even in the absence of spatial coupling asymmetry. Channel dissipation further drives topological transitions that reverse the skin effect, with a critical point at matched channel and lattice decay rates. We validate the anomalous skin effect and its dissipation-controlled reversal through full-wave simulations and microwave experiments. Our results establish time nonlocality as a fundamental degree of freedom in non-Hermitian topology, revealing phenomena inaccessible within the Markovian paradigm.

articles.title: Reconfigurable Generation of Terahertz Spiral Vector Beams Based on All-Dielectric Cascaded Metasurfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The reconfigurable generation of complex structured terahertz (THz) fields, and vector beams in particular, remains a significant challenge. Here, we propose a novel all-dielectric cascaded-metasurface scheme for the reconfigurable generation of THz spiral vector beams. By combining an isotropic phase-compensation layer with an anisotropic circular-polarization-sensitive layer, together with a new phase design tailored to spiral beams, we achieve independent control of the left- and right-handed circularly polarized (LCP and RCP) components through the relative rotation angle between the two layers. Under linearly polarized THz wave illumination, THz vector beams with switchable spiral numbers of 1-3 and reversible circular-polarization handedness are demonstrated at frequencies around 0.9 THz. Moreover, owing to the longitudinal evolution characteristic of spiral beams, the three generated THz vector beams exhibit azimuthal rotations of 279.9deg, 125.7deg and 75.5deg, respectively, along the propagation direction. Such complex THz vector beams, which combine reconfigurability with longitudinal evolution, are expected to find applications in emerging fields such as next-generation wireless communications and THz imaging. The proposed generation scheme also offers a useful reference for the reconfigurable generation of high-dimensional vector beams.

articles.title: Ultraviolet Raman spectroscopy using multimode aluminum oxide waveguides
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Waveguide-based Raman spectroscopy offers a route toward compact and integrated photonic sensors. While most waveguide Raman platforms operate in the near-infrared, extending excitation toward the visible and ultraviolet is attractive because shorter excitation wavelengths can provide substantially stronger Raman scattering and access to resonance-enhanced molecular responses. This transition, however, places greater demands on the photonic material because of optical loss, absorption and waveguide-generated spectral background. Here, we investigate aluminum oxide (Al₂O₃) waveguides as a low-background platform for Raman spectroscopy at 532 nm and 325 nm using a back-collected excitation and detection geometry. At 532 nm, after normalization to the incident excitation power-time product, the measured Al₂O₃ background was more than two orders of magnitude lower than that of Si₃N₄. Under 325 nm excitation, the waveguides maintained a weak and reproducible spectral background across the investigated widths. Using immersion oil as a model analyte deposited over the waveguide surface, we demonstrate that analyte-specific Raman fingerprints can be recovered above the waveguide background at both wavelengths. Signal-to-background ratio and spectral contrast were used to quantify analyte visibility relative to the waveguide background, and both metrics consistently confirmed clear detection of the analyte bands. These results demonstrate that Al₂O₃ combines low measured spectral background with operation from the visible into the ultraviolet, providing a promising route toward integrated Raman spectroscopy at shorter excitation wavelengths.

articles.title: Surface Hopping Dynamics on Adiabatic States Propagated with Real-Time TDDFT
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-time time-dependent density functional theory (RT-TDDFT) is widely used to simulate ultrafast electron dynamics, but it is usually coupled to the nuclei through the mean-field Ehrenfest approximation, which cannot describe wavepacket branching and violates detailed balance. Surface hopping avoids these problems, but has not previously been combined with RT-TDDFT because real-time propagation does not directly provide the necessary adiabatic states. In this work we introduce an energy-scaled time-dependent Kohn--Sham (TDKS) propagation scheme, motivated by the quantum adiabatic theorem. Scaling widens the separation between electronic and nuclear timescales, so that each propagated state follows the adiabatic surface selected by its initial condition: either the ground state or a non-Aufbau self-consistent-field (ΔSCF) solution. The propagation thereby avoids the convergence failures of static SCF solvers in regions of strong nonadiabatic coupling. Because the independently propagated states are complex-valued and not mutually orthogonal, we reformulate the mapping approach to surface hopping (MASH) in a complex adiabatic basis and introduce a dynamical transition orbital (DTO) gauge that restores a well-defined particle--hole representation for evaluating time-derivative couplings and nonadiabatic coupling vectors. Applied to the photoisomerization of trans-diimide, the scheme converges systematically as the scaling factor is increased and yields an excited-state lifetime in good agreement with previous nonadiabatic simulations based on static SCF.@ These results establish real-time propagation as an efficient and numerically stable route to the adiabatic states and couplings required for first-principles surface hopping.

articles.title: High-fidelity simulation and reduced-order modeling of optical pumping in quantum devices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41778v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatially resolved modeling of optically pumped alkali-metal vapors requires the solution of a high-dimensional nonlinear diffusive quantum master equation (DQME) coupled to state-dependent light propagation. We develop a structure-preserving computational framework for this coupled three-dimensional system in the high-pressure limit. The high-fidelity solver combines second-order finite differences, explicit pseudo-time marching, and an exponential-integrator discretization of the light-propagation equation. The scheme preserves the density-matrix trace, while a derived global pseudo-time-step restriction guarantees nonnegative, bound-preserving population updates and frozen-coefficient 1-norm stability. In the absence of a closed-form solution for the general coupled problem, the solver is verified against complementary analytical reductions, pumping-rate asymptotics, and a light-propagation invariant, all of which are accurately recovered. Tensorized GPU implementation reduces the per-iteration cost by more than two orders of magnitude relative to a single-core CPU. For repeated parameter queries, we further construct an intrusive POD--Galerkin reduced-order model. The quadratic spin-exchange term is treated by an exact nonlinear quadratic expansion, whereas the nonpolynomial and nonlocal optical-pumping term is hyper-reduced using the discrete empirical interpolation method. At out-of-sample parameter points, the reduced model closely reproduces the full-order population and polarization fields while achieving speedup of more than (7×10³) relative to the single-core CPU full-order solver. The resulting hierarchy connects verified high-fidelity simulation with efficient reduced-order prediction for spatially resolved alkali-metal spin dynamics.

articles.title: Query-Efficient Quantum Multi-Objective Optimization for Materials Configuration Search via Bayesian Weight Selection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Materials design is a multi-objective problem, and recent advances in quantum optimization make it possible to bring quantum solvers to bear on such problems. The realistic near-term win, though, is not raw quantum advantage but making an expensive, noisy quantum solver usable by spending its calls wisely. Quantum Approximate Multi-Objective Optimization (QAMOO) traces a Pareto front by solving a family of scalarized Ising problems, one per objective-weight vector, with QAOA --- but chooses those weights emphnon-adaptively, sampling them at random, blind to what it has already found. We recast weight selection as emphmulti-objective Bayesian optimization: our method, BW-QAMOO (Bayes-Weighted QAMOO), picks each next weight by expected hypervolume improvement (EHVI) under a Gaussian-process (GP) surrogate over the weight-to-objective map. On a frustrated alloy-configuration benchmark across min3,4 objectives and nin10,11,12 sites, BW-QAMOO reaches the same Pareto hypervolume as QAMOO's random sampling with a median 33% fewer scalarized solves across the 90/95% targets and 60--74% fewer than a uniform-grid baseline), on a genuine (simulated) QAOA solver; a paired Wilcoxon test confirms the saving is significant, and the advantage grows with the objective count m as the weight simplex expands and blind sampling wastes more of the budget. This is a emphquery-efficiency result, and we close with the open challenges on the path to real alloy data and hardware.

articles.title: Transverse Confinement in Cascaded Inverse-Cherenkov Acceleration via Phase-Trajectory Control and Injection Matching
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41806v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sub-relativistic electrons in micron-scale dielectric laser accelerators face coupled challenges of longitudinal dephasing and transverse defocusing, often imposing stringent requirements on injector emittance. Here, we demonstrate a combined strategy of phase-trajectory control and injection matching for sustained, confined acceleration. By coordinating the refractive-index and section-length sequences with the injected beam's Twiss parameters, we control accumulated phase slippage while maintaining transverse confinement. In a seven-section inverse-Cherenkov accelerator simulation, a 100-keV electron bunch with an initial normalized transverse emittance of 1 nm-rad and a relative kinetic-energy spread of 0.1% reaches 1154.7 keV over 1.545 mm, with a transverse rms beam size below 1 μm throughout the accelerating channels. The exit normalized emittance is 1.92 nm-rad, and the relative RMS kinetic-energy spread is 0.6%, with no particle loss under the specified tracking-acceptance criterion. The results demonstrate that coordinated structural sequencing and injection matching can relax injector-emittance requirements by up to approximately two orders of magnitude, offering a route toward compact dielectric accelerators for ultrafast electron diffraction, microscopy, and chip-scale coherent radiation.

articles.title: Estimating Irving-Kirkwood pressure profiles from per-atom virial and density profiles: a closure for the contour-dependent term in planar liquid films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The local pressure tensor of an inhomogeneous fluid is not unique. Two tangential profiles are in common use in planar simulations: the Irving-Kirkwood (IK) profile, which requires a dedicated pass over every pair of atoms for every slab, and the per-atom virial (PAV) profile, which molecular-dynamics codes produce at negligible cost and coincides with the Harasima contour. The two differ by the derivative of a pair quantity, P_T^IK - P_T^PAV = dQ/dz. We show that, for Lennard-Jones free-standing films, Q(z) can be predicted from the density profile and the bulk radial distribution function of the coexisting liquid: under the closure rho2(r1,r2) ~ rho(z1) rho(z2) g(r12), with a pair-local interpolation of g between its liquid and dilute limits, Q is a double integral of rho(z) against a kernel built from u'(r) g(r). The estimator P_T^IK,est = P_T^PAV + dQ/dz is tested against IK profiles measured on the same trajectories for 20 films (thicknesses 7-25 sigma, three cutoff radii, two temperatures): the root-mean-square residual is 0.001-0.002 epsilon/sigma³, against 0.010-0.021 for the uncorrected profile, and Q, the amount that the contour choice transfers between the two interfaces of a film with non-equivalent surfaces, is recovered to within 0.6% of the surface tension. Applied to the normal component, the same closure removes 83-92% of the spurious structure of the per-atom zz profile, a test that needs no IK run. Its mixture form is validated on three two-component films with an adsorbate unequally distributed between their faces, where it resolves the tension of each face; a clean face recovers the tension of the pure film.

articles.title: Laboratory study of mineral dust optical properties extending in the far-infrared spectral range
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mineral dust is one of the most abundant atmospheric aerosol types and remains a major source of uncertainty in estimates of aerosol radiative forcing. This uncertainty is particularly important in the far-infrared (FIR) spectral region, where the optical properties of natural mineral dust, especially its complex refractive index (CRI), remain poorly known. Previous measurements have commonly relied on pellet- or film-based methods, which can alter particle size, shape, and vibrational modes, inducing errors in the CRI determination. In this study, we present a laboratory investigation on six natural mineral dust samples with contrasting compositions and originated from major dust source regions worldwide, including Arizona, Atacama, China, Niger, Saudi Arabia, and Tunisia. Suspended dust aerosols were generated under controlled dry conditions and characterized using extinction spectroscopy from the infrared 250 to 4000 cm⁻¹ (2.5 to 40 micrometers) to the Ultraviolet-Visible (UV-Vis) from 10000 to 40000 cm⁻¹ (0.25 to 1 micrometer) spectral range, combined with particle size distribution measurements. The real and imaginary parts of the CRI were retrieved for all six samples, revealing a significant absorption and pronounced spectral variability in the FIR. These variations should be accounted for in remote sensing and dust radiative effect studies.

articles.title: Focusing through coupled multimode fibers for miniaturized single-atom tweezer arrays
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-world deployment of quantum technologies requires systems in low SWaP-C packages. Quantum platforms based on ultracold atoms typically trap and control atoms with optical tweezers using light focused through bulky objective lenses, which are costly and sensitive to misalignment. Multimode fibers (MMFs) offer a compact route to focusing light, but their use in forming optical tweezers for cold atoms has been limited to a single fiber. Here we use a 2x1 MMF fused coupler to obtain two independent control paths sharing a common distal facet. We form near-diffraction-limited tweezers through each channel, suppress interference by applying a small frequency offset between the channels, and demonstrate that the tweezer separation is insensitive to misalignment of the input coupling. This work provides a route to reconfigurable single-atom arrays in low SWaP-C environments.

articles.title: Penetration of a sphere in a pool: Secondary pinch-off
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The water entry of solid bodies, in particular spheres, has been the subject of numerous studies due to its relevance in multiple applications, especially focusing on cavity dynamics and the resulting forces and subsequent trajectories. The role of wettability in cavity formation and sustainability has been experimentally and theoretically addressed in the past; however, typically only up to the occurrence of a primary air cavity pinch-off. What is less explored is how wettability can influence higher-order pinch-offs. In the following study, especially secondary pinch-offs are shown to determine whether a sphere trajectory is terminally ascending, i.e., the sphere returns to the surface, or terminally descending: wettability is shown to be a strong influencing factor. This study begins with a series of systematic experiments, comparing the entry and trajectory of spheres over a range of impact Reynolds and Froude numbers, but also with varying surface wettability. From time resolved trajectories, a force balance is computed, illustrating the role of buoyancy, arising from the volume of any sustained air cavity in the wake of the sphere. Secondary pinch-offs alter this volume; hence, the terminal trajectory. A force-scale comparison and local radial balance at the cavity neck are then presented, suggesting how wettability influences the secondary pinch-off.

articles.title: Compound drop impacts on substrates of different temperatures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we report the impacts of isothermal compound drops for various combinations of viscous fluids. We extend an existing parameter-free model based on kinematic closure of drop impact to predict the maximum spreading diameter of both the core and the shell of compound drops. Then, we report impacts of compound drops on a cold surface. By using two liquids with different melting/freezing temperatures, it is possible to freeze either one of the two liquids or both and doing so, different patterns of frozen drops are obtained.

articles.title: A Momentum-weighted Interface Stabilization Approach for Fluid-Structure Interaction with Strong Added-Mass Effects
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.42034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Partitioned fluid-structure interaction (FSI) schemes permit the reuse of optimized standalone solvers but can become unstable under strong fluid added-mass effects, particularly when structural inertia is small relative to fluid inertia. This work traces the instability to the discrepancy between the interface pressure Schur complements of the monolithic and Dirichlet- Neumann partitioned systems, as revealed by a fixed-point analysis of the linearized FSI problem. Motivated by this analysis, a momentum-weighted interface stabilization (MWIS) is proposed, in which the interface pressure block of the fluid subproblem is augmented by an operator constructed from the fluid and structural interface momentum operators. The augmentation is consistent by construction, vanishing at convergence so that the monolithic solution is recovered. A sparse diagonal approximation of the operator, derived from element metrics, limits intersolver data exchange to quantities comparable in size to standard interface coupling data while requiring minimal modifications to the standalone solvers. Numerical experiments, spanning a linear model and established nonlinear FSI benchmarks, demonstrate improved coupling robustness in regimes of strong added-mass where the standard Dirichlet-Neumann scheme diverges.

articles.title: Soft X-Ray Detection Down to the Nitrogen K-Edge Using a Pixelated iLGAD Sensor
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.42064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hybrid pixel detectors represent the state-of-the-art technology for hard X-ray experiments at synchrotron light sources and free-electron lasers, owing to their high frame rates, extended dynamic range, and scalable detection areas. However, their application in the soft X-ray regime remains bottlenecked by the challenge of developing a sensor that can achieve high quantum efficiency and an sufficient signal-to-noise ratio at low photon energies. Here, we present inverse low-gain avalanche diode (iLGAD) sensors integrated with a thin entrance window, demonstrating single-photon resolution down to 390 eV (below the Nitrogen K-edge) with a signal-to-noise ratio of 5. Two gain layer designs, standard gain layer and shallow gain layer, were systematically investigated to evaluate their spectral response as a function of photon energy and operating temperature. A double-peak feature is observed in the energy spectrum, arising from the dependence of charge multiplication on photon absorption depth. Furthermore, a phenomenological spectral fitting model was established, enabling the quantitative extraction of the effective n⁺ layer thickness and gain layer depth. Beyond providing a fundamental understanding of iLGAD charge multiplication mechanisms and characterization results in the soft X-ray regime, these findings lay the foundation for developing large-area, high-frame-rate hybrid pixel detectors for soft X-ray. This advancement directly benefits soft X-ray photon science applications, including high-resolution ptychography, spectroscopy, and resonant scattering at synchrotron and FEL beamlines.

articles.title: Vacuum amplification across a programmable bosonic Bogoliubov stability boundary in a trapped-ion chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A quantum oscillator always carries vacuum fluctuations, and modulating its parameters converts them into correlated pairs of real quanta. This vacuum amplification underlies squeezed light and Hawking radiation. In a closed quadratic system, pair creation competes with the energy splitting of the modes, and growth turns exponential only once pairing overcomes the splitting. Here we realize this competition in two motional modes of a trapped-ion chain. A two-mode-squeezing drive creates the pairs, and a beam-splitter coupling splits the motion into two coupled modes at different frequencies. The two rates are tuned and calibrated independently. Starting near the motional ground state, we cross the stability boundary in two ways. First, with the drive at the sum of the two bare-mode frequencies, the phonon number stays bounded until the pairing rate exceeds the splitting and grows exponentially beyond it. Second, tuning the drive into resonance with one coupled mode lowers the threshold to zero, and only that mode is amplified into a squeezed vacuum. Separate control of the two interactions makes the threshold for vacuum amplification programmable. This control can be used to simulate particle creation and quantum phase transitions, and to operate parametrically driven bosonic devices close to their stability limit.

articles.title: Quantum Advantage in Beam-Displacement Estimation for Inter-Satellite Quantum-Secure Time Transfer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we investigate the practical feasibility of achieving a quantum advantage, in the context of inter-satellite quantum communication, of satellite position estimation. The investigation focuses on a quantum-enhanced scheme in which squeezing is added to the derivative mode of a Gaussian probe beam as a means of estimating photon-beam displacement. The performance of the scheme is compared against the standard quantum limit achieved by an optimal classical beam-displacement estimation scheme under a fair same-total-energy constraint. We find that although the benefit provided by squeezing rapidly diminishes as the inter-satellite distance increases due to diffraction-induced beam spreading and subsequent truncation by the finite receiver aperture, a quantum advantage can still be expected over inter-satellite distances up to approximately 100 km under practical satellite configurations. This distance scale between satellites is anticipated for Starlink-type satellite constellations.

articles.title: Parametric Enhancement of an Optical Spring in a Dark Signal-Recycling Cavity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optical springs tailor the response of precision sensors. Parametric amplification of the signal field stiffens the spring, extending the precision to higher frequencies. A Michelson interferometer operated at a dark fringe is the most direct way to separate the signal from the carrier for amplification. We experimentally demonstrate such quantum manipulation of the optical spring by placing an optical parametric amplifier in a cavity at the dark port, showing a significant increase of the optical-spring constant with the parametric gain within a factor of four below the oscillation threshold.

articles.title: Cryogenic Optical Characteristics of S-FPL51 and S-LAH71: Refractive index, Transmission and Thermal expansion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41481v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Several near-infrared instruments on upcoming extremely large telescopes use a combination of OHARA S-FPL51 and S-LAH71 glass prisms to correct for the atmospheric differential refraction. Because large parts of these instruments are contained within a vessel cooled to liquid nitrogen temperatures, the changes in optical and mechanical properties should be considered during the design phase. In this report, we provide an update to our continuing efforts to characterize the S-FPL51 and S-LAH71 glass under cryogenic conditions. These efforts include a measurement of the refractive index (293 K, 100 K and 80 K), transmission measurements (293 K, 77 K and 43 K) and a determination of the coefficient of thermal expansion (between 293 K and 45 K). We will describe the cryogenic test setups that we have used to obtain our results, and provide summarizing equations of these material properties. This characterization will prove useful for conceptual design trade-offs, mechanical interface solutions and detailed optical design for future near-infrared instrumentation on large telescopes.

articles.title: High-efficiency photonic GHZ measurements with linear optics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41524v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Probabilistic and destructive Bell-measurements, also known as fusions, constitute a fundamental primitive for photonic quantum technologies. These operations rely only on pairwise photonic interference, whereas the computational power of photonic quantum systems originates from many-body interference. Here, we introduce a family of high-efficiency linear-optical GHZ measurements based on four-mode interferometers and show that incorporating many-body interference into this ubiquitous primitive leads to more efficient entangling operations. For the four-photon case, the success probability is 9/32, and adaptive variants ensure that unsuccessful events project onto useful stabilizer states. We further show that the approach naturally generalizes to larger GHZ measurements, yielding an exponentially higher success probability than previous linear-optical schemes. Finally, we demonstrate practical advantages for graph-state resource generation, entanglement distribution between remote spin-photon interfaces, and fusion-based quantum computing. Our results establish high-efficiency many-body measurements as a new primitive for scalable photonic quantum information processing.

articles.title: Locality, Probability and the Relevance of History
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41944v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Relativistic theory and experiments teach us that causal influences are constrained by the speed of light. Deterministic theories incorporate this lesson in functional terms: whether an event occurs or not is functionally determined by events that occur in its immediate causal past. In this paper we suggest a natural generalization of this constraint that applies to probabilistic theories: the probability that an event occurs is to be functionally determined by the probability of the event-occurrences in its immediate causal past. This constraint differs from Bell's criterion of local causality and turns out to imply it only under an additional assumption that requires history to be, in a sense, irrelevant. Bell-inequality-violating quantum phenomena are thus arguably not in tension with relativity, locality, "statistical independence", nor with a supposed "realism". What they instead show is that history is, in a sense, relevant.

articles.title: EnsAI: An Emulator for Atmospheric Ammonia Ensembles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2504.16024v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ensemble-based methods for data assimilation and emissions inversions are a popular way to encode flow-dependency within the model error covariance. While most ensemble methods do not require the use of an adjoint model, the need to repeatedly run a geophysical model to generate the ensemble can be a significant computational burden. In this paper, we introduce EnsAI, a new AI-based ensemble generation system for surface ammonia concentrations. When trained on an ensemble for ammonia generated by the GEM-MACH air quality model, it was shown that the ensembles produced by EnsAI can accurately reproduce the meteorology-dependent features of the original ensemble, while generating the ensemble 3,300 times faster than the original GEM-MACH ensemble. While EnsAI requires an upfront cost for generating the ensemble used for training, as well as the training itself, the long term computational savings can greatly exceed these initial computational costs. When used in an emissions inversion system, EnsAI produced similar inversion results to those in which the original GEM-MACH ensemble was used while using significantly less computational resources.

articles.title: Effect of initial Rayleigh mode on drop deformation under impulsive acceleration
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.20248v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: One of the fundamental ways of representing a droplet shape is through its Rayleigh-modes, where each mode corresponds to distinct surface-energy. Previous studies have focused on the effect of these modes on free oscillations of drops. In this paper, we systematically quantify how the different prescribed initial axisymmetric Rayleigh modes modulate aerodynamic energy uptake and the resulting deformation of an impulsively accelerated drop. Using experimentally validated VOF-based multiphase numerical simulations, we isolate the coupled effects of finite-amplitude surface oscillation modes and the associated initial surface-energy state by initialising the drops with well-defined (n,0) modes and phases 0,π, while conserving the equivalent drop volume. We find that the deformation outcome is governed by the drag due to the drop's initial geometry, and the dynamic coupling between the free modal oscillations and the forced aerodynamic deformation. We find that constructive superposition amplifies deformation, whereas destructive superposition can stabilise the drop even when the aerodynamic forcing is sufficient to deform an analogous spherical drop to breakup. Initial modes and phases that channel a larger fraction of the input power into deformation, in the form of oscillatory kinetic energy and additional surface energy, attain larger deformations and are closer to the fragmentation threshold. These couplings are especially pronounced in high-viscosity systems, where viscous dissipation is large and facilitates the transfer of a larger fraction of the total energy to translational kinetic energy instead of oscillatory kinetic energy. For low density-ratio systems, early-time coupling and energy transfer are the dominant mechanisms that govern drop deformation.

articles.title: A Diagrammatic Method for Non-Gaussian Photon Correlations in Weakly Coupled Atomic Ensembles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.03970v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a scattering-theory formalism and use it to predict that a resonantly driven atomic ensemble weakly coupled to an optical mode can generate light with non-Gaussian correlations. Our approach---based on a perturbative diagrammatic expansion of multi-photon interactions---shows that photon-photon interaction mediated by the emitters causes the transmitted light to have a connected third-order correlation function g_c⁽³⁾ containing non-Gaussian field correlations. The temporal pattern of g_c⁽³⁾ is explained using the microscopic transport processes in terms of our diagrams. We derive an optical-depth-dependent bound on the perturbative truncation error and benchmark our predictions against cascaded master-equation and quantum trajectory simulations for small ensembles with OD≤ 2, identifying a regime of controlled accuracy under weak driving. Our predictions can be experimentally demonstrated in state-of-the-art nanofibre-coupled atomic ensembles.

articles.title: Separation-Dependent Bell Correlations from Prepared Coherence in Dirac Wavepackets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.12258v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We calculate separation-dependent Bell correlations for a fixed pair of Dirac electron wavepackets in a free, weakly relativistic packet model, treating the prepared joint wave as a physical wave--entity. Each station separation is sampled at the corresponding central packet arrival time. For the illustrated phase (χ=π/4), the magnitude of the prescribed-setting Bell--CHSH response decreases and revives; optimizing the spin measurement directions retains the modulation. It occurs already at leading spin order, including for equal prepared branch weights. Interference between direct and exchanged assignments of the electron waves to the stations changes the relative weights and phases of the sampled spin amplitudes, thereby modulating the optimized response. Representative finite spatial and timing windows reduce visibility while retaining broader suppression and revival. This wave--entity account gives a quantitative, testable correlation pattern from prepared coherence, deterministic propagation, and local sampling, without postulating transmission between detectors.

articles.title: Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel (MCRWK), an estimator whose per-pair cost is independent of graph size and derived directly from the random walk kernel (RWK) expansion. By normalizing the kernel coefficients, MCRWK samples a shared walk length and estimates its contribution using random walks on the input graphs. This gives a simple way to approximate RWK without constructing the product graph. For a fixed expected walk length and efficient neighbor sampling, each pairwise estimate takes O(m) time for m Monte Carlo samples, allowing the sample budget to control the trade-off between runtime and accuracy. We evaluate MCRWK against Graph Voyagers and classical RWK methods on synthetic and real graph datasets. In the reported experiments on large synthetic graphs, MCRWK is faster than Graph Voyagers and, at matched runtime, more accurate. It also has the lowest Gram-matrix runtime on the five real datasets studied. Code and experiments are available at https://github.com/arslan-yam/random_walk_kernels_computations

articles.title: Quantile Propagation Planning for Budgeted Tail-Risk Evaluation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Risk-aware planning must identify rare, costly outcomes using only a limited number of model evaluations. Monte Carlo rollouts spend this budget on noisy tail estimates, while planning from the mean can miss the tail entirely. We introduce quantile propagation planning (QPP), which propagates a small, fixed set of disturbance quantiles through the dynamics and integrates the resulting cost curve to evaluate both mean and tail risk. The method is exact at the propagated levels, converges as the quantile grid is refined, and admits a one-sided conservatism guarantee under stated structural conditions. In controlled overload and inventory tasks, QPP reduces realized tail cost and constraint violations relative to mean-rollout planning. On overload, it remains competitive with sampled evaluators that use substantially more trajectories. These results position QPP as a transparent, budget-controlled approach to tail-risk evaluation.

articles.title: From fleet trajectories to single-cell promises: hierarchically weighted conformal prediction for battery SOH monitoring
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interval predictions from conformal prediction are usually read as "90% coverage", but on nested battery data that number promises the fleet average, not the individual cell. We measure the gap on 124 public LFP cells under a preregistered three-tier reporting protocol (fleet, batch, cell): pooled coverage looks healthy (0.875-0.906 across splits) while the worst cell is covered 0.1-2% of the time, with exact binomial tests against the nominal level. We then repair part of the gap with a hierarchically weighted conformal engine whose weights consume only side information frozen at prediction time - signature features, batch labels, cycle indices - and never touch residuals. The preregistered repair criterion passes: 10th-percentile cell coverage moves 0.750 to 0.830 (53% of the gap), the worst cell 0.642 to 0.694, with zero deferrals and a flat sensitivity spectrum. What the engine does not repair is localized rather than left open: under protocol drift the frozen weights harm monotonically on the SOH scale (the absolute scale is reported in full), a structural dead end we report instead of tuning away; and repair capacity is bounded by calibration-pool battery diversity, measured on both datasets. On a cross-chemistry external set the calibrated intervals collapse (0.286), while the within-domain skeleton replicates (pooled 0.933, worst cell 0.686). The deliverable is a reporting protocol - three tiers of promise anchored to measured regimes, worst-cell statistics, deferral share - that makes per-cell interval claims auditable before deployment.

articles.title: Estimation of Quantum Umlaut Information
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41282v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantifying correlations is important for understanding how quantum states and channels support information processing. Quantum umlaut information U connects such correlations to reliability in hypothesis testing and certain communication settings, but its known formulas require classical descriptions of the underlying states. To estimate correlations without these descriptions, we introduce measured quantum umlaut information U^M by replacing Umegaki relative entropy with measured relative entropy. Its variational formulation leads to a quantum generative adversarial framework for estimating U^M from measurement statistics of unknown bipartite states and classical-quantum channels. This framework optimizes reference states and measurements without reconstructing the target states or channel outputs. For classical-quantum channels, it also optimizes the input probabilities. We further analyze the relation between U^M and U, deriving a state-dependent gap bound and characterizing equality for full-rank bipartite states. Numerical simulations show trained estimates close on average to independently computed numerical references for U^M across the tested states and channels. These estimates could help assess how well quantum memories preserve correlations and how noise or drift affects input-output dependence in quantum transmitters and state-preparation devices.

articles.title: PDE-Residual-Informed Kriging
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41590v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics-informed Gaussian process (GP) methods provide a probabilistic framework for PDE solving. Existing approaches incorporate PDE information in different ways: pointwise conditioning uses the governing equation only at finitely many selected locations, globally constrained GPs restrict the admissible functions to satisfy the PDE exactly, and residual-penalized methods control the PDE mismatch over the whole domain through an additional penalty weight. What is still missing is a GP formulation that directly incorporates global PDE-residual information of the entire domain into its covariance structure, while retaining model flexibility and standard GP conditioning without a separate residual-weight parameter. To solve this issue, this study proposes PDE-residual-informed Kriging (PRIK) based on a PDE-residual kernel. The PDE-residual kernel is constructed by equipping a kernel-section space with an inner product defined by the L² inner product of PDE residuals. This construction makes PRIK yield the posterior mean with minimum integrated squared PDE residual. It also provides direct statistical interpretations: the variance-scale estimate equals the normalized PDE-residual energy (i.e., the integrated squared PDE residual of the posterior mean divided by the number of labeled observations), and the profile likelihood balances this residual energy against model complexity. Under the stated regularity and stability conditions, we establish H²-quasi-optimality and convergence rates for the posterior mean, together with a nonasymptotic bound for its PDE-residual norm. We further show that the normalized posterior kernel converges to a variational Green-type kernel and derive a uniform nonasymptotic contraction bound for the posterior variance. Numerical studies provide empirical evidence consistent with the theory and demonstrate the PDE-solving capability of PRIK.

articles.title: Beyond Plausible Prediction: Safety Sufficiency in Web World Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40798v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web world models increasingly predict the consequences of candidate actions before agents act, yet a plausible predicted future does not necessarily support the correct safety decision. In a matched human evaluation of 3,000 predictions from ten frozen open models, 86.1% are judged semantically plausible. However, several models exhibit highly asymmetric authorisation behaviour, combining low false-safe execution with poor recall of clarifiable ASK cases and a strong preference for BLOCK. This motivates safety sufficiency: whether a predictive interface preserves and exposes the policy-decisive information required to distinguish actions that may be EXECUTED, require clarification through ASK, or should be BLOCKED. We introduce SafeWebWorld, a benchmark for evaluating safety sufficiency across five web-safety domains through action-conditioned futures, policy-decisive evidence, and policy-conditioned decisions. Under a controlled Security-Aligned Supervised Fine-Tuning protocol, evidence preservation can improve substantially while authorisation-sensitive decisions deteriorate. To determine whether this deterioration reflects loss of authorisation-sensitive score structure or a failure of the decision readout, we introduce Latent Authorisation Recovery (LAR). Frozen-score recalibration reveals substantial but backbone-dependent recovery, while paired recovery provides only a modest additional gain. Yet within-family and matched-authorisation evaluations remain poor, showing that aggregate recoverability does not imply robust fine-grained authorisation behaviour. Overall, plausible prediction, evidence preservation, and aggregate recovery are each insufficient on their own to establish robust authorisation.

articles.title: Towards Portable Specification of the Agent Harness
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models act only through the infrastructure that surrounds them. That infrastructure, the harness, determines what a model can accomplish and how it fails, yet it has no settled definition. To address this gap, we decompose the harness into eight functional components that can be specified and compared across systems, and we propose a portable specification framework that records which model ran in which harness. The record is needed because different harness configurations can yield several-fold differences in reported scores for the same model, and because much of an agent's attack surface lies in its harness. Existing model cards and agent cards provide release and operational information, but do not establish the sequence of effective configurations within a run. Harnesses can change between releases and between runs, and, where agents edit their own tools and configuration, within a run. Enacted AI laws contain documentation duties relevant to covered systems, subject to their respective scopes and application dates, but do not prescribe the common harness record proposed here. Therefore, the harness has to be explicitly described and specified as a versioned part of the system.

articles.title: Agentic World Modeling for Agent Test-time Scaling without Environment Replica
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40927v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Test-time scaling (TTS) improves large language model agents by sampling and selecting among multiple candidate trajectories, but common realizations assume that these trajectories can be executed in parallel. This assumption breaks in realistic deployments, where enterprise workspaces and cloud services are shared and persistent, costly or infeasible to replicate, and actions may introduce irreversible side effects or cross-trajectory interference. Existing generative world models avoid direct execution, but typically compress environment state into a single prompt, limiting their ability to reliably simulate transitions under partial observability. Instead, we introduce Agentic World Modeling (AWM), which reformulates next-observation prediction as a multi-turn evidence-acquisition task. For each hypothetical action, an agentic simulator adaptively queries the real environment through safe read-only interfaces, reasons over the returned evidence, and uses executable computation to construct the resulting observation without mutating shared state. Integrated with trajectory-level TTS, AWM enables parallel exploration over a single shared environment. Across τ-bench, AppWorld, and OfficeBench, AWM outperforms a single-shot simulation baseline by 40.07% on average, and surpasses a trained world-model baseline by 12.36% on average. These results establish interactive, read-grounded simulation as a practical foundation for safe and scalable agentic test-time scaling in shared, non-resettable environments.

articles.title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials RD
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. The strongest general-purpose model scores only 53.7%, and on matched problems, cross-scale problems score 8.7 points below single-scale ones. Half of the problems are solved by at most one model, and models fail chiefly by endorsing what is plausible rather than what was observed. A domain-adaptation study with meta-weighted continued pretraining and scale-modular self-distillation raises an open-weight model from 36.7% to 55.4%, matching the strongest proprietary model, with improvements on public materials benchmarks and no decline in aggregate performance on general benchmarks. FrontierMat provides a testbed for measuring progress toward language models that support frontier materials R&D.

articles.title: Researcher-in-the-Loop Evolutionary Discovery of Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Code Families
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41183v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-guided program evolution can produce mathematical constructions, but validity, generality, and reproducibility require distinct evidence. We develop a researcher-in-the-loop discovery pipeline that combines program evolution, exact evaluation, mathematical generalization, certified nonexistence checks, and formal proof checking. We apply it to entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes (EAQECCs). Starting from tasks that did not specify a family formula, evolved programs produced finite qubit constructions whose structure researchers generalized to the family [[n,1,n-1;n-q-1]]_q for prime powers qge3 at nge2q+1 and for q=2 at odd nge5. Lean checks the algebraic certificate underlying this family. Together with entanglement lifting, the family closes 54 gaps in archived EAQECC tables. The released evidence includes 115 verified code records, ten nonexistence results with checked DRAT proofs, family implementations, and preserved search programs for exact checks and seeded replay. In a controlled cohort of eight paired generation blocks, validation-selected iterative programs achieve success in 46.1% and 31.6% of held-out executions at unseen lengths n=13,15, compared with 19.5% and 3.1% for independently generated programs. In this setting, program evolution and researcher analysis turn finite computational discoveries into a proved family with independently checkable evidence.

articles.title: Cross-Interface Authorization for AI Computer-Use Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computer-use agents act through graphical interfaces, command lines, APIs, scripts, and Model Context Protocol servers. A policy decision can be interface-invariant while its executable authorization is not: another route can bypass mediation, alter a security-relevant default, or commit after the authorized state has changed. We present a profile-bounded protocol for a fixed, versioned computer-use deployment. It enumerates effect-bearing routes and durable sinks, checks a route-to-sink enforcement cut, normalizes each concrete request to a canonical effect, issues a route-bound prepare ticket, and verifies the route, effect, grant, trace, profile, inventory, and authoritative state again at commit. A committed result requires an agreeing sink receipt. Under explicit assumptions, we prove profile-bounded refinement, matched-effect decision invariance, resistance to alternate-route laundering and declared cross-surface recomposition, commit-time state safety, and receipt-grounded outcomes. The reference profile registers 12 effect families, five interfaces, and 60 routes. Two structurally distinct runtime mappings produce 3,464 traces over 1,732 scenarios each: 960 commits, 2,312 denials, and 192 commits after re-preparation. An independent checker accepts every retained trace and pair and rejects 26/26 semantic regressions; coverage and normalizer suites reject 24/24 and 720/720 mutants; and 168/168 commit probes match their declared outcomes. A frozen-source audit passes 52 checks over 12 files from two independent hybrid runtimes and one public authorization substrate. Source-shaped adapter refinements commit 48/48 instrumented calls and reject 15/15 unbound cases. The resulting guarantees bind the declared profile and its effect semantics.

articles.title: Evidence-Guided Recovery for AI Agents with Ambiguous Tool Outcomes and Partial Execution
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool timeouts can leave AI agents facing ambiguous tool outcomes and partial execution: an action may have failed, committed or remained in flight while other workflow steps have already completed. We formulate evidence-guided task recovery over approved obligations, provider capabilities and states compatible with public evidence. A shared admissibility check handles key expiry, authorization timing, dependencies and residual effects; a terminal certificate separates actual goal satisfaction from publicly supported safe completion. The known-model implementation combines standard observation-contingent planning with a separately implemented effect-history adjudicator. In a finite study of 37 assignments, planning and three active controls each certify 28 completions; four saved synthetic fee units incur additional computation. A preregistered assignment-held-out comparison then evaluates planning advice against evidence prompting with two local model bundles. Across 58 paired units in 19 previously developed task families, advice certifies 30 completions versus 9, a 36.2-percentage-point difference (exact family sign-flip p=0.0078), using 272 proposals versus 399. All 116 trajectories pass independent replay. Both models exhibit a positive completion difference. The comparison measures the evaluated advice interface under a common shield; search-versus-rule advice requires a separate matched comparison. Unknown and handoff outcomes remain explicit, with guarantees tied to the declared provider capabilities rather than arbitrary third-party exactly-once execution.

articles.title: ARK: Avoiding Routing Collisions for KV Cache Transfer in Disaggregated LLM Inference
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Disaggregated LLM inference separates the prefill and decode phases across GPU pools, generating massive KV-cache transfers. Because these transfers last hundreds of milliseconds to seconds, they behave as mega elephant flows that dominate link bandwidth utilization. In this regime, stateless ECMP can perform poorly: hash collisions may overload one spine link while leaving others idle, stretching transfer times by seconds. Yet this same persistence makes coordination practical. Since these flows are long-lived, even lightweight one-to-all coordination can be amortized over their lifetime. We present ARK, a distributed elephant-flow path reservation mechanism. ARK coordinates senders to choose source ports whose hashes map concurrent flows onto distinct spines, without requiring switch changes or receiver-side packet reordering. Packet-level RDMA simulations show that ARK reduces mean and P95 FCT by up to 27.3% and 34.0% under moderate load, and further reduces mean TTFT by up to 12.9%.

articles.title: ROSTrans: Empirically Benchmarking LLMs for ROS1-to-ROS2 Migration
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.41168v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Although large language models have shown strong capabilities in domain-specific code generation, their performance in robotics software development, especially for the Robot Operating System (ROS), remains largely unexplored. ROS code generation presents distinctive challenges, including complex inter-node coordination, middleware configuration, and lifecycle semantics that go far beyond standard coding benchmarks, and many important correctness properties become observable only once migrated nodes are launched and communicate. We present ROSTrans, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on ROS1-to-ROS2 code migration, a representative and practically important setting for ROS code generation. ROSTrans comprises 108 scaffolded completion tasks drawn from a diverse set of 70+ open-source ROS1 repositories and organized into a hierarchical taxonomy assessing interface-level, behavioral-level and system-level correctness. For every task we establish an executable reference: a verified ROS2 implementation, a runtime test suite that launches the nodes and exercises their topics, services, actions and parameters, and a container ensuring reproducibility. Candidates are scored by injecting only their target files into an otherwise fixed copy of the reference package, so a candidate can neither supply nor weaken the tests it is judged by. Evaluating six frontier LLMs over five stochastic generations per task, we find pass@1 below 10.9%, and that 56.5% of all samples build successfully and then fail at runtime,and 32.0% fail runtime assertions on the migrated interfaces, a class of error no compile-only oracle can detect.
