We evaluate on numerous synthetic targets and real-world problems, demonstrating strong performance of the proposed method, as well as favorable scaling with the dimension of the problem and the number of points used for the Monte Carlo estimate.

articles.title: From Many Models, One: Macroeconomic Forecasting with Reservoir Ensembles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.13642v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Model combination offers an alternative to selecting a single forecasting model, particularly when individual models are sensitive to random initialization and hyperparameter choices. We study online aggregation through Follow-the-Leader (FTL) and Hedge-type algorithms, with an application to ensembles of Multi-Frequency Echo State Networks (MFESNs) for macroeconomic forecasting. On the theoretical side, we derive Hoeffding- and Bernstein-type expected-regret bounds for FTL and decreasing Hedge under independent and ϕ-mixing expert losses. Under a positive gap between the best expert's expected loss and those of its competitors, the bounds are uniform in the number of forecasting rounds and exhibit logarithmic dependence on the number of experts. Monte Carlo experiments investigate the effects of temporal dependence and the separation between experts' expected losses. Empirically, we construct MFESN ensembles for forecasting U.S. quarterly GDP growth using mixed-frequency macroeconomic and financial indicators. The results show that adaptive aggregation, particularly FTL and AdaHedge, achieves substantial reductions in out-of-sample mean squared forecasting error relative to individual MFESN models and conventional forecast combinations.

articles.title: VerifiedLab: Harnessing Knowns for Unknowns
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Across human history, knowledge has undergone several transitions, from orality to writing and then to digital archives. At each transition, humans established new conventions to preserve knowledge for the new era. Nowadays, as research agents are increasingly deployed for laboratory experiments, knowledge is crossing another boundary: from records written for humans to those for machines. In this work, we introduce VerifiedLab, a multi-agent harness framework for this human-to-machine transition of knowledge. VerifiedLab transforms research output from passive artifacts into active systems that accelerate downstream use, adoption and prediction of future trends. In VerifiedLab, a team of AI scientists with distinct roles reasons over records verified field by field: a principal investigator plans, a librarian computes the evidence directly from the records, specialists draft, and a gate and a critic check each claim against the measured reliability of its data before the harness decides whether to release or withhold it. We demonstrate the efficacy of VerifiedLab through extensive experiments on perovskite solar cells: VerifiedLab recovers known physical trends, anticipates devices reported a year later, and lets AI scientists inherit the literature together with a measure of how far it can be trusted. By scaling the inference-time verification compute, VerifiedLab introduces a new pathway for knowledge dissemination and machine harness for AI co-scientists.

articles.title: Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly adopted in long-horizon tasks and interact with diverse external environments. Despite their growing capabilities, these agents remain vulnerable to real-world attacks such as indirect prompt injections, which manipulate agents through malicious instructions embedded in external environments. While existing risk assessment work has primarily focused on the injection content, the effect of where an injection appears has not been systematically characterized. Studying injection placement requires agents to operate over longer-horizon tasks and interact with diverse environmental surfaces. Thus, we build three agentic testbeds spanning tool use, coding, and daily workflow domains with diverse injection surfaces. Holding the injection content fixed, we find that agent susceptibility varies across injection placements. We refer to this phenomenon as the trust region effect: agents implicitly assign different levels of trust to different regions of their environments. For example, an agent powered by GPT-5.4 follows an unsafe injection instruction placed in a repository documentation file (i.e., a README or TODO file) 2.6 times more often on average than the same instruction placed in a code or data file. Building upon this observation, we develop learning-based attackers that generate injection content and select better injection placements. Our approach demonstrates that both where an injection is placed and what content it contains can affect the strength of indirect prompt injection attacks. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first systematic characterization for the effectiveness of different injection placements, spanning both coarse-grained environmental surfaces and fine-grained positions. The uneven trust that agents implicitly place across their environments provides important insights for future attack and defense design.

articles.title: Online Dense Reinforcement Learning with Planning-Grounding Agent for UI Navigation on Live IOS Apps
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39264v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While frontier vision-language models demonstrate strong capabilities in user interface (UI) navigation, their high inference costs prohibit everyday use. Conversely, smaller models trained via supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or offline reinforcement learning often memorize static trajectories, leading to brittle execution and an inability to recover from errors. To address these limitations, we propose a novel online reinforcement learning framework that trains UI navigation agents directly on live iOS applications. Our framework decouples the agent into two specialized components: a Planning agent and a UI Grounding model. We rely on an LLM-as-a-Judge to provide comprehensive reward signals, combining dense, step-level feedback to evaluate intermediate progress with a terminal reward for overall task completion. To effectively leverage this dual reward structure, we optimize the agent using Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with step-level advantage estimation. Furthermore, we introduce GiGPPO, a novel neighbor-conditioned value estimation method that improves critic stability by leveraging reward signals from visually similar states across concurrent trajectories. To support this online training paradigm at scale, we introduce an efficient infrastructure that orchestrates hundreds of concurrent virtual iOS devices. Evaluations on rigorous benchmarks, including UINavBench, iOSWorld, and AndroidWorld, demonstrate that our online RL trained agents substantially outperform both SFT and terminal-only RL baselines while accelerating training convergence. Notably, our 8B RL agents achieve nearly a sevenfold improvement over the SFT baseline in out-of-distribution generalization to Android environments, while outperforming Gemini-3.5-Flash and tying with Gemini-3.1-Pro on real iOS applications.

articles.title: LLM-Assisted Optimization for Simulation-Based Redesign
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Engineering design frequently involves redesigning a prior solution to adapt to changes in context, such as material prices or system requirements. Redesign often leverages simulators too complex and/or computationally intensive for traditional numerical solvers, which lack engineering knowledge and context, to ensure global solution quality. Large language models (LLMs) can interpret semantic information, including engineering knowledge about the system and changes in context, to help guide search, and recent studies have shown that incorporating this knowledge into optimization can improve search performance. However, how best to combine LLMs with numerical solvers in redesign remains unclear. We develop and test an integrated LLM-optimization approach for redesign and compare three methods for leveraging LLMs (warm start, variable fixing and ReAct) and four black-box solvers (Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithms, mesh adaptive direct search and random search) on an electric vehicle battery pack cost minimization case study across four types of redesign scenarios. We find that the integrated approach can match feasible design discovery of the numerical-solver baselines with 80% fewer simulator evaluations while tripling the fraction of runs that find near-optimal solutions. We find that the best LLM-solver integration approach and the way the prior solution is leveraged depend on the structure of the design requirement change, and that the benefit of increasing LLM model size grows with the extent to which the LLM controls the search. These results show clear potential for LLMs in redesign tasks for guiding or replacing numerical solvers.

articles.title: Verifiable LLM-Guided Focal SMT Solving for Quantified Arrays
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models can often identify useful semantic structure in formal artifacts, but their outputs cannot be trusted as proofs or solver decisions. We study whether LLMs can instead guide formal reasoning systems through a narrow, solver-verifiable interface. We instantiate this idea in quantified array SMT solving, where modern instantiation-based techniques can fail when key ground terms and equalities are hidden by auxiliary variables, axiom guards, and nested array terms. We observe that many instances are largely driven by a small set of focal ground terms or constraints, similar to the backdoor sets in SAT solving. Building on this, we present LinguaArray, a framework where an LLM proposes a small Semantic Focus Set (ground terms/constraints), while a conventional SMT solver remains the sole proof engine and certifies all results. LinguaArray uses these LLM-suggested, solver-validated finite sets to significantly enhance solver capability, solving additional satisfiable and unsatisfiable instances that the backend alone fails to solve. It interacts within a finite time and then falls back to the backend solver to mitigate potential regressions. Evaluation on 1015 SMT-LIB instances across five logics under 1200s timeout (including LLM latency) shows that LinguaArray solves up to 69.1% of instances and increases solved-instance counts by 105%--397% over the corresponding backends.

articles.title: PAPERBENCHX: Can AI Reproduce Science Across Disciplines?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Before AI can be trusted to discover new science, it should be able to reproduce what science already knows. Reproduction provides a rigorous checkpoint for an AI scientist: the target claim is known, yet recovering it still requires translating an incomplete scientific description into an executable experiment and producing evidence that can be independently verified. Existing research-reproduction benchmarks largely focus on AI and machine learning, where experiments share relatively homogeneous software stacks. Extending this capability across scientific disciplines introduces a different challenge: agents must operate domain-specific scientific software, make physical and numerical choices, diagnose long-running computations, and distinguish valid evidence from merely plausible outputs. We introduce PAPERBENCHX, a benchmark of 93 expert-constructed paper-reproduction tasks spanning 12 research areas across electromagnetics, photonics, chemistry, materials science, biology, and robotics. Each task provides the source paper, a public task specification, and a domain-native scientific environment involving specialized scientific software. Agents must reconstruct a key experiment, execute and diagnose it, and deliver a runnable workflow that supports the target scientific claim. To evaluate scientific validity rather than surface-level agreement, we replay every submission from scratch and score only regenerated evidence against expert-validated criteria. Across 10 frontier agent configurations, the best configuration fully reproduces only 14% tasks under the 90% threshold. Meanwhile, mean rubric scores range from 27.53% to 59.08%, indicating that substantial partial progress rarely translates into complete scientific reproduction. These results reveal a large gap between paper understanding and reliably producing reproducible scientific evidence.

articles.title: Efficient Learning of Mechanism Designs and Compositionality
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning mechanism behaviour requires a representation of how connected parts jointly constrain motion. We study whether exposing reusable constraint subassemblies improves prediction from limited data. Assur-KB represents planar mechanisms through irreducible modules, boundary interfaces, and solve dependencies while retaining source geometry. Our theoretical results characterize transfer through module interfaces and establish physical limits arising from missing interface information and accumulated sensitivity. To test the representation claim directly, the experimental design compares matched mechanism-curve pairs across training budgets within the same multilayer-perceptron family. This controlled comparison establishes the utility of the complete representation in the evaluated learning setting. Assur-derived features provide a geometric-mean 1.8× advantage in sample efficiency over flattened adjacency and position inputs across budgets of 50-10,000 mechanisms. Separate experiments establish invariance under tested joint relabelings, higher valid-generation rates under dyadic composition, and a coarser structural index over 10.02 million mechanisms. In summary, the theory and experiments identify how physical constraint structure supports limited-data prediction and which interface conditions govern compositional reuse.

articles.title: Search-Guided Reasoning Trace Curation for Verilog Generation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37706v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have improved Verilog generation. However, most training pipelines distill natural-language reasoning traces whose intermediate design decisions are weakly structured and are primarily selected according to the correctness of the final generated RTL. We present MCTS-SFT, a verifier-guided framework for curating reasoning traces for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of Verilog generation models. MCTS-SFT formulates trace construction as search over intermediate reasoning states and uses Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to propagate functional feedback from complete Verilog rollouts to earlier design decisions. Within this framework, we introduce Plan-MCTS, which searches over compact hardware-design plans that explicitly represent interfaces, timing, state, behavior, and update rules. We further study plan-preserving supervision, in which the searched structured state is retained as part of the downstream SFT target. Our experiments find that Plan-MCTS achieves the highest functional trace yield, with 84.2% correct traces compared with 81.9% for one-shot structured planning and 82.0% for unguided tree exploration. For identical Plan-MCTS trajectories and Verilog outputs, retaining the explicit searched plan during SFT raises pass@10 from 52.56% to 57.7%, demonstrating that the representation of intermediate design decisions materially affects downstream learning. In a separate 6,000-trace study, MCTS-curated supervision improves pass@10 over full-response chain-of-thought distillation by up to 3.7 points while reducing downstream generation length by approximately 50% on VerilogEval-v2. These results demonstrate that structured hardware planning, verifier-guided search, and explicit intermediate-state supervision provide complementary mechanisms for constructing more effective and token-efficient training data for Verilog generation.

articles.title: Power Quality Enhancement in Industrial Networks Using a Transformerless Shunt Hybrid Active Power Filter with MVF-PLL: System Design and Experimental Validation
articles.abstract: This paper proposes a transformerless Shunt Hybrid Active Power Filter (SHAPF) designed to mitigate harmonic distortion and compensate for reactive power demand induced by non-linear industrial loads. The active filter control algorithm is implemented within the Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) framework, employing a Multi-Variable Filter (MVF) coupled with a robust Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) for precise reference current generation. The structural arrangement comprises a single 7th-harmonic tuned LC passive filter per phase directly interfaced in series with a low-power three-phase Voltage Source Inverter (VSI), eliminating the requirement for a heavy coupling transformer. Consequently, the power rating requirement of the active converter is significantly reduced compared to standard active topologies. The dynamic performance of the system and control algorithm is verified through MATLAB/Simulink modeling and validated on a 20 kVA experimental laboratory setup developed at the LIAS Laboratory, University of Poitiers. Steady-state and dynamic transient results confirm that the proposed SHAPF reduces grid current Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) from 27.38% down to 2.71% in simulation and 3.9% experimentally, fully meeting IEEE-519 standards.

articles.title: Crystallographic Control of the Initial Electrochemical Reduction of Hematite
articles.abstract: Electrochemical reduction of iron oxides enables low-temperature, sustainable iron production, yet how crystallographic orientation affects the initial reduction of hematite remains unclear. Here, we combine density functional theory + U calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics to study the initial electrochemical reduction of the (:left(0001right),left(10stackrel-10right)), and ((:1stackrel-210)) facets of α-Fe2O3 at different hydrogen coverages. The potential-dependent descriptor Gmax(U) reveals a pronounced crystallographic dependence: the (:left(0001right)) facet consistently exhibits the lowest limiting free-energy span and thus the highest thermodynamic reduction propensity. High hydrogen coverage, the thermodynamically preferred surface state under cathodic conditions, leaves (:left(0001right)) and (:left(10stackrel-10right)) essentially unaffected but strongly suppresses the reduction of ((:1stackrel-210)), revealing facet-dependent surface passivation. Upon reduction, a more metallic, Fe-rich surface forms, and the O p-band center shifts most strongly on (:left(0001right)). The predicted preference for (:left(0001right)) agrees with experiments on the hydrogen reduction of hematite single crystals, pointing to an intrinsic facet dependence of reducibility. Our results identify crystallographic orientation and interfacial hydrogenation as key factors in the initial electrochemical reduction of hematite and provide atomistic guidelines for controlling electrochemical iron extraction.

articles.title: Strategic Enhancement of Photocatalytic, Piezoelectric and Dielectric Properties of Solid-State Synthesized BaFe12O19 Nanoparticles Reinforced into PMMA Polymer Matrices Nanocomposites for Energy Storage Applications
articles.abstract: This research focuses on the synthesis and characterization of nanocomposites consisting of barium hexaferrite (BaFe12O19) nanoparticles reinforced into poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) polymer matrices. The nanocomposites were prepared using a solution-casting technique, while the barium hexaferrite nanoparticles were synthesized via a conventional solid-state reaction method, followed by calcination at 800°C for 1 hour. Structural, morphological, photocatalytic, piezoelectric, and dielectric properties were evaluated using several characterization techniques, including FTIR, XRD, SEM, UV-Vis spectroscopy, d33 meter, and LCR analyzer. FTIR analysis identified absorption bands corresponding to Ba-O and Fe-O, as well as organic functional groups associated with the PMMA polymer matrices. XRD analysis confirmed the hexagonal structure of BaFe12O19 nanoparticles, with an average crystallite size of 15.23 nm. SEM analysis determined the particle size to be approximately 28 nm. UV-Vis spectroscopy evaluated the nanoparticles band-gap 1.76 eV and assessed photocatalytic activity. Under UV irradiation, all nanocomposites progressively degraded methylene blue (MB), where the 40 wt% BFO/PMMA nanocomposite achieving comparatively higher degradation efficiency of 67.22% than 61.78% for 50 wt% BFO/PMMA nanocomposite after 60 min. The maximum piezoelectric coefficient was determined 40 pC/N for 50 wt% BFO/PMMA nanocomposite with d33 meter analysis. The dielectric, impedance and modulus characteristics were observed over the low-high frequency range 40–110 MHz. As barium hexaferrite nanoparticles reinforcement increased into PMMA polymer matrices, the 50 wt% composition exhibited relatively high dielectric constant 7.1 and ac conductivity 2.25(:×:10⁻³) S cm− 1, along with low dielectric loss 0.08 at high frequency range (1M-110M) Hz. Impedance and electrical-modulus analysis further revealed broad non-Debye relaxation behavior associated with heterogeneous BFO/PMMA interfaces and localized charge-transport processes. The dispersion observed in the plots of Z″ and M″ with increasing frequency indicates the occurrence of dielectric relaxation. Overall, relatively higher BaFe12O19 reinforcement enhanced multifunctional properties of the nanocomposite, demonstrating their potential for energy storage, sensing, actuations, dielectric and photocatalytic pollutant-remediation applications.

articles.title: Convolutional neural network versus persistence for forecasting syndrome rate threshold crossings
articles.abstract: Calibration drift makes the reliability of quantum processors change over time, motivating tools that forecast degradation from data already produced during error correction. We test whether a convolutional neural network (CNN) can predict, from eight cycles of syndrome statistics, whether the next cycle's nonzero-syndrome rate in a simulated three-qubit bit-flip code will exceed a fixed threshold. Fifteen independent drifting-noise trajectories (6,000 cycles) were split by trajectory into training, validation, and test sets, so no cycle was shared between sets. On three held-out trajectories the CNN reached 89.6% accuracy and 98.0% recall for threshold crossings, while a last-cycle persistence baseline reached 91.2% accuracy. Short-horizon crossings are therefore predictable under slow drift, but the CNN shows no accuracy advantage over persistence. The results show why trajectory-disjoint evaluation and simple temporal baselines are needed when assessing machine-learning monitors for quantum error correction.

articles.title: Catalytic and inhibitory architecture of comammox ammonia monooxygenase
articles.abstract: Complete ammonia oxidizers (comammox) are widespread nitrifiers that can dominate ammonia oxidation in diverse environments by efficiently converting ammonia to nitrate within a single cell, yet the molecular basis distinguishing their ammonia monooxygenase (AMO) from those of canonical bacterial AMO remains unresolved. Here we report cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of AMO from the comammox Nitrospira inopinata (NiAMO) in inhibitor-free and allylthiourea (ATU)-bound states at 2.47 Å and 2.68 Å resolution, respectively. NiAMO displays distinctive auxiliary-subunit organization, copper-site configuration and hydrophobic-channel architecture. Integrative molecular dynamics (MD) and quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations support a methyl-plastoquinol (methyl-PQH2)-coupled, CuD-centric catalytic model, with CuC potentially facilitating quinone redox cycling. N. inopinata exhibited broad susceptibility to several known nitrification inhibitors, and ATU-bound NiAMO structure localized the inhibitor to the CuC–CuD region, accompanied by constriction of the hydrophobic channel, which is consistent with the competitive role of ATU demonstrated in recovery assays. Multi-omics analyses further revealed an energy-limited stress response to ATU, including induction of urea transport and utilization systems. Collectively, these findings define a methyl-PQ-linked catalytic and inhibitor-responsive architecture of comammox AMO and establish a mechanistic framework for lineage-aware management of nitrification in natural and engineered ecosystems.

articles.title: Port-Range Rule Management and Matching-Path Measurement for eBPF-Based Network Functions
articles.abstract: eBPF is increasingly used to implement programmable network functions on Linux hosts, including boundary filtering, transparent proxying, and firewall-like access control. For network and systems management, such functions require not only correct policy installation but also predictable rule-processing behavior in the data path. This paper studies ZFW, an open-source eBPF-based network function, and identifies an insertion-order-sensitive port-range matching path. In the original implementation, port-range entries are kept in insertion order, so hot-port traffic may traverse many unrelated ranges before reaching the matching rule, while selected miss traffic cannot terminate early even when later ranges are impossible to match. We propose a lightweight management-plane optimization that combines ordered rule insertion and data-plane early termination. The user-space rule maintenance path keeps port-range indexes in ascending order of low_port, while the TC-BPF hot path stops scanning once the destination port is smaller than the current low_port. We further add scan-step instrumentation and reset/read interfaces to support measurement-driven operation and ablation analysis. Experiments covering hit position, rule scale, public-cloud access, local netns/veth environments, mixed workloads, and ablation variants show that the method reduces average scan steps from 100.00 to 1.00 in the core N = 100 scenario. Controlled local tests reduce average latency from 8.10 ms to 6.63 ms and from 3.98 ms to 2.63 ms under lower concurrency. The results show that lightweight rule organization can improve the predictability of eBPF network-function management, while end-to-end latency remains affected by external system and network noise.

articles.title: Integrating Density Functional Theory, Machine Learning, and Device Simulation for Perovskite Photovoltaics: A Review
articles.abstract: Metal halide and lead-free double perovskites are promising materials for next-generation photovoltaics. But it is a challenge to navigate their huge compositional space and to simultaneously control long-term stability and non-radiative recombination. This review provides a critical synthesis of the cross-scale computational paradigm that brings together Density Functional Theory (DFT), machine learning (ML) and macroscopic device simulations like SCAPS-1D. We discuss how to transform first-principles atomistic parameters such as band edge alignments, dielectric constants and effective masses into meaningful device parameters without physical oversimplification. This work does not see parameter transfer as a "plug-and-play" process, but rather explains the bridging mechanisms that must be developed between microscopic energetics and macroscopic transport equations. We critically assess functional dependencies, active learning efficiencies, device-level limitations, and uncertainties related to ion migration and transient dynamics. This review provides actionable roadmap towards high-throughput physics-informed computational discovery of robust perovskite solar cells.

articles.title: Hierarchically Porous ZnTiO₃/Zeolite Composites with Optimised
articles.abstract: Applications Abstract cycling stability at high current densities. Thus, there has been a considerable surge in the 58 development of cutting-edge electrode materials like aerogels, metal organic frameworks (MOF), 59 covalent organic frameworks (COFs), MXenes, and metal nitrides that aim to increase 60 capacitance, electrical conductivity, and cycle stability, ultimately focusing on enhancing the 61 energy and power densities of supercapacitors [13,22]. 62 Composite electrode materials achieve synergistic effects by combining components in a 63 balanced manner, overcoming the drawbacks of each. A pertinent example is the integration of 64 carbon nanotubes (CNT) or graphene within activated carbon composites, which results in a compatibility, multiple redox-active sites, and favorable ionic transport characteristics. electrode structure that improves both capacitance and durability. Thus, a ZnTiO₃-zeolite 131 composite represents a novel and potentially practical approach to addressing the common 132 limitations faced by traditional supercapacitor materials. The research investigates how the 133 synergistic combination of ZnTiO₃ and zeolite influences capacitance and cycle stability. Commercial synthetic zeolite (aluminosilicate, CAS No. 1318-02-1, Product No. 96096) was 137 purchased from Sigma-Aldrich and used as the porous support material. Zinc acetate dihydrate 138 (Zn(CH₃COO)₂·2H₂O, Loba Chemie, India) and titanium(IV) isopropoxide (TTIP, 97%, Sigma-139 Aldrich) were employed as zinc and titanium precursors, respectively. Methanol, acetic acid, N-140 methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP), poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF), and conductive carbon black 141 (Super P) were of analytical grade and used without further purification. Deionised water (18.2 142 MΩ cm) obtained from a Millipore purification system was used throughout the experiments.

articles.title: Hybrid enzyme action optimizer CatBoost ensemble for drawbar load prediction with graphical user interface and comparative evaluation against nature inspired metaheuristic algorithms
articles.abstract: Cognitive intelligence of standalone machine learning models is constrained by target leakage, weak data mining, inadequate hyperparameter tuning, and premature convergence to local optima. This study integrated Base-CatBoost Ensemble learner with 25 recent nature-inspired metaheuristic algorithms and evolved new hybrid-CatBoost models for predicting drawbar load (HDb). These included, Aurora Intelligent Metaheuristic-AIM algorithm, Artificial Lemming Algorithm-ALA, Bobcat Optimization Algorithm-BOA, Bacteria Phototaxis Optimizer-BPO, Chicken Swarm Optimization-CSO, Enzyme Action Optimizer-EAO, Grizzly Bear Fat Increase Optimizer-GBFIO, Gazelle Optimization Algorithm-GOA, Grey Wolf Optimizer-GWO, Harris hawks optimization-HHO, Hippopotamus Optimization Algorithm-HO, Jellyfish Search Optimizer-JSO, Mantis Shrimp Optimization Algorithm-MShOA, Osprey Optimization Algorithm-OOA, Parrot Optimizer-PO, Pufferfish Optimization Algorithm-POA, Reindeer Cyclone Optimization Algorithm-RCOA, Secretary bird optimization algorithm-SBOA, Swift Flight Optimizer-SFO, Snake Optimizer Algorithm-SO, Walrus Optimization-WAOA, Warthog Optimization Algorithm-WartOA, Wolf-Bird Optimizer-WBO, Whale Optimization Algorithm-WOA and White Shark Optimizer-WSO. A scikit-learn library for the Base-CatBoost learner was created, and critical hyperparameters of hybrid ensemble models were heuristically optimized, targeting the experimental HDb obtained from 3360 values in the 14 soil-machine database. Total multi-metric accuracy (R, R2, R2adjusted, EVS, RAE, RRMSE, RMSRE, NRMSE, SI, PI, WMAPE, VAF, PA, CV) and noise robustness (MSE, RMSE, MAE, MedAE, Huber loss-Lδ, Log-Cosh loss-LCL) score ranking (980), regression error characteristic curve-REC (AOC = 0.236), Taylor reference clustering (R-σ-cRMSE), and convergence stability (perturbation score, 0.005, generalization gap, 4.545e-06) confirmed hybrid EAO-CatBoot as the superior model. SHAP explainable hybrid AI-XHAI revealed that tractive thrust most significantly dominated HDb prediction dispersion and convergence decision path attribution in EAO-CatBoost. Python-based GUI for hybrid EAO-CatBoost is presented for user-friendly HDb prediction in engineering practice.

articles.title: GLA-YOLO: A Lightweight YOLO-Based Network for Industrial Surface Defect Detection
articles.abstract: Surface defect detection is essential to quality assurance in modern manufacturing, affecting product reliability, production efficiency, and operational safety across diverse industrial sectors. Despite significant advances in deep learning-based object detection, industrial defect inspection remains uniquely challenging because defects exhibit extremely low contrast against textured backgrounds, highly irregular morphologies, severe scale variations, and marked class imbalance in which critical defect types may appear in fewer than twenty training samples. Deployment on resource-constrained edge devices in factory environments additionally demands real-time inference that many high-accuracy architectures cannot deliver. This paper introduces Gated Local Attention YOLO (GLA-YOLO), a lightweight architecture built upon YOLO11, featuring three innovations: Lightweight Fusion Convolution (LFConv) for efficient shallow feature extraction with channel attention, a Dynamic Local Attention Fusion Block (DLABlock) integrating local depthwise convolution with Performer-inspired linear attention, and DLAC3k2/C2DLA composite modules that embed DLABlock into the YOLO CSP framework. On a self-collected industrial defect dataset (4 categories, 1,367 instances) and the GC10-DET benchmark (10 categories), GLA-YOLO achieves mAP@50 of 90.21% and 80.59%, improving upon YOLO11n by 3.15 and 4.40 percentage points respectively, with only 2.70M parameters and 6.2 GFLOPs, while delivering 168.57 FPS inference and establishing state-of-the-art performance among nano-scale detectors.

articles.title: Heterogenous Aging of Local Tissues Is a Major Contributor to the Age-Related Decline in Glycosaminoglycans and Fracture Toughness of Cortical Bone
articles.abstract: Bone fragility fractures increase with age as bone toughness declines, potentially in part due to the loss of glycosaminoglycans (GAGs). However, the mechanisms linking GAG depletion to bone quality remain unclear, partly due to the dynamic and heterogeneous nature of bone remodeling during aging. During bone remodeling, newly formed secondary osteons and older interstitial tissue are randomly distributed throughout the bone, each with distinct material properties. This microstructural heterogeneity adds complexity to studying age-related changes in bone quality that cannot be explained by donor age alone. This study hypothesized that the age-related decline in bulk bone fracture toughness originates from changes in local tissue GAGs with tissue aging and is amplified by an increasing proportion of old tissue relative to new tissue with advancing donor age. To test this, local tissues in human cortical bone samples across different ages and sexes were analyzed using Raman spectroscopy, DMMB, Alcian blue, histomorphometry, microcompression, and fracture toughness testing. The results showed that compositional and mechanical properties of local tissues changed significantly with tissue age, but not with donor age or sex. The volume fraction of old tissue as well as GAG heterogeneity (FWHM) increased significantly with donor age. Furthermore, age-related changes in bulk bone GAG content were strongly correlated with bone fracture toughness. These findings suggest that age-related loss of bone quality arises from the combined effects of tissue age-dependent deterioration in local properties and donor age–dependent accumulation of older tissue.

articles.title: Design and Simulation-Based Verification of an 1100‑kV AC Grid Substation Supplying a 10‑GW Load
articles.abstract: This paper presents the design of an ultra-high-voltage (UHV) ac substation with a highest voltage for equipment of 1100 kV that delivers 10 GW into a 400-kV network and verifies every rating-determining decision by simulation. Four 1100-kV feeders (2 × 280 km and 2 × 320 km, 8 × ACSR 630/45, surge-impedance loading 4203 MW) supply five banks of 3 × 1000-MVA single-phase autotransformers, and twelve 420-kV feeders on six double-circuit routes distribute it. One consistent set of models supports the design: Carson–Deri line parameters, a 24-bus Newton–Raphson load flow with N-1, N-2 and P–V analysis, IEC 60909 sequence-network short-circuit analysis, multimachine transient stability, a three-phase Bergeron electromagnetic-transient model with Monte Carlo switching, IEC 60287 and IEC 60076-7 thermal models, and a two-layer boundary-element grounding model. Simulation revealed six findings missed by a deterministic preliminary design: with solidly grounded neutrals the single-phase fault at a two-bank 420-kV section reaches the full 63-kA rating, which a 10-Ω neutral reactor reduces to 48.4 kA; 1600 Mvar of switched capacitors is needed to keep the STATCOMs in reserve; a stuck center breaker gives a critical clearing time of 108 ms, shorter than the 150-ms breaker-failure clearing, which 1.1-GW generation rejection raises to 166 ms; transformer-terminal and bay-located gas-insulated arresters are indispensable; the 420-kV transformer connections require gas-insulated lines in hot desert soil; and autotransformer neutral-current reversal makes the grid discharge 69.8 kA, more than the fault current. The verified design has 1800/2400-kV switching/lightning withstand levels with 3.7–8.5% and 15.5% margins, a 55% voltage-stability margin and 99.83% full-load efficiency.

articles.title: Eco-Friendly Synthesis of Silver Nanoparticles Using NARC-G1 Garlic and Their Antimicrobial Potential
articles.abstract: The increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has intensified the need for alternative antimicrobial agents. Green synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using plant-derived materials offers a sustainable approach to developing nanomaterials with antimicrobial activity. This study aimed to synthesize AgNPs using NARC-G1 garlic (Allium sativum) extract and evaluate their physicochemical characteristics, hemolytic and antioxidant properties, and antibacterial activity against standard and multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacterial strains. G1-AgNPs were synthesized using aqueous NARC-G1 garlic extract and 10 mM silver nitrate (AgNO₃) under varying pH, temperature, and incubation conditions. The synthesized nanoparticles were characterized using UV–visible spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and particle-size analysis. Hemolytic activity was evaluated using human erythrocytes, antioxidant activity was assessed using the DPPH radical-scavenging assay, and antibacterial activity was determined using agar well diffusion and broth dilution assays against American Type Culture Collection (ATCC) and MDR bacterial strains. Optimal synthesis was achieved at pH 10 and 40°C after 7–8 h, with a characteristic surface plasmon resonance peak at 420 nm. FTIR analysis indicated the involvement of hydroxyl, carbonyl, amine, and sulfur-containing functional groups in nanoparticle formation and stabilization. XRD confirmed a crystalline face-centered cubic structure, while particle-size analysis showed prominent populations of approximately 0.8 and 10–15 nm. Hemolytic activity increased with concentration, ranging from 4% at 7.5 µg/mL to 51% at 250 µg/mL. DPPH radical-scavenging activity reached 48% at 250 µg/mL. G1-AgNPs exhibited concentration-dependent antibacterial activity against both ATCC and MDR strains, with inhibition of up to 97% against Proteus spp. and 96% against Salmonella spp. at 125 µg/mL. NARC-G1 garlic-mediated AgNPs demonstrated successful green synthesis, defined physicochemical characteristics, antioxidant activity, and broad-spectrum antibacterial effects against MDR bacteria. The concentration-dependent hemolytic response indicates that biological activity should be evaluated alongside safety parameters when considering their potential antimicrobial applications.

articles.title: A First-Order Phase Transition in Spin-Imbalanced BCS Theory of Superconductivity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38961v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a translation-invariant BCS functional of superconductivity for a system of spin-1/2 fermions with spin-dependent chemical potentials, μ₊≠μ₋. Numerical work of Caldas and Mota and analytical work of Freiji, Hainzl, and Seiringer has suggested an unusual first-order phase transition in spin-imbalanced BCS models, in which the normal state becomes globally unstable while remaining locally stable. Here, we prove that a first-order phase transition occurs in such spin-imbalanced BCS functionals. For each sufficiently small fixed spin imbalance and sufficiently low temperature, there is a coexistence coupling λfₒ strictly below the linear-stability threshold λₗᵢₙ of the normal state at which the Cooper pair density exhibits a nonzero jump and the minimized energy has a kink. The methodological insight is a coercivity estimate obtained by decomposing the BCS energy minimization into two parts, where the ``inner'' problem minimizes over the one-particle density matrices at fixed pairing and can be exactly solved by a Legendre--Fenchel transform.

articles.title: Exact holographic superfluid at the Bogomolny point: transport, large charge, and Rényi entropies
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40371v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Abelian Higgs model in AdS₅, in the probe limit, is a standard holographic model of a strongly coupled superfluid, usually solved numerically. When the scalar mass saturates the Breitenlohner-Freedman bound and the quartic coupling takes the Bogomolny value, its condensed phase can be found in closed form on every static, uncharged AdS₅ background with maximally symmetric spatial sections. We prove that it is linearly stable, as is any nodeless probe-limit condensate in the standard quantization with a nonnegative quartic coupling and no superflow. On each slicing it answers a different question about the dual conformal field theory. On the planar black brane it is the superfluid at all temperatures below T_c: the superfluid fraction follows the Gorter-Casimir two-fluid law exactly, and the speed and the attenuation of sound are found in closed form. In global AdS₅ it describes a state of charge Q on R× S³, arguably the lowest-energy one, and gives its scaling dimension in closed form at all Q, classically in the bulk. Its excitations include towers that the superfluid effective theory does not describe; they come from an infrared fixed point of the probe sector. The hyperbolic slicing gives in closed form a homogeneous hairy phase of the black holes that compute the charged Rényi entropies of a ball. Its condensate does not vanish at the entangling surface. When sourced by operators inserted there, the phase sets in at Rényi index exactly one at zero chemical potential, as found for a neutral scalar.

articles.title: Framework-Conditional Open Materials Generation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Theoretical predictions of novel materials rely on a variety of techniques, from data-mining-based ion substitution methods to fully de novo generative models. Each approach imposes specific constraints and encounters unique challenges when extrapolating beyond the distribution of known materials to discover new ones. The foremost goal of materials generation is to produce stable, unique, and novel (S.U.N.) structures. Predicted structures that meet these criteria, however, typically result from novel chemical compositions mapped onto known structural prototypes or frameworks. We leverage this heuristic insight to present a new generative paradigm for the de novo prediction of inorganic crystalline materials constrained by their structural framework---i.e., the unit cell shapes and respective particle positions. Our method, termed OMatG-FC (Open Materials Framework-Conditional Generation), learns via a combination of discrete flow matching on the atomic species and stochastic interpolants for the volume scaling of the unit cell lattice, while fixing in-place the fractional coordinates and the unit-volume lattice vectors, dramatically reducing the dimensionality of the problem compared to unconstrained (framework-free) generation. Our method is more flexible than existing prototype-constrained methods, demonstrating capability for discovery of unseen, stable prototypes derived from known structural frameworks. We also investigate the number of unique frameworks in the MP-20 dataset, demonstrating the propensity of duplicate frameworks within the dataset and providing a framework-split version. We benchmark the performance of our model using the LeMat-GenBench suite using three ML interatomic potentials and achieve state-of-the-art S.U.N. rate below the convex hull, eschewing the need to learn atomic packings for materials discovery.

articles.title: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40528v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce NEOPIC, a framework for learning the field operator in particle-based methods applied to kinetic plasma simulations. Its key novelty is a neural operator that acts directly on the empirical measure of the particles, rather than on a grid, and is evaluated at the particle positions. No mesh or tree is needed and, unlike grid-based neural operators, no deposition onto a mesh takes place, so the particle noise that dominates the inputs of particle simulations is not aliased. Since it replaces only the field solve, it serves as a plug-and-play field solver for particle-based methods: it can be trained on data from particle-in-cell, particle-in-Fourier or tree codes, and combined with any time integrator, including implicit schemes. We prove that the discrete evaluation coincides with the continuous operator at any number of particles (representation equivalence) and derive an error analysis that separates sampling, learning and time-stepping errors: up to the learning error, NEOPIC has the error structure of standard Monte Carlo particle methods. We show that the particle noise in the training data acts as an implicit regularizer, which gives guidance on the number of training particles in relation to the particle numbers used at inference. A complexity analysis shows that NEOPIC is an O(Nₚ) method whose constants are set by the architecture alone, independently of any mesh or tree. Numerical experiments on electrostatic benchmarks in two and three dimensions, including Landau damping, two-stream and bump-on-tail instabilities, a cyclotron mini-app and a Penning trap, confirm the theoretical findings. A single model trained on several mini-apps generated by different reference methods captures all of them and remains stable up to twice the training time window, which points towards foundation models for fields in particle-based methods.

articles.title: Grow, Compress, and Perturb: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Pathway to Scalable Quantum Chemistry on Quantum Computers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40561v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) variants are among leading candidates for electronic structure calculations on quantum computers, gradient-based operator selection limits their scalability. To solve this, we introduce the Hamiltonian-gradient-free VULCAN (Variational Upbuilding, Layered Compression, Adaptive N-body perturbation) layered VQE framework. Our method dynamically generates ansatz operators using Variational Double Bracket Flow (VDBF) equations. Combined with a linearly scaling minimal complete pool, it creates a pool 4-12 times smaller than QEB (Qubit-Excitation-Based) pools. By appending entire layers simultaneously, Hamiltonian gradient measurements are completely eliminated. Circuit depth is managed via a grow-then-compress scheme using efficient state-overlap measurements, and qubit requirements are reduced by projecting the Hamiltonian onto a dominant-determinant subspace. Using high-performance emulation up to 32 logical qubits, we achieve chemical accuracy at just 5-20% of the measurement cost of batched ADAPT-VQE for hydrogen chains, BeH2 and H2O. For the 32-qubit C3H6, where batched ADAPT-VQE does not reach chemical accuracy, a single VULCAN layer combined with a GPU-accelerated stochastic Epstein-Nesbet (ENPT2) correction does. This stochastic ENPT2 post-processing step enables early termination at chemical accuracy.

articles.title: Algebraic strong-to-weak symmetry breaking and partial decodability in the surface code
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40567v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coherent noise can give rise to unconventional regimes of quantum information recovery and mixed-state order. We study these phenomena in two settings related by Wegner duality: the triangular-lattice surface code subject to single-qubit Pauli-Z rotations followed by syndrome measurements, and a Z₂ paramagnet subject to strongly symmetric decoherence. Increasing the rotation angle drives a transition from a decodable phase to a emphpartially decodable critical phase in the code, and from a strongly symmetric phase to a phase with emphalgebraic Z₂ strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SWSSB) in the dual paramagnet. We develop a common description of these phenomena in terms of a weakly coupled SO(n) nonlinear sigma model in the replica limit n→1. Taking this replica limit analytically, we derive universal signatures of the critical phase: an optimal Pauli decoding fidelity that approaches a universal function of the system's aspect ratio in the thermodynamic limit, and a dual fidelity correlator that decays as a universal power law. These observables relate to correlations of twist operators in the sigma model description. Large-scale numerical simulations confirm these analytical predictions. We also argue that the algebraic SWSSB phase cannot be realized by any Pauli dephasing channel acting on the Z₂ paramagnet. We probe this "non-classical" character through the output state's sensitivity to well-separated Z₂ fluxes inserted in the initial state, which reveals persistent coherence between distinct Z₂ charge trajectories at long distances.

articles.title: Disorder as a route to topological spin textures in amorphous magnets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2311.07725v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Topological phases in solids are typically associated with crystalline symmetry and periodic order. Recent work has shown, however, that reciprocal-space topology can persist even in amorphous materials. Whether real-space topology, encoded directly in magnetic textures, can emerge without crystalline symmetry remains unresolved. Here, we show that structural disorder itself can generate the interactions required to stabilize topological spin textures in amorphous FeGe. Using first-principles calculations to construct a statistical magnetic Hamiltonian, we find that local structural asymmetry and broad distributions of exchange couplings produce a frustrated magnetic network with net ferromagnetic character rather than spin-glass freezing, supporting vortex-, antivortex-, and skyrmion-like textures that self-organize into emergent spin superstructures. Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the experimental Curie temperature and show that these textures persist even when Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya and anisotropy terms are suppressed. In contrast, homogenizing the Hamiltonian strongly suppresses the topological response, identifying bond-to-bond heterogeneity as the essential ingredient. Our results show that real-space topology in a magnet need not be inherited from crystalline chirality, but can emerge from disorder itself.

articles.title: Quantum noise spectroscopy of superconducting dynamics in a cuprate thin film
articles.abstract: arXiv:2502.04439v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Characterizing the low-energy dynamics of quantum materials is crucial for understanding strongly correlated electronic states, yet remains experimentally challenging, particularly in two-dimensional systems. Here, we leverage nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond as a non-invasive quantum sensor to study thin-film Bi₂Sr₂CaCu₂O₈₊δ (BSCCO), revealing several distinct dynamical phenomena across the superconducting phase diagram. At zero magnetic field and low temperatures, NV depolarization (T₁) spectroscopy captures GHz-scale noise from nodal quasiparticle excitations, consistent with Bardeen--Cooper--Schrieffer (BCS) mean-field theory. Near the critical temperature T_c approx 90 K, supercurrent-fluctuation-induced noise sharply reduces T₁. By analyzing the temperature scaling of T₁, we observe clear deviations from mean-field prediction, reflecting the importance of order parameter fluctuations and enabling the determination of critical exponents. Under a small magnetic field, a broad and asymmetric reduction of T₁ unveils a liquid-like phase of mobile vortices. NV decoherence (T₂) spectroscopy further probes MHz-scale noise and reveals complex vortex-solid fluctuations well below T_c. Our results establish quantum noise spectroscopy as a non-invasive probe of superconducting dynamics over frequency and length scales complementary to existing techniques.

articles.title: Quantum-inspired space-time PDE solver and dynamic mode decomposition
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.21767v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The numerical solution of time-dependent PDEs posed over the combined space-time domain, instead of treating time sequentially, leads to space-time methods. Treating time as another spatial dimension allows parallelization across time and simultaneous adaptivity in spatial and temporal discretizations. However, space-time formulations suffer from the curse of dimensionality due to the (d+1)-dimensional domain. Time-series forecasting methods, such as dynamic mode decomposition (DMD), also suffer the same scaling for storing and processing measurement data. In this work, we investigate whether quantum-inspired tensor network methods can mitigate this curse for both solving PDEs and data-driven modeling. We formulate a space-time matrix product state (MPS) encoding to represent either the space-time solution or time-series data. Using this representation, we develop a unified framework that combines an MPS space-time PDE solver with an MPS-DMD algorithm. We benchmark our MPS space-time solver for linear and nonlinear PDEs in both (1+1) and (2+1) dimensions, including non-diffusive regimes such as shockwave formation and Allen-Cahn phase separation. We observe that the MPS ansatz efficiently captures the spatio-temporal correlations of the solutions, with a 99% reduction in parameters with respect to the grid size. We demonstrate the MPS-DMD algorithm in two cases. First, the MPS space-time solver generates the MPS encoding of the time-series data. We then apply MPS-DMD directly to predict the dynamics without solving PDEs. Second, for the general case where data is available as dense arrays, MPS-DMD needs an intermediate compression step. We implement a streaming-like compression algorithm and observe a 97% reduction in memory, with MPS-DMD predictions matching those of exact DMD.

articles.title: Crystal Orbital Guided Iteration to Atomic Orbitals: A Pathway to Chemically Adaptive Atomic Orbitals from DFT
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.19725v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Atomic orbitals underpin our understanding of electronic structure, providing intuitive descriptions of bonding, charge transfer, magnetism, and correlation effects. Despite their utility, an atomic basis that is adaptable, strictly localized on atomic centers, and enables accurate tight-binding interpolation has remained elusive. Here, we introduce Crystal Orbital Guided Iteration To atomic-Orbitals (COGITO), a framework that constructs an optimal atomic orbital basis by identifying and resolving key mathematical obstacles inherent to nonorthogonal bases -- particularly uncontrolled orbital mixing, and the fixed-overlap constraint between orbitals. We demonstrate that COGITO enables tight-binding models as accurate as MLWF-based approaches, while preserving the ability of tight-binding parameters to represent the projected atomic basis -- an essential feature lost in schemes that enforce orbital orthogonality or maximal localization. By creating accurate and chemically interpretable models of electronic structure, COGITO reveals the orbital-resolved covalent bonds and charge transfer that is encoded in the Kohn-Sham wavefunctions of DFT. Our method thus offers a powerful tool for any physics- or chemistry-based application that relies on a faithful description of local electronic structure.

articles.title: Point-Group Equivariant Neural Networks for Local Dynamics in Lattice Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.04104v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop point-group equivariant neural networks for learning local mappings used in dynamical simulations of lattice systems. The same network acts on a finite neighborhood around each site, respecting lattice translations through shared parameters. The local configuration is decomposed into features that transform according to irreducible representations of the point group, and hidden features retain this organization throughout the network. Equivariant linear maps and symmetry-allowed tensor products then learn nonlinear spatial correlations while preserving the required transformation laws. This approach avoids constructing a fixed set of hand-crafted invariant descriptors, whose selection requires choices about which local correlations to retain. It also allows the complexity of the learned mapping to grow without enlarging its spatial cutoff. We demonstrate the construction by learning the forces governing adiabatic dynamics in the square-lattice Holstein model. Comparisons with exact diagonalization test the accuracy of the predicted forces and the evolution of spatial correlations. Force evaluation scales linearly with system size, allowing the trained model to simulate charge-density-wave ordering on large lattices. These simulations reproduce anomalously slow coarsening of the charge-density-wave domains, illustrating the use of the learned local mapping for collective dynamics.

articles.title: Reducing the Computational Cost Scaling of Tensor Network Algorithms via Field-Programmable Gate Array Parallelism
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.05900v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Improving the computational efficiency of quantum many-body calculations from a hardware perspective remains a critical challenge. Although field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) have recently been exploited to improve the computational scaling of algorithms such as Monte Carlo methods, their application to tensor network algorithms is still at an early stage. In this work, we propose a fine-grained parallel tensor network design based on FPGAs to substantially enhance the computational efficiency of two representative tensor network algorithms: the infinite time-evolving block decimation (iTEBD) and the higher-order tensor renormalization group (HOTRG). By employing a quad-tile partitioning strategy to decompose tensor elements and map them onto hardware circuits, our approach effectively translates algorithmic computational complexity into scalable hardware resource utilization, enabling an extremely high degree of parallelism on FPGAs. Compared with conventional CPU-based implementations, our scheme exhibits superior scalability in computation time, reducing the bond-dimension scaling of the computational cost from O(D_b³) to O(D_b) for iTEBD and from O(D_b⁶) to O(D_b²) for HOTRG. This work provides a theoretical foundation for future hardware implementations of large-scale tensor network computations.

articles.title: Meta-generalized gradient approximation made in the Hartree gauge
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.11517v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In density functional theory (DFT), exact constraints, fundamental mathematical properties of the exchange-correlation (XC) energy and its underlying XC hole, along with paradigm systems such as the uniform electron gas and the hydrogen atom have been instrumental in developing exchange- correlation (XC) density functional approximations (DFAs). However, since the spatial XC energy density is not uniquely defined, its exact constraints can only be formulated within a chosen gauge and are therefore seldom utilized in DFA construction. Here, we propose a meta-generalized gradient approximation for the exchange energy, explicitly constructed within the Hartree gauge, using the hydrogen atom's exchange energy density for gauge alignment in core and asymptotic regions. By formulating DFAs at the XC energy density level, this approach expands reference datasets for machine learning and establishes a foundation for more accurate nonlocal density functionals requiring gauge alignment.

articles.title: Variational Framework for Quantum Molecular Reaction Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.13923v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work describes a geometric framework on molecular reaction dynamics based on the variational principle, where the Schrödinger equation must be solved to ``see'' how a reaction occurs. First, the mathematical preliminaries are given by discussing the principle of least action and the mountain pass theorem. Second, we discuss the physical preliminaries, including the principle of equivalence for deriving the kinetic energy operator (KEO) and artificial intelligence (AI) techniques to build the potential energy surface (PES) in general spacetime. Moreover, we simplified electromagnetic interactions in curved spacetime within the molecular system and consequently, we are able to construct the nuclear Hamiltonian in nonzero curvature spacetime. This indicates possibility to introduce gauge fields through the curvature, such as additional term in the nuclear KEO near a conical intersection. Third, the single-particle approximation provides a powful ansatz to solve the Schrödinger equation by variational principle. Thus, one can formulate the variational approaches for either electronic structure or quantum dynamics. In this work, based on previous discussions (it Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. bf 27 (2025), 20397) we unified them by a geometric description, where the geometric phase is naturally introduced. Finally, due to optimization characteristic of the present theory, further discussions on the present theory from optimization insight are also given, including two postulates, generative AI techniques, role of perturbation, and Markov process in optimization.

articles.title: First-order polarization process as an alternative to antiferroelectricity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.27590v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Antiferroelectrics generate significant interest since their polarization versus electric field (P-E) curves show typical double-hysteresis loops appealing for various applications. Unfortunately, antiferroelectrics are rare. In magnetic compounds, magnetization versus magnetic field (M-H) curves can show analogous double hysteresis loops not only in antiferromagnets but also in systems exhibiting field-induced first-order reorientation of the magnetization through a so-called first-order magnetization process. Here, we show that appealing double-hysteresis P-E loops can also appear from an unprecedented first-order polarization process. Focusing on non-polar CaTiO3, which can be turned ferroelectric under tensile strain, we study epitaxial thin films on differently-oriented NdGaO3 substrates using a combination of theoretical and experimental techniques. We uncover that a certain configuration exhibits double-hysteresis P-E loops that we rationalize from a field-induced abrupt rotation of the polarization. Such a first-order polarization process establishes a promising alternative pathway to achieve double hysteresis P-E loops appealing for practical applications.

articles.title: CATAPULT: A CUDA-Accelerated Timestepper for Alpha Particles Using Local Tricubics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.07617v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a CUDA-Accelerated Timestepper for Alpha Particles Using Local Tricubics (CATAPULT) for use in Monte Carlo calculations of alpha particle confinement in stellarators. Our GPU implementation is significantly faster than CPU-parallelized implementations of the same field representation such as SIMSOPT, and handles both equilibrium magnetic fields and Shear Alfven Waves. We test our implementation on several example stellarators to exhibit both the speed and correctness of our code. The source code is included in the firm3d Python package.

articles.title: Dynamic Behaviors of Materials Under Angle-Resolved Experiments: A Matrix Framework for Nonlinear Physics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.13752v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Matter and external stimuli interact dynamically almost everywhere in nature. Under an applied field, a material seldom stays in the state in which it was characterized, and its properties change with time. Angle-resolved experiments are the standard way to resolve direction-dependent properties, however, current theoretical tools for data analysis are built for static states, leaving dynamic behaviors largely neglected. Here, we develop a generalized ``input-coefficient-output'' (ICO) approach that constructs spatial operation matrices and symmetry-reduced coefficient matrices across diverse physical systems, as we verify for nonlinear optics, elasticity, electrostriction and magnetostriction, and a Python program is released for convenient application. Using angle-resolved polarized second-harmonic generation (SHG) as an example, we focus on the dynamic modeling of material properties under angle-dependent stimuli, construct dynamic matrix equations that capture the time-dependent evolution of material responses, and propose three dynamic models and a point-to-point data fitting method. For the SHG experiments performed on T_d-WTe₂, the discrete dynamic model captures the asymmetric characteristics of the measured polar pattern with a significantly improved coefficient of determination (R² increasing from 0.567 to 0.773), whereas conventional static models are constrained to a symmetric curve. The evolution operator extracted from the dynamic model connects the macroscopic measurement to microscopic intermediate states during their interaction with stimuli. This work provides a practical matrix framework for dynamic modeling of material properties, paving the way for exploring complex nonlinear physics under realistic experimental conditions.

articles.title: Enhancement of superconducting stiffness in hybrid superconducting-metallic bilayers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.28187v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Boosting superconductivity by metallic reservoirs is the essence of Kivelson's bilayer proposal. One layer provides pairing to the electrons, while the weakly coupled metal provides additional phase coherence to those pairs by mediating extended-range pair-pair coupling. Demonstrating significant and unambiguous performance gains with strong-coupling methods for such set-ups had been difficult. In the present work, we study these systems doped away from half-filling, corresponding to a partially spin-polarized 1D Anderson- or Kondo-lattice. We show that this breaks the coexistence of dominant superconducting and density-density correlations decisively in favour or the former. Consequently, we provide evidence that in this doped regime, superconducting near-long-range order is not precluded by a small charge-gap in the thermodynamic limit, as we have recently shown to be the case at half-filling [J. E. Ebot et al., Phys. Rev. B 113, 174530 (2026)]. We study the complex manner in which the enhancement of superconductivity in the pairing layer depends on the parameters of the metal, and especially that both pairing-limited and stiffness-limited regimes may appear in these systems. In addition to superconducting bilayers, our results are relevant, via a particle-hole transformation, for heavy-fermion Kondo-lattice materials in magnetic fields, as we provide previously lacking insight on the competition between antiferromagnetic and easy-plane magnetism, as well as a route for comprehensive indirect tests of Kivelson's bilayer proposal well beyond previous capabilities.

articles.title: Single-stripe magnetic order and bilayer spin dynamics in single-crystalline La3Ni2O7
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.03448v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-temperature superconductivity in pressurized and thin-film nickelates has generated intense interest, yet magnetism in their ambient-pressure parent phases remains poorly understood, despite its potentially crucial role in pairing. Progress has been limited by the lack of large single crystals suitable for neutron spectroscopy. Here we overcome this limitation and map the spin order and excitations of single-crystalline La3Ni2O7. We find single-stripe magnetic order with a finite spin gap, anisotropic in-plane excitations and pronounced bilayer modulation revealing antiferromagnetic interlayer coupling. The dispersion is captured by a bilayer Heisenberg-type model with strong interlayer exchange and competing in-plane couplings. Absolute normalization reveals that, although the spin-wave bandwidth is only about 25% of that in cuprates, the local dynamic susceptibility at comparable energies is enhanced, yielding a comparable total fluctuating moment. These results highlight intense mid-energy spin excitations rooted in substantial electronic correlations, establishing a magnetic framework distinct from cuprates and relevant to superconductivity in nickelates.

articles.title: Finite-temperature micromagnetic model bridging atomic- and macro-scale magnetism
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.29617v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A multi-scale finite-temperature micromagnetic model is presented, based on the Landau-Lifshitz equation and the Bernoulli differential equation. This model accurately reproduces classic Maxwell magnetostatics of paramagnets for high temperatures and accurately reproduces standard micromagnetics described by the conventional Landau-Lifshitz model in ferromagnets. The Landau-Lifshitz-Bernoulli (LLBe) model can, by design, directly couple atomic-scale simulations with micromagnetics and output consistent predictions of bulk magnetic properties at finite temperatures, from below to above the material's Curie temperature. The LLBe model is validated against established solvers: MUMAX3 for zero-temperature micromagnetics, and FEMCE for high-temperature classic magnetostatics. We present an application of the LLBe model by simulating Heat-Assisted magnetic recording on a thin magnetic track with local heating, demonstrating the multi-scale finite-temperature capabilities of the LLBe.

articles.title: Excitonic-Superconducting Coexistence and Emergent Nematic Superconductivity Driven by Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.01785v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Excitonic insulating (EI) and superconducting (SC) orders are generally regarded as mutually exclusive electronic instabilities. Within a self-consistent microscopic theory, we study electronic systems hosting an EI phase in the presence of SC pairing and show that an intrinsic mismatch between electron and hole Fermi surfaces fundamentally reshapes this competition. This mismatch stabilizes FFLO-like electron-hole pairing and drives spontaneous symmetry breaking of the EI state. The resulting symmetry breaking reconstructs the pairing phase space for SC and EI state, such that different regions of the Fermi surface complementarily support either EI or SC correlations, leading to a natural coexistence of the two orders. Notably, the emergent SC state consequently breaks rotational symmetry and develops intrinsic nematic superconductivity, even in the absence of explicit symmetry-breaking fields (such as magnetic fields, spin-orbit coupling, or bare band-structure anisotropy). Our results suggest that candidate materials such as monolayer 1T'-MoTe₂ and the square-net semimetal NaAlSi may provide promising platforms for observing this phenomenon. More broadly, these findings reveal a unique mechanism by which competing many-body orders generate electronic nematicity, suggesting a broader route toward spontaneous anisotropic electronic states in correlated quantum materials.

articles.title: Efficient Large-Scale STEM-EELS Simulations With Torched-TACAW
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.02236v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The time auto-correlation of auxiliary wave functions (TACAW) method enables efficient simulations of ultra-low-loss electron energy loss spectra (EELS) arising from vibrational and magnon excitations. In practical applications to realistic materials systems, however, TACAW calculations become challenging due to the large system sizes required for models containing defects, interfaces, impurities, or grain boundaries, as well as the substantial computational cost and data throughput associated with molecular dynamics and multislice calculations. Here we discuss a practical methodology for large-scale TACAW simulations and present torched-TACAW, a freely available implementation of the TACAW part of the described workflow for efficient STEM-EELS simulations. The overall approach combines molecular dynamics based on foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials, partitioning of elongated supercells, and on-the-fly processing of multislice outputs in order to enable near ab initio quality simulations with tractable memory use and data flow. Using rutile TiO2 as a model system, we analyze important numerical aspects of the method, including windowing and supercell partitioning, and demonstrate atomic-resolution STEM-EELS simulations for thick samples.

articles.title: 1+1d Lattice Dirac Fermions from Non-Onsite Vector and Axial Symmetries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.02722v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct an exactly solvable Hamiltonian lattice model realizing a 1+1d Dirac fermion, with exact microscopic vector and axial vector U(1) symmetries. The mixed anomaly between these is accommodated by the not-on-site action of the symmetries. Our Hilbert space is a Z₂-graded tensor product of local Z₂-graded Hilbert spaces which include infinite dimensional rotor degrees of freedom. The Hamiltonian becomes manifestly exactly solvable after a locality-preserving unitary mapping to an equivalent fermionic Villain Hilbert space. Our construction also allows an exactly solvable realization of interacting fermionic Luttinger liquids. At the free Dirac fixed point, our Hamiltonian contains irrelevant interactions, which we compute to leading order.

articles.title: Unravelling carbene moiety role in the N-heterocyclic carbene-phosphinidenes coordination chemistry: bonding and reactivity in gold chemistry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.16472v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The coordination properties of the emerging class of N-heterocyclic carbene-phosphinidene (NHCP) ligands have been reported to be strongly affected by the carbene (NHC) moiety, but a clear understanding remains strikingly limited. In this work the bonding features and reactivity of 13 NHCP gold hydride complexes, [NHCPAuH], bearing different classes of NHCs have been systematically explored and compared to carbene analogues, using a consistent computational protocol. The analyses reveal that, although the π-acceptor ability trend of NHCPs qualitatively parallels that of NHCs, the σ-donor ability trend reverses, with more σ-donating NHC moieties generating less σ-donating NHCP ligands. Concurrently, the nature of the NHC moiety impacts the coordination geometry at the P center, with the CNHC-P-Au bond angle appearing as a structural descriptor to monitor and/or design NHCP ligands with desired σ-donor properties. The NHCPs stronger σ-donor and weaker π-acceptor abilities compared to NHCs and their unique structural flexibility and electronic adaptability have been showcased to be directly controlled by the carbene moiety via modulation of the HOMO lone pair energy and its atomic phosphorous 3p character. The reactivity of [NHCPAuH] complexes with CO2, taken as a probe for potential NHCP applications in small molecule activation processes, demonstrates qualitatively similar mechanisms, with remarkably different activation barriers, which directly correlate with the NHCPs σ-donor ability, thus reflecting the high tunability of their bonding properties. This work provides insights and perspectives on the design principle of NHCP ligands, with a spotlight on the pivotal role of NHC moiety in modulating their electronic and steric properties, offering opportunities for burgeoning applications across diverse fields.

articles.title: Machine-learned exchange-correlation functionals for molecules, solids, and reactive surfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.21525v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The application of density functional theory to heterogeneous catalysis is hindered by the shortcomings of conventional density functional approximations. We combine machine learning with explicitly non-local physically informed descriptors and introduce an exchange-correlation functional (CIDER26SS) framework regularized for wide transferability. CIDER26SS is size-extensive, highly efficient, provides a balanced and accurate description of both molecular and solid-state systems, and is specifically well-optimized for transition metal surface chemistry. Surpassing existing conventional functionals, CIDER26SS resolves the CO/Pt puzzle, identifying the correct binding site for CO adsorption on the Pt(111) surface, along with an accurate adsorption energy, Pt lattice constant, and surface energy. Predictions agree well with the experimental values, even when all bulk and surface data for Pt are excluded from the training set. Remarkably, CIDER26SS exceeds the accuracy of semilocal approximations even for systems far outside the training domain.

articles.title: Unusual quantum states in six-layer graphene offer clues to superconductivity
articles.abstract: Graphene, a material consisting of a sheet of carbon atoms arranged in a honeycomb pattern, has proved promising for various technological applications. Materials in which several layers of graphene are stacked together can exhibit different advantageous properties.

articles.title: New X-ray method isolates faint signals from water at material surfaces
articles.abstract: A research team from Toyohashi University of Technology, the Institute for Molecular Science and the Institute of Science Tokyo, led by Yu Kinjo and professor Ryugo Tero of Toyohashi University of Technology, has developed a new method to investigate the state of water near material surfaces using X-rays. By combining X-ray absorption spectroscopy with data analysis, the researchers separated the weak signals of interfacial water from those of the much larger amount of surrounding water.
