articles.title: Electrical guardrails for charge carriers: A new approach to harness graphene for solar cells
articles.abstract: Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms in which electrons can move with high mobility, making it promising for high-speed electronic components. Yet it is not very efficient at converting light into electricity. While light absorbed by graphene does excite electrons, leaving behind positively charged carriers called 'holes,' the absorbed light energy cannot be harnessed effectively unless electrons and holes are separated and directed to different contacts.

articles.title: How the quantum vacuum perturbs atoms, could shrink black holes and may have helped form galaxies
articles.abstract: The word "vacuum" may conjure the image of empty space. Maybe you think of a region far outside the solar system without planets, debris, gas clouds or light. According to quantum theory, however, a vacuum is never truly empty. Quantum mechanics extends the Heisenberg uncertainty principle—which states that we cannot measure the position and the velocity of an object exactly at the same time—to a vacuum. The result is that a vacuum can never be still.

articles.title: A blue laser for underwater communication and sensing
articles.abstract: Researchers at EPFL have developed a chip-scale blue laser that combines stable light emission with rapid frequency control, opening possibilities for underwater communication, environmental sensing and quantum technologies.

articles.title: A B₁g phonon unlocks d-wave superconductivity in the repulsive Hubbard model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using numerically exact finite-temperature quantum Monte Carlo, we demonstrate that a B₁g phonon coupled to the doped t-t' repulsive Hubbard model produces genuine d-wave superconductivity at a substantial transition temperature, in excess of either interaction alone. The observed trends suggest that stronger Hubbard repulsion may cooperate with the phonon to further raise the pairing scale. The enhancement persists at stronger repulsion within the accessible window, limited by the fermion sign problem, and follows a common trend across phonon frequencies Ω when organized by a retardation scale 2π T/Ω. We also find a well-defined superconducting dome in doping, echoing a characteristic feature of correlated superconductors. Our results identify the B₁g phonon as a plausible microscopic ingredient for robust d-wave superconductivity in the Hubbard model and suggest a concrete, physically motivated route toward materials with higher superconducting transition temperatures.

articles.title: Long-Range Toric Code: Finite-Temperature Topological Order in Two Dimensions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce two-dimensional toric code models with additional long-range loop interactions. Our models preserve the topologically ordered ground states of the ordinary toric code, while confining anyons at zero temperature. For sufficiently long-ranged interactions, we argue that this confinement persists at finite temperatures, strongly constraining anyon mobility and giving rise to finite-temperature topological order. This topological phase acts as a self-correcting quantum memory and exhibits long-range entanglement. For shorter-ranged interactions, signatures of topological order survive only up to an exponentially large length scale at finite temperature, yielding a partially self-correcting quantum memory.

articles.title: Few-Electron Partitioning in the Fractional Quantum Hall Regime
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by few-electron partitioning experiments [Shaju et al., Nature 642, 928 (2025)], we study the partition statistics of N-electron states at a fractional quantum Hall point contact. At the solvable point g=1/2, we obtain nonperturbative current and noise formulas for arbitrary drives, while for Lorentzian pulses (Levitons) the full counting statistics reduces to an N× N determinant. We show that the charge is transferred solely in units of e, and that symmetrized cumulants for N=2,3,4 reveal strong antibunching and higher-order correlations, observable in a (ν₁,ν₂)=(1,1/3) junction.

articles.title: Analytical framework for interpreting thermoreflectance measurements of nanoline gratings under finite spot illumination
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR)-based technique is presented to measure the effective thermal properties of a material stack whose surface is patterned with metallic nanoline gratings that are heated and probed by lasers. An analytical heat diffusion model is derived for predicting the FDTR phase response that incorporates a finite laser spot radius with a Gaussian intensity profile for the pump and probe lasers, as well as the dimensions of the nanoline grating. The model is validated by comparing with measurements of Au nanoline gratings, with widths ranging from 100 to 1000 nm, fabricated on a-SiO₂ and c-sapphire substrates. Due to the short phonon mean free paths (MFPs) in these substrates, thermal transport remains in the diffusive regime for the whole range of nanoline widths. The model and the measurement show excellent agreement across different laser spot radii and nanoline widths, with a bulk thermal conductivity value of c-sapphire and the thermal boundary conductances at the Au-Cr/a-SiO₂ and Au-Cr/c-sapphire interfaces comparable to our prior measurements and the literature. The validated model will serve as a robust baseline for extending this method to measure effective thermal conductivity as a function of the heater size. This approach is particularly relevant for materials where non-diffusive thermal transport regimes enable probing phonon MFP dependent contributions to the thermal conductivity.

articles.title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface morphology is widely considered an indicator of thin-film quality, with smoother films generally expected to exhibit more uniform optoelectronic properties. Here, we demonstrate that substantial surface evolution does not necessarily lead to increased electronic heterogeneity in mixed-dimensional perovskite heterostructures. We investigate how low-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper capping layers derived from the sterically hindered 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium cation affect the spatial distributions of photoluminescence (PL) characteristics and quasi-Fermi level splitting (QFLS) in 3D perovskites. By combining statistical atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis with confocal, spatially resolved PL spectroscopy, we correlate surface topography with microscale optoelectronic properties. Although capping increases surface roughness and height asymmetry, it does not increase electronic inhomogeneity. Instead, the heterostructures exhibit enhanced PL, reduced non-radiative recombination, and improved spatial uniformity of radiative QFLS compared with pristine 3D films. Under accelerated aging, this contrast becomes more pronounced: pristine films develop substantial spatial fluctuations in emission and QFLS, whereas capped heterostructures largely preserve their optoelectronic homogeneity. These findings indicate that the low-dimensional capping layer suppresses aging-induced optoelectronic disorder, demonstrating that electronic uniformity can be maintained despite morphological irregularity. This decoupling provides a design principle for developing durable, high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.

articles.title: Thermal laser evaporation of superconducting Nb films
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Thermal laser evaporation (TLE) is an emerging physical vapor deposition (PVD) technique that uses continuous-wave lasers to evaporate even the most refractory elements. The deposition and characterization of superconducting refractory elements are of interest to assess the quality of films deposited by TLE. Here, we report the deposition of niobium (Nb) on c-plane sapphire using a home-built TLE system equipped with a 1070 nm continuous-wave fiber laser. A deposition rate of 0.19 Å/s was achieved with 533 W of laser power focused to a diameter of approximately 500 μm on a Nb target. A film with a thickness of 22.47 ± 0.05 nm and a root-mean-square (RMS) roughness of 0.23 ± 0.02 nm exhibited a room-temperature resistivity of 21.60 ± 0.05 μOmegacm and a residual-resistivity ratio (RRR) of 5.71. The superconducting transition temperature, T_c, of the film was measured as 9.24 K, only 10 mK below the bulk value, with a transition width of 29 mK. Among films deposited without substrate heating, the electrical and superconducting properties of the present films meet or exceed those deposited by other techniques. This work contributes to the emerging consensus regarding TLE as a versatile PVD method for refractory elements and compounds.

articles.title: Emergent higher-order optical nonlinearity in self-assembled polar supertextures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Giant optical nonlinearities enable advanced materials control and bridge exotic light-matter phenomena to next-generation photonics. However, materials exhibiting strong higher-order optical nonlinearity beyond the second order are typically rare. Here, we report the discovery of a giant and ultrafast second-harmonic generation (SHG) in self-assembled polar skyrmions under mid-infrared excitations. The transient SHG intensity exhibits a distinctive power dependence originating from higher-order nonlinearity. More generally, we show that large higher-order nonlinearity emerges across diverse domain structures in polar superlattices. Phase-field simulations demonstrate a strong and periodic local permittivity variation within each polar texture at equilibrium, and further confirm the fast polarization oscillation in polar skyrmions with mid-infrared excitations. This intense local permittivity modulation can satisfy epsilon-near-zero conditions, unlocking dramatically enhanced nonlinear optical responses without photonic engineering. Consequently, the self-assembled polar topologies with strong inherent optical nonlinearity could establish a platform for quantum information processing and high-speed optical communications.

articles.title: Incoherent dark excitons extend Floquet-like physics across time and momentum
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Floquet phenomena - where a coherent, time-periodic drive hybridizes the conduction band with energy-replicated copies of the valence band - have been demonstrated with intense optical fields and, more recently, other bosonic excitations. However, within mean-field approximations and the current understanding of Floquet phenomena, these effects survive only for the coherence time of the drive, limiting practical use and current demonstrations to the sub-picosecond regime. Here, consistent with recent theoretical predictions beyond the mean-field picture, using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy in WSe₂/MoS₂ heterostructures, we show that incoherent, dense populations of dark interlayer excitons hybridize the conduction band with energy-replicated copies of the valence band, mimicking Floquet-like phenomena - now persisting for nearly a nanosecond. With increasing interlayer exciton density, the valence band and its replica evolve from an inverted-parabolic to a Mexican-hat dispersion, a signature of the predicted non-zero static coupling that hybridizes the bands and scales linearly with the exciton density. By tuning twist angle, we further show that dark excitons with net momentum create replicas that hybridize with bands offset not just in energy but also in momentum, providing another powerful degree of freedom beyond conventional Floquet engineering. These results establish a robust, long-lived route to engineering electronic states, beyond a coherent, zero-momentum drive.

articles.title: Charge Filling-Dependent Valley Polarization and its Dynamics Driven by Correlated Interlayer Exciton States in WSe2/WS2 Heterobilayer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Moiré heterostructures of transition metal dichalcogenides provide an emerging platform for studying the strongly correlated electronic and excitonic states. The valley degree of freedom and its dynamics in the strongly correlated electronic and excitonic states in the moiré system are crucial for fundamental understanding and applications of valleytronics. Although the strongly correlated states in moiré systems have been extensively investigated, their impact on valley degrees of freedom and its dynamics remains unexplored. Here, we study the charge filling-dependent valley relaxation dynamics of interlayer excitons (IXs) in WSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayer system. The evolution of moiré IXs dynamics across the Mott transition is elucidated by combining time-resolved optical spectroscopy with Monte Carlo simulation. Our results show that the radiative decay and recombination rate of IXs are enhanced at the integer filling factors n (=-1). Moreover, the valley relaxation rate of IXs at n=±1 is significantly decreased. The resulting reduction in wavefunction overlap and phonon scattering process suppresses the nonradiative recombination and intervalley scattering of IXs. These anomalous behaviors are attributed to the modification of IXs recombination pathways and enhance excitonic coherence due to the localization of introduced charge carriers at integer filling of moiré site. Our results explore exciton and valley dynamics as sensitive probes of strongly correlated states in moiré systems and highlight possible ways to control excitonic coherence and valleytronic properties in two-dimensional quantum materials.

articles.title: The Flexoelectric Twist: Persistence of Heavy Fermion Picture in Small-Angle Twisted Bilayer Graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) near the first magic angle (θapprox1.05cⁱrc) hosts flat bands that provide a fertile ground for exploring strongly correlated and topological phases. At smaller twist angles (θ<1cⁱrc), attice relaxation profoundly alters the moiré landscape. The extent to which moiré lattice reconstruction at different length scales affects the electronic structure through electro-mechanical coupling remains unresolved. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy on small-angle TBG devices (θapprox0.3-0.7cⁱrc), we observe a pronounced dI/dV peak at the AA site of the moiré lattice on top of a spectrum that is asymmetric about the charge neutrality point, lattice reconstruction over moiré lattice length scales, as well as a dilation of the atomic lattice at the AA sites. We demonstrate at a phenomenological level that the inclusion of moiré lattice reconstruction supports compact localized heavy fermion f- states localized at AA sites. The additional inclusion of atomic lattice dilation enerates a strong flexo-electric response that explicitly breaks particle-hole symmetry, pushing compact, localized f-states at the AA sites down in energy. Consequently, these heavy fermion states energetically coexist with itinerant c-electrons at the AB/BA sites. Our spatially resolved spectroscopic measurements quantitatively visualize this coexistence, confirming the persistence of the heavy fermion model in the small-angle regime θ<1cⁱrc. Our findings provide microscopic insights into how flexo-electricity affects the low-energy electronic structure of small-angle TBG. More broadly, our study establishes small-angle TBG as a new class of moiré materials to explore the interacting Kondo lattice problem with high tunability of the f-occupation and c-density through twist-angle and electrostatic back gates, respectively.

articles.title: Time evolution in the multi-component dynamical Keldysh models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38338v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a time evolution operator for a dynamical quantum models with a multi-component random Gaussian field characterized by a long correlation time. We analyze three paradigmatic cases: non-Abelian SU(2) symmetry class for the three-component Gaussian noise and Abelian symmetry classes U(1) and Z₂ for the two- and one-component noises correspondingly. Starting with a limiting case of the infinite correlation time (Keldysh model) we shown that statistics of the two-component random field with a non-zero mean is described by the Rice distribution. We derived and solved the system of coupled linear differential equations for the exact diagonal and off-diagonal single-particle Green's functions. We showed how the finite time correlation in Keldysh models are accounted by a continuous fractions method.

articles.title: Direct real-space imaging of sign-reversal superconducting state by scanning Josephson tunneling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase-sensitive experiments based on Josephson tunneling have been considered as a pivotal method to determine the pairing symmetry in high-temperature (high-Tc) cuprate superconductors. However, in iron-based superconductors, traditional phase-sensitive experiments face setbacks because of the complexity of pairing symmetry in multiband systems. Here, using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM), we report the half-unit-cell periodic Josephson tunneling modulations in monolayer high-Tc Fe(Te,Se) film epitaxially grown on SrTiO3(001). The Josephson tunneling almost vanishes along the lines connecting next-nearest-neighbor Fe atoms under an s-wave superconducting tip. Combined with single-particle tunneling spectra showing the full superconducting gap, our experimental results are consistent with the sign-reversal nodeless d-wave pairing symmetry. Our findings provide sub-unit-cell scale superconducting phase information for understanding the mechanism of high-Tc superconductivity. We anticipate our work as a starting point for atomically resolved Josephson interference experiments using SJTM in various unconventional superconductors.

articles.title: Tan's Contact for Trapped Spin-Orbit-Coupled Fermi Gases at Finite Temperature
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tan's contact, bridging microscopic features of many-body quantum systems to two-body contact interactions, is pivotal in the description of quantum gases. However, past studies of Tan's contact of the spin-orbit coupled Fermi gases have been exclusively discussed at zero temperature. The thermal effects on that, which cannot be neglected in most experimental conditions, has not been explored so far. Here, through a path integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) study, we show that thermal effects fundamentally alter the scaling relation between spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and Tan's contact. The linear scaling of Tan's contact with respect to the strength of SOC found at zero temperature is drastically undermined by the thermal effects. And a new mechanism based on the competition between the mean occupancy and the energy-reweighted occupancy of the opposite spin fermion pairs within the interaction range has been unveiled, which radically changes the above linear scaling to a non-monotonic dependence. Our work should be useful for future experiments to explore the preternatural thermal effects on Tan's contact of the strongly interacting spin-orbit-coupled Fermi gas.

articles.title: Gravitational anomaly spectroscopy of a Kitaev spin liquid
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The chiral central charge c measures the gravitational anomaly of a two-dimensional topological phase. It fixes the heat current carried along the edge. So far, it has been accessed through thermal transport, where phonons complicate the signal, or through wave-function probes that need a pure ground state. Here we show that c is a spectroscopic quantity of the edge. A weak modulation of the edge couplings that travel along the edge is absorbed according to the Virasoro algebra. Normalized by the response to a static change of the same couplings, the absorbed weights obey Dₙ=2nlangle L₀rangle+fracc12(n³-n), so that Cequiv2D₂-4D₁=c in any state of the ideal edge theory, thermal or not. The central charge thus appears in transition weights, although it cancels from excitation gaps. The ratio of line weights with and without a vison in the bulk, Λ=4h_σ/c, needs no calibration and fixes the conformal spin h_σ of the non-Abelian Ising anyon. For the Kitaev honeycomb spin liquid we find C=0.49999 and h_σ=0.06250 on 7168 spins. Calibrating with the shift of the measured line itself gives c within about 1% on 96 spins and within 1% under 20% random coupling errors. Interacting edge Majoranas in a fixed flux sector, treated with DMRG, keep C within 1.5% while the edge velocity changes by ±13%. An exact simulation of a quantum-processor protocol, including the native Floquet circuit, returns c within 3.5% on 96 to 600 spins.

articles.title: Mixed-State Topological Transition and Emergent Fractionalized Supersymmetry in the Non-Abelian Kitaev Spin Liquid
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38741v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a mixed-state topological transition in the non-Abelian Kitaev spin liquid driven by a bond-dephasing channel. In the vectorized picture, bond dephasing maps onto interactions between two time-reversed fractionalized Majorana systems coupled to gapped mathbb Z₂ gauge fields, enabling sign-problem-free Monte Carlo simulations. We show that increasing dephasing condenses an inter-copy fermion pair, converting rm IsingboxtimesoverlinermIsing to toric-code order in the Choi state and yielding intrinsically mixed-state topological order upon unfolding. More interestingly, at a temporal interface between topological and trivial Kitaev states, a Chern-number mismatch enforces a gapless Majorana mode. Dephasing then drives a mixed-state topological transition at which the gapless mode develops emergent mathcal N=1 supersymmetry. Our Monte Carlo simulations yield ν=1.27(3) and η_bsimeqη_fsimeq0.40, consistent with the exact supersymmetric values 5/4 and 2/5. The supersymmetric partners are fractionalized and appear physically as distinct gauge-invariant spin strings, providing concrete observables for future experiments.

articles.title: Multiscale evaluation of the elastic response of polycrystalline NiAl using molecular statics, EBSD-based finite element and analytical homogenization methods
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The presented work proposes a multiscale framework for the numerical and analytical determination of the elastic constants of the intermetallic nickel aluminide (NiAl) at the microscopic scale. Molecular dynamics (MD) calculations have been employed to evaluate the stiffness tensors of a single NiAl monocrystalline body with cubic Pmbar3m symmetry. The atomistic results were transferred to the upper scale as an input to micromechanical models. Here, finite element modeling (FEM) and analytical homogenization methods were used to simulate the elastic behavior of polycrystalline NiAl, with special attention to grain anisotropy and its morphology. The microstructural features of the heterogeneous body were evaluated experimentally using electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and subsequently used to generate a 3D polycrystalline geometric model that preserves realistic distributions of grain orientations and grain sizes. The reconstructed NiAl polycrystal was subjected to uniaxial tensile test simulations using FEM to evaluate the effective Young's modulus (E) and Poisson's ratio (ν). The numerical results were confronted with the experimental values of E and~ν. With these model assumptions, a very good agreement between numerical and experimental results was achieved. Finally, the experimental results were compared with classical analytical estimates. Among the analytical approaches, the Hashin-Shtrikman upper bound and self-consistent approximation reproduced the experimental Young's modulus with minor deviations.

articles.title: Effect of the surface on the energy levels in PbS and PbSe nanocrystals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38874v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The structure of the electron and hole quantum confinement levels in spherical PbS and PbSe nanocrystals (NCs) is studied within the framework of a four-band effective-mass model. This level structure was initially calculated within the Kang--Wise model, which employs the standard boundary condition of vanishing carrier wave functions at the NC surface. This model, however, does not allow one to account for the effect of the NC surface on the level structure. Here, the effect of the NC surface is modeled using general boundary conditions (GBCs) imposed on the envelope wave functions at the surface. We show that the surface properties modify the size dependence of the electron and hole confinement levels and lead to an additional spin--orbit splitting of the 1Pₕ,ₑ levels. Using the GBCs, we are able to quantitatively describe the size dependence of the lowest optical transitions in bare PbS and PbSe NCs and explain the differences between the absorption spectra of bare and Cl-passivated PbS NCs

articles.title: Comment on "Is there a density-gradient expansion for the electronic exchange energy?"
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Perdew et al. [arXiv:2610.07201 (2026)] dispute our finding [Phys. Rev. B 113, 115136 (2026)] that the separate exchange (bₓ) and correlation (b_c) contributions to the q² coefficient of the long-wavelength proper polarization function depend on the infrared regularization of the Coulomb interaction, although their sum bₓc=bₓ+b_c does not. We question their claim that the conventional exchange coefficient is uniquely determined. In Qian's [J. Math. Phys. 56, 111901 (2015)] derivation, which Perdew et al. cite in support of their claim of a unique exchange-gradient coefficient, an integral of the form int₋ₐbdx/x crosses a singularity and does not exist as an ordinary improper integral. Its finite Cauchy principal value (which is a particular way of regularizing the integral) is obtained only by excluding equal intervals on the two sides of the singularity; unequal exclusions give different answers. Independently, Sham's calculation with the screened interaction e⁻λ₀ r/r gives an exchange-gradient coefficient different from the bare-Coulomb calculations of Svendsen--von Barth [Int. J. Quantum Chem. 56, 351 (1995)] and Engel--Vosko [Phys. Rev. B 42, 4940 (1990)]. The discrepancy remains when λ₀>0 is so small that 1/λ₀ is comparable to the size of the observable universe, making the two interactions experimentally indistinguishable on laboratory scales. Why should the exactly unscreened result be preferred, even if its calculation is accepted as valid? Our calculation shows that the ambiguity of the separate contributions cancels in the combined, regulator-independent coefficient bₓc.

articles.title: Separating the Density Wave Phase from Zero-Resistance Superconductivity in La₄Ni₃O₁₀
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identifying the key ingredients for superconductivity under pressure in the Ruddlesden-Popper nickelates remains a formidable challenge, due to a complex interplay between structural variations, oxygen content and location, electronically ordered phases, and the need for high pressures to reach the superconducting phase. To disentangle these complex inter-dependencies, here we study a series of clean single crystals of trilayer La₄Ni₃O₁₀. We discover that enhanced biaxial, compressive pressures induce a zero-resistance state at a 60% lower pressure compared to previous reports. At the same time, we completely separate the low-pressure density wave phase from superconductivity, effectively ruling out that soft, quantum critical fluctuations of the density wave order parameter act as the pairing glue in this system. Our results establish biaxial, in-plane pressures as a powerful tool for promoting superconductivity in nickelates, unifying the required pressure scales for superconductivity in different Ruddlesden-Popper structures, and providing a connection to the recently discovered thin film samples.

articles.title: HERA: Assessing an Autonomous Agent for Quantum Device Measurement
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents have begun to carry out laboratory measurements, but their scientific conclusions are useful only if they hold up under scrutiny. Demonstrating this requires controlled studies because models are stochastic and the context a model is given steers its conclusions. Here we introduce HERA, an autonomous agent designed to carry out cryogenic transport measurements of quantum devices. HERA draws on a knowledge base curated by lab members that holds measurement protocols, software tools, and literature references. We assessed HERA with a blinded trial against an expert on the stacking order of two multilayer graphene devices, an ablation of its knowledge base, and hundreds of offline replays in which models designed the trial's central measurement without running it. HERA's conclusions matched the expert's sealed conclusions on both tested devices. The ablation and the replay studies measured the impact of the knowledge base across different models, showing that with it every model designed better measurements and reasoned more soundly. To test how readily HERA extends to a new problem, we tasked it with finding and characterizing superconductivity in a different material system. This required a few hours of expert time to develop a new experimental protocol, after which HERA did both autonomously. These results show that, with a knowledge base designed for the task, language model agents are capable of sound experimental science.

articles.title: The Constructive Cavity Method for the Ising Perceptron
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39141v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We apply the Constructive Cavity Method (CCM) to the Ising perceptron. The process starts from positive soft channels admitting an auxiliary representation  U(x)=intR etxρ(dt),qquad ρge0,  with an auxiliary measure having a finite exponential quadratic moment. This rewrites the perceptron as a dense, bipartite Gaussian model with an Ising layer and a continuous auxiliary layer. The CCM blanket geometry then gives two constructive variance profiles, Q_ell on the Ising side and Γ_ell on the auxiliary side. The bipartite shell scale is  Qₑₗₗ₊₁Γₑₗₗ₊₁-Q_ellΓ_ell,  and Gaussian core comparison removes the core contribution Δ Q_ellΔΓ_ell under blanket refinement. The scalar cavity functional has three terms,  Aₚₑᵣc(ν)=Eleft[loglangle2cosh xrangle_ν+αloglangle U(s)rangle_ν-loglangle e^yrangle_νright],  where x is the new-spin field, s is the new-constraint field, and y is the cavity correction. CCM identifies the constructive cavity variables with the Aizenman--Sims--Starr random overlap structure (ROSt) variables. Parisi's recursive averaging then gives  GₚₑᵣcCCM(ζ,Q,Γ)=X₀(0)+α Y₀(0)-frac12sumₑₗₗ₌₀Rζ_ellleft(Qₑₗₗ₊₁Γₑₗₗ₊₁-Q_ellΓ_ellright).  The replica-symmetric specialization gives Gardner's formula for the generalized Ising perceptron. Specializing the constraint terminal to the hard channel gives the Krauth--Mézard functional for the binary perceptron.

articles.title: Atomic Charge Chirality from Electric Multipoles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish an electric-multipole (Qₗₘ) criterion for chirality of local atomic charge distributions. For the 11 crystallographic chiral point groups, we identify representative lowest-rank multipole contents required to distinguish the opposite handednesses. For the axial groups Cₙ and Dₙ with n=2,3,4,6, chirality arises from the relative orientation of two azimuthal anisotropies with m=n, belonging to consecutive ranks l=n and n+1. Their coexistence produces a latitude-dependent twist of the n-fold charge distribution. The polar component, although allowed in Cₙ, is distinct from this chiral mechanism and is not required for handedness. The cubic groups T and O exhibit distinct realizations, with octahedral chirality first appearing at rank nine. We further show that, within a spinless s-p-d-f atomic basis, the scalar charge density contains multipoles only up to rank six and therefore cannot encode the handedness of C₆, D₆, or O. These results connect electric-multipole content and atomic orbital degrees of freedom to the microscopic encoding of crystallographic handedness.

articles.title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39213v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. Layered bismuth oxychalcogenides, Bi2O2X (X = S, Se, Te), are mixed-anion crystals whose covalent slabs and ionic sheets are bound electrostatically rather than by van der Waals forces and whose Bi3+ 6s² lone pairs can become stereochemically active. Despite the rapid development of Bi2O2Se for fin and gate-all-around transistors, its fundamental thermal expansion and heat transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we show that lone-pair stereoactivity, not chalcogen mass, governs both properties. Path-integral molecular dynamics shows that the volumetric thermal expansion coefficient at 300 K decreases from 8.14 x 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹ in Bi2O2S to 6.72 x 10⁻⁵ and 6.61 x 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹ in Bi2O2Se and Bi2O2Te, respectively, despite a 13% larger unit cell in the telluride, whereas substituting the S mass into Bi2O2Se changes its value by only 0.6%. Lone-pair-driven Bi off-centering in orthorhombic Bi2O2S makes b-axis expansion 1.63 times a-axis expansion yet leaves in-plane thermal conduction isotropic within 3%. Phonon transport calculations including four-phonon scattering and Wigner coherence predict a thermal conductivity maximum in Bi2O2Se (1.83 and 0.95 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ in the in-plane and cross-plane directions, respectively, at 300 K) because Bi2O2S is limited by anharmonic scattering and Bi2O2Te by slow cross-plane phonons. Thermoreflectance measurements from 300 to 500 K and in situ X-ray diffraction on Bi2O2Se single crystals agree with these predictions within 6.4%. Phonon Boltzmann transport simulations of 12-nm-wide fins, which run hotter than Fourier diffusion predicts, show that Bi2O2Se minimizes the hotspot temperature and the thermal-mismatch strain at the gate dielectric.

articles.title: Polarization-locked chiral persistent spin textures in two-dimensional lead-halide perovskites
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chiral spacer cations crystallize two-dimensional hybrid perovskites in the polar Sohncke group P2₁, which places the polar axis in the inorganic layer. We analyze the spin-orbit field that this geometry allows and test it against first-principles spin textures of ten polar chiral lead-halide perovskites, their mirror enantiomers and four halide-substituted analogues. The point group C₂ with the twofold axis in the layer forbids the helical Rashba field and allows a linear term γ₁ kₓ σ_z, the Rashba interaction of the in-plane polar axis, together with chirality-related Dresselhaus and radial terms. Thirty-four two-band k · p models were fitted to each band pair and ranked by the agreement of their spin directions with the calculation rather than by the band energies, which cannot distinguish them. In all strongly polar compounds, the conduction band is described by the persistent term alone, with γ₁ = 1.09-1.98 eV Å and a spin agreement of at least 0.98, whereas the best Rashba or Dresselhaus model reaches 0.20. The R and S enantiomers of each compound have opposite polarizations, and therefore opposite γ₁ and opposite persistent spin textures of equal magnitude, as required by the mirror that relates them; this holds in all ten compounds, so the choice of the enantiomer selects the spin direction. The magnitude of γ₁ correlates with the disparity of the in-plane Pb-X-Pb angles (r = 0.95). With electron masses of 0.26-0.43,mₑ along the spin-splitting directions, the associated persistent spin helices have wavelengths of 3.4-8.2 nm.

articles.title: Dissipation dilution enhances SiV coupling to vdW diamond nanomechanics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solid-state color centers embedded into mechanical resonators, where orbital states mediate interactions between spins and long-lived phonons, are a promising platform for hybrid quantum systems. The negatively charged silicon vacancy center in diamond (SiV-) is particularly favorable for strain-coupling to nanomechanical resonators because of its large spin-strain susceptibility and compatibility with device integration. Tensioned nanomechanical resonators offer an attractive route due to their ultra-long mechanical coherence times enabled by diluting defect-induced dissipation, though it is unclear if the same dilution effect undermines strain-mediated coupling to material defect centers. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a tensioned diamond nanobeam platform that enables enhanced strain coupling to SiV- orbital states. Through monitoring the optical response of the SiVs to the static and dynamical strain of the mechanical resonator, we observe that dynamical strain localizes near the clamps of these resonators under static strain. This allows us to enhance SiV-mechanical coupling and the mechanical coherence simultaneously, and provide a SiV-strain sensitivity with greatly improved accuracy over previous literature values. Thus, our work opens a pathway towards seconds-long coherence hybrid quantum systems utilizing point defects in diamond nanomechanics for quantum information processing.

articles.title: Th⁴⁺ ion cluster structures and electric field gradients in ²²⁹Th:CaF₂
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The low-energy nuclear isomeric transition of ²²⁹Th is a promising frequency reference for a solid-state nuclear optical clock. Wide-band-gap fluoride crystals such as CaF₂ offer transparent hosts for embedding Th nuclei at high density. Substitution of Th⁴⁺ for Ca²⁺ requires charge compensation, linking the local defect structure to nuclear quadrupole splitting. We use first-principles calculations to examine neutral Th dimers compensated by four interstitial F ions (Fᵢ⁻). Screening different compensation geometries by their relative formation energies identifies a family of low-energy configurations with closely similar local structures. These configurations share large electric field gradients and small asymmetry parameters, consistent with the experimental high-EFG site 3. Their calculated quadrupole splittings are further compared with the measured C13 spectra. Together, the energetic and spectroscopic results support Fᵢ⁻-compensated Th dimers as candidate microscopic structures for site 3 in Th:CaF₂.

articles.title: Ten-loop fixed-dimension renormalization-group functions of the three-dimensional O(N) model from distributed GPU-accelerated parametric integration
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The renormalization-group functions β, η and ν of the three-dimensional O(N) model in fixed dimension (massive zero-momentum scheme) were known to eighth order in the coupling. We extend them to tenth order, and β to eleventh, for general N, which requires the two- and four-point functions to ten loops (1,593,254 graphs at the last order), and re-evaluate all lower orders. Through the Callan-Symanzik equation every coefficient follows from per-order sums that are linear in finite, zero-momentum bar R-subtracted parametric integrals, one per graph, which we sample on GPUs by tropical Monte Carlo with densities adapted to the forest terms. The computation reproduces the known sums from two to seven loops within three standard deviations and agrees at ninth and tenth order, at lower precision, with an independent route through an intermediate scheme. The new coefficients have relative uncertainties of a few 10⁻⁵ or better, and the eighth-order coefficients of η and ν improve by factors of 120 and 4. The time needed to integrate an order to fixed relative precision grows by only 2.4-2.9 per loop from seven loops on, while the construction of the integrands still grows factorially and, at tenth order, costs more than the integration. Resummed, the tenth-order series give ν=0.62997(51), η=0.0333(18) and ω=0.803(14) for N=1, against 0.62997097(12), 0.036297612(48) and 0.82968(23) from the conformal bootstrap; at N=3 the deviations grow, so that the uncertainty is now dominated by the resummation rather than by the coefficients. Every result is generated automatically from, or checked against, a public ledger of independent, exactly pooled runs, hosted on GitHub, to which anyone is welcome to contribute computing time.

articles.title: A Zoo of Fermionic Relative Rényi Negativities in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Models
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental resource that gives rise to correlations with no classical counterpart in strongly correlated fermionic systems. However, its characterization in mixed quantum states remains challenging. Established entanglement diagnostics, such as logarithmic negativity, are computationally demanding in interacting systems, and their evaluation by exact diagonalization is restricted to small system sizes. Meanwhile, conventional Rényi proxies, including twisted and untwisted Rényi negativities, can be positive even for separable states. In this work, we introduce a family of relative Rényi negativities that serve as entanglement witnesses. By relating fermionic partial time reversal to the size superoperator, we establish a path-integral representation for these Rényi negativities, enabling their evaluation in thermal states of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model and its generalizations via a large-N expansion. Applying this method, we investigate entanglement in both the original SYK model and the Maldacena-Qi coupled SYK model. We identify a special class of relative Rényi negativities which serve as plausible proxies for logarithmic negativity and uncover first-order entanglement transitions that are invisible to simple observables. These results highlight the utility of relative Rényi negativities as probes of mixed-state entanglement in strongly correlated fermionic systems and suggest the existence of a new class of transitions where these negativities serve as free energies.

articles.title: Hop rates of H and D on Pt(111) at finite coverage: the memory equation and the collective friction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39436v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Helium scattering measures the coherent intermediate scattering function of an adlayer, the characteristic function of the separation between adparticles at two times. Published dephasing rates of H and D on Pt(111) are analysed with its memory equation and a nearest-neighbour Ising lattice gas. The measured rate belongs to the adlayer. The hop rate of a single adsorbate is extracted from it by dividing out an interaction factor, without a model of the barrier. This factor lies between 0.97 and 1.17 at 0.1~ML, so that the published single-adsorbate analyses hold there. At 0.4~ML and 80~K it lies between 1.2 and 4.7, depending on how the occupied neighbours modify a tunnelling jump. The memory function is interpreted as a friction, the collective friction, which the adlayer exerts on its own density fluctuations. The lateral coupling, fixed by the coverage series, is the free energy of a neighbouring pair, with a vibrational pair entropy. The small deformation of the measured curves from the Chudley--Elliott form, the tilt, is proposed as an observable of the coupling. The tilts at 0.15 and 0.2~ML are consistent with it, although they are hard to extract from the published curves. The memory equation provides a transition-state theory for the adlayer, with the collective friction in the role of the friction of the substrate and without divergence at the crossover. Combined with the standard quantum transition-state theory of a single adsorbate, the extracted hop rates give the friction of the substrate, 124 and 75~ps⁻¹ for H and D, independent of the coverage.

articles.title: Fractal dimensions of paths on three-dimensional random-walk traces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study four paths that join the starting site to the final position of a simple random walk of (N=L²) steps on the infinite cubic lattice. The paths are selected on the walk trace---the graph of visited sites and traversed bonds---by different rules: the undirected shortest path (S₁), the directed shortest path (S₂), the time-respecting shortest path (S₃), and the depth (Dₑ) of the final site in a depth-first-search tree. Monte Carlo simulations for (L) up to 32768 give mean lengths scaling as (Ld_O), with (dS_₁=1.48005(9)), (dS_₂=1.49868(5)), (dS_₃=1.51205(5)), and (dD_ₑ=1.7099(7)), so that (dS_₁

articles.title: Observation of light-induced topological state in graphene
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39695v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Driving quantum materials with light can reshape not only their electronic band structures but also the geometry of their electronic wavefunctions. In graphene, circularly polarized light is predicted to open gaps at the Dirac points and induce a pseudospin texture and Berry curvature characteristic of the Haldane model, realizing a Floquet Chern insulator. Transport and all-optical measurements have provided evidence for a light-induced anomalous Hall response, but cannot resolve the underlying electronic states in both energy and momentum space. Time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy has revealed Floquet-Bloch sidebands and hybridization gaps at crossings between Floquet bands. However, these experiments used linearly polarized driving, which preserves time-reversal symmetry and thus does not induce a topological phase. Here, we combine circular-dichroic time-resolved extreme-ultraviolet momentum microscopy with ab initio theory to investigate graphene driven by circularly polarized light. We observe a pump-induced photoemission circular dichroism near the Dirac point that reverses sign with pump helicity and across the Dirac energy, in agreement with our calculations. These results link the measured dichroic response to the light-induced pseudospin texture and its associated Berry curvature, providing spectroscopic evidence for the Floquet-engineered topological insulating state in graphene.

articles.title: Phonon Fluctuations Enhanced Superconductivity in a Three-Band Cuprate Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The microscopic origin of high-T_c superconductivity in cuprates remains an outstanding puzzle due to the interplay of intertwined orders. Experimental observations and theoretical studies have suggested crucial roles of phonons, with the B₁g oxygen buckling mode emerging as a promising candidate. Here, we investigate the microscopic influence of this phonon in a three-band cuprate model. We find that the B₁g phonon plays opposite roles in superconductivity depending on whether it lies in the adiabatic or antiadiabatic regime at a given temperature. Thermally populated adiabatic phonons suppress d-wave pairing through the loss of quasiparticle coherence, whereas antiadiabatic phonons simultaneously enhance coherence and the attractive d-wave pairing vertex, strengthening superconductivity across multiple diagnostics. This enhancement also exhibits pronounced electron-hole asymmetry arising from the different orbital characters of doped carriers. Our results therefore establish a microscopic mechanism through which B₁g phonons can cooperate with electronic correlations to substantially enhance d-wave superconducting pairing in cuprates.

articles.title: I₄ complex acting as near-infrared emitter with a quantum memory in silicon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I₄), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. Using hybrid-functional (HSE06) density functional theory, we unambiguously establish the bare I₄ complex as the origin of the X-line: our calculations quantitatively reproduce the zero-phonon line, the complete phonon sideband structure---identifying the prominent secondary peaks as one- and two-phonon replicas of strongly coupled quasi-local modes---and the EPR hyperfine constants. The charge transition level is found at VBM+0.08~eV, conclusively ruling out the previously proposed association with the B3 EPR center and its correlated deep donor level. Most significantly, we identify a metastable spin-1 triplet excited state separated from the singlet by sim1.6~meV, consistent with the NL51 EPR signal. The D₂d symmetry of the defect suppresses intersystem crossing and phosphorescence by first-order spin--orbit coupling, implying an exceptionally long spin--lattice relaxation time. Combined with a spectrally resolvable zero-field splitting and near-infrared emission, the triplet state of the I₄ complex constitutes a viable spin quantum memory intrinsic to silicon.

articles.title: Moiré-enabled chiral plasmons in twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Twisting two stacked graphene layers superimposes a moiré superlattice that reshapes their electronic structure, yet how it shapes the collective optical response of finite, nanoscale bilayers remains largely unexplored. Using an atomistic tight-binding and self-consistent density-matrix approach, we compute the twist-dependent plasmonic response of twisted bilayer graphene nanoislands comprising thousands of atoms. The spectra are strongly tunable and split into two regimes at a critical angle where a single moiré wavelength spans the island; beyond it, an ordered ladder of resonances emerges whenever an integer number of moiré periods fits within the overlapping bilayer. In doped islands, the interlayer coupling also produces a moiré-enabled Born--Kuhn chiral plasmon: opposite transverse dipoles in the two layers form an electric quadrupole that hybridizes with the bright dipole, opening an anticrossing near the critical angle, with a handedness that reverses with the twist direction. Triangular islands confirm that the moiré lattice, not the flake boundary, governs both effects, establishing twist as a mechanical handle on chiral graphene plasmons.

articles.title: Direct Observation of Electron Trapping States in SiO₂ by Constant-Final-State Photoelectron Yield Spectroscopy: Insights into the Electron-Transfer Model of Contact Electrification
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding electrostatic charging of silicon dioxide (SiO₂) is important for electrostatic control in a wide range of applications. Contact electrification (CE) is a major source of such charging, and electron transfer is considered one of its leading mechanisms. Several electron-transfer models have been proposed to explain CE; however, the density of states (DOS) involved in electron transfer has not been experimentally characterized. Determining this DOS is therefore essential for understanding the charging mechanism. However, measuring the DOS of insulating materials such as SiO₂ remains challenging: photoemission spectroscopy, the standard technique for probing the DOS of materials, is unsuitable for highly insulating materials because sample charging during measurement can cause spectral distortion or even complete signal loss. Here, we directly and quantitatively determined the in-gap DOS of amorphous SiO₂ using constant-final-state photoelectron yield spectroscopy (CFS-YS). Weak occupied states were observed within the band gap, and their marked increase after electron injection revealed that electron-trapping states are distributed over a broad energy range. Vacuum annealing markedly altered the in-gap DOS and electron-trapping behavior. The observed changes suggest a role for surface adsorbates, including water, in the charging behavior of SiO₂. Charging simulations based on the experimentally measured in-gap DOS approximately reproduced the previously reported charging behavior and showed that the accumulated charge was concentrated near the surface. These findings indicate that in-gap states distributed over a broad energy range mediate electron transfer during CE and highlight the importance of considering experimentally determined DOS when evaluating proposed electron-transfer models.

articles.title: Growth and morphology of core-shell nanowires incorporating dissimilar hexagonal semiconductors: the case of InAs-ZnTe
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Core-shell nanowires incorporating semiconductors from two groups, III-V for the core and II-VI for the shell, have been grown by molecular beam epitaxy in two dedicated chambers connected under ultra-high vacuum, and studied by electron microscopy. During the growth of the shell, the wurtzite structure of the core is replicated in the shell, without any creation of defects. This is true for a wide range of shell thickness, from about one monolayer, up to 25 nm thanks to the good lattice match between the InAs material of the core and the ZnTe material of the shell. While (1 100) m-facets and (11 20) a-facets coexist on the sidewalls of the core, during the growth of the ZnTe shell the size of the m-facets progressively increases at the expense of the a-facets which eventually disappear. A fast growth of the ZnTe shell is observed for the first few monolayers, with a high sticking; this is followed by a slower growth, of the same order of magnitude as observed on a ZnTe core, with a dependence on the nanowire radius which points to the occurrence of mononuclear nucleation

articles.title: Two-dimensional binary Lennard-Jones mixtures with ECMC
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss reversible and non-reversible local Monte Carlo algorithms for long-range two-dimensional binary Lennard-Jones mixtures. We illustrate how the factorized Metropolis filter efficiently handles long-range interactions even for binary mixtures, using an adapted cell-veto strategy. We then benchmark the non-reversible event-chain Monte Carlo (ECMC) algorithm against the factorized Metropolis algorithm. For simple test cases, we demonstrate speedups of several orders of magnitude in the equilibrium and the out-of-equilibrium dynamics. Using the ECMC algorithm, we provide an overview of the physics of binary Lennard-Jones mixtures, from the case without depletion (no interaction between solute and solvent) all the way to the depletion limit (with a diverging number of solvent particles). We analyze the algorithms in different thermodynamic phases and in the corresponding limits.

articles.title: Ammonium thiocyanate enables in-situ structural templating of MAPbI3 via quasi-2D perovskite scaffold
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39887v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ammonium thiocyanate (NH4SCN) has been used extensively to improve the current extraction and device performance of quasi-two-dimensional perovskite solar cells. Whilst this additive has been shown to influence quasi-2D perovskite crystallisation, a detailed understanding of its mechanism has not yet been established. Through spectroscopic and structural studies, we demonstrate that NH4SCN enables quasi-2D perovskite phases to structurally template the dominant 3D phase. Contrary to previous reports, we suggest that the benefit of this additive comes from an improvement to the 3D perovskite structure, not from charges transferring through vertically oriented 2D perovskite layers. We show that this additive provides kinetic control over the quasi-2D phase formation, suppressing the unfavourable n = 1 perovskite phase and promoting the growth of high-n 2D scaffold phases by extending the nucleation window. This promotes the in-situ templated growth of MAPbI3. We provide robust structural analysis demonstrating highly (110)-ordered 3D perovskite, with the mechanism confirmed by close lattice matching between this phase and quasi-2D phases. Furthermore, we show that this structural control is cation dependent, requiring both close lattice matching between quasi-2D and 3D perovskite phases, and successful kinetic control of the relevant quasi-2D phases.

articles.title: Excitons in solid molecular hydrogen from quantum Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39894v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods to investigate the lowest neutral excitation of solid molecular hydrogen in phase-I under increasing compression, with emphasis on structural and response properties. We employ QMC wave functions for the excited state that feature only a single orbital substitution, or a multideterminant expansion including every single particle-hole transition, and compare the results with the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) and time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT). We examine a number of nuclear configurations representing thermal and quantum fluctuations. The effect of the multideterminant expansion is marginal on the QMC excitation energies but crucial on the exciton localization and related quantities, irrespective of full optimization and imaginary time projection. In the strong insulating regime at low density, multideterminant QMC results match and in some cases surpass the degree of localization afforded by BSE. A similar trend is observed for transition dipole moments and excitation-induced forces, with generally good agreement between QMC and BSE but marked discrepancies for nuclear configurations where localization differs significantly. TDDFT generally gives a more extended exciton with correspondingly weaker transition dipole moments. These differences decrease upon compression, as the system approaches a semiconducting regime where multiple particle-hole transitions are less important.

articles.title: Kelvin-Wave Multiplication by Sound Emission
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A subsonic Kelvin quantum can emit a phonon and split into two softer quanta, increasing Kelvin population while losing energy. In the soft-phonon limit, rotational invariance relates the leading acoustic shear amplitude, odd under reversal of phonon axial momentum, to the energy released. Microscopic calculations support this dispersion dependence. In a reflecting cavity with coherent sound and Kelvin seeds, Gross--Pitaevskii evolution shows Kelvin gain, larger mean-square displacement and smaller mean-square slope; a π shift of the initial sound phase reverses these changes.

articles.title: Majorana Zero Modes in Fractional Vortices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Majorana zero modes (MZMs) are promising for topological quantum computation, with vortices in topological superconductors serving as a leading platform. Recent experiments show that integer Abrikosov vortices in iron-based superconductors can split into fractional vortices (FVs) carrying fractional flux quanta. We show that due to topological protection, MZMs hosted by FVs are spatially unfolded over the FV cores, while fermionic bound states remain localized at individual FV cores. This yields zero-bias conductance peaks in both local tunneling and nonlocal crossed Andreev reflection, offering an alternative MZM signature.

articles.title: Nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics of a small quantum system coupled to quantum reservoirs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A statistical mechanical formulation where nonequilibrium averages of selected quantum observables are given exactly as averages over local density operators is used to describe the dynamics and thermodynamics of a small quantum system coupled to reservoirs. The local density operators are functionals of constraint variables that play the role of thermodynamic forces that satisfy a set of equations of motion. A focus of the work is on the evolution of the average internal energy of the quantum subsystem that may be subject to external autonomous driving that does work on the system, and on entropy production in the system. The nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics the quantum subsystem coupled to reservoirs, as well as that for the isolated subsystem and reservoirs, are discussed. When the subsystem is coupled to large quantum reservoirs, the effects of the quantum subsystem on the reservoirs can be captured through boundary conditions on the reservoir equations, and these boundary conditions are derived. The formulation is illustrated by considering the heat transfer through a system comprising a quantum system coupled to two heat reservoirs with different temperatures.

articles.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moiré Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. The stripe phases were revealed by electrical transport studies as a thermodynamic phase transition from a high temperature isotropic phase to a low-temperature anisotropic phase accompanied by a Fermi surface reconstruction. Near the stripe-to-superconductor transition, we also observed an additional thermodynamic phase transition from metallic stripes to pinned insulating stripes. The stripe-to-superconductor transition further exhibits an intriguing self-similarity that highlights the intimate relationship between the two orders. Our results pave the path for studying intertwined orders in moiré materials.

articles.title: Non-Bloch Dynamical Quantum Phase Transitions with Memory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dynamical quantum phase transitions (DQPTs) of periodic chains are determined by real Bloch momenta. We identify non-Bloch DQPTs, which occur only in open chains and are determined by complex momenta instead. They arise in a Hermitian chain coupled to a simple substrate, whose memory is treated exactly, and originate from the point-gap winding number W of the projected propagator: for W≠0, open boundaries change both the dynamical free energy and the critical times, even in the thermodynamic limit. We find that both follow from an analytic continuation to complex momenta, and show that W can be measured by particle counting. This reveals a dynamical bulk-boundary correspondence, in which non-Hermitian topology emerges from Hermitian dynamics with memory.

articles.title: Influence of pairing and correlations on transport properties in three-terminal superconducting nanostructure
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the local and nonlocal charge transport properties of three-terminal nanostructure, consisting of the correlated quantum dot embedded between two metallic electrodes and superconductor. Using the linear response theory, we analyze interplay of the induced on-dot pairing with the correlation effects, inspecting their influence on the conductance and thermopower. Our calculations predict negative values of the nonlocal conductance and reversal of the Seebeck coefficient when the quantum dot ground state is represented by the BCS-type singlet configuration. These phenomena are realized when the subgap charge transport is predominantly contributed by the crossed Andreev scattering. In contrast, on the doublet side, we obtain signatures for the Kondo effect manifested by the low-temperature enhancement of the charge conductance and clearly evident in the thermopower. Such temperature-dependent local and nonlocal transport properties can unambiguously identify the specific configuration of the correlated quantum dot and reveal the rich physics emerging in the doublet-to-singlet crossover region.

articles.title: Quantum Metric Scaling and Its Exceptions in Classical Flat Bands
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The quantum metric length has been proposed as the localization length scale in one-dimensional flat bands. Here, we study this quantum metric scaling and the exceptions to it in a classical flat band formed by a locally resonant mass--spring system. We find that the localization length follows the quantum metric length near the flat band but departs from this proportionality at the exact flat-band frequency. Selective mass disorder also produces divergent localization lengths or arbitrarily short tails near the flat-band frequency without changing the clean metric. These exceptions show that disorder can select localization scales beyond those predicted by the quantum metric alone.

articles.title: Single-atom billiards in an ultracold bath with energy-tunable collisions and threshold-sensitive detection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transport processes at the microscopic scale can differ strongly from their macroscopic counterparts, particularly when the environment is not a well-defined surface but an unordered thermal medium. Ultracold quantum gases offer a high degree of controllability and directly observable dynamics, thereby providing a versatile platform to study such transport processes under precisely controllable conditions. Here, we realize an energy-tunable single-atom collider by transporting individual cesium atoms at controlled velocity through an ultracold rubidium bath. The constant lattice velocity sets the directed contribution to the collision-energy distribution, while the lattice depth provides a tunable energy threshold for collision-induced transport disruption. By independently varying these parameters together with bath density and temperature, we separate the number of collision events from their probability to disrupt transport. Across a regime with only a few expected collisions per passage, the inferred single-collision ejection probability rises from small values to near unity as the collision energy exceeds the lattice confinement scale. The experiment thus converts microscopic collisional energy transfer into a binary single-atom observable and provides a controlled link between individual scattering events and emergent dissipative transport.

articles.title: Continuous tuning of quantum critical behavior in hybrid Josephson junction arrays
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report finite-temperature scaling of voltage-driven quantum phase transitions in hybrid Josephson junction arrays. A dual-gate geometry separately tunes interisland coupling and proximity-induced superconductivity, providing access to superconducting, insulating, and metallic transport regimes. The critical resistivity and scaling exponent evolve continuously with electrostatic tuning. Where the three regimes converge, the critical resistivity approaches h/4e², consistent with the self-dual limit, while the scaling exponent approaches the quantum-percolation estimate. Tuning toward stronger insulating behavior raises the critical resistivity and shifts the scaling exponent toward the classical-percolation value, while both parameters decrease toward the metallic regime. These results connect scaling regimes previously reported in different two-dimensional superconducting systems through continuous electrostatic control.

articles.title: Cubic-Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te optical modes across the phonon and phonon-polariton regimes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40157v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alloying offers a convenient route to tune the physical properties of semiconductors, at the price, however, of local lattice/bond distortions needed to accommodate the lattice mismatch. Being nearly lattice-matched and moreover highly resistant to lattice and bond distortions thanks to a largely covalent bonding, cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te sets a benchmark to test the sensitivity of lattice vibrations to minimum lattice and bond distortions induced by alloying. We explore experimentally the two transverse optical regimes of cubic Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te (x<0.7), with ab initio calculations in support: (1) the phonon-polariton regime at quasi-infinite (photon-like) wavelengths averaging over the alloy disorder, probed by forward-Raman scattering, and (2) the purely-mechanical phonon regime down to minimum wavelengths nearly matching the lattice constant zooming into the alloy disorder, achieved by inelastic neutron scattering. The short Zn-Te bond is found to exhibit a compact optical duo distinguishing homo from hetero local bond environments (1 bond: 2 mode), as explained by the percolation model. This deviates from the historical Zn(1-x)Mn(x)Te MREI (modified-random-element-isodisplacement) scheme inspired from classical Raman and infrared studies, in which the optical modes are blind to the bond environment (1-bond: 1-mode). So, the test is positive, reinforcing the status of the percolation scheme as a robust decryptor of (even small) lattice distortions induced by alloying through the lattice dynamics.

articles.title: Topological Quantum Spin Liquids in a Ladder with Majorana fermions and p-wave Superconductivity
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40297v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we address the possibility of topological quantum spin liquids with only short-range (spin) correlations in the whole phase diagram in a ladder system, through an exactly solvable model which represents a generalization of the two-dimensional Kitaev honeycomb spin model to a ribbon geometry. This system gives rise to Z₂ gauge fields emerging in a static way in the ground state through Majorana fermions which then produce either 0 or π flux. Through a quantum field theory perspective, mathematical and Density Matrix Renormalization Group results, we present our progress on the geometrical, topological and physical classification of this model through observables navigating on the whole phase diagram presenting three spin-liquid phases with a spin gap and a metallic phase in the sense of Majorana fermions. We propose a bulk-edge correspondence revealing the presence of protected zero-energy Majorana fermions at the edge in the phases with a gap and revealing also the presence of itinerant Majorana fermions in the bulk in the topological liquid phase. The proposed approach allows us to distinguish between properties of the brickwall ladder giving rise to a special line and those of the square ladder allowing for the gapless Majorana liquid phase. This model gives some hope on finding solutions for topological quantum spin models, e.g. with π flux, on a square lattice geometry. This approach also allows for a correspondence onto models of topological superconductivity.

articles.title: Transport in spinful non-Hermitian gauge lattices
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40317v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the generalized transfer-matrix method introduced in [H. Ghaemi-Dizicheh, Phys. Rev. B 107, 125155 (2023)] to one-dimensional spinful non-Hermitian tight-binding lattices with matrix-valued Abelian and non-Abelian gauge couplings. We derive a minimal channel-resolved transfer matrix and identify its eigenvalues with the generalized Bloch factors. The same transfer matrix determines the periodic- and open-boundary spectra, generalized Brillouin zone, skin localization, and finite-sample scattering conditions. In the Abelian limit, the model separates into fixed spin sectors, yielding exact spectral results and closed finite-length transport expressions in terms of Chebyshev polynomials. These results reveal bipolar spin-dependent skin localization and distinguish the reciprocal hopping scale, which governs poles, zeros, and reflectionlessness, from the directed-amplification factor controlling transmission asymmetry, transparency, and invisibility. For non-Abelian gauge fields, noncommuting link matrices coherently mix the spin sectors, such that four transfer eigenmodes jointly determine the non-Bloch spectrum and transport eigenchannels. We show that this mixing produces spin-hybridized lasing and coherent-perfect-absorption channels, Zeeman-tunable lasing thresholds, and direction-dependent reflectionless transport accompanied by pronounced spin conversion. The resulting boundary-condition criteria describe lasing, coherent perfect absorption, reflectionlessness, transparency, and invisibility, while identifying spin polarization and conversion as experimentally accessible signatures that distinguish Abelian from non-Abelian non-Hermitian transport.

articles.title: Multidimensional revival dynamics in a bosonic many-body system
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The collapse and revival of localized states in many-body systems is a quintessential example of a quantum interference phenomenon that cannot be explained purely within mean-field theories. Historically, the majority of previous work on quantum revivals has been in a Schrödinger mechanics context, typically for effectively 1D systems with a focus on the autocorrelation function as the key detection observable. The general revival subject acquires a far greater complexity in the bosonic many-body context that offers a larger variety of observables and intrinsically implies high dimensionality. Here, the focus is on the simplest nontrivial (i.e., not 1D) bosonic many-body system, namely a symmetric two-site Bose-Hubbard model. The non-equilibrium situation of a coherent initial state prepared on one of the two sites of this integrable 2D system in the strongly self-trapping regime is considered. The revival behaviors emerging from the resulting dynamics within expectation values, coherences, and the autocorrelation function are theoretically derived, and the entanglement behavior is illustrated. Several new features, unknown so far in the Schrödinger context and identified here in terms of five ``puzzles'', are encountered and discussed, among them, a synchronized resurgence behavior, differing revivals times depending on the specific observable, and a manifestation of a precession that appears in the underlying mean field dynamics. These new phenomena can be entirely understood through a comprehensive semiclassical theory, building upon the underlying classical (mean-field) phase-space structure. A quantitative comparison of the latter with semiclassical predictions and quantum perturbative calculations yields an overall excellent agreement and confirms that a full semiclassical theory is pivotal for the understanding of these genuinely quantum many-body interference phenomena.

articles.title: Static dipolar impurity in a Fermi gas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a static dipolar impurity immersed in a Fermi gas and show how dipolar interactions shape both the few-body scattering properties and the resulting polaron physics. Using Fumi's theorem, we connect the anisotropic phase shifts directly to the ground-state energy, and compute the exact impurity spectrum via the functional determinant approach. The resulting spectrum is a convolution of independent even- and odd-wave contributions, giving rise to a ground state with simultaneously occupied even- and odd-wave bound states whose separation is tunable via the dipole length. A variational ansatz limited to one particle-hole excitation fails to capture this doubly occupied ground state. We further find that long-range dipolar interactions weaken Anderson's orthogonality catastrophe, reducing the power-law decay of the quasiparticle weight. These effects can be tested with ultracold polar molecules, where microwave shielding and independent tunability of interactions enable experimental access to the predicted regimes.

articles.title: Chiral p-Wave Superconductivity Proximate to a Fractional Chern Insulator and a Topological Charge Density Wave in a Moiré Chern Band
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a spin-polarized moiré Chern band of twisted MoTe₂ with short-range repulsion, finding superconductivity proximate to a fractional Chern insulator at filling ν=2/3 and a topological charge density wave at ν=3/4. Exact diagonalization reveals pair binding over 0.7lesssimνlesssim0.77, consistent with experiment, along with finite superfluid stiffness, chiral p-wave pairing correlations, and adiabatic connectivity to an attractive model. At weak repulsion, Kohn-Luttinger theory supports a Fermi-surface instability with the same pairing symmetry. The superconducting state has a Bogoliubov-de Gennes Chern number CBdG=-1, opposite to the normal-state Chern number at ν=1. Our results reveal interplay among superconductivity, fractional topology, and charge order.

articles.title: High-throughput quantification of interfacial protein load in monodisperse oil-in-water emulsions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40506v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Food proteins play a critical role as emulsifiers, where adsorption at the oil and water interface governs emulsion formation and stability. However, quantitative characterization of interfacial protein load remains challenging due to polydispersity in conventional emulsification methods. We combine microfluidic generation of monodisperse emulsions with colorimetric protein quantification to measure the post-collection initial interfacial load (Γ₀) and subsequently monitored over 48 h to obtain the saturation load (Γ_infty). Interfacial load exhibited a strong bulk concentration-dependent trend and was well described by a pseudo-first-order model. Both Γ₀ and Γ_infty followed sublinear scaling with concentration (Γ₀ ~ C⁰.²¹, Γ_infty ~ C⁰.¹²). Interfacial loads were largely independent of droplet diameter, with modest reductions in initial loading for the smallest droplets at low protein concentration.
