The main known dimension-free result concerns the randomized midpoint discretization in Wasserstein-2 distance (Liu et al.,2023), while dimension-independent guarantees for ULD discretizations in KL divergence have remained open. We close this gap by proving the first dimension-free KL divergence bounds for discretized ULD. Our analysis refines the KL local error framework (Altschuler et al., 2025) to a dimension-free setting and yields bounds that depend on tr(H), where H upper bounds the Hessian of V, rather than on d. As a consequence, we obtain improved iteration complexity for underdamped Langevin Monte Carlo relative to overdamped Langevin methods in regimes where tr(H)ll d.

articles.title: SciGame: Let Agents Play the Scientific Discovery Games in the Real and Counterfactual World
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly used for scientific discovery. However, existing benchmarks mix law inference with programming, score data fitting instead of prediction on unseen inputs, and do not separate empirical evidence from pretrained priors. We introduce SciGame, a controlled benchmark that converts scientific literature into structured scientific cards. Each card yields a pair of Original and dimensionally consistent Counterfactual environments with the same task interface. SciGame contains a Historical collection of canonical laws and a live Temporal collection curated from papers published after model knowledge cutoffs. It evaluates agents in candidate-guided Identification and open-ended Discovery settings. Each setting runs under Prior-only, Fixed, and Adaptive protocols. Experiments on five frontier models yield three findings. First, familiar priors hurt performance once the governing relation is altered. Second, adaptive experimentation helps the strongest models but harms weaker ones under limited budgets. Third, good explanations can hide quantitative failures. Recovering the exact symbolic form remains the main bottleneck, even when agents interpret evidence correctly. Current agents can investigate systems actively, but inducing exact laws in unfamiliar settings remains an open challenge.

articles.title: GAUSS: A Workload-Aware Analytical and Monte-Carlo Simulator for LLM Inference Serving
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference has become an operational workload that fleets must provision, monitor, and bill against latency service-level objectives (SLOs). A single throughput number cannot answer the questions operators actually face, because generative serving couples two phases with very different service characteristics, continuous batching reshapes the effective service process, and user-visible tail latency can degrade long before aggregate throughput saturates. We present GAUSS, a workload-aware analytical and Monte-Carlo simulator that predicts the full distributions of time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-between-tokens (TBT), together with the sustainable request rate, for a given workload, engine, and accelerator. GAUSS pairs calibrated, phase-specific latency surfaces for prefill and decode with a Lindley-recurrence model of queueing under stochastic arrivals and estimates performance by ensemble Monte-Carlo sampling rather than by replaying a single trace. This lets GAUSS reason about workloads, routing policies, and hardware that have never been deployed, and to capture the latency tails that trace-driven simulators systematically under-sample. We describe the model and show how it supports operating-point selection, traffic segmentation, and shortest-remaining-processing-time scheduling capacity questions that trace-driven simulators cannot address.

articles.title: Decompose, Don't Expand: Capability-Independent AI Systems by Construction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A recurring design choice in building AI systems is whether, when a task is too hard for a model, to expand the model (make it larger, better-prompted, fine-tuned), or to decompose the task (extract the parts that admit a deterministic solution to a host, leaving the model only the irreducibly fuzzy residue). We make three claims. First, that many tasks commonly delegated whole to a model are in fact deterministic tasks with a small generative core. Second, and our central empirical result, that decomposing such a task yields a measurable and desirable property we call parity by construction: on the extracted sub-tasks the model-size performance curve becomes flat, because no model performs them at all. We measure this across nine models spanning a 494M-parameter local checkpoint to a frontier Opus-class model, a thirty-fold parameter range on the local family alone: once the host resolves the context, operation selection scores identically for all nine models and selector resolution for eight of nine, while the one task that does not decompose, labelling, remains sloped across the same range. Because the task leaves the model, a stock checkpoint suffices: no task-specific training and no fine-tuning. Third, that this is a general design discipline, not a domain trick: we show the same move recurring across physics setup, motion retargeting, and object-model editing, and in a Web-CLI tool family (same author, so not an independent replication). We give a method for locating the cut, the construction that makes a cut exist (a deterministic surface and a closed grammar over it), and a way to make the residue safe (resolve the deterministic context; verify the generative output), position the work against neuro-symbolic AI, tool-augmented language models, and generate-and-verify approaches, and are explicit about what is measured (one domain) versus illustrative (the rest).

articles.title: Prototype-Guided Dynamic Domain Modulation and a Large-Scale Multi-SKU Benchmark for Shampoo Bottle Surface Defect Detection
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38194v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Industrial shampoo-bottle surface defect detection must operate across many stock keeping units (SKUs), where differences in bottle geometry, material, label layout, reflectance, and imaging conditions can substantially alter the appearance of the same defect. Existing industrial defect datasets rarely provide both instance-level defect annotations and product-variant identities, making it difficult to study SKU-aware detection under realistic manufacturing conditions. We introduce Bottle-SKU, a large-scale multi-SKU benchmark for shampoo bottle surface defect detection. Bottle-SKU contains 13,119 images, 20,419 instance-level bounding boxes, seven defect categories, and 48 bottle SKUs, enabling evaluation of both shared defect recognition and SKU-specific appearance variation. To address the challenge of SKU-specific appearance variation, we propose Prototype-Guided Dynamic Domain Modulation (ProDMM). ProDMM constructs a visual prototype for each SKU from training images and predicts a soft SKU distribution for each input. The resulting prototype-conditioned representation dynamically generates low-rank Query/Value modulation for the visual backbone and residual conditioning for defect-text-to-visual attention, while preserving the pretrained Grounding DINO detection pathway. The model is trained jointly with detection, SKU-domain classification, and modulation-regularization objectives. Experiments on Bottle-SKU and the public GC10-DET-SKU metallic surface defect dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of prototype-guided domain conditioning for industrial surface defect detection.

articles.title: From Natural Language to Real Schematics: An Automated Workflow for Power Electronics Schematic Synthesis
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38201v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing power electronics converters traditionally requires intensive human expertise across topology sizing, commercial component selection, circuit simulation verification, and schematic drafting. While Large Language Models (LLMs) show promise in electronic design automation (EDA), applying standalone LLMs directly to board-level power electronics schematic synthesis suffers from severe engineering hallucinations, including inaccurate analytical sizing, fabricated or mismatched component part numbers, violated voltage derating margins, and broken topological connectivity. In this paper, we propose a Bounded Dual-Loop Automated Schematic Synthesis Framework that translates natural language specifications into verified, editable KiCad schematics and manufacturing deliverables. Our workflow integrates six stages across three functional columns: (1) requirement parsing and knowledge-driven power stage synthesis covering non-isolated (Buck, Boost) and isolated/resonant (Flyback, DAB, half-bridge LLC) topologies; (2) contract- and evidence-coordinated component selection grounded in distributor APIs and OEM datasheets, coupled with closed-loop ngspice transient verification and stress feedback; and (3) modular control hardware integration and multi-format deliverable generation featuring native KiCad netlist round-trip verification. End-to-end case studies on a 24-36V to 12V,2A Buck converter (29 positions, 83 verified terminals) and an isolated 48V to 24V, 0.5A, Dual-Active Bridge (DAB) converter (87 positions, 341 verified terminals), alongside comparative evaluations against a Vanilla LLM baseline, demonstrate that our framework improves component verification coverage from 22.2 to 98.6, nominal value consistency from 0 to 97.7, and SPICE simulation pass rates from 0 to 100.

articles.title: FACTS-MAS: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Adaptive Forecasting from Heterogeneous Evidence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-world forecasting often requires integrating heterogeneous evidence whose predictive value varies across horizons, operating regimes, and domains. We introduce FACTS-MAS, a domain-agnostic multi-agent forecasting framework that decomposes evidence into specialized channels for temporal dynamics, exogenous context, seasonality, structural information, and discrete events. Each agent generates an independently testable forecast through a common interface, while leakage-safe historical validation measures its predictive skill relative to a naive reference. These skill estimates are used to weight and combine agent forecasts, so that uninformative evidence is either removed or downweighted rather than forced to participate. A calibration procedure selects domain-specific constant means based on historical validation folds. We evaluate FACTS-MAS on weekly for-sale housing inventory from Zillow and weekly unemployment insurance claims from FRED, for 15 U.S. metropolitan areas at 4-, 8-, and 13-week forecasting horizons. Our method outperforms both a naive last-value forecast method and the TimesFM foundation model. However, a factor-adjusted exponential smoothing model performs as well as the fused forecast. The evidence therefore supports FACTS-MAS as a systematic protocol for testing, calibrating, and recomposing evidence channels before assembling them into the strongest single model for a specific application domain. Code, data, and results are available at https://github.com/Madumita24/FACTS-MAS.

articles.title: An Alignment Benchmark for Enterprise Agents on Era by Eon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are widely used in enterprises to access business systems and act on them in pursuit of a goal. However, fulfilling a user's request can cause harm. Era by Eon is a product that creates a digital twin of a company by simulating its business systems and data. Its simulators implement the programming interfaces of real products. Our benchmark uses ten of these systems, including Salesforce, Zendesk, Jira and Slack. We tested whether agents would carry out harmful business requests or trust misleading information in company records. We ran 19 models on 41 tasks three times, for 2,337 runs. Of the 2,304 runs that produced an answer, 918 (40%) contained a violation. The most common were false claims about actions or records (290 runs), following planted instructions (266) and disclosing sensitive data to the wrong audience (249). Every attempted change was recorded and blocked before it took effect. Misleading Slack messages caused 16 models to report an incorrect ticket status in 47 of 57 runs. No model was free of violations. The four best models violated in 22 to 24% of their runs. Yet one of them, Nova Pro, did the task correctly in only 30 runs.

articles.title: Auditable Belief Updates as a Missing Safety Layer for LLM-Powered Multi-Agent Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.38869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly being used as cognitive interfaces that shape how users interpret evidence, communicate, and make decisions. As deployed systems become more multimodal, tool-using, and multi-agent, safety failures no longer arise only from isolated harmful outputs, but also from how agents update, store, and propagate epistemic commitments across retrieval, memory, tools, and peer communication. In this paper, we define belief as an engineering abstraction for evidence-based commitments that guide downstream action. Building on this view, we propose the Explicit Belief Multi-Agent System (EB-MAS), which externalizes belief states into a structured substrate, uses belief operators to propose candidate updates, and applies a Cognitive Firewall to bound or reject updates that are weakly evidenced but strongly driven by vulnerability cues. We also discuss the risk of group belief at the group level, including manufactured consensus, collusion, and cascading misinformation, and outline practical integration challenges around grounding, false positives, scalability, and ethical misuse. Therefore, scalable agent safety requires not only better output filtering or stronger base models, but also explicit interfaces for tracing, calibrating, and constraining belief revision at runtime.

articles.title: FIRME: Registry-Anchored Memory Graphs for Evolving, Heterogeneous Investor Knowledge
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Financial AI workflows that reuse investor knowledge need persistent memory that integrates observations across sources and periods without losing identity or provenance. In a knowledge graph, recurring observations may use different surface forms, fragmenting relationship histories and preventing evidence from accumulating. We introduce Fusion and Identity Registry for Memory Evolution (FIRME), a registry-anchored memory graph that reconciles incoming observations to persistent canonical relationships and retains their source, time, and context. Within periods, rule-based fusion links investor-call discussions to portfolio cash-flow signals, directly or through a fixed product-topic ontology. Across periods, canonical identities and persistent aliases direct recurring observations to the same relationship history; deterministic updates summarize reinforcement, inactivity, and reactivation. We evaluate FIRME on proprietary investor-call and cash-flow records and on S&P 500 earnings-call transcripts. Compared with a historical registry that retains canonical identities and semantic fallback but omits alias memory, FIRME increases final-period Correct Match Rate by 7.8-12.1 percentage points across four dataset-backend settings under a fixed-judge and fallback-review protocol. A blinded human audit of 200 incoming observations per setting finds Correct Match Rate gains of 9.0-16.5 points and reattachment-recall gains of 22.5-29.0 points, with higher observed merge precision in all four samples. A separate audit finds valid evidence paths for 293 of 300 outputs from full within-period fusion in the investor-call setting. Extraction-faithfulness and round-trip diagnostics assess source grounding and preservation of extractor-derived graph content.

articles.title: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An autonomous research laboratory could conduct an entire study, from formulating questions to preparing manuscripts. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers one route towards this goal. Recent AI systems take on several research roles, but may draw conclusions that the evidence does not support. Here, we present an autonomous research laboratory in which agents based on large language models assess one another's work and can stop or redirect investigations. They can generate and reject research questions, require separate theoretical checks and conduct experiments designed to challenge their claims. We demonstrate these capabilities by investigating ensembles of quantum spins in diamond. The agents derived the minimum number of calibration settings needed to predict responses to a defined family of microwave pulse sequences. They checked the result computationally and designed experiments to distinguish competing predictions. An initial experiment agreed with the theoretical predictions, but repeated reference measurements showed that the signal was drifting during data collection. The agents therefore treated the result as inconclusive and revised the measurement protocol without relaxing the acceptance criteria. The revised experiment met those criteria and supported the theoretical predictions. This study demonstrates that collaborating AI agents can select research questions, derive theoretical results and test their predictions experimentally.

articles.title: Where Planning Changes the Outcome of Orbital Games
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper introduces OrbitalGym, a simulation environment for studying when planning algorithms or system design determine the outcome of adversarial orbital encounters. In an orbital game, two non-cooperative teams of satellites maneuver during rendezvous and proximity operations to win a differential-reward objective. Advances in terrestrial game playing have prompted many methods for orbital games, but studies typically evaluate one method in one scenario, often against a passive or random defender. It is unclear whether better planning matters once vehicle capability (maneuverability, sensing, communications) and adversarial responses are considered. OrbitalGym is a JAX-based environment supporting varying numbers of agents, state representations (position, velocity, attitude, fuel), explicit or implicit communication, and proximity or conical field-of-view sensors. It compiles games to batched GPU code, enabling large-scale parallel simulation of policies across many configurations. This identifies regimes where policy choice affects outcomes and regimes where system capability dominates. We study two close-range games: pursuit-evasion, where one spacecraft tries to capture another, and lady-bandit-guard, where a guard prevents an attacker from reaching a protected asset. We compare PD, LQR, model predictive path integral control, and Monte Carlo tree search over ratios of thrust and propellant, initial separation, game duration, sensor capability, and the definition of capture. In pursuit-evasion the propellant ratio decides most encounters: against five of six evader policies, pursuer policy changes capture probability by 10 percent or more in at most 15 of 90 capability configurations. In lady-bandit-guard, policy matters more: against bandits able to reach the asset, a better guard policy raises defense probability by at least 10 percent in 56 to 74 of 90 configurations.

articles.title: One Confidence Threshold, Unequal Coverage: Language Gaps in Typed Decision Interfaces and How Translating Inputs Reduces Them
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37688v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deployed classifiers often act on a prediction only when its confidence clears a threshold and pass the rest to a person. We ask whether one threshold serves all languages equally on typed decision interfaces, APIs that return a probability for each option of a fixed multiple-choice question. In a confirmatory study with a written analysis plan, three vendors' interfaces classified 1,000 MASSIVE items, each in 51 languages, with a threshold of 0.9. Even when a request is answered correctly in both English and another language, the English version clears the threshold more often, by 8.6-11.7 percentage points on average. Observed coverage, the share of requests handled automatically, is lower than English's in every other language, while the requests the gate handles are rarely wrong. The gap remains when every language is reweighted to the same accuracy, and a standard calibration metric (ECE) does not detect it on one interface. In exploratory analyses, English's coverage stays higher when each language gets its own threshold fitted to the same 5% error target. Translating inputs into English nearly closes the gap at 0.9 but leaves English ahead at that error target. Requests written natively in African languages show a gap in the same direction when English is their human translation. We recommend reporting per-language coverage at the operating threshold.

articles.title: Cassette-Editor: A Video Editing Agent That Edits the Way You Do
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37690v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language agents increasingly work by calling tools on a persistent artifact, such as a code repository, and the result of each call shapes their next step. Video editing is a demanding case of this pattern: what a frame shows depends on how every clip is trimmed, retimed, cropped, and nested, so knowledge about the footage holds only for particular uses of it, and an invalid edit can leave the timeline structurally broken. Existing video editing agents keep their edits valid with critic agents, reviewers, or restricted output formats. We present Cassette-Editor, a video editing agent with a deliberately simple interface: one tool reads the project and one tool writes to it. Every write passes through the same executor, rules, and commit service as the user's manual edits, and either commits atomically or is rejected with located diagnostics and repair options, while the model keeps the creative choices and decides how to recover. Reads relate stored analysis of the footage to each use of it on the timeline. In a controlled experiment, a real model is shown 277 of its own committed edits after damaging them. It corrected nearly every call with full or minimal feedback, but locating each problem cut the input tokens a correction needed to less than half, and its corrections dropped other values the model had written in one case rather than seven.

articles.title: FVH-Bench: Evaluating Image Generator Safety Beyond Overtly Harmful Imagery
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37722v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern image generators can produce complex visual artifacts, including diagrams, interfaces, and records that combine text, graphics, and layout to convey detailed information. They may refuse requests for overtly harmful imagery yet still generate artifacts that guide dangerous actions or support deception. We call the risk arising from what such images enable, rather than only what they depict, functional visual harm (FVH). Existing safety benchmarks focus largely on overtly harmful content, such as pornography and graphic violence, leaving image generators' safety alignment against FVH insufficiently evaluated. To address this gap, we introduce FVH-Bench, comprising 669 prompts across five harmful visual functions and ten risk domains. The 11 evaluated image generators rarely refuse these requests and frequently generate artifacts that fulfill the targeted harmful functions. High scores for target harm realization and harmful artifact usability further indicate that these outputs can support the intended harmful purposes. A further analysis finds that existing safety detectors also provide limited coverage of FVH, indicating gaps in their ability to recognize harmful visual functions. Together, these findings show that evaluating image-generator safety alignment requires considering not only what images depict, but also what they may enable.

articles.title: Poisoned Skills: Propagating Jailbreaks Through Agent Markdown Files
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37738v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern agent frameworks allow users to provide Markdown files containing system prompts, tool descriptions, and skill definitions (e.g., SKILL.md), which are incorporated into the agent's context during initialization. In this work, we investigate whether this configuration mechanism can also serve as an injection channel: can a jailbreak embedded in a Markdown skill file propagate through an agent and induce prohibited behavior? To answer this question, we construct a LangChain-based question-answering agent whose system prompt is assembled from a user-provided Markdown file. We embed a jailbreak combining persona manipulation with a GPTFUZZER-based attack and evaluate its effectiveness across seven contemporary open-weight models using 270 forbidden questions spanning nine harm categories. Under a benign system prompt, the models exhibit near-complete refusal behavior, with a mean attack success rate (ASR) of just 0.5%. In contrast, the injected skill file raises the mean ASR to 45%, reaching 68.9% for individual models. We further evaluate two payload obfuscation strategies: an invisible zero-width character-based stealth payload and a phonetic payload based on grapheme-to-phoneme transformations. Neither outperforms the plain-text injection; notably, the phonetic variant reduces mean ASR to 30%. These findings identify Markdown skill files as an underexplored attack surface for AI agents and suggest that vulnerability to configuration-based jailbreaks depends more strongly on the underlying model than on the specific payload obfuscation technique.

articles.title: From Envy to Aspiration: How Travel Influencer Characteristics Shape Travel Aspiration Through Benign and Malicious Envy?
articles.abstract: Social media travel influencers have emerged as powerful catalysts of travel aspiration, yet the emotional mechanisms connecting influencer characteristics to audience aspiration remain underexplored. Drawing on Social Comparison Theory and Dual Envy Theory, this study proposes and tests an integrated framework in which attractiveness, popularity, and perceived similarity shape travel aspiration through the parallel mediating pathways of benign and malicious envy. Data were collected from 311 followers of travel influencers and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results reveal that influencer popularity is the strongest direct predictor of travel aspiration, while perceived similarity is the strongest antecedent of benign envy. Benign envy significantly and consistently mediates the relationships between all three influencer characteristics and travel aspiration through complementary partial mediation. Contrary to theoretical expectations, influencer attractiveness does not significantly predict malicious envy, and malicious envy exerts no significant influence on travel aspiration, nor does it mediate any relationship. These findings reveal a meaningful asymmetry between the two envy pathways, demonstrating that not all envy translates into behavioral outcomes. The study extends Social Comparison Theory and Dual Envy Theory to the travel influencer domain and offers actionable guidance for destination marketers and influencer strategy practitioners on designing relatability-driven content that activates aspirational emotional responses.

articles.title: Does Citizen Science Reach the Citizen? Exploring the Science–Society Interface Through Scholarly and Societal Attention
articles.abstract: The study applied an Altmetric approach to examine the science-society interface in citizen science research. Bibliographic data were collected from Scopus for 10,285 articles published between 2016 and 2025. Altmetric data corresponding to the 100 most highly cited articles were collected from the Dimensions database. Python was used for various statistical analyses. Spearman’s ρ was computed to assess the association between scientific impact and social influence. Mann-Whitney U test was used to analyze how open access (OA) status affected scholarly and social constructs. The results showed 2017 having the highest number of publications (23) and citations (8,172). Altmetric Attention Score (AAS) was highest in 2018 (5,093). The articles spanned across 73 journals and 57 countries, with the US being the most productive. X was the most prominent among social media platforms. Correlations among citations, AAS, and Mendeley were found to be weak to moderate (ρ = 0.437 for Citation-AAS, ρ = 0.570 for Citation-Mendeley, and ρ = 0.350 for AAS-Mendeley). OA status of articles significantly increased AAS but not citations or Mendeley readership. The relation between scientific impact and societal attention of citizen science research was relatively close, yet enough distinction remained. The results would benefit researchers, journals, funders, and practitioners of citizen science.

articles.title: Scenario-Based Assessment of Thermal Performance, Battery Degradation, and Total Cost of Ownership for EV Battery Thermal Management in Tropical Logistics Operations
articles.abstract: Battery thermal management affects electric-vehicle (EV) battery service life, replacement frequency, lifecycle cost, and the timing of battery entry into end-of-life (EOL) management systems. This study develops a deterministic scenario-based framework for tropical logistics operation by linking prescribed battery-temperature trajectories, state-of-health (SoH) decline, replacement events, and an eight-year total cost of ownership (TCO) model. Passive air cooling, reactive liquid cooling, and predictive pre-cooling are compared under a 28--38~^circC tropical peak-day profile. The respective peak battery temperatures are 51.07, 33.41, and 31.00~^circC, while first-pack 80%-SoH crossing times are 3.43, 5.87, and 10.14 years. Over eight years, the three strategies produce two, one, and zero battery-replacement events, respectively. The resulting TCO values are USD~77,700, USD~72,500, and USD~62,000 per vehicle, giving predictive pre-cooling a 20.21% saving relative to passive air cooling. Predictive pre-cooling also defers two traction-battery EOL entries per vehicle beyond the study horizon. The results indicate that improved thermal management can extend battery service life, reduce replacement-related cost, and slow battery material turnover, although the numerical results remain scenario-based and require experimental validation.

articles.title: Unsteady Surface Pressure Measurements on a Laminar Wing submerged in a Propeller Slipstream
articles.abstract: High-frequency surface pressure measurements on a Natural Laminar Flow (NLF) airfoil submerged in the wake of a propeller were conducted in the Laminar Wind Tunnel (LWT) of the Institute of Aerodynamics and Gas Dynamics (IAG) of the University of Stuttgart. Based on the measured unsteady pressure signals, the laminar-to-turbulent transition on the airfoil is investigated. The resulting data can be used to further understand the interactions between a tractor-propeller and the boundary-layer (BL) flow. By gaining insights into BL-flow behaviour under such conditions, more efficient airplane propulsion and wing designs could become viable. With the aid of high-frequency pressure sensors, it is possible to create a 2-dimensional resolution of the boundary layer state, along the spanwise position behind the traversable propeller and the chord of the airfoil. At certain advance ratios, laminar regimes are recorded reaching up to x/c = 80 %, far beyond the steady chord transition location of the NLF configuration. Depending on the advance ratio, the mean portion of laminar flow still varies in between 35 − 44 %, corresponding to 63 − 81 % of the NLF distance of the steady reference configurations without a propeller installed. This clearly demonstrates the importance of considering the partly laminar boundary-layer flow behaviour on the airfoil, even when submerged in a propeller wake.

articles.title: Hexplorer: A Biomimetic Amphibious Hexapod Robot for Locomotion in Terrestrial and Aquatic Environments
articles.abstract: For locomotion in both terrestrial and aquatic environments, amphibious robots require appendages that can bear loads on land and generate propulsion in water. This paper presents the design and experimental evaluation of Hexplorer, a hexapod robot equipped with six identical leg--fin units that provide a total of twelve actuated degrees of freedom. Each unit combines a vertical prismatic hip with a rotary leg--fin comprising a rigid fan-shaped contact frame and a compliant fin. The mechanical parameters of the leg--fin units are jointly optimized to improve adaptability during terrestrial locomotion. A central pattern generator (CPG)-based gait generation algorithm coordinates the twelve joints and automatically switches between crawling and swimming gaits by changing the gait mapping. In experiments, the robot traveled at 0.0208 m/s on flat indoor ground, 0.0250 m/s on outdoor unstructured ground, 0.1250 m/s at the water surface, and 0.0357 m/s on an underwater substrate. Using the same appendages and actuators, Hexplorer achieves coverage of four locomotion scenarios. JIRS categories: (3) and (6)

articles.title: Embedded True Proportional Navigation Guidance for a High-Dynamic Flight Vehicle: Real-Time MIL--HIL Validation
articles.abstract: Real-time embedded implementation can produce substantial differences between theterminal performance predicted by numerical simulation and that realized by aphysical guidance-and-control processor. This study characterizes that gap througha controlled Model-in-the-Loop (MIL) and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) evaluation ofterminal guidance for a high-dynamic flying vehicle. The two environments use thesame nonlinear six-degree-of-freedom plant, aerodynamic database, actuator model andconstraints, fixed-step plant solver, controller update rate, and paired seededvon Kármán turbulence realizations. True Proportional Navigation Guidance (TPNG)and a gain-scheduled modified PI autopilot with direct angular-rate damping areexecuted on an STM32F429 ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller at 50 Hz, while the nonlinearvehicle and disturbance models are propagated on a real-time target computer. Forthe four investigated disturbance realizations, the MIL configuration yields planarterminal errors of 0.027--0.460 m, whereas the HIL experiments yield137.6--1865.6 m. The embedded guidance-and-control computation requires an averageof 0.356 ms within the 20 ms control interval, corresponding to 1.78% execution-timeoccupancy. Thus, computational overload is excluded as the direct source of theobserved degradation. The results demonstrate that end-to-end implementation effects,including communication, task scheduling, sample alignment, and data representation,must be treated as part of the closed-loop guidance design. The current experimentsquantify their aggregate effect; causal attribution to individual mechanisms requirescontrolled delay and interface-ablation tests.

articles.title: Optical, Spectroscopic and Band-Gap Characterisation of Natural Dyes Extracted from Delonix regia Flower, Curcuma longa (Turmeric) and Their 1:1 Mixture as Photosensitisers for Dye-Sensitised Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Natural dyes are inexpensive, abundant and environmentally benign photosensitisers for third-generation dye-sensitised solar cells (DSSCs), but their light-harvesting behaviour is governed by pigment chemistry, extraction solvent and the mode of anchoring on the semiconductor surface. In this study, natural dyes were extracted from Delonix regia (royal poinciana) flower and Curcuma longa (turmeric), together with a 1:1 (v/v) mixture of the two extracts, using a 50:50 distilled water-methanol solvent, and their optical properties were characterised in solution and after adsorption onto a nanoporous titanium dioxide (TiO₂) film. Ultraviolet-visible-near-infrared (UV-Vis-NIR) spectra recorded from 230 to 1100 nm showed that all three extracts absorbed strongly in the ultraviolet (333 and 375 nm) and visible regions; the D. regia extract additionally exhibited a broad near-infrared band at 764 nm in solution which extended to 1028 nm after adsorption on TiO₂. From the measured absorbance, the absorption coefficient, an absorbance-based extinction parameter and the light-harvesting efficiency (LHE) were derived; the D. regia extract sustained an LHE of approximately 99% over 305–541 nm. Optical band gaps obtained from Tauc analysis, assuming a direct allowed transition, were 2.02 eV for D. regia, 1.98 eV for turmeric and 2.35 eV for the mixture. The results indicate that D. regia is the most promising single sensitiser of the three and that the 1:1 mixture is optically superior to the single turmeric extract, although co-pigmentation redistributes rather than simply superimposes the component bands. The dataset provides the optical baseline required for rational sensitiser selection and co-sensitisation.

articles.title: Memory-Driven Pattern Selection in Fractional Reaction--Diffusion Models of Metamorphic Rocks
articles.abstract: This study models striped and orbicular patterns in metamorphic rocks using a Caputo time-fractional Gray--Scott reaction--diffusion system. Simulations for (αin0.99,0.95,0.90,0.85) and six mafic diffusivities ((Dᵤ₀in{1×10⁻⁴,4×10⁻⁴,5×10⁻⁴,6×10⁻⁴,8×10⁻⁴,1×10⁻³})) reveal a spot-to-stripe transition, with lower (α) producing more diffuse patterns. Stability analysis at (α=0.85) gives a Matignon angle of (76.5^circ), Turing instability for (μin[0.0597,0.1003]), critical wavenumber (k_c=17.77), and dimensionless wavelength (λ=0.3535). A parameter scan over 800 values of (μ) identifies 456 equilibria, of which 160 are linearly stable and 66 satisfy the fractional Turing condition. At the representative value (μ=0.05971), the homogeneous steady state is ((u^*,v^*)=(0.546024,29.814209)). Convergence tests at (α=0.95) confirm second-order spatial accuracy, with grid-refinement (L²) errors (5.85×10⁻⁵), (1.42×10⁻⁵), and (6.26×10⁻⁶), and L1 temporal accuracy with time-step errors (7.18×10⁻⁶), (4.74×10⁻⁶), and (2.39×10⁻⁶). The Lyapunov functional decays monotonically and (Λ=0.032603>0), confirming dissipativity. The model qualitatively reproduces the four interface morphologies reported from the Chotanagpur Granite Gneissic Complex, India, and is presented as a complementary framework to thermodynamically based geophysical models for memory-driven transport in metamorphic rocks.

articles.title: Voltage-Dependent Dielectrophoretic Response of Bacterial Cells: Implications for Reliable Cell Manipulation
articles.abstract: Rapid bacterial detection is important for environmental monitoring, particularly for identifying microbial contamination in water resources. Dielectrophoresis (DEP) provides a label-free approach for bacterial detection by exploiting differences in cellular dielectric properties. Our previous studies established bacterial movement velocity, force, and crossover frequency as quantitative parameters toward the development of a DEP-based detection platform. However, optimization of the operating conditions is necessary to ensure reliable measurement. During voltage optimization, unexpected positive DEP (pDEP) was observed at low frequencies where negative DEP (nDEP) was expected, particularly at 20 Vpp. This study therefore investigated whether applied voltage affects bacterial viability and membrane integrity during DEP experiment. Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus (pH 7), were exposed to 3–20 Vpp at 50 kHz, followed by pDEP quantification, colony-forming unit (CFU) analysis, Live/Dead fluorescence staining, and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Despite increasing pDEP occurrence at higher voltages, CFU analysis showed no significant differences in culturability (p > 0.05). In contrast, fluorescence and TEM analyses revealed voltage-dependent changes in membrane integrity and structure. These findings indicate that DEP exposure can induce sublethal membrane perturbation sufficient to alter bacterial dielectric response without measurable loss of culturability. Appropriate voltage selection is therefore critical for preserving measurement reliability in DEP-based bacterial detection and its future application to environmental monitoring.

articles.title: Knowledge-Guided Probabilistic Forecasting of Urban Land-Surface Temperature in Three Moroccan Cities
articles.abstract: Urban heat forecasting is important for climate adaptation, yet reliable multi-city prediction remains diffcult because short-term meteorology interacts with persis- tent urban form, this study evaluates a knowledge-guided probabilistic framework for next-day land surface temperature (LST) forecasting in Casablanca, Mar-rakech, and Tangier, a seven-day dynamic sequence and six static descriptors feed a heteroscedastic recurrent baseline, while a matched-seed warm-start resid- ual introduces prescribed directional contributions for built-up, impervious, and vegetation fractions. A sentinel-clean audit retained 365,500 valid daily targets from 440 verified cells and reproduced 24,902 canonical forecasting sequences, the point benchmark evaluates six models over five seeds on identical train, valida- tion, and test target sets (14,917/4,008/5,977), using minimum validation RMSE for checkpoint selection, the probabilistic dynamic+static baseline achieved the lowest mean test RMSE and MAE, 2.998 ± 0.043 and 2.313 ± 0.017◦ C; the proposed model ranked second in RMSE and third in MAE at 3.034±0.119 and 2.349±0.090◦ C, in the separately preserved validation-Gaussian-NLL-selected paired analysis, the 95% moving-block-bootstrap intervals for RMSE and Gaus- sian NLL included zero, whereas MAE favored the baseline by 0.0336◦ C. The structured mean residual nevertheless satisfies the prescribed directions exactly and raises complete-predictor consistency by 7.6, 10.4, and 24.7 percent- age points for built-up, impervious, and vegetation responses at the primary perturbation, calibration and hot-tail analyses do not show an overall uncertainty advantage, and transfer to an unseen city is mixed. The contribution is therefore a reproducible accuracy–physical-consistency trade-off within a probabilistic forecasting pipeline rather than a claim of predictive or uncertainty superiority.

articles.title: II. Micronutrients, pH, and Eh variations in the rhizosphere of two maize genotypes
articles.abstract: Soil-root interface (rhizosphere) is the unavoidable link in the transfer of nutrients from soil to plant. Field measurements of two maize genotypes (Zea mays L., cv. Pioneer-3732 and − 3737) have shown differences in plant nutrient uptake which appeared to be accentuated in eroded calcareous soils. Rhizotron studies were conducted to: (1) determine the effect of soil CaCO3 on plant micronutrients (Cu, Fe, Mn, and Zn) availability in the rhizosphere; and (2) characterize the rhizosphere properties of these two maize genotypes. Maize seedlings were transferred to rhizotrons containing the Ap horizon of clay loam soils with low (5 g kg− 1) or high (204 g kg− 1) levels of CaCO3. Rhizophere pH, Eh, and CO2 were monitored with pH-glass, platinum, and ρCO2 microelectrodes. At the six-leaf stage, the soil was thin-sectioned at 1-, 2-, and 3-mm distances from the root. The soluble soil ions and plant nutrient uptakes were determined. Higher Mn2+ and Fe2+ concentrations were found in the rhizosphere of P-3737 relative to P-3732. Higher Mn2+, Cu2+, and Zn2+ uptake for Pioneer-3737 were observed in the high CaCO3 soil relative to Pioneer-3732. The plant shoot/root ratio was reduced by 21.4% for P-3732 while increased by 15.7% for P-3737 in the calcareous soil compared to those in the non-calcareous soil. The rhizosphere pH, Eh and ρCO2 differences correlated to nutrient uptake and were dependent on plant genotype in addition to bulk soil concentration. As rhizosphere physicochemical properties differ from bulk soil, bulk soil micronutrients values do not reliably indicate plant nutrient availability. 248 words

articles.title: Observation of Excess Benzene in Post-Fire Crude Oil and Risk Communication Implications
articles.abstract: This investigation examines whether benzene in heat-affected crude oil declines as a volatility-only model would predict after tank-fire extinguishment with fluorine-free foam (F3). Among BTEX compounds, benzene has the highest vapor pressure and the lowest molecular weight and boiling point; it should therefore be depleted from the surface layer at least as fast as toluene, ethylbenzene, and the xylenes (TEX), and faster if evaporative loss dominates. Liquid samples were collected from the top 12 in. (30 cm) of a 2.4 m diameter × 2.19 m high test tank before burning and after repeated F3-extinguished burns. Aliquots were aerated in a closed vapor chamber and the headspace was analyzed as whole air. That assay characterizes an enriched source profile; the reported concentrations are not outdoor or breathing-zone exposures. Absolute benzene in the chamber headspace declined (81 ppmv in the single fresh-oil sample versus a post-burn mean of 31 ppmv), but TEX declined far more (for example, toluene from 680 ppmv to a post-burn mean of 26.5 ppmv). Benzene’s share of ΣBTEX vapor therefore rose from about 5% before burning to about 43% after burning (about 60% in overnight mixed-oil samples). A volatility-only account does not explain that pattern. A source term is required: conversion of precursors in the hot zone (thermal or steam-related cracking) and/or resupply of benzene from the cooler bulk liquid. Distinguishing those mechanisms is outside the scope of this observational study. The practical implication is that post-fire crude oil in deep tanks should not be assumed to have been stripped of benzene the way thin-film in situ burns are, and risk communication for responders should treat the residual liquid as a continuing benzene source.

articles.title: GeoAI Platform for Natural Language Exploration of Multidimensional Flood Risk Scenarios
articles.abstract: While many coastal jurisdictions increasingly use flood models that incorporate future climate change projections, floodplain managers, planners and community organizers frequently need to answer questions that draw on multiple data sources and model outputs. A single compound planning question requires stitching together results from inundation outputs, infrastructure records, and so- cioeconomic datasets that currently live in disconnected silos. The need for complex workflows and specialized tooling constrains the questions practitioners can ask and the speed with which they can get the results. This paper presents a geospatial AI platform that addresses this gap through three architectural contributions: (i) A multidimensional scenario store that organizes 141 flood scenarios within a single queryable structure along with other physical and socioeconomic datasets; (ii) A deterministic tool-routed LLM agent that maps compound natural language queries into geospatial tool calls; and (iii) A bidirectional map-chat interface that preserves spatial grounding throughout the analytical workflow.

articles.title: A new perspective on the stratospheric polar vortex, sudden warmings and the ENSO modulation
articles.abstract: Circulation anomalies in the stratosphere, and particularly sudden stratospheric warmings (SSWs), have a strong impact on climate predictability at subseasonal-to-seasonal timescales. Understanding the effects of El Niño-Southern Oscillation on the occurrence and typology of SSWs remains a challenge. Here, we re-diagnose the three-dimensional structure of the stratospheric polar vortex by analysing relative vorticity – the local spinning motion of the flow – and show that it is characterised by strong positive (cyclonic) vorticity over the pole with two regions of maximum rotation that can be traced as two columns down to the troposphere, one over northern Canada and the other over Eurasia. During El Niño, enhanced wave activity over the eastern North Pacific acts as a source of negative (anticyclonic) vorticity in the upper troposphere, weakening the Canadian maximum; hence, the polar vortex appears displaced over Eurasia, favouring displacement-type SSWs. During La Niña, strengthened positive (cyclonic) vorticity over northern Canada, reinforcing the Canadian column of rotation, results in an elongated polar vortex with two well-separated centres of similar amplitude, facilitating split-type SSWs. Our results offer a novel framework for interpreting troposphere-stratosphere interaction and enhancing prediction skill of SSW events.

articles.title: A multifunctional self-assembled monolayer for perovskite lasing diodes
articles.abstract: Perovskite lasing diodes (PeLDs) require charge transport, optical gain, resonant feedback and high-density electrical injection to be integrated within a single thin-film device. Conventional hole transport materials (HTM) can, however, introduce non-radiative recombination and optical loss in nanophotonic cavities. Here we develop RS-3, a self-assembled monolayer that acts as a multifunctional hole-transport contact. The ultrathin RS-3 layer reduces buried-interface loss, increases net modal gain and preserves the periodic profile of the distributed-feedback (DFB) cavity after deposition of the quasi-two-dimensional N2F8 gain layer, enabling us to realize room-temperature current-assisted lasing under synchronized optical–electrical co-injection. RS-3-based light-emitting diodes also show lower turn-on voltage, higher current density and higher luminance than poly(9-vinylcarbazole)-based controls. Under pulsed optical pumping, the complete device lases near 550 nm at a threshold of 28 μJ cm⁻². With synchronized optical–electrical co-injection, the threshold decreases monotonically to 19 μJ cm⁻² as the pulsed current density increases to 1.30 kA cm⁻², with a minimum linewidth of 0.25 nm.

articles.title: A Cost–Benefit–Reliability (CBR) Framework for Additive and Hybrid Manufacturing of Electronic Assemblies
articles.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) processes for metals, polymers, and ceramics are increasingly applied to high-reliability electronic assemblies. These applications require manufacturing routes that meet aggressive size, weight, and power (SWaP) targets while satisfying environmental standards like MIL-STD-810H and MIL-STD-883. This paper proposes a reliability-aware Cost–Benefit–Reliability (CBR) framework to evaluate when additive and hybrid manufacturing provide measurable advantages over conventional methods. A taxonomy of relevant AM technologies is mapped to specific electronic functions and material properties. Decision criteria—including geometric complexity, production volume, lead time, and failure-mode mitigation—are quantified using the CBR model. Four defense-electronics case studies demonstrate quantitative trade-offs in SWaP, cost, and reliability across metal and hybrid workflows. AM-specific failure mechanisms are addressed through design-for-additive-manufacturing (DfAM) guidelines and qualification pathways. A correlation-aware Monte Carlo formulation and global sensitivity analysis show that AM failure rate and nonrecurring engineering (NRE) cost are the dominant drivers of CBR decision uncertainty. The results indicate that additive and hybrid manufacturing are most advantageous for low-volume, high-complexity assemblies, and that process qualification is essential for successful adoption.

articles.title: Fate of Quantum Magic
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39059v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Magic, a quantum resource distinct from entanglement, measures departure from states stabilized by products of Pauli operators. Such stabilizer states can be maximally entangled yet admit efficient classical description: quantum advantage requires magic. We develop a powerful framework to evaluate the degree of magic in generic many-body states. We use it to study the fate of magic under thermal and dynamical evolution. In the transverse field Ising model, we find a thermal sudden death of magic that saturates with system size, and occurs after the death of entanglement. We reach similar conclusions in generic spin chains, and in the Kitaev quantum spin liquid on the honeycomb lattice, where the threshold shows an intricate dependence on subregion shape. We then study how magic equilibrates after a quantum quench. In quenches of generic spin chains, the magic of a subregion typically dies before entanglement, contrary to thermal trajectories. An explanation is given in terms of the geometry of non-magical states. As a third type of trajectory, we examine the fate of magic with separation with an appropriate notion of non-local magic and establish a sudden death. Finally, we show how to experimentally witness a volume law of frame-robust magic in quantum materials by using neutron scattering.

articles.title: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40235v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the three-dimensional chiral Zₚ Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun--Yang--Wang--Tantivasadakarn--Chen are, for every odd prime p, not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. The key ingredient is a new invariant of invertible subalgebras, which we conjecture to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares.

articles.title: Single-Temperature Ranked Greedy Cluster Exchange for Max-Cut on Two-Dimensional Tori
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40515v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ground-state search in two-dimensional Ising spin glasses on large toroidal lattices remains challenging for local-update heuristics because rugged energy barriers impede relaxation across metastable states. Equivalent to zero-field toroidal Max-Cut problems, these spin-glass instances also serve as standard benchmarks for optimization heuristics. Many Monte Carlo approaches combine single-spin flips or cluster moves with temperature ladders or annealing schedules, yet even with tuned parameters, rarely achieve rapid, reliable ground-state convergence at scale. Here, we address the need for faster ground-state search through cooperation between replicas. We introduce ranked greedy cluster exchange (RGCX) and combine it with fixed-temperature Metropolis sweeps to form single-temperature RGCX. Replicas are ranked by cut to determine the pair-processing order. Each pair deterministically exchanges every disagreement cluster that raises the better replica's cut, retaining the complement and conserving the pair's summed cut. On the 20,000-spin Gset instance G81, the estimated runtime to reach the certified optimum with 99% success probability (TTS99) was 12.1 s on an 8-core desktop computer. With the same population size, exchange interval and temperature, the method reached the best known cuts on all 17 toroidal Gset graphs, including 9 certified optima. These findings advance ground-state search on large two-dimensional tori by establishing single-temperature RGCX as an efficient population-based method that combines ranked greedy cluster exchange with fixed-temperature Metropolis dynamics.

articles.title: Toric codes all the way down: decoupling translation-invariant topological CSS codes in higher dimensions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40592v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Topological Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes in more than two spatial dimensions offer features useful for fault-tolerant quantum computation, such as transversal non-Clifford gates and single-shot decoding, but a systematic understanding of them is still lacking. One approach is to decouple a code: map it to a stack of higher-form toric codes by a finite-depth local CSS-preserving Clifford circuit, possibly after adding ancillas. For translation-invariant p-ary CSS codes, where p is prime (p=2 for qubits), we require the circuit to commute with the translations of a superlattice. In two dimensions, such a decoupling exists once these translations act trivially on every anyon type. In higher dimensions, excitations are sorted by their dimension into superselection layers, which can remain glued together even when translations act trivially on each layer. We show that this gluing is the only remaining obstruction: a code can be decoupled on a superlattice exactly when, after coarse-graining to it, translations act trivially on every layer and the gluing vanishes. Moreover, for a code with finitely many excitation types in each layer and m nonzero layers, once translations act trivially on every layer, further coarse-graining by a factor of pm⁻¹ in every direction removes the aforementioned gluing. Physically, the same criterion determines when the code encodes the maximal number of logical qudits on a finite torus. Finally, we give an explicit algorithm that constructs the decoupling as a circuit of SUM (qudit CNOT) and SWAP gates.

articles.title: Entanglement diagnostics of stochastic-resetting steady states: theory and measurement on superconducting qubits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.40638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stochastic resetting drives quantum systems into nonequilibrium stationary states unreachable under uninterrupted unitary evolution, and their entanglement depends on whether the reset history is resolved or averaged over. We study this interplay in the transverse-field Ising chain, deriving closed-form results for two qubits and evaluating chains of up to 12 qubits exactly. In the two-qubit system, these closed-form results show that phase matching between energy eigenstates produces resonances, and their visibility in the stationary state is determined by the symmetry of the reset state. Measurements on an IBM superconducting processor show the entropies evaluated before and after the reset average closely following noiseless predictions with no fitted parameter, while concurrence lies below prediction across most of the hardware measurements. The two diagnostics respond differently because they read different components of the same reconstructed state, and a depolarizing model captures the concurrence suppression with one fitted parameter. The difference between the two entropies, i. e., the Jensen gap of entanglement entropy, equals the Holevo information that a subsystem retains about the time since the last reset. With a Bell-state reset, this information grows with chain length across a half-chain cut over the sizes studied, without visible saturation at the smaller reset probabilities. Since reset times are sampled and recorded classically, the trajectory-averaged entropy, and with it the Jensen gap, is obtained without postselection, in contrast to monitored circuits, where trajectory-resolved entanglement requires sampling exponentially rare measurement records.

articles.title: Giant bubbles of Fisher zeros in the quantum XY chain
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.05899v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We demonstrate an alternative approach based on a complex-valued inverse temperature and partition function to probe quantum phases of matter with nontrivial spectra and dynamics. It leverages thermofield dynamics (TFD) to quantitatively characterize quantum and thermal fluctuations, and exploit the correspondence between low-energy excitations and Fisher zeros. Using the quantum XY chain in an external field as a testbed, we show that the oscillatory gap behavior manifests as oscillations in the long-time dynamics of the TFD spectral form factor. We also identify giant bubbles, i.e. large-scale closed lines, of Fisher zeros near the gapless XX limit. They provide a characteristic energy scale that seems to contradict the predictions of the low energy theory of a featureless Luttinger liquid. We identify this energy scale and relate the motion of these giant bubbles with varying external field to the transfer of spectral weight from high to low energies. The deep connection between Fisher zeros, dynamics, and excitations opens up promising avenues for understanding the unconventional gap behaviors in strongly correlated many-body systems.

articles.title: TRAILS-MD: Mapping complex conformational landscapes and transition pathways via lightweight lineage-aware adaptive sampling
articles.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are fundamentally limited by the timescale gap between rapid atomic fluctuations and slow, activated conformational transitions. While adaptive sampling accelerates the exploration of metastable states, conventional implementations often obscure the dynamical connectivity between discovered basins, confusing broad configurational coverage with the sampling of physically viable transition pathways. Here, we present a lightweight, engine-agnostic adaptive sampling framework (TRAILS-MD) that iteratively launches short trajectory ensembles across either fixed or on-the-fly machine-learned (ML) collective-variable (CV) spaces. A defining feature of our approach is explicit trajectory lineage preservation, which allows for the rigorous reconstruction of connected pathways from highly parallelized, disjointed exploration stages. We demonstrate the efficacy of this framework across a hierarchy of molecular challenges: overcoming low-dimensional barriers in peptide isomerization, navigating entropic bottlenecks in protein folding (Trp-cage and WW domain), mapping transient exit tunnels during ligand unbinding (HSP90), and exploring large conformational changes in adenylate kinase. Finally, we show how lineage-aware exploratory ensembles can seamlessly seed unbiased production trajectories for the construction of Markov state models (MSMs). By bridging the gap between deep-learning-driven coordinate discovery and strict parent–child trajectory tracking, this framework democratizes advanced data-driven sampling for routine computational biophysics workflows.

articles.title: Ab initio investigation of excited states and absorption spectra of small mercury clusters (Hg 2 – 5 )
articles.abstract: We report a systematic ab initio investigation of the excited states and absorption spectra of small mercury clusters (Hg 2 – 5 ). Benchmarking multi-reference configuration interaction (MR-CISD) and equation-of-motion coupled-cluster (EOM-CCSD) methods shows that EOM-CCSD/aug-cc-PVTZ-PP reproduces atomic excitation energies within ±500 cm −1 of experiment, whereas MR-CISD deviates by about ±1100 cm −1 . For the mercury dimer, EOM-CCSD potential energy curves yield absorption bands in excellent agreement with experimental transitions, while asymptotic excitation energies closely match atomic references. Extending this methodology, we present the first systematic ab initio study of absorption spectra of Hg 3 , Hg 4 , and Hg 5 , which display broad bands in the range of 37 000–60 000 cm −1 . The consistent agreement with experimental benchmarks and diagnostics confirming single-reference character validates EOM-CCSD as a robust approach for describing excited states and optical spectra of mercury clusters.
articles.journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue

articles.title: Diffusion models for the O(3) nonlinear sigma model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A score-based diffusion model is trained on the two-dimensional classical Heisenberg model, the lattice representation of the O(3) nonlinear sigma model. Neural networks are trained on three different coarse-grainings of the same training set to implement a multiscale sampling scheme that modestly improves both the accuracy and computational cost of direct sampling on the finest lattice. Stein (or Schwinger-Dyson) diagnostics for the two-point correlation function are introduced to assess the quality of the learned score without relying on reverse diffusion sampling. These diagnostics are also incorporated into an additional training loss. We discuss several technical considerations relevant to implementing diffusion models on S². These include a consideration of lifting the network input to S³, as in the CP¹ representation, and developing a boundary-layer approximation to the short-time spherical heat kernel that extends its usefulness to larger diffusion times.

articles.title: Selective effects of selenium substitution on superconductivity and magnetic memory in 4Hb-TaS2
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.39969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Disorder plays a central role in correlated quantum materials, but its effects can be highly selective when several electronic orders coexist. The van der Waals heterostructure 4Hb-TaS2 provides such a case, combining superconductivity, charge-order tendencies, strong scattering, and magnetic memory manifested through spontaneous vortices. Here we use Se substitution as a controlled local perturbation of the disorder landscape in 4Hb-TaS2. We find that superconductivity remains remarkably robust while the magnetic memory is strongly suppressed at higher Se concentrations. These results show that Se substitution does not create the hidden magnetic memory, but instead selectively weakens its macroscopic manifestation. More broadly, they reveal a sharp separation between robust superconducting and hidden-memory phases, and a highly disorder-sensitive spontaneous-vortex response in 4Hb-TaS2.

articles.title: Differentiable Systematic Resampling for Variational Sequential Monte Carlo
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.12094v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Particle filters are a standard tool for nonlinear state estimation, but their resampling step is discrete, preventing gradient-based learning in variational sequential Monte Carlo. We introduce Differentiable Systematic Resampling (DSR), a temperature-controlled relaxation of systematic resampling, that preserves the CDF-ordered, banded structure of systematic resampling while enabling full gradient flow. DSR converges to exact systematic resampling as the temperature vanishes, and we prove a pointwise exponential convergence rate for the induced bias. Compared to optimal-transport-based differentiable resampling, DSR avoids iterative solvers and has substantially lower computational overhead. Experiments on stochastic dynamical systems and real-world handwriting data show that DSR achieves comparable or superior filtering and dynamics learning performance.

articles.title: Assessment and Modeling of Air Gap Membrane Distillation Unit
articles.abstract: This research presents an extensive thermodynamic and transport model for an Air Gap Membrane Distillation (AGMD) system, aimed at assessing thermal efficiency. This research presents an extensive thermodynamic and transport model for an (AGMD) system, aimed at assessing thermal efficiency. under varying operational conditions. The MATLAB-implemented model incorporates essential heat and mass transfer processes, such as Knudsen-molecular diffusion and conductive heat losses, to calculate key performance metrics like permeate flux, thermal efficiency, (GOR), and (STEC). The AGMD configuration utilizes a hydrophobic polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) membrane featuring a 5 mm air gap, a pore dimension of 0.45 µm and a surface thickness of 150 µm. Experimental simulations investigate operational parameters, with feed temperatures varying from 40°C to 70°C and coolant temperatures fluctuating between 10°C and 25°C. Research demonstrates that elevating the feed temperature improves system efficiency, resulting in a peak permeate flow rate of 12.77 kg/m²·h, a thermal efficiency of 50.62%, and a minimum (STEC) of 29.04 kWh/m³ at a feed temperature of 70°C and a coolant temperature of 10°C. These results highlight AGMD’s potential as an energy-efficient desalination method, supporting sustainable freshwater generation in regions facing water scarcity. Future studies could explore optimizing membrane materials, minimizing thermal losses, and coupling with renewable energy to enhance performance and scalability. The model’s accuracy is validated by a ~ 60% increase in GOR, closely matching experimental outcomes. A custom built, solar integrated AGMD test rig equipped with a flat-plate solar collector and Arduino-based real-time monitoring was used to verify the model. Predictions showed strong alignment with experimental data and existing literature, confirming the system’s scalability and robustness. With an advantageous freshwater production expense of 2.52 per cubic meter, the system emerges as a practical solution for decentralized, off-grid applications. This research establishes a validated MATLAB modeling framework to guide AGMD design optimization, promoting its adoption as an affordable, renewable energy-powered desalination technology.

articles.title: Reproducible Coordinated P--Q Dispatch Optimization of a Smart-Inverter BESS for PV--EV Distribution Networks
articles.abstract: This study develops a 24-hour coordinated active- and reactive-power dispatch framework for a battery energy storage system (BESS) interfaced through a four-quadrant smart inverter in a radial distribution network with photovoltaic generation and electric-vehicle charging. The IEEE 33-bus feeder is evaluated under identical operating profiles and fixed hardware for three cases: no BESS, optimized active-power-only dispatch, and coordinated P--Q dispatch. A backward/forward-sweep power-flow solver is integrated with sequential least-squares programming to minimize a normalized objective combining feeder active-energy loss and system-wide voltage deviation, subject to BESS power limits, inverter apparent-power capability, charge/discharge efficiencies, state-of-charge (SOC) bounds, and terminal SOC equality. For an 800-kWh BESS with a 200-kW active-power limit and a 250-kVA inverter connected at Bus~18, P-only dispatch reduces daily feeder loss by 2.65%, whereas coordinated P--Q dispatch reduces it from 4267.86 to 3842.57~kWh/day, corresponding to a 9.97% reduction. The coordinated strategy further decreases daily voltage deviation by 17.77% and improves the worst-case minimum bus voltage from 0.83871 to 0.86695~p.u. The SOC remains within 19.41--95.00% and returns to 50% at the end of the scheduling horizon. Under deterministic load, PV, and EV perturbations applied without re-optimization, the fixed P--Q schedule maintains feeder-loss reductions of 9.42--10.61% and voltage-deviation reductions of 16.48--19.37%. These results demonstrate the additional network benefit of coordinated reactive-power support while also revealing the practical limitations imposed by fixed inverter capacity.
