Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD), by contrast, provides high spatial resolution across large sample areas and therefore, has the potential to enable the local investigation of interlayer spacing and site lattice occupancy with improved statistical reliability. The objectives of the study are to benchmark EBSDs capability for resolving these subtle features and to correlate them with compositional and mechanical properties. In this case study, we therefore show that EBSD can resolve key crystallographic features of mu-phase intermetallics, specifically interlayer spacings. We combine pattern matching with large-scale dynamical simulations of template libraries guided by XRD based information on lattice parameters. For this, we generate structures that vary in the spacing between triple-layer and Kagome layer and in the site lattice occupancy of the 3a site. This approach successfully predicts the change of interlayer spacing between Kagome and triple layers in Nb-Co and Nb-Ni mu-phases, in good agreement with XRD and HR-TEM.
articles.abstract_zh: 在有序金属间化合物中，晶格位点占有率和特定层间间距的微小变化已被确定为临界分辨剪切应力显着变化的来源，从而导致给定相如何影响合金性能。到目前为止，原子位置和晶格位点占用传统上是通过高分辨率透射电子显微镜 (HR-TEM) 和 X 射线衍射 (XRD) 来表征的，这些方法要么提供局部细节，要么提供高统计显着性，但不能同时提供两者。相比之下，电子背散射衍射 (EBSD) 可以在大样本区域提供高空间分辨率，因此有潜力能够对层间间距和位点晶格占用进行局部研究，并提高统计可靠性。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 在有序金属间化合物中，晶格位点占有率和特定层间间距的微小变化已被确定为临界分辨剪切应力显着变化的来源，从而导致给定相如何影响合金性能。到目前为止，原子位置和晶格位点占用传统上是通过高分辨率透射电子显微镜 (HR-TEM) 和 X 射线衍射 (XRD) 来表征的，这些方法要么提供局部细节，要么提供高统计显着性，但不能同时提供两者。相比之下，电子背散射衍射 (EBSD) 可以在大样本区域提供高空间分辨率，因此有潜力能够对层间间距和位点晶格占用进行局部研究，并提高统计可靠性。该研究的目的是对 EBSD 解决这些细微特征的能力进行基准测试，并将其与成分和机械性能相关联。因此，在本案例研究中，我们表明 EBSD 可以解析 mu 相金属间化合物的关键晶体学特征，特别是层间距。我们将模式匹配与模板库的大规模动态模拟相结合，该模拟由基于晶格参数信息的 XRD 引导。为此，我们生成了三层和 Kagome 层之间的间距以及 3a 位点的晶格占用率不同的结构。该方法成功预测了 Nb-Co 和 Nb-Ni mu 相中 Kagome 和三层之间的层间距变化，与 XRD 和 HR-TEM 吻合良好。

articles.title: Thermal Hall Signatures of Distinct Schwinger-Boson Flux Sectors on the Honeycomb Lattice
articles.title_zh: 蜂窝晶格上不同施温格-玻色子通量扇区的热霍尔特征
articles.abstract: arXiv:2608.29792v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thermal transport offers a bulk probe of charge-neutral excitations in frustrated magnets. It remains challenging, however, to determine whether such transport can distinguish different parton mean-field structures of the same spin system. This question is particularly relevant on the honeycomb lattice, where distinct 0-flux, π-flux, and chiral π/2-flux sectors have been proposed. In this paper, we compare self-consistent saddle-point solutions in these three sectors for a frustrated J₁-J₂ Heisenberg model with a next-nearest-neighbor Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and a perpendicular magnetic field. Using finite-temperature Schwinger-boson mean-field theory and the Kubo formula for bosonic Bogoliubov-de Gennes systems, we evaluate the intrinsic spinon thermal Hall conductivity. At a common parameter point where all three branches remain gapped, the 0-flux response is positive and the π-flux response is negative for D>0 and h>0 under the sign conventions used in this paper, whereas the π/2-flux response changes sign with increasing temperature. We further show that a projective symmetry combining a sixfold rotation with time reversal forces the zero-field response of a fixed chiral π/2-flux domain to vanish. Within the mean-field regime examined in this paper, the sign and temperature dependence of κₓy/T therefore provide a flux-sensitive transport signature.
articles.abstract_zh: 热传输提供了受挫磁体中电荷中性激发的整体探针。然而，确定这种传输是否可以区分同一自旋系统的不同部分子平均场结构仍然具有挑战性。这个问题与蜂窝晶格特别相关，其中已经提出了不同的 0 通量、π 通量和手性 π/2 通量扇区。在本文中，我们比较了受抑 J₁-J2 海森堡模型与次近邻 Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya 相互作用和垂直磁场的这三个扇区中的自洽鞍点解。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 热传输提供了受挫磁体中电荷中性激发的整体探针。然而，确定这种传输是否可以区分同一自旋系统的不同部分子平均场结构仍然具有挑战性。这个问题与蜂窝晶格特别相关，其中已经提出了不同的 0 通量、π 通量和手性 π/2 通量扇区。在本文中，我们比较了受抑 J₁-J2 海森堡模型与次近邻 Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya 相互作用和垂直磁场的这三个扇区中的自洽鞍点解。使用有限温度施温格玻色子平均场理论和玻色子 Bogoliubov-de Gennes 系统的 Kubo 公式，我们评估了本征自旋热霍尔电导率。在所有三个分支都保持间隙的公共参数点，根据本文使用的符号约定，对于 D>0 和 h>0，0 通量响应为正，π 通量响应为负，而 π/2 通量响应随着温度的升高而改变符号。我们进一步表明，将六重旋转与时间反转相结合的射影对称性迫使固定手性 π/2 通量域的零场响应消失。因此，在本文研究的平均场范围内，κₓy/T 的符号和温度依赖性提供了通量敏感的输运特征。

articles.title: A Hierarchy of Exact Lower Bounds on the Laughlin Spectral Gap
articles.title_zh: 劳克林谱间隙的精确下界的层次结构
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.18854v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a bootstrap approach to deriving lower bounds on the spectral gap of the first Haldane pseudopotential Hamiltonian on the sphere with N_Φ flux quanta for arbitrary N_Φ, including in the thermodynamic limit N_Φ → infty. This method can in principle be generalized to pseudopotentials describing other model wavefunctions such as the Moore--Read state or Read--Rezayi sequence. Our approach is based on Knabe's observation that if H is a Hamiltonian with ground state energy zero then the spectral gap is at least ϵ > 0 if and only if H² succeq ϵ H. To show this inequality, we split H² into two parts, one that can be analytically bounded and another that can be bounded using a finite semidefinite program (SDP). Crucially, the size of this program is determined only by cutoff parameters, and the program depends on N_Φ only parametrically, allowing us to obtain numerically exact (up to solver precision) lower bounds on the gap. In order to turn these numerical bounds into mathematically rigorous results, we introduce an algorithm that can produce nearly-optimal exact interior feasible points for large rational SDPs even if the affine constraints are highly redundant and ill-conditioned. We additionally provide an algorithm that establishes the rank stability of the SDP in the N_Φ → infty limit, which is needed to certify the bound in the thermodynamic limit. Beyond establishing a Laughlin gap greater than 1/100 in the thermodynamic limit and revealing a potential method for deriving spectral gap lower bounds for other pseudopotentials, our work provides a general method for turning numerical SDP bounds into rigorous mathematical proofs, which may have wide applicability. In particular, this work demonstrates that bootstrap methods can be used to rigorously resolve major open problems in quantum many-body physics.
articles.abstract_zh: 我们开发了一种自举方法，用于导出任意 N_Φ 具有 N_Φ 通量量子的球体上第一个 Haldane 赝势哈密顿量的谱间隙下界，包括在热力学极限 N_Φ → infty 中。该方法原则上可以推广到描述其他模型波函数的赝势，例如 Moore--Read 状态或 Read--Rezayi 序列。我们的方法基于 Knabe 的观察，即如果 H 是基态能量为零的哈密顿量，则当且仅当 H² 成功 ϵ H 时，谱间隙至少为 ϵ > 0。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 我们开发了一种自举方法，用于导出任意 N_Φ 具有 N_Φ 通量量子的球体上第一个 Haldane 赝势哈密顿量的谱间隙下界，包括在热力学极限 N_Φ → infty 中。该方法原则上可以推广到描述其他模型波函数的赝势，例如 Moore--Read 状态或 Read--Rezayi 序列。我们的方法基于 Knabe 的观察，即如果 H 是基态能量为零的哈密顿量，则当且仅当 H² 成功 ϵ H 时，谱间隙至少为 ϵ > 0。为了证明这种不等式，我们将 H² 分为两部分，一部分可以分析有界，另一部分可以使用有限半定程序 (SDP) 有界。至关重要的是，该程序的大小仅由截止参数决定，并且该程序仅在参数上依赖于 N_Φ，从而使我们能够获得数值上精确的间隙下限（达到求解器精度）。为了将这些数值界限转化为数学上严格的结果，我们引入了一种算法，即使仿射约束高度冗余且病态，也可以为大型有理 SDP 生成近乎最优的精确内部可行点。我们还提供了一种算法，用于建立 SDP 在 N_Φ → infty 极限中的秩稳定性，这是证明热力学极限中的界限所必需的。除了在热力学极限中建立大于 1/100 的劳克林间隙并揭示一种推导其他赝势的谱间隙下界的潜在方法之外，我们的工作还提供了一种将数值 SDP 界限转化为严格的数学证明的通用方法，该方法可能具有广泛的适用性。特别是，这项工作证明了引导方法可以用来严格解决量子多体物理中的主要开放问题。

articles.title: Protonic thermoelectric effect of Superionic H₂O and magnetic field generation in Uranus and Neptune
articles.title_zh: 超离子水的质子热电效应以及天王星和海王星的磁场产生
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.03659v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The origin of the anomalous magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune, with significant tilts and multi-dipole configurations, is central to understanding the internal structure and evolution of the ice giants. Recent investigations confirmed that superionic H₂O ice is thermodynamically stable and constitutes the dominant H₂O phase within their icy mantles. Here, we use deep learning and ab initio molecular dynamics to investigate the thermal and protonic transport properties of superionic H₂O ice. We demonstrate that superionic H₂O ice exhibits a pronounced protonic thermoelectric effect, with a maximum Seebeck coefficient that can reach sim 620 μV K⁻¹ within the interior of Uranus, whereas Neptune's is lower, within the range of 570-585 μV K⁻¹. Consequently, the temperature gradients in the icy mantles can induce proton migration, thereby driving magnetic field generation. Based on this mechanism, and within a dipolar approximation that captures the mean field, the disparities in mean dipolar magnetic field strength between Uranus and Neptune can be explained exclusively by their differing internal temperature gradients, and the predicted mean field strengths are comparable to those observed by Voyager 2.
articles.abstract_zh: 天王星和海王星异常磁场的起源，具有显着的倾斜和多偶极结构，对于理解冰巨星的内部结构和演化至关重要。最近的研究证实，超离子 H2O 冰具有热力学稳定性，并构成其冰幔中的主要 H2O 相。在这里，我们使用深度学习和从头算分子动力学来研究超离子 H2O 冰的热和质子输运特性。我们证明超离子 H2O 冰表现出明显的质子热电效应，在天王星内部的最大塞贝克系数可以达到 sim 620 μV K⁻1，而海王星的塞贝克系数较低，在 570-585 μV K⁻1 范围内。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 天王星和海王星异常磁场的起源，具有显着的倾斜和多偶极结构，对于理解冰巨星的内部结构和演化至关重要。最近的研究证实，超离子 H2O 冰具有热力学稳定性，并构成其冰幔中的主要 H2O 相。在这里，我们使用深度学习和从头算分子动力学来研究超离子 H2O 冰的热和质子输运特性。我们证明超离子 H2O 冰表现出明显的质子热电效应，在天王星内部的最大塞贝克系数可以达到 sim 620 μV K⁻1，而海王星的塞贝克系数较低，在 570-585 μV K⁻1 范围内。因此，冰幔中的温度梯度可以引起质子迁移，从而驱动磁场的产生。基于这一机制，在捕获平均场的偶极近似中，天王星和海王星之间平均偶极磁场强度的差异可以完全用它们不同的内部温度梯度来解释，并且预测的平均场强度与航海家二号观测到的平均场强度相当。

articles.title: Shortcuts to Adiabaticity via Adaptive Quantum Zeno Measurements
articles.title_zh: 通过自适应量子芝诺测量实现绝热性的捷径
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.17786v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Stroboscopic measurements of a time-dependent projector generate a quantum Zeno dynamics whose effective Hamiltonian is the Kato-Avron Hamiltonian for parallel transport, which reduces to counterdiabatic driving in the case of a nonselective measurement of the instantaneous eigenprojectors of the system. The same generator arises under continuous monitoring of a time-dependent observable and under a time-varying complex absorbing potential. Departures from the ideal Zeno limit are governed, in all three settings, by a single positive leakage operator with a dynamical and a purely geometric contribution. Matching the corresponding generators yields a model-independent generalized Schulman relation for the quantum Zeno dynamics in the three scenarios, and a purely geometric bound on the measurement resources needed to steer a subspace along a prescribed path.
articles.abstract_zh: 与时间相关的投影仪的频闪测量会生成量子芝诺动力学，其有效哈密顿量是并行传输的加藤-阿夫伦哈密顿量，在系统瞬时本征投影仪的非选择性测量的情况下，它会减少到反非绝热驱动。在连续监测与时间相关的可观测值和随时间变化的复吸收势下会产生相同的发生器。在所有三种设置中，与理想芝诺极限的偏离均由具有动态和纯几何贡献的单个正泄漏算子控制。匹配相应的生成器会产生三种情况下量子芝诺动力学的独立于模型的广义舒尔曼关系，以及沿着规定路径引导子空间所需的测量资源的纯几何界限。

articles.title: Discovering quantum phenomena with Interpretable Machine Learning
articles.title_zh: 通过可解释的机器学习发现量子现象
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.16015v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Interpretable machine learning techniques are becoming essential tools for extracting physical insights from complex quantum data. We build on recent advances in variational autoencoders to demonstrate that such models can learn physically meaningful and interpretable representations from a broad class of unlabeled quantum datasets. From raw measurement data alone, the learned representation reveals rich information about the underlying structure of quantum phase diagrams. We further augment the learning pipeline with symbolic methods, enabling the discovery of compact analytical descriptors that serve as order parameters for the distinct regimes emerging in the learned representations. We demonstrate the framework on experimental Rydberg-atom snapshots, classical shadows of the cluster Ising model, and hybrid discrete-continuous fermionic data, revealing previously unreported phenomena such as a corner-ordering pattern in the Rydberg arrays. These results establish a general framework, which constitutes an important step toward the autonomous discovery of physical descriptors from diverse quantum datasets. All methods are available through qdisc, an open-source Python library designed to make these tools accessible to the broader community.
articles.abstract_zh: 可解释的机器学习技术正在成为从复杂的量子数据中提取物理见解的重要工具。我们以变分自动编码器的最新进展为基础，证明此类模型可以从广泛的未标记量子数据集中学习物理上有意义且可解释的表示。仅根据原始测量数据，学习到的表示就揭示了有关量子相图底层结构的丰富信息。我们进一步用符号方法增强学习管道，从而能够发现紧凑的分析描述符，这些描述符充当学习表示中出现的不同状态的顺序参数。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 可解释的机器学习技术正在成为从复杂的量子数据中提取物理见解的重要工具。我们以变分自动编码器的最新进展为基础，证明此类模型可以从广泛的未标记量子数据集中学习物理上有意义且可解释的表示。仅根据原始测量数据，学习到的表示就揭示了有关量子相图底层结构的丰富信息。我们进一步用符号方法增强学习管道，从而能够发现紧凑的分析描述符，这些描述符充当学习表示中出现的不同状态的顺序参数。我们展示了实验里德堡原子快照、簇伊辛模型的经典阴影和混合离散连续费米子数据的框架，揭示了以前未报告的现象，例如里德堡阵列中的角排序模式。这些结果建立了一个总体框架，这构成了从不同量子数据集中自主发现物理描述符的重要一步。所有方法都可以通过 qdisc 获得，qdisc 是一个开源 Python 库，旨在让更广泛的社区可以使用这些工具。

articles.title: Boundary-Canceled Score-Hamiltonian Sampling
articles.title_zh: 边界取消分数哈密尔顿采样
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.05904v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Diffusion sampling is related to imaginary-time quantum annealing through a forward/backward Schrödinger equation pair and its one-sided counterdiabatic connection. For a smooth, gapped Score-Hamiltonian path, the exact connection transports the target density at any evolution time. We apply quantum-annealing performance analysis to residuals from approximating this connection with a trained score. If the first r terminal schedule derivatives vanish, the squared Hellinger error scales as T⁻²r⁻², with a prefactor determined by the terminal learning residual and inverse gaps. Direct two-dimensional imaginary-time evolution with one fixed neural score reproduces these powers and prefactors. Terminal schedule design thus suppresses the distributional effect of imperfect score learning without retraining the network.
articles.abstract_zh: 扩散采样通过前向/后向薛定谔方程对及其单侧反绝热联系与虚时间量子退火相关。对于平滑、有间隙的 Score-Hamiltonian 路径，精确的连接在任何演化时间都传输目标密度。我们将量子退火性能分析应用于通过训练分数来近似这种连接的残差。如果前 r 个终端调度导数消失，则平方海灵格误差将缩放为 T⁻²r⁻²，其前因子由终端学习残差和逆间隙确定。具有一个固定神经分数的直接二维虚时间演化再现了这些能力和先因子。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 扩散采样通过前向/后向薛定谔方程对及其单侧反绝热联系与虚时间量子退火相关。对于平滑、有间隙的 Score-Hamiltonian 路径，精确的连接在任何演化时间都传输目标密度。我们将量子退火性能分析应用于通过训练分数来近似这种连接的残差。如果前 r 个终端调度导数消失，则平方海灵格误差将缩放为 T⁻²r⁻²，其前因子由终端学习残差和逆间隙确定。具有一个固定神经分数的直接二维虚时间演化再现了这些能力和先因子。因此，终端调度设计可以抑制不完美分数学习的分配效应，而无需重新训练网络。

articles.title: Walshness: an intrinsic neural-network representability metric for quantum states
articles.title_zh: Walshness：量子态的内在神经网络可表示性度量
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.00505v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Neural quantum states (NQS) have emerged as powerful representations of quantum states with rapidly expanding applications across quantum many-body physics. Yet our understanding of when neural networks can efficiently represent physical quantum states remains limited, in part due to the nonlinear parameterization of NQS, the intricate sign structure of quantum states, and the sensitive dependence on basis choice. We introduce Walshness, a complexity metric of a quantum state which quantifies whether it admits a compact neural-network representation. We rigorously prove that a general quantum many-body state admits an efficient NQS representation if it has bounded Walshness, and vice versa, for various NQS architectures. We provide an algorithm for finding the optimal basis by minimizing the energy of a corresponding classical spin model. This allows us to empirically improve the learnability of various physical quantum states, including ground states of the transverse-field Ising model and mixed-field toric code, often reducing infidelity by orders of magnitude, and generalizes the basis choice given by the well-known Marshall sign rule in frustrated antiferromagnets. Our results provide an intrinsic complexity metric for quantum states with provable connections to their neural-network representability.
articles.abstract_zh: 神经量子态（NQS）已经成为量子态的强大表示，在量子多体物理领域的应用迅速扩展。然而，我们对神经网络何时能够有效表示物理量子态的理解仍然有限，部分原因是 NQS 的非线性参数化、量子态复杂的符号结构以及对基选择的敏感依赖性。我们引入了 Walshness，一种量子态的复杂性度量，用于量化它是否接受紧凑的神经网络表示。我们严格证明，对于各种 NQS 架构，如果通用量子多体态具有有界 Walshness，则它承认有效的 NQS 表示，反之亦然。
articles.abstract_zh_full: 神经量子态（NQS）已经成为量子态的强大表示，在量子多体物理领域的应用迅速扩展。然而，我们对神经网络何时能够有效表示物理量子态的理解仍然有限，部分原因是 NQS 的非线性参数化、量子态复杂的符号结构以及对基选择的敏感依赖性。我们引入了 Walshness，一种量子态的复杂性度量，用于量化它是否接受紧凑的神经网络表示。我们严格证明，对于各种 NQS 架构，如果通用量子多体态具有有界 Walshness，则它承认有效的 NQS 表示，反之亦然。我们提供了一种通过最小化相应经典自旋模型的能量来找到最佳基础的算法。这使我们能够凭经验提高各种物理量子态的可学习性，包括横向场伊辛模型和混合场环面码的基态，通常可以将不忠实性降低几个数量级，并概括出受挫反铁磁体中著名的马歇尔符号规则给出的基础选择。我们的结果提供了量子态的内在复杂性度量，并与其神经网络可表示性有可证明的联系。

articles.title: Theoretical study of high-order harmonic generation in solids based on deep-learning methods
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids provides a compact and coherent EUV radiation, which has attracted considerable attention. Many theoretical methods for laser-crystal interactions are developed. However, an approach to treat large-scale amorphous systems with ab-initio accuracy is still lacking because of the enormous computational cost. Here, we incorporate molecular dynamics and tight-binding electron Hamiltonians based on deep-learning methods to solve the problem efficiently. Its accuracy is validated by comparing the HHG spectra of monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) with those obtained using existing methods. Then we use it to study the temperature-dependent HHG in bulk Si. We uncover a distinct harmonic-order-dependent thermal response: low-order harmonics are enhanced with increasing temperature, whereas high-order harmonics are suppressed. The former is caused by the modification of the inter-site hopping in the system, while the latter is mainly influenced by the structural disorder induced by the thermal effects, in agreement with experimental observations. This work establishes a scalable computational strategy for investigating HHG in solids and provides new insights into the interplay between lattice fluctuations and ultrafast electron dynamics.

articles.title: Parity-doublet spin interactions in ultracold polyatomic molecules
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precision measurements exploit internal molecular structure to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. Reaching the entanglement-enhanced regime requires preparing and preserving correlated molecular states within the same manifold used for sensing. Parity-doublet states are central to proposals for precision measurements with polyatomic molecules because they enable large molecular polarization for enhanced sensitivity, and provide internal state co-magnetometry to suppress systematic errors. Here we report the observation and control of resonant dipolar exchange interactions in a parity-doublet sensing manifold of ultracold polyatomic molecules. Using laser-cooled CaOH molecules in a crossed optical dipole trap, we encode a pseudospin in the ell-type parity-doublet states and observe two complementary signatures of interactions: a density-dependent Ramsey contrast decay and a spin-projection-dependent mean-field precession whose sign reverses with the initialized population imbalance. Both observables are well described by a common discrete truncated Wigner model using independently calibrated experimental parameters. We further Floquet-engineer the interaction anisotropy and observe suppressed many-body dephasing near the SU(2)-symmetric Heisenberg point, identifying a protected regime relevant for spin squeezing and precision measurement with dense molecular ensembles. Our results establish parity doublets as a coherent, interacting, and programmable molecular degree of freedom, connecting the polyatomic precision-measurement platform to dipolar many-body physics and opening a route to entanglement-enhanced tests of fundamental physics.

articles.title: A generative foundation model for 2D magnetized plasma turbulence
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a proof-of-principle study demonstrating a conditional generative foundation model for self-organizing magnetized plasma turbulence. Built on a multichannel flow-matching framework with a spectral decomposition strategy, the model is trained on direct numerical simulations of 2D modified Hasegawa-Wakatani (MHW) turbulence across the hydrodynamic to adiabatic parameter range. Without retraining, this single model successfully performs three distinct downstream tasks: (i) unconditional generation of statistically faithful quasi-steady-state snapshots that recover the directional energy spectra and amplitude statistics, from which statistical transport quantities, including turbulent flux and effective diffusivity, alongside their uncertainties, are inferred directly; (ii) super-resolution from 4× and 8× downsampled observations to reconstruct fine-scale turbulence and large-scale zonal structures; and (iii) full-field inpainting from sparse spatial observations covering as little as sim 10% of the domain. The generated fields faithfully reproduce regime-dependent turbulence vs. zonal-flow states and energy partitioning. Under extreme sparsity the long-correlation zonal flows are pinned by only a handful of observations, while the residual uncertainty concentrates in the small-scale turbulent fluctuations. These results establish flow-matching generative models as powerful, unified surrogates for state generation, statistical inference, and sparse-data reconstruction, providing a scalable baseline for 3D plasma turbulence and experimental applications.

articles.title: Elasticized magnetohydrostatics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The modern approach to modeling equilibria in stellarators features two blind spots: lack of foundational agreement between theory and computation, and inability to reliably explore economically-attractive high-β concepts. These blind spots originate at a technical level from lack of a useful existence theory for the partial differential equations believed to describe equilibria, and from the encumbrance of crude, inflexible models for the topology of the confining magnetic field. This Article proposes the first stellarator equilibrium model that rigorously guarantees existence of an equilibrium with any chosen magnetic topology. It completely separates determination of the magnetic topology from the equilibrium existence question, and thereby enables importing realistic tearing physics into equilibrium computations. The new model replaces the standard plasma potential energy functional with its ensemble average over rapid kinetic-scale fluctuations. Averaging ``elasticizes" the potential by energetically penalizing separation of field lines. The elasticized potential's super-linear dependence on plasma strain embodies a phenomenological model for profile stiffness, and plays an essential role in the existence theory.

articles.title: Reduced magnetohydrodynamics with electron inertia in pseudodipole coordinates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the altitude-dependent structuring of field-aligned currents by driven Alfvén waves in an expanding auroral flux tube. The model uses the reduced magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) long-thin ordering assumptions along with electron inertia. We derive a magnetic tension operator consistent with energy conservation in the expanding geometry. We compare uniform density with a prescribed profile containing a dense ionospheric end and a low-density upper region. The simulations produce localized current concentrations near the lower boundary and filamentary structures at greater heights. Broad structures remain visible in the magnetic and velocity stream functions while their perpendicular derivatives reveal finer magnetic field, velocity, and current structure. With the nonuniform density profile, the run with additional upper boundary reflection shows finer current structure and greater numerical dissipation. Spectral diagnostics show forward nonlinear energy transfer and altitude-dependent power-law-like intervals without a broad constant-flux range. The narrowest current concentrations span only a few grid cells, so their physical widths remain unresolved.

articles.title: Spatially-Adaptive Neural-Network Based Extraction of Significant Wave Heights from HF Radar Data
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Significant wave height (SWH) retrieval from high-frequency (HF) radar data conventionally relies on Doppler-spectrum processing and interpretation of the weak second-order scattering continuum. This article investigates adaptive spatial processing for time-domain SWH estimation using ordered envelope statistics. In our previous study, a physics-guided linear ordered-statistics estimator (LOSE), motivated by first-order rough-surface scattering assumptions and radar-envelope statistics, mapped the largest rank-ordered magnitudes of Bartlett-beamformed voltages to buoy-observed SWH through least-squares regression. The LOSE framework is extended using three trainable complex spatial filters initialized around the buoy look direction. Ordered magnitudes are extracted independently from each spatial output, concatenated, and mapped to SWH through least-squares regression, while the spatial weights are optimized using gradient-based updates. Both estimators use causal sliding-window averaging. Evaluation used measurements from a 13.385-MHz, 12-receiver element WERA radar at Argentia, Canada, paired with directional-wave buoy observations. Under a common chronological training-evaluation partition, the selected adaptive configuration reduced root-mean-square error by approximately 14.3%, while maintaining the Pearson correlation coefficient at 0.949. These results support the potential of adaptive multi-beam processing to improve time-domain SWH estimation relative to fixed Bartlett-based LOSE. Feature counts and smoothing windows were selected using the evaluation interval; independent testing is therefore needed to establish the generality of the improvement.

articles.title: A flexible regularization for magnetic vector inversion with petrophysical, structural, and sparsity constraints
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic vector inversion (MVI) is widely used because it can account for both induced and remanent magnetization by inverting for a magnetization vector model. This flexibility comes at the cost of nonuniqueness, since the number of unknowns is three times that of scalar inversion, and prior information can be required to make the result geologically useful. Recent work has applied sparse norms to the vector model, but many of the other tools for incorporating prior information within scalar inversions remain either unavailable for a vector model or unavailable without introducing artifacts or significant nonlinearity. We introduce a vector regularization, formulated in Cartesian coordinates, that generalizes existing sparse Cartesian formulations. We formulate the smallness term to admit a Cartesian reference model, from susceptibility and oriented remanence, and a magnitude reference model, from unoriented remanence or total magnetization. Because a nonzero magnitude reference model makes the Hessian of the smallness term indefinite, we derive its eigendecomposition analytically and modify the eigenvalues so that standard conjugate-gradient solvers can be applied. We formulate the smoothness term to penalize changes in both the direction and magnitude of magnetization. It is independent of the choice of Cartesian basis, so sparse norms can be applied without coordinate-aligned artifacts, and it admits arbitrary preferred smoothing directions through a rotated gradient operator. We demonstrate the method on synthetic data from a folded body with spatially variable magnetization direction, where each form of prior information improves the recovered model. We then apply it to airborne magnetic data over the DO-27 kimberlite, where incorporating petrophysical measurements yields a model more consistent with the measured properties and the geologic model inferred from drilling.

articles.title: Expert lithological labels do not improve learning when used to predict marine sediment properties
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36410v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific drilling has produced large archives of physical, chemical and magnetic measurements linked to descriptions of the rock recovered. These archives are mostly incomplete: instruments sample at different intervals, recovery is partial, and destructive analyses preclude later measurement of the same material. We train an self-supervised embedding model on the LILY ocean drilling database using six routinely logged properties (bulk density, magnetic susceptibility, natural gamma radiation, and red, green and blue reflectance) across 236,963 observations from 296 boreholes, with a masked variational autoencoder that has a heteroscedastic Gaussian decoder and learnable mask tokens. The embeddings separate geologist-assigned lithologies as well as a variant trained with those labels, and increasing the weight on the labels degrades reconstruction while leaving classification unchanged. The labels are recoverable from the measurements geologists use to assign them, so training on them adds nothing. Lithological categories compress continuous measurements into classes, and compressing them discards what the measurements record about the processes that produced the rock. The embeddings also predict physical properties that were absent from training, on boreholes the model has never seen. While depth should account for this since sediments compact with burial, it does not. On held-out boreholes depth alone reaches a median R² of -0.02, against 0.20 for the embedding.

articles.title: Multiple-relaxation-time total enthalpy lattice Boltzmann model for liquid-vapor phase change
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, a multiple-relaxation-time (MRT) total enthalpy lattice Boltzmann (LB) model is proposed for liquid-vapor phase change. The pseudopotential LB method is employed to describe the liquid-vapor multiphase dynamics, while the thermal field is solved using an MRT LB formulation with total enthalpy as the evolution variable, thereby incorporating sensible and latent heat into a unified framework. A latent heat expression based on the equation of state (EOS) is further derived to provide a thermodynamic reference for its specification. Multiscale analysis demonstrates that the proposed model recovers the target macroscopic energy equation without introducing the nonlinear thermodynamic source term commonly required in temperature-based formulations, thereby avoiding the explicit evaluation of nablacdotu. The model is validated through free droplet evaporation, droplet evaporation on a heated surface, and bubble growth and departure during boiling, showing good agreement with published results. Simulations with different prescribed latent heats are further conducted in all three cases, demonstrating that the latent heat can be independently specified according to the physical conditions considered without altering the equation of state.

articles.title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. The prediction of the Hamiltonian is essentially the prediction of the electron electrostatic potential energy; however, for heterogeneous systems, this potential energy is often determined by faraway features, such as interface or surface dipoles, or even an applied voltage in a nanodevice. Thus, it cannot be determined by local atomic structures alone. In this sense, one needs to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently using intrinsic atomic dipoles, the applied external potential energy, and polarizabilities. Fortunately, the intrinsic dipoles and polarizabilities are local properties, whereas the applied potential energy is a prescribed input. In this work, we propose DeepH-Polar, a physically informed machine learning Hamiltonian model that explicitly predicts intrinsic atomic dipoles and polarizability tensors and uses them to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently. Benchmarks on polar GaN systems and crystalline-Si/amorphous-SiO₂ interfaces demonstrate improved Hamiltonian accuracy and reproduction of thickness-dependent electrostatic variations, as well as spatially nonuniform field-induced screening that models without polarization fail to capture. Our model also allows us to study nanoscale electronic devices. By iteratively solving the Hamiltonian eigenproblem and self-consistently updating free-carrier occupations and the electrostatic potential, we simulate an 8,194-atom gated semiconductor device.

articles.title: Self-organized hybrid scenario mediated by fishbone modes in the EAST tokamak
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-organized hybrid scenario mediated by fishbone modes in the Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak (EAST) is reported in this work. In this regime, internal transport barriers(ITBs) and a flat core safety factor profile were maintained simultaneously by fishbone modes. First,the drive of low-frequency flows by fishbone modes is clarified, which subsequently suppresses turbulence transport. Besides, fishbone-induced poloidally symmetric (m = 0) toroidal current sheets were first reported experimentally, which drive outward current redistribution that mitigates core current peaking. Together, these effects enable hybrid operation with stable ITBs and robust magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) stability, revealing a self-organized pathway for sustaining hybrid scenario for fusion reactors.

articles.title: Magnons in α-Fe2O3 microdisks: from thermal to coherent excitation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hematite is a prototypical antiferromagnetic insulator for spintronic and magnonic applications, yet controlled studies of coherent magnons in thin films remain challenging due to strain sensitivity and spatial inhomogeneity. Here, we investigate magnon excitations in lithographically patterned hematite microdisks, and obtain reproducible magnon spectra from multiple individual microdisks. Brillouin light scattering reveals bulk-like field-dependent thermal magnon resonances with an ultralow effective damping parameter on the order of ~10-5. Coherent magnons are further excited using a stripline antenna adjacent to the microdisk, revealing a power-dependent frequency blue shift accompanied by a nonlinear evolution of the coherent response under strong microwave driving. Field-dependent analysis indicates a power-dependent increase of the effective magnetic anisotropy field, suggesting a tunable nonlinear response of antiferromagnetic magnons in laterally confined microdisks. These results establish patterned hematite thin films as a platform for exploring coherent and nonlinear antiferromagnetic magnon dynamics.

articles.title: Catastrophes in Reconnections of Optical Vortex Rings
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A small change in parameters leads to a small change in the outcomes, in most cases. For instance, an optical vortex ring, created in the superposition of two laser beams, can slightly shrink if the phase changes minutely. However, dynamical systems can also experience significant changes due to small perturbations in parameters; the vortex rings can reconnect, nucleate or collapse into a point. Parameters that cause such striking outcomes are at the focal point of catastrophe theory - a branch of bifurcation theory that studies degenerate critical points of a potential function. We present theoretical study of topological configurations of optical vortex rings in elliptic Gaussian beams, which change dramatically at specific beam parameters. We identify two types of catastrophes, cusp and butterfly, near which very small changes of elliptic deformations lead to complex topological transformations of vortex rings.

articles.title: Quantum circuit simulation with high-order optical tensor processing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36172v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classical simulation is essential for developing and testing quantum circuits, but the exponential growth of Hilbert space challenges conventional digital processors. Here, we introduce a classical optical quantum simulation architecture that treats gates and batches of input states as independent tensor dimensions rather than separate simulation instances, while mapping eligible tensor network contractions onto the same processor. Using co-designed multidimensional encoding and readout across spatial and wavelength degrees of freedom, we experimentally realize high-order tensor-matrix multiplication in a single propagation and process all computational-basis inputs for each 4-qubit gate. Using a physics-based optical propagation model, we further numerically evaluate the architecture for the Deutsch algorithm and for the tensor network of all 128 target instances of a 7-qubit Grover algorithm. These results establish a unified framework for gate-state batch and tensor network simulation, providing a route to exploit optical concurrency across quantum simulation tasks.

articles.title: Calculation of distant retrograde orbits and their use in space weather forecasting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36315v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: There is current renewed interest in using Sun-Earth distant retrograde orbits (DROs) for a space weather forecasting mission, which would temporarily place spacecraft at a position near the Sun-Earth line, but closer to the Sun than the L1 point (such as the ESA HENON mission and ESA SHIELD concept). With in situ observations of the magnetic field on a DRO, the southward (B_z < 0) magnetic field of interplanetary coronal mass ejections (ICMEs), which is not routinely accessible remotely, could be measured several hours in advance. This B_z < 0 field is a decisive factor for forecasting geomagnetic storm intensity. We present an analysis of DROs at different sub-L1 distances for their efficacy for a space weather forecasting mission. An open-source numerical framework to generate DRO trajectories is presented. Our pre-calculated orbits in Heliocentric Earth Ecliptic coordinates can be introduced into numerical or empirical simulations of the ambient solar wind and ICMEs. We then analyze the corresponding forecast lead times, the resulting observational gaps depending on the number of spacecraft and distance of a DRO, and the "cone of acceptance" of the maximum longitudinal separation of a spacecraft to the Sun-Earth line. We define different domains regarding radial evolution and longitudinal CME structure, and show the historical coverage of sub-L1 ICME observations with our ICMECAT catalog. An optimal mission configuration can be selected based on the characteristics of DROs presented here, depending on the requirements of such a mission deemed acceptable with respect to results on CME evolution and coherence.

articles.title: High-Fidelity Aerostructural Dataset of Transonic Wings in Cruise Conditions
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in machine learning (ML) have the potential to substantially accelerate aircraft wing design, a process that has traditionally required extensive high-fidelity simulation and design iteration. Existing public datasets for ML-based wing design have focused primarily on aerodynamic performance, with limited consideration of the multidisciplinary interactions that govern practical aircraft design. In particular, efficient wing design requires simultaneous consideration of aerodynamic performance and structural integrity, yet no publicly available datasets capture this coupled aerostructural behavior at high-fidelity. To address this need, a high-fidelity multidisciplinary dataset for static aerostructural analysis of transonic wings is introduced. The dataset includes 2471 samples, along with three out-of-distribution samples. The wing planform geometry is parameterized by span, sweep, dihedral, tip chord, and tip twist, while the airfoil cross-sections are parameterized using the class-shape transformation method. The analysis is further parameterized by Mach number, angle of attack, altitude, and structural load factor. The utility of the dataset is demonstrated by training state-of-the-art ML models to predict aerodynamic surface quantities, integrated aerodynamic performance quantities, and the failure distribution of the wingbox. ML models achieve at most 0.0309 normalized root mean squared error (NRMSE) in the prediction of aerodynamic quantities and at most 0.1189 NRMSE in the prediction of failure distribution of the wingbox. By providing coupled aerodynamic and structural responses for a diverse set of transonic wings, this dataset establishes a benchmark for developing, evaluating, and comparing multi-physics ML models for wing design. Broadly, it is intended to encourage creation of similar high-fidelity multi-physics benchmark datasets across engineering domains.

articles.title: diff-soup: GPU-native Differentiable Simulation and Inference for Large-scale Stiff Dynamical Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37333v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning physical models from spatiotemporal data requires simulating systems of partial differential equations (PDEs) and differentiating through their solution. Upon spatial discretization, these models give rise to stiff dynamical systems that require repeatedly solving large, sparse linear systems. Traditional scientific computing frameworks are largely CPU-based and require problem-specific tuning to accelerate, scale, and differentiate. In this work, we introduce diff-soup, a differentiable, sparse-oriented, unified PDE suite for GPU-native simulation and inference of large, stiff dynamical systems. Built in JAX, diff-soup provides 1) a fully differentiable design for problems with sparse structure, 2) scaling to large problems through the NVIDIA cuDSS sparse direct solver with model and data multi-GPU parallelism, and 3) end-to-end PDE-constrained optimization, from classical statistical inference to embedded deep learning. On stiff PDE benchmarks, diff-soup outperforms established CPU- and GPU-based frameworks by one to two orders of magnitude in both forward solves and gradients. We demonstrate both a classical Bayesian inference workflow, identifying constitutive relationships, and a modern deep learning workflow, training a neural field for the catalyst activity of a three-dimensional packed bed reactor. We provide diff-soup as an open-source repository to facilitate research in computational science and engineering.

articles.title: Electric-Field Induction Motor with Discrete Circuit Elements and Improved Rotor Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37452v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electric-field-based actuators and machines lead the design space at the nanoscale and in biological systems, while having the potential to be used in favorable macroscale applications which prioritize minimal mass, performance in a vacuum, or performance in high temperatures. Electric-field induction motors consist of a set of stator electrodes which induce opposite charges onto a movable rotor surface. In earlier work, rotor surfaces for electric-field induction motors have been made of single continuum materials, which are limited in possible resistivity, permittivity and circuitry characteristics. To enhance design freedom, we develop a rotor for electric-field-based machines which may be constructed out of discrete circuit components between a finite number of conductive vanes. Magnetic-field induction motors, which are common in machinery, often utilize ``deep bar'' rotors, consisting of conducting bars which decrease the rotor time constant with increasing frequency using the skin depth effect. We propose, analyze, design and demonstrate a macro-scale electric-field induction motor which uses circuitry on the rotor surface to emulate the ``deep bar'' design, providing improved torque over a wide range of speeds.

articles.title: AMOR: Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement for Operator Learning on Arbitrary Meshes and Irregular 3D Geometries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parametric PDEs in science and engineering are often posed on irregular meshes with geometries that may contain holes or complex boundaries, yet popular operator-surrogate architectures such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) rely on structured geometries for fast computational kernels. We introduce Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement (AMOR), which replaces FNO's Fourier-based spectral convolutions with reduced-basis blocks and supports both data-driven and prescribed input/output bases through a common encode/decode interface. AMOR thus applies unmodified to arbitrary meshes and, because its spectral parameterization has no tensor-product dependence on the spatial dimension, it scales favorably to three dimensions, where FNO's spectral weights grow as m³ with the number of spectral modes m. We prove that AMOR is a universal approximator of continuous operators. On two-dimensional structured-grid benchmarks, AMOR is competitive with FNO overall and surpasses PCANet: it outperforms FNO on nonlinear diffusion and Helmholtz problems, while a static snapshot basis keeps it from matching FNO's accuracy on the time-dependent Kolmogorov flow problem. On three-dimensional problems it matches or exceeds FNO's accuracy at lower inference cost on linear elastostatics while trailing FNO on a turbulent lid-driven-cavity flow and scales favorably to problems demanding high capacity. On irregular meshes, where FNO is not directly applicable, AMOR reduces the relative L² error over the FNO extension Geo-FNO by 31% (airfoil) and 42% (elasticity). Finally, AMOR maintains strong performance across three physically distinct, experimentally motivated loading regimes on a topologically nontrivial three-dimensional aircraft-rib mesh, demonstrating its applicability to realistic engineering problems without modification.

articles.title: Quantum structured light: Non-classical spin texture of twisted single-photon pulses
articles.abstract: arXiv:2102.13248v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Classical structured light with controlled polarization and orbital angular momentum (OAM) of electromagnetic waves has varied applications in optical trapping, bio-sensing, optical communications and quantum simulations. The classical electromagnetic theory of such structured light beams and pulses have advanced significantly over the last two decades. However, a framework for the quantum density of spin and OAM for single-photons remains elusive. Here, we develop a theoretical framework and put forth the concept of quantum structured light for space-time wavepackets at the single-photon level. Our work marks a paradigm shift beyond scalar-field theory as well as the paraxial approximation and can be utilized to study the quantum properties of the spin and OAM of all classes of twisted quantum light pulses. We capture the uncertainty in full three-dimensional (3D) projections of vector spin demonstrating their quantum behavior beyond the conventional concept of classical polarization. Even in laser beams with high OAM along the propagation direction, we predict the existence of large OAM quantum fluctuations in the transverse plane which can be verified experimentally. We show that the spin density generates modulated helical texture beyond the paraxial limit and exhibits distinct statistics for Fock-state vs. coherent-state twisted pulses. We introduce the quantum correlator of photon spin density to characterize the nonlocal spin noise providing a rigorous parallel with fermionic spin noise operators. Our work paves the way for quantum spin-OAM physics in twisted single photon pulses and also opens explorations for new phases of light with long-range spin order.

articles.title: Non-Ambipolarity of Microturbulent Transport
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.15661v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: When exact magnetic surfaces are assumed to exist, the gyrokinetic theory of microturbulence gives the same radial transport for ions and electrons. But, exact magnetic surfaces do not exist in the presence of what is called electrostatic microturbulence. When the plasma pressure is non-zero, a turbulent electric potential is accompanied by a turbulent magnetic field, which splits the rational magnetic surfaces with which it resonates. If the magnetic field is assumed to have an ideal topology-conserving evolution, delta function current densities arise on resonant surfaces. The singularity of the current density allows islands to open quickly, but there is no singularity that allows a rapid closure. Islands remain and do not flutter into and out of existence. A relative rotation of the electron fluid in neighboring island chains produces a non-dissipative force that can lock the islands together and produce a non-ambipolar transport. At sufficient plasma pressure, the islands associated with different resonant rational surfaces can overlap. When this occurs some magnetic field lines will cross the entire radial region occupied by overlapping islands. The effect on the electron fluid is to create a viscosity-like force, which is dissipative and tends to remove gradients in the electron rotation. This also produces a non-ambipolar transport. Under many assumptions, the island locking force is larger than the viscosity-like force.

articles.title: A Non-Foster Superconducting Broadband Matching Network
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.10039v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The nonlinear inductance of the Josephson junction has enabled the development of a wide range of continuous-variable amplifiers and qubit-based devices with unprecedented sensitivity. We present an alternative use of the Josephson junction in the context of broadband impedance matching. The idea poses a potential solution to a longstanding problem in the field of high energy particle physics. The axion, a compelling candidate for the dark matter, converts to a weak electromagnetic signal at an as-yet unknown frequency. As such, the ideal axion detector does not compromise bandwidth for sensitivity, a trade-off intrinsic to all linear, time-invariant and passive circuits. We propose a circuit that uses a Josephson junction in an impedance matching network to overcome these gain-bandwidth constraints and increase the scan rate of axion searches. The Josephson junction can be biased to exhibit negative inductance capable of canceling geometric inductance similar to a capacitor but across a wider frequency range.

articles.title: Data-driven synthesis of high-fidelity triaxial magnetic waveforms for quantum control
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.24052v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a system for generating arbitrary, triaxial magnetic waveforms with a spectral content spanning from DC to tens of kHz, a critical capability for quantum control and spin manipulation. To compensate for amplifier-coil dynamics, we implement a data-driven approach to identify a numerical compensation model. The method parametrizes the system response using a Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter calibrated on the specific waveform to be generated. The application of a driving signal designed via frequency-domain inversion of the identified model enables the synthesis of complex field sequences with sharp transitions between static and single- or multi-frequency temporal segments. The work is validated with experimental results demonstrating waveform fidelity and transient performance, thereby showcasing the precision and feasibility of the method.

articles.title: Generalization of the Froissart-Stora formula to piecewise-linear spin-orbit resonance crossings
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.24510v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spin-polarized beams are important for some nuclear and high-energy physics experiments, such as those planned for the future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). However, maintaining polarization during the acceleration of a charged-particle beam is difficult because the periodic nature of circular accelerators leads to spin-orbit resonances where the spin-precession frequency is a sum of integer multiples of the orbital frequencies. Usually, the dominant depolarization mechanisms are first-order spin-orbit resonances and the depolarization associated with crossing such a resonance can be computed using the Froissart-Stora formula. However, accelerating polarized hadron beams to high energy requires special magnet structures called Siberian snakes. When these are implemented to maintain a spin-precession frequency of one-half the revolution frequency, there will be no first-order spin-orbit resonance crossings. The dominant depolarization mechanisms are then higher-order spin-orbit resonances. The Froissart-Stora formula can be applied to higher-order resonances when the slope of the amplitude-dependent spin tune is constant. However, the slope of the amplitude-dependent spin tune often changes at the moment of resonance crossing. This work introduces a generalization of the Froissart-Stora formula which is applicable when the slope changes in this manner. The applicability of this formula is demonstrated through tracking simulations of a higher-order resonance crossing in both a toy model and the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC). It is additionally shown that the Froissart-Stora formula is mathematically equivalent to the Landau-Zener formula for the diabatic transition probability in two-level systems with a linearly increasing energy gap and constant coupling. This work therefore also extends the Landau-Zener formula to the case of changing slope.

articles.title: Pfirsch-Schlüter Current
articles.abstract: arXiv:2605.21637v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Pfirsch-Schlüter current is a current that flows along the magnetic field lines in a toroidal plasma equilibrium that is required to make the plasma current density divergence free in the presence of a plasma-pressure gradient. A distortion in the plasma shape is caused by the Pfirsch-Schlüter current, and it is desirable to minimize both the strength and the distance this current flows along the magnetic field lines. The Pfirsch-Schlüter current is localized within a half period of a stellarator when dell/B integrated over the half period is the same for all lines in the magnetic surface. It is shown that within parts in a thousand this is the same condition as the distance ellₛ required for a field line to cross the half period being the same for all lines in the surface. To make the ellₛ's the same, the lines started on the small major radius side of the plasma must undergo wiggles to make their ellₛ as long as those started on the outboard side. This is generally achieved using modular coils with a large helical component on the small major radius side but could be achieved with a central column carrying a helical current.

articles.title: Enabling quantum communication in ultra-large-scale networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.08326v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The recent development of small-scale quantum networks poses the question of which network-level mechanisms could enable quantum communication to operate at scale in a future Quantum Internet. The question can be answered within a well-established framework where a quantum network is mapped into a classical weighted graph, and communication reliability is assessed using methods from network theory. Previous work relied on this framework to determine sufficient conditions for viable network-wide communication only on special network topologies, such as regular lattices, and to devise communication protocols applicable only to small- and moderate-sized real networks. Here, we overcome both limitations by introducing a family of quantum communication protocols that scale to networks with hundreds of millions of nodes. We show that the competition between increasing communication distance and path redundancy determines their large-scale behavior, and that degree heterogeneity can provide sufficient redundancy to sustain communication in small-world networks. These conclusions are supported by a systematic analysis of both real network topologies and synthetic networks, and an analytical treatment in the limit of infinitely large random scale-free graphs.

articles.title: Super-resolution technique enabled by higher-order Bessel beams in nanoscale optical structures
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.17458v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In conventional optical microscopy, accessing subwavelength information is classically constrained by the Abbe diffraction limit which remains a significant challenge in nanophotonics. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a scheme that generates a tightly confined near-field focal spot under non-diffracting Bessel beam illumination, employing a series of high refractive-index nanoscale structures. Furthermore, the utilization of higher-order Bessel beams enables additional resolution enhancement beyond the diffraction limit. Our results demonstrate that the pyramidal nanostructure can generate a highly localized near-field confinement with a characteristic width of 10 nm, enabling subwavelength optical intensity localization. To elucidate the factors governing the localization behaviour, we systematically investigate the influence of different geometrical parameters related to the incident Bessel beam on the near field localization and shows that these factors critically determine the stability and spatial profile of the focal spot. These findings highlight the potential of the proposed approach for various applications in super-resolution techniques and quantum technology.

articles.title: Rapid Vacuum Response Calculations for Non-axisymmetric Plasma Geometries
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.00536v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a fast, open-source calculation of the vacuum response matrix and surface inductance in non-axisymmetric geometries capable of running with up to 10⁵ boundary points in tens of seconds on a laptop. Ideal magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) stability modeling for free boundary modes requires the perturbed vacuum energy. We extend the VACUUM code to non-axisymmetric geometries in the new Julia implementation of the Generalized Perturbed Equilibrium Code, combining a collocation approach to the boundary integral equations with a high-order singularity correction scheme. The correction is recast into explicit quadrature weights acting on the collocation values, which allows the corrected operator to be assembled explicitly rather than applied to a given surface field, and the structure of that matrix under field-period and stellarator symmetry is then exploited to reduce storage and solve cost. We find that the vacuum response matrix converges at fourth order or greater in the grid spacing, reaching a given accuracy on a coarser grid than previous implementations without the high-order method. The non-axisymmetric calculation converges to the axisymmetric VACUUM result for a tokamak and the CAS3D result for a W7-X stellarator equilibrium. This work enables fast free boundary ideal MHD stability and perturbed equilibrium calculations in stellarators.

articles.title: Surveying exogenous species in Saturn with ALMA I. Detecting and Mapping CO
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.05090v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The origin of carbon monoxide (CO) in Saturn's stratosphere remains uncertain, with proposed sources including internal thermochemical production, cometary impacts, and exogenic material from the rings and icy moons (i.e. Enceladus). We aim to constrain the vertical and meridional distribution of stratospheric CO and assess the relative contributions of these potential sources. Here, we analysed high-spectral-resolution ALMA observations of the CO (J=3-2) line obtained on 25 May 2018, sampling Saturn's limb from 20degS to 69degN. CO vertical profiles were retrieved using a line-by-line radiative transfer model combined with spectral inversion techniques, testing multiple prior scenarios representative of different source hypotheses. CO is confined to a narrow layer between 0.1 and 1 mbar, with a robust negative vertical gradient and mean abundances of (3.7+/- 0.8) x 10⁻⁸ at 0.1 mbar and (7.2 +/- 0.9) x 10⁻⁸ at 1 mbar. The meridional distribution is statistically homogeneous, with a marginal enhancement near 60deg N plausibly related to Enceladus. No significant equatorial enhancement is detected. The absence of a strong equatorial enhancement rules out a long-lived steady source associated with ring infall. The observations are most consistent with a relatively recent (approx200-year-old or younger) cometary impact whose material has since been horizontally mixed, while any Cassini Grand Finale ring influx was either too recent or inefficient to affect CO abundances at the probed pressure levels.

articles.title: Hamiltonian Chaos
articles.abstract: arXiv:2604.12976v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Through semiclassical methods the subject of quantum chaos motivates and depends on Hamiltonian chaos research. Presented here is a selection of some of the most important Hamiltonian chaos topics that in this way get directly related to any of a variety of quantum chaos research problems. The overall emphasis is on intuitive explanations and illustrations of various ideas with the references containing more mathematically rigorous expositions. The chapter begins with a description of various useful theoretical and computational tools of chaos research, e.g.~surfaces of section, paradigms of chaos, stability analysis, and symbolic dynamics... This is followed by discussions regarding the geometry of chaos, how chaotic systems respond to perturbations, and the complexification of Hamiltonian dynamics. Most of the contents concern topics that are long established and well known by now. The exceptions involve complications that arise from the complexification of phase space variables and time. There are relatively recent results summarized regarding the appropriate branches of determinant phases and how to distinguish complex trajectories that are associated with classically allowed processes versus those associated with non-allowed ones.

articles.title: Nonthermal Particle Acceleration by Magnetic Pumping in Pulsating Plasmas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2606.05286v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a new pulsating box setup to investigate particle acceleration in high-beta plasmas undergoing compression--expansion cycles. Our fully kinetic simulations show that particles are efficiently accelerated by magnetic pumping, producing nonthermal energy distributions with power-law tails. Numerical results are in excellent agreement with a generalized maximum entropy model that we derive, linking the power-law index of distributions to the injected energy. Our results could be relevant for understanding the origin of high-energy particles in certain high-beta space and astrophysical plasmas.

articles.title: Relativistic Chiral MHD with application to the early Universe
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.22816v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a systematic derivation of the equations of relativistic chiral magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) for a plasma of charged fermions in an expanding universe. Through a combination of a coordinate transformation and a rescaling of the dynamical variables, we bring the full system to the same form as in the Minkowski metric, with the Hubble expansion surviving only in the chirality-flipping rate and the kinematic viscosity. Retaining all four contributions to both the electric and the axial current yields terms absent from standard chiral MHD: charge-density corrections to the evolution equations for the chemical potentials, and an electric current proportional to the charge chemical potential μ and the bulk velocity. The latter is mandated by current conservation, requires no chirality imbalance, and drives the charge-flow instability studied in a follow-up paper. For the radiation-dominated era, we evaluate all the coefficients in physical units and use them to estimate the magnetic Reynolds number, the attainable magnetic field strength, and the minimum temperature at which the chiral dynamo can operate. The resulting equations are cast in a form ready for direct numerical implementation.

articles.title: The Natural Formulation of Cubic-Phase Dynamics in the Linear Potential
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.25627v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A quantum wave packet in a linear potential, i.e. a constant force such as gravity, accumulates a cubic-in-time phase, universal across Schrödinger-type platforms. The natural formulation of the cubic phase dynamics follows from their canonical realization, the Airy eigenstates. The eigenforce, the potential gradient for which the Airy profile is stationary and hence the intrinsic force behind its known self-acceleration absent any applied force, derives from the eigenvalue problem and characterizes the state uniquely up to a rigid translation. Alongside the applied force, it underlies the analytically closed form of these dynamics, comprising three known contributions, intrinsic, force-induced, and a cross term. The force-induced one alone is shape-independent, whereas the Airy eigenstate renders the other two non-dispersing. The cubic coefficient factorizes into two Newtonian force balances, vanishing at the stationary eigenstate and at a non-trivial zero where the phase cancels while the packet keeps accelerating. This exposes the eigenforce as an effective antagonist to the applied force, not only in the caustic's self-acceleration but here also within the phase, while leaving the centroid untouched by Ehrenfest's theorem. Spatially uniform within each packet, it escapes direct measurement, accessible only as the relative phase of two colliding packets, each in its own potential. The relative cubic coefficient is symmetry-forbidden for identical packets and activated by preparation asymmetry. Simulated interference of two truncated Airy packets demonstrates the extraction. Spanning ultracold atoms, paraxial optics, and surface-gravity water waves, it provides a platform-independent probe of the cubic phase and, through its force dependence, of the constant force itself.

articles.title: Jaxnasium: Embracing PyTrees For Any-Agent, Cross-Suite Reinforcement Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hardware-accelerated reinforcement learning in JAX has gained rapid popularity in recent years and has proven to be a successful method of scaling online reinforcement learning. The resulting ecosystem, however, is fragmented: environment suites define their own interfaces, and algorithm implementations are typically written for a single suite, a single type of space, and either JAX-native or host-based environments. Here we present Jaxnasium, a library for JAX-based reinforcement learning, aiming to make the field more accessible. Jaxnasium represents observation and action spaces as PyTrees, and uses this structure to build networks and support multi-agent processing. Through this, its near-single-file implementations run on discrete, continuous, image, and composite spaces, as well as in multi-agent environments, without any changes to the algorithm code. The same files serve as readable, research-friendly algorithms, as well as importable algorithms for more applied workloads. Through a minimal Gymnasium-style interface and wrappers for 11 suites, over 300 environments are available on which a small PPO implementation with default hyperparameters is able to run. Additionally, through a simple wrapper, we can run Gymnasium and EnvPool environments with the same algorithm and training loop, with no performance loss compared to architectures specifically built for training JAX algorithms on host-based environments. Jaxnasium further provides tools for multi-seed evaluation, hyperparameter sweeps, and project scaffolding. Jaxnasium is open-sourced at https://github.com/ponseko/jaxnasium

articles.title: Scaling and Renormalization in Neural Networks: An Effective Renormalization-Group Description of Grokking
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Grokking is a delayed transition from memorization to generalization in deep neural networks (NNs). We examine whether scaling and renormalization group (RG) theories can describe this dynamics, establishing a quantitative physical framework for neural generalization transitions. For modular addition on a two-layer NN, an ensemble of trained models defines an order parameter (the squared weight norm) and fluctuation proxies for the heat capacity and the susceptibility, with training epoch and weight decay serving as thermal and field control coordinates. To bridge neural architectures to real-space RG, we construct an exact coupling matrix via a second-order expansion of the loss with respect to per-neuron norms and use its Fiedler vector to define an effective geometry. This spectral ordering yields a monotonic spatial decay of coupling strength that is absent under random permutations. We then execute real-space RG by block-spin aggregating adjacent neurons and parameterizing the coupling matrix into off-diagonal band strengths. Linearizing this local RG map yields relevant scaling exponents and five derived critical exponents, with direct empirical estimates matching RG predictions within 1-10%. Overall, our framework provides a consistent effective description of grokking, suggesting the scaling and renormalization group formalism as a tool to investigate NN dynamics.

articles.title: Concorde: Geometry-Aware Link Prediction via Decoupled Energy Minimization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36204v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Link prediction remains difficult in sparse graphs, where diffusion heuristics lack connectivity and geometric methods suffer spectral instability when coupling learned representations with diffusion operators. We introduce Concorde, an energy-based framework that resolves this by decomposing link likelihood into three structurally decoupled branches: (i) a parameter-free spectral anchor that establishes permutation-invariant topological stability; (ii) a mixed-curvature residual on a learnable Hdₕc_ₕ × Sdₛc_ₛ product manifold, regularized by a feature-aware Ollivier-Ricci curvature proxy; and (iii) a continuous vector field on the tangent bundle of hyperbolic space for non-local structural alignment across topological gaps. The branches are fused via learned gating and trained with an N-pair ranking loss aligned with retrieval-style evaluation. Across five benchmarks spanning sparse, dense, featureless, and attributed regimes, Concorde establishes state-of-the-art early retrieval precision, nearly doubling P@10% over leading baselines in sparse settings.

articles.title: CoHARL: Co-Evolving Agent Policies and Executable Harnesses with Reinforcement Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36469v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents interact with their environments through executable harnesses that govern tool use and feedback. Optimizing a harness for a fixed policy overlooks how its behavior changes during learning, while training a policy under a fixed harness leaves the interface that generates its training experience unchanged. This motivates adapting the harness throughout policy training. We introduce CoHARL, a population-based reinforcement learning framework that co-evolves a shared policy and a population of executable harnesses. The policy learns from rollouts across the population, and a proposer uses its execution traces to revise harness code during training. CoHARL achieves a 27.6% mean resolved rate on SWE-rebench, improving over harness-only search by 6.4 percentage points. Experiments on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0 show gains in software engineering and terminal-based tasks. Under matched training budgets, CoHARL also outperforms searching for a harness once before RL and alternating policy updates with revisions to a single active harness.

articles.title: Underdamped Anchored Langevin Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical Langevin Monte Carlo algorithms, such as the unadjusted Langevin algorithm (ULA), are based on discretization schemes of the overdamped Langevin dynamics and are widely used for sampling in machine learning because they scale to high dimensions and large datasets. However, they require differentiable log-densities, and are less efficient for sampling heavy-tailed distributions. Although various approaches have been proposed in the literature for sampling non-differentiable and heavy-tailed targets, all of them are developed in the overdamped setting only. We propose a novel momentum-based underdamped anchored Langevin dynamics (UALD), and underdamped anchored Langevin Monte Carlo (UALMC) algorithm based on a discretization scheme of UALD. Our paper is the first to provide a kinetic (momentum-based) Langevin algorithm for non-differentiable and heavy-tailed targets that is free of asymptotic bias. The method replaces the original potential with a smooth reference potential and modifies the underdamped Langevin dynamics via multiplicative scaling in the drift term. We establish non-asymptotic guarantees in the 2-Wasserstein distance to the target distribution and show that the resulting iteration complexity has better dependence on dimension and accuracy level compared to overdamped-based anchored Langevin algorithms. We provide numerical experiments to illustrate the theory and practical performance of our proposed approach.

articles.title: Generative Refinement Learning for Temporal Interpolation in Scientific Machine Learning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.36751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computationally expensive simulations and real-world observations often provide data at a lower temporal resolution than downstream tasks require. Averaging observations at fixed grid points can introduce errors, and motion estimates alone do not determine how the physical field values change. In this work, we study whether learning to correct a simple numerical interpolation improves the reconstruction of intermediate scientific fields. Our model, interpolative FLow EXpert (iFLEX), first estimates the missing field by taking a weighted average of the two observations at each grid point, giving more weight to the observation closer to the requested time. During training, subtracting this estimate from an observed intermediate field gives the residual that a conditional diffusion model learns to generate. Both observations condition the model, together with the target time, the interval between observations, and available physical parameters. To reconstruct an unobserved intermediate field, the generated residual is added to the weighted average. We evaluate iFLEX on Navier-Stokes Kraichnan turbulence, Shanghai radar precipitation, and sea surface temperature. Across these datasets, iFLEX achieves lower reconstruction error than the evaluated baselines, including optical-flow and diffusion models developed for video frame interpolation in computer vision. In a controlled turbulence comparison at a Reynolds number of 36,000, learning the residual reduces relative Frobenius norm error from about 13.7 for direct field generation to 10.5, with the diffusion backbone and training setup held fixed. Code is available at https://github.com/paulpuren/iflex.

articles.title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language model agents are post-trained and deployed through a harness, the prompts, tools, and control logic that present a task to the model and execute its outputs. Harnesses are often revised and judged by how an already trained model performs under them, which assumes that what the model learned under one harness carries over to the next. We ask what a policy learns from its harness and what survives when the harness changes. Under KL-regularized control, we show that the log odds of an optimal policy recover how strongly its harness favors each action over the others, so a trained policy carries the preferences of its harness. Deployed return then equals the ceiling of the harness, the best return it offers, minus the mismatch of the policy, the return lost to its own suboptimal decisions. Training changes only the mismatch, while changing the harness moves both terms. Comparing harnesses with a fixed model therefore mixes what each harness offers with how well that model uses it. In MiniWoB++, post-training makes a model's preferences specific to its training harness. Reversing the order of the observation fields leaves every optimal decision unchanged yet lowers a trained model's success from 85.0% to 19.2%. Conversely, every new harness that a fixed-model comparison rejects but that raises the ceiling outperforms the original agent after further training under it, and ceiling and mismatch measured beforehand predict these gains. For coding-agent harnesses on Terminal-Bench Lite, ceiling minus mismatch estimated with a stronger model as a stand-in for the optimum reproduces the accuracy ranking, while either term alone does not. Code is available at https://github.com/2020-qqtcg/HRP.

articles.title: Structured Representation Probing for Risk Anticipation in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: End-to-end driving policies form structured internal representations of traffic, ego behavior, and road constraints. These representations offer a monitoring interface for anticipating failures, complementing risk signals from trajectories, controls, and manually designed features. We introduce the Structured Representation Probe (SRP), a lightweight monitor that reads actor, ego, and map representations from a frozen policy. SRP learns a separate linear risk direction for each source and aggregates element scores through cardinality-normalized log-mean-exp pooling, retaining sensitivity to salient evidence while reducing dependence on token count. Event-window supervision links the readout to upcoming hard failures, and auxiliary event type heads jointly train the source directions across failure modes. Online alerting uses a single generic score without modifying the driving policy. Bench2Drive experiments on DriveTransformer, UniAD, and VAD show higher frame-level PR-AUC and ROC-AUC than the evaluated runtime baselines. On DriveTransformer at a horizon of 2 seconds, ROC-AUC reaches 0.833 versus 0.715 for temporal consistency, with 2.67% readout runtime overhead. The trained probes also retain the ability to distinguish impending failures on new routes.

articles.title: Displacement Moments and Path-Terminal Separation in Brownian Interpolant Sampling
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.37413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Brownian stochastic interpolants connect paired endpoint samples, yet their sampling error can depend on displacement moments even when neither endpoint has a first moment.
