Currently, polarized X-rays with tunable polarization and photon energy are available only in large facilities like synchrotrons. Here, we theoretically predict and experimentally demonstrate the generation of linearly polarized X-rays from free electron-driven van der Waals crystals, without the need for additional optical stages like polarizers. We show that precise, real-time control over the polarization can be achieved by simply re-orienting the van der Waals crystal. Furthermore, we show that a high degree of polarization can be achieved across all polarization angles - from perpendicular to in-plane - with intensities exceeding 10⁹ photons s⁽⁻¹⁾ sr⁽⁻¹⁾ mA⁽⁻¹⁾. Using our findings, we present a scheme for table-top XANES, achieving performance comparable to that of synchrotron facilities. In the process, we develop a new methodology for performing XANES using high-quality polarized X-rays with larger spectral linewidths, named ORIXANES (Orientation-controlled XANES). Our findings pave the way to greater accessibility and smaller carbon footprint for advanced X-ray modalities.

articles.title: Wave-branch classification of ideal MHD discontinuities in Q-variables
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Q-variable formalism combines velocity and magnetic field into branches aligned with a selected MHD wave. For homogeneous ideal MHD, appropriate choices of the branch parameter α correspond to the fast, Alfvén, and slow characteristic families, with the background variables boldsymbolQ₀± representing the propagation direction and speed of the corresponding characteristics. In structured plasmas, α may instead be selected from the dispersion relation of a global mode such as a kink wave. Recent work reformulated the ideal-MHD Rankine-Hugoniot conditions in Q-variables and established their exact equivalence with the classical conservative jump conditions. Here, we apply this formulation to the standard ideal-MHD discontinuity catalogue. We determine how the two discontinuity-frame branches boldsymbolQprⁱme⁺ and boldsymbolQprⁱme⁻, their sums, and their α-normalised differences are constrained across contact, tangential, and rotational discontinuities and across the principal shock families. Material interfaces are distinguished by their normal branch content, rotational discontinuities by an Alfvénic tangential relation, and fast, slow, and intermediate shocks by the magnitude or orientation of the α-normalised tangential branch difference. Perpendicular, parallel, switch-on, and switch-off shocks appear as geometrical or limiting cases. The resulting classification expresses the classical discontinuity conditions in a wave-aligned form and, through the characteristic interpretation of boldsymbolQ₀±, shows how ideal-MHD discontinuities constrain changes in characteristic propagation direction and speed across the interface. It therefore establishes the background interface structure required for subsequent studies of reflection, transmission, coupling, and mode conversion.

articles.title: Accurate measurement of Lithium Tantalate birefringence in whispering gallery resonators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lithium Tantalate (LTA) is an important ferroelectric crystal widely used in piezoelectric, electro-optic, and nonlinear optical devices. Although this crystal is very common, there is an ongoing debate regarding its birefringence magnitude, and even its sign. While some sources claim it to be negative, others maintain that it is positive. The issue is further complicated by the sample-to-sample variation in the crystal composition, ranging from congruent to stoichiometric. Here we report the experimental exploration of this question based on high-resolution spectroscopy of optical whispering gallery resonators fabricated from this crystal. These sensitive measurements unambiguously indicate that in the near-infrared range at room temperature the stoichiometric LTA is negative, while the congruent LTA is positive.

articles.title: Generalization of the Rosenbluth-Putvinski avalanche growth rate to the drift kinetic regime
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A new collisionless detrapping mechanism is shown to modify the rate of runaway electron (RE) generation by as much as a factor of two for strong inductive electric fields. This detrapping mechanism results from the magnetic well inherent to tokamak geometry being tilted by the strong inductive electric fields present during tokamak disruptions. The impact of this collisionless detrapping mechanism is found to be described by a single dimensionless parameter, whose identification enables the transition between distinct regimes of RE generation to be characterized. Using this composite parameter, it is shown that modifications to the avalanche growth rate by tokamak geometry across a broad range of plasma parameters collapse onto a one-dimensional curve that can be accurately fit with a two parameter function. The resulting analytical formula extends the classic Rosenbluth-Putvinski avalanche growth rate expression beyond the bounce-averaged limit into RE regimes where collisionless detrapping strongly modifies RE generation rates.

articles.title: Nonreciprocal magneto-optic beam steering of thermal emission
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which ties absorptivity to emissivity and places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies and sensing systems. This constraint can be overcome using magneto-optic materials, which exhibit nonreciprocal thermal emission under an applied magnetic field. While the spectral nonreciprocity of magneto-optic devices has been explored theoretically and experimentally, nonreciprocal control over the direction of thermal emission has received far less attention. Here, we propose and numerically demonstrate nonreciprocal beam steering of thermal emission, wherein an applied magnetic field lifts the degeneracy between guided modes at +/- kx, enabling asymmetric and tunable directional thermal emission. We highlight a III-V semiconductor photonic structure operating at 24.5 um, a wavelength with few laser sources. This structure exhibits a nonreciprocity greater than 0.5 between +/- 75 degrees at 50 mT, a peak emissivity asymmetry over 0.6 at 150 mT, and 22 degrees of beam steering between 0 and 1 T. Our approach provides a solid-state means of steering a thermal beam, offering a potential route to magnetically controlled beam scanning of incandescent sources.

articles.title: Identification of rippling interface between laser-ablated plasma and ambient uniform plasma at rest
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present laboratory experiments on the early stage of the formation process of quasi-perpendicular supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks using laser-produced plasmas in an ambient uniform nitrogen (N) gas with 1~Torr under the external magnetic field with controlled polarity. An expanding aluminum (Al) piston plasma arising from laser irradiation interacts with a magnetized ambient N plasma, producing a bright, asymmetric self-emission whose global morphology reverses with the magnetic-field polarity. Two-dimensional ideal-magnetohydrodynamics simulations reproduce the main features of the observed structures and indicate that the ripple formation is unlikely to be driven by the Kelvin--Helmholtz instability, but is instead associated with vortex formation at the rounded leading edge of the piston plasma. We show that the bright, rippling emission delineates the Al-N interface, whose intrinsic width is consistent with an electron kinetic scale, and that its upstream side is predominantly composed of N plasma. This identification allows the formation of a supercritical collisionless shock in the magnetized N plasma to be discussed with minimal Al contamination.

articles.title: Experimental Evidence for Reflected Ions and Ion Temperature Anisotropy in a Forming Supercritical Magnetized Collisionless Shock
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks require ion reflection for dissipation, yet its role during formation remains unclear. Using high-power lasers, self-emission imaging, and collective Thomson scattering, we investigate a forming quasi-perpendicular shock. An upstream emission tail is consistent with a foot-like structure, while ion heating and temperature anisotropy extend upstream of a ramp-like region. These observations provide evidence of reflected-ion-related heating during early shock formation, although the incident and reflected ion populations are not separately resolved. Future measurements of ion distributions and plasma waves could clarify how this heating mediates shock dissipation and particle energization.

articles.title: Clustering Templates: A Data-Driven Framework for Dimensionality Reduction and Compression of Brain Strain in Head Impact
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Purpose: Finite element (FE) models are indispensable for studying the biomechanics of traumatic brain injury (TBI), and modern head FE models typically comprise thousands to millions of elements. The resulting brain strain is therefore high-dimensional, and when combined with dense temporal sampling and large numbers of head impact cases, this produces datasets of substantial data volume. Accordingly, this study investigates the effective dimensionality required to accurately represent brain strain and proposes a data-driven framework to reduce the dimensionality of FE simulation data while maintaining high spatiotemporal fidelity. Methods: We developed a series of "clustering templates" by applying K-means clustering to feature vectors derived from the maximum principal strain (MPS) time-history curves of 118,840 brain elements over 3,693 impact simulations using the THUMS head model. The performance of these templates, with cluster counts (K) ranging from 8 to 8192, was rigorously evaluated by quantifying the fidelity of data reconstruction. Results: The clustering templates demonstrated high-fidelity reconstruction of the original FE data. A template with K = 512 achieved a compression ratio of over 200:1 while maintaining a low mean element-wise peak MPS root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.027, and a template with K = 4096 (30:1 compression ratio) achieved an RMSE of 0.016. Conclusion: The proposed clustering templates provide an effective and automated method for the dimensionality reduction and compression of large-scale brain strain data. This framework mitigates critical data management bottlenecks and enables the development of subsequent data analysis and machine learning models, thereby accelerating research in TBI biomechanics.

articles.title: Suppression of Sedimentation in Polystyrene Microsphere Suspensions via Femtosecond Laser Irradiation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Micrometer-sized particles denser than their medium settle out of suspension within hours, and Brownian motion is too weak to prevent it. We report that femtosecond laser irradiation at 1030 nm slows this settling in suspensions of 8 um polystyrene microspheres in water, without altering the particles themselves. Suspensions at three concentrations were treated for up to 3 h under weak acoustic agitation or vigorous magnetic stirring, each with and without simultaneous irradiation, and the particles remaining in the probe volume were quantified optically by angle-resolved Mie scattering. Under acoustic agitation, irradiation raised retention in eleven of twelve paired comparisons, at every concentration, by 0.17 on average against a measured aliquot-to-aliquot scatter of 0.02; the twelfth comparison lies within that scatter. Under stirring, which already keeps most particles suspended, it produces no resolvable change. The angular positions of the Mie maxima are unchanged to within about 1% over 3 h, so the particles are neither fragmented nor aggregated and the effect arises from particle transport rather than from changes in the particles. An order-of-magnitude analysis rules out optical forces, the optical Kerr effect, and transient photochemistry, and leaves laser-driven convection: the power absorbed by the water sustains flows orders of magnitude faster than the 1.8 um/s settling velocity. Femtosecond irradiation therefore acts as a non-contact, supplementary agitation source, most effective where mechanical mixing is weak.

articles.title: Yb/Sr optical clock comparison at 2.2E-18 uncertainty over a 1350-km fiber link
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Redefining the International system of Units (SI) second requires independent frequency-ratio measurements between clocks based on different laboratories, with an overall uncertainty below 5E-18, to validate individual clock evaluations through consistency checks. Reaching this uncertainty over long distances has remained challenging. So far, comparisons at this level have been achieved only a few times, between co-located clocks, and their results disagree markedly. Previous high-precision comparisons have therefore been limited to local or kilometre-scale links. Here we compare a ytterbium optical lattice clock in Wuhan with a strontium optical lattice clock in Shanghai over a phase-stabilized fiber link spanning 1350 km, and determine the Yb/Sr frequency ratio to be 1.207 507 039 343 337 716 0(26), with a Bayesian statistical uncertainty of 1.14E-18 and a total uncertainty of 2.18E-18. To our knowledge, this is the first intercity long distance frequency-ratio measurement, whose total uncertainty reaches the level required by the redefinition roadmap. The measured ratio exhibits a significant correlation with Earth tides and its response agree with the model within the statistical uncertainty. At intercity scale, this comparison demonstrates the capability of an optical-clock network for frequency comparison and Earths gravitational-potential sensing, a key step toward a wide-area optical-clock network.

articles.title: Second order N-Electron Valence state Perturbation Theory for polaritonic systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecules strongly coupled to optical cavities often show multi-configurational character, which the cavity can enhance by mixing electronic states. Describing them accurately requires a complete treatment of correlation between all the involved quantum particles. The available QED ab-initio methods do not treat it in its completeness except for QED-FCI. We extend second-order N-electron valence state perturbation theory (NEVPT2) to polaritonic chemistry, in its state-specific (QED-NEVPT2) and quasi degenerate (QED-QD-NEVPT2) forms. Here, the correlation due to the interaction of more degenerate configurations comes from a QED-CASSCF reference, while that associated with instantaneous interactions between the particles is added by second-order perturbation theory. Application of the methods to ammonia, ethylene and formaldimine revealed that this approach represents the perfect alternative to the well established QED-Coupled Cluster approach when the molecular system is described by more degenerate configurations. The approaches developed in this work have the potential to become state-of-the-art methodologies for the description of reactivity and photochemistry in polaritonic systems.

articles.title: Λ-Gravity from Entropy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34496v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Gravity from Entropy (GfE) theory treats the metric of spacetime as quantum operators and proposes the GfE action for gravity. The GfE Lagrangian is given by the Geometric Quantum Relative Entropy (GQRE) between the true metric and the metric induced by the matter fields and curvature. The theory leads to modified gravity equations and predicts the emergence of a dynamical cosmological constant ΛG. In the low energy, small curvature limit the GfE gravity equations reduce to Einstein equations with vanishing cosmological constant, i.e. in the weak field linear approximation ΛG vanishes. In this work, we propose a generalisation of the GfE theory, called Λ-Gravity from Entropy (ΛGfE). Following a thermodynamic approach, we introduce a Lagrange multiplier Λ to define the local volume of the theory. By enforcing local Weyl stationarity of the ΛGfE action modulo the volume constraint of the theory, we derive the equation for Λ. The ΛGfE equations of motion include two dark energy contributions: the emergent and dynamical contribution given by ΛG plus a constant contribution given by Λ where Λ can be identified with the cosmological constant in the low energy small curvature limit. While this theory cannot predict the exact value of Λ, here it is shown that the vacuum contributions to the dressed stress-energy tensor cancel from the trace-free equations of motion of the ΛGfE theory. Within the GfE framework, the ΛGfE also offers a novel interpretation of the dark energy terms, with potentially testable consequences for cosmological observations.

articles.title: Competitive exploration in structured environments
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Organisms must constantly weigh exploiting the resources they know against exploring for better ones. When foragers compete, the best behavior for each forager also depends on what its competitors do. How does competition change the strategic balance between exploration and exploitation? Here we address this question in a minimal model: two ϵ-greedy temporal-difference learners on a one-dimensional lattice, who start at a small reward at one end and are unaware of a larger reward at the other. For a lone forager, the optimal exploration rate increases monotonically with the value of the distant reward, and with its distance up to a critical distance. When two foragers share the lattice and split rewards, the choice of exploration rate becomes a game whose Nash equilibria have both foragers exploring, both staying, or one exploring while the other stays (anti-coordination). Under local best-response dynamics, pairs of foragers often converge on both exploring or both staying, even when anti-coordination would be socially optimal. This social dilemma arises for a wide range of parameters, and it persists even in a simplified model without explicit spatial structure. A minimal, naturalistic signal, in which one forager informs the other that it has found the distant reward, can remove many of the dilemmas in which both foragers explore, and can produce a Nash equilibrium whose collective payoff exceeds that of every outcome available without signaling.

articles.title: Explosive instability, quiet plasma: phase-space cascades, coherent vortices, and transport suppression in a dipole pair plasma
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Turbulence in a magnetised dipole pair plasma can transfer electrostatic energy into coherent flows while carrying entropy to small scales. This occurs via a dual cascade in a four-dimensional phase space, whereby advection by the fluctuating electric field nonlinearly phase-mixes the transit-averaged particle motion. Below a critical pressure gradient, zonal bands suppress the kinetic mode, leaving a transport floor. When the fluid mode is unstable, an explosive burst collapses into a zonal condensate on which two vortices "breathe" by reversible energy exchange, without causing net transport.

articles.title: Maximization of accelerated charge in multibunch-driven plasma wakefield accelerators
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Driving the plasma wakefield with a train of multiple particle bunches has the potential to significantly increase the accelerated charge, provided that the witness bunches also form a train. In this scenario, the driver bunches can replenish the wave energy after the passage of the witness bunches, yielding comparable charges in both trains. However, implementing this method at high wakefield amplitudes is complicated by the reshaping of the driver bunches as they reach radial equilibrium with the wave. The witness bunches cannot preserve their quality during this process; nevertheless, they must load the wave to prevent it from reaching the amplitude at which the wakefield period elongates and the wave destroys the driver. The proposed solution is to form an equilibrium train of initially inefficient driver bunches, which becomes efficient upon the injection of the witness bunches. This concept is demonstrated using the example of a self-modulating driver beam. Several factors favoring a high witness charge are identified: injecting additional ``phaser'' bunches at the zero-accelerating-field points, suppressing the formation of an electron halo around the plasma, and operating at the highest possible wakefield amplitudes.

articles.title: Rydberg atomic field-enhanced feed beyond electrically small antennas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The reception of electromagnetic signals becomes increasingly challenging at longer wavelengths, as conventional antenna feeds must scale with the operating wavelength, making it difficult to reconcile compactness with high sensitivity. Rydberg atoms enable direct field-to-optical conversion within deeply subwavelength sensing volumes, yet an effective receiving feed that couples incident fields into the atomic interaction volume remains underdeveloped. Here, we introduce a Rydberg atomic field-enhanced feed (RAFEF) that integrates electromagnetic field capture and enhancement with Rydberg-atomic transduction. We establish a physical model to quantify its receiving capability, Phi, that jointly accounts for sensitivity enhancement, receiving bandwidth and normalized three-dimensional volume, and experimentally obtain Phi_dB = 70.81 dB. Compared with a conventional loop-antenna feed, the RAFEF provides a higher received SNR and overall receiving capability, while its tunable narrowband response enables frequency selectivity directly at the receiving-feed stage. We further demonstrate selective recovery of a target channel from simultaneously incident signals and reception of a 93.5 MHz FM broadcast after approximately 10 km of over-the-air propagation. These results establish the RAFEF as an atomic receiving-feed architecture that exploits localized electric-field transduction to extend Rydberg-atomic reception beyond conventional electrically small antenna feeds.

articles.title: A Density-Matrix Formulation of Vibrational Circular Dichroism Spectra for Møller-Plesset and Configuration Interaction Methods
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We reformulate the overlap of wave-function derivatives that defines the atomic axial tensors (AATs) and velocity-gauge atomic polar tensors (VG-APTs) used to compute vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) rotatory strengths. In place of our earlier determinant-level derivatives, the new approach expresses these tensors as contractions involving molecular-orbital derivative integrals, perturbed and unperturbed one- and two-electron density matrices, and dot products of the perturbed correlated wave-function amplitudes. Following the elegant treatment of the diagonal Born-Oppenheimer correction by Gauss and co-workers, the formulation holds for any real, normalized CI-like wave function. The two-electron density contribution vanishes exactly, because one perturbation is real (nuclear) and the other imaginary (magnetic field or momentum); this removes multiple terms from our earlier AAT and VG-APT expressions for second-order Mø{}ller-Plesset perturbation theory (MP2) and configuration interaction singles and doubles (CISD). We also present a simplified form of the origin-independent length-gauge [LG(OI)] rotatory strength that avoids the singular-value decomposition of the outer product of the length-gauge APT and VG-APT vectors for each mode, and that clarifies how the LG(OI) and velocity-gauge rotatory strengths are related. Applying the density-based AATs and VG-APTs to (P)-hydrogen peroxide, (S)-methyloxirane, and (S)-3-chloro-1-butyne, we find that discrepancies among the gauges arise chiefly from basis-set incompleteness in the VG-APT. The charge-sum rule serves as a useful measure of that incompleteness, independent of the correlation method.

articles.title: Delayed maximum energy solar energetic particle events: Statistical analysis from Solar Orbiter
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Investigations of solar energetic particles (SEPs) have long utilized the dispersive nature of onset times, as in, the earlier arrival of higher-energy particles compared to lower-energy particles, to infer information such as the path length to the acceleration site at the time of initial particle release. However, recent observations by Solar Orbiter and Parker Solar Probe have begun to characterize SEP events with an apparent delay in arrival times of the higher energy portion of the particle distribution, above a critical energy separating the delayed particles from that of the typical velocity dispersion signature at lower energies. Features of these delayed maximum energy (DME) SEP events, sometimes referred to as "inverse velocity dispersion" events, could provide new insight into the impacts of magnetic connectivity to locations along an expanding coronal mass ejection-driven (CME-driven) shock wave, variations of acceleration along the shock surface, and transport effects in the inner heliosphere. This study focuses on the occurrence rate and characteristics of DME events observed by Solar Orbiter relative to their footpoint locations with respect to the initial flare site. These DME events show a bias in occurrence rate towards events when the observer's footpoints were westward of the associated flare location. Additionally, estimated locations at which the highest-energy particles of DME events are released into the flux tube suggest continued release of increasingly higher-energy particles from the CME-driven shock into the connected flux tube well into the inner heliosphere. This indicates that DME events could be attributed to inner heliospheric effects and are not actually coronal in origin. This finding is consistent with previous observations and interpretations of SEP events connected westward of the associated flare.

articles.title: Lanthanide Crystal Field Theory in the J-Mixing Regime: fⁿ Configurations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The low-energy sector of the lanthanide fⁿ shell is to first approximation governed by the interplay of three interactions: Coulomb repulsion, spin-same-orbit coupling and the ligand crystal field potential. To rationalize the energy landscape in different chemical environments, it is desirable to extract the phenomenological crystal field parameters from experimental data; however, in practice, high-dimensional fitting procedures complicate their routine determination. Here, we present a computational extraction procedure based on real tensorial sets and the U(7) canonical chain that, unlike existing operator equivalent methods, takes all J multiplets of the lowest-energy LS term into account, ensuring meaningful results even in the presence of considerable J-mixing. Two series of lanthanide compounds, [Ln(III)(C₈H₈)₂]⁻} and doped Ln(III):Y₂O₃} (Ln in Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu) serve as examples for high- (D₈ₕ) and low-symmetry (C₂) scenarios. Consequences for the generalisation toward actinides are briefly discussed.

articles.title: Scale-Dependent Statistics of Coherent Magnetic Structures in Early IMAP Observations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35634v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze early Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP) magnetic field observations (November 2025 to May 2026) to quantify the statistical properties of helical magnetic structures and their relationship with turbulence intermittency. Intermittent structures, such as current sheets, are identified using the Partial Variance of Increments (PVI) method, and the scale-dependent normalized magnetic helicity is computed over scales corresponding to 0.5-3 correlation lengths. Prior studies have typically applied the PVI-helicity method to individual events; here we extend this technique to the ensemble statistics of a multi-month sample spanning many correlation times. To separate coherent helical structures from random turbulent fluctuations, significance thresholds for helicity are determined using phase-randomized surrogate realizations. We find a clear scale dependence in the occurrence, duration, and waiting time of coherent magnetic helicity, reminiscent of the scale-transfer arguments underlying inverse cascade, selective decay, and Taylor relaxation theories. Event duration and waiting-time distributions are well described by power-law and exponential models over different ranges, consistent with previous findings. In addition, PVI and magnetic helicity are anticorrelated, suggesting that high-PVI regions are preferentially associated with the boundaries of flux ropes, while their interiors tend to exhibit lower PVI and stronger magnetic helicity.

articles.title: Plasma and light: Shaping High Harmonic Generation in Time-Varying Media
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High harmonic generation in solids is typically described under the assumption of a stationary medium. This assumption is rarely questioned because the electronic properties of most media evolve on timescales much slower than the harmonic emission process itself. However, in strongly driven time-varying transparent conductive oxides the plasma frequency, carrier density, and effective mass can evolve on the same femtosecond timescale as harmonic generation. Under these conditions, harmonic generation and material evolution are no longer independent processes. Within this context, we consider a two-field pumping scheme in which a strong field generates a comb of high-order harmonics across a broad spectral window, while a weaker field simultaneously reshapes its own individual spectral lines. Distinct from geometry-dependent wave-mixing processes, the evolving electron plasma reshapes multiple collinear harmonic channels simultaneously. A fully self-consistent hydrodynamic-Maxwell framework reveals that even- and odd-order harmonics naturally emerge from free- and bound-electron dynamics without the typical need to invoke phenomenological nonlinearities. Our model captures the full spectral evolution on an ultra-broad bandwidth, while experiments performed on ITO confirm the distinct behavior of bulk-driven odd harmonics and interface-driven even harmonics under strong pumping. These results establish time-dependent plasma dynamics as a powerful new tool for broadband hyperspectral shaping of multiple harmonic channels beyond the framework of four-wave-mixing processes. Our findings are of particular relevance to ultrafast science, with potential applications in ultrafast pulse manipulation and the generation and control of tailored multi harmonic waveforms.

articles.title: Tapering to Enhance the Performance of Nanowire-Based Fluorescent Biosensors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-refractive-index nanowires are of interest for signal enhancement in fluorescence-based biosensing. Here, through electromagnetic modelling, we demonstrate substantial fluorescence signal enhancement by incorporating a tapered section into a cylindrical nanowire and investigate two complementary tapering configurations to address practical implementation challenges. Under near-normal excitation, the excitation enhancement increases approximately linearly with taper length, reaching more than three times that of the corresponding non-tapered nanowire at a taper length of 8000 nm. In a non-imaging signal detection scheme using a low numerical aperture (NA), the proposed tapered nanowire achieves more than three orders of magnitude enhancement in fluorescence signal compared with a planar biosensor. Thus, the tapered nanowire should enable efficient fluorescence detection using compact, low-NA optical configuration. In imaging mode, similarly as for non-tapered nanowires, imaging sharpness beyond conventional microscopy limitations is obtained when imaging from the non-tapered nanowire end, while strongly increased excitation enhancement is simultaneously obtained when exciting from the opposite, tapered end.

articles.title: An Ab Initio Quantum-Chemistry-Based Three-Temperature Approach for Non-Equilibrium Hypersonic Flows: Application to Homogeneous 0-D Chemical Systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work presents an ab initio quantum-chemistry-based one-bin, three-temperature (1-bin 3T) model for non-equilibrium thermochemistry of homogeneous chemical systems in their electronic ground state, derived using the multi-group maximum-entropy principle. The proposed framework captures both vibrational and rotational non-equilibrium effects, thereby enabling an accurate representation of thermochemical behavior in high-temperature gases. To account for departures from equilibrium dissociation, a non-equilibrium correction factor derived from ro-vibrational State-to-State (StS) analysis is incorporated into the population distribution. Because this correction is constructed from the quasi-steady-state (QSS) distribution, the resulting model is valid only for systems and conditions under which the QSS assumption holds. The proposed 1-bin 3T model is validated across a broad range of zero-dimensional test cases through comparisons with high-fidelity StS simulations and Direct Molecular Simulations (DMS). The results demonstrate excellent agreement between the reduced-order model and high-fidelity approaches for both dissociating and recombining environments. Overall, the 1-bin 3T model shows strong potential as an efficient and accurate framework for modeling non-equilibrium thermochemical behavior, while keeping computational costs orders of magnitude lower than the high fidelity ro-vibrational StS simulations.

articles.title: On the Energy Minimizing Problem in Plasma Dynamics
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33040v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A fundamental question in plasma physics and its applications to fusion theory is to find minimum energy stares of plasma.. Hong Qin has suggested the use of what he calls "Gromov ground states" which take into account the phenomenon of symplectic rigidity, as opposed to Gardner's classical approach which only use volume-preserving diffeomorphisms. Howev4er Qin's approach leads to topological difficulties because his constructions remain in the classical (Hamiltonian) domain. We circumvent these difficulties by introducing a quantum-mechanical formulation of the problem, based on the Wigner transform and the symplectic geometry of Gaussian state

articles.title: Trapped sausage modes in magnetic pores: existence criteria and viscous damping
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33251v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The conditions governing the existence and evolution of trapped sausage waves in photospheric magnetic pores are investigated, with particular emphasis on the limitations of analytical cut-off criteria and the role of viscous dissipation. A pore is modelled as a cylindrical magnetic flux tube with smoothly varying radial profiles of magnetic field and density, subject to the constraint that its temperature is lower than that of the surrounding atmosphere. For finite plasma-β, the linearised equations governing sausage-mode perturbations are derived, and an initial-value problem is solved numerically to obtain the full spatio-temporal evolution of the waves. The applicability of the analytical cut-off relation derived for a flux tube with step-function equilibrium profiles is examined, revealing that its predictions depend on the equilibrium parameters. The simulations reveal distinct wave behaviours across different parameter regimes, including the simultaneous excitation of trapped fast and slow sausage waves for a representative photospheric parameter set. Viscous damping is further investigated through the temporal evolution of the wave energy. Energy dissipation increases with decreasing viscous Reynolds number, increasing longitudinal wavenumber, and increasing radial magnetic-field contrast. These trends are consistent with enhanced viscous damping associated with increasingly fine spatial gradients generated through phase mixing. The findings highlight the importance of radial equilibrium structure in assessing sausage-wave trapping and demonstrate the sensitivity of wave-energy dissipation to the physical parameters of photospheric magnetic pores.

articles.title: Real Time Motion Detection in Video Inspired by Photonic Time Stretch
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motion perception is fundamental to computer vision and physical AI, and plays a central role in robotics, autonomous vehicles, human-computer interaction, and video compression. Traditional approaches such as background subtraction, frame-differencing and optical flow algorithms often struggle in complex or dynamic scenes, typically sacrificing spatial resolution for computational tractability. Here we introduce MoViD (Motion estimation via Virtual dispersion and phase Detection), a physics-inspired algorithm grounded in the principles that govern photonic time stretch - a highly successful ultrafast realtime data acquisition platform. Drawing inspiration from the optical physics therein, MoViD treats video as a collection of optical time series waveforms associated with pixels. Motion of an object through a pixel broadens the time series spectrum and, after group delay dispersion, induces a temporal phase that exists only if there is motion. Spatiotemporal group delay dispersion templates, corresponding to dielectric functions, classify specific motion trajectories. Unlike conventional empirical phase-based motion-analysis pipelines that require narrow-band spatial channelization and pyramid reconstruction, the physics-based MoViD operates directly on the broadband video signal, vastly increasing its computational speed. The resulting algorithm achieves unprecedented performance in both motion characterization and motion magnification, providing full-resolution motion mapping in real time at nearly 200 frames per second at 4K resolution and 70 frames per second for 8K video - orders of magnitude faster than classical optical flow approaches or learning-based methods. Notably, such extreme performance enables real time motion analysis at ultrahigh resolution for motion detection and compensation in robotics and other autonomous devices.

articles.title: A Global Magnetohydrodynamic Simulation of the Birth and Cannibalism of Homologous Coronal Mass Ejections
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33614v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Homologous coronal mass ejections (CMEs) are sequential eruptions from the same active region. They are of particular space weather interest because they can interact and coalesce into compound ejecta, potentially amplifying their geomagnetic impact. Yet the full chain from recurrent initiation to magnetic merging has not been captured self-consistently in a single global simulation. We present a three-dimensional magnetohydrodynamic model that generates three homologous CMEs from a bipolar active region by recurrent photospheric shearing. All three eruptions follow the same initiation mechanism by tether-cutting reconnection within a recurrently formed sigmoid, while the later CMEs propagate significantly faster than the first. We demonstrate that this speed hierarchy arises from progressive coronal preconditioning; preceding eruptions evacuate the overlying corona, reducing both mass loading and ambient drag. The faster later CMEs catch up with their predecessors, and the compression between them forms inter-CME current sheets. Reconnection within these current sheets then progressively merges the interacting flux systems, completing the cannibalistic process. Synthetic coronagraph images reproduce the apparent coalescence of multiple white-light fronts. This simulation provides the first self-consistent global view of the birth, preconditioning, and cannibalistic interaction of homologous CMEs, bridging recurrent eruption initiation and inter-CME magnetic merging in the near-Sun corona.

articles.title: Efficient Block Encodings of Vibrational Hamiltonians
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33800v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulation of molecular vibrations is emerging as a promising application of quantum computing in quantum chemistry. In this work, we develop new strategies for block-encoding the second-quantized n-mode representation of the vibrational Hamiltonian, whose algebraic structure closely parallels that of the second-quantized electronic Hamiltonian. We derive linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) representations of this Hamiltonian based on Pauli decomposition and tensor hypercontraction (THC) and construct efficient circuits for the corresponding block encodings. We also extend the Block-Invariant Symmetry Shift (BLISS) technique to vibrational Hamiltonians, yielding a lower LCU 1-norm and, consequently, a lower overall circuit cost. For the molecules considered here, BLISS-THC reduces the Toffoli cost of quantum phase estimation by more than two orders of magnitude relative to existing block-encoding approaches. In comparison with recent Trotter-based methods, it shows up to a ninefold reduction in the T-gate count, with the relative savings tending to increase with system size. Asymptotically, and up to polylogarithmic factors, both the Pauli and THC LCUs trade additional ancillas for a quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modes, while THC provides an additional quadratic improvement in scaling with the number of modals. These results highlight the importance of Hamiltonian factorizations and Toffoli-qubit tradeoffs for reducing the computational cost of quantum simulations of molecular vibrations.

articles.title: V-Representability Beyond Singular Times in Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory: The Hubbard Dimer Case
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33837v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the global V-representability problem in time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) for the two-particle Hubbard dimer model in the spin-singlet sector. In particular, we investigate whether the time-dependent density of the interacting system obtained for a given one-body external potential u (the tunable control variable) can be reproduced by a non-interacting Kohn--Sham system beyond the singular times at which the usual inversion formulas break down. We deal with both the conventional formulation of TDDFT based on some time-dependent variational principle and the recently introduced geometric formulation of TDDFT (Phys. Rev. Lett. 136 (2026) 256401, Phys. Rev. A 113 (2026) 062222). For both principles, we prove global-in-time V-representability, show that singular times induce non-uniqueness of the time-dependent effective potential, and classify the set of solutions.

articles.title: Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Network for Single-Shot 3D Reconstruction from Fringe Patterns
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33988v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep learning facilitates rapid single shot three dimensional (3D) reconstruction using fringe projection profilometry (FPP), but recovering accurate surface height from a single high frequency fringe image remains challenging because both long-range spatial consistency and fine geometric details must be preserved. Convolutional networks are limited in modeling long range dependencies, whereas window-based Transformers establish global interactions only progressively with increasing depth. To address these limitations, a hybrid Mamba Transformer network is proposed for fringe to height regression. The network adopts a Swin based U shaped architecture and introduces visual state space modeling at the intermediate resolution encoder stage. An axial and dilated vision state space (ADVSS) block is further developed to enhance prescan feature encoding through local, dilated, and axial depthwise convolutions while retaining four directional selective scanning. This design combines linear complexity long range modeling with direction aware preservation of local fringe structures. Experiments on a publicly available FPP dataset show that the proposed method outperforms hNet, SwinConvUNet, UHRNet, and HiDNet in mean absolute error(MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), absolute relative error, and structural similarity index measure (SSIM). Using only one deformed fringe image, the proposed method achieves an RMSE of 0.548 mm and an SSIM of 0.9985, reducing RMSE by 65.2% and 59.6% relative to UHRNet and HiDNet, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining selective state space modeling with hierarchical window based attention for accurate single-shot FPP reconstruction.

articles.title: Magnetic Topological Evolution and the Predictive Role of Winding-flux-based Masked PILs in Extreme Solar Flares from AR13664 and AR13842
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using vector magnetogram data from the Helioseismic Magnetic Imager (HMI) on board the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), we present detailed case studies of precursor activity in Active Regions (ARs) 13664 and 13842, which produced several intense flares. We examined the spatiotemporal evolution of key magnetic topological parameters, including winding, helicity, winding-flux-based masked polarity inversion lines (PILs), and PIL gradients, from the precursor to the post-flare phases. The temporal evolution of the winding flux showed a significant enhancement during the precursor phase, and this trend was consistent across the seven X-class and five M-class flares (>= M5.0). The spatial distribution of both raw and Gaussian-smoothed winding-flux enhancement is co-located with flare footpoint regions of highly twisted core fields, as indicated by the photospheric magnetic topology. The winding-flux-based masked PILs that persisted around the flare locations showed a significant increase in strength and area during the precursor activity. These masked PILs spatially coincide with regions likely hosting non-potential core magnetic fields associated with the observed flares. Furthermore, the gradient of strong PILs extracted from the ARs was positively correlated with flare-associated locations and typically increased several hours (approx. 3-5 h) before flare onset. By imposing a gradient threshold on strong PILs, we isolate magnetic regions repeatedly associated with flare initiation, providing useful constraints in regimes where current flare-forecasting models remain uncertain. Therefore, the combined analysis of the spatiotemporal evolution of different magnetic topological parameters enhances our understanding of intense solar flare forecasting and the identification of potential triggering sites, thereby contributing to improved space weather prediction frameworks.

articles.title: Magnetic switchback development from the evolution of torsional Alfvén waves
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34518v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Magnetic switchbacks are mostly Alfvénic local deflections, or even reversals, of the ambient magnetic field of the solar wind. Despite intense research their origin remains unclear and is highly debated. Here we describe a new simulation study demonstrating how torsional Alfvén waves can evolve into switchbacks. We use surface rotational motions to launch torsional Alfvén waves into the super-radially expanding magnetic field of a coronal hole. The simulations demonstrate that in such an expanding wind, the waves initially steepen as they propagate while also inducing a cylindrical parallel plasma jet. A combination of shear from the jet and wave evolution under the constraint of approximate spherical polarisation (|B|approx const.) then leads to the formation of switchbacks in a ring configuration. We explore the 3D nature of the switchbacks, how and where they from, and present scalings for their peak deflection and parallel and perpendicular length scales. We also derive an expression for switchback deflection in the linear regime which we contrast against our results. The results are discussed in relation to recent observations and previous switchback formation studies.

articles.title: LHμC: A high energy, high luminosity muon-hadron collider at CERN
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The latest developments regarding the feasibility of muon-hadron collisions, achieved through the major reuse of LHeC infrastructure, are presented - at the LHμC, a 1 or 2 TeV μ⁺ beam collides with a 7 TeV proton beam, resulting in the μ^+p centre-of-mass energy of 5.3 or 7.5 TeV, respectively, at an average luminosity close to 10³⁴cm⁻²s⁻¹. First, a concise scientific motivation is given, including exceptional prospects for neutrino science, and is followed by a presentation of the LHμC concept in a nutshell - from the source of ultra-cold anti-muons, through the muon booster, to the main muon ring. Basic considerations regarding the machine-detector interface and the general-purpose detector are also presented. The paper concludes with an outlook underlying unique and powerful synergies between the LHμC, LHeC, FCC and Muon Collider projects.

articles.title: mdRNAcat: A Molecular Dynamics RNA Catalog of REST2 Conformational Ensembles
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35204v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning molecular models of RNA requires simulation data that capture conformational variability and provide consistent physical training signals. Here, we introduce mdRNAcat, a curated dataset of all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of 48 RNA systems selected to promote sequence diversity. Each system is simulated using replica-exchange with solute scaling (REST2), with 32 Hamiltonian states and production lengths of 200-300 ns per state. The dataset provides atomic coordinates, instantaneous forces, and forces reevaluated under the unscaled reference Hamiltonian, together with structural annotations and replica-exchange metadata. Coordinates and forces are available at 1 ps intervals for the reference state and 100 ps intervals across all states in a standardized HDF5 format. We characterize conformational sampling, exchange behavior, base pairing, and sugar-pucker distributions to document the properties of the simulated ensembles. mdRNAcat provides a reusable resource for developing and evaluating data-driven RNA models, including coarse-grained force fields.

articles.title: Interaction of Strong X-mode Waves with Magnetized Pair Plasmas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The interaction of strong (a₀>1), superluminal X-mode electromagnetic waves with magnetized pair plasma falls into two regimes set by εᵣₘ Bequiv a₀ωᵣₘ B/ω₀, the ratio of the wave strength parameter to its frequency, in units of cyclotron frequency. For εᵣₘ B<1 the wave propagates until induced scattering disrupts it. Using analytical theory and kinetic simulations, we show that the background magnetic field introduces a restoring frequency Ωᵣₘ B to scattering; when Ωᵣₘ B exceeds the scattering rate, the unattenuated length grows from simeqεᵣₘ ₚ⁻²/³ to simeqεᵣₘ B¹/²/εᵣₘ ₚ wavelengths (εᵣₘ ₚequiv a₀ωᵣₘ ₚ/ω₀; ωᵣₘ ₚ is the plasma frequency). When a₀²>εᵣₘ B>1, the plasma current is nonlinear, and the wave is damped while riding a motional electric field, so one half-cycle appears attenuated. This framework has implications for the duration of fast radio bursts and whether they can escape their surroundings.

articles.title: Omnigenous stellarators with improved ideal and kinetic ballooning stability
articles.abstract: arXiv:2410.04576v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Omnigenity is a property of a magnetic field which ensures confinement of trapped particles. It is a necessary requirement for any high-performance stellarator. After creating an omnigenous equilibrium, one must also ensure reduced transport resulting from kinetic and magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) instabilities. To this end, we leverage the GPU-accelerated DESC optimization suite, which is used to design stable, finite-β omnigenous equilibria with poloidal, toroidal, and helical symmetry, achieving Mercier, ideal ballooning, and as a consequence, improved kinetic ballooning stability. We discover stellarators with second stability, a regime of large pressure gradient where an equilibrium becomes ideal ballooning stable, and demonstrate and explore both using theory and gyrokinetic simulations the connection between ideal and kinetic ballooning stability.

articles.title: Landscape of scattering universality with general dispersion relations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2509.01782v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Universality in physics describes how disparate systems can exhibit identical low-energy behavior. Here, we reveal a rich landscape of new universal scattering phenomena governed by the interplay between an interaction and a system's density of states. We investigate one-dimensional scattering with dispersion relations ϵ(k)=|k|^m and ϵ(k)=sgn(k)|k|^m for any real m>1. For emitter scattering and separable potentials, including contact potentials, we classify the zero-energy S-matrix limits. These universal S-matrix fixed points depend solely on the dispersion exponent m and a finite set of integers characterizing the low-momentum interaction structure. This classification extends far beyond the standard quadratic-dispersion case (m=2). We further derive a generalized Levinson's theorem relating the total winding of the S-matrix determinant to the number of bound states. Finally, for contact potentials and analytic monomial dispersions, we analyze the leading low-energy expansion of the scattering phase near these fixed points and extract the corresponding Wigner-delay scaling. Our findings are directly relevant to synthetic quantum systems, where engineered dispersion relations in atomic arrays and photonic crystals offer a platform to explore these universal behaviors.

articles.title: Voltage-Dependent Photocurrent and Crossover Behavior in Crystalline Silicon Solar Cells
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.27577v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Contrary to the conventional assumption of voltage-independent photocurrent, we show that the photocurrent in monocrystalline silicon p-n junction solar cells depends explicitly on voltage. By applying physically realistic boundary conditions to the classical p-n junction solar-cell model, we derive an analytical expression for the photocurrent that incorporates both the built-in potential and the applied voltage. The model predicts a crossover point between the dark and illuminated I-V characteristics, irrespective of illumination intensity. This prediction is experimentally validated by lock-in measurements on a commercial monocrystalline silicon solar cell. These results establish a more consistent understanding of the quantitative role of the built-in potential in the photovoltaic effect.

articles.title: Ultra-broadband Mid to Long-wave Infrared Spintronic Poisson Bolometer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.11733v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Infrared detectors have traditionally been divided into two fundamental classes, mid-wave (MWIR, 3-5 um) and long-wave (LWIR, 8-14 um). Integrating MWIR and LWIR within a single device is challenging due to distinct materials, cooling needs, and detection mechanisms, while such integration is critical for improved object recognition, temperature estimation, and environmental sensing. In this work, we demonstrate a Spintronic Poisson (SP) bolometer enabling room-temperature ultra-broadband sensing across 3-14 um. Unlike conventional bolometers that rely on continuous analog signals, the SP bolometer implements a Poisson-counting detection paradigm, encoding temperature in discrete stochastic events, which turns thermal noise from a limitation into the basis of the estimator itself. We fabricate the SP bolometer using a spintronic transduction layer integrated with a plasmonic nanoantenna array to enhance broadband infrared absorption. Using spintronic transduction, the device achieves the noise-equivalent temperature difference (NETD, thermal sensitivity metric) of 80-100 mK at 300 K, surpassing uncooled detectors and approaching cooled technologies. This work establishes a statistical detection paradigm for room-temperature infrared sensing with broad application potential.

articles.title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Designing building energy systems is a high-dimensional, mixed-integer search problem: when each design is evaluated by a year-long simulation, black-box optimizers typically need hundreds of evaluations. This paper presents AutoEnergyDesign, a framework in which a Large Language Model (LLM) agent reasons over previous simulation results, proposes configuration changes and learns in context from each outcome, while a git-based mechanism automatically reverts unsuccessful changes. The agent couples a reasoning model with an explicit memory organisation (procedural, semantic, episodic and reflective), a constrained action interface and an environment-grounded keep/revert signal. The simulator covers eight technologies (photovoltaics, micro-wind, combined heat and power, solar thermal, gas boilers, batteries, heat pumps and inverters) and computes the 25-year Net Present Cost (NPC), including capital and operating costs and salvage value. On a case study with measured building load profiles, the agent, run with Claude Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 (ten runs of 50 simulations each), is compared with random search, Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization and a (1+1) evolution strategy sharing the agent's acceptance rule (300 evaluations, ten seeds). With all three models the agent reaches an NPC of about 3.53 MEUR, 1.20% below the best TPE result and 0.23% below the best evolution-strategy result. It comes within 1% of this design after a median of 18 (Opus) to 27.5 (Haiku) simulations, whereas among the baselines only the evolution strategy does so, in half of its seeds and after a median of 192 evaluations. Opus reaches the best design in all ten runs, Sonnet in six (two runs never come within 1%), and Haiku comes within 1% in every run but reaches it exactly only once. Every decision is recorded in an auditable trace.

articles.title: Repulsive Ensembles for Bayesian Inference in Physics-informed Neural Networks
articles.abstract: arXiv:2505.17308v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have proven an effective tool for solving differential equations, in particular when considering the inverse problem. When inferring solutions and parameters of the differential equation from data, uncertainty estimates are preferable to point estimates, as they give an idea about the accuracy of the solution. In this work, we consider the inverse problem for a selection of basic differential equations and employ repulsive ensembles of PINNs (RE-PINN) to obtain such estimates. The repulsion is implemented by adding a particular repulsive term to the loss function, which has the property that the ensemble predictions correspond to the true Bayesian posterior in the limit of infinite ensemble members. Where available, we compare the ensemble predictions to Monte Carlo baselines. Whereas the standard ensemble tends to collapse to maximum-a-posteriori solutions, the repulsive ensemble produces significantly more accurate uncertainty estimates and exhibits higher sample diversity. The experimental results demonstrate that RE-PINN can accurately infer the Bayesian posterior in low-dimensional problems, establishing repulsive ensembles as a promising framework for uncertainty quantification in PINNs.

articles.title: Determinantal sampling on general spaces: fast approximation via diffusion geometry
articles.abstract: arXiv:2607.06644v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Determinantal point processes (DPPs) have recently emerged as a kernel-based alternative to standard independent sampling for constructing efficient minibatches, coresets, and other compact representations of large-scale datasets. One of the key strengths of DPP based samplers is that they can be deployed over very general spaces, in contrast to more classical sampling methods beyond i.i.d. which tend to be tailored to particular well-structured settings, principally Euclidean spaces. In this work, we establish explicit rate guarantees for determinantal sampling in spaces that extend far beyond known Euclidean setups, focussing on spectral kernels obtained from eigenspaces of naturally associated Markov diffusion operators, including in particular the Laplacian on manifolds and nearest-neighbour type graphs on data point clouds and the discrete Schrodinger operator on large scale networks. This covers, in particular, the settings of Riemannian manifolds and discrete networks, as well as the problem of batch sampling from discrete datasets. Overall, our approach achieves guarantees comparable to big(sample sizebig)⁻frac¹²⁻frac¹²dᵢₙₜ , which match with the rates for well-known determinantal samplers on Euclidean spaces of comparable dimension. In terms of techniques, we connect to the celebrated Weyl's Law for spectra on general spaces, and leverage tools from the theory of Markov diffusion operators and Dirichlet forms, which could be of independent interest in this area. Our approach is applicable to a very wide plethora of ambient spaces beyond Euclidean as soon as these ingredients are available, including e.g. fractals, leading to guarantees that will be governed by the intrinsic structural constants of such spaces.

articles.title: Biogeographic divergence in mangrove resilience to accelerating sea-level rise
articles.abstract: Mangrove forests raise their soil surface in response to relative sea-level rise (RSLR), a biogenic capacity that underpins their value for coastal protection and blue-carbon storage. Whether this capacity is approaching its upper limit, and whether that limit differs between the far-field Indo-West Pacific and intermediate-field Atlantic-East Pacific settings distinguished by Holocene stratigraphy, has not been tested against contemporary observations at a global scale. Here we synthesise for the first time the global mangrove surface elevation table–marker horizon (SET-MH) record: 601 stations across 141 sites in 21 countries, of which 480 resolve an elevation trend. Mangrove surface elevation gain (3.59 ± 9.51 mm yr⁻¹) lagged behind mean RSLR of 5.21 3.42 mm yr⁻¹. The capacity to build elevation was constrained by a non-linear increase in shallow subsidence with accretion. Structural equation modelling revealed tidal range as the dominant control on this constraint. An elevation deficit becomes very likely (P ≥ 0.90) at 8.1 mm yr⁻¹ of RSLR in the Indo-West Pacific but at 6.3 mm yr⁻¹ in the intermediate-field Atlantic-East Pacific sites sampled, and at only 2.4 mm yr⁻¹ in reef settings, mirroring the relative vulnerability to RSLR inferred from palaeo-stratigraphy. Elevation deficit, rather than RSLR itself, predicts conversion to open water across the network of Surface Elevation Tables. Mangrove resilience to sea-level rise is therefore bounded and regionally unequal, and in intermediate-field Caribbean settings and on reef islands this limit is a present condition rather than a future projection.

articles.title: Experimental zero-added-loss multiplexing Bell-pair source for long-haul quantum networks
articles.abstract: Boosting the communication rate of quantum networks is a central challenge in quantum information science. Recently, an efficient entanglement distribution scheme employing quasi-deterministic Bell-pair sources based on time-frequency multiplexing, referred to as zero-added-loss multiplexing~(ZALM), has been proposed. Its implementation, however, requires high-fidelity entanglement swapping across densely multiplexed time-frequency modes, which has remained an experimental challenge. Here we demonstrate entanglement swapping across 16 parallel frequency modes with a high average fidelity of 93.9±SI1.4%. Notably, polarization-entangled photon pairs in each frequency mode are spectrally single-mode using only off-the-shelf 50-GHz dense wavelength-division multiplexing~(DWDM) filters, eliminating the need for additional narrowband filtering. Furthermore, in order to fully exploit the temporal degree of freedom, the pump pulse is operated with a repetition frequency of SI3.0GHz. By combining the frequency and time multiplexing, the total swapping rate reaches 5.38±0.17,sipairs,s⁻¹, which corresponds to the ZALM Bell-pair rate of SI8.2e2pairs,s⁻¹. Our results establish the key experimental capabilities required for ZALM and demonstrate a scalable route toward practical high-rate quantum repeaters and long-haul quantum networks.

articles.title: When Does the Non-Hermitian Effective Description Fail? A Finite-Size Reliability Map
articles.abstract: The no-click (postselected) non-Hermitian Hamiltonian (:Hₑff=H-fraci2sum:ⱼwⱼLⱼ†Lⱼ) is an exact unraveling of the Lindblad equation, but nothing in that unraveling says how far the postselected state may drift from the unconditional one. We measure the drift, over one period (:T) and averaged over initial states, by the trace distance (:Ddyₙ=frac12hspace0.17emoverline{parallel:ρ:ᵤₙcₒₙdleft(Tright)-Pcleft(Tright)parallel:ₜᵣ}) ((:Pc): the normalized conditional projector), and show that its leading coefficient in (:Kₙ=γ:/ω:) is fixed by the fluctuation of the jump operators along the unitary orbit, computable without any dissipative simulation. For excitation-number-conserving systems whose jump operators are ladder-type (each shifting the conserved excitation number by a nonzero integer) we prove a conservation-integral theorem reducing the dimensionless coefficient to (:2π:wNₑₓc) ((:w): dimensionless channel weight; (:Nₑₓc): conserved excitation number; time-integral form (:2π:wNₑₓc/ω:)), verified to the (:10⁻⁵) level or better across spin chains and chiral waveguide pairs, and, for gain–loss cavities with non-uniform channel weights, through the block-diagonal lemma, with no microscopic parameters beyond (:Nₑₓc). The crossing scale degrades with system size as (:KD*left(Nright)propto:N⁻¹), confirmed by exact diagonalization and corner-space calculations up to (:N=12) and by single-parameter data collapse. The result yields platform-independent design rules—maximum dissipation, postselection cost and an explicit switch criterion—and a guide for exceptional-point experiments.

articles.title: Quantum-Inspired Deep Spatio-Temporal Network for Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Turbofan Engines
articles.abstract: Accurate Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction of aircraft turbofan engines under dynamic, multi-regime operating conditions is vital for industrial prognostics and safety management. However, existing data-driven methods struggle with multimodal sensor feature distributions, unmodeled cross-sensor spatial correlations, and symmetric loss functions that treat safety-critical over-predictions and conservative under-predictions equally. To address these challenges, this paper introduces the Quantum-Inspired Deep Spatio-Temporal Network (QIDSTN), a compact and safety-aware architecture. The proposed model incorporates an operating condition-aware preprocessing module using K-Means clustering and RobustScaler normalization to eliminate operational bias in heterogeneous datasets. Feature representations are enriched via a novel Quantum Rotation Layer employing learnable trigonometric transformations inspired by quantum rotation gates, without requiring quantum hardware. A dual spatial-temporal attention pipeline, combined with parallel multi-scale convolutions and bidirectional gated recurrent units, effectively captures multi-resolution spatio-temporal dynamics. Furthermore, a composite asymmetric loss function penalizes dangerous over-predictions while prioritizing near-failure engine states. Evaluated across all four NASA C-MAPSS benchmark subsets, the model achieves root mean square errors (RMSE) of 14.84, 17.39, 15.58, and 17.31 on FD001 through FD004, respectively, maintaining a coefficient of determination exceeding 0.83 with only 180,000 to 220,000 parameters. On the complex multi-regime FD004 dataset, it reduces RMSE by 16.6% and NASA score by 86.6% compared to standard baseline models, demonstrating competitive accuracy, safety-oriented error alignment, and practical CPU-level industrial deployability.

articles.title: Predictive value of current HEC-RAS 2D water levels for machine learning flood postprocessing in southeastern Louisiana
articles.abstract: Machine-learning postprocessing quantified information in current water-surface elevation (WSE) and its recent history from the Hydrologic Engineering Center's River Analysis System (HEC-RAS 2D). The analysis used 130 hydrographs and 5,134 paired 3-h records from eight southeastern Louisiana floods. Cross-validation excluded one complete flood from training per outer test fold. Event-macro hydrograph root-mean-square error (RMSE), which weighted floods equally, was 1.63 m for uncorrected HEC-RAS and 0.81 m for a model using forcing, time, location, and static descriptors without time-varying WSE. Adding current WSE reduced RMSE to 0.67 m and improved all eight floods. Adding recent history reduced RMSE to 0.62 m and improved seven floods. When each test gauge was excluded from training, models without WSE, with current WSE, and with current plus history scored 1.62, 0.96, and 0.87 m, respectively. The history model improved on uncorrected HEC-RAS at only 16 of 33 gauges, and the largest gains occurred at deeply incised lower-Amite mapped cells. WSE-informed hydrograph models improved high-water and centered errors but not exact 3-h changes, peak magnitude, or peak timing. A separate exploratory peak-magnitude model reduced mean absolute error from 0.48 to 0.44 m but did not estimate peak time. One-third of scheduled mapped outputs lacked supported WSE. Current WSE supplied the largest and most consistent increment, while recent history added a smaller and less consistent benefit. The analysis used completed floods and did not evaluate hydraulic-model validity or future-flood forecasts.

articles.title: Knee extension motor imagery paired with single-pulse TMS facilitates corticospinal excitability in the tibialis anterior muscle, but not in the rectus femoris muscle
articles.abstract: The rectus femoris (RF) muscle is recruited during a wide range of movements and restoring its function is relevant to both rehabilitation and sports performance. However, previous studies have reported difficulty in inducing facilitatory changes in corticospinal excitability of the RF muscle. We investigated whether and how a method combining motor imagery and transcranial magnetic stimulation (MI+TMS), which has been effective for low plasticity muscles in the upper limbs, modulates the corticospinal excitability in the RF muscle and other lower limb muscles. Twenty healthy participants underwent an MI+TMS protocol consisting of 120 repetitions of knee extension MI paired with single-pulse TMS. Motor evoked potentials (MEPs) were recorded from the RF, biceps femoris (BF), tibialis anterior (TA), and soleus (SOL) muscles at baseline (Pre), immediately after (Post 0), and at 15 (Post 15) and 30 minutes (Post 30) post-MI+TMS. MI+TMS did not significantly modulate MEPs in the RF muscle, an agonist for knee extension, and RF muscle activity during maximum voluntary contraction was significantly reduced. By contrast, MEPs in the TA muscle were significantly increased at Post 0 and Post 15 compared to Pre, whereas no significant changes were observed in the BF and SOL muscles. Additional measurements with 15 participants in the MI-only condition showed no significant changes in MEP amplitude in any muscle. These findings indicate that MI+TMS facilitates corticospinal excitability in a muscle specific manner and suggest that the corticospinal pathway to the RF muscle may be less susceptible to facilitatory plastic changes.

articles.title: X-ray investigations of stainless steel 316L produced via directed energy deposition
articles.abstract: Directed energy deposition (DED) can produce complex pore populations and residual stress states in stainless steel 316L (SS316L), requiring quantitative evaluation to assess suitability for high-consequence structural applications. This work combines laboratory X-ray computed tomography (XCT) with X-ray diffraction (XRD) to characterize 18 DED-fabricated SS316L specimens produced over a range of laser power, scan speed, and powder feed conditions. XCT, with a voxel size of ~ 8µm/voxel, imaged the specimens and analyzed the porosity while XRD measurements evaluated phase constitution, texture, and near-surface residual stress. A sparse-view machine-learning image processing workflow reduced XCT acquisition from 4801 to 481 projections, corresponding to an 89% reduction in scan-time while maintaining 90% flaw detection. Porosity was observed to range from 0.01 to 6.77 vol%, with 16 of the specimens below 0.5 vol%. The largest porosity occurred in low-energy, low-power conditions near the build plate. XRD confirmed a single-phase face-centered-cubic structure with persistent (111)-type preferred orientation, with integrated intensity ratios of (111)/(200) of ~ 1.6–2.8. Residual stresses were predominantly compressive and non-equibiaxial. The largest in-plane stress component was between − 200 and − 450 MPa. The combined XCT-XRD workflow provides quantitative, spatially resolved evidence linking DED processing conditions to defect formation, texture, and residual stress.

articles.title: Carbon nanotubes and cubic silsesquioxanes nanohybrids as a new potential platform for dipyrone sensing
articles.abstract: This study reports the synthesis, characterization, and electroanalytical application of a nanohybrid platform based on carboxylated carbon nanotubes functionalized with octa(aminopropyl)silsesquioxane and copper(II) hexacyanoferrate(III) for dipyrone determination. The material, designated CNTmSCuH, was prepared through the coordination of Cu²⁺ ions onto the silsesquioxane-modified carbon nanotube surface, followed by reaction with hexacyanoferrate(III). Structural and surface characterization by FTIR-ATR, TEM, XPS, and N₂ physisorption confirmed the successful formation of the bimetallic complex, the presence of cubic nanostructures, Cu/Fe species, and mesoporous features. When incorporated into a graphite paste electrode, the CNTmSCuH/CPE exhibited well-defined electrochemical behavior associated with the Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ redox couple and favorable stability under optimized conditions. The modified electrode showed electrocatalytic activity toward dipyrone oxidation, shifting the oxidation potential to lower values compared with the unmodified electrode. Under optimized conditions using 1.0 mol L⁻¹ KCl at pH 7.0 and a scan rate of 20 mV s⁻¹, the sensor presented a linear response from 5.0 × 10⁻⁴ to 5.0 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ and a detection limit of 5.69 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹. The platform was successfully applied to commercial pharmaceutical samples by the standard addition method, demonstrating its potential for dipyrone sensing.

articles.title: Adaptive Shot Allocation for Recursive QAOA via Reinforcement Learning
articles.abstract: Recursive QAOA (RQAOA) solves combinatorial optimization problems by using shallow quantum circuits to estimate pairwise correlations and recursively eliminate variables until a classical solver can handle the residual instance. Each elimination step requires measurement shots, and the total shot cost grows with the number of recursive stages. On near-term quantum devices, increasing shot counts can translate directly into greater exposure to hardware-level noise sources such as readout errors and decoherence, making shot-efficient execution not merely a cost-reduction measure but a factor with direct implications for solution reliability. While shot reduction has been studied broadly across NISQ algorithms, step-wise measurement control inside the recursive loop of RQAOA has received little attention.We formulate this step-wise allocation as a sequential decision problem and propose two complementary strategies for depth-1 RQAOA on weighted Max-Cut instances. A hand-crafted heuristic assigns shots based on local indicators of step difficulty, and a tabular Double Q-learning agent learns a residual policy that adjusts this baseline under a Lagrangian-constrained objective. Both methods are evaluated under a fixed-cap fairness protocol that equalizes the per-step budget across all strategies, and the elimination rule itself is kept unchanged so that the contribution of adaptive measurement control can be isolated.On a diverse set of weighted graph instances spanning a range of sizes and structures, the heuristic reduces total shots by approximately 23% relative to uniform allocation, and the RL policy achieves a 36% reduction with a lower effective shots per success ratio than both baselines. The improvement persists on problem sizes not seen during training, suggesting that reinforcement learning can serve as an effective tool for discovering efficient, instance-adaptive measurement strategies in recursive quantum optimization.

articles.title: SAM-NeuroAdapt: an atlas-guided, training-free pipeline for skull-stripping in infant and adult MRI
articles.abstract: Skull-stripping, the removal of non-brain tissue from magnetic resonance images, is an early step of most neuroimaging pipelines whose errors propagate to later measurements. However, current methods such as HD-BET, SynthStrip and LifespanStrip depend on task-specific training on large image collections. To test how much of this benefit survives without training, this study presents SAM-NeuroAdapt, a training-free pipeline. First, an age-matched template is selected from a library of 21 atlases and registered to the image. The registered atlas then supplies the prompts of a frozen Segment Anything Model 2, and the mask is refined by classical boundary correction. The pipeline was compared with HD-BET on three whole-head benchmarks, with multiplicity-adjusted p-values. On infants (Baby Open Brains, 71 visits, 51 participants), it achieved higher Dice (0.920 versus 0.905) and a lower average symmetric surface distance (ASSD; 2.07 versus 5.11 mm). On adults, no Dice difference was detected; ASSD was ower on Mindboggle-101 (n = 101) and, under one of two adjustment procedures, on IBSR-20 (n = 20).
