The two indicators probe distinct physical mechanisms, lattice anharmonicity and bandgap renormalization, and together provide contact-free thermometry for monolayer WS2 from 5~K to 1273~K, an approach applicable to 2D semiconductors more broadly.

articles.title: Interfacial bacteria-driven rotation of free-floating active droplets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active droplets provide a platform for converting microscopic propulsion into macroscopic flow. Previous realizations of bacteria-driven droplet rotation typically rely on nearby solid boundaries, external fields, or dense active nematics. Here, we report autonomous rotation of droplets in a three-dimensional aqueous two-phase system driven by interfacial population of Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Combining confocal microscopy with fluid particle dynamics simulations, we show that amphiphilic bacteria accumulate at the dextran--polyethylene glycol interface and preferentially move and orient along the local tangent. Interfacial localization partitions the force-free swimming dipole between the two liquid phases, allowing either phase to experience a finite active torque while the combined system remains torque balanced. The simulated interfacial population is more spatially heterogeneous than in the experiments, emphasizing that both the bacterial distribution and its signed orientational organization can influence the instantaneous torque. Over the accessible size range, the macroscopic angular velocity exhibits an inverse-radius (R⁻¹) dependence. We also formulate a theoretical model to rationalize this scaling law, revealing how the macroscopic rotation is governed by collective interfacial swimming and surface coverage. These results identify a fluid-interface-mediated route for converting swimmer activity into macroscopic rotational flow and establish a strategy for harnessing interfacial active matter to regulate droplet dynamics.

articles.title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-term stability remains a critical challenge limiting the photovoltaic and optoelectronic applications of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites. In these materials, the choice of the organic spacer plays a key role not only in enhancing environmental stability, but also in determining their structural characteristics and carrier dynamics. Here, we present an environmental photo- and thermal-stability analysis of BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 two-dimensional lead halide perovskites by means of confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy techniques. We have investigated two different organic spacers, n-butylammonium (BA) and 2-phenylethylammonium (PEA), which provide comparable room-temperature luminescence in freshly exfoliated perovskite nanoflakes and degrade similarly through the removal of organic components and fast crystal phase decomposition into PbI2 and Pb0. However, we observed that the PEA organic cation significantly improves crystal morphology and suppresses lattice defects, resulting in slower degradation and enhanced resistance to light and thermal stress under ambient conditions. Our findings indicate that structural and chemical engineering, along with surface passivation and encapsulation strategies, are essential for achieving long-term stability in two-dimensional halide perovskite devices. Nevertheless, optimizing the balance between stability and device performance remains a critical consideration.

articles.title: Synchronization-controlled transport near an absorbing transition: Effective Enskog kinetic theory of a driven granular monolayer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35270v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synchronization with vibrating boundaries can qualitatively alter the dynamics of confined granular fluids and control the collision-induced transfer of energy to horizontal motion. We develop an Enskog kinetic theory for the active phase of a driven granular monolayer within the framework of the Δ-model, which accounts for the transfer of energy from the vertical to the horizontal degrees of freedom of grains. Synchronization effects are incorporated through a state-dependent effective collision rule governed by the interplay between the local collision frequency and a characteristic synchronization time. A viscous drag force is also included to account for energy dissipation arising from interactions with the confining plates. Within this framework, we characterize the homogeneous active state and use it as the reference state for a Chapman--Enskog expansion. The solution of the Enskog equation to Navier--Stokes order then yields explicit expressions for the shear and bulk viscosities, the thermal conductivity, the diffusive heat coefficient, and the first-order contribution to the cooling rate, consistently accounting for inelasticity, damping, finite-density effects, and synchronization. Event-driven molecular-dynamics simulations show that the theory accurately describes the steady temperature and shear and bulk viscosities over a broad region of the active phase. Close to the discontinuous synchronization-controlled absorbing transition, deviations are mainly attributed to the mean-field coarse-graining of the microscopic synchronization dynamics: fluctuations of the collision-dependent injection amplitude and correlations between synchronization and pre-collisional velocities become increasingly important. These results provide a kinetic description of synchronization-controlled transport and delineate its range of validity near the absorbing transition.

articles.title: Momentum-resolved thermodynamics and barrier-free order-parameter collapse in spin-orbit-coupled superconductors under a Zeeman field
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin-orbit coupling (SOC) can enhance the critical Zeeman field of clean superconductors beyond the Pauli limit. We develop a momentum decomposition of the zero-temperature free energy to investigate spin-singlet s-wave superconductors with general time-reversal-symmetric SOC. The SOC component perpendicular to the Zeeman field enhances the critical field and suppresses first-order features, whereas the parallel component favors Pauli-limited thermodynamic behavior. Applying this framework to Rashba superconductors and Ising superconductors with weak Rashba SOC, we identify the origin of the abrupt collapse of the superconducting order parameter at the critical field. Competing angular contributions produce a nearly flat free-energy landscape, allowing a barrier-free order-parameter collapse distinct from the conventional Pauli-limited first-order transition.

articles.title: Phonon-assisted shift-current from first-principles: application to AlN monolayer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we present a first-principles approach to investigate phonon-assisted shift current in extended systems. Our method combines the special displacement technique with real-time simulations based on the dynamical Berry phase. Merging these two frameworks enables direct access to non-linear optical responses at finite temperatures, while naturally incorporating phonon scattering and phonon-assisted electronic transitions into the time-dependent dynamics. This allows us to capture temperature-dependent features and lattice fluctuations that are essential for a realistic description of non-linear photocurrent generation. As a representative example, we apply our approach to the shift-current response of a monolayer of hexagonal AlN (h-AlN). This system provides an ideal testing ground because it features an indirect band gap and lacks inversion symmetry. Moreover, h-AlN layers of different thicknesses have been fabricated and characterized in a variety of experimental settings, opening the concrete possibility of testing our predictions. Our results demonstrate the relevance of phonon-mediated processes and the importance of temperature in determining the magnitude and spectral features of the shift current in layered materials.

articles.title: Wrinkling dynamics of thin crystalline sheets and its dependency on topological defects
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the wrinkling dynamics of thin crystalline sheets under uniaxial compression using a Surface Phase-Field-Crystal-Helfrich (SPFCH) model, which captures the coupling between crystalline order, out-of-plane deformations, and topological defects. In particular, the model allows us to track and characterize two distinct classes of defects, namely those forming in the underlying hexagonal crystal lattice, such as dislocations and grain boundaries, and defects in the wrinkling patterns, known as wrinklons. By resolving the evolution and interactions of these defects, we investigate how the interplay between in-plane and out-of-plane relaxation mechanisms influences wrinkling onset and the coarsening regime. Our results indicate that crystalline defects do not affect coarsening scaling, but they quantitatively affect the onset of wrinkling and the emerging wrinkling wavelength, promote more irregular wrinkle patterns with a higher density of wrinklons, and modify long-timescale morphological evolution.

articles.title: Information-theoretic entropy imaging of quantum matter
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase transitions can generate intricate spatial organization invisible to spatially averaged probes, yet quantitative measures of this organization remain limited. Here we develop "entropy imaging," an information-theoretic technique that harnesses lossless compression to quantify spatial complexity, predictability, and order in quantum materials. Using this approach, emergent spatial textures can be imaged and converted into an experimentally-accessible observable: the computable information density (CID), a compression-based measure of information complexity that approaches the Shannon entropy rate in the large-system limit. Applied to millikelvin microwave impedance microscopy of graphene, the method reveals a pronounced maximum in the CID near quantum Hall transitions, a quantitative measure of the information-rich spatial organization of the critical landscape. A disordered Hofstadter model reproduces this behavior and shows that the CID can identify the quantum critical point from a sequence of images, without ensemble averaging over disorder realizations. The same framework tracks fractional quantum Hall transitions and resolves isolated fractional puddles that coexist with a disordered background. By contrast, the trivial band-edge crossover in a MoSe2/WS2 moiré heterobilayer exhibits qualitatively different behavior, suggesting that the pronounced CID enhancement observed at the quantum Hall critical point is not simply a generic feature of a conductive-insulating crossover. We further show that the geometric information encoded in CID is not reducible to a correlation length, and it can even distinguish spatial textures with identical multifractal statistics. Together, these results establish lossless compression as a framework for quantifying emergent spatial organization in quantum materials, with portability across imaging modalities and physical systems.

articles.title: Modeling the CNOT gate in Germanium double quantum dots
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35799v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We model a controlled-NOT (CNOT) gate mediated by exchange interactions in a realistic Ge/GeSi hole spin-qubit device. We use for that purpose a computationally efficient framework based on a compact dressed basis of many-body singlet and triplet states, which enables fast time-dependent simulations that would be prohibitive within a conventional configuration-interaction approach. We discuss the dominant sources of infidelity in ideal (noise-free) devices. On the one hand, the nonadiabaticity of the tunnel barrier ramps, enhanced by the transverse component of the exchange interaction, imposes limits on the speed of the CNOT gate. On the other hand, the AC Stark shift of the conditional resonance and the off-resonant driving of the complementary transition can significantly degrade the gate fidelity and call for a careful optimization of the driving conditions. Finally, we investigate the impact of quasi-static charge noise on the fidelity of the CNOT gate. We find that the capture of charges near the qubits can strongly disrupt the conditional operation, while the nanometer-scale motion of charges results in a loss of fidelity that sensitively depends on the position and strength of the corresponding dipole. Our results quantify the requirements on barrier control, microwave driving, and charge-noise stability for high-fidelity two-qubit operations in Ge/GeSi hole-spin qubits.

articles.title: Quantum Reversibility Meets Classical Reverse Diffusion
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.18512v3 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bayes' rule connects forward and reverse processes in classical probability theory, and its quantum analogue has been discussed in terms of the Petz (transpose) map. For quantum dynamics governed by the Lindblad equation, the corresponding Petz map can also be written in Lindblad form. In classical stochastic systems, the analogue of the Lindblad equation is the Fokker-Planck equation, and applying Bayes' rule to it yields the reverse diffusion equation underlying modern diffusion-based generative models. It is known that a semiclassical approximation of the Lindblad equation yields the Fokker-Planck equation for the Wigner function, which is a quasiprobability distribution defined on phase space as the Wigner transform of the density operator. Here we demonstrate that applying the same approximation to the Lindblad equation associated with the Petz map produces an equation that coincides with that obtained from the Fokker-Planck equation via Bayes' rule. This finding establishes a direct correspondence between the Petz map and Bayes' rule, unifying quantum reversibility with classical reverse diffusion.

articles.title: Ground-state spaces of generalized stabilizer codes
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33221v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we determine the complete ground-state spaces for a broad class of generalized stabilizer quantum models defined over CW-decompositions of non-compact manifolds of arbitrary dimensions and topological type. We introduce a C^*-algebraic framework in which the quantum spin algebra A is realized as the twisted group C^*-algebra of an infinite discrete Pauli module P endowed with a symplectic structure. We establish a correspondence between stabilizer models and isotropic subgroups of P: Every Lagrangian extension of such a subgroup determines a C^*-diagonal of A, whose Weyl groupoid encodes the dynamics through a continuous 1-cocycle. This realization yields an explicit family of extremal ground-states for every admissible Lagrangian model, together with their decomposition into sectors. When the sector space is T₀, this gives a complete characterization of the ground-state spaces. We also prove that every Lagrangian stabilizer model admits a unique frustration-free ground state with a spectral gap. Our framework applies in arbitrary dimension, including higher abelian quantum doubles, homological codes, and a broad class of stabilizer models.

articles.title: Hidden Fisher Information in Many-Body Quantum Sensors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33893v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum Fisher information (QFI) determines the ultimate precision of a quantum sensor after optimization over all allowed measurements, but it does not quantify how difficult the optimal readout is to implement. We introduce a moment Fisher hierarchy F_M⁽k⁾, which measures the fraction of QFI accessible to collective spin moments up to degree k, together with a readout-complexity scale k₉₀ defined by the minimum degree required to recover 90% of the QFI. Applying this framework to a nonlinear collective-spin sensor, we show that many-body dynamics can preserve large QFI while transferring the optimal readout into high-rank SU(2) tensor sectors inaccessible to low-order collective observables. For system sizes up to N=100, first moments access only sim 10⁻² of the available QFI, while the degree required to recover 90% of it grows to k₉₀simeq 28. A rank-resolved analysis of the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) under weak damping shows that the nonlinear protocol pushes the optimal readout toward the highest available tensor ranks while strongly depleting its low-rank weight. These results identify nonlinear tangent-space shear as the mechanism behind a finite-size readout-complexity bottleneck in many-body quantum metrology.

articles.title: Lifshitz Phase of Quantum Gravity: The Infrared Fixed Point of the (2+1)D Unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34024v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a nonrelativistic gravity theory in (2+1) dimensions with w_infty gauge symmetry that we call unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons gravity. The theory has three dimensionless couplings, one of which is the Chern-Simons level κ. At large |κ|, the theory flows from an asymptotically free UV fixed point to an IR fixed point with anisotropic scale invariance characterized by a dynamical critical exponent z=2-tfrac32|κ|⁻¹. We speculate that unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons gravity undergoes a phase transition from this scale-invariant phase to a confining phase when κ drops below a critical value.

articles.title: Real-Time Correlation of Relaxation, Dephasing, and Two-level System Dynamics in Transmon Qubits
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Materials improvements in transmon qubits have yielded remarkable advances in qubit lifetimes (T1)and coherence times (T2). However, state-of-the-art superconducting qubits experience temporal fluctuations in their performance, which limit gate fidelities and quantum processor performance. We observe correlated increases in qubit relaxation and dephasing rates that last for minutes to hours, which we call T1 and T2 excursions. Using interleaved lifetime and coherence time measurements, noise spectroscopy, and two-level-system (TLS) spectroscopy, we find that these excursions are caused by single or few strongly-coupled TLS defects that spectrally diffuse into resonance with the qubit frequency. Our measurement protocol provides a powerful tool for understanding the noise sources that cause temporal fluctuations in superconducting qubit performance.

articles.title: Methyl radicals dynamics on (100)--(2x1):H diamond surfaces based on refined variational transition state calculations of gas-surface reaction rate coefficients
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Theoretical modelling of diamond growth should ideally provide estimates of the growth rate depending on experimental conditions. To that end, a description of all possible reactions related to the competing adsorption, desorption and migration mechanisms is required. Here, we provide precise calculations of the reaction rate coefficient of methyl-related reactions on hydrogen-terminated (100) diamond surface, as CH₃ is known to be the main growth precursor in chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth of diamond. To achieve this goal, we successfully combined Density Functional Theory (DFT) and variational transition state theory (VTST), allowing to extend our analysis to barrierless reaction. Our rigorous treatment of the quasi-free rotation of CH₃ adsorbates on the surface allows us to overcome numerical errors for the finite difference calculations of the vibrational spectra for evaluating the partition functions of the system. Our results suggest that the mechanism that deplete the CH₃ concentration the most is the absorption on a surface radical site. We also evidence the anisotropy of CH₃ migration along the dimer of the (100)-(2x1):H surface. In a more general perspective, the calculated reaction rates coefficient for methyl reactions and migration presented in this work, together with the data for hydrogen reaction and other main gas surface reactions, bridge the gap between the atomic-scale description and the large-scale modelling of diamond growth.

articles.title: External-field-modified entropic exchange in confined quantum systems: static versus time-dependent electric fields
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35178v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We review how external electric fields reshape the information content of spatially confined atoms, and we contrast the response to a uniform static field with that to a monochromatic, time-dependent laser field. The central quantities are the Shannon entropies in position and momentum space, Sr and Sp, and their sum ST = Sr +Sp, which obeys the BBM bound. Using the confined hydrogen atom (CHA) and the particle in a spherical box (PISB), its tight confinement limit, as reference systems, we first show that the field-free total entropy of the CHA depends non-monotonically on the confining radius whereas that of the PISB is strictly scale invariant. We then present Stark maps of the entropies for the ten lowest m = 0 levels at the confining radius of 6 a.u. The ground-state polarizability is reduced from the free-atom value 4.5 a.u. to 4.06 a.u. in the CHA but is 46.8 a.u. in the PISB, and the entropic response of the two systems differs correspondingly.

articles.title: Multipartite dynamics beyond bipartite entanglement equilibration
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35377v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Entanglement equilibration need not mark the end of quantum-information dynamics in quantum thermalization. We show that the complete Schmidt spectra of a fixed tripartition can become stationary while its multipartite correlation structure, distinguished by local-unitary invariants, continues to evolve. This separation occurs exactly within a finite window in self-dual kicked-Ising dynamics and asymptotically in Haar-random circuits. We further demonstrate an independently tunable timescale for multipartite dynamics using quantum-error-correcting codes. When coupled to a locally scrambling bath, ordinary entanglement approaches equilibrium through rapid local scrambling, while weak logical--bath coupling drives a slower reorganization of multipartite correlations. These results reveal a deeper distinction than the ordering of equilibration times: bipartite entanglement and multipartite correlation structure can probe distinct physical channels of quantum-information dynamics, rather than merely different stages of the same relaxation process.

articles.title: Negative-Power Density of States in Chiral-Orthogonal Disordered Systems and the IR Phase of QCD
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35524v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The recently discovered IR phase of QCD is characterized by an infrared (IR) sector of Dirac modes that separates and dynamically decouples from the bulk of the spectrum, becoming scale invariant in the process [1]. Among key features of this IR sector is the negative power-law behavior of Dirac spectral density near zero with power p close to -1. Here we start investigating to what extent can this behavior be mimicked by chiral Anderson models. In particular, we study 3-D chiral-orthogonal systems with logarithmic off-diagonal disorder where negative-power ``spikes'' have been observed [2]. We find that at finite disorder strength W of moderate strength, these models in fact do not have a power-singular density of states (DOS) at zero energy in the thermodynamic limit. Rather, this power p₁ vanishes and the spectrum features a very accurate power behavior with p<0 on an interval around E = 1 spreading increasingly closer to E=0 and E = infty with increasing W. We connect this to the fact that random hoppings t in these quantum systems are drawn from a scale-invariant 1/t distribution regularized via t in [e⁻W/², eW/²], and DOS with negative power can naturally arise inside that range. We show that limW → ᵢₙfₜy p(W, E)=-1 for all energies accessible by our data. This indicates that, upon removing the cutoff W, quantum mechanics transforms the scale-invariant 1/t noise into a scale-invariant 1/E distribution of eigenstates, which mimics the interpretation of scale-invariant Dirac spectral densities in the IR phase as being due to scale-invariant glue backgrounds [1]. Our results imply that, to model the IR sector of the IR phase, the IR cutoff in chiral Anderson systems needs to be viewed as descending from the randomness strength W rather than the lattice size L.

articles.title: Theoretical description of high-harmonic spectroscopy for uniaxial nematic and isotropic liquid crystals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35672v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Enabled by their controllable optical anisotropy, liquid crystals form a cornerstone of linear optical and display technologies. Bringing the versatile platform into the nonlinear regime, we explore its nonlinear optical anisotropy by high-order harmonic generation spectroscopy. Through a comprehensive study targeting gas, liquid, nematic, and crystalline phases, we present a semi-empirical tight-binding approach that provides insight into the intermolecular character of ultrafast light-driven electron dynamics across soft-matter mesophases. We demonstrate how intermolecular electron hybridization enables spectroscopic access to structural properties, such as the nematic director and order parameter. Outlining such foundational mechanisms opens avenues towards nonlinear liquid crystal devices and ultrafast soft-matter spectroscopies.

articles.title: Twist-controlled imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35784v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a controllable imaginary-time Mpemba effect in quantum spin systems using spatially modulated local rotations without changing initial bipartite entanglement spectra and correlation magnitudes. This feature unambiguously isolates the redistribution of spectral weights as the sole driver of the anomalous relaxation. Using the compact-boson description, we reveal that these twists act as precise mode selectors: higher-harmonic twists exclusively populate high-energy standing waves, structurally bypassing slow-decaying infrared modes to accelerate convergence. We derive exact analytical crossing times for these reversals and demonstrate that intentionally reintroducing the slow-mode population systematically delays the ITME. This exact mechanism is validated beyond the fixed-point theory via calculations on interacting XXZ chains and ladders. Furthermore, a twelve-qubit simulation of variational quantum imaginary-time evolution reproduces the reversals and their controlled delay, providing a concrete route to realize this protocol in realistic quantum circuits. Ultimately, these results provide a strictly controllable and exact starting point for realizing and investigating the imaginary-time Mpemba effect, establishing a foundational paradigm to harness anomalous non-equilibrium relaxation in quantum ground-state preparations.

articles.title: Anomalous mass renormalization in two-dimensional electron systems on ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor β-Ga₂O₃
articles.abstract: arXiv:2507.16137v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two-dimensional electron systems (2DESs) at wide-bandgap semiconductor surfaces and interfaces are fertile ground for emergent quantum phenomena. Here, we use micro-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to resolve the momentum-space electronic structure of a surface 2DES in β-Ga₂O₃, an ultra-wide bandgap semiconductor with a band gap of 4.7 eV. In situ electron doping of cleaved, high-purity β-Ga₂O₃ single crystals produces an essentially circular Fermi surface. With the self-consistent Poisson-Schrödinger model, the 2D electrons are estimated to be confined within approximately 1.2 nm beneath the surface, with an internal electric field of approximately 18 MV cm⁻¹. Our analysis based on ARPES measurements reveals nearly a twofold increase in the electron mass at high sheet carrier densities. This trend deviates from the conventional behavior reported for wide-bandgap semiconductors and indicates mass renormalization beyond the conventional screening-based picture. Our results provide quantitative momentum-space benchmarks for the Fermi-surface geometry and density-dependent quasiparticle dispersion of the β-Ga₂O₃ 2DES, opening a route to studying density-tunable interfacial quantum states in the UWBG regime.

articles.title: Space-time Floquet operator: Nonreciprocity and fractional topology of space-time crystals
articles.abstract: arXiv:2510.16562v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a space-time Floquet operator for crystals whose spatial and temporal translations are intertwined. Unlike the conventional Floquet operator, which describes evolution over a full time period, the space-time Floquet operator evolves the system over a fraction of the period paired with a spatial shift that generates the primitive space-time unit cell. Its eigenmode spectrum defines a space-time band structure that unfolds conventional Floquet bands to reveal the consequences of the intertwined crystal symmetry in reciprocal frequency-wavevector space. We relate the topology of these space-time bands to quantized transport phenomena, such as Bloch oscillations and adiabatic charge transport, and uncover an intrinsically fractional charge pump enabled by the primitive space-time cycle. Numerical simulations quantitatively support these predictions with small deviations controlled by the speed of the modulation. We also demonstrate how nonreciprocal parametric resonances are naturally anticipated and accurately predicted by our framework. Our approach applies broadly to both classical and quantum systems with space-time symmetry, including non-Hermitian crystals.

articles.title: Sound waves in a backreaction-affected analogue spacetime: acoustic metric, mass, and correlations in Bose-Einstein condensates
articles.abstract: arXiv:2512.24233v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Analogue gravity describes sound as a field propagating on an effective spacetime set by the background flow, which is usually treated as given; in reality, however, quantum fluctuations also feed back on the medium that defines this spacetime. This raises the question of whether a condensate modified by this backreaction still defines a spacetime for the quantum field, which has not been established so far. Using a number-conserving expansion of a Bose-Einstein condensate, which keeps the classical background and the quantum fluctuation distinct while retaining their mutual coupling, we show that in the sound-wave and eikonal approximations the first-order phase fluctuation still propagates on an acoustic metric of the backreaction-corrected condensate, but is no longer massless: it obeys a Klein-Gordon equation with a spacetime-dependent mass that is generated by the backreaction sources in the continuity and Euler equations and cannot be absorbed into the metric. Backreaction in a Bose-Einstein condensate is thus a change of the analogue spacetime, supplemented by a mass term that has no geometric counterpart. Solving the coupled condensate-Bogoliubov dynamics for a finite, quasi-one-dimensional gas quenched from a noninteracting state, we find that, while the depletion remains below 2%, backreaction enhances the canonically normal-ordered equal-point phase correlation by about 10% in the bulk and up to about 20% near the walls, and that the bulk enhancement survives a finite-resolution imaging model.

articles.title: Electric-field controlled nonlinear anomalous Nernst effect in two-dimensional time-reversal symmetric systems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.17252v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It's established that the nonlinear anomalous Nernst effect (NANE), originating from Berry curvature near the Fermi energy, is symmetry-permitted only when the crystal symmetry in the transport plane of two-dimensional (2D) materials does not exceed a single mirror line. Here, we show that an applied direct electric field can lift this symmetry constraint, enabling an electric-field-induced NANE emerge in time-reversal symmetric 2D systems with higher crystallographic symmetries. This electric-field-induced NANE originates from two contributions: the Berry connection polarization, which roots in the electric-field-corrected Berry curvature, and the anomalous-velocity-modified nonequilibrium Fermi distribution function. Additionally, we propose an alternating temperature gradient as a driving force instead of the conventional steady one, ensuring experimental detection of NANE via second-harmonic measurement techniques. The behaviour of electric-field-induced NANE in the monolayer graphene has been theoretically and systematically investigated.

articles.title: Eutectic and peritectic equilibria in coherent binary alloys
articles.abstract: arXiv:2602.15251v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work extends the Cahn--Larché thermodynamic framework to binary alloys in which two coherent solid phases coexist with an incoherent liquid and investigates how coherency strain energy modifies classical eutectic and peritectic equilibria. We derive equilibrium conditions for three-phase coexistence that include an elastic energy term dependent on the molar fractions of the solid phases and apply them to model binary eutectic and peritectic systems. We find that coherency stress transforms the eutectic point into a finite three-phase equilibrium field spanning a continuous range of compositions and temperatures. In systems whose equilibrium compositions are peritectically ordered, coherency stress progressively destabilizes the two-solid equilibrium without generating a stable three-phase field and can suppress the peritectic reaction entirely. This asymmetry is governed by the geometric relationship between the compositions of the phases: when the liquid composition lies between those of the two solids (eutectic configuration), the liquid serves as a thermodynamic buffer against the coherency penalty on the solid--solid pair; when it lies outside (peritectic configuration), no such mechanism is available. These results demonstrate that coherency stress can fundamentally alter three-phase equilibria involving a liquid and suggest that such effects may be significant in systems with large coherent misfits.

articles.title: Wave propagation analysis for a second strain gradient rod theory
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, an enriched model describing the longitudinal wave propagation is established based on Mindlin's Second Strain Gradient (SSG) theory, which can describe the heterogeneity caused by the micro-structure interactions in the frame of continuum mechanics. The governing equation and associated boundary conditions are derived based on Hamilton's principle, then the dispersion relation of non-classical longitudinal wave together with the extra-waves appearing exclusively in SSG theory model are investigated. The investigations are based on the modal density, energy flow, and forced response of the rod. Wave transmission and reflection through planar interfaces based on the proposed model have been calculated. Finally, the results of the enriched model are well interpreted by comparing with the classical theory results, and some useful conclusions are derived on the SSG theory based model in the wave propagation characterization.

articles.title: An Efficient Quantum Spectral-Galerkin Method for Linear Elliptic Equations
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents an efficient quantum spectral-Galerkin method for constant-coefficient second-order linear elliptic equations. The method employs a boundary-adapted Jacobi tensor-product basis that incorporates the boundary condition into the approximation space and produces Galerkin systems with polynomially bounded condition numbers and sparsity. For analytic solutions satisfying a suitable uniform regularity condition, spectral convergence allows the normalized Galerkin coefficient state to be prepared with complexity poly(d,log(1/ϵ)), where d is the spatial dimension and ϵ is the error tolerance, under standard sparse-access and state-preparation assumptions. At the state-preparation level, this improves the precision dependence over fixed-order finite-difference and finite-element discretizations. We further show how to estimate prescribed linear functionals of the solution, with an additional O(1/ϵ) factor arising from norm and inner-product estimation.

articles.title: Cavity Loss in QED Coupled-Cluster Theory: Polariton Linewidths, Driven Steady States, and the Rabi Splitting
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecular polariton experiments are performed in lossy cavities, whereas correlated ab initio polariton theory has been developed almost entirely for lossless cavities. In this work, cavity loss is added to real-time QED coupled-cluster theory (QED-CCSD-22) through a complex cavity frequency, which gives the non-Hermitian no-jump part of the Lindblad master equation. The resulting polariton linewidths and driven-dissipative steady states are, to our knowledge, the first from QED coupled-cluster theory. The linewidths obtained from the complex Jacobian and from real-time propagation agree and are partitioned by the biorthogonal photon numbers of the two polaritons. A closed-form continuous-wave drive of the cavity gives driven steady states and their lineshapes.

articles.title: Polarization-resolved haze in transparent wood - towards wooden glass
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transparent wood (TW) composites possess residual haze that limits image clarity despite their high light transmission, yet the physical origin of this scattering has not been established. Here, polarization-resolved measurements reveal a pronounced polarization dependence of scattering by a wood-polymer composite with improved refractive index matching. Polarization- and spectrally-resolved haze as low as 21% (40-45% at 550 nm for unpolarized light) with transmittance of approximately 92% for polarization perpendicular to the fibers was detected. It is found that the low-haze spectrum closely follows an inverse-square relation over the 400-800 nm range, well described by a weak-index-contrast Rayleigh-Gans-Debye (RGD) model invoking subwavelength birefringent heterogeneities within the cell wall. This physical mechanism was previously obscured by haze-limiting strong scattering from debonding gaps or refraction at the lumen-cell wall interface. Scanning electron diffraction independently reveals spatially distinct domains with markedly different cellulose diffraction responses within the infiltrated cell walls. The observed polarization-dependent refractive-index mismatch is attributed to inherent cellulose birefringence. Time-resolved measurements further support nearly scattering-free quasi-ballistic transport of the sampled transmitted light. It is demonstrated that selecting only a preferential polarization markedly improves image visibility through TW without further material modification. These findings connect polarization-dependent haze to the internal structure of transparent wood and identify ways to engineer a refractive-index match in hierarchical anisotropic composites towards glass-like clarity.

articles.title: Optical imaging with only the evanescent fields and without diffraction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on a conceptual framework for optical imaging utilizing exclusively evanescent fields, effectively eliminating or attenuating standard optical diffraction. We present the theoretical foundation of this concept based on the decomposition of dipole radiation into evanescent fields and homogeneous propagating waves, exploring the explicit conditions required to suppress the latter. By successfully decoupling and removing the homogeneous component, optical tasks, such as sub-diffraction imaging, can be executed solely via evanescent channels, bypassing traditional diffractive limits. We discuss the physical feasibility of this approach and provide concrete examples of how this conjecture can be realized using currently available laboratory and industrial techniques. The realization of this concept promises to redefine core paradigms in optics and fundamental physics. Because the minimum achievable feature size is no longer governed by the operating wavelength, this approach enables an unprecedented increase in spatial resolution, offering a direct pathway to advance state-of-the-art semiconductor lithography and chip manufacturing.

articles.title: Surface Functionalization with Lasers: from Nanostructures to Applications
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pulsed laser sources stand out as remarkable and versatile tools in the growing interdisciplinary field of materials science, offering capabilities for tailoring and customizing materials to meet specific requirements. Their ability to induce different controlled material alterations allows enhancing material properties that might otherwise remain elusive. In essence, laser-induced material modifications encompass a spectrum of transformative processes, ranging from subtle topographical changes in the nano- and microscale, to intricate chemical modifications. Among the challenges to overcome are the creation of approaches that allow tuning the properties of light to optimize interactions on various types of solids, including metals, semiconductors, and dielectrics. Understanding these interactions is paramount towards efficiency increase of the processing techniques. This chapter embarks on a comprehensive exploration of the intricate dance between pulsed laser beams and their interaction with matter at the surface. The applications of laser-induced surface modifications are far-reaching and extend into widespread industrial fields. Examples of these include tribology, where the study of friction, wear, and lubrication is paramount. Besides that, the modified surfaces find applications in wetting phenomena, changing surface energy and contact angle control, enhanced welding processes, and optimizing molecular adhesion for stronger and durable interfaces. The ability to precisely engineer material surface properties through laser processing opens new frontiers in materials and surface sciences, offering innovative solutions and pushing the boundaries of what can be achieved in various industrial and technological domains.

articles.title: Two-dimensional framework for modeling load transfer in nanocomposites with thin, stiff, and prestressed reinforcements
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for simulating load-transfer mechanisms in nanocomposites reinforced by thin, stiff, and prestressed reinforcements, such as, e.g., nanosheets or nanoplatelets. The reinforcements are modeled as open material surfaces treated as membranes endowed with their own elastic properties and residual surface tension; the matrix is assumed to be isotropic elastic. In the two-dimensional plane-strain setting considered here, each material surface is represented by a sufficiently smooth curve of otherwise arbitrary shape. The theoretical part of the framework is based on the Gurtin--Murdoch theory in which the surfaces are represented by traction jumps across them. The elastic fields in the matrix are exactly expressed by the integral representations written in terms of the unknown traction jumps that are functions of the second-order derivatives of the displacements. The computational part is based on the isogeometric boundary element method (IGABEM) that utilizes non-uniform rational B-splines (NURBS). The unknown traction jumps are found from the numerical solutions of the coupled system of singular boundary integral equations, after which the elastic fields in the matrix are evaluated. The procedure of extracting the values of the stress intensity factors (SIFs) at the tips of the surfaces is described. The proposed algorithm is validated against available benchmark solutions for multiple surfaces located along either straight segments or circular arcs. Selected parametric studies are performed to examine the influence of surface curvatures, relative spacing, orientation, and interactions. An example involving a graphene nanoplatelet-reinforced epoxy is presented.

articles.title: Amplitude-Dependent Damping of Gravity--Capillary Waves in Power-Law Fluids: An Energy-Dissipation Framework
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical gravity--capillary theory locates the restoring-force crossover, but the wave amplitudes and depths for which energy losses remain measurable depend on the constitutive response and on where viscous dissipation occurs. We develop a weak-loss mechanical-energy model for small-steepness progressive surface waves in memoryless power--law liquids. The full invariant of the leading inviscid strain field yields the deep-water bulk law dd A/dd t=-CₜAⁿ, with Cₜ=4Kk²(2kΩ)ⁿ⁻¹/[(n+1)ρ], and the corresponding spatial law dd A/dd x=-(Cₜ/v_g)Aⁿ. For finite depth we calculate bulk dissipation using a phase- and depth-resolved quadrature Jₙ(kh) and formulate a separate oscillatory power--law bottom layer. We solve the latter numerically in periodic state, obtaining dimensionless integrated wall losses I₀.₆simeq0.5432 and I₁.₄simeq0.4708 and recovering the exact Newtonian benchmark I₁=1/2. These values make it possible to evaluate conditional finite-depth bulk--wall dominance boundaries rather than only their amplitude exponents. The theory is organized into restoring-force, attenuation, local propagation-length, and dissipation-mechanism regime maps; at fixed wave steepness it additionally predicts a capillary-side maximum of normalized temporal damping for 0<2/3. Grid, time-step, domain, and energy-work checks support the reduced wall calculation, while the coupled bulk--wall approximation still requires independent free-surface numerical or experimental validation. The results provide a reproducible single-fluid reference for subsequent two-liquid interfacial-wave modeling.

articles.title: Is the arXiv Apocalypse upon us? A break in preprint growth coincident with agentic AI
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As an experiment in agentic assisted analysis, we used an agentic AI model to analyse the effect of agentic AI on arXiv submissions; data acquisition, analysis and the first draft were carried out by the model under the author's direction. Monthly arXiv submissions have grown exponentially for three decades, at about 9% per year. Fitting a piecewise log-linear trend with seasonal modulation to the full record, we find two post-pandemic breaks in growth rate. The first, in mid-2022, precedes ChatGPT and is carried by the expansion of AI research within computer science (CS); outside CS, growth from 2022 to 2025 remained at 8% per year. The second, between December 2025 and February 2026, follows the release of models capable of extended autonomous work and is absent from the AI categories themselves. Since December 2025 submissions without a CS listing have run 17% above trend, and in September 2026 total submissions reached a record 40,363. The excess is largest in mathematics, where submissions doubled within a year, and follows a gradient from formal and theoretical fields to experimental ones that is not ordered by surveyed rates of AI-tool adoption. In mathematics the increase is distributed across subfields and authors, two-thirds of it arising from a larger number of distinct authors rather than from a few prolific submitters. Across fields the clearest signature is a shift to single authorship: solo-authored papers rose by 70% within a year in mathematics and condensed matter, and by 44% in quantitative biology even as its total output fell, but not in experimental particle physics. The analysis is deliberately agnostic of LLM-detection methods: it uses only submission counts and metadata, with treatment timing fixed by calendar dates, and is therefore free of the outcome-triggered timing bias of author-level studies.

articles.title: Why Emission Spectral Profile of Diverse Fluoro-phores Look Alike with Thick Polymer Overlayers?
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fluorescence from fluorophore-polymer overlayers reflects an interplay between molecular photo-physics and thickness dependent optical propagation. Combining spectrally resolved single mole-cule measurements, transition dipole moment orientation analysis and ensemble fluorescence, we show that structurally and photophysically distinct fluorophores can exhibit similar red shifted emission profiles under thick polymer overlayers even without additional reflecting surface. This similarity indicates a common optical transfer function imposed by the overlayer rather than a pure-ly fluorophore specific molecular response. Although local molecular interactions, excited state dy-namics and vibronic coupling govern intrinsic emission, the overlayer modifies detected spectra through refractive index contrast, dielectric boundary reflections, cavity effects and collection ge-ometry. Vibronic energy spacing distributions remain largely preserved as thickness changes, whereas spectral positions and relative intensities vary systematically. Thus, polymer thickness pri-marily reshapes detected spectrum through optical propagation and outcoupling while retaining vi-brational modes. Time dependent density functional theory identifies candidate Franck-Condon and Herzberg-Teller active dye modes contributing to spectral fluctuations and dipole reorientation.

articles.title: Preparing State-Selected Molecular Beams with high Efficiency using Quantum Cascade Lasers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.34948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate the ro-vibrational state-selective preparation of CO molecules (v = 0, J = 0 → v = 1, J = 1) in an internally cold molecular beam using a continuous-wave, narrow-linewidth distributed feedback type quantum cascade laser, with an output wavelength of 4.65 μm. Using a modulation-free wavelength stabilization scheme, we show that population transfer to near saturation levels can be obtained with sufficient long term stability, as needed for state-resolved scattering experiments. We show preliminary results of CO molecules prepared in the v = 1 state, scattering from a clean Cu(100) surface. This study showcases the promise of QCL based excitation for state-selected molecular beam based scattering experiments, especially involving transitions in the mid-infrared domain (λ > 4.5 μm) which are otherwise difficult to access using conventional sources.

articles.title: Instability of exact finite-amplitude acoustic-gravity waves
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35210v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Godin (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 767, 2015, pp. 52--64) showed that compressible fluids in a uniform gravity field support finite-amplitude incompressible wave motions, in which every parcel conserves pressure and density, and constructed exact Gerstner-type surface and edge waves, possibly carried by currents. Using the short-wavelength instability method for compressible flows, we show that these waves are linearly unstable above a critical steepness. The stability of each fluid level reduces to a Floquet problem depending on two parameters: the steepness mathfrake=eka₂ and ν²=(1-mathfrake²)ν₀², where ν₀²=cos²α,N₀²/Ω², N₀ is the buoyancy frequency of the hydrostatic reference state, α the inclination of the plane of motion and Ω=(gkcosα)¹/² the intrinsic orbital frequency. In an isentropic fluid, a level is unstable if mathfrake>1/3, recovering Leblanc's threshold for Gerstner waves (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 506, 2004, pp. 245--254) and extending it to compressible surface and edge waves; weak stable stratification lowers the threshold to frac13-frac3281ν₀²+O(ν₀⁴). In an isothermal atmosphere, ν₀²=κcosα/(kH), where H is the pressure scale height. For horizontal wavelengths near 5.5,H/cosα, principal subharmonic resonance makes the critical steepness vanish. For the fast airglow wave observed by Hecht et al. (J. Geophys. Res., vol. 107, 2002, D20, 4444), which Godin interpreted with his solution, the lidar temperature places the layer in which this interpretation is consistent on this resonance, where the critical steepness is typically 0.1 instead of 1/3. Instability is confined to a layer beneath the free surface of surface waves and to a wedge at the shoreline of edge waves.

articles.title: Effects of Pulse Duration on Kerr Self-Focusing and Weld Formation in Ultrafast Laser Welding of Fused Silica
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kerr self-focusing can shift the laser interaction region away from the geometrical focus, making energy deposition near the joining interface difficult to control. Here, the effect of pulse duration on nonlinear focusing and weld formation is investigated from 262 fs to 10 ps. ICCD imaging shows clear changes in the axial position and shape of the plasma emission. Different pulse durations already produce distinct axial positions during the initial 2000 pulses, and these positions continue to evolve with pulse accumulation. The final weld morphology, weld position, and shear strength show corresponding changes. A ray-optics model including the Kerr effect is used to calculate the focal shift. The simulated trend agrees with the experiment and supports the role of Kerr self-focusing in the observed focal position change. These results clarify the relationship between pulse duration, nonlinear focusing, interaction position, and weld formation.

articles.title: Bistability of ice-shelf cavity circulation and melt under coastal polynya forcing
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Antarctic ice shelves play a key role in controlling the mass loss of the Antarctic Ice Sheet. Increasing evidence from regional studies suggests the possibility of abrupt transitions from low to high basal melt regimes under future climate forcing. The computational cost and complexity of these realistic simulations yet limit their ability to systematically investigate the steady-state response of ice shelves to incremental forcing, the reversibility of abrupt transitions and the underlying positive feedback loops. Here, we report a detailed analysis of abrupt regime changes in an ice-shelf cavity with idealized geometry, subject to prescribed temperature and salinity stratifications in the far field and near-ice-front surface salt fluxes representing the impact of sea-ice production in coastal polynyas. We show that a cold regime emerges when the buoyancy loss in the polynya is sufficient to trigger deep convection, while a warm regime develops otherwise. The steady response of the system exhibits hysteresis, characteristic of irreversible transitions, and scaling laws are proposed for both melt rates and transition thresholds. We demonstrate that bistability emerges when a gyre recirculates the meltwater within the ice-shelf front area. The bistable forcing range increases with far-field ocean temperature but decreases with background stratification. We also show that increasing horizontal viscosity limits bistability, which may explain the range of behaviors reported in previous studies.

articles.title: HarP: a simulation tool for high-order harmonic generation and propagation in gases
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurately simulating high-order harmonic generation (HHG) for attosecond science requires connecting the microscopic single-atom quantum dynamics and the macroscopic propagation of intense driving laser fields. HarP is an open-source Python code designed to address this multiscale problem. It solves the wave equations for both the driving laser field and the generated harmonics, using precomputed dipole tables for the nonlinear polarization density. This tabulation enables the direct integration of accurate microscopic models while avoiding costly calculations during the propagation. The methodology builds upon the approach of [L'Huillier et al. (1992) PRA 46, 2778] and has already facilitated multiple studies on phase matching, propagation effects and HHG optimization. This paper presents the underlying physical model, its numerical implementation, and comparison against alternative simulation frameworks.

articles.title: Thermosolutal Marangoni instabilities in a weakly viscoelastic falling film with soluble surfactant
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine the linear stability and nonlinear evolution of a heated falling film containing a soluble surfactant and a weakly viscoelastic liquid. The stress response is described by the short-memory Walters model, while surface tension depends on temperature and surface concentration. An Orr--Sommerfeld analysis and its long-wave limit determine how elastic memory and the two Marangoni stresses enter the instability threshold. A five-field weighted-residual model is then derived to describe finite-amplitude disturbances. The bulk and surface transport equations are written with compatible fluxes, which conserve their combined projected surfactant inventory in a periodic domain. The numerical examples show that solutal Marangoni stress suppresses disturbance growth and reduces the amplitude of the nonlinear waves. Thermal Marangoni stress increases the maximum growth rate, although its effect on the width of the unstable wavenumber band is different. Elastic memory changes both the onset and the finite-wavelength response. The nonlinear profiles develop a main hump and capillary ripples, accompanied by variations in bulk concentration, surface concentration, and interfacial temperature. These results describe the competition between thermocapillary forcing, surfactant redistribution and elastic stress within the retained long-wave model. The larger elastic parameters are interpreted as formal predictions of the truncated constitutive equations, rather than as a controlled extension to strongly elastic flow.

articles.title: Transverse detuned loading for modulation bandwidth enhancement in VCSELs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Directly modulated vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) are central to short-reach optical interconnects, where modulation bandwidth and power efficiency are critical factors for increasing data transfer capacity. Conventional oxide VCSELs still require power-hungry signal processing to achieve high-speed data transmission above 100 Gb/s. Here we report an experimental implementation of detuned loading in a VCSEL to enhance the modulation bandwidth. The detuned loading is achieved by carrier-induced index variations that reshape an engineered transverse mode so its overlap with spatially selective optical losses decreases with increased carrier density. This produces a negative differential loss reminiscent of that in detuned-loaded DBR lasers lasing on the long-wavelength reflectivity flank. The resulting 850 nm single-mode VCSEL exhibits an enhanced carrier-photon relaxation frequency of 44 GHz, yielding a 3dB electrical modulation bandwidth exceeding 50 GHz. The enhancement persists from 25 degC to 75 degC showing the robustness of the mechanism introduced. The same device supports 106.25 Gb/s NRZ transmission without digital signal processing, transmitter pre-emphasis or receiver equalization. These results establish transverse detuned loading as a robust alternative approach for extending the modulation bandwidth of vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers.

articles.title: Chirpons: elementary local phase oscillations associated with complex zeros
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a complex wave, the local phase variation provides the instantaneous frequency in time, the local wavenumber in space, and the local momentum in quantum mechanics. Here we study this quantity from the complex-zero structure of the analytic continuation of the wave. A single nonreal zero produces a localized Lorentzian phase variation on the real axis, whose position, width, sign, amplitude, and integrated phase are fixed by the zero itself. We call this elementary zero-associated oscillation a chirpon. The representation is exact for finite products and finite Fourier sums, and extends to entire and band-limited functions through canonical factorization. We illustrate the construction with superoscillatory sequences and discrete Fourier sums, showing how local anomalous oscillations can be reconstructed from periodic families of complex zeros. We further show how linear systems transform chirpons through the displacement of their associated complex zeros, and illustrate this dynamics for quadratic dispersive propagation and a resonant harmonic oscillator. This establishes a direct relation between local phase structure and the amplitude and phase response of the transfer function, suggesting a zero-based form of spectroscopy in which system parameters can be inferred from the motion, width, and orientation of chirpons. More broadly, the chirpon description provides a unified framework for instantaneous frequency, local wavenumber, superoscillation, backflow, and other local phase phenomena, while offering a new route for probing linear systems through the dynamics of their complex zeros.

articles.title: Critical velocity and dissipation mechanism in finite superfluid ⁴He nanodroplets
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A hallmark of superfluidity is the frictionless motion of an object below the Landau critical velocity; Whether this concept applies to nanoscale droplets remains unclear. Using time-dependent density functional theory, we investigate the motion of a sodium atom on the surface and inside a superfluid helium nanodroplet. For surface motion, we identify a critical velocity above which energy dissipation through ripplon excitation and the formation of surface-bound quantized vortices leads to rapid deceleration. Inside the droplet, the atom is slowed down to a steady-state velocity that depends on the initial speed, contrasting experiments reporting a critical velocity for dopants ejected from droplets [Phys. Rev. Lett. 111, 153002 (2013)]. Remarkably, the velocity of the ejected atom is nearly independent of its initial velocity. We demonstrate that this behavior results from the bursting of the bubble surrounding the atom at the droplet surface, challenging the previous experimental interpretation.

articles.title: Lunar tidal response-induced clock frequency variations on the Moon
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33117v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As clock performance improves, the instability and uncertainty of the clock's fractional frequency shift (FFS) become comparable to the FFS caused by the lunar tidal response (LTR), so the influence of the LTR on lunar time needs to be investigated. In this paper, we used the Keplerian expansions method to study the FFS to the level of 10⁻¹⁸ caused by the LTR between two clocks placed in different positions on the Moon. We consider the case of the Moon orbiting in an elliptical orbit, which is closer to the actual situation compared to the case of the Moon moving in a circular orbit. An interesting phenomenon is found that the longitude difference between two clocks can cause a change in the amplitude and phase of the FFS due to the LTR, but the latitude difference only changes the amplitude of the FFS. We further estimated the clock difference between two clocks near the Moon caused by the LTR. When one clock is on the lunar surface, and the other is on the Earth's surface, the LTR will cause a clock difference of % -5.68× 10⁻⁷ μ s/day between the two clocks. These are significant for the construction of a lunar time and clock synchronization near the Moon.

articles.title: Kaonic Atom Measurements with the SIDDHARTA-2 Experiment at the DAΦNE accelerator
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.35399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Kaonic atoms provide a unique experimental tool to investigate low-energy strong interactions in systems containing strangeness and, through high-lying transitions, to test bound-state quantum electrodynamics. The SIDDHARTA-2 experiment at the DAΦNE electron--positron collider performs high-precision X-ray spectroscopy of kaonic atoms using low-momentum charged kaons produced in φ-meson decays. Its primary goal is the study of kaonic deuterium through the measurement of X-ray transitions to the ground state, providing direct access to the low-energy K^-d interaction. In parallel, SIDDHARTA-2 has carried out a broad experimental programme with gaseous targets, including kaonic helium-4 and kaonic neon, as well as measurements of high-n transitions in intermediate-mass kaonic atoms formed in the materials of the experimental setup. In this paper, the main SIDDHARTA-2 measurements and their physics motivations are reviewed, together with the experimental strategy developed for kaonic deuterium and the future perspectives of the collaboration within the EXKALIBUR programme.

articles.title: From First Principles to Multi-scale Decomposition: Mutual Information as a Segregation Index
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.23069v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Segregation operates across demographic and spatial scales and requires careful and principled measurement. In this work, we derive mutual information from well-known general approaches to constructing segregation indices and interpret the mathematical properties that are unique to it. The properties relate mainly to its behaviour when demographic identities and spatial units are coarse-grained. Mutual information decomposes into the contributions of regions and supergroups, which reveals insights that would be inaccessible otherwise. We demonstrate this with an exploratory case study of residential ethnic segregation in England and Wales. Overall, we help researchers identify when mutual information is the only suitable segregation index and provide open source software to support multi-scale analysis.

articles.title: A Stable, High-Order Time-Stepping Scheme for the Drift-Diffusion Model in Modern Solar Cell Simulation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2603.09063v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a one-dimensional transient drift-diffusion simulator for advanced solar cells, integrating a structure-preserving finite-volume spatial discretization with Scharfetter-Gummel-type fluxes and a high-order, L-stable implicit Runge-Kutta (Radau IIA) temporal integrator. The scheme ensures local charge conservation, handles sharp material interfaces, achieves second-order spatial and fifth-order temporal convergence, and exhibits excellent computational efficiency and numerical stability. Its accuracy is verified against the classical depletion approximation in p-n junction and validated against four independent software implementations for an organic photovoltaic device under a common protocol. The framework's extensibility is demonstrated by incorporating exciton kinetics in organic solar cells, capturing multi-timescale dynamics, and by modeling mobile ions in perovskite solar cells, reproducing characteristic J-V hysteresis without empirical parameters. This work provides a robust, high-order numerical foundation for simulating coupled charge, exciton, and ion transport in next-generation photovoltaic devices.

articles.title: Hessian-Similar Optimization with Capped Participation: Lower Bounds and Virtual Masters
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.33835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: What is the round complexity of Hessian-similar optimization when each round can contact at most s of m clients? Prior rates permit a free master or full participation and do not characterize strict caps. We count every one-vector query and reply. A hidden-client chain gives a lower bound for zero-respecting local algorithms with adaptive cohorts and random stopping: on strongly convex quadratics, the required rounds are Ω((m/s)sqrtminδₐ,barδ/sqrt m/μ,log(1/ϵ)) for s≤(m-2)/2 in the high-accuracy, high-dissimilarity regime. Here μ is strong convexity, while δₐ and barδ bound anchor and average Hessian variation. To remove dependence on a poor anchor, virtual-master SVRS uses independent estimator and proximal cohorts and averages the proximal replies. With Catalyst, it reaches relative gap ϵ in tilde O(m/s+(sqrtm/s+m³/⁴/s)sqrtbarδ/μ) expected rounds on quadratics with strongly convex clients, independent of δₐ. Combining this method with charged analyses of existing algorithms matches the lower bound's polynomial dependence for s≤sqrt m and s=Ω(m); the worst gap is O(m¹/⁸). A held-out 12-seed synthetic study finds fewer rounds than tuned SVRP in nine of ten dip-family incomplete-cohort cells, versus two of 30 other cells. The lower bounds concern zero-respecting algorithms and do not cover unrestricted messages.

articles.title: Beyond Exact Recovery: Operational Success Probability and Sampling Cost for Approximate Quantum Optimization under Stochastic Uncertainty
articles.abstract: Approximate optimization algorithms are commonly evaluated through exact optimum recovery or objective-space approximation, although these criteria need not coincide with the quality of the resulting decision in its downstream operating environment. This paper develops an end-to-end evaluation framework that separates three notions of solver success: exact recovery of the mathematical optimum, near-optimality with respect to the optimization surrogate, and operational acceptability under stochastic downstream evaluation. We study the framework using a small binary inventory-control benchmark represented by a calibrated and held-out-validated QUBO surrogate and solved with exact enumeration, greedy search, simulated annealing, uniform feasible sampling, and ideal QAOA at depths p=1,2,3. The results show that mathematical near-optimality and downstream operational acceptability define distinct solution sets. For QAOA, the probability mass assigned to operationally acceptable solutions can differ materially from both exact-recovery and QUBO-near-optimal probability, producing substantial differences in the number of measurements required to observe an acceptable solution. For n=8 at p=2, the median number of shots required for 95% observation probability decreases from 392 under exact recovery to 84 under QUBO near-optimality and 31 under the operational criterion. However, operational success alone can be misleading when acceptable states are abundant. We therefore use a descriptive enrichment comparison against uniform feasible sampling. Statistically supported enrichment is observed only in selected regimes, while classical greedy and simulated-annealing baselines outperform QAOA on these small instances. The results therefore do not indicate quantum advantage; rather, they show that solver evaluation can change materially when success is defined in terms of downstream decision consequences rather than surrogate-objective recovery alone. The QAOA statevector implementation and selected frozen confirmatory cases were independently reproduced with Qiskit and Qiskit Aer to floating-point precision.

articles.title: 21st-century global urbanization drives disproportionate change beyond urban areas
articles.abstract: Urbanization is a critical anthropogenic process with largely irreversible effects on the Earth’s surface. However, the implications of future urbanization for other land-dependent systems, through changes in land availability and prices, remain poorly understood, largely due to simplified modeling assumptions and static urbanization constraints. Here, we quantify the impacts of urban land dynamics with a factorial scenario design combined with enhancements to a global multisectoral economic equilibrium model. We simulate divergent scenarios combining urbanization pathways, socioeconomic changes, and bioenergy deployment levels. Across all scenarios, global changes in non-urban land types by 2100 are almost twice as large as urban land changes. This is because managed land losses from urbanization are offset by expansions elsewhere or increased investment in yield-enhancing technologies or higher imports. These changes can increase crop prices, with some regions seeing up to a 20% increase. These results show that urban land expansion can have an indirect footprint that is much higher and beyond the physically urbanized area.

articles.title: Endpoint definitions and censoring in battery lifetime prediction across sources
articles.abstract: Reliable comparison of battery lifetime predictors requires a common endpoint and explicit treatment of incomplete trajectories. We examine how capacity references, right censoring and access to completed tar get lifetimes affect evaluation across experimental sources. A seven-source registry contains 220 physical cells; 214 contribute 318,707 cycle records. At an 80% threshold, changing from effective nominal to first observation references changes SNL observed events from 50 to 35 and HUST events from 0 to 77. For SNL predictions at cycle 100, event-only mean absolute percentage error is 36.31%, whereas 11 censored cells imply a full-cohort identification range of 45.37–47.80% without imputing lifetimes. At the observed 85% HUST endpoint, three-label calibration reduces allocation-averaged error from 75.64% to 16.25%, compared with 20.25% for a matched target-only constant and 14.23% for ordinary unshrunk calibration. Exhaustive evaluation of all 73,150 HUST and 19,600 SNL three-label allocations reveals consistent im provement on HUST but a harmful tail on SNL, where average event-only error rises to 48.50%. The allocations describe selection variability in fixed cohorts, not independent replications. These retrospec tive case studies support an engineering evaluation procedure that declares endpoint references, separates observed and censored outcomes, reports cohort-level error bounds, and compares adaptation methods us ing identical label budgets and test cells.

articles.title: Tuning in Dielectric and Electrical Transport Properties of CuFe2O4 with Incorporation of Metal oxides (ZnO, WO3 & MgO) Nanostructures
articles.abstract: Copper ferrite (COF) nanocomposites with different weight fractions (10 to 50 wt. %) of metal oxides (MOs; M = Zn, Mg & W) were synthesized by powder mixing method. The phase analysis and microstructure were examined by XRD, SEM and TEM techniques. The XRD analysis showed the formation of required nanocomposites without any other impurities. The examination of microstructure revealed the different morphology like; spherical, nano-discs, nano-plates and nano-spindle etc. The bahavior of dielectric constant (ε′), and dissipation factor (tanδ), of (MOs)x/(COF)1−x are consistent with Maxwell-Wagner polarization and Koop’s phenomenological theory. Moreover, the ε′ & tanδ show decreasing behavior with incorporation of MOs nano-structures. The a.c. conductivity with frequency follow the dynamical law σ (ɷ) = A ɷs. Finally, the incorporation of MOs wt. fractions reduce the conductivity due to substitution of Fe3+ and Fe2+ ions by metal cations (Zn2+, Mg2+ and W3+) from lattice site.

articles.title: Root-gap-dependent process window and weldability transition map for DCEN-GTAW butt joining of 0.08 mm AA3003 aluminum foil
articles.abstract: Establishing a suitable operating region for joining ultra-thin aluminum foil is challenging because small changes in thermal input can cause a transition from insufficient fusion to burn-through. This study experimentally investigates the weldability transition of 0.08 mm AA3003 aluminum foil during butt joining using direct-current electrode-negative gas tungsten arc welding (DCEN-GTAW) with dual argon shielding. Welding current was varied while travel speed, arc length, electrode geometry, and shielding conditions were kept constant. Three root-gap conditions of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 mm were investigated. Weld formation was classified as no stable weld, stable weld, or burn-through, with stable welds further evaluated through bead-width measurements and transverse metallography. Nominal heat input was calculated from the measured arc voltage, welding current, and travel speed. No stable weld was obtained at the 0.5 mm gap. At 1.0 mm, stable welding occurred at 5–10 A, while burn-through occurred at 15 A. At 2.0 mm, stable welding was maintained at 5–9 A before burn-through at 10 A. Bead width and HAZ generally increased with heat input. The results demonstrate that weldability is strongly influenced by both welding current and root gap, providing an initial weldability-transition map for parameter selection in ultra-thin aluminum foil joining.

articles.title: Comparative Study on Axial Compression Performance of Steel Tube–RCC–Timber Composite Columns using FEM Analysis
articles.abstract: This study presents a finite element (FE)-based comparative investigation into the axial compressive behaviour of steel tube-confined reinforced cement concrete (RCC)–timber composite columns versus their unstrengthened counterparts. Two column configurations were analysed: a nominal RCC–timber composite column (NTC) and an identical column externally strengthened with a 2 mm thick mild steel tube (STC). Both specimens share a 230 × 300 mm rectangular cross-section, 1000 mm height, four corner longitudinal bars of 12 mm diameter (Fe500), 25 mm nominal cover, M30 grade concrete, and a centrally placed 100 × 100 mm structural timber core extending the full column length. Three-dimensional nonlinear FE models were developed and subjected to monotonic axial compression, with the steel tube, concrete, timber core, and reinforcement idealised using calibrated elasto-plastic and orthotropic material models, coupled with surface-based contact formulations at all material interfaces to capture interaction effects. Results indicate that external steel tube confinement substantially enhanced structural performance: peak axial capacity increased by 33.5% (1128 kN for STC versus 845 kN for NTC), initial axial stiffness improved by 27.6%, and the ductility index rose by 43.2%. Peak corner stress concentration was reduced by approximately 19% relative to the nominal section. Behaviourally, NTC exhibited a brittle post-peak response dominated by corner-concentrated cracking, whereas STC demonstrated gradual, ductile softening characteristic of confined concrete action. The FE-derived load–deformation responses, stress contours, and comparative performance indices establish the quantitative structural benefit of external steel tube confinement in RCC–timber composite columns, offering design-oriented insights for subsequent experimental validation.

articles.title: Towards optimal preparation of triangular quantum cycle shifts
