Crucially, nematic order is locally preferred at each momentum, but the optimal nematic directions are incompatible across the Brillouin zone due to the broken rotation symmetry. This momentum-space frustration still enables a chiral ground state at large fillings or weak interactions in a symmetric parent state. Including heterostrain or inter-valley coherence further stabilizes the nematic ground state and sets the nematic direction. Under heterostrain, this direction shows a double winding with the strain axis, revealing the d-wave nature of the pairing, while inter-valley coherence makes it filling dependent. Our results thereby provide a unified understanding of superconductivity in TBG, in which electron- and phonon-mediated pairing cooperate, and clarify the microscopic origin of the competition between the chiral and nematic superconducting states.

articles.title: Thermoelastic wave-based logic for mechanically cognitive materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2511.00647v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent advances in metamaterials and fabrication techniques have revived interest in mechanical computing. Contrary to techniques relying on static deformations of buckling beams or origami-based lattices, the integration of wave scattering and mechanical memory presents a promising path toward efficient, low-latency elastoacoustic computing. This work introduces a novel class of multifunctional mechanical computing circuits that leverage the rich dynamics of phononic and locally resonant materials. These circuits incorporate memory-integrated components, realized here via metamaterial cells infused with shape memory alloys which recall stored elastic profiles and trigger specific actions upon thermal activation. A critical advantage of this realization is its synergistic interaction with incident vibroacoustic loads and the inherited high speed of waves, as opposed to recent adaptations of mechanically intelligent systems that employ innately slower mechanisms such as elastomeric shape changes and snap-through bistabilities. Through a proof-of-concept physical implementation, the efficacy and reconfigurability of the wave-based gates are demonstrated via output probes and measured wavefields. Furthermore, the modular design of the fundamental gates can be used as building blocks to construct complex combinational logic circuits, paving the way for sequential logic in wave-based analog computing systems.

articles.title: Eigenstate condensation in quantum systems with finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces
articles.abstract: arXiv:2601.18869v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Random quantum states drawn from the Haar ensemble with a constraint on the energy expectation value Eₐᵥ = langle ψ | H | ψrangle display eigenstate condensation: for Eₐᵥ below a critical value E_c, they develop macroscopic overlap with the ground state. We study eigenstate condensation in systems with finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. These systems display three phases: a ground-state phase, in which energy-constrained random states have macroscopic overlap with the ground state; a high-temperature phase, in which they have exponentially small overlap with each energy eigenstate; and an anti-ground-state phase, in which they have macroscopic overlap with the most highly excited state. In local spin systems the ground-state and anti-ground-state phases approach the middle of the spectrum as 1/[system size], but -- because the condensation phase transitions have exponential, rather than polynomial, finite-size scaling -- the crossover becomes exponentially sharp in system size and the high-temperature phase is best understood as an extended phase.

articles.title: Solution-phase fluorination of nanodiamond: near-surface NV⁻ activation and spin relaxation
articles.abstract: arXiv:2609.06605v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Nanodiamonds hosting luminescent point defects, known as fluorescent nanodiamonds (FND), are a leading platform for quantum technology. The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre is the most intensively studied of these; its negatively charged state (NV⁻) can serve as a qubit at room temperature, and its stability is governed by surface functional groups. We present two solution-phase fluorination routes for stabilising NV⁻: direct C-F bond formation by decarboxylation with xenon difluoride via a radical mechanism, and the Balz-Schiemann reaction, which replaces surface amino groups with fluorine. The two routes were compared by infrared, X-ray photoelectron, energy-dispersive X-ray, Raman and photoluminescence spectroscopy. Both gave a high NV⁻ fraction, up to sim85% on average, which to our knowledge is among the highest reported for surface-terminated nanodiamonds of this size and, in particular, for fluorine termination. We attribute the stabilisation to the fluorination treatment, which removes acceptor-like carboxyl groups and forms C-F bonds that give the surface a positive electron affinity. Frequency-domain relaxometry shows that the fluorinated particles retain a long spin-lattice relaxation time, 733±56 and 712±20 μs for the XeF₂ and Balz-Schiemann routes, several times the values reported for commercial HPHT nanodiamonds, although shorter than the 1173±123 μs of the as-received material. Fluorination thus activates near-surface NV⁻ centres, which dominate relaxometric sensing, at the cost of a moderate shortening of T₁.

articles.title: Economic Corridor Detection from Multi-Source Earth Observation and Commercial Geospatial Data Across Nigeria's Kilometre-Scale Grid
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identifying economic corridors at national scale is challenging where firm registries, transaction flows, and local economic-output statistics are incomplete or unavailable. This paper develops a reproducible multi-proxy screening framework for detecting economic-corridor candidates across Nigeria using a kilometre-scale analytical grid. The framework combines built-up land cover from ESA WorldCover, night-time light radiance from NASA VIIRS Black Marble, building-footprint density from Google Open Buildings, a static urban-intensity proxy derived from population, built-up share and night-time light level, and commercial point-of-interest density from Overture Places and OpenStreetMap. A dual proxy gate requiring both built-up evidence, defined as built-up fraction above 0.1, and night-time luminosity, defined as radiance above 1 nW cm-2 sr-1, identifies active corridor cells, which are then clustered into corridor objects and assigned interpretable typologies. The analytical frame contains 762,751 cells: national, state, and geopolitical-zone summaries use 749,191 canonical national-grid cells, while 13,560 configured metropolitan area-of-interest overlay cells are reserved for an eight-metro comparison. Applied to Nigeria, the framework identifies 11,243 active corridor cells on the national grid, representing 1.50% of cells, and 598 corridor objects spanning 10,682 retained cells and approximately 36.3 million people. Corridor activity concentrates around Lagos and other southern commercial geographies, while the method also surfaces emerging and constrained corridor candidates for review. All outputs are proxy-based screening signals for spatial planning, infrastructure prioritisation, and market-intelligence triage; they do not measure GDP, firm revenue, transaction volume, freight movement, infrastructure capacity, service adequacy, or official corridor designation.

articles.title: Multiport photonic routing with a single cavity-based electro-optic phase shifter per port
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Programmable photonic meshes can perform general linear transformations, but universal transformations on N modes require O(N²) programmable phase shifters, which cannot simultaneously achieve low drive voltage, gigahertz speed, zero static power, lossless modulation, and a compact footprint. Signal routing does not require universal transformations, which allows considerable circuit simplifications. We present a compact reflective circuit architecture that connects all input-output pairs across N modes in N steps using only O(N) programmable phase shifters. The circuit comprises a single passive N× N interferometer and a single column of programmable reflective phase shifters. We demonstrate the architecture by implementing a 3× 3 router in x-cut thin-film lithium niobate with a passive multimode interferometer and phase shifters based on single-sided photonic-crystal nanobeam cavities. Our programmable devices exhibit a 1.92 GHz/V resonance tuning efficiency via the Pockels effect, a footprint of 100,mum², sub-5-V drive voltage, and a 6.2 GHz electro-optic bandwidth. Through voltage-space characterization and physical modeling, we identify routing states with extinction ratios exceeding 11 dB at each output and demonstrate sequential routing at an equipment-limited speed of 10 MHz. Our results establish cavity-enhanced Pockels switching as a routing layer for classical and quantum computing interconnects across visible and near-infrared wavelengths.

articles.title: Photoelectrons resolve the phase-dependent variance of bright squeezed vacuum
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The variance of bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) is not only strong but also phase dependent, yet recent strong-field experiments with BSV have recorded only its magnitude. A coherent field of the same color provides the phase reference that resolves this phase-dependent noise. Strong-field ionization of xenon by this light shows that the photoelectron yield follows the BSV quadrature along the coherent field, and that the nonlinearity of ionization amplifies the quadrature noise many times over in the electron yield. The noise is moreover distributed unevenly over the photoelectron momentum distribution, differing by an order of magnitude between ionization channels. Strong-field ionization thus offers a phase-sensitive, channel-resolved detector of quantum light, while the quadrature noise of quantum light offers a probe of the intensity dependence of individual ionization pathways.

articles.title: Anchored HLLD: A Riemann solver for a hypoelastic diffuse-interface model of compressible fluid-solid interaction
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an HLLD Riemann solver for a multicomponent hypoelastic diffuse-interface model of compressible fluid-solid interaction, with no separately computed interface and a deviatoric stress advanced by an objective hypoelastic rate law outside conservation-law form. The difficulty specific to this model is that the stress evolution is nonconservative and, unlike the familiar volume-fraction terms of Kapila-type models, cannot be left outside the Riemann solve once the shear waves are resolved. The shear coefficient ρ(G+τₓₓ) sets the impedance of the resolved shear waves and so belongs to their eigenstructure. Anchored HLLD carries it inside the solve by evaluating the HLLD fan twice at each face, anchored in turn to each adjacent cell-centered state, with every cell advancing from the flux anchored to its own state. HLL, HLLC, and anchored HLLD form a three-tier hierarchy of increasing wave resolution in one framework. We prove local structural properties: consistency at the reconstruction order, exact species-mass conservation, and tangential-momentum and energy drift vanishing under refinement at the reconstruction's face-jump order on smooth fields, with one-dimensional tests illustrating these structural properties and demonstrating first-order drift convergence on discontinuous fields. Across one-dimensional tests and two-dimensional production simulations in the open-source solver MFC, anchored HLLD resolves both the material contact and the shear waves, HLLC the contact alone, and HLL neither sharply. Where refinement studies are shown, anchored HLLD converges toward exact or semi-analytic solutions. A three-dimensional shock-ellipsoid interaction demonstrates the solver with all six stress components active.

articles.title: Zero photoemission from icosahedral superatoms
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photoemission is expected to occur when the photon energy exceeds the binding energy of an electron, with the photoemission yield generally remaining non-zero above this threshold. Yet, it can be suppressed at specific photon energies, a phenomenon known as the Cooper minimum. Although complete suppression represents an extreme limit of this phenomenon, such zero photoemission has previously been reported only for atoms with an outermost s-type orbital and has never been observed in non-atomic systems. Here, we demonstrate the deliberate realization of zero photoemission from Ag12W-, an artificial icosahedral superatom, by observing a vanishing photoemission cross section 0.85 eV above the detachment threshold and reproducing this behavior in theoretical simulations. These simulations predict that zero photoemission can be common in nearly spherical nanoclusters, a prediction we experimentally confirm using Ag12Mo-, an isoelectronic counterpart of Ag12W-. Because superatoms offer systematic control over both size and elemental composition using the periodic table, our findings establish a route toward active control of photoemission in finite-size quantum systems and stimulate further investigations of underexplored physical phenomena such as nondipole effects.

articles.title: Predicting Negative Triangularity Edge Confinement with a Neutral-Coupled Full-f Gyrokinetic Model
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Global full-f gyrokinetic simulations coupled to a reduced neutral-fluid model reproduce key DIII-D experimental trends and identify mechanisms underlying improved confinement in negative triangularity (NT) configurations relative to positive triangularity (PT). Using Gkeyll, we simulate DIII-D inner-wall-limited discharges across the confined edge, scrape-off layer (SOL), and sheath boundaries, allowing the edge electric field to evolve self-consistently. Compared with an adaptive recycling-source model, the reduced neutral fluid model improves particle and energy balances and brings the simulated density and temperature profiles into closer agreement with measurements, with minimal additional computational cost. In NT, suppressed turbulent fluxes coincide with a broad, stationary zonal flow inside the last closed flux surface, whereas PT develops transient, fragmented shear layers. Spectral analysis indicates that modified fluctuation phase relationships and enhanced zonal shear both contribute to transport suppression despite broadly comparable fluctuation amplitudes. The larger co-current departure from a locally matched bi-Maxwellian in NT suggests a velocity-selective kinetic process that may help establish the edge radial electric field by modifying flows or current balance. These results identify kinetic and turbulent mechanisms associated with improved NT confinement within an experimentally established ELM-free regime and demonstrate the importance of coupling gyrokinetic plasma dynamics with neutral interactions across the confined plasma and SOL.

articles.title: Heat vortices and the vorticity triplet in kinetic phonon transport: a fluid-dynamical perspective
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: From a novel fluid-dynamical perspective, the present study investigates the heat-current vortices and heat vorticity in heat conduction process of solid materials. The heat vorticity bmω, defined as the curl of the heat-flux field, is decomposed into the orbital-rotation bmR and spin bmS, which collectively constitute the heat-vorticity triplet (bmR,bmS,bmω), extending beyond the existing single-vorticity research paradigm. As an illustrative example, kinetic phonon transport in a 2D porous solid structure is examined based on the numerical solutions of the Peierls-Boltzmann equation under the Callway dual-relaxation-time approximation. The physical characteristics of heat vortices and the vorticity triplet patterns are analyzed across different kinetic regimes in the phase diagram of the normal (N) and resistive (R) scattering processes.... In the hydrodynamic limit, the boundary generation mechanism of heat vorticity is further elucidated based on the Guyer-Krumhansl (G-K) equation generated from the truncated Chapman-Enskog (C-E) expansion. The boundary heat vorticity flux (BHVF) is proposed as a new concept for describing the local rate at which heat vorticity is generated at the boundary of a solid material. The general expression for the BHVF is rigorously derived for phonon hydrodynamics, and for the 2D steady hydrodynamic phonon transport case, we find that the BHVF is solely attributed to the tangential component of the net heat flux deviating from the classical Fourier heat flux. Furthermore, we show that the total vorticity contained in a control volume arises from the spatiotemporal accumulation of the BHVF, weighted by the memory kernel arising from the R scattering. The proposed theory and findings herein could be valuable for understanding the diverse vortical-flow phenomena in condensed matter systems.

articles.title: Single-step SU(3) Hahn Echo in a Qutrit Atom Interferometer
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Hahn echo is a well-known dynamical decoupling method that refocuses the dephasing due to energy inhomogeneities of a spin-1/2 ensemble and is widely used to extend phase coherence in quantum computers and sensors. Extensions of such techniques beyond the spin-1/2 have been reported, but have mainly used SU(2) gates, limiting their scalability. Here, we generalize the Hahn echo to qutrits using single-step SU(3) gates and extend the coherence time by more than an order of magnitude. The gates are generated through optimal control theory and implemented in an ultracold atomic ensemble in free fall. A quantum process tomography procedure benchmarks the gates and yields fidelities of ~ 93%, limited mainly by state preparation and measurement errors. Due to the geometry of the laser beams, the generalized Hahn echo also realizes a three-path Mach-Zehnder atomic interferometer with two independent interferometric phase differences. Our results therefore establish SU(3) control for dynamical decoupling of qutrits and multi-path atom interferometers, with the latter opening the possibility for vector force measurements and interferometric tests of the validity of Born's rule.

articles.title: Revealing and Mitigating Transmittance and Reflectance Errors in Integrating-Sphere Characterization of High-Albedo Scattering Media
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate optical characterization of high-albedo scattering media is fundamentally limited by integrating-sphere measurement errors. Scattering events spatially redistribute photons, leading to lateral beam spread and angular divergence that bias measured reflectance and transmittance. Here, we investigate these deviations, which are quantified and interpreted by using the point spread function (PSF), guided by the radiative transfer equation. Experiments and Monte Carlo modelling show that the widely used external-mount integrating-sphere configuration introduces systematic, configuration-dependent errors that become pronounced when scattering-induced lateral spreading is substantial. Using a normalised PSF to quantify photon redistribution, we map the characteristic lateral spreading length across a broad (taus,g) parameter space in the high-albedo limit, providing a basis for evaluating errors in specific measurement geometries. We further quantify the influence of measurement geometry and show that, in the pencil-beam limit, maintaining L/Dₚₒᵣₜlesssim 0.01 reduces the discrepancy arising from the finite collection aperture to approximately qty1percent. In addition, we introduce an internal-mount integrating-sphere protocol that suppresses scattering-related losses and yields transmittance and reflectance measurements in good agreement with theoretical predictions. Overall, our work helps users of integrating-sphere measurements identify scattering-related errors and improve the reliability of transmittance and reflectance characterization across a wide range of application areas.

articles.title: A Large-Volume GAGG(Ce) Detector Module for In-Beam γ-Ray Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report on the development and characterization of large-volume GAGG(Ce) scintillation detector modules equipped with silicon photomultiplier (SiPM) readout. Each module houses four large-volume GAGG(Ce) crystals within a compact thin carbon-fiber enclosure, minimizing the passive material budget and enabling the construction of high-efficiency, large-solid-angle detector arrays for in-beam γ-ray spectroscopy. The performance of 10 GAGG modules (40 detectors), including the energy linearity, energy and timing resolution, and intrinsic full-energy peak efficiency, was evaluated using standard γ-ray sources and ¹⁴N(p,γ)¹⁵O reactions, covering a γ-ray energy range from about 0.3 MeV to 8 MeV. Non-linear energy response across the measured energy range was observed due to the non-linear response of the SiPM. The detector modules exhibit good energy resolution (FWHM below 5% at 1.33 MeV), good timing resolution (FWHM sim500 ps at sim1 MeV), and intrinsic full-energy peak efficiencies in good agreement with Geant4 simulations, making the detector modules a promising solution for next-generation high efficiency in-beam γ-ray experiments at RI-beam facilities.

articles.title: Supercontinuum-driven broadband Fourier-transform photothermal microspectroscopy
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chemical characterization of microscopic samples often requires resolving multiple, widely separated vibrational absorption bands, including their positions and spectral shapes. Photothermal microspectroscopy provides a route to localized vibrational measurements by detecting absorption-induced thermal responses with a separate optical probe. However, rapid acquisition of broadband photothermal spectra remains challenging when spectral information is collected through sequential wavelength tuning. Here, we develop a supercontinuum (SC)-driven Fourier-transform photothermal (FT-PT) microspectroscopy platform that combines broadband near-infrared excitation with rapid-scan interferometric acquisition for localized vibrational measurements. In this approach, an interferometrically modulated SC pump induces wavelength-dependent photothermal responses in the sample, which are detected through a co-propagating visible probe beam and reconstructed by Fourier transformation. Using a 1.65-2.35 um spectral window, we demonstrate broadband photothermal spectra of aqueous samples with acquisition rates of approximately one spectrum per second. The system simultaneously resolves multiple molecular absorption features in a water-dimethyl sulfoxide mixture and reproduces the near-infrared absorption characteristics of liquid water with high spectral fidelity. Extending beyond homogeneous liquids, a dark-field detection configuration enables broadband photothermal spectroscopy of an individual 6 um polystyrene particle in an aqueous environment. This SC-based FT-PT microspectroscopy approach provides a rapid and broadband platform for localized vibrational characterization of liquid and microscopic samples, enabling chemical analysis with microscale spatial selectivity.

articles.title: Scaling the Wavelength to Optimize Ultrafast Laser Processing of Bandgap Materials
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The spectral characteristics of ultrashort laser pulses offer unique possibilities to control interactions in space and time as well as the subsequent material responses. In particular, selecting the wavelength predefines the fundamental mechanisms governing laser-matter interaction, and thus, how energy is deposited. This Chapter provides an overview on how the essential physical effects in ultrafast laser-matter interaction scale with the wavelength, and the consequences for bandgap material processing applications. First, we recall the main spectral properties of bandgap materials and discuss the important question of the expected processing resolutions depending on wavelength. Then, recent studies on the impact of the wavelength in ultrafast laser-dielectric interaction are presented. Finally, we present how the latest developments in infrared ultrafast laser sources can be advantageously utilized to internally process narrow-gap materials despite challenges related to increased nonlinearities.

articles.title: Covariance-Informed Ensemble Score Filtering: Embedding Localized Covariance Geometry into Score-Based Transport
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Background-error covariance models are central to atmospheric data assimilation because they spread partial observational information across space, variables, and dynamically coupled scales. Ensemble and variational methods exploit this covariance geometry efficiently, but their standard analysis formulations are largely built around Gaussian or locally quadratic approximations. Score-based ensemble filtering provides a framework for nonlinear distributional transport, but existing Ensemble Score Filter (EnSF) formulations lack an intrinsic covariance-mediated pathway for propagating likelihood information from observed to unobserved state components. We introduce a covariance-informed ensemble score filter (CI-EnSF) that embeds localized forecast-error covariance geometry directly into the forward diffusion and reverse transport. The proposed forward diffusion is covariance-shaped in standardized state space and becomes isotropic under the corresponding control-variable transformation. This covariance structure continuously propagates observational information from observed to unobserved state components throughout the reverse transport analysis trajectory. Experiments with Lorenz-96 and surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) dynamics show a clear regime dependence. For linear observations, a well-tuned LETKF is more accurate, while CI-EnSF maintains stable cycling and effective covariance-mediated information propagation. Under strongly nonlinear observations and under climatological initialization, CI-EnSF achieves lower analysis error and greater cycling robustness than Gaussian ensemble benchmarks such as the LETKF, with improvements extending across spatial scales in the nonlinear SQG experiment. These results suggest that the principal benefit of CI-EnSF arises from combining nonlinear distributional transport with the mature covariance geometry used in conventional data assimilation.

articles.title: Photon-Number Discrimination from Increasing Time-of-Arrival Separation in Wide Superconducting Microstrip Single-Photon Detectors
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Measurements of photon-number-dependent time-of-arrival (TOA) distributions in wide NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detectors (SMSPDs) are presented. Two SI10um-long devices with widths of SI3.2um and SI6.4um are characterized under pulsed SI515nm excitation. The TOA histograms are described by sums of exponentially modified Gaussian (EMG) components, with the wider device exhibiting components assigned to photon numbers up to (n=8). Adjacent TOA peaks become more distinguishable relative to their widths at higher photon number, in contrast to the compression of neighboring photon-number timing shifts observed in conventional narrow-wire SNSPDs. For the components assigned to (n=7) and (n=8), the FWHM-normalized peak separation is (2.15), and the fitted EMG distributions yield an equal-prior pairwise TOA-assignment fidelity of (99.6%). The EMG exponential-tail parameter (τₙ) decreases strongly with photon number, while the Gaussian-location parameter (μₙ) continues to shift between neighboring components. A phenomenological model motivated by absorption-site-dependent vortex processes and collective current redistribution captures these timing trends. These results support wide SMSPDs as a platform for TOA-based photon-number discrimination at high photon number, relevant to multiphoton-state characterization and photonic quantum information processing. The same geometry also provides a setting to examine how the spatial distribution of photon absorption affects vortex-assisted detection.

articles.title: High Resolution Hyperspectral Quantum Infrared Imaging with Undetected Photons
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32292v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum sensing in the infrared regime often demands the use of expensive and cryogenically operated detectors. Nonlinear interferometry has paved the way for information transfer from the infrared to the near--infrared or visible regime in various quantum technologies. A particularly interesting application of these interferometers involves spectrally--resolved quantum imaging using undetected photons, enabled by the use of temperature--tunable parametric amplifiers. In this work, we demonstrate spectrally resolved transmission imaging with undetected photons around 1550 nm using a spontaneous parametric down conversion based folded nonlinear interferometric scheme, registering the attenuation of a zebrafish larva as a biological feasibility test. We characterize and calibrate the interferometer, having achieved spectrally resolved interference fringes with a maximum baseline visibility of sim 74% in the near--infrared regime. Phase--stepped readout of a grating spectrometer gives a resolving power of sim1460 (from the spectrometer's point spread function) at 1550 nm, and sim 730 from the coherence length, the finest reported for imaging with undetected photons, over an instantaneous spectral window of approx 51 cm⁻¹.

articles.title: QuantumBilliards.jl: An extensible, user friendly, high-performance Julia library for the large scale computation of spectra and eigenstates of quantum billiards and related problems
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32605v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present QuantumBilliards.jl, an open-source Julia library providing a suite of numerical solvers for the two-dimensional interior Helmholtz eigenproblem with Dirichlet boundary conditions, a paradigmatic model in quantum chaos. The library implements conventional wavenumber-sweep techniques together with several accelerated eigensolvers: the Vergini--Saraceno scaling method, the expanded boundary integral method (EBIM), Beyn's contour-integral method, and the Compact Rational Krylov (CORK) method. It provides a common framework for constructing billiard geometries, exploiting discrete symmetries, computing eigenvalues and eigenstates, and treating smooth, cornered, and multiply connected domains. The library further includes reconstruction of eigenfunctions from boundary normal derivatives and the computation of Poincaré--Husimi (PH) phase-space representations. Available at: https://github.com/Quantum-Chaos-Julia/QuantumBilliards.jl.

articles.title: A Multiscale Eulerian Vlasov-Rosenbluth-Fokker-Planck Algorithm for Thermonuclear Burning Plasmas
articles.abstract: arXiv:2506.06672v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate treatment of energetic fusion byproducts in laboratory plasmas often requires a kinetic description, owing to their large birth kinetic energy and long mean free paths compared with the characteristic system scale lengths. For example, alpha particles produced by deuterium-tritium fusion reactions are born at high energies (qty3.5MeV) and predominantly slow down through interactions with electrons traveling at comparable speeds. As an alpha particle slows, its distribution collapses near the background ion-thermal speed, forming a sharp structure in velocity space. Such sharp features pose numerical challenges in grid-based Eulerian methods: capturing the full alpha-particle energies demands a large velocity domain, while resolving the near-thermal region requires a sufficiently fine mesh. Inspired by the work of Peigney et al.~[J. Comput. Phys. 278 (2014)], we present a two-grid approach that splits the alpha-particle distribution into energetic (suprathermal) and ash (thermal) components. A Gaussian-based sink term transfers particles from the energetic population to the ash population as they slow to the thermal regime, and a conservative projection scheme ensures that mass, momentum, and energy of the slowing energetic alpha population are conserved when it is remapped onto the ash grid. Unlike the formulation of Peigney et al., our method does not require a strict asymptotic separation of velocity scales, which can, in principle, be arbitrary. We demonstrate the robustness of this approach on challenging multiscale problems, including a surrogate for an igniting inertial confinement fusion capsule.

articles.title: End-to-End Differentiable Diffusion Conditioning for Physics-Informed Optimization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimizing high-dimensional physical systems under expensive evaluations and complex constraints is a central challenge in science and engineering. In offline model-based optimization (MBO), methods must improve designs using only a fixed dataset and no test-time access to the true objective. However, existing methods typically suffer from conservatism, unconstrained surrogate exploitation, or function as static inference-time samplers that cannot refine candidates against precise physical objectives. In this paper, we propose Differentiable Diffusion Conditioning (D2C) for offline MBO, which leverages the fact that deterministic sampling makes the reverse denoising chain differentiable with respect to the conditioning signal. D2C turns a frozen conditional diffusion model into an end-to-end gradient-based optimizer by directly optimizing conditioning variables at test time via gradients from frozen surrogate objectives and physics-informed penalties backpropagated through the reverse chain. We implement this idea in a composed proposer-evaluator framework and evaluate it on laser pulse optimization for inertial confinement fusion, sustainable data-center workload scheduling, and four Design-Bench tasks. Our method achieves the strongest results on the two real-world tasks and the best average rank across four Design-Bench tasks.

articles.title: Correct but Unselectable: The Hidden Interface Tax in Multi-Candidate Reasoning
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small language models deployed under cost, latency, or privacy constraints cannot simply switch to larger models when reasoning fails. Multi-candidate generate-then-rerank offers a natural test-time scaling route. However, more candidates do not always yield higher accuracy. We identify a previously overlooked bottleneck between generation and selection: a correct answer may appear in the candidate pool yet fail to be selected because it is incomplete, unparseable, or misaligned with the answer mode the fixed selector expects. We term this loss the hidden interface tax and formalize a coverage-conversion decomposition that distinguishes raw oracle coverage from selectable coverage, the subset of problems where a correct candidate can actually be consumed by the selector. We propose Compatibility-Aware Candidate Construction (CACC), an interface layer between the candidate source and the fixed selector that repairs fragments, aligns answer modes, and removes selector-confusing noise without retraining either component. On numeric reasoning (GSM8K, competition_math), CACC raises both oracle coverage and final accuracy. On GPQA Diamond, CACC alone improves final accuracy from 5.6% to 19.2% (+13.6 pp); combined with proposer-side strengthening it reaches 25.8% (+20.2 pp). On MMLU-Pro, CACC exposes a coverage-conversion gap: answer-mode-compatible construction raises oracle coverage, but final accuracy decreases by 0.85 pp under the original selector; adding proposer-side strengthening improves final accuracy.

articles.title: Reuse, Rewrite, or Reject: Evidence-Constrained Trace Reuse for Repeated Mobile GUI Control
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31712v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mobile GUI agents frequently perform repetitive tasks with similar interaction procedures. Reusing previous executions can reduce redundant LLM inference and execution overhead, but variations in user instructions and execution environments may invalidate previously successful actions. We systematically characterize these variations into six representative categories and observe that such changes do not necessarily invalidate entire procedures: individual transitions can remain reusable when validated against the current task context and interface state. Based on this insight, we propose graph-text templates for selective execution-trace reuse. The graph captures UI states and action transitions, while the text encodes task intent, procedural structure, and typed slots for variable content. A record-template-replay framework constructs templates from verified executions and leverages the current instruction and live UI state to reuse, adapt, or discard individual transitions. Given an execution trace, our framework reduces LLM inference token consumption by approximately 80% on average across five base agents on AndroidWorld, with most agents achieving at least 1.5-fold execution speedup over LLM-only execution. In real-device evaluations on Android and HarmonyOS, our framework achieves action reuse ratios of 70.7-79.8% while maintaining over 2-fold execution speedup in most evaluated configurations.

articles.title: MPQ: A Message-Passing View of Post-Training Quantization
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32127v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) is a key technique for efficiently deploying large language models, as it compresses weights into low-bit representations without retraining. Existing PTQ solvers, including GPTQ, LDLQ, and block coordinate descent, commit each weight block to a single codeword before its neighbors are considered, leaving near-optimal alternatives unexplored. In this work, we cast row-wise PTQ as posterior inference over discrete codebooks, in which existing solvers correspond to a zero-temperature, hard-decision limit retaining only the top codeword per block. We propose Message-Passing Quantization (MPQ), which preserves soft posterior information across blocks during inference and commits to hard codewords only at the output stage. MPQ first uses vector approximate message passing to compute approximate blockwise posteriors, then refines a hard-decision initialization by exact block coordinate descent. Across 2-bit lattice and 3- and 4-bit scalar quantization on dense language models from Llama, Qwen, and Mistral families, MPQ improves perplexity and zero-shot accuracy over strong hard-decision baselines, and composes favorably with preprocessing techniques such as activation-aware scaling and incoherence processing. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/poseidonchan/MPQ.

articles.title: Quantum-Classical Link Prediction on Dark Web Hyperlink Graphs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We analyze HTML content and hyperlinks from an offline Tor crawl containing 383 onion hosts and 2,067 directed cross-host links. The study combines semantic analysis with degree-controlled quantum--classical link prediction. Two directory groups emit 94.8% of the observed host links. Directed preferential attachment reaches ROC-AUC 0.976 with random non-edges, but falls to 0.550±0.014 under source-conditioned target-degree matching. With disjoint training and test pairs, multimodal logistic regression reaches 0.672±0.021, GAE 0.899±0.016, and VGAE 0.906±0.016. A four-qubit variational quantum classifier (VQC) comparison tests two encodings across 20 disjoint-pair graph splits under exact and 1,024-shot simulation, with classical controls using the same inputs and training examples. Its best exact mean ROC-AUC is 0.549±0.023, compared with 0.551±0.016 for RBF SVC and 0.573±0.029 for a 16-parameter MLP on the same inputs and training examples. These results support predictive signal in combined graph/content features and show why degree control, feature compression, and optimization conditions matter in quantum--classical comparisons.

articles.title: Reproducible Evaluation as the Substrate for Safe Prompt Compression in Production Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.31972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating conversational agents that act on live, mutable enterprise data is hard: replayed sessions drift as backend state changes, and a benchmark built today can silently go stale as the data it describes moves on. We present an offline evaluation harness for a production conversational agent that stays reproducible despite the live data it operates on changing, and that can be regenerated on demand once it goes stale. We then use this harness as the fitness function for GEPA-based prompt optimization under a correctness gate that guards against reward hacking. Applied to a production merchant-facing agent, correctness-gated compression shrinks the agent's full prompt surface by 3.5-7.6% without regressing held-out task correctness, consistently across three independent subject-model families, and for one, correctness measurably improves.

articles.title: Who Verifies the Tools? How Warped Formatters Mislead Agents and Their Verifiers
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents and verifiers often rely on the text a tool prints, and that text can misrepresent what the tool actually did, even when the tool's computation is correct. We saw this happen in a production RAG research system used by the Pilsudski Institute in New York, where tool output formatters misled an agent into giving wrong or incomplete information to users. Each tool did its job correctly, but its output omitted search limits, result caps, or identifier namespaces. We also recreated an unlabeled estimate caught in code review before release. We studied whether these formatters misled agents and verifiers and how much the repaired wording helps. We fed tool results to agents using two formatter versions: one with the key omissions and one with all missing details clearly stated. That difference alone changed what the agents claimed and what the verifiers accepted. Unsupported agent claims dropped substantially for three of the four failure types. In one test, verifiers went from accepting incorrect answers 90 out of 90 times to rejecting them 90 out of 90 times. A control showed the verifiers could catch the errors once they were given the missing facts and asked to judge correctness. We include the audit prompt we used with Codex and Claude Code in an exploratory demonstration, written with prior knowledge of our own system's defects. When pointed at an old version of our own system, it rediscovered the defects that were still live and surfaced twelve more we had not catalogued. When pointed at OpenClaw and Hermes, two of the best-known open-source agentic systems, it found warped formatters in both. We opened PRs to fix both, and the OpenClaw fix has already been merged. Practitioners can run the same prompt on their own systems today.

articles.title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent harnesses repeatedly invoke reasoning after tool feedback, even when an earlier call has already fixed the next action. We introduce HarnessMM (Harness Minus Minus), a method for improving harness token efficiency through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement (RSI). RSI iteratively refines companion harness configurations from training feedback, with validation selecting the configuration for deployment. A controller at the model-tool boundary reuses resolved decisions to replace later reasoning callbacks while actor weights remain fixed. Executable Decision Graphs store exact actions, literal arguments, causal dependencies, and public guards. Guarded Decision Reuse activates these persistent decisions from observed receipts; Certified Callback Substitution executes them through the native interface and records removal of the registered slow callback. New semantic decisions, unsupported evidence, and selector abstention invoke the original actor again. The representation restricts what feedback may change, while complete-task measurements establish quality and cost. On HumanEval, HarnessMM preserves Codex success at 90.82% while reducing Tokens/task (k) from 66.72 to 47.02 (29.54% saving). For DeepSeek Harness, success rises from 71.43% to 85.71% while Tokens/task (k) fall from 96.28 to 11.62 (87.93% saving). A separate MBPP ablation measures 26.91% lower cost than single-use graphs and 19.52% lower cost than retained callbacks. These results establish guarded decision reuse as a practical way to reduce repeated reasoning in existing harnesses.

articles.title: AgentTrace: Execution-Level Fingerprinting of Black-Box LLM Agents
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32092v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Verifying the provenance of autonomous LLM agents is a critical security challenge. Existing semantic attribution is easily obfuscated by system prompts, while active watermarking conflicts with schema-constrained tool generation. We propose AgentTrace, an active framework that identifies the foundation model behind a black-box agent via observable execution traces. AgentTrace injects structurally ambiguous probes to trigger tokenization-sensitive serialization failures at rigid tool interfaces. While these initial failures provide coarse-grained separation across model families, the temporal sequence of subsequent repair operations reveals fine-grained, model-specific recovery behaviors. By modeling these multi-step trajectories with lightweight Markov chains, AgentTrace achieves 96.0% attribution accuracy under adversarial identity spoofing. Crucially, sequential repair modeling successfully distinguishes the evaluated intra-family variants sharing identical tokenizers (e.g., Llama-3 8B/70B), substantially outperforming unordered behavioral statistics while remaining robust against prompt obfuscation and temperature scaling.

articles.title: "Not" is Not Lost in Translation: A Causal Analysis of Negation Representations in Multilingual LLMs
articles.abstract: arXiv:2610.32281v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Negation occurs in every language, yet its surface realization differs drastically. Despite this, multilingual large language models (LLMs) translate negation robustly, raising the question of whether they share an underlying representation of negation across languages. We study this question in six open models across English, French, Vietnamese, and Chinese, using causal interventions on a synthetic contrastive dataset and a negation translation dataset derived from FLORES-200. Across models, we find strong evidence that negation representations are causally controllable and largely shared across languages. In particular, we show that a contrastive activation direction extracted from one language can induce or remove negation in the others, and directions extracted from different languages are substantially aligned. We further find that negation is represented in sparse features: a single sparse autoencoder (SAE) feature per model suffices to control polarity across languages, while responding selectively to negated inputs. Finally, both dense and sparse interventions generalize to four additional languages and FLORES-derived sentences. We release data and code to support future work: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/negation-translation/.

articles.title: Nested Multilevel Monte Carlo with Preintegration for Efficient Risk Estimation
articles.abstract: Nested Monte Carlo is widely used for risk estimation, but its efficiency is limited by the discontinuity of the indicator function and high computational cost. This paper proposes a nested Multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) method combined with preintegration for efficient risk estimation. We first use preintegration to integrate out one outer random variable, which effectively handles the discontinuity of the indicator function. We then construct the smoothed MLMC estimator to reduce the computational cost. We prove that the strong convergence rate of the MLMC combined with preintegration reaches -1, compared with -1/2 for the standard MLMC. Consequently, a nearly optimal computational complexity is achieved. Besides, our method can also handle the high-kurtosis phenomenon caused by indicator functions. Numerical experiments verify that our MLMC with preintegration outperforms the standard MLMC and the optimal computational cost can be attained. Combining our method with quasi-Monte Carlo further improves its performance in high dimensions.

articles.title: Circular valorization of crayfish shell waste via pyrolysis: Biochar production, characterization, and adsorptive application for ciprofloxacin and aquaculture effluent remediation
articles.abstract: This study investigates the production and application of crayfish shell waste-derived biochar as a versatile adsorbent for ciprofloxacin (CIP) removal from aqueous solution and ammonium nitrogen removal from aquaculture pond water, addressing concurrent challenges of antibiotic contamination, aquaculture waste disposal, and effluent remediation within a circular economy framework. Crayfish shell biochars were produced via pyrolysis at 450, 700, and 800 °C without chemical activation and characterized using BET, SEM, FTIR, and XPS analyses. Batch adsorption experiments evaluated CIP removal under varying pH, dosage, contact time, and concentration. NH₄⁺-N adsorption was assessed in real aquaculture pond water.The biochar produced at 700 °C (CFSB700) exhibited optimal mesoporous architecture (pore diameter 3.8 nm, surface area 30.04 m2 g-1) and achieved >94% CIP removal within 80 minutes across pH 5,7 and 9. Pseudo-second-order kinetics (R² = 0.99) and Langmuir isotherm (qₘ = 5.73 mg g-1) confirmed monolayer chemisorption driven by hydrogen bonding, π–π interactions, and Ca-mineral complexation. In separate experiments using real aquaculture pond water, CFSB700 also achieved effective NH₄⁺-N removal (qₑ = 20.47 mg g-1) via complementary ion-exchange pathways.CFSB700 offers a scalable, low-cost circular economy strategy integrating aquaculture waste valorization with effluent remediation, demonstrating effectiveness for both CIP in aqueous solution and NH₄⁺-N in real pond water, without requiring chemical activation or pH adjustment

articles.title: Influence of activated carbon moisture on microwave assisted decomposition of HDPE
articles.abstract: This study examines the influence of activated-carbon moisture on the low-temperature microwave-assisted decomposition of high-density polyethylene (HDPE). Untreated and dried activated carbon were compared as microwave absorbers and catalysts. Moist activated carbon favoured n-alkane-rich wax, whereas dried activated carbon favoured gas production with a higher hydrogen yield. The wax obtained with dried carbon contained a larger aromatic fraction. The results indicate that activated-carbon moisture influences product distribution during microwave-assisted HDPE decomposition.

articles.title: Pinning-Controlled Reaction–Diffusion–Advection Dynamics of Iron Band Formation in Zebra Rocks
articles.abstract: Zebra rocks from East Kimberley exhibit rhythmic hematite banding with spacings of 0.5–2.0 mm. We test whether this pattern arises from self-organization during hydrothermal alteration using a reaction–transport model coupling Darcy flow, diffusion, and nonlinear precipitation kinetics. Following the continuum-phase approach of Baruah et al. (2023), we treat the felsic (Fe2+-bearing fluid) and mafic (Fe3+-precipitate) constituents as two petrologically interacting continuum phases. Linear stability analysis reveals that the system exhibits a saddle-focus instability (Tr(J) = 0.023 > 0, det(J) ≈ 0) rather than a pure Turing instability; pattern formation is driven by nonlinear reaction kinetics and advective transport. Host-rock heterogeneities—represented as pinning sites following the pinning field concept of Baruah et al. (2023)— provide the localized perturbations (η = 10−4) that break spatial symmetry. Two-dimensional simulations reproduce key field characteristics with mean spacing of 1.45 mm, dominant wavelength of 1.25 mm, pattern contrast of 0.986, CV = 3.8%, and Liesegang coefficient p = 1.001 ± 0.056, all consistent with natural observations. The 95% confidence interval (p ∈ [0.891, 1.112]) includes p = 1.0, confirming nearly constant band spacing in the advection-dominated regime (v ≈ 6.36×10−6 m/s). The four interface pattern types recognized by Baruah et al. (2023)—planar, wavy, fingering, and incoherent—are shown to emerge naturally from our model under varying diffusion coefficients, pinning strengths, and reaction coupling. This study provides a quantitative framework linking millimetre-scale mineral textures to self-organized hydrothermal processes, with pinning heterogeneities providing the symmetry-breaking mechanism for pattern initiation.

articles.title: Decision-Dependent Adversarial Planning for Cyber-Resilient Solar-Rich Power Grids
articles.abstract: The rapid expansion of solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity has exposed the grid to escalating cyber threats that exploit the growing digital footprint of renewable infrastructure. Existing joint planning methods for PV and battery energy storage systems (BESSs) largely optimize techno-economic performance without capturing how deployment decisions reshape cyber threats. Temporal aggregation can obscure seasonal operations and storage-state evolution, while plan-dependent attacks create a costly mixed-integer search. To bridge the gap, we develop a simulation-driven Decision-Dependent Adversarial Bayesian Optimization (DD-ABO) framework that combines hourly full-year simulations preserving seasonal operations and BESS trajectories, candidate-specific adversarial PV-curtailment evaluation, and a random-forest surrogate with expected improvement for sample-efficient PV-BESS planning. Experiments using 2025 New England load and solar data mapped to the IEEE 39-bus system show that approximately half of the selected worst-case attacks begin at the upper neck of the duck curve, and meanwhile the resulting plans exhibit cross-zone and vendor diversification under the modeled dependencies. Relative to attack-agnostic Bayesian optimization, DD-ABO reduces the mean worst-case attack-induced operational penalty and mean expected energy not served within the evaluated scenarios by 80.2% and 85.0%, respectively, with only a marginal increase in base-case operational cost and no statistically significant increase in annualized investment or fixed maintenance costs. These results demonstrate that, in this case study, decision-dependent adversarial planning can improve cyber resilience through deployment structure rather than capital or maintenance over-provisioning.

articles.title: CFD Based Geometry Re-Design & Performance Analysis of a Scramjet Intake
articles.abstract: The aerodynamic performance of a scramjet intake depends on efficient supersonic compression, reduced total-pressure losses, and suitable flow distribution at the combustor interface. The present study investigates multiple redesigned scramjet intake configurations using 2-dimensional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations. Systematic geometric modifications are introduced to the baseline configuration to examine their influence on internal shock-wave interactions, compression characteristics, and downstream flow development. Numerical simulations are performed using a density-based, steady-state solver coupled with the SST (k-omega) turbulence model. The redesigned configurations are evaluated at an inlet static pressure of 52 kPa over a Mach-number of 4. A structured computational grid is employed, and grid-independence assessment is performed to minimize spatial discretization effects. The flow field is evaluated using Mach number, static pressure, static temperature, velocity distribution, shock-wave structure, pressure recovery, and total-pressure losses. Particular attention is given to oblique shock-wave interactions with the intake walls and their influence on compression and exit-flow characteristics. The comparative analysis provides insight into the aerodynamic response of modified intake geometries and their suitability for effective supersonic compression with controlled aerodynamic losses.

articles.title: Simulation-Driven Design of Guardrail Structural Spacers: Influence of Geometry on Impact Response
articles.abstract: The dynamic performance of road restraint systems is strongly influenced by the local behaviour of structural spacers, whose role is sometimes simplified or neglected in impact analyses. In particular, the spacer geometry governs load transfer paths and the localization of deformations, with direct effects on the global dynamic response of the barrier. In this study, the effect of spacer geometry on the impact behaviour of a steel guardrail system is investigated by means of an explicit finite element model, validated against experimental acceleration time-histories acquired from full-scale crash tests. Two spacer configurations are considered: a conventional solution and a rhomboidal geometry analysed under identical impact conditions to isolate the effect of spacer topology on the structural response of the system. In addition to the numerical assessment of deformations, stresses, and performance indicators, the study includes an analysis of manufacturing considerations, highlighting the compatibility of the proposed geometry with industrial cold sheet metal forming processes and a design for manufacturing approach. The results show that the rhomboidal configuration promotes a more controlled deformation behaviour, limiting the propagation of deformations along the barrier and producing a more regular overall dynamic response, while remaining compatible with conventional sheet-metal manufacturing. The proposed approach provides an integrated design- and manufacturing-oriented framework for the evaluation of spacer geometries in road restraint systems.

articles.title: Near-Infrared-Responsive Au Nanorod/UiO-66-NH₂ Hybrids for Photocatalytic Carbon Dioxide Conversion
articles.abstract: The efficient conversion of carbon dioxide into value-added chemicals using solar energy remains a critical scientific and technological challenge, particularly due to the limited utilization of the near-infrared (NIR) region of the solar spectrum. In this study, we report the design and synthesis of an ultrabroadband plasmonic–metal–organic framework (MOF) hybrid photocatalyst capable of driving the carbon dioxide reduction reaction under NIR irradiation. Gold nanorods with tuneable longitudinal surface plasmon resonance were successfully integrated into a UiO-66-NH₂ framework through an in-situ encapsulation strategy followed by mild thermal treatment to enhance interfacial coupling. The resulting composite exhibits strong and continuous light absorption across the 300–1200 nm range, enabling efficient harvesting of low-energy photons. Under 808 nm irradiation, the optimized catalyst demonstrates a CO production rate of 152.3 μmol g⁻¹ h⁻¹ with a selectivity exceeding 90%. Detailed spectroscopic and electrochemical analyses reveal that plasmon-induced hot carrier generation and efficient interfacial charge transfer play a decisive role in enhancing photocatalytic performance. This work provides a viable pathway for extending photocatalytic activity into the NIR region and contributes to the advancement of solar-to-chemical energy conversion technologies.

articles.title: Receiver-Limited Fisher Information for Quantum Sensors under Realistic Readout
articles.abstract: Quantum Fisher information quantifies the sensitivity encoded in a parameter-dependent quantum state, whereas the performance of a practical sensor is limited by the information that survives the physical channel and can be extracted by the available receiver. We introduce an accessible Fisher-information framework based on a physically admissible family of measurements and use it to separate state-level sensitivity, channel degradation, and receiver limitations. The framework is applied to Ramsey and NOON interferometry, squeezed-state displacement sensing, two-level thermometry, and multiparameter qubit sensing. We show that resource normalization, finite visibility, readout errors, measurement rank, shot allocation, calibration uncertainty, and nuisance parameters can substantially modify the experimentally available advantage. For squeezed-state sensing, homodyne-axis misalignment produces a finite optimal squeezing, while bounded calibration uncertainty leads to a robust operating rule. In the pure-loss model considered here, attenuation reduces the attainable information without shifting this optimum. The results provide practical design rules that connect quantum-enhanced state preparation with realistic measurement constraints and experimentally extractable sensing performance.

articles.title: Categorization of scientific publications using large language models as applied to atomic spectroscopy
articles.abstract: We present an automated framework employing large language models to categorize atomic spectroscopy literature for NIST bibliographic databases. The system processes native PDFs and supplementary materials via instruction-driven reasoning agents to assign structured search keywords encompassing target species, subject codes, and experimental methodologies. Validation against human-curated datasets demonstrates high precision in elemental species identification, while establishing that granular subject code assignment remains the primary source of categorization error.

articles.title: Aspect-ratio-dependent stall delay and spanwise separation topology of a finite NACA 2412 wing at Re = 2.2 x 106
articles.abstract: This study presents a systematic RANS-based investigation of the NACA 2412 wing at Re = 2.2 × 106 across AR = 1, 2, and 4, using the k–ε model with standard wall functions. A wall-shear-stress-based separation fraction metric S is introduced to quantify separation and extended spanwise as S(z/b) to map the three-dimensional separation topology. The two-dimensional results were validated against experimental measurements, predicting pre-stall lift within 2–3% with 1–2° stall-angle overprediction. For three-dimensional cases, the stall onset is progressively delayed with decreasing AR, from α = 20° at AR = 4 to α = 32° at AR = 1, compared to the two-dimensional baseline of α = 16°. This delay is attributed to tip-vortex downwash suppressing trailing-edge separation across a larger span fraction. The spanwise separation profiles reveal a smooth root-to-tip gradient at higher AR, whereas the profiles collapse into a broad inner-span plateau at AR = 1. These results demonstrate how aspect ratio affects chordwise and spanwise trailing-edge separation from onset to deep stall and provide a surface-resolved reference dataset for low-AR cambered-wing stall prediction and finite-wing aerodynamic design.

articles.title: Real-time measurement of dielectric properties of lunar regolith simulants
articles.abstract: Establishing a permanent settlement on the Moon will require infrastructure capable of protecting astronauts and equipment from the abrasive effects of lunar dust, radiation, micrometeorite impacts, and extreme thermal fluctuations. Lunar regolith is a dielectric material that can be efficiently heated to its melting temperature using microwave energy, providing an abundant, and cost-effective feedstock for energy-efficient construction. In this study, we measured the complex permittivity of two lunar regolith simulants, the mare simulant JSC-1A and the highland simulant NU-LHT-4M, from room temperature to melting. A dual-mode permittivity measurement technique enabled simultaneous measurement of complex permittivity while the simulant was heated using a single-mode microwave system operating at approximately 2.45 GHz. For both simulants, the real and imaginary parts of the permittivity increases significantly with temperature. The resulting temperature-dependent data will enable more accurate numerical modelling of microwave heating of lunar regolith, supporting the optimisation of microwave heating devices and improved energy efficiency in lunar ISRU processing.

articles.title: Surface State Decouples Normal Detachment and Slip Initiation in Grip- Optimized Rubber Contacts
articles.abstract: Rubber surface condition can influence both normal detachment and resistance to tangential slip, but these responses are not necessarily governed by the same interfacial mechanisms. This study investigated how surface preparation of a grip-optimized climbing shoe rubber affects pull-off and slip initiation against smooth and textured rigid spherical counter-surfaces. The same rubber compound was tested in four surface states: the original moulded surface (P0), a cut surface exposing subsurface material (CUT), and surfaces ground with P100 or P60 abrasive paper. Normal detachment was characterized using maximum pull-off force and work of detachment, while tangential response was evaluated using static and steady sliding friction coefficients and the static-to-steady friction drop.Surface preparation strongly altered both detachment and friction, but the responses were not directly coupled. The ground surfaces generally showed higher detachment resistance but lower static and steady sliding friction than P0, with the magnitude of these effects depending on counter-surface texture. CUT further emphasized this decoupling: despite having nearly the same arithmetic mean height (Sa) as P0, it produced markedly greater pull-off force and work of detachment, particularly against the smooth pin, while exhibiting lower static friction. This demonstrates that surface preparation affects the response through more than roughness amplitude alone.Resistance to normal detachment therefore cannot be used alone to predict resistance to tangential slip. Pull-off and friction tests provide complementary information, and both rubber surface preparation and representative counter-surface texture should be controlled when evaluating climbing shoe rubber performance.

articles.title: Role of recycled fine aggregates in regulating hydration behavior and mechanical performance of alkali-activated slag mortars
articles.abstract: Recycled fine aggregates (RFA) contain old cement paste with relatively high alkalinity, which may provide additional activation in alkali activated slag systems. In this study, RFA was used to replace river sand at replacement ratios of 0%, 50% and 100% in alkali activated slag mortars. Liquid and solid sodium silicate with Na2O concentrations of 0%, 3%, 6% and 9% were investigated. The setting time, flowability, compressive and flexural strengths, heat evolution and microstructure were evaluated. The results showed that increasing the RFA content shortened the setting time but reduced the flowability of the mortars. RFA also promoted strength development, particularly at early ages and moderate alkali activator dosages. For mortars activated with 6% liquid sodium silicate, the 28-day compressive strength increased from 50.9 MPa for 0% RFA to 57.2 MPa for 100% RFA. Even without an external alkali activator, the mortar containing 100% RFA achieved a 28-day compressive strength of 13.7 MPa. The main hydration peak of mortars containing 0%, 50% and 100% RFA appeared at approximately 81, 68 and 51 h, respectively, confirming the accelerating effect of RFA on slag hydration. SEM and EDS observations further indicated that RFA promoted early-age microstructure densification, while the attached old paste introduced a double-layer interface transition zone. Overall, the effect of RFA on alkali activated slag mortar results from the competition between enhanced hydration and the adverse effects associated with reduced flowability and interfacial defects.

articles.title: Finite Local Information Capacity in Continuum Dynamics
articles.abstract: Finite-dimensional local Hilbert spaces are widely used as microscopic regulators and have also been proposed as a fundamental information-capacity property of space-time. A finite local dimension, however, is not equivalent to a spatial lattice spacing, and neither is equivalent to a coarse-graining scale. We formulate a regulator-resolved framework that keeps these three notions separate and defines finite-information deviations operationally as the failure of microscopic and effective time evolution to commute with a specified coarse-graining channel. The resulting deviation is a state- and observable-dependent quantity in a common effective state space, rather than a formal subtraction of generators acting on different domains. We derive a decomposition into capacity, spatial-discretization, and coarse-graining contributions; a finite-time capacity bound controlled by discarded state weight and leakage through the cutoff boundary; observable error bounds; and a sharp continuity bound for subsystem entropies. We further show that block entropy and averaged one-cell entropy differ by a relative-entropy measure of total correlation and therefore cannot be interchanged. An information-geometric expansion of neighboring reduced states yields a nonlinear sigma-model effective action on the manifold of coarse-grained states. A single entropy field follows only under an additional one-dimensional closure condition. Finally, we test the framework in an exactly evolved periodic Klein--Gordon chain with independently variable lattice spacing and local number-state cutoff. Spectral peaks are extracted from dynamical matrix elements rather than imposed. Ground-state, dispersion, reduced-state, and entropy errors converge rapidly with local capacity, while the remaining lattice--continuum discrepancy persists at fixed spacing. The results provide a controlled mathematical and numerical foundation for finite-information models without claiming a unique microscopic theory of quantum gravity.

articles.title: Rare-Earth-Element-Doped ZnO Thin Films for Gas Sensing and Solar-Cell Applications A Critical Review of Structure–Property Relationships, Defect Chemistry, Surface Morphology and Device-Level Performance
articles.abstract: Rare-earth-element (REE) modification provides a route to tune the structure, surface chemistry, optical response and carrier transport of zinc oxide (ZnO), a wide-band-gap semiconductor used in resistive gas sensors and as a transparent or electron-transport layer in photovoltaic architectures. Yet the performance consequences of REE incorporation are strongly dependent on dopant identity, concentration, oxidation state, synthesis route, defect compensation and device architecture. This critical review examines how Ce, La, Nd, Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Er, Yb and related ions influence wurtzite phase stability, lattice strain, crystallite growth, surface morphology, optical absorption, Tauc-derived band-gap estimates, conductivity and interface behaviour. For gas sensing, the discussion connects adsorption and surface charge transfer to depletion-layer width, grain-boundary barriers, humidity dependence and selectivity. For photovoltaics, it distinguishes film-level optical/electrical indicators from complete-device metrics such as short-circuit current density, open-circuit voltage, fill factor, power-conversion efficiency and operational stability. Published examples include Nd-modified ZnO showing 43 s response and 12 s recovery to 25 ppm NH₃ at room temperature in a particular SILAR-prepared sensor, and recent Sm/Eu/Gd-doped samples with dopant-dependent ammonia response [1, 2]. These values are not directly comparable without harmonized protocols. The review emphasizes evidence quality, the danger of assigning visible photoluminescence uniquely to oxygen vacancies, and the need to verify dopant location using complementary methods. A composition–process–structure–defect–property–function framework is proposed to guide reproducible materials development and to prevent the mistaken assumption that a formulation optimized for gas adsorption will also optimize photovoltaic charge extraction.

articles.title: NHC-Modulated Fe (II) Complex for TADF-Assisted Multiphoton Lifetime Imaging: Concurrent Apoptosis Monitoring and Quantification
articles.abstract: The application of luminescent iron complexes in bioimaging is severely constrained by ultrafast excited-state deactivation and cellular background interference. Herein, we present [Fe(imp)2]2+, the first Fe (II) complex that enables the emergence of both three-photon excited fluorescence (3PEF) and thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF), accessed via stepwise substitution of terpyridine with N‑heterocyclic carbene (NHC) ligands to circumvent the intrinsic drawbacks of traditional Fe‑based materials. Mechanistically, the enhanced ligand field reshapes the relative energetics of the metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) and metal-centered (MC) state manifolds, disfavoring MC-mediated nonradiative decay and opening a thermally activated emissive pathway. More significantly, [Fe(imp)2]2+ serves as an apoptosis-related spatiotemporal cascade-targeting agent, sequentially targeting the plasma membrane, mitochondria, and the entire cell. The TADF-assisted lifetime-resolved signatures render [Fe(imp)2]2+ capable of distinguishing apoptosis from mixed cell death, with a global lifetime evolution spanning 1.1-2.4 ns and a pronounced lifetime heterogeneity of 0.43 ns. Co-incubation of [Fe(imp)2]2+ with anti-apoptotic agents demonstrated that effective cytoprotection is achieved when the probe lifetime dropped below 1.2 ns. This work pioneers NHC-regulated Fe (II) complexes TADF-mediated lifetime probes, offering a new paradigm for transition-metal bioimaging.

articles.title: Transient AMOC weakening during overshoot warming masks committed Greenland ice sheet loss
articles.abstract: Climate mitigation strategies increasingly rely on temporarily exceeding the Paris Agreement’s warming targets (well below 2 °C, preferably 1.5 °C) before drawing temperatures back down through large-scale carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Whether such ”overshoot” pathways can protect vulnerable components of the Earth system — including the Greenland Ice Sheet, which holds enough ice to raise global sea level by more than 7 meters — remains unclear. We use one-way coupled Earth system and ice sheet model simulations to show that temporary weakening of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) during overshoot warming cools the North Atlantic and temporarily mitigates ice loss in southwest Greenland, despite sustained global warming of up to 3 °C. However, once the AMOC recovers, renewed regional warming over Greenland triggers accelerated surface melt under global mean temperatures compatible with the Paris targets. In particular, after AMOC recovery, southwest Greenland becomes highly sensitive to small additional warming above 1.5°C, thus suggesting that this region may have a critical threshold within Paris-compatible temperature limits of 1.5 to 2°C. Our results suggest that, where overshoot pathways trigger substantial AMOC weakening, large-scale Greenland mass loss may emerge only after ocean circulation, and regional warming, recover — meaning AMOC weakening during overshoot would not prevent, but merely postpone, committed ice sheet destabilization.

articles.title: Engineered protein cages with phosphate-dependent reversible opening
articles.abstract: Engineered protein cages are promising nanocarriers for molecular delivery. Reversible and non-destructive control over their structural opening and closing for cargo manipulation remains a key challenge. Here, we present protein cages formed by an engineered variant of Aquifex aeolicus lumazine synthase, called AaLS-POF, that exhibits a rapid and reversible transition between closed dodecahedral and open tetrahedral states in response to phosphate or analogous oxyanions. This dynamic opening-closing behavior, induced by a non-invasive stimulus, enables controlled retrieval and packaging of various cargoes through enzymatic methods. Cryo-EM and mutagenesis identified a key phosphate-binding site and revealed how local recognition of a simple oxyanion is transmitted across subunit interfaces to reshape the geometry of a megadalton-scale assembly. The elucidated molecular mechanism and design principles make the AaLS-POF system a promising platform for engineering customized nanocontainers with desired opening characteristics.

articles.title: Quantum Entanglement Optimization and Prototype Design in Positronic Simulation Frameworks
articles.abstract: We present a simulation-driven framework for optimizing quantum entanglement in engineered positronic substrates. Using high-resolution parameter sweeps of a coupling coefficient g and ensemble time-domain traces, we identify a reproducible global entanglement maximum at g ≈ 32.786 and robust secondary plateau regions near g≈60 and g≈100. We quantify entanglement using concurrence-like measures and present a prototype architecture that implements adaptive feedback to maintain maximal entanglement under dynamic perturbations. The archive includes full simulation code, figure-generation scripts and prototype design notes to enable reproducible experimental follow-up.

articles.title: Complex dynamical regimes of the Tayler-Spruit dynamo
articles.abstract: Author(s): Paul Barrère, Jérôme Guilet, Basile Gallet, and Raphaël Raynaud The amplification of large-scale magnetic fields via the Tayler-Spruit dynamo has been invoked to explain the slow rotation of stellar cores and the formation of magnetars. The existence of this mechanism has recently been proved via 3D MHD numerical simulations of a differentially rotating stably stratified fluid. Using the same setup, we show that the dynamo can produce a wide variety of magnetic field dynamics, including reversals and hemisphericity, by varying thermal stratification. In a fiducial simulation, we interpret the appearance of reversals as the result of the coupling of two large-scale magnetic modes with opposite equatorial symmetries by the symmetry breaking of the flow. articles.abstract: Author(s): Eirini Katsipoulaki, Adlen Smiri, Panagiotis Spiliotakis, Konstantinos Mourzidis, Danae Katrisioti, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Georgios Kopidakis, Zdeněk Sofer, Gang Wang, Emmanuel Stratakis, George Kioseoglou, Iann C. Combining complementary optical spectroscopy techniques with first-principles calculations, the work provides a more comprehensive understanding of how alloy composition influences excitonic behavior and its connection to electronic, vibrational, and spin-valley properties.
